Transcriber's note

The old magician Mong Tham preached this sutra three times, recorded in the following lecture notes: The first version is titled Contemplating Good and Evil Karma Sutra (edited by layperson Ngo Bich Dao, published by the New York Bodhi Mind Study Association in 1989). The second version is recorded as Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma and Retribution Sutra (1999 at Pho Tho Pagoda, Ngu Dai Mountain), and the third version only records the title Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma and Retribution Sutra (2009). Because the Giang Ky version has been translated into Vietnamese for a long time (no translator's name is mentioned), and compared to the second lecture, the third lecture is more detailed, so we chose to translate this version (and title it as Brief Lecture on the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to avoid confusion with the main sutra) to satisfy our desire to introduce the lectures of the Ksitigarbha San Sutra to encourage ourselves as well as our fellow practitioners to strengthen faith, deeply believe in cause and effect, and eliminate karmic obstacles. Develop Bodhi mind and courageously recite Buddha's name.

Lecture 1

Bodhisattvas, I wish everyone good health, good health in body and mind.

Now I will tell everyone why you must study the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, and talk about the historical causes and conditions of this sutra. Since this sutra was translated into Chinese, no one has studied it. The sutra was translated from the Sui Dynasty [by Bodhi Dang], until the Ming Dynasty, Great Master Nguu Ich used his supernatural powers and wisdom to observe Nam Thiem Bo Chau, wanting to find five pure monks, but there were none! He wished to receive precepts, but could not attain them. Therefore, find in the Tripitaka how to achieve purity of precepts. Therefore, he found the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma.

Starting from Master Ngai Ich, because he was unable to invent the contemplation of the wheel of life according to the teachings of King Ksitigarbha in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra; There was no other way, so he used paper to write lots [instead of wooden wheels]. Therefore, there is no way to spread or propagate this dharma. However, he wrote a commentary for the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, named it Contemplation of Meaning. After that, this dharma was also abandoned, no one learned it. Until the time of Master Hoang Nhat, Master Hoang Nhat also specialized in propagating the Ksitigarbha dharma, vowing to propagate the Ksitigarbha dharma. Dharma Master Hong Yi told me: “The Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, the Mahayana Sutra on the Ten Wheels, and the Ksitigarbha Sutra all belong to the Avatamsaka system”. Sometimes we consider the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma as a kind of divination, criticizing the eight characters[1], [that view] is completely wrong, isn't that the meaning! The meaning of this sutra is: Because we are currently living in the Dharma Ending era, karma is deep and heavy, and there is no way to understand causes and conditions, nor is there a way to understand ourselves. Therefore, we must use the contemplation method in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra. This way of contemplation is due to the supernatural power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Even though we don't have supernatural powers, we pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to grant us supernatural powers, which means that by using contemplation in the Contemplation Sutra, you will be able to know the past, you can know the present, and you can also know the future. Therefore, Master Hoang Nhat proposed this method. He proposed, although he did not preach, but because he had the technology, because he studied technology, he relied on the large and small scale in the Sutra of Divining Good and Evil Karmic Retribution to successfully create the Cham Sat Wheel.

The Buddha taught the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, which also has another name, “Dharma method of Roots Gathering”. “Gathering of Roots”: Roots are six senses, plus six sense objects, along with six consciousnesses, that is, Roots, Objects, Consciousness, and Basic Ignorance gathered together. Therefore, this method is called “Can Tu method”. After you learn this method, you will be able to strengthen your own faith. Because right now, our faith is not complete. The Dharma friends present are all disciples of the Three Jewels who believe in Buddha; We often think that we have faith and confidence. But judging from the teachings taught by the Buddha, our faith is just "delightful mind" (a liking mind), not faith! According to the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra teachings about faith, faith has certain standards. Let each of us, our Dharma friends, remember and reflect on whether you have complete faith or not? What is the standard of complete faith? Recognizing that the previous thought evoked evil, then stopping and not allowing the next thought to arise, is considered a Bodhisattva who has faith. A Bodhisattva who has faith can display supernatural powers. Currently, we do not have, cannot control our own thoughts, cannot "if an idea is not right, immediately stop it, do not let it continue". Each Dharma friend can test himself, [to recognize] the strength of your faith, whether it is at this level or not? If you meet this level, you belong to the First Pillar position, have perfected the Ten Faiths, and entered the First Pillar position. Speaking according to the standards of the Avatamsaka Sutra, the First Pillar position will be able to reach one hundred worlds and manifest as Buddha, with quite great magical powers. So let's test ourselves, do we have such strength? No! Therefore, our faith is not complete! We must make our own faith steadfast and ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for blessings.

The reason for the origin of this sutra is that Bodhisattva Firm and Pure Faith (Dṛḍhamati) requested the Buddha. He said: During the End of the Dharma, the time of the End of the Dharma of the Buddha is ten thousand years, or five thousand years, or three thousand years [depending on the different way of saying it in each sutra]. At that time, sentient beings' faith was not steadfast. Not being steadfast means that your faith has retreated, and you cannot [diligently practice] until the end of birth and death and penetrate the Buddhadharma! Your faith is not enough, which means your faith has regressed. How can your faith be steadfast and strengthen your faith? That is the cause and effect of this sutra. Because you have faith, only then can good roots grow and eliminate karma, causing good karma to grow and bad karma to disappear. When the Buddha was in this world, there was this kind of phenomenon. Let alone in this world, the Buddha has passed away for nearly three thousand years. Our faith cannot be steadfast or complete. Why is this sutra so necessary to explain it, yet still unable to spread it widely? Because everyone is disturbed by a social attitude, considering this dharma as a form of fortune-telling, eight-word criticism, and physiognomy! The Buddha forbade [those forms], it was a violation of the precepts. Why when Bodhisattva of Steadfast Faith asked the Buddha to teach, the Buddha did not tell him? Because the Buddha has restricted precepts, not allowing fortune-telling or criticizing the eight characters, everyone knows this! The Buddha told Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to tell [this method], Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has skillful means. Bodhisattvas practice all skillful means that belong to the Bodhisattva path. Moreover, for this method, the Bodhisattva is extremely skillful in means and also has extremely vast magical powers. Therefore, the Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva then told this method.

This method consists of eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, plus eye consciousness, ear consciousness, tongue consciousness, tongue consciousness, body consciousness, consciousness, three times six eighteen, plus basic ignorance, into nineteen items. Therefore, this Root Gathering method is based on your six senses, your six consciousnesses, and the realm of the six senses coming together and gathering in one place. What karma do you contemplate that is heavy? Because all the thoughts we raise will produce results, there is no way for you, so when the cause arises, you should transform it, don't let it feel the effect. That is, as soon as you start thinking, you will be able to stop it. Therefore, this sutra is called the Can Tu method, the meaning is roughly like that.

The Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is broadly divided into two volumes, Upper and Lower. The Upper book is intended to prepare for the Lower book. [This method] is also known as the Can Tu method, also known as the Mind and Earth method. The mind in the Lower volume is based on the Upper volume: Your karma has been eliminated, then you can enter the two types of contemplation, the realm of One Truth. The One True realm is the Avatamsaka teachings, the two types of contemplation are cultivating Concentration and cultivating Hue. At first, you won't benefit from the Upper book, you won't master the practice [taught] in the Upper book, but if you immediately practice in the Lower book, you will absolutely not succeed! When you practice every day, wake up early in the morning, use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate for a while, [to realize]: Currently, do you still have deep or shallow karma, what type of karma is heavy? It is not at all the case that karma in each sense, each door is heavy, it has a focus. After you study this method, you will be able to know which aspect of your body, mouth, and mind [karma] is heaviest in order to repent at the right point. Until you have learned, every morning when you wake up, contemplate once. Please pay attention, what should we do today? How do we destroy our karma? Once karma disappears, wisdom will increase. The more wisdom grows, the more karma is destroyed. These two things help each other achieve. Then you will have wisdom and practice will not be entangled. That is the basic idea of ​​this sutra, I introduce it to everyone a little like that.

This sutra has only two volumes, the Upper volume and the Lower volume. The Upper volume is entirely intended to initiate the practice in the Lower volume. Before we have that foundation, you can consider every single thing in daily life. That is a skillful means, the original intention of the sutra is completely for you to use in practice. There are many people who belong to the two groups of lay disciples (Dharma friends). In daily life, whether you are doing business or pursuing education, you want to choose whether going out the door today is good or not, you can contemplate for a while. After contemplation, if [Contemplation Sat Luan] tells you it is not auspicious. Even though it is not auspicious, but you cannot help but worship Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has taught you a method, which is to recite His name a thousand sentences. After reciting Ksitigarbha's name for a thousand sentences and then doing it, the accident will turn into good luck. Therefore, this sutra is urgently necessary for us.

If it's urgently needed, shouldn't it be widely promoted? There must also be fate! Dharmas arise from causes and conditions; If you don't have fate, you won't get it! Since being translated, no one has preached the sutra, only Master Nguoi Ich composed the work Nghia So, shaman Hoang Nhat created the wood wheel (Chiem Sat Luan), no one commented. Dharma Master Hoang Nhat did not preach, he let me preach, but when he (Dharma Master Hoang Nhat) passed away, I began to preach. It must be fate! There is no fate, even if you want to preach, you won't be able to! What does fate mean? Meaning “promote achievement”. I gave my first lecture at the New York Bodhisattva Association. The Bodhi Hoc Association is a learning association founded by Master Hoang Giac himself, [the audience] are all our Dharma friends. There weren't many people listening to the sutra, two or thirty people came to listen to the Sutra's teaching on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. The first lecture was in 1989. The second lecture was in 1999, exactly ten years later, at Pho Tho Pagoda, Ngu Dai Son. Speaking at that time, the cause and effect was more outstanding, the monastic community alone (on the occasion of the summer retreat) was nearly a thousand, and there were still many lay people. That was the second time, from 1989 to 1999. This time was the third time, also in 2009, roughly ten years apart each time. It's not that I'm lazy, it's because no one comes to me and invites me to preach. I can't say: "Let me explain the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to you!" [If I say so], surely someone will say that I'm not a crazy person, but also an idiot! Buddhism must be requested by others before you can speak it. No one invited you, you preach to people, do they listen to you? The cause and effect that arose this time was introduced by Dharma Master Hoang Giac, and Tran Van Long, Duong Van Nghi, as well as many Dharma friends asked me to introduce the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to you.

If it is Contemplation, then Contemplation is “contemplation” (contemplation, divination), Observation is consideration. You make a prediction and then consider whether [what you just predicted] corresponds to you or not. This sutra always asks for correspondence, [like] finding out whether the numbers match or not! If “Number” matches, it will be effective. This Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is roughly divided into three parts. Historically, for the scriptures translated into Chinese, in the Jin Dynasty, lawyer Dao An divided [the texts of] all the translated scriptures into three parts: The first part is Tu Thuyet, the second part is Chanh Tong, that is, the part that relies on the teachings in this sutra to practice; The third part is Flow. Each sutra is divided like that. That is the rule that shamans preaching sutras follow to judge based on each sutra: Which part of a sutra is Self-Treatise, which part is intended to display the morality in that sutra (Chan Tong), which part is intended to be passed down in the future (Luu Thong), has such a meaning. You've probably heard a lot of these things, I won't go into detail, I'll just tell you a little bit. In this Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, the first thing said is the origin of causes and conditions. The cause and condition that arises is the Self. Now we first talk about Self Part. I'm talking about the scriptures, everyone please watch!

(Kinh) Nhu Thi Van. boundless numbers of great assemblies spoke and spoke about the profound Root Gathering Dharma.
(Sutra: I heard like this: Once upon a time, the Venerable Lady of the Old Lady (Bhagavān, the World-Honored One) is the Omniscient One who resides in the city of Rajagaha, in the mountain of Ky Xa Quat, using his supernatural powers to display the solemn, pure, unobstructed ashram, together with the boundless and boundless masses of people gathered, expounding the very profound Root Gathering Dharma).

This part is often called the Tu Part, which narrates what this sutra has just begun to talk about. Not only this set of sutras, all the sutras that have just begun are “such as the self” (Evaṃ Mayā-śrutam, I heard like this). Every sutra is like that. These words come from the Venerable Ananda, when compiling the sutras, the first thing he did was to make others believe. The six types of [compulsory achievements in the Self-Section of each sutra] are intended to make people believe, “at the moment”, where the Buddha is, to whom he speaks... These things are called the Six Accomplishments of Self-Confidence, [meaning] six types of dharma methods aimed at “accomplishing” that is, achieving, proving, showing that this dharma is trustworthy. The Evidence of Confidence in the Self-Confidence of all sutras says so. Because these words were spoken by Venerable Ananda when he compiled this sutra. “Like this” refers to this sutra, I personally heard this sutra, [saying so] to make people believe. [I say that with intention]: Firstly, it's not fake, because I heard it myself. When did you listen and who said it? Buddha said.

All Buddhist scriptures say “temporary”, for what reason? There is no standard time! “Momentary” means when causes and conditions cause the listener and speaker to meet. Sometimes the Buddha preached in heaven, sometimes in the human world, sometimes in this land, sometimes in another, the time is not the same, no time [standard] can be used to determine the [specific] time, only this expression (“momentary”) can be used to determine the time. That is, when the causes and conditions match, someone speaks, the Dharma Lord, and someone listens (the audience), it is called “temporary”; Time conditions like that!

Buddha is Omniscience, extremely great wisdom, complete with all wisdom. Therefore, He can speak all dharmas, He is the one who preaches the dharma. That is the Cause [ie the Master of Achievement in the six items of Attainment of Faith and Achievement].

Where? At Rāja-gṛha, in Gṛdhrakūṭa mountain. We often call [this mountain] Linh Vu Son. Probably people who have worshiped India have come to Linh Thuu Mountain. The Buddha used his supernatural powers to decorate the Dharma teaching place with utmost superiority and mystery, creating a spacious, dignified, pure ashram with no obstacles. [Just imagine] how many people come to listen, [that place] can accommodate it, you can imagine its vastness.

How many listeners? Countless and boundless masses of people gather together.

What speech? The Root Gathering method is very deep. If it is very deep, it will not be superficial or superficial, it will not be the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind as we often say. Root Gathering is the six senses, the six senses, the six consciousnesses, and the eighteen realms; That is called the Can Tu method. Why add the word “deep” (very deep)? Add the word “deep” to make a clear distinction. Some people think that this is a Hinayana dharma. [Such an opinion] is absolutely wrong; Therefore, it must be said that this method is "profound", six senses, six objects, six consciousnesses, eighteen precepts gathered together. [That is] Root Gathering, according to the scriptures [and explained like that].

But the Buddha spoke all the sutras, sometimes in the Self-Professions including Insight and Distinction. “Nha Thi Van” is Thong, “in Ky Xa Qua mountain, appearing without hindrance ashram, expounding this Dharma” is Biet. Because talking about the Root Gathering method, not talking about any other dharma, is not talking about the Lotus Sutra. The Lotus Sutra is also said at Vulture Mountain. That is Biet, Biet is not Thong, “like thi ta van” is Thong. The Buddha resides somewhere, [this belongs to the Land of Accomplishments] in the Six Cities of Faith. These six types are intended to prove that this dharma is trustworthy, not a fabrication, not an arbitrary statement.

Because when the Buddha entered Nirvana, Ananda asked the Buddha: "After the Buddha's nirvana, when I compile the sutras spoken by the Buddha, how should I say it at the beginning, how should I say it at the end, please decide." The Buddha said: “At the beginning, we must say: As it is, [at one time], where the Buddha lived, what kind of great assembly gathered there”. One is time, one is country, and one is personnel. That is the way to speak according to Time, Place, Matter, and Matter, clearly stating that the dharma is trustworthy. Because Ananda first asked him, the Buddha taught him that at the beginning of the sutras, he should say that. Saying it like that will make people believe. He said like that, other people's beliefs will be achieved.

“As it is” implies: Those words were not said by me, I just said them

listen, I'm just an aggregator. Venerable Ananda clearly expressed his attitude and expressed the words of someone who compiled the sutras. [The reason for establishing] Faith and Achievement is because the dharmas spoken by the Buddha are as vast as the ocean; If there isn't a standard definition, you can translate it any way you like, as long as it doesn't go beyond the sea of ​​Buddhism, it's okay to have the flavor of the Dharma. But Buddha prescribed that rules must be followed to make people believe. Especially in this sutra, the incumbent is Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. Buddha Dharma is as deep as the ocean, only Faith can enter! This type of Root Gathering method is very difficult for others to believe in, so it must be initiated by Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. [Kien Tinh Faith] means pure faith, making others believe and trust! What can you believe? This Dharma is not disguised, it was said by the Buddha himself, aimed at achieving faith, so it is called Faith Accomplishment.

The second thing (“text”) is the listener. This second thing is called Van Thanh Tuu, Van means saying "who heard [that dharma]?" This dharma is trustworthy, but who heard it, "who heard" is Van Thanh Tuu. Venerable Ananda said, the text was spoken by Venerable Ananda: "I personally heard the Buddha, I heard it myself." “Thu Thi” is to say that this Dharma was said by the Buddha, and is trustworthy, [and “Nguyen Van”] is that Ananda clearly said: This Dharma was said by me personally from the Buddha. But there is a question, for example, when we talk about Ksitigarbha Sutra, Ananda is not present. Many of the sutras of Ananda were not present at the scene, so why are they still “like the text”? Because in the future, the scriptures will be compiled to be passed down to the next generation. Any dharma spoken by the Buddha that Ananda has not yet heard, the Buddha will tell him again. For example, in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, Ananda is not present, but is compiled by Ananda. There are also many sutras in which Ananda is not present. Some sutras were compiled together by Manjushri Bodhisattva and Ananda, but usually Ananda plays the main role. Therefore, Van Thanh Tuu represents that I (Anan) personally heard the Dharma spoken by the Buddha. This belongs to Faith Achievement and Literature Achievement.

Time of Accomplishment: All [times] of the dharmas spoken by the Buddha are “temporary”, there is no [specific] time! How can time in heaven be determined according to the human world? As the Ksitigarbha Sutra says in heaven, how do you determine the time in the human world? Therefore, for that time, just say “temporary”. What does “Temporary” mean? Listen and speak. When listening and speaking, that is the time when the Buddha preached that Dharma and the predestined sentient beings were touched by the Dharma; Therefore, the Buddha spoke that Dharma. [The things just said above] are:

1) Faithful Accomplishments (“like thi”).

2) Van Thanh Tuu (“vanilla”).

The speaker is the Master, to whom is the Master referring? [Sutra] spoken by the Buddha, He is the Master of Accomplishment. [Thus, there are four attainments]: Faith Accomplishment, Literature Accomplishment, Time Accomplishment, and Master Accomplishment. The fifth thing is the Land of Accomplishments, that is, where is it mentioned? The Buddha's teachings all have a place. Before each sutra, there are six types of [attestation] like that, called the Six Successes of Confidence. That dharma has six types of achievements, so it is trustworthy! Somewhere? As this sutra was said in Rajagaha city, in Ky Xa Qua mountain. There was a time, a place, a listener, a preacher, and a large audience. The Buddha preached the Dharma to a great assembly of Bodhisattvas, or to a great assembly of Shravakas. This is called Accomplishment. Every dharma conference to preach sutras must meet all of the conditions mentioned above. Without those six types of causes and conditions for achievement, it will not be possible. They are called Luc Thanh Confidence. This is what I heard, so I spoke exactly as I heard. The listener was Ananda, the speaker was Śākyamuni Buddha, the place was Vulture Mountain, and there were many Bodhisattvas; that is They [Accomplishments].

Because I often preach this meaning of “freedom”, which is also the meaning of “becoming a free Buddha”. Why are the six types mentioned above [sometimes] not translated? Why not translate? Sometimes translated, sometimes not translated. "No translation" is due to the type of blessing meaning: Tathagata is forever free from afflictions, He has no afflictions. He is free in all dharmas, so he does not translate. Second, the Buddha's wisdom is like a fire, meaning "burning, able to refine and burn away all your afflictions". [Buddha's physical body] also has thirty-two generals and eighty good qualities, [so] it has solemn meaning. Because the Buddha has completed all the outstanding merits; Due to the complete perfection of all outstanding merits, there are times when there is no translation. When the Buddha benefits himself, he is perfect and complete. The means of wisdom that he develops are all aimed at benefiting others and living beings; It contains a lot of meanings. In the sutras, sometimes it talks a lot [about this part of Attestation], sometimes it doesn't talk, sometimes it talks about the nature, sometimes it talks about the appearance. If we talk about nature, it is usually taught to great Bodhisattvas, like the realm mentioned in the Avatamsaka Sutra. Specializing in corresponding to a certain sutra or treatise, each thing has a different way of saying it. Because we are speaking in general here, so for the six types of the Self-Confidence section at the beginning of the sutra, I will only say a little roughly.

Because this sutra aims to demonstrate what is about to be taught is the Root Convergence method, in one day, we regularly bring our eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, eye consciousness, ear consciousness, mouth consciousness, tongue consciousness, body consciousness, consciousness, gathering six senses, six objects, six consciousnesses, i.e. eighteen precepts, ten The eight realms united together are called Root Gathering. Can Tu is the gathering of all realms to discuss this method. People often consider this dharma to be Hinayana, because the things said are all physical. The Dharma gate of Root Convergence is the form of existence, i.e. Root, Dust, and Consciousness; But that is the meaning in the first half of the series, the second half is not like that, but will separate this Can Tu method to talk about. Each sense, each object, each consciousness contains many meanings. When I talk about the corresponding scriptures, everyone will know this.

To talk a little more deeply, it is talking about our mind, meaning “the mind can change scenes, it will be like Tathagata”. In the Root Gathering methods, each method is the mind; If your mind turns around the appearance of the external realm, you will become a Buddha. But our mind is rotated by the senses, rotated by objects, rotated by consciousness. The eighteen precepts are all mind, but if they are changed, they are not mind. That's delusion. The mind is moved by the scene, you see the mountain, you will be moved by the mountain; If you see water, you will be carried away by the water. The mind is not moved by the scene. Ten years ago, we saw mountains as mountains, saw water as water, ten years in the middle, we saw mountains as not mountains, saw water as not water, ten years later we saw mountains as mountains, saw water as still water. During those three processes, in the first ten years of being an ordinary person, everyone sees mountains and water as mountains and water. In the last ten years, cultivating the path has been accomplished, mountains are not mountains, water is not water. Wait until you reach the Bodhisattva realm, reach the Buddha realm, mountains are still mountains, water is still water. That is the meaning of “depending on conditions”, depending on how all sentient beings speak, then speak accordingly. The Can Tu method has that meaning. Through the example, everyone will understand the meaning of the Can Tu method.

Due to this dharma, that is, from the dharma with form to dharma without form, from the belief in understanding form to reach the goal of formlessness, do not doubt, must transform step by step. The Bodhisattva Kien Tinh Bodhisattva is the one who is in the right position, the cause and condition to request the Dharma, allowing us sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age to be able to rely on the divine power of the Buddha, or rely on the divine power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, to use the Contemplative Wheel Form. Contemplating the Wheel of Light is entirely the divine power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, only relying on the method taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to handle it. We don't have that power, but if we use Contemplation Sat Luan, we will be able to know the past, but we can also know the future.

We have a story that arises, if you observe it, you will know which part, which life, which part has the problem, you will be able to know. How to solve that problem is not just a matter of knowing! In the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught: You want to transform, you want to cultivate the path, you hope to achieve, transform mortals into saints. For example, when it comes to transforming mortals into saints, we get sick and the hospital doesn't treat us well. Sowing the Wheel of Contemplation, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches that it is due to karma, or teaches us to worship, or teaches us to recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, how many sentences, if you do it fully, you will be able to change that karma. Because karma has changed, appearances have also changed. When karma does not change, appearance will not change. But this must depend on you, the first condition is that you must have faith in the decision, don't have three thoughts and two thoughts, it will not be effective.

Because sentient beings' minds are extremely afflicted with afflictions, no matter what they believe, they cannot be steadfast, nor can they be born pure. Now the incumbent is Mr. Kien Tinh Tin; not only steadfast, but also pure, so Mr. Kien Tinh Tin is the one in charge. In the Buddha's meeting, when the masses gathered, Mr. Kien Tinh Tin was the one who initiated this sutra. Because of his great compassion, he saw that sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age, especially in the chaotic world, could not perceive anything clearly. We are confused, troubled, and don't know anything. Out of great compassion, He made a request for us, asking "what method should we use to make them (living beings) know".

(Sutra) Ear Thoi, Association of the Bodhisattva, the name of Kien Tinh Tin, the throne of children, correct robe Respect, heaven and earth must endure, join the palm, and say to the Buddha: "The golden ego tries to be loyal to the people, all desires and wishes are inquiring, four requests to the World-Honored One, I wish to hear and promise."
(Sutra: At that time, in the assembly there was a Bodhisattva named Kien Tinh Tin, from his seat stood up, straightened his clothes, dislodged his right shoulder, and said to the Buddha: "I am now in this great assembly, and I have something I want to ask. Please, World-Honored One, please allow me to ask").

When the Buddha was in the world, he wanted to request the Dharma; First of all, we must ask Him to respond. We are like that now, if you want to ask others to do something, only if they accept it will you be able to do it. Like someone else wants me to preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, I accept that person's words and then speak. That is the meaning of the word “promise” here. It is a kind of ceremony. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva had compassion on sentient beings in the future, and wanted to invite the Buddha to preach the Dharma. He performed a ritual, that is, the monk took off his robe on one shoulder, his head was pressed against the ground, and he bowed to the Buddha. After bowing, he said: "I would like to invite the Buddha to explain, please accept." When He approves, you speak; If you don't agree, you won't be able to speak!

Originally from Nothingness comes Being, what do these words mean? In the world of One Truth, there are no all forms, no words; But how can we reach the One True realm? Before reaching the realm of One True, one must have money and means. The first means is: If you want to reach the One That realm, at least you must have solid faith. We disciples of the Three Jewels believe in the Three Jewels, so you have faith. We have faith, but we are still not solid. Our belief is often said to be “developing the Bodhi mind, practicing the Bodhisattva path”, but [that belief] is founded on illusion, not true! Because our mind does not know the realm of One Truth; Even if I know, I still don't know how to enter! If you want to reach the One True realm, what realm is the One True realm? Steadfast, pure faith! The One True realm has no realm, then it is called the One True realm. Whenever there is a realm, it will not be One Truth. At the same time, if you have faith yourself, you can make others have faith as well. I myself have solid faith, causing all sentient beings to have solid faith. That is Kien Tinh Tin.

We separate to lecture and explain in detail. When your right faith is very solid, thanks to external conditions, conditions can make others pure. Even though we develop a very sincere mind, [still need] your external conditions to be good. The external conditions are not good, your mind will not be pure! Pure mind is the cause, it still needs to be promoted and achieved by conditions, that is, to promote that cause to achieve. We divide it up like this: What you really start with is Kien, the external conditions that promote your achievement are called Tinh. Faith is understanding. The cause of the willow is Faith, the cause of the willow and the cause of the willow is Humanity, that is, what is achieved by the help of fate is called Humanity. That is a detailed division [to explain]. Without division or separation, it is called Kien Tinh Faith, which makes our faith solid. Whenever you encounter some circumstances and become shaken [it is not Kien Tinh Tin], don't waver!

In our lives, you encounter many challenges. No matter which Dharma friend, when you have not yet developed Bodhi mind, it is quite favorable. As soon as you develop your great mind, there are more and more challenges to test! Everyone knows this story, "If you don't receive a demon, you can't become a Buddha" (If you don't get tested by a demon, you can't become a Buddha). Normally speaking, that's how it is. Because, as soon as you develop your mind, all your resentment and harm will arise, causing obstacles to arise in your own nature. Obstacles are karma. We often say obstacles are karma. Karma means the things you have done that will prevent you from developing your mind to cultivate the path in the present. Every Dharma friend is like that, it is not smooth sailing until he becomes a Buddha. There is no such thing! No matter which Bodhisattva or Buddha, they all make many great vows, and "anything that is detrimental to sentient beings, without saving sentient beings, will not be able to become a Buddha". You can only be an Arhat by yourself.

Therefore, the Buddha taught us that, if we have not yet achieved Buddhahood, we must first make karma with others, so that when you become Buddha, you will help others make karma with you first. You only care for yourself and don't help others. That means you don't practice the Bodhisattva path and yet expect to become a Buddha. There's no way!

Pure Faith Bodhisattva has developed Bodhi mind and great compassion, because he has experienced that, his faith is not steadfast. Now he can be steadfast [faithful], having gone through that experience. Like us cultivators, when you first develop your mind, are sincere, sincere, go through one or two trials, you cannot be steadfast, your devotion recedes, until all cultivators have obstacles like that, even bowing to Chiem Sat Sam is obstructed! It's not that as soon as you make up your mind, you immediately become steadfast. How to overcome those afflictions? Based on your studies. The more you read the sutras and treatises, the more methods you will have to treat afflictions and obstacles. Otherwise, you will have no way to fix it! The obstacle has just arrived, if it is interrupted, it won't be for a few days, but I don't know how many years!

I remember I [started] practicing in 1937, after going through many accidents, until I came to America; Can you tell me how many years were between 1937 and 1989? I recently encountered the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. A group of Dharma friends in New York recently asked me to preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. After finishing the lecture, I still haven't practiced [the method of Contemplation again]! From that time, another ten years later, that is from 1989 to 1999, at Pho Tho Pagoda in Ngu Dai Son, people invited me to preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. Some people suggested, I also satisfied their wishes, I also wanted to [preach that sutra]. It's been ten years now, I still haven't practiced again, and I still don't use the Contemplation Wheel. This dharma must be used every day. All the dharmas you have just broken, after being broken, they will continue, back to the beginning. Each of us Dharma friends, no matter what mantras you recite or what dharma you practice, pay attention to the most obstructive thing, the most important thing, [which is] absolutely not to interrupt!
