noi_dung:
Lecture 2

Last time, we talked about "skillfully using the mind", that is, learning the Dharma must be skillful. What is "skillfully studying the Dharma?" This sentence is Manjushri Bodhisattva teaching us to skillfully use the mind, that is, when you study the Dharma, you must skillfully use your own mind. The meaning of “skillful application” is that now you are here, everyone is studying this sutra together. Your current body has no problems, no mistakes at all, but your mind can easily make mistakes. Now while you are studying this sutra, be single-minded, don't think about anything else, external conditions will all fall away. Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us: You must subdue the mind in one place, that is to use the mind skillfully.

The essence of “skillful use of the mind” is the Mahayana teachings. According to Mahayana teachings; First of all, you must practice Contemplation. When everyone comes here, I hear people talking outside, chatting with each other. When you enter this lecture hall, when listening to the lecture, first of all, calm down a bit, contemplate your mind, that is practicing Contemplation. First of all, make your mind that is constantly in turmoil on the outside quiet. That is “listening to the Dharma”, which means that whenever you enter this ashram, the external worldly conditions will fall. The person who listens to the Dharma is like that, and the person who preaches the Dharma is like that. “Dharma Master” means using the dharma as a teacher, there is no “ego, cause” (self and other people), [that is, there is no] Self View and Self Attachment, using the dharma as a teacher, using the dharma to cling. Did the magician say something wrong? If you say the wrong thing or define a word incorrectly, it will be illegal. According to worldly dharma, if one breaks the law, there will be a prescribed law [punishment]. If a magician violates the law to any extent, he or she will receive karmic retribution [corresponding to that level]. Teaching the Dharma incorrectly will result in karmic retribution: “If you say one wrong word in translation, you will fall into hell as a fox for five hundred lives”. So that in the future there will be a fate, I will tell everyone about that story. The meaning of propagating the Dharma of a shaman is “to continue the prosperity of the Buddha's nature, to inherit the Buddha's Dharma”. Therefore, Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us to skillfully use our minds to continue the prosperity of the Buddha race. The meaning of preaching the Dharma is like that!

What about studying Dharma? The speaker must speak skillfully and not go against the Buddha's will. Teaching this sutra, what is the meaning of this sutra? Do not contradict the meaning of this sutra! Those who listen to the Dharma must be steadfast in their own faith. If I say this, everyone will probably be a little skeptical and say: "We came here to listen to the sutra but still can't gain faith?" I bring up the standard of faith and ask everyone: "How can one be considered to have faith?" We can't hope for a high realm, but what about a low realm? Now, within this hour and a half, we will temporarily let go of external conditions, be a little more peaceful, and everyone will study together with one mind. I have nothing to suggest to everyone, but if you use your mind, you still have to reflect for yourself, use your mind to learn, use your mind to connect with the dharma. When the clothes we wear are dusty and dirty, you feel uncomfortable. If in your mind there is a defilement, wouldn't it be the same? When you study the dharma, it is not easy to study and enter! Please understand this meaning! Therefore, now we start learning the main text first. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva requested the Buddha to speak this sutra, which is about the retribution of good and evil karma in the human world.

(Sutra) Buddha's words: “Good man! If you ask anything, you can explain it easily.” chi”.
(Sutra: Buddha said: “Good man! If you want to ask anything, just say it out”).

Now you request, I accept. Buddha praised Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: "Good man! What do you want to ask? What do you want to ask, I will tell you." If the Buddha asked, he would answer, not rejecting all questions.

(Sutra) Pure Faith Bodhisattva's words: “As the Buddha prophesied, the weakness of the ego passes away, the Dharma is destroyed after all, Stating the Dharma towards the end of the world, like the time of the end of the world, sentient beings are blessed, many people are depressed, the country is in chaos, disasters arise frequently, all kinds of misfortunes are interfered with by parents, self-centered disciples have seven good thoughts, only greed, anger, jealousy, pride. When the mind cultivates the essence of the Dharma, at the same time, sentient beings fall into chaos, their minds are often frightened and weak, they are worried about their own bodies and relatives, and are unable to take care of their lives. Because of all the many obstacles and causes, the Buddha Dharma has little faith, and when one attains the path, one attains perfection in the three vehicles, with one's faith one becomes a siddha, one who cultivates the worldly meditation, develops all karma, and is self-sufficient in one's life. If you are like this, you will enter the Nine Dharma Ending Sutras, attain enlightenment, plan your faith, meditate, and be able to understand all karma, and be completely non-existent."
(Sutra: Pure Faith Bodhisattva said: “As the Buddha said before, if we enter After the destruction of the Dharma, the Statue of Dharma is about to end, entering the age of Dharma Ending. During such a time, sentient beings have little blessings, many depressions, many times of chaos in the country, many disasters arise, all kinds of disasters are terrifying, oppressive, and harmful. My disciples lose their good thoughts, only increase in greed, anger, jealousy, and pride. If someone practices things similar to good dharma, it is mainly for the sake of gain and fame in the world At that time, sentient beings saw the world's disasters and chaos, their minds were often frightened, and they were afraid that they and their relatives would not have food and clothing to support their bodies and lives. Because of so many obstacles and conditions, in Buddhism, there were many people who were ignorant and had little faith. Until gradually, in the three vehicles, those who had faith and achievements were very few. All the people who practiced Zen in the world had great karma. knowledge, knowing how to be self-sufficient, will gradually become non-existent. Then, after entering the Dharma-Ending Age for such a long time, the person who attains enlightenment, attains faith, meditation, supernatural powers, etc., all of which are completely gone).

“Pure Faith Bodhisattva's words” means that Kien Tinh Bodhisattva said: “As the Buddha prophesied” (as the Buddha said before), wasn't it true that in the past, when preaching sutras, the Buddha often said like that? “The weak self has passed away, the Dharma has passed away, the Dharma image is facing away”, [meaning] the Dharma no longer exists; The Buddha entered nirvana, the Dharma no longer exists. When the Buddha was in this world preaching the Dharma, the Dharma was five hundred years old, [during that time] those who attained enlightenment, those who attained enlightenment immediately heard the Dharma, and those who became enlightened became enlightened. What about Dharma statues? Although there are few people who witness the Dharma, those who hear the Dharma all have steadfast faith. After that, the Dharma Statue is about to end, the Dharma Statue of five hundred years, the Dharma Image of five hundred years have all ended, reaching the end of time, that is, the Dharma Ending. In other sutras, the Buddha said that the end of the Dharma is ten thousand years, during that time, the Dharma and the Dharma Image will all be destroyed. At that time, sentient beings will have little merit and virtue, very thin merit, and sentient beings will have no blessings.

“Multiple brain failures”: “Death” means failure, whatever you do, there are few successes, many failures. People are born, get old, get sick, and die. People don't even wait until old age to get sick. Many people who are not yet old die. What is the phenomenon of society in the world? “The country is in chaos” means that the country often has frequent accidents and the country is very chaotic. The hardships and tribulations are beyond words! Everyone is in a state of fear, oppressed and harassed by all sorts of things. [Use these things] to imagine that in the Dharma-Ending Age, society had such a phenomenon. This story is very easy to understand, everyone knows!

In general, when the Buddha Dharma entered the Dharma-Ending Age, currently [already after the Buddha's death] nearly three thousand years, it has entered the Dharma-Ending Age for nearly two thousand years. At this time, evil dharma was very prevalent, good dharma and good karma were greatly reduced. If you compare the two sides of good and evil, [you will see] good decreases, evil increases, evil increases! Looking at social phenomena, everyone can understand that afflictions are very heavy, no matter which country it is, it is very abnormal! Because chaos, insecurity, fire, water disasters, storms, earthquakes, and disasters arise constantly on this earth! I won't go into detail about this phenomenon, everyone has seen it!

“My disciples have lost their good thoughts” (My disciples have lost their good thoughts): We Triple Gem disciples easily lose our good thoughts, and our evil thoughts grow easily. Increased greed, anger, jealousy, and obstacles. There are also people who do similar things, that is, like practicing good dharma, meaning that when we do good things, we always mix in a lot of bad things! Why? Because of the pursuit of fame and benefits in the world, the pursuit of fame and benefits is considered the main thing, so the focus on cultivating the Dharma beyond the world is minimized. I think all Dharma friends have seen this phenomenon. I don't need to elaborate, because phenomena in society have shown us this situation.

When Pure Faith Bodhisattva turned to the Buddha to request, he said: Currently, in this world, there is stinginess, greed, jealousy, everyone is skeptical, even among relatives, fathers, children, spouses, they all doubt each other, between people there is no mutual trust, practicing at that time is extremely difficult. difficult. Meanwhile, how can we as practitioners connect with the masses? Because at that time, good and evil mixed together, in the old saying, “the saints were involved”, at that time, there were no saints, there were no saints living with us anymore. At the same time, during that time, thoughts were extremely chaotic, what about beliefs? If you believe in everything, it is not true faith, you will lose true faith. Each person's mind is full of greed, anger, ignorance, jealousy, obstacles, and pride, giving rise to a mind that is disadvantageous to others, trying their best to think of ways to swallow more and take over more. Currently, in this world, materials are limited, if you take more, naturally others will have less. There are many situations like this! Each living being, due to karma, has a very unstable personality, extremely hot-tempered, violent, gets angry when touched, and even punches and kicks others. Why does this type of phenomenon occur? Internal cultivation, that is, cultivating internal virtue, is not enough, there is no internal virtue. Even when making offerings, there are not many offerings to the Three Jewels and not a few prayers to ghosts and gods. That is a real phenomenon, [practicing, doing good deeds] there are many people dedicated to being famous, but actually very few are just for the sake of life and death!

Therefore, this Sutra of Good and Evil Karma analyzes for us to recognize what is good, truly good, and to recognize what is evil; But when you can recognize [good and evil] before your eyes, it is towards yourself, not outward, towards others! Can you know your good and bad karma in the past? Simply put, in the past, goodness was very thick, good karma was very much, in this life, you will have very few accidents, life will be very happy, very calm, very peaceful, always blessed by the Three Jewels. Everyone can see this. If your bad karma is heavy and your good karma is little, everything will be unsatisfactory. At the same time, in your mind you often feel scared, worried about gaining, worried about losing, afraid that what you have will be lost. In fact, it's also very easy to lose! Therefore, our minds are extremely impure, so the sutras advise us to develop Bodhi mind and practice the Bodhisattva path. We often hear our Dharma friends talking to each other like that, and the magicians often propagate like that, hoping that the disciples of the Three Jewels can increase their good mental factors and reduce their evil mental factors.

At the same time, here we specifically talk about the Sangha. When the Buddha was in this world, among his chief disciples, there was one who vowed to specialize in saving rich people. Why? Subhuti specializes in finding rich people, turning to them for alms, and even looking for rich people to beg for alms. What does it mean? He said: "They are rich, it is very difficult to obtain! If they do not cultivate merit again, do not sow the merit field again, they will lose the merit field. While they live comfortably, their hearts are happy; one day, when they lose it, living a miserable life, they will have no way to survive!" That was Subhuti's idea. Therefore, he held an alms bowl and specialized in going to rich people to seek karma. Venerable Kasyapa contrasts, specializing in finding poor people. Those saints did not start at all from whether their food was good or bad, they begged for alms to cultivate blessings for sentient beings. Because Kasyapa said: "If sentient beings suffer in this present life, create good roots for them, so that in the future, they will not have to suffer anymore!" But the Buddha criticized that approach! Specializing in transforming the fate of the rich is not right, but specializing in transforming the fate of the poor is also wrong! [It must be] that whenever you encounter any fate, you choose that fate! While you practice, how you use your mind is very important! Therefore, we often say: “When we develop our mind, let's use our mind wisely.” How to develop our mind? We must develop Bodhi mind.

In the beginning, when I preached the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, there were friends, that is, initially when I preached the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma in New York, USA, the disciple who recorded my teachings, Ngo Bich Dao, raised that question. Specializing in the fate of the rich, or specializing in the fate of the poor, means having a choice. Buddha taught us: "Don't choose! If you meet someone, get married to that person." Developing equality in mind, that is developing Bodhi mind.

Bodhicitta, normally speaking, will be many, but according to the Mahayana Arising of Faith, there will be three main minds. These three minds combine to form the Bodhi mind, which is the direct mind, the deep mind, and the great compassion mind. With all three of those minds, in one thought, when you want to do something, you must use your direct mind, deep heart, and great compassion. But it's not until then that you analyze what you do. We have to be like this to have a straightforward mind, like that to have a great compassion. No! Right in one thought. That is your daily practice, it is not until you face the scene [that you use those minds]. Every day you must often think about your direct heart, your deep heart, your great compassion. When doing daily work, you must think like that, until when you use it, the three minds are one mind. There are Esoteric Buddhism and Esoteric Buddhism, so we often talk about Esoteric Buddhism. No matter what, there is no separation from these three minds, but the words are different!

Therefore, Manjushri Bodhisattva collectively calls [the use of] those things "skillful use of the mind", just saying in general that you know how to use the mind skillfully. Speaking from our side, speaking according to ordinary Mahayana teachings, it would be mindfulness, True Suchness. Anyone who studies the Avatamsaka sect, at the beginning, practices the Contemplation magic called Perfect Emptiness Contemplation, which does not have all the appearances, not the nouns as I just mentioned above. But now we are teaching the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, is it appropriate or not? When I lecture on the scriptures, I will tell everyone. Direct mind, mindfulness, Truthfulness: Direct mind is the absence of even the slightest crookedness. Zen Buddhism says that when one-pointedly practices Vipassana, the direct mind is “mindfulness, True Suchness”, without thinking about anything else, thinking and thinking, you will directly reach the Tathagata realm. According to Hien Giao, it is “mindfulness, True Suchness”, while Zen Buddhism says “clear mind and see the nature”. Clear mind and see the nature is mindfulness, True Suchness. We recite Amitābha Buddha, people chant Amitābha Buddha, what mind do you use to recite? Direct mind, mindfulness, Truth. Amitābha Buddha is me, I am Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha is me. That is direct mind, mindfulness, Truth. Deeply reciting Amitābha Buddha means going one step further. "Buddha is the mind, the mind is Buddha. Buddha is our mind, our mind is Buddha", this kind of explanation is called "deep mind". The inner mind means that all the good dharmas we have practiced do not exist, it is only our mind that manifests. Regardless of great goodness or small goodness, they are inseparable from one mind. Goodness is neither great nor small. Giving alms to others of one coin, giving alms to others of ten thousand, or one million dollars, are all equal, there is no more or less, no big or small. That's the deepest heart. Without distinction, our mind is the alms giver (the alms giver) and the mind of the alms recipient (the alms recipient) are equal, there is no alms giver and alms recipient. That is a deeper manifestation! Direct heart, deep heart, great compassion: “Great compassion” is universal compassion, giving alms to all sentient beings. Can living beings achieve it or not? It just depends on your mind. If your mind gives alms to sentient beings, sentient beings will be able to be blessed.

I just said “developing Bodhi mind”. It is necessary to complete all three types of mind, the three minds are unified, then it can be called “develop Bodhi mind”. We often say “develop Bodhi mind”, simply put, it is Enlightenment, Bodhi is Enlightenment, that is, the mind of enlightenment and understanding. When the mind of enlightenment clearly understands, we and others will both benefit, up to the point of no self, no human, no sentient beings, no fake life, these three minds are complete in one thought. When you explain, you analyze it like that, but when you apply it, the three minds are one mind, right in one thought. In normal times, you practice visualization, the three minds are one mind. When I studied in Tibet, we always spoke according to Tantra. [In Tibetan Tantra], the first mind is called renunciation, which has the same meaning as direct mind, mindfulness, True Suchness. However, Tantra teaches: First of all, you must put everything down, you must leave. If there is one thing or one thing attached to the world, you will not be able to leave! That is, the mind of renunciation is free from all attachments, not only for oneself, but also enables all sentient beings to be able to renounce. Therefore, why is it called Honey? The profound meaning of Secret is that, for example, when talking about the mind of renunciation, it will cause all sentient beings to renounce.

When I recite Amitābha Buddha, hoping to be born in the Pure Land, I hope that all sentient beings who are suffering in this world and I will be born in the Pure Land at the same time. That person recites a sentence of Amitābha Buddha, not because he wishes to be reborn in the Pure Land, but rather hopes that all those who are suffering and suffering will be born with me at the same time in the Pure Land. That is great compassion! According to Tantra, the first mind is the mind of renunciation, the second mind is the mind of great compassion. In the Existential Teachings, it is said that the third mind is the mind of great compassion, different in order, because Tantric Buddhism adds the mind of Prajna. I was taught in Tibet that way. The mind of renunciation, the mind of great compassion, ourselves have the mind of renunciation, allowing all sentient beings to be able to renounce. The meaning of that wish is great compassion. While he himself had just prayed for renunciation, that person did not think that his own renunciation was complete! Whenever I wish to renounce, I hope that all sentient beings and I will renounce at the same time, causing all living beings to renounce. That is true compassion. We often say that "great compassion is not a loving view, it is not a feeling", but is a Dharma precept of the mind. Must understand this principle! It's not acting based on feelings, it's not acting out of infatuated love. Why? The third mind is Prajna. Prajnaparamita is wisdom. Prajna means wisdom, translated into “wisdom”. People who are full of great wisdom will wish to achieve the achievements of all sentient beings, hoping that they will reach the other shore.

Therefore, with all these types of minds, you visualize all the signs of the world. Visualizing the world's appearance will change the world, from within your mind, the world will change. Therefore, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva saw all kinds of disasters in this world, then thought about how to change them, make living beings know good and evil, and then penetrate them. Above, I just mentioned the goal, the next part of the text talks about the method, that is, what measures must be used to achieve that goal. Therefore, Bodhisattva Firm and Pure Faith (Dṛḍhamati) spoke again to the Buddha.

“At that time” (at that time) means that while this world is in turmoil, shaking, insecure, sentient beings see all kinds of disasters and chaos in the world, their minds are often frightened, they have a feeling of panic in their hearts, they are worried about themselves and all their relatives, even about food and clothing in life. Neither is there enough food or food to sustain one's life. The causes and obstacles of such sentient beings are even more numerous. Can they still believe in Buddhism? Those who are ignorant in Buddhism have little faith, that is, they say their karma is very heavy and do not believe in Buddha. Even if you believe but don't believe, can you still attain enlightenment? There will be few people who believe in Buddha, there will be few people who do good deeds, there will be few people who practice the Way, and there will be very few people who attain enlightenment, even none! At that time, among the three vehicles, there will gradually be very few who have accomplished faith. Regardless of Hinayana, Middle Vehicle, or Mahayana, no matter which dharma, belief cannot arise. Learning to meditate in the world, developing magical karma, knowing self-sufficiency, will gradually become non-existent, essentially non-existent. Those who attain supernatural powers and wisdom do not exist in this world, nor do those who know the past and attain Sufficient Life. That is called the end of the Dharma, people who attain enlightenment, people who cultivate the Way, practice Zen, and steadfast faith, all of it is gone. That was the phenomenon during the Dharma Ending period, now we are very close [to that state], although we have not yet reached [that level]. [Currently], there are still many friends who believe in Buddha, and many people who study Buddhism. The end of the Dharma is ten thousand years old, now we are only one or two thousand years old, we have not sunk to that depth yet!

At that time, not knowing the essential dharma, that is, not knowing the important way to escape the three evil destiniess. Studying Buddhism and practicing to escape the three evil destiniess, there is no one who does not know [that]. If you don't know, how can you practice? If you don't know, you won't be successful in cultivating! People at that time (Dharma Ending Period), had extremely slow mental capacity, and were ignorant people. In other words, there is no wisdom. Regarding Buddhism, there is no belief, or little belief, until there is no superior fate. In other words, there is no superior fate for monks, no meeting good fellow monks, nor meeting a famous teacher to teach, no superior fate for monks!

Not only is there no one who has achieved the One Vehicle, the path and fruition of the three vehicles, Small, Middle, and Great, are completely gone. Have you heard of anyone attaining enlightenment at this time? Very little heard! I have been a monk for eighty years, I have met people who have attained enlightenment, and think that there are not many people who have attained enlightenment! In my mind's eye, there are roughly a dozen of the venerable monks I respect; But those dozen people did not attain enlightenment, nor did they tell me that in this life they had attained Arhatship, up to practicing the Bodhisattva path, and attained enlightenment, I just thought that [they had attained enlightenment]! As we know, in the Tang Dynasty, there was a Taoist Lawyer who attained the Four Fruits of Arahantship. There was a god who proved it and offered food to him. That god said he had attained the Four Fruits. But in this world, there are still great Bodhisattvas that we do not recognize. They appear not much different from us. In fact, They are completely different from us.

During the Dharma Ending period, although there were few people who attained enlightenment, Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteshvara, Ksitigarbha, and Maitreya were all in the human world and did not leave the human world. Are we aware or not? That depends on each person's merit and wisdom. You personally have merit and wisdom and will meet. You don't have the cause of merit and wisdom, so you won't recognize it. Because here, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva said, His main purpose is to make us clearly understand good and evil, guide good, and eliminate evil. He turned to the Buddha to request for this reason. The Buddha did not speak to him, but told him to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In the next section, we will talk about this again.

In the question of Bodhisattva Firm and Pure Faith (Dṛḍhamati), [the reason for] this question is because the Buddha often said, Buddhist scriptures often mention the end of the Dharma, what are those phenomena? However, Kien Tinh Tin repeats what the Buddha said so you don't forget. That's what it means. Now, the time has come, what should we do to make those people enlightened, have dharma to rely on, have dharma to be able to learn? Therefore, in the previous section, I pointed out that Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us to "use the mind skillfully". That is what I base on the teachings in the Avatamsaka Sutra. In the Pure Hanh chapter, Manjushri Bodhisattva said, when we study the Dharma, we must know how to study! What is knowing how to learn, what is not knowing how to learn? At what level can one be considered to know how to learn Buddhism? The Buddha taught us to "use the mind skillfully", that is, Manjushri Bodhisattva taught us "use the mind skillfully". But when it comes to using the mind, we don't know how to use it. Must learn from Manjushri Bodhisattva in the Pure Conduct chapter of the Avatamsaka Sutra. Among them, there are more than a hundred types of [pure conduct]. How you use your mind will be a skillful use of your mind. But saying and doing are very difficult to match. If we speak and act, that is, the language and conduct are appropriate, until the mind can guide the conduct, the conduct can open the mind, it will be even more difficult to have!

First of all, we must let go of greed, anger, and ignorance. We recite every day, our Dharma friends must recite every day. We have not yet let go of our greedy mind! No matter what you are greedy for, if you have attachment, it will not be easy to see from the outside. Previously, in a temple, there was an old monk who practiced very well. From the outside, it appeared that he practiced very well; But greed cannot be abandoned! It's an old story. Accumulated for decades, all the money saved, at that time using scrap silver, the Master had it cast into a block of great yuan treasure (silver coin), put it on his belt, and never left it when he went to sleep. One time, when the Master urinated, he was a bit careless and the strap broke. Because the monk wore silver [for a long time] without changing the string, the rope tied to his back broke. As soon as the wire broke, the heavy block of silver fell into the toilet and disappeared! In temples and pagodas at that time, the toilet was a large thatched tent, unlike the [small toilets of today]. The toilet [as it is now] won't fall off! The silver fell into the septic tank, what should I do? That old monk couldn't let go, kept saving for so long, and died with his money. The monk still has moral power and a certain amount of practice! Having died, he turned into a black turtle, crawled into the dung hole, and held that silver bar. Hugging that silver coin, the monk again told the visiting monk in a dream, saying: "Because I can't let it go, because of attachment I have fallen. Now please help me, save me." In the dream, [the visiting monk asked]: “How can I save you?” "Please hire someone to clean out that dung hole. After cleaning, take that silver coin as payment, and give the remaining money to the Sangha's son to repent for me." The knowledgeable teacher immediately followed that idea and did it for him. Having finished, he was saved and liberated, but he still had some practice. Besides greed, other practices are still very good. Without other techniques, it would be impossible to tell the dream to the visiting monk. That's an old story.

Therefore, when we practice diligently, can you check whether your own body and mind are particularly focused on anything? Why do I tell that story? The monk's concentration and all his energy were used to accumulate money. If it wasn't the most focused thing, if it wasn't focused on one scene, this phenomenon wouldn't exist. Why not use that concentration on one scene to recite Buddha's name? There is no such good root. For all of us, when it comes to our practice, we either recite Buddha's name, or we specialize in one practice, or we chant sutras, chant the Diamond Sutra, every day without interruption, forever. That is called “force”. Even if you recite an Amitabha Sutra, when you die, you will absolutely be reborn in [Ultimate Bliss], what are you afraid of? Interruption! Interrupted chanting. For us practitioners, if decades of years are the same as one day, we can specialize in one practice! I met a person, I won't name him or say who he is, who is the current person. As for Buddha, would you say whether he believes or not? I don't believe it! Do you [see] him not believe? He recited the Great Compassion Mantra. I heard him chanting the Great Compassion Mantra, chanting it so much that I was blind, not knowing what he was chanting the Great Compassion Mantra! But he recited the same thing for decades, lived to the age of ninety, still eating meat, not vegetarian, but when he died, extremely alert, he was probably ninety-three years old! He instructed his children to write a will: "I'm about to die, I'm about to leave, I won't eat anymore. You guys help me invite the masters to come and recite the sutras. Just recite the Great Compassion Mantra for me, don't recite anything else!" Besides believing in Mantra Dai Bi, he doesn't believe in anything else! He can know before he dies, he knows he's about to leave. Others also told me that when he passed away, he was extremely wise. He said Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara came to lead him, came to call him along, and continued to lead him. Although he did not mention the Pure Land, he recited the Great Compassion Mantra, and Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) saved him. Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) led him away.

We are people who believe in Buddha very much, I also believe very much. Don't worry about all his other mistakes, don't pay attention! He chanted the Great Compassion Mantra for several decades like a day; As long as you have one practice in the Dharma, that is called “dong”. Just afraid of what? Practicing this method today, practicing that method tomorrow, or interrupting, will not be effective! In this time of the End of the Dharma with the five evil defilements, we must penetrate one subject, no need to study it in depth! You recite a single sentence of Amitābha Buddha, until now, without a single day of interruption, Amitābha Buddha cannot even receive you? But you must rely on the teachings of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, just reciting the Buddha cannot be, “Remembering the Buddha, reciting the Buddha, and definitely seeing the Buddha” (remembering the Buddha, reciting the Buddha, and definitely seeing the Buddha). You recite with your mouth, but in your mind you still have to think. The mind that thinks is called “remembering the Buddha” (remembering the Buddha). The mouth recites the Buddha's name, the mind thinks of the Buddha, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva said [practicing like this], you will definitely be able to see the Buddha. That is, in the twenty-five methods of Perfection of the Shurangama Sutra, Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva said that he had attained the method of [Buddhist Recitation] Perfection, which is “recollection of thoughts”. Because these phenomena existed during the Dharma-Ending Age, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva saw that this evil life had not ended and continued. The evil karma of sentient beings is getting heavier and heavier. At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva saw [this], what did he say in the future?

Asking Tathagata, using the iron river method, enlightens and transforms the path, the soul gives birth to faith, and overcomes mental breakdown. Of course, sentient beings are subject to evil, many obstacles, and regression of good intentions. In the midst of this world, beyond the world of cause and effect, doubt arises, and one cannot persevere in pursuing good dharma. Like this, sentient beings are sensitive and saveable. World-Honored One, All Kinds of Wisdom, wish to promote expediency and understand what the simile is, to be free of doubts, to eliminate all obstacles, to gain faith and increase, to follow the vehicle, to quickly plan without retreating?
(Sutra: This one is for those who have a little good root in the evil world when the Statue of Dharma is about to end and in the End of Life Dharma, I asked the Tathagata to establish a means to enlighten, educate, and guide them, to help them develop faith, except for mental breakdowns. Because those living beings encounter evil times and many obstacles, they will lose their good mind towards worldly and extra-worldly dharmas, many times they will have doubts, and they will not be able to steadfast their minds and pursue good dharma. Such sentient beings are pitiful and worthy of salvation Conveniently teach them, make them leave the trap of doubt, eliminate obstacles, increase faith, rely on which vehicle will quickly achieve non-regression?)

This is because in the evil future life, the Statue of Dharma is about to end, our time of Statue of Dharma has ended, which is the end of the Dharma. “Updating the End of Dharma with few good roots” (And in the End of Dharma there are people with few good roots): Now we all have good roots, but we read and recite the Mahayana sutras, which means the good roots are very deep. The request of the Bodhisattva of Pure Faith is due to this meaning. In the age of the five defilements and evils, the Dharma Statue has ended. Entering the Dharma-Ending Age, there are still a few people with good roots, that is, friends with good roots. What means should we use to educate and guide them. He wished to invite the Buddha to preach the Dharma, also to invite the Buddha to speak to everyone, to make them have faith, to be able to make their faith steadfast, without failure or sadness. Because at that time, those sentient beings encountered evil times during the Dharma-Ending Age, with too many obstacles. Because there are many obstacles, even if they develop a good mind, they cannot bear to be crushed and will lose their good mind.

Each of us Dharma friends should remember, how diligent we are, are we thinking about birth and death for twenty-four hours? I don't do that, but every day in general, I have to think about it several times, not every twenty-four hours, but when I sleep, I absolutely think: Whether I can get up tomorrow or not, it's not certain! Maybe, if you sleep then you die, no one can guarantee your life! Just remember a little, what did we do today, did we leave the Three Jewels quite far away, or did we rely on the Three Jewels very close? Whether it's far or near, I understand it very clearly! Today, when reciting the Buddha's name, worshiping the Buddha, reciting sutras, or hoping to help all sentient beings, every thought brings forth a mind of great compassion to save sentient beings. Is that mind many, or does it raise greed, anger, and ignorance, for the sake of one's own reputation and benefit, for the sake of keeping one's own body healthy? Which mind accounts for the most?

Therefore, the Bodhisattva Firm and Pure Faith (Dṛḍhamati) asked the Tathagata, in the Dharma-Ending Age, for sentient beings with few good roots, what skillful means must be relied upon to lure them neither to lose faith nor to lose their good mind. So that there is no doubt about the dharma of cause and effect in this world and the world beyond, is there any kind of dharma that eliminates doubt for them? Because they have doubts, they cannot be steadfast in their faith and pursue good dharma. This type of living beings is the most pitiable! The Bodhisattva of Pure Faith turned to the Buddha to make a request, creating the main causes and conditions to arise. That means that we living beings in the Dharma-Ending Age have doubts, cannot steadfastly believe in our minds, and also cannot steadfastly seek good dharma. Therefore, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva has the most compassion for this type of living beings. Therefore, he turned to the Buddha to request. We ourselves feel that every Dharma friend can compare: Whatever sutras or dharma they preach, they all aim to make us do them, not just talk! What's the benefit of just talking? It is said that we sow good roots, but sowing good roots is not trustworthy! It's best for you to practice and then you can achieve it. People say "this table of food is very delicious", you don't eat it, how do you know if it's good or bad? You must eat! You are very hungry and refuse to eat, what should you do? Still not achieving anything, hungry, still hungry!

Now we reduce the good roots. Maybe there are some Dharma friends, I heard that many people are very satisfied, thinking that their own faith is very complete. I don't criticize them enough! The Buddha's words are intended to teach us the method, not for us to arbitrarily define. You yourself can use the Holy Doctrine, that is, use the sutras and dharma spoken by the Buddha to compare and see if you have reached that position or not? If you haven't reached that position, it means your faith is not enough. Believe it or not? If you don't believe it, just use the scriptures to compare it! How can one be considered a Bodhisattva with faith? There are standards! Realize that the previous thought is evil, then stop it, do not let the next thought arise; That proves that you have participated in the Faith, are true disciples who believe in the Three Jewels, believe in Buddha, believe in the Dharma, and believe in the Sangha. If you do not participate in Faith, then you must cultivate faith. But this story has the Holy Doctrine, that is, there are all the words said by the Buddha for you to compare. Even if you are not yet complete in Faith, can you escape birth and death? Is it possible to not rotate in samsara? Speaking according to the Avatamsaka Sutra, relying on the Bodhisattva of Faith can recognize that our thoughts are not correct, know that the previous thoughts are evil, then stop and stop the later thoughts from arising. If my faith is complete, faith has been achieved!

Faith has been achieved, what kind of scene is that when participating in the First Pillar? Generous divine powers. Do I have faith or not? To what extent is divine power extensive? You can manifest as a Buddha in a hundred worlds and save sentient beings. The Avatamsaka Sutra teaches like that, I'm not saying it arbitrarily. That is called “The Ten Faithful Minds” (Having perfected the minds belonging to the Ten Faithful status). Now we are the “delightful mind” (the mind of liking), with great confidence and great liking for the Buddha Dharma, but not yet able to participate in the Faith. We cannot "The previous thought has just raised evil, then stop it, not allowing the next thought to arise". If any Dharma friend feels that he or she has no evil thoughts, pure good thoughts, and not a single evil thought arises, you have complete faith. If you don't have it, if you don't enjoy it with someone, you'll still get angry. So that's not possible!

Therefore, in the worldly conditions, in the suffering of birth, old age, illness, and death, especially while sick, when the illness is serious, when the suffering is extreme, you soon forget about Buddha and only think about eliminating pain. Can you trust Buddha to eliminate disasters for you? You must have that faith and surrender everything to Buddha and Bodhisattva. If you have that faith, you don't need to worry about your illness. There are two cases: One is that your life span is over and you have to die. After death, you will be reborn in a good place, will not fall into the three realms, and will not fall into the three evil realms. Now that the Buddha's disciples are present, having received the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, when they die, they absolutely will not fall into the three realms! You must believe this, don't doubt it, be steadfast in your faith without doubting, forever and ever progress higher. But if you can vow to be born in the Pure Land, [but want] to be able to make that vow when you die, then in normal times, you must train. What are the training methods? At night, when you are about to sleep, when you are about to sleep but still not asleep, you must make a vow.

The first thing is that you must bring what you did today, something in accordance with Buddhism, to increase faith, to benefit sentient beings, I pray it will grow. Whatever we have done wrong today, thought wrongly in our mind, said wrong words, we turn to the Three Jewels to repent, then sleep. Every night, you must do it. In the morning, it cannot be said that we do everything according to the Dharma! Even if we have not yet entered the Faith, we have not yet reached the First Pillar, every day we should not procrastinate, repent on the same day, make a vow on that day, it will gradually grow. You make your vows for a long time, and when you are about to sleep, you seem to vaguely make your vows. I often have that happen, but I'm not very alert, I forget it, but after a while I think about it, I quickly make a vow, and then I don't forget it anymore. You say it's fake, but this is more real than anything else, more real than eating food, wearing clothes, until you die, you will be able to gain great benefits. Hope everyone doesn't forget; That's called "skillful use of the mind".

Pure Faith Bodhisattva said to the World-Honored One: - World-Honored One! He is a great merciful and compassionate being, he is one who has all wisdom, he is all-wise. Can he practice expedient means or not? Speak out a method of skillful means, making everyone gain benefits. Because sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age have too many doubts, [the doubts are called] “net of doubt” (net of doubt), causing [beings] to leave the net of doubt. Simply put, when I was at Wutai Mountain, many people came to the mountain and asked me: "Master! I have been reciting the Buddha's name for so many years. When I die, can I be reborn in the Pure Land?" I said: "Why do you ask me that?" That person said: "I have been reciting Buddha's name for many years, but it seems to have no effect at all, and there is no response. So when I am about to die, can I be reborn or not?" I replied: "I cannot be reborn!" That person asked: "Why?" I said: "You ask me 'can I be reborn or not' because you have doubts. Being born in the Pure Land has no doubts. If you still doubt 'can you be reborn', that means you don't believe! From now on, you must eliminate that idea, 'birth is a decision to be born!' If you have doubts, you will really not be able to reach [Ultra Bliss]. Basically you have not made up your mind! You still have doubts about the Buddha Dharma." How can anything else be achieved?”

Therefore, I advise my friends: "No matter what Dharma you study, do not doubt!" Doubt is the biggest obstacle, always doubting yourself: "My strength is not enough, my karma is very heavy!" I often hear each Dharma friend tell me that his or her karma is very heavy, [that person] believes that his or her own karma is very heavy, and does not believe that his or her own Buddha nature and Buddha's Buddha nature are not two or different. Why don't you believe it? That is a sign of heavy karma. Isn't that a sign of heavy karma? I believe my friends, if you had any doubts before, I relied on what the Buddha said, I relied on the teachings in the Avatamsaka Sutra, I did not deceive you. First of all, you should eliminate doubts. Doubt is one of the ten afflictions. Regarding Buddhism, you should not have doubts. Suppose you have doubts, you won't be able to learn anything, you won't be able to achieve anything! Doubt is an obstacle, doubt, Or (defilement) and your karma causes you to doubt. You have entered Buddhism, please believe in the Buddha's teachings. No matter what the Buddha said, in our mind, there is nothing Mahayana or Hinayana, there is no need to distinguish between that. Do you recite a sentence Amitābha Buddha, is it Mahayana or Hinayana? There are sutras that teach you the Supreme Vehicle. If you recite “Amitābha Buddha is me, I am Amitābha Buddha”, you are the Supreme Vehicle. Small or Great does not depend on the Buddha's teachings being large or small, but on the minds of sentient beings. Regarding Suffering, that is, [Suffering in] Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, if while you endure a little suffering due to an accident, right while you are suffering, your first thought is "due to this suffering of mine, may sentient beings not have to suffer this kind of suffering", the first thought is wishing sentient beings [not to suffer that kind of suffering], that is not Hinayana.

Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, everyone knows, right? As for Suffering, although it is also suffering in the human world, your mind transforms it, that is Mahayana. People with perfect foundation receive the dharma, there is no dharma that cannot be fulfilled. That person is a person with great and perfect qi. Whatever Dharma he hears, he will be perfect. If your mind is very limited, even if it is a Mahayana dharma, if you read Avatamsaka you still cannot end birth and death, not even a Hinayana dharma! Dharma does not have a certain Body. All dharmas are neither Great nor Small; [Great or Small] depends on the mind of living beings. People with perfect foundation receive the dharma, there is no dharma that cannot be fulfilled. You use the Hinayana mind to receive dharma, every dharma is Hinayana! You are skeptical about any dharma, so you cannot enter any dharma. Definitely don't be skeptical, "the spirit of doubt" (makes you leave the net of doubt). But there is one difference: trust Buddha's words, don't get caught in the net of doubt, don't trust anyone else, trust Buddha. Normally, our Dharma friends study the Shurangama Sutra, because that sutra has been commented on by fifty or so people, each of us is attached to our own views and interpretations. Among those who study the Shurangama Sutra with each other, we ourselves become confused! It's best to learn from Buddha, don't let your own doubts get in the way. As your faith grows, you will achieve it very quickly regardless of any vehicle. That is the [intent] of Kien Tinh Bodhisattva's invitation to the Buddha: Is there such a good method that makes all sentient beings have no doubts, that all obstacles in studying Buddhism, obstacles in studying the Dharma, and obstacles in their practice are all eliminated, their faith grows forever, and cultivating any vehicle can quickly reach the state of Non-Regression.

That is the vow power of Bodhisattva Firm and Pure Faith (Dṛḍhamati); Those sentences are His will. He hoped that the Buddha would teach such a good method, causing sentient beings to not retreat and gain benefits. But for us, the feeling about this place will be like this: Every time I talk about, or look at this place, [we realize] that is the great compassion of the Bodhisattva. Because sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age had many doubts, the Bodhisattva asked the Buddha to teach a method that would make sentient beings free from doubt. That method is to eliminate our karma and is the best method, please tell the Buddha. Because Kien Tinh Bodhisattva sees that we sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age are skeptical about everything. It's not that they [inherently like] to be skeptical, but rather that changes in society make them skeptical. As soon as Kien Tinh Bodhisattva made such a request, the Buddha immediately told the Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) Buddha's report to Kien Tinh Faith: "Good ear! Good ear! Enjoy consulting, even like In the heart of the crowd, the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, whose name is written by Ksitigarbha, asked him to ask, and to establish the means, explain, and make his wishes.
(Sutra: The Buddha told Kien Tinh Tin: "Good! Good! Good question." "That's very pleasing to me. Now in this great assembly, there is a Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, named Ksitigarbha. You should ask him about this. He will establish the means for you, explain and explain, and achieve what you wish."

“Buddha advised Kien Tinh Bodhisattva” (Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva): He requested, Buddha answered. Not only did he answer, because the Bodhisattva's request was so good, the Buddha said "good ear, good ear". "Good ear" means "very good". You asked a very correct question, asked a very good question, very much in line with my thoughts, very pleasing to me, worthy of praise! Great praise for Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. After praising, the Buddha should speak. The Buddha did not speak, after praising, he did not speak again. Without speaking, I introduced someone: - Now in this great assembly there is a Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, named Ksitigarbha. You asked this question very well, at the right time, but for that question, I will introduce someone who will tell you. In this Dharma assembly, there was a great Bodhisattva named Ksitigarbha. You ask him about this, he will teach you a method of skillful means to benefit sentient beings. He will give a speech that can satisfy your wishes.

That's speaking according to Facts. If we speak according to reason, why did the Buddha not speak, but instead asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak? You have to read the next part of the sutra to know. This sutra is called Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. The Buddha has set the precepts, not allowing his disciples to divination, cast hexagrams, criticize the eight characters, all of which are not allowed, that is called "wrong livelihood". Bodhisattva asked this, the Buddha knew that in the Dharma Ending period, if you knew how to predict lives, know how to judge the eight characters, know how to predict hexagrams, it would be very easy to help others, but others would use it in evil ways. Regarding this Wood Wheel Contemplation Dharma, the Buddha knew Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva would definitely speak that Dharma; That's why the Buddha said that Mr. Kien Tinh Tin asked very well, asked very cleverly. Bodhisattvas practice expedient means to save sentient beings. Unlike the Buddha, who has established precepts, the Buddha cannot speak. It has that kind of meaning. That meaning was not said by the Buddha, but by my speculation. Why did the Buddha not speak, but instead told Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to contemplate the wood wheel and use the method of [contemplation] of the wood wheel's appearance. In other words, among them are the eight-word criticism and destiny prediction, and among the one hundred and eighty-nine types [of reincarnations]. When I get to the corresponding part of the scriptures, I will explain it to everyone.

That Bodhisattva was named Ksitigarbha. Regarding the title Ksitigarbha, here, we must first say the meaning contained in that title. When we talk about the sutras, we will not say more. Earth is great earth. We understand the great earth; Speaking according to Ly, it is our mind, that is, speaking according to the mind-ground method. The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is a method of the mind. The Mahayana Sutra of the Ten Wheels is the mind-ground method, the Ksitigarbha Sutra is the mind-ground method, and all three sutras are in agreement. Because the great earth contains boundless merit, the things we wear, wear, use, all the lives and lives of sentient beings, all come from the great earth. The Great Earth is the closest beneficial and nurturing parent of sentient beings. Therefore, this Bodhisattva has the title Ksitigarbha. The great earth contains immeasurable amounts, what does that mean? The lives and lives of living beings. Falling into hell, this hell, that hell, and the great earth have the same meaning. At the same time, when preaching the Ksitigarbha Sutra, we said: “There is no hell”. Since hell doesn't exist, why fall into hell? Whenever you commit a sin, there is [hell], can you believe it or not? I can give everyone a simple example as follows: Is there a prison in Tho Thanh[2] or not? No matter who you ask, they always say yes. Are you in there or not? Who has been there? For you, there is none! I went there, shaman Tinh Dieu took me there to talk to the prisoners. The prison in Tucheng, the prison in Taichung, I have been to, but I was not imprisoned, not locked up in prison, but came to preach to them. Fate is different! Even though [those prisons] exist, they have nothing to do with us, so they don't exist! We haven't done anything wrong, hell is "only the mind exists". When you commit a sin, hell is absolutely there. If you don't have that, hell will absolutely not exist! Disciples of the Three Jewels do not fall into hell because of the blessings of the Three Jewels; But if you destroy the Three Jewels, violate the Three Jewels, go against the Three Jewels, you will fall there.

Therefore, this sutra is spoken by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In the Mahayana Sutra, the Ten Wheels also ask about the same dharma. At that time, there was a great Bodhisattva who asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. That great Bodhisattva's name was Hai Hue Bodhisattva. He saw all the floods, all the way to space, all over the dharma realm were floods. At the same time, after the flood, it was completely empty. All the floods in the great world are absent, completely empty. Why? Void Store Bodhisattva arrives. As soon as Void Store Bodhisattva arrived, due to his supernatural powers manifesting, the great earth was completely empty. Hai Hue Bodhisattva comes, the entire earth is a sea, it does not hurt humans, it does not submerge everyone. This is visualized by the story of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's arrival [at Khu La De Da mountain], the earthly realms increased in prosperity and material prosperity. That is due to the Bodhisattva's power. That's what I added!

(Sutra) Thoi, Kien Tinh Tin Bo Satfu said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One, the Tathagata, who is supremely wise, has no thoughts, what does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva speak?"
(Sutra: At that time, the Bodhisattva of Pure Faith said to the Buddha: “World-Honored Tathagata Supreme wisdom, why does he not speak, but wants Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak?”)

The Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva was skeptical and not very happy! He said: "I originally asked the Buddha to speak. Why did the Buddha not speak, instead telling me to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?" At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! You are a supremely wise person, for what reason do you not speak? For what reason do you not tell me? You do not speak, but rather introduce me to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to explain, hoping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to explain?" Bodhisattva has doubts. We listen to this sutra, Bodhisattva Kien Tinh Bodhisattva is a solid faith, a Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, a great Bodhisattva. He requested the Dharma on behalf of sentient beings, because he had great compassion and knew that all sentient beings were skeptical about this matter, so he requested the Dharma from the Buddha on their behalf. The Buddha is Omniscient. He did not speak for himself, but also taught me what is the meaning of asking another Bodhisattva? That means you're already skeptical, and you're even more skeptical!

(Sutra) Buddha's report to Kien Tinh Tin: - High and low thoughts give rise to high and low thoughts.
(Sutra: The Buddha told Kien Tinh Tin: - You should not giving birth to ideas of high and low).

Buddha immediately told Kien Tinh Tin, “Buddha reports Kien Tinh Tin: - The higher and lower thinking of the higher and lower realms”, [meaning] you should not think that all dharmas must be spoken by the Buddha. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and I are exactly the same, there is no high or low. Buddha is Ksitigarbha, Ksitigarbha is Bodhisattva. Because, in the second chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it is written: The Buddha told Manjushri Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva could have become a Buddha a long time ago, but because of the power of his vow, he wanted to save all sentient beings before attaining Bodhi. We all know this. In this assembly, the Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva to say: "Do you think that what I say is correct, but Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's words will not be correct? That's wrong! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is already in the Buddha position, don't give birth to high or low ideas!"

Because all sentient beings do not know the difference between Buddha and Bodhisattva, we think that Buddha is higher, Bodhisattva must be one level lower. That is the psychology of ordinary people! For example, how should we see Manjushri Bodhisattva? Manjushri Bodhisattva is the teacher of seven Buddhas, all seven Buddhas were taught by Him, Bodhisattva is their teacher, Bodhisattva became Buddha a long time ago! There is also Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), we see Him standing next to Amitābha Buddha as an attendant. Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) became Buddha a long time ago! Don't give birth to thoughts of high or low, don't think Buddha is high and Bodhisattva is low! That is the false discrimination of us ordinary people, even Kien Tinh Bodhisattva also makes this kind of distinction! [Indeed], it is He who appears! If He [really] made that kind of distinction, would he still be called Kien Tinh Faith? He achieved steadfast faith and set an example for ordinary people.

If Kien Tinh Bodhisattva did not address the Buddha like that, our minds [would wonder]: "Why didn't the Buddha speak, but had to find a Bodhisattva to speak?" Because we think that Buddha must be one level higher than Bodhisattva. Because we practice and have to go through the Bodhisattva positions before we can become Buddhas. Because of that idea of ​​"high and low", there is the idea of ​​attachment to high and low. Sometimes [Bodhisattvas] are “lobes”. The lobe is a manifestation of his practice at Tich Mon; When he said Tich Mon, he was a Bodhisattva, and at Bon Mon, he became a Buddha. Therefore, in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it is written that Śākyamuni Buddha told Ksitigarbha: "I absolutely not only always manifest the Buddha's body to preach the Dharma in this world, I also manifest the Bodhisattva's body, manifest as sentient beings. In the nine dharma realms, all manifest".

Therefore, we all must have this thought, like Bodhisattva Manjushri transforming into a pig. This story in Wutai Mountain, you see the stories about Manjushri Bodhisattva, there is a story about a pig. Bodhisattva transformed into that pig. How do we know that Manjushri Bodhisattva transformed into that pig? There was an old monk who went to the mountain to worship Ngu Dai Son. When he was about to go down the mountain, he suddenly met an old man herding goats. The old goatherd gave him an envelope and said: "You take this envelope and give it to someone on the way to deliver the letter for me." That person received the letter and accepted the old man's request. [The old man advised]: "On the way, you will definitely meet me!" The person asked for the address, [the old man said] "I don't have an address. If I hear someone call me by the right name, I'll give it to that person." Then, give that person an envelope, instructing him to go to that place, etc. Actually, Bodhisattva Manjushri appeared as a pig. Arriving there, that person held the envelope, heard the pig's owner call the correct name, and saw that it was a pig. The old monk thought: "Regardless of whether it is a pig or a human, just leave it to it." The monk entrusted the letter to that pig named Bo Ha, and I don't know whether he read it or not. The pig immediately stood up straight. Pigs have four legs, they stand upright on their hind legs and then die. That pig was incarnated by Manjushri Bodhisattva. The old monk [herding goats] on the mountain is also the incarnation of Manjushri Bodhisattva, [sending a letter] advising: "You should return." Another person opened the letter and saw only four words "please return". As soon as the pig stood up, it died, showing that it was a holy scene. “Holy realm” is the realm manifested by saints. Whatever scene, whatever status He appears and manifests. Appearance is not true; If true, it is [the effect of] karma.

Therefore, the Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: "You should not have high or low ideas", which means that we Dharma friends should not have high or low ideas. Now I am preaching the Sutra on Contemplation of Karma, but my friends sitting below may preach it much better than me. Don't give birth to ideas of high and low, but be equal.

inconceivable Asaṇṣa-kalpa, the nine-fold ability to guide the Tathagata Yahai, the merit is complete, the original vow is self-sufficient in strength, the power and skill are manifested, and the influence is reflected in the ten directions.

boundless and inconceivable, the Asang-kyūka, was able to cross the sea of All-Wisdom a long time ago, his merits were complete, only by relying on the power of his original free will, his cunning power manifested, silhouetted in the ten directions).

Buddha immediately told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: - This good man. Who is “Tnow man” referring to? That is to say Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The Buddha introduced Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva not to have high or low thoughts. Do you know what Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is like? That good man, from the time he developed the Bodhi mind until now, has gone through countless, boundless, inconceivable Asanga kalpas. Saying "boundless A-sang-kalpas", also adding "inconceivable", that is, there is no form of time, it is very long! He was able to cross the sea of ​​Sarvajña a long time ago, which means he soon became a Buddha. The sea of ​​Nhat Thiet Tri, Tat Ba Nha translated into Nhat Thiet Tri. Sea of ​​Omniscience, complete merit. Why hasn't he become a Buddha yet? By relying on the power of his original vow, he was free. I think all Dharma friends remember the following two sentences: “Hell is not empty, vows are not to become Buddha” (Hell is not empty, vows are not to become Buddha). How do I explain those two sentences? How do people explain? Let me explain so everyone can see if it's true or not! Hell is inherently empty, Ksitigarbha has become a Buddha a long time ago. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas manifest all kinds of bodies; Therefore, he should use the body of a Bodhisattva to save him, so he appeared as a Bodhisattva. Everyone saw that all the Bodhisattvas were dressed in lay clothes, had hair, and wore necklaces of happiness, with jewels all over their bodies, extremely precious. Which Bodhisattva does not have ten noble qualities? These treasures are all priceless, I'm afraid we wouldn't be able to buy them, they're not treasures in the human world!

Why did Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva shave his head? Among the Bodhisattvas, only Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva manifests as a monk, this is extremely special! Therefore, this passage is a clear evidence. He manifests according to the power of his original wishes, don't take it as real! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, from the moment he developed the Bodhi mind and practiced the Bodhisattva path, has gone through time that is incalculable. Asāṃkhya is Infinite Number, meaning "there is no number [to calculate]". That incalculable number spans countless and boundless Asanga kalpas, it will be an incalculable amount of time! Because in the manifestation of all Bodhisattvas, when they appear, the purpose is to help sentient beings gain benefits and be able to save sentient beings, considering that as the main thing. Therefore, Manjushri Bodhisattva in Ngu Dai Mountain appears in all forms. As I just mentioned just now, He is currently a pig, that is not a human being! He can also manifest as a pig and manifest as all sentient beings. Why does He have to appear as a pig? Of course, there is a legend that says: As I just said, that pig's name is Bot Ha. The owner of Bo Ha is special to it, especially respectful of Bo Ha, the living space is all swept clean. That owner raises a lot of pigs, and the pigs are raised to be fat and fat. If Bo Ha wanted to kill a pig, he would walk around it and the pig would come out and let people kill him in an orderly manner. This is unthinkable! That story is still very long, so let me briefly introduce it!

(Sutra) Although the universal journey necessarily kills, always starts industry, but the five defilements and evil worlds bring benefits to heaven. After spending the past ten lifetimes, I dignified the world and matured all sentient beings. (Sutra: Although it roams all over the world, often sparking industry, Paying special attention to educating and benefiting [living beings] in the evil life of the five defilements, also depending on the strength of their innate vows, and also due to the karma of living beings worthy of receiving education, from eleven lifetimes up to now, He has adorned this world, matured living beings. Therefore, in this assembly, His physical appearance is dignified, His virtue is superior, except Tathagata, no one is superior! Furthermore, His teaching career in this world, except for such people Transforming Sand, Contemplating World Sound, etc., none of the great Bodhisattvas can compare. Due to the power of their original vows, that Bodhisattva can quickly satisfy all the wishes of living beings, can destroy all the serious sins of living beings, except for obstacles, making them peaceful in the present).

Buddha said: Although Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears in all Buddha realms, walking throughout all lands, "perpetually gives rise to merit" that is to say, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's manifestation is not far away and has no place. Or in other words, in the evil life of the five defilements, He was in this world, the Sa Ba world that we are in, because of his especially profound karma to save sentient beings. Especially due to the strength of his original vow, the strength of his accumulated vows, his willingness to suffer on behalf of sentient beings, appearing like sentient beings. Therefore, we see that the Ksitigarbha Sutra says that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva manifests more bodies than humans in this world, infinitely, infinitely. He came to countless worlds, but due to the power of His vows, he manifested the appearances of all kinds of living beings, not all of them necessarily Bodhisattva appearances as in the present. When he arrived in hell, he immediately appeared in hell. To what extent is he sensitive? Like our Dharma friends, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has feelings for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and whenever he asks for them, he feels them. I tell a story of induction from the book Ksitigarbha Induction Luc.

A carpenter was traveling and saw a stick in a rotten wooden tent, which looked like a walking stick. He said this stick was very strange, so he picked it up and looked at it: The tip of the stick had a shape engraved on it, but it couldn't be seen, it was black and dark. He then picked up the stick and brought it home, placing it at the head of the bed. He examines every day, there is no affection, and there is no respect for respect at all! I don't know what it is, I just feel that the tree is unusual, that's the fate. Due to karma, he became seriously ill. Severe illness is probably caused by evil karma that has matured and is taken to hell. Having gone to hell, he saw a monk, a monk, coming there. As soon as King Yama saw the monk coming, he immediately got down from the throne and paid his respects to the monk. He saw that the monk seemed very familiar, but he didn't recognize or understand clearly what it was like? Seeing that monk say a few words to King Yama La, the monk left. King Yama immediately told him: "Since King Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told me that you are His Dharma protector, I will let you go back. In the future, you should try to practice." It's like he's dreaming. Until he recovered, he said: "It seems I have never come into contact with that monk, why did he save me?" Suddenly, he saw the monk's appearance on the top of that stick. Wow! Exactly like this! At that time, he no longer considered it a stick and immediately worshiped it. Because he had such a predestined relationship with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva saved him. Let us consider whether our Dharma friends read Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, will Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva save us or not? While you chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and follow it, you will forever think of Him and will forever not fall into the three evil destiniess.
