noi_dung:
Lecture 3

There was a Dharma friend who asked: "The Buddha once imposed precepts, Buddhist disciples were not allowed to practice divination, etc. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva made a declaration. The Buddha also prohibited disciples from displaying supernatural powers to others. Only this Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, just at the beginning, the Buddha used his supernatural powers to display an ashram. spacious, dignified, pure, unobstructed. There must be a deep meaning in it, I respectfully hope that the old magician will kindly explain it."

In Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Three Sutras, all are manifestations of supernatural powers. Everyone knows that when the Buddha spoke the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it was not in the human world, but in Dao Loi Thien. Furthermore, when the Buddha spoke the Ksitigarbha Sutra, there were no Sravakas, no Arhats, all were great Bodhisattvas. From the first chapter, Manjushri Bodhisattva, to the thirteenth chapter, Void Store Bodhisattva; That is the Ksitigarbha Sutra. That sutra is full of Bodhisattvas, there are no Arhats. The Buddha established the precepts as the Shravaka dharma. I think everyone has received the three great precepts at the same time, what does the Bodhisattva Precepts teach us? The Bodhisattva Precepts are intended to treat the mind, but we in Dong Do, in this country, receive three great precepts at the same time. Among all four of our disciples, there are many who have received the Bodhisattva Precepts, but violate them every day. Can we keep the Bodhisattva Precepts or not? That is the mind, the world of mind! As long as you just start thinking, you have violated the precepts. We also receive ten important precepts and forty-eight minor precepts, that is, the precepts spoken by the Sambhogakaya Buddha to the Nirmanakaya Buddha, said in the Truly Solemn Sambhogakaya. Vairocana Buddha spoke to hundreds of thousands of Śākyamuni Buddhas. Hundreds of thousands of Śākyamuni Buddhas spoke the Bodhisattva Precepts to hundreds of thousands of Sakyamuni Buddhas. Hundreds of thousands of millions of Śākyamuni Buddhas were born in the human world and all in all lands said the Bodhisattva Precepts. How do you fellow monks understand this? Therefore, the Buddha made the precept "not allowing Buddha's disciples to use their supernatural powers to reveal to others", which is the Hinayana teachings. Mahayana teachings are all about Bodhisattvas. Bodhisattva Manjushri in Wutai Mountain often displays supernatural powers. Therefore, we must use the Bodhisattva mind to learn the Bodhisattva Dharma. That's one thing.

But due to the name of the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, people see it as fortune-telling, but it's not! Wait until we explain the scriptures and you will understand them thoroughly. You must bow to Chiem Sat Sam before you can use Chiem Sat Sam. Bowing to Contemplation Sam means bowing to the Buddhas of the ten directions. If you bow to Chiem Sat Sam, you will attain the pure appearance of the wheel. The purpose of using the Contemplation Wheel is to achieve pure wheel form. Having achieved the pure form of the wheel, you can practice the two types of contemplation in the One True realm. When you contemplate the True Form, contemplating the True Form of all dharmas is an inconceivable realm. In the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, hearing that word seems to be a form of fortune-telling (fortune-telling, hexagram drawing), is not so! You're wrong, you're thinking wrong. After listening to the Contemplation Sutra, you immediately understand clearly that you must bow to the Buddhas of the ten directions, bow to all Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, bow to the ten directions of Dharma, and bow to all the sages and monks in the ten directions. That is called the Dharma of Contemplation and Contemplation. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, wait until you finish listening to the sutra and you will understand, it is not arbitrary, it is not a hexagram, it is not a trigram, it is completely different!

As for the noun Contemplation, what is contemplation (contemplation, consideration)? Good and evil karma. Furthermore, when speaking this Dharma, in the previous part, everyone also heard a passage of Self-Compassion, Steadfast Faith Bodhisattva directed to the Buddha, He said that in the Dharma Ending Period, the thoughts [of sentient beings] are extremely chaotic, the minds of sentient beings are extremely chaotic, do not know how to do it well? It is true that while surrounded by karma, no matter what dharma you practice, your achievements will be very little. I don't say this casually. It has been eighty years since I became a monk, and I have heard with my own ears that "this person has attained enlightenment, that person has attained fruition", but in this Dharma Ending world, there really is no such thing! Don't say that in the present period, right during the time of Great Master Nguoi Ich, that is, at the end of the Ming Dynasty, several hundred years ago, he wanted to become a monk. He observed Nam Jambudvipa (this world of ours), wanting to invite five pure monks to receive the bhikkhu precepts, but he could not do it, absolutely none. Therefore, he searched in the Tripitaka for a way to attain purity of precepts, so he found the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. Master Nguu Ich studies and studies very seriously. Could it be that he proposed divination and criticized the eight characters? No way! Furthermore, several hundred years after Master Nguu Ich, no one proposed the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. Dharma Master Hoang Nhat inherited Master Nguoi Ich and propagated the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, because Master Nguich Ich could not create the Contemplation Wheel. He did not have that skill, so he used paper to write lots to draw lots, unlike the magician Hoang Nhat. Master Hoang Nhat studied art. Therefore, He made a set of Contemplation Wheels consisting of nineteen types of karma. These nineteen things include basic ignorance.

Does the Second Vehicle know how to end ignorance? Don't know! Not only is it not a Hinayana dharma, it is also not an ordinary Mahayana dharma! That way, everyone will clearly understand why the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is said, making our faith steadfast. Being steadfast is not enough, you still have to have pure faith. Pure faith not only eliminates delusions and afflictions, but also eliminates ignorance. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva is a great Bodhisattva among Bodhisattvas. He cut off ignorance and was not an ordinary Bodhisattva. Therefore, our Dharma friends who study this Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma must consider this a Bodhisattva Dharma to learn. Furthermore, [the masses] listened to the sutras in this dharma assembly, there were no Sravakas, no Arhats. The Buddha's sixteen great regular disciples were not present. In [the mass listening to the Dharma of] Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, there are no Arhats, all are great Bodhisattvas. Therefore, when people learn, a feeling of superiority must arise.

Because this world propagates the Ksitigarbha Sutra, in the beginning there were still misconceptions, saying Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is fake, do not believe it! But we have Nine Flowers Mountain, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appearing in the Tang Dynasty, it's not fake! To the four great famous mountains, we Buddhist disciples, whether lay or monastic, have the utmost respect. Everyone knows that Cuu Hoa Son is the place where Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva revealed his holy relics. At the top of Cuu Hoa Son is the place where Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva worships the Avatamsaka Sutra. The stone with the two footprints he stood on is still there, I think everyone who has worshiped Cuu Hoa Son has seen it. I was very lucky. In 1931, when the court worshiped Nine Flowers Mountain, they opened the stupa of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva on Nine Flowers Mountain: [The physical body of] an old monk passed away for more than a thousand years, his hair still grew long, his fingernails still grew long. Open the tower once every sixty years and cut it once. Each cut takes sixty years, each time it is placed there, no one dares to touch it, no one is allowed to take it away. But when cutting, I will take out the nail clippers and tidying tools [the beard, hair, fingernails, and toenails that were used last time], and exchange them for a new set to put in there. That's how I saw it for myself in 1931. Waited until 1991, when I came again, I didn't open the tower anymore. [Chinese authorities] didn't allow the tower to be opened anymore, they sealed it up. That is all true, that is the reincarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

In this sutra, when Kien Tinh Bodhisattva asked the Buddha for guidance, the Buddha praised Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. Having finished praising, the Buddha should have spoken, but he did not. Recently, a Dharma friend asked me, "The Buddha made a precept that prohibits Buddhist disciples from reading hexagrams or divination", then the Buddha said that the method of contemplation would not be very suitable. Bodhisattvas can, Bodhisattvas can say, [Therefore tell Kien Tinh Bodhisattva] please request a Bodhisattva Mahasattva in this assembly, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In this assembly, the Great Wisdom Manjushri was present, Manjushri and Samantabhadra were both present. Why did the Buddha instruct Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak? Everyone must research this, I won't explain it clearly to everyone. Each of you must research for yourself what the cause is, I'll just briefly explain it like that. Connotation in the purpose of absolute explanation is superior.

This sutra was translated and transmitted to East India [by Bodhidharma[3]], although Great Master Nguich Ich preached, he did not preach at all, nor did Dharma Master Hoang Nhat preach. Master Nguu Ich wrote a commentary for the Sutra of Divining Good and Evil Karmic Retribution, and shaman Hoang Nhat created the Chiem Sat Luan. Contemplation of the Wheel of Light includes nineteen wheeled signs created by shaman Hoang Nhat. Master Hoang Nhat told me to explain; At first, I didn't preach either. After coming to America, the two of us, Master Hoang Giac and I, went to America. [Master Hoang Giac said]: "You preach the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, and no one listens to the great sutras. I think you should preach the Contemplation Sutra of Good and Evil Karma." When it comes to fate, it's very good. When we returned, in Taiwan, we started working on Chiem Sat Luan General. In Taiwan, I started making Chiem Sat Luan General for layperson Vuong Thuc Phan in Phuong Quang, and gradually it became widely popular. I can't preach many times! In 1989, he preached once in New York, and in 1999 he preached once at Ngu Dai Son. This time they invited me to lecture here, this year is 2009. Roughly [each lecture] is ten years apart. It is preached once every ten years, but only three times. Fate is like that, I don't understand it myself. Anyway, without fate, it won't be possible. All dharmas are born of causes and conditions, without dependent origination. If you preach, who will listen to you? If there is no one to request Buddhism, it will not be possible to speak casually. I want to preach, if you want to preach something, will someone invite you? Everyone, think about it, people ask you to recite certain sutras, that's called "having a predestined relationship", so you obey and respond to predestined conditions! There are also times when there is a predestined request, but there is no response, because the cause is not ripe. This time, I was in Ngu Dai Son. Last year I was very sick, my body just got a little better, I went to Thai Nguyen. Having arrived in Thai Nguyen, feeling a little better, I said: "Let's go to Taiwan first!" That's why I just started going to Taiwan. Due to illness, I went to Taiwan and met a few people who asked me to preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, and I felt very victorious. Because it is only in Taiwan that our Cham Luan Contemplation is widely circulated. Currently, it is also very popular in Mainland, but we started from Taiwan. Although he preached in New York, he did not do [the reincarnation]. At Ngu Dai Son, it is only limited to Ngu Dai Pho Tho Pagoda and does not propagate outside. This is the third time, the most recent lecture.

Now we will continue teaching the part we talked about the previous day. "Even though the universal journey necessarily kills, it always gives rise to industry, but the five defilements and evil worlds, bring benefits to the future, the heron wears the power of the original vows to gather and strengthen, and causes sentient beings to receive and transform the karma of the past" (Although they roam all realms, often giving rise to industry, but especially focus on educating and benefiting the five impurities in the evil life, it also depends on the power of the original vows to accumulate, and also due to their karma. born worthy of receiving education). In this passage, the Buddha praises Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vow power is especially great. We all know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Great Vow, “great vow” is to save all sentient beings, mainly to save sentient beings in hell. “Hell is not empty, I swear I will not become a Buddha” is His great vow, clearly stating that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in all lands, not only in this Saha world, but in all Buddha lands, He benefits sentient beings. He has no concept of nationality, no concept of territory, and no distinction between sentient beings. His merit, that is, the merit of benefiting sentient beings, is called Merit. Karma refers to His Intention, because of His intention, all merit arises. The intention is to benefit all sentient beings, do all the work of saving sentient beings, and establish the cause of saving all sentient beings.

Especially in the present, this world of ours is called “the five evil worlds”, everyone knows this. Every Dharma friend feels what situation we are in right now! The body is exposed to whatever situation you encounter, that is called “karmic accumulation”. The Mahayana Treatise on Arising Faith says there are two types of accumulation:

- One is that good karma collects your bad karma, turning bad karma into good karma.

- The second type is evil karma that accumulates good karma, all good turns into evil.

I don't need to explain this in detail, everyone is personally in it, you feel it, see it with your own eyes, hear it yourself. Currently, what kind of world is ours? I think you all know, I won't go into detail. This world is the five evil worlds, not a good place. In this world to save sentient beings, everyone knows that the two great Bodhisattvas who stand out in particular are Quan Am and Ksitigarbha. Everyone worshiped Cuu Hoa Son, worshiped Ngu Dai Son. Seventy years ago, the phenomenon at Cuu Hoa Son when I worshiped was nothing like the current phenomenon! The Jiuhua Mountains start from Qingyuan County, Anhui Province, along the road there are all disabled people all the way up the mountain, with missing arms, missing legs, blind eyes, all with six incomplete senses. All over the mountain there are [disabled people], I don't know why this phenomenon occurs! At that time, I did not understand Buddhism and had not long since become a monk. Afterwards, I studied Buddhism and the Ksitigarbha Sutra to learn: That is the appearance of hell. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva saves sentient beings from hell, not in hell, but in hell in the human world! Currently, Cuu Hoa Son does not have this phenomenon. It has been completely eliminated and does not allow this phenomenon. But the ultimate truth is that in this evil world of five defilements, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva this time appears in this body, next time appears in that body, at Cuu Hoa Mountain [can be seen] very clearly, other incarnations of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva are many. The stories [about the manifestations of Bodhisattvas] are also very numerous!

Śākyamuni Buddha told Pure Faith Bodhisattva: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva from eleven lifetimes up to now, has been in this world to save suffering beings, to adorn this world, to benefit sentient beings, to mature sentient beings. Don't you see, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in this assembly, his body is dignified, his virtue is sublime, "except for Tathagata, he is too incompetent" (except for Tathagata, no one can be better than him), meaning that except for me (Buddha), only can I be equal to Him, can I be better than Him! Except for Tathagata, all other Bodhisattvas do not have the profound virtue and dignity of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. [Saying these things to] visualize the praise of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva from many eons ago until now. In this world, saving sentient beings does not last for a day or two. He has saved all eleven eons. How long is a lifetime? Since the lifespan of a human being is ten years, every hundred years the age increases by one year, increasing until the lifespan of a human being is eighty-four thousand years. After eighty-four thousand one hundred years, that is, when [the lifespan] has reached eighty-four thousand years, every hundred years after that, the age will be reduced by one year, until the lifespan of humans is only ten years. Such a cycle of one increase and one decrease is counted as one kalpa. The original name in Indian is Kalpa. Kiep Ba translated into Chinese is Thoi Phan. It's a period of time in the timeline. The longest period of time is called Kiep Ba. The shortest time is called kṣaṇa, like the blink of an eye is ninety moments. Our time in the blink of an eye is ninety moments, we cannot use mental energy to calculate the quantity. Therefore, the cycle of one increase and one decrease [of human lifespan] is called a Kalpa. After eleven kalpas, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in this world saved sentient beings. He went through eleven lifetimes, helping sentient beings in this world attain salvation and mature all sentient beings. Therefore, his appearance is extremely dignified, his dignity is extremely sublime, except for Tathagata, no one else can compare.

Furthermore, all karma in this world, “karma” is the karma of saving sentient beings. In this Saha world, not only Ksitigarbha, but also other great Bodhisattvas. “Only except for the Sands, Avalokiteśvara Avalokiteśvara” (Except only those like the Sands, Avalokiteshvara, etc.). “ Equal ” means there is also Manjushri Bodhisattva, there are also other Bodhisattvas! Samantabhadra, good everywhere, is Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), and even other great Bodhisattvas can be compared and on par with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Because of His own power of aspiration, He hopes to save all sentient beings to become Buddhas, He can satisfy the wishes of all sentient beings. In this world, sentient beings often encounter accidents, praying to Bodhisattva to eliminate disasters and avoid accidents. Praying to the two Bodhisattvas with the best effect and the fastest response is Avalokiteśvara and Ksitigarbha. In the twelfth chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, when the Buddha was about to finish speaking the Ksitigarbha Sutra, in the twelfth chapter, the Buddha instructed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. The Buddha told Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to propagate the Ksitigarbha Dharma. Every time I recited the twelfth chapter, my mind thought: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva himself has taught boundless and limitless sentient beings in this world. Why did the Buddha still instruct Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to propagate Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Dharma?" That is because it makes sentient beings in this world believe more in the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. I just feel that, in America, I went to a number of places, and there were Dharma friends who asked me to dedicate it to them. I said: "I don't have the strength. I'm an ordinary person, I don't have any strength! It's best for you to recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra. I also help you recite, I can only be a helper. Don't expect me to pray for relief from disasters." I said: "I can't do it! My own misfortune hasn't been eliminated yet. Can I help you eliminate misfortunes and avoid misfortunes? Then since you requested, how can I do this? I can introduce to you, let's all pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva together." I said: "But I've been practicing a little longer than you. I've been studying for decades and have never stopped."

Therefore, praising the merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Why did the Buddha praise Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's merits like that? Making people believe, that's the goal. The Buddha praised Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, making it so that when we encounter difficulties, sentient beings encounter many difficulties, in the economy, in life's habits, in illness, in accidents, in encountering demons, evil spirits, [encountering] problems that cannot be solved, it is best for you to close the door, recite ten thousand sentences of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, it will have the effect of “building a pole, seeing the shadow”. Those are Buddha's teachings, I'm not talking nonsense to you. He can satisfy the desires of all sentient beings, quickly satisfy the desires of all sentient beings, and is extremely effective. We living beings all have karma; Without karma, you will not be born in Sa Ba. He can eliminate your karma. [Reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva] can eliminate your serious sins, and for now you will be at peace. That is the effect, that is, the effect of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) A Bodhisattva known as the Good An Envoy, the position of cunning and profound Dharma, good at enlightenment beginner learning to develop the intention to seek Greatness Vehicle

fake, flexible and fearless.

(Sutra: Again, that Bodhisattva is called the One Who Speaks Skillfully in Consolation, that is, He skillfully speaks profound Dharma, can skillfully inspire and guide beginners to develop the mind to seek the Mahayana, making them not afraid or weak.

Furthermore, the Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is called Thien An Commissar. That is, in addition to the title Ksitigarbha, he also has another name, that is, the name of virtue, that is, the title of virtue, which is Thien An Huyet Jia ( one who speaks well of comfort). Thien An Commissioner means that he is very skillful in preaching the Dharma, able to display skillful meanings in the depth of Buddha Dharma, skillful in speaking profound Dharma! Why does the Buddha here refer to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva who is skillful in speaking profound dharma? To tell you: The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is not a shallow belief, but a very deep dharma. How deep is the Dharma? It is the second half that [talks about] the realm of One Truth and the two types of contemplation

Dharma Master Hong Yi told me that he classified Ksitigarbha San Sutra into the Avatamsaka system. Why? In Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, there is no mention of the name Thanh Van, or the name of any Arhat, none! All are dharmas spoken by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, there is no Second Vehicle, and Bodhisattvas are all Mahayana Bodhisattvas Ma Ha Tat. He can inspire and guide all those who have just developed their minds and teach you to pray for the Mahayana. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches all sentient beings to seek Mahayana dharma until he becomes a Buddha, but practicing Mahayana dharma does not give rise to Bodhi mind. Why? Practicing the Mahayana Dharma, you must benefit sentient beings. Since you started cultivating the Dharma, you have benefited others. When you study Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches you, first of all, teachings you to benefit others; After that, talk about yourself. For example, in this Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, if you contemplate for others the effect is very good, but if you contemplate for yourself it is not certain. The effect will be slow! You ask about anything, pray for something for yourself, when you use the Contemplation Sat Wheel, the effect will be very slow, one contemplation will not be successful, two contemplations will not be successful; But when you pray for others, your contemplation will come true! Therefore, for those who seek the Mahayana Dharma, they have already believed and then are courageous and diligent. Why? Because when you use contemplation for that person, your mind is not afraid. When encountering all kinds of difficulties, such as roads that are not clear, you wish to go smoothly and pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, then changes will arise. Therefore, it makes people who develop a great mind, people who practice, feel that their future is unclear and their mind cannot be concentrated, so you use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate a little.

At the same time, for this profound method, I tell everyone a little more. All of us who develop Bodhi mind, as students of the Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, you must believe in yourself. I often ask friends whether they have faith or not? Often, Dharma friends understand wrongly. Whenever asked if they have faith or not? They wrongly interpret [thought of faith] as "do you believe in the Three Jewels or not?" That's not the meaning! “Do you have faith in your mind or not” means saying “do you believe in your own mind or not?” I often ask my Dharma friends whether they have developed the mind or not? Have faith or not? The Dharma friend replied: "Yes! I believe in Buddha, believe in Dharma, believe in Sangha", that is not faith. Do you have faith in your mind or not? That means do you trust your own mind or not? What is trusting our mind? The mind is Buddha, believe in the mind is Buddha, believe in the mind to become Buddha, mind is Buddha, Buddha is mind. That is called “deep dharma”. Regardless of the Mahayana Sutra, the Mahayana Collection of Ten Wheels, the Ksitigarbha Sutra, or the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva all makes you develop deep within your heart and believe that you are a Buddha. These three sutras all teach you to understand the True Form. Therefore, Master Hong Yi told me: “[Ksitigarbha] Three Sutras all belong to the Avatamsaka system”. When using the Avatamsaka Sutra, impurities will no longer exist, and you will attain True Dharma Nature, One True Dharma Realm. The three sutras of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva all teach you to reach the ultimate goal of entering True Suchness and Dharma Nature. But Bodhisattvas use extremely skillful means, such as the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, which uses the Contemplation Wheel to tell you about good and evil cause and effect, with the aim of making you reach profound dharma, so that you yourself can become Buddhas. Because whenever you study Ksitigarbha Sutra, you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, there is no fear at all, no feeling of panic, no feeling of fear, and no panic anymore! What morality is that? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught to transform demons. People who are afraid of ghosts, if you recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the ghosts will see you and pay homage! Your physical eyes cannot see it, but while you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, when you recite Ksitigarbha Three Sutras, there are many dharma-protecting deities around you. Like Kien Lao Earth God in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the great earth belongs to Kien Lao Earth God; Other dharmas Kien Lao Dia Than[4] do not protect. [As for the dharma methods of] Manjushri, Samantabhadra, and Avalokiteśvara, she does not protect them, but specifically protects Ksitigarbha. Therefore, she was called Kien Lao Dia (solid soil). If everyone has recited the Earth Store Sutra, the eleventh chapter is the Earth Spirit Kien Lao chapter. She said that all over the earth are her descendants: "Wherever there is great earth, there will be my descendants. My descendants all protect Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva". Therefore, deeply believing in the Dharma means that our own mind is Buddha, "this mind is Buddha". However, we have not cleared, we have not undergone cultivation, and the clearing has not been successful. Since you don't practice, how can you be enlightened? Through cultivation, your Buddha will radiate light, until you reach completion and can be enlightened!

(Sutra) If everything is equal to cause and effect, if you try the world, sentient beings yearn for it, and attain enlightenment. Thi co, the golden spirit bi theory chi.
(Sutra: Due to such causes and conditions, in this world, sentient beings yearn to admire and be taught by Him. Therefore, now I tell him to speak.)

So, in the end, the Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: Because there is such a cause and effect, there are such causes and conditions, in this world, that is, the Sa Ba world, which is the teaching world of Śākyamuni Buddha, all sentient beings yearn to be enlightened by Him. The Buddha turned to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to introduce Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, introducing Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's merit, wisdom, and power to save sentient beings. Therefore, he turned to me to request a sermon, and I told him to come and request him. That was the purpose of telling him to request Him. From this passage of scripture, I tell everyone: Based on the Buddha's introduction, do not consider the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma as fortune telling or hexagram guessing. That way of thinking is absolutely wrong. For now, don't hesitate to say it first. You use Chiem Sat Wood Lun, the first thing is to purify your body, change your clothes, and rinse your mouth. Then, worship. The first bow must be bowed to Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva; After that, bow to the Buddhas of the ten directions, all of them in the ten directions: the Dharma of the ten directions, the sage Sangha of the ten directions, and all the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions. Only then can you use the [Contemplation] wheel. Whether you use the wheel for the first time, or use it the second time, or use it ten or more times, it doesn't matter; “not corresponding” means not answering exactly what you asked. That's because you are not sincere. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches you: "The mind is still not sincere and does not appear to you." If you want to use it, you must retreat for three days or five days, or seven days or more, and meditate every day. Every time you use it, it's magical; Whatever you ask, [Bodhisattva] will tell you. Whenever you ask or tell you "this should not be done", you absolutely cannot do it. [Contemplation Sat Luan teaches] "You should do this", if you do it, you will absolutely succeed, without any shortcomings!

(Sūtra) At the ear of the time, the Bodhisattva of pure faith records the Buddha's intention, thinking about inviting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva said: "Good disaster! True savior. Good disaster! Great wise man. Just as the self is confused, the evil beings in the world are able to transform the path through means, eliminate all obstacles, gain firm faith. The Tathagata is a golden man, the desire of the spirit and the word speaks of the means, doubts and understanding of the time, those who are sensitive speak."
(Sutra: At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva understood the Buddha's intention and immediately recommended Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat said: "Good! Ba true savior. Good! Ba wise pioneer. As I asked, what means should be used to educate and guide living beings in the evil world to leave behind obstacles and have solid faith. Now Tathagata wants you to tell me that means, please You should know the time and have mercy on me."

At present, the Buddha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva so, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva immediately understood, no longer doubting. Before that, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva originally wanted to invite the Buddha to tell him. Not only did the Buddha not speak, but he also introduced another person to speak, so he was skeptical and unwilling. The Buddha knew that Kien Tinh Bodhisattva did not like it, so he introduced Ksitigarbha's merits, making Kien Tinh Bodhisattva understand clearly.

“At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva interpreted the Buddha's intention” (At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva already understood the Buddha's intention), because he understood the Buddha's intention, so he would go to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's seat and invite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak. “Good disaster! True savior” (Good! True savior saves life): He is the true great man who saves the world. That is praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. “ Good disaster! A wise wise man”: He is a person with great wisdom, opening up and guiding all living beings. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva praises Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. "As the self asks" means as I asked the Buddha just now, have you heard, at the time of the evil life in the Dharma-Ending Age, for those sentient beings, what method and means must be used to make them leave all obstacles? Every believer, that is, every disciple of the Buddha, has many obstacles. Their faith is not steadfast. What method should be used to make their faith steadfast?

Even if your faith is not steadfast, can you still achieve it? I discussed this with everyone a little more. We should not think that we have entered the Three Jewels for ten or twenty years. Nowadays, I'm probably a little older than you. I've been entering Buddhism and becoming a monk for eighty years. Now that I count the total eighty years, I feel like I haven't entered the Buddhist religion yet! I say that, people are probably skeptical, this introduction is not an easy thing. We can recognize that the previous thought gave rise to a bad thought, and immediately cut off the next bad thought. When the six senses (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind) come into contact with the six sense objects, there is no distinction between them, can it be done or not? [Currently, we are all six senses in contact with six senses], the six consciousnesses immediately distinguish, good, bad, love, hate. Love and hate are clear, if you don't like it then you want to avoid it, if you like it then you hope to achieve it. I think everyone is almost like me! Those are all not steadfast beliefs, can it be considered an initiation? You must speak honestly, not to outsiders, you must speak honestly to yourself. Why is it so difficult for us to become enlightened? It's always difficult for us to cut off Views and Thoughts like that. When we see something, we then distinguish it. If it's good, you hope to achieve it. If it's bad, you hope to throw it away. If you throw it away, you can't throw it away! Even if you want to achieve it, you can't achieve it! Creating karma in there, if you want to throw it away, in the process of throwing it away, you will create a lot of karma. Everyone can think carefully!

In the evil world of the Dharma-Ending Age, what skillful means can be used to make them practice with peace of mind, without obstacles, to make them achieve steadfast faith and not retreat? Unrelenting faith has great power. Just now, I turned to the Buddha to make a request. The Buddha taught me to ask him, so that he would tell me that method. Then you should know that the time is right, now is the time to speak, you should have compassion on living beings and speak. At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva addressed Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. That is the beginning of the most primitive cause and effect. Below, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva officially speaks to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva.

saying: "Good man! Emperor listens, speaks in the same position."
(Sutra: At that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva told Pure Faith Bodhisattva Tat Ma Ha Tat said: "Hey good man! Listen! I will tell you").

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva immediately said: "Now I can tell you." Agree to tell Kien Tinh Faith Bodhisattva. But you must listen carefully and listen attentively. Every time he preached the Dharma, the Buddha told his disciples to listen. “listen” (listen) means to observe with certainty, that is, you observe carefully, reasonably, and do not fiddle with the general. The meaning of the word “hearing” is very deep! Therefore, once the Buddha preached the Dharma, Manjushri Bodhisattva acted as a yana. Manjushri Bodhisattva immediately recited a verse: “The dragon statues of the Dharma” (The dragon statues at the Dharma banquet). Meaning: Those who listen to the Dharma, are not dragons, are all elephants, that is, all are great Bodhisattvas. “Dharma Dien Long resembles the assembly, contemplating the First Noble Truth”: You should all visualize the First Noble Truth. “Contemplating the Dharma King”: Be reasonable, consider, contemplate, do not use words, listen well, observe [the Dharma of the Dharma King] according to reason. “Contemplating the Buddha's Dharma, Dharma King as it is” (contemplating Buddha's Dharma techniques, Buddha's Dharma is like that): The Buddha immediately stepped down from the Dharma throne. The Buddha finished his sermon without saying a single word. Everyone contemplate: Manjushri recited that praise verse, the Buddha has finished preaching the Dharma! There was also a time when the Buddha preached the Dharma, without saying anything, holding a flower, [the scriptures often write it as] “nam hoa”, that is, holding a flower, Venerable Kasyapa smiled. Buddha put down the flower, stepped down from the throne, and finished speaking! The meaning in those two types of events is mainly “the theory of hearing and hearing”. The meaning of “hearing” is “listen to reason, don't listen to appearances”. As for listening to stories, you should listen [with the state of mind] like that, don't think about the appearance, but contemplate on the Reason, it's called "idea understanding, mind reflecting" (mind understanding, mind reflecting); that is Emperor. “The Emperor” will tell you. Don't listen to this story and then call it a day, that's not what I'm talking to you about! Therefore, in every sermon of the Buddha, there are many people who attain enlightenment, many people attain enlightenment, precisely because they have listened and thought correctly!

(Sutra) After Buddha's destruction, in the middle of the evil world, monks, Bhikkhunīs, upasakas, upasādi, in the world, beyond the world of cause and effect dharma, the one who has attained decisive faith, cannot practice impermanent perception, suffering perception, non-self perception, impure perception, achieves the present, cannot need to contemplate the Four Noble Truths, up to the twelve dharmas of cause and effect, does not need to meditate on the Truth as it really is, no birth, no destruction equal dharmas. It is too sinful not to meditate like a dharma master, not to be able to act at all on the Ten Evils, it is too sinful to be in the Three Jewels of merit and virtue, to be unable to specialize, to be in the middle of the three vehicles, and to have no direction.
(Sutra: If after the Buddha passed away, there were monks in the evil world, Bhiksunis, upasakas, upasakas, regarding the dharma of cause and effect in this world and beyond, have not yet achieved decisive faith, cannot practice impermanent perception, suffering perception, non-self perception, impure perception, attain present achievements, cannot diligently contemplate the dharma of the Four Noble Truths and the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions, nor diligently contemplate the Truth as it really is, the dharmas of non-birth, non-destruction, etc. Due to not diligently contemplating dharmas such as Therefore, it is impossible not to commit fundamental sins belonging to the Ten Evils, one cannot be confident in the meritorious realms of the Three Jewels, and one has no direction in the three vehicles).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: After the Buddha passed away, “Buddha” refers to Śākyamuni Buddha, that is, after Śākyamuni Buddha passed away, this world turned into an evil world, called “the five evil worlds”. Everyone knows [the five defilements are] Defects of Life, Defects of Views, Defects of Defilements, Defects of Lives, and Defects of Living Beings. It is all impure, confused, and unclear; By then, the Buddha had passed away. It has now been more than two thousand years since the Buddha passed away. At that time, the Buddha was about to enter nirvana. After speaking the Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, he entered nirvana. In this world, even in the midst of the evil five defilements, one wants to practice the Dharma beyond this world; In other words, we hope to get rid of afflictions, hope to clear birth and death, and attain enlightenment beyond this world. Not to mention attaining the Four Arhats, at least “entering the throne”. “Entering the taste” will be able to end birth and death, but cannot end the eighty-eight pieces of history belonging to Kien Or. But we who study Mahayana are not just that! Not only Kien Tu, we also have to cut off Tran Sa's troubles. But in this world at the end of the world, even Kien Tu's afflictions cannot be stopped. What is happening at this time? Neither the world nor the world, whether it is cause or effect, do not believe in cause and effect. Current society does not believe in cause and effect, and believes that doing bad things will not result in retribution, and doing good things will not result in retribution. They don't believe in cause and effect, they don't have faith, they definitely don't have faith! Bhikkhus, bhiksunis who have become monks, or lay disciples of the Three Jewels, i.e. upasakas and upasakas, at this time, their faith is not steadfast.

Here, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said, right in the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma: He said at that time they could not practice the four pure dharmas, could not practice impermanence, could not practice suffering, could not practice selflessness, could not practice impurity. Even if you don't think about it, can you still achieve it? Unable to achieve! Because Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path are the dharma of the Holy Truth, the four types of dharma of the Holy Truth are the beginning, up to the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions are all dharmas of cause and effect belonging to the world. In the dharma of worldly cause and effect, Suffering and Experience are worldly cause and effect. Suffering is a worldly fruit. Practice is the cause of the world. Because you summon so many causes and do so many bad things, of course you have to suffer and suffer the consequences. Cessation is beyond the world, [the cause of] Cessation is the Way, cultivating the Way aims to achieve beyond the world. In Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, Suffering and Origin are worldly cause and effect, Cessation and Path are worldly cause and effect. The Tao is cultivating the cause, Practicing is the cause, there will definitely be an achievement. Ordinarily speaking, when one reaches the Four Arhats and puts an end to the afflictions of Self-Reflection, the Four Noble Truths will be achieved. Because normally, when people study Buddhism, they will learn [these things], we do not preach the Four Noble Truths, we mainly teach the stories of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Also “not diligently contemplating the Truth as it really is”, that is considering the Four Noble Truths of Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, twelve causes and conditions. Practicing the twelve causes and conditions is the self-cultivation of an Arhat. In the mountains he will attain enlightenment, while there is no Buddha, he will attain enlightenment on his own. Based on the Four Noble Truths taught by the Buddha to practice, that type of Arhat is called Shravaka. Relying on the twelve causes and conditions to practice is called Pratyekabuddha. Among the vehicles, they are the Second Vehicle, practicing the Second Vehicle method. [During the End of the Dharma], there were very few people practicing the Second Vehicle, and even fewer people practicing the Mahayana. Due to not being diligent in contemplating the Truth as it really is, that is an idealistic method. The mind-only method, mind contemplation, is “clear mind and see nature” as we often say. Relying on the Bodhisattva path to practice, as taught by the Avatamsaka Sutra, after fulfilling the Ten Faiths, belonging to the position of Tam Hien Bodhisattva, can recognize True Suchness, gradually enter and seek, similar to attaining True Suchness, is not truly attained. Having reached the position of the First Level Bodhisattva, attaining a part of the Dharma Body, destroying all ignorance, moving from the First Level to the Ten Levels. I say these things are based on the Avatamsaka Sutra, because this is the Avatamsaka Mahayana. This type of [practitioner who practices] the dharma of no birth and no death does not exist. Even those who practice the Four Noble Truths and the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions are very few. Can they still practice the Mahayana dharma? Is it possible to diligently contemplate the Dharma like that? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: "There is none." At that time, practicing the method of the Four Noble Truths, practicing the method of twelve causes and conditions, the saints of the Second Vehicle will no longer exist, and even less will there be those who practice the method of Bodhisattvas! If you want to cut off the Ten Evil Karmas, can you do it? At that time, people who commit crimes basically belong to the Ten Evil Karmas quite a lot. That is our current phenomenon.

As for the merits of the Three Jewels, and all kinds of realms, you cannot be single-minded, just move forward and backward. Last time, I told everyone about the standard of faith. While you believe in the Three Jewels, you are faced with a fateful fate that forces you to not believe in the Three Jewels, yet you can believe steadfastly and without doubt. I would rather believe in the Three Jewels and die, I would rather not believe in the Three Jewels in order to live. Is it possible to have that kind of willpower? Can you recognize that the previous thoughts are evil, know that the thoughts in your mind are not correct, then stop immediately and not let the next thoughts arise? Do you have faith in your mind like that? The Buddha's teachings were not vague, but had certain standards. You yourself cut off quite a lot Or, you will attain quite a few pure states, which you yourself understand very clearly. Can you see all forms without distinction, without raising any thoughts? Can you treat both good and bad without distinguishing between good and bad? Distinguishing between good and bad is not an idiot; Don't consider that person an idiot, an idiot can't tell the difference. In there, you do not choose, do not give birth to the mind that distinguishes between good and bad, good and evil, and at the same time do not seek peace and happiness for yourself. If you don't wish for peace and happiness for yourself, why do you still have to do good things? Just wish for all sentient beings to be happy. This is very common, it is a Bodhisattva.

During this time, if you have such Dharma friends, you can diligently contemplate the Truth as it really is, that is, the method of contemplation of the mind, contemplation of your own mind. True Reality is observing the mind, all false thoughts are not entangled, all dharmas arising and passing away are also not entangled. Contemplate all dharmas that are non-born, non-destructive, immaculate, and impure. Everyone understands these things and has read many Mahayana scriptures. Because if you don't often practice Contemplation like that, if you don't practice like that, you can't help but create bad karma. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: That person cannot completely avoid committing fundamental sins belonging to the Ten Evils, that person will commit a sin! Past, present, future, and even more fundamental ignorance. That is the ten chakras [belonging to the first subtype in Wood Wheel Contemplation], that is, ten wheels. When we get to the corresponding part of the scriptures, we will explain it in detail again. After that, we will use Moc Luan as a model for you to see.

That is called the three wheels (three types of wheels). Use that wheel to contemplate (contemplate, consider) what? Contemplate your past good or bad karma. Therefore, when you want to use the Contemplation Wheel, you must first recognize whether it (appearance) is real, or illusory, or destroyed. The scriptures will tell you that if you use the Contemplation Wheel, [those appearances] will appear. Do you know how heavy your past karma is? Luan General will tell you. If you regularly worship, [those karmas] will be greatly reduced, [the wheel of life] will also speak very clearly to you. But reducing it to [the level of remaining] basic ignorance is very difficult. Therefore, you just keep worshiping! When you worship to the point that all the wheel signs are red[5]. The four faces of each wheel are sometimes red, sometimes black. The big red line means great goodness, the small red line means small goodness. The big black line means the evil is too serious. Small black lines are small evils. The transformation of the wheel is determined by your repentance. Our human life has disasters and blessings, good and evil. No matter who is pure good or pure evil. That person sometimes does good things, sometimes does bad things, good and evil are mixed. But when you bow, while you are being taught how to practice by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the red color will gradually increase (ie good things increase), evil things will gradually disappear. However, not for a short time. Some people pray for two or three years, some people just pray and then obstacles appear. In Taiwan, I have a young Dharma friend, he bows to Chiem Sat Sam very appropriately, what about now? It is complete. That's called karma's discovery, it can't resist karma!

(Sutra) Like the emperor contemplating good and evil karma, understanding the metaphor from the heart, thinking about the matter, deciding on the matter.
With doubtful matters, use this method to make decisions).

Therefore, using the contemplation of good and evil karma is certainly like that. “True contemplation” is the correct way to contemplate, contemplate the karma due to your good karma and bad karma. “Understanding your own mind”: Makes your mind understand very clearly what is right and what is wrong! You don't know, the wheel will tell you, you can choose. You give birth to this mind incorrectly. When you worship without the highest mind, or the lower will (the lower level mind) also does not have it, then [when sowing the wheel signs], it is completely ineffective. The first thing is to be single-minded, to control the mind in one place. In the following scriptures, we will talk about this again. When “true contemplation” [then planting the Wheel of Contemplation] is not a Thing (that is, it is not done in a superficial way, with the nature of inquiry like divination, not really used as a means to encourage and self-evaluate your own practice), unlike when you plant the Wheel of Contemplation and then look, [doing so] is a Thing. “Truth” is the mind that must correspond to it. The mind is Reason, you must be reasonable, don't be a dreamer. In other words, you must dream according to reason, you must really use your heart. [Contemplation] is not divination. Go to the fortune teller to guess the hexagram and check the eight characters. I'll give you a few coins and you can calculate one hexagram for me. [Only superficially considering the method of Contemplation as divination], what effect does it have? Don't! In this Dharma, one must wholeheartedly bow and repent. [This dharma] is originally formless, formless becomes formless, formless turns into formless. “Existing form” means that all of your criminal careers have a form. When you bow, you will be formless, [then the sin hindrances] will disappear, and you will be formless. If you have any doubts, [or questions] about how to do it, you cannot decide for yourself, then you should ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! You burn incense and pay respects. After bowing, you use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate. [Even though the wheels are only nineteen, from the combination of aspects in each wheel, the result] will be one hundred and eighty-nine types. Why? One hundred and eighty-nine types are because they correspond to the six senses, i.e. Eyes, Ears, Snakes, Tongues, Body, Minds are the six senses, plus Eyes, Ears, Nose, Tongue, Body, and Mind six consciousnesses. Six senses, six consciousnesses, plus form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, three times six is ​​eighteen, those eighteen plus basic ignorance, make nineteen types [so there are nineteen wood wheels]. There is a huge change in it. Where did that transformation come from? Because of your mind. Throughout the day, one moment you think of one thing, the next moment you think of something else, the wheel of appearances will change at any time. But when you bow, you bow with one mind and one mind. If today you worship very appropriately, then the power of your worship will correspond to the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. When you worship, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will definitely come.
