[Eye] Aligned with Color and Dust, in the middle there is Eye Consciousness, Eye Consciousness perceives colors. Because the three types of six senses, six objects, and six consciousnesses combine to form eighteen. When we create all karma, there will be no more than those eighteen types, and we will also add basic ignorance, making it nineteen cycles. Those nineteen chakras will calculate and display the karma you have created in the past, present, and future.

The future has not yet arrived, how can it be revealed? What you have done in this life. The karma you have done in this life is the cause, and in the future you will suffer the consequences or enjoy the results, depending on what karma you have created, you will have to receive the corresponding retribution. Because the karma you have done in the past is the cause, what you personally experience in the present is the effect. That is called “the three worlds of cause and effect”, all three types of rotation can appear. As soon as you plant [the universal form], you can unlock supernatural powers. What magic is that? Knowing what karma we have done in the past, what consequences we will suffer in this life! All the things we have done in this life are cause; In the future, you will definitely receive retribution. Luan General tells you that. If you want to know the great retribution due to good or bad karma committed in a previous life, [you should know that the retribution] is what you have to suffer in this life. The wheel also tells you clearly: What karma you have created will result in this life. Good is rewarded with good, evil is rewarded with evil. Not retribution is because the time has not yet come; The time has come, there will be retribution.

But in all the things we have done, in your activities, whether good karma or bad karma, you are creating karma. All the words you utter, the things your mind thinks, the things your body creates [are all karma]. Your mouth lies, embellishes, doubles, and says harsh words. Don't lie, don't embellish, don't say double words, don't say harsh words; that is goodness. Lying, embellishing words, double-talking, and harsh words are evil. Body karma creates killing, stealing, lust, and thoughts of greed, anger, and ignorance. All your activities throughout the day, at night, when you sleep, there is a single consciousness[7] that is still creating karma non-stop, day and night without stopping! Because the basis of those eighteen types is ignorance. The deepest type of ignorance is Doubt. It is the deepest karma, all born from ignorance, so when you want to recognize it, you must use nineteen types of wheel signs, that is, use wood wheel signs to sow.

(Sutra) If you meditate on the difference between good and evil karma in the world, you will overcome the ten karma. He tries the ten rounds, the secretary of the name of the Ten Goods, the one good master in the one wheel, the one-face record. Second, the Ten Evil Books are equivalent to the Ten Good Books, and the Spiritual History is equivalent, and the Herons are at the same level.
(Sutra: If you want to contemplate the difference between good and bad karma created in a previous life, you should carve wood into ten For those ten wheels, write the name of the Ten Virtues. Next, write the name of the Ten Evils corresponding to the Ten Goods, so that they correspond to each other, each is also written on one side [opposite the good side] on each wheel.

Of course, you still have to learn how to use this type of dharma. Based on the text, I'm afraid it's still not very clear! When you contemplate and compare with the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva [you will understand better]. You contemplate good karma and bad karma in the past, they are called “seeds”. You sow the wheel, sow good things, showing that good karma is very heavy, bad karma is very light. Therefore, seeing the red form of the wheel (the form of the wheel showing red text) represents good things. Evil karma is written in black, to represent bad karma. But if you neither belong to good nor fall to evil, the wheel is left blank and no words are written. Each wheel form [of this first type] has two sides [written opposite each other, good karma written in red, bad karma written in black, the remaining two sides left blank], depending on whether you have good or evil seeds or not.

The second type of rotation is to identify whether your good or evil is strong or weak. In the past, we created strong negative karma, or strong good karma. [Strong evil karma] will be [represented by a line] black, rough, heavy; The universal form appears to you [like that]. Great good karma is [represented on the wheel of appearance] by a very long red line. [The line represents] short good karma means small good karma. If you create good karma that is not great, it is indicated by a short red line. The second type of rotation is to contemplate whether your good or bad karma is strong or weak.

The third type of wheel is the retribution in the three past, present, and future lives [represented on each wheel] by numbers, including one hundred and sixty numbers, that is, the retribution to be suffered in the present. When you cast the wheel to ask questions, or when you do business, or you ask whether your illness will get better or worse, nothing goes beyond that number of one hundred and sixty. There are eleven numbers belonging to the past, eighteen numbers belonging to the future, that is, twenty-nine numbers belonging to the past and future, plus one hundred sixty numbers [belonging to the present], making a total of one hundred eighty-nine cases. That is how the number [one hundred and eighty-nine] was born. Six senses, six senses, six consciousnesses, three times six eighteen, plus basic ignorance into nineteen items, forming nineteen wheels.

Due to that one hundred and eighty-nine number, when using the wood wheel in connection with the three lifetimes, if you want to ask something, then sow the wheel of that type, not all of them [all three types of wheel]. When you ask about the past, you sow the wheel of the past; If you ask about the future, you cast the wheel of the future; if you ask about the present, you cast the wheel of the present. The usage of these three types of wheels is different; But when using the wheel, it must be based on worshiping, praying for repentance, and worshiping Chiem Sat Sam. The Contemplation Sutra has the Contemplation and Contemplation Dharma and the General Dharma. You sit in a pure retreat, bow for seven days, use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate and see whether your good karma or bad karma exist, big, small, strong, weak, many, few, and the appearance of the wheel will all let you know in detail. For to one hundred and sixty [present numbers], add eleven [past numbers], to make one hundred seventy-one, and add eighteen [future numbers], to make one hundred eighty-nine. Because three times six makes eighteen, eighteen multiplied by ten makes one hundred eighty, plus the past, present, and future of this life, [the previous life, and the next life, that is, three times three makes nine], so one hundred eighty plus nine equals one hundred eighty-nine. That's the origin of those numbers. They all show your karma. Therefore, when you repent, the important thing is to reveal your repentance. If any karma is heavy, repent of that karma first.

Therefore, at first, when you start to worship and sow the wheel of signs, roughly the Ten Karmas in the body, mouth, and mind will be much black, red may be none, or very little. Until you worship, it will gradually change. Those who look at the wheel will know that gradually it is no longer black and turns red. “Red” means turning negative karma into red (into good). What is evil? That's about us Buddhist disciples. After you receive the precepts until after you have received the Three Refuges, that is good, good karma is deep and heavy, when it is heavy, [the physical form] will turn red. If good karma is deep and heavy, the black color of bad karma will gradually disappear. Until your entire wheel turns red, your repentance has been successful! At that time, when you practice the Way, whether you practice Meditation, practice Contemplation, or worship and recite the Buddha's name, the wheel of light will tell you: If everything turns red, you will definitely achieve success.

The penance dharma in the first half of the sutra is intended to be used for the second half, not to ask about our good and evil in the human world. You can ask about good and evil in the human world, mainly for the sake of cultivating the Way. When you lose your mind and sow the form of the wheel, you will know to what extent your own karma has been eliminated. Because there is a limit, you will know how much your own good karma has grown! But [sometimes] your physical karma is not heavy, or none at all, but your verbal karma is especially heavy. Therefore, you should specialize in repenting your verbal karma. While repenting, he addressed Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. When you have finished your repentance, when you are about to dedicate, you must speak clearly and address Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. At the same time, while worshiping, when practicing this repentance method, when using the wheel form, the incarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will definitely appear. Why? Regarding your red and black karma, if Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not come, your repentance will not be successful!

While practicing, you can experiment a little. There are many Dharma friends who practice. When I worship, I do the same. When you have a lot of negative karma, when you repent, your heart is very sincere. At that time, what was specifically required? Sincerely! Sincerity is sincerity. The scriptures in the following section will say how to be considered “willing mind”, there is a preliminary mind (lower mind), a middle level mind, and a higher level of mind, which must be controlled in one place. At the lowest level, the mind will not be complete, and repentance will not be successful. No matter how much you bow, [due to not having enough will], the effect is not great!

(Sutra) The words of the Ten Good Ones, because they are necessarily fundamentally wholesome, they are bound to retain all good dharmas. The words of the Ten Evil Ones, because of the evil nature of all evil things, they can take advantage of all the remaining evil dharmas.
(Sutra: Speaking of the Ten Virtues, it is the basis of all good deeds, which can include all All other good deeds. Speaking of the Ten Evils, they are the basis of all evil deeds, and can include all other evil deeds).

Because the Ten Virtues are the basis of all good karma, the Ten Evils are the basis of all evil karma; Therefore, the Ten Evils and Ten Goods are the preliminary basis for repentance. When repenting, you sow the wheel of the wheel every day. The wheel of the wheel will tell you which karma is especially heavy, so you specifically repent of that karma. Whatever karma is heavy, your mind will pay attention to it. Because usually, what is the biggest obstacle to our practice? It's not greed, anger, or ignorance, it's doubt. While you worship, the first thing you do is eliminate your doubts, you must first repent of your doubts. If you don't believe in the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, why are you still bowing to the sutra? It doesn't work! Do you doubt whether Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will appear or not? Whenever there is a thought like that, it is doubt! If you have doubts, can you still achieve it? If you doubt, you won't achieve it! Even more important is that you must be sincere, urgent, and do not have the slightest bit of arrogance! If you have a haughty mind, a haughty mind is the supporting condition of greed, anger, and ignorance. Greedy and foolish mind are arrogance. Pride is the basis of [afflictions].

Therefore, pay attention, while you sincerely bow, without any arrogance! Why? Because whenever you enter a penitentiary[8], for your afflictions, visualize yourself first and cut off the afflictions first. Afflictions, arrogant afflictions, doubt afflictions must be cut off first. When you enter the penitentiary to worship, there is not the slightest doubt. The first thing is to believe in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the second thing is to eliminate greed. Arrogant dependence on greed. Greed is too heavy, doubt is too heavy; Those are two great taboos in repentance. Furthermore, when worshiping, you absolutely should not have a mind of resentment, a mind of hatred, a mind of harming others, or a mind of jealousy. When worshiping, enter the repentance room, then cut off greed, anger, and ignorance. Pride belongs to greed, doubt belongs to ignorance, several types of [mental factors such as] attachment, harm, anger, and anger all belong to anger, that is, the mind of anger. While you are bowing and entering the repentance room, keep your mind calm. The first thing is peace of mind, people say “a peaceful mind is achieved”, meaning your mind must be peaceful to be able to achieve it!

We have all studied Mahayana teachings. If we speak according to the teachings of perfection, how can we be considered perfect and without hindrances? Just one word is complete, that is, when you enter the penitentiary, everything will fall, and it will be good. Because that is the retribution of good and evil karma, [contemplating the cycle of appearances is to] contemplate the retribution of good and evil karma. Of course, if you do not develop Bodhi mind, you will not enter the penitentiary, nor will you bow to Chiem Sat Sam. When you wish to develop Bodhi mind and enter a penitentiary, when you seek repentance, repentance, ignorance, afflictions, habits, and Thoughts or Thoughts in the past must all be completely eliminated, that's why you repent. Because in normal times, we ourselves do not have that power, why do we have to bow to Chiem Sat Sam? In order to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to bless us, so that we can gain more strength. When you have bowed for one day, the next day when using the Contemplation Wheel, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not incarnate. At that time, he does not incarnate, but your intention and appearance will not be able to be determined. According to my experience, the wheel signs sown in the first seven days are neither true nor appear. After the first seven days [of repentance] are completed, you begin the second seven days [of repentance], [the reincarnation] will be effective, the effect will be effective. Therefore, the appearance of red or black is the appearance of appearances, letting you know which karma in the past is heavy and which karma is very light. That is called “the key point of repentance”. Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's incarnation will appear, you will successfully sow the wheel. If Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not appear, his reincarnation does not come, your physical appearance will forever be uncertain, your answer will not match the question, and the physical appearance displayed will not be accurate.

You must pay attention to this, what are you paying attention to? Don't take fake appearances as sincere. When you worship, you should pay attention to this! When you worship, you will be able to use the Contemplation Wheel. Today we worship all day long, today we do not sow [the moral form]. Today I worshiped all day, early tomorrow morning, as soon as I entered the penance room, I used Chiem Sat Luan first. After contemplating, then worship again. On that day, do not use the Contemplation Wheel. After repenting, early the next morning, we will use the Contemplation Wheel first to observe our harvest of the previous day. After you have bowed for seven days for the second time, during the third seven days, the wheel form will change at any time. Until you have performed [repentance] four times and seven days, the samsara will return. How to return? At that time, the red color [obtained by sowing the wheel of the wheel is usually considered] pure, but it is not pure[9]! Why? That's called the karma of discovery. You have repented and purified the current [karmic strains], the correct karma will immediately come! You have not yet paid off your current debt, your past karma does not appear. When the present [debt] is purified, it (the reincarnation) will return to calculate past karma. You must repent twice as much! After repenting for three sessions, four sessions, five sessions, the karma gradually becomes pure. At that time, your mind is very pure, your afflictions are light, and your repentance is very peaceful. At that time, the body and mind will achieve a state of lightness and peace. You must have worshiped before you can experience this. If you don't worship, you won't have it!

(Sutra) Weak desire to contemplate the false appearance of the wheel, the first person to study wholeheartedly in the ten directions Buddha. Nimmediately made a vow: "May the spirits of all sentient beings in the ten directions, with all their disabilities, be close to them, make offerings, and receive the Dharma." The second person learns with all his heart to pay homage to the collection of teachings in the ten directions. Nimmediately makes a vow: "May the spirit of all sentient beings in the ten directions, quickly receive and maintain them, recite them alone, practice like the Dharma, and speak to others." The second student wholeheartedly pays homage to all the sages of the ten directions. Nimmediately makes a vow: "May the souls of the ten directions all sentient beings, quickly attain the ability to be close to them, make offerings, develop Bodhi mind, and not regress." Later, he learned to pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva. The person immediately made a wish: "May the spirit of all sentient beings in the ten directions, quickly eliminate the evil karma of serious sins, get rid of all obstacles, and all sentient beings will be prosperous."
All the Buddhas.Dso, immediately make a vow: "May all sentient beings in the ten directions quickly be close to, make offerings to, and receive the Dharma." Next, you should sincerely study and pay homage to all the teachings of the ten directions. Therefore, immediately make a vow: "May all sentient beings in the ten directions quickly receive, recite, and practice the Dharma." practice, and speak for others." Next, you should learn to wholeheartedly pay homage to all the sages of the ten directions. DSo, immediately make a vow: "May all sentient beings in the ten directions quickly be close to, make offerings to, and develop Bodhi mind, until there is no turning back." Then, you should learn to wholeheartedly pay homage to me, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. Therefore, set up Prayer: "May all sentient beings in the ten directions quickly eliminate serious evil karma, be free from obstacles, and have all the necessary things for life in abundance."

It is absolutely not that we take the form of the wheel and then contemplate it, it is impossible! When you want to contemplate the wheel of life; First of all, you must learn to be mindful. The first thing is to learn to be mindful. Anyone who wants to contemplate the universal form, if you want to practice this method, first of all, you should learn to sincerely pay homage to all the Buddhas of the ten directions. When you pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions, you immediately make a vow, [that is the meaning of the phrase] “a cause immediately makes a vow”, what is that vow? May all sentient beings in the ten directions quickly approach, make offerings, and receive the Dharma. The first wish is the first thing that comes to mind. If you want to worship and repent, if you want to use the Contemplation of the Luan General, first of all, you must learn the mind. “Single heart” is your mind that is sincere, urgent, and focused on your mind, that is “one mind”. Everyone worships whatever dharma they worship with one mind. Does our mind still have two? Making you single-minded is teaching you that at that time there are no false thoughts at all, let go of any thing. The mind is not as [simple] as I just said. In the following section, the scriptures will talk about what single-mindedness is like. There are three types of single-mindedness. One is to wholeheartedly pay homage to all the Buddhas of the ten directions. While bowing to Buddha, he made a vow. Why do we have to pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions? My goal is to hope that all sentient beings in the ten directions can make pure offerings to the Dharma. Speaking of the dharma first, [hope that they] will “receive the true dharma” (please receive the true dharma).

Next is to study wholeheartedly and respectfully pay homage to all Dharma collections in the ten directions. Therefore, I immediately made a vow, praying that all sentient beings, that is, sentient beings in the ten directions, will quickly receive, recite, and practice according to the Mahayana dharma. You can accept and maintain any sutra. The Diamond Sutra, the Samantabhadra Sutra, the Amitabha Sutra... All the sutras are included in it, all of which are the ten method collections. But when you chant, you must make a vow. I have asked many Dharma friends, they also recite the Mahayana, but do not make vows, nor do they dedicate themselves! So what are you chanting for? If you don't make a vow, the effect won't be great!

Therefore, before wanting to do something, you must make a vow: What goal do you want to achieve? Hope for what? Not only the Ksitigarbha dharma, other dharmas are also like that. The first thing is to pay homage to the Buddhas, the second is to pay homage to the ten methods, and the third is to pay homage to the ten sages and monks. That is, first of all, we pay homage to the Three Jewels, which is usually the case. But Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us that when you worship all the Buddhas in the ten directions, you must make a vow, praying that all living beings can make pure offerings and receive the Dharma just like you. Turning to the Buddha to request the Dharma, asking the Buddha to preach the Dharma is called "receiving the Dharma". [That way] is the Buddha's Treasure ceremony.

The second thing is to worship all dharma stores. You must also make a vow, vowing that all sentient beings will be able to accept, uphold, read, recite, practice in accordance with the Dharma, receive and maintain the Buddha's Mahayana teachings, and be able to follow the teachings of the sutras to practice, not just simply accept and uphold the Dharma, just ask the Buddha to preach the Dharma, but also rely on the Dharma to practice. Next, you should wholeheartedly pay homage to all the sages and saints of the ten directions, so immediately make a vow: May all sentient beings in the ten directions quickly be close to them, make offerings to them, and develop the Bodhi mind until they do not regress. Normally, if you perfect the mind of the Ten Faiths and reach the position of First Pillar, you will not retreat. That is [the order of status of Vien Giao Bodhisattva] according to the Avatamsaka Sutra. That's what Hoa Nghiem teachings say. According to the five common teachings of the Mahayana, reaching the Seven Bodhisattva Levels will not regress, but normally, [lower positions] still regress. In the Avatamsaka Sutra, perfecting the mind of the Ten Faiths, participating in the First Pillar [will not regress]. Saying “Abiding” means “not regressing”. The Three Jewels ceremony is like that.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us, if you want to study the Contemplation Wheel, study the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma; First of all, you must sincerely and earnestly pay homage to the Three Jewels, then you must make a vow, that is, make a vow to make it possible for all sentient beings to pay homage to the Three Jewels. It is not just me, but the countless sentient beings of the ten directions. After bowing to the Three Jewels, he bowed to me, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. You should learn to pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva. When worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you must also make a vow: "May all sentient beings in the ten directions be able to eliminate the evil karma of serious sins, be free from obstacles, and have all the necessary things for life in abundance." Paying homage to the Three Jewels, that is the main dharma, that is, the main dharma of the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. As people in the world are polite, only praising the Three Jewels, not talking about themselves, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not follow that custom, [He teaches bluntly]: "You must pay homage to me, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva." Because you study Ksitigarbha Dharma and want to use the Contemplation Wheel, you must pay homage to me, that is, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. At the same time, you must also make a vow, [the scope of the vow] is also in the ten directions: "Pray for all sentient beings to eliminate evil karma and heavy obstacles, allowing them to have all the necessary items in life." Simply put, it means making everyone rich. Only when you become rich will you have the necessary items for life, there will be no shortage, everything will be prosperous and abundant!

This passage is an homage to the Three Jewels, known as the Four Great Vows. In all the Mahayana sutras and sutras, the Four Great Vows are fulfilled. What the mind is, will be detailed in the following section, I will only give an outline. The mind must reach the level of no self, no human, no sentient beings, there is no self as the person paying homage, nor are there the Three Jewels and Bodhisattvas as the objects of worship. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to take such a solemn vow, it is called “single heart”. That is called the Four Great Vows of Non-action, no action, no wish. Right in wishing, wishing is not wishing. Non-action: Action is non-action, you should not be attached to it in your mind. Therefore, first of all, make yourself single-minded. Only when you let go of your single-mindedness, there is no attachment at all, only then can you reach your single-mindedness in all ten directions. Otherwise, how can we cover all ten directions? Our minds are very attached, so when you enter the penitentiary, you must let go!

Since we all use the Contemplation Wheel, at first glance it seems very simple! You use the Contemplation of the Wheel Form, before contemplating the wheel form, there will be a sadhana. That sadhana is the homage to the Three Jewels. Paying homage to the Three Jewels is not just one or two, but is immeasurable, boundless, all the Buddha Treasures throughout the dharma realm of the ten directions, all the Buddhas in the dharma realm of the ten directions, all the Sangha gems in the dharma realm of the ten directions; You also have to make pure offerings. These two words are very difficult! In a pure mind, without any other distracting thoughts, if we persevere, we can do it easily once in a while. We can do it, but we can't keep it for long. You enter the penitentiary, from morning until night, can it all be the same mind? Is it always possible to not give rise to false thoughts? Can we always pay respect to the Three Jewels? I examined myself, realizing I couldn't do it. I think there is a great Bodhisattva present here who can do it, this is not easy! When it comes to developing the mind, it is very easy. You can develop a strong mind. As soon as you hear it, the mind of repentance for bad karma can easily arise, but keeping that mind for a long time is very difficult! We bow all day long, we can patiently let go of anything, what about the second day? What about day three? A strong mind is easy to arise, a mind that can be maintained for a long time is difficult to be born! That's why when you worship, in the first three days, you use Chiem Sat Luan and you will feel chaos, it simply doesn't correspond! Because your mind is not yet concentrated, using the Contemplation Wheel needs to be single-minded. Isn't it like going to a fortune teller's stall, I give you a few coins, you calculate a hexagram for me and that's it. It's not that simple, it's not that simple!

I see that we Dharma friends have all developed Bodhicitta. Developing a mind is easy, but wanting to perfect that mind is very difficult! Compassionate mind, compassionate mind, great compassion mind, all three minds are complete, then “develop Bodhi mind”. I think among you, there are many who have received the Bodhisattva Precepts, all of whom are great Bodhisattva minds. I tell a story, the story of Sariputra. Sariputta intended to develop the Bodhi mind and leave the Sravakas. To develop Bodhi mind, one must save sentient beings. He has just developed his great heart, Emperor Thich Thien, we often call him the Jade Emperor. That is the incarnation of Bodhisattva, not the ordinary Emperor Thich Thien. When Sariputta had just developed Bodhi mind in the human world, Emperor Thich Thien immediately came to test the Venerable, waiting for him right by the roadside. Sariputta developed Bodhi mind, Emperor Thich Thien immediately turned into a poor little girl, waiting on the side of the road, crying. Sariputta had just awakened his mind and saw that realm appear, so he asked the little girl: "Why are you crying? Can I help you?" The girl replied: "You can't help me!" He said: "I have the ability to help you, tell me what you need?" The little girl said: "My mother is sick and is about to die. The physician prescribes and cuts the medicine. The prescription is very easy to buy, but the drug's substance is hard to find!" Venerable Sariputta asked her: "What should I use to administer the medicine?" She said: "You must use the eyes of a living person." After hearing this, Venerable Sariputta thought: "I had just developed the Bodhi mind and immediately encountered this incident. The reality of the realm was sent immediately!" He thought: "Okay, I'm satisfied for the girl", then gouged out an eye for her. The girl cried out: "It's wrong! You pulled it out wrong. I need the left eye. You took the right eye, it won't work!" Venerable Sariputta replied: "Why didn't you say it sooner?" There have been some mistakes, the will power is still lacking! He thought for a moment: "Okay! Anyway, I have heavenly eyes, it's okay," and gouged out the other eye for her. The little girl took it, smelled it and cried: "Oh my God! It stinks, I'm going to vomit to death! How could it be put in medicine!" Throw it on the ground, then step on it. Venerable Sariputta said, "Great mind is difficult to develop." As soon as he develops Bodhi mind, he immediately encounters such a realm. Both eyes were gouged out, but still not satisfied! Emperor Thich Thien immediately said: "Give your eyes back. You cannot develop Bodhi mind."

When you hear this story, what do you think? Currently, we develop Bodhi mind, I think our Dharma friends all develop Bodhi mind, but no one wants to ask for our eyes, nor does anyone want to ask for our nose. Why? We have not yet reached that realm, knowing that we are illusory. If you rely on repentance to confirm that you have developed the mind of Bodhisattva, and are blessed by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will develop the mind of enlightenment.

(Sutra) As the market offers, according to the offerings of incense, flowers, and offerings.
(Sutra: After such a ceremony, depending on the flowers and incense you have, you should make offerings).

After you have finished worshiping the Three Jewels of the ten directions, and having finished worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, do your best. Depending on what you have, the same goes for incense, the same for flowers, depending on your own strength to make offerings to the Buddhas, that is "making offerings". After paying homage to the Three Jewels, you must practice making offerings. “offering” is still making offerings to the Three Jewels. This offering is optional. It is best to use the great power of visualization to make offerings. You don't need to buy some flowers, why buy some fruit! Please apply the method of offerings. The Dharma of offering refers to the mind; You use the vow power of your mind to make offerings. I have told many Dharma friends: Early in the morning, when you want to make offerings to the Buddhas, you sit there, calm your mind and contemplate. Whatever markets, department stores, shops, or fruit stalls you have been to, visualize moving them all back. It's the same in America, it's the same in Beijing, Shanghai, Taipei, Taichung, Tainan, you use it all to make offerings. That's called “memories”. I once said that to a Dharma friend, and he said: "You speak a very false statement!" I said: "That's real, how can it be fake? If you make an offering in the way you say, it will already be lost in two days, but my way of offering is forever indestructible. As long as my mind is immortal and my vow exists, [the things offered by that visualization] will forever exist." People should not compare whether it is fake or real. Actually, everything is fake, your aspiration is real! Are our vows all fake? That's not true! That's the truth! If it's fake, it will be ruined. After explaining it like that, it is just “making offerings”.

(Sutra) Cultivate false offerings, recollect the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, TThe body is constantly changing, never existing.
(Sutra: “Practicing offerings” means remembering all Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, Te is always all-pervading, it does not exist anywhere).

After you have finished making offerings, you must calm down and think. That is, after you have entered the repentance room to worship, make offerings to the Three Jewels, and pay respects. Then, remember. Having made offerings, there are still memories, what memories are there? After making offerings, he recited the Three Jewels: Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the Three Jewels are everywhere, they exist nowhere. That's the truth. Right in our ashram, the Three Jewels of the ten directions are present; Your mind is sincere and earnestly contemplating. Buddhist scriptures often teach: "Faith is the source of path, mother of merit, nourishes all good roots" (Faith is the source of path, mother of merit, nourishes all good roots). If I say this, you probably won't believe it! Where? Are there Three Jewels here? We are all Three Jewels! Don't limit yourself to this house, expand it, expand your mind. Expand to what extent? Endless in space, all over the Dharma world, there is no place where the Three Jewels are not permanent. No matter how big your mind is, how big your capacity is, the dharma will be that big. This has a very important relationship, it's not fake; that's the truth. Other things are easy to perish, but also easy to disappear! Your mind is forever indestructible. Having said that, isn't my death “ruined”? You die [your body dies], but your mind does not die. Your power of visualization, your power of practice and repentance is not lost at all, it remains intact! What's the problem? It's because you don't believe it, it's over! Therefore, if you want to bow to Contemplation and Repentance, you must believe in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, believe that while we worship, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will prove it to us, bless us, eliminate our karma, allowing us to become a Buddha right in this body, a little faster. If you don't have that mind, it's best not to bow! It is necessary to establish that faith. Therefore, the Contemplation Sutra teaches you to be single-minded. With sincerity and diligence, anything can be achieved. Therefore, it is said: While you make offerings, you must remember the Three Jewels. The Dharma entity of the Three Jewels always exists, and is not present anywhere, it is everywhere! Don't think Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is in hell saving sentient beings! In the depths of space, throughout the dharma realm, there is no place that is not Ksitigarbha.

(Sutra) May the spirit be able to taste the fragrance of flowers and be of the same dharma nature, and bestow all Buddhas to watch over and pray. Buddhist works.
(Sutra: Pray that those incense, flowers, etc. are equal to the dharma nature, pervading all all Buddha lands, performing Buddhist work).

At the same time, we must also make a vow: May all the incense and flowers we have offered be of dharma nature, equal to the dharma nature, everything we have offered, everything is dharma nature. All Buddha lands have me in them performing Buddhist work. So if you wish to be born in the Pure Land, it will be easy. You make offerings and do Buddhist work there. The world of Ultimate Bliss, the Glamorous world in the East, the Immovable world above, all the worlds have me making offerings in them, the Dharma nature is complete everywhere. Therefore, everyone who learns to contemplate Good and Evil Karma should greatly expand their minds. When you enter the penance room, you must do that! I heard someone say to me: "Dear old master! You have taught Avatamsaka, why do you still teach the Hinayana dharma, teaching about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?" Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's three sutras are all Avatamsaka, don't misunderstand! Everyone has heard me preach this passage of the Three Jewels Offering Sutra. Next is the contemplation of the wheel form. Please open your mind!

(Sutra) Reciting the ten directions must necessarily worship the instrument, timeless and non-existent. The ten directions possess all kinds of incense, flowers, roses, garlands, phantoms, treasures, precious gems, music, lights, fire blessings, food, clothing, sleeping utensils, herbal medicine, and herbs. Even ten directions have all kinds of solemn offerings.
(Sutra: Think again of all the offerings in the ten directions, never without them. I will use them now. All kinds of incense, flowers, pearls, mala, jeweled parasols, magical decorations, music, lights, torches, fire, food, clothes, blankets, medicine in the ten directions, and all the solemn offerings in the ten directions.

Think of all the offerings in the ten directions. To make offerings to the Buddha, he arranged offerings. You set out a tray of fruits as an offering, incense and flowers are all offerings, there is no time, no place without offerings. There is never a time when it is not there, it is always there. I bring all kinds of incense, flowers, pearls (jade necklaces, or necklaces made of precious things), rosaries, phantoms, jeweled parasols, all pearls, agates, all mysterious ornaments to adorn the ten directions. There are also all kinds of music, lights, torches, fire, food, clothes, blankets, medicine, and all kinds of solemn offerings in all ten directions.

(Sutra) Thoughtful thoughts, all sentient beings worship and make offerings, constantly reciting the essential practice of the intermediate world It seems fake, the golden fall depends on joy. Those who practice making offerings wish to attain enlightenment and spiritual practice make offerings.
(Sutra: Think and hope that all sentient beings will make offerings, often think of In all worlds there are people who practice making offerings. I now congratulate them. If there are those who have not practiced making offerings, may they be guided and instructed to practice making offerings.)

Thinking, remembering, hoping, using my contemplation to hope that they all make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us how to make offerings? It is not just me, but all sentient beings who make offerings to me. It was as if the entire assembly present [in this sutra lecture assembly] were making offerings at the same time. Don't we all wish to be reborn in the Pure Land? First of all, make offerings to Amitābha Buddha. As soon as you pay attention, you have made an offering. You tell me, is it real or fake? You buy ten pounds of apples, buy ten pounds of bananas, set up a house full of flowers, limited, very few! If you expand your mind and make offerings far away, it will be great. If you always remember and always make offerings like that, who can destroy your offerings? No one can destroy it! You buy a few fragrant flowers, buy a kilo or two of apples, they will spoil very quickly, they will all rot!

I'm not the only one who makes offerings like this! Think often that in all worlds, practitioners make offerings in large numbers. They practice and make offerings, all of which are mine. When they practice making offerings, there is also me, I also participate in the offerings. Those are the vows"to dedicate the universal stage" and "to rejoice in merit" in the ten great vows of Samantabhadra. In the worlds of the Buddhas in the ten method precepts, there are many great Bodhisattvas who are requesting Dharma and making offerings, and we all participate and rejoice. That is “rejoicing in the merits” of Samantabhadra's ten great vows. I often think that whoever makes offerings to me will be rejoicing. Those who have not yet practiced making offerings, I will advise them and everyone else to practice making offerings, causing them to practice making offerings.

(Sutra) Wishing for the self to quickly transform the will to attain, the oneness of Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and others. Of course, all kinds of solemn offerings should be made, and all sentient beings should worship and worship.
(Sutra: Again, I pray that my body can quickly reach all the lands, to every Buddha place, The Dharma and Sangha all use all kinds of solemn offerings to share with all sentient beings equally.

Before you use the Contemplation Wheel, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches you to make that many vows and do that many things. You still have to make a vow, what is it? It is possible to quickly reach all the killing states, just like the Avatamsaka Sutra says: “The number of Buddhas in the Dharma world is as many as the number of motes in the Dharma world.” There are as many Buddhas as there are dust particles, each Buddha has a Kṣetra, a Buddha realm. The Buddha realms are as numerous as the number of dust particles. In each Buddha realm, there is the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, the Three Jewels. We use all the offerings to adorn them everywhere. We and all sentient beings make offerings. “Equality holding” is holding countless offerings equally.

(Sutra) Offerings to all Buddhas, Dharma Bodies, physical bodies, relics, images, temple talismans stupa, necessarily Buddhist work, offerings necessarily possessing Dharma treasures, access to Dharma teachings, offerings to necessarily sages and monks.
(Sutra: Offerings to the Dharmakaya, body, relics, images, stupas and stupas of All Buddhas, all Buddha's work, offerings to all Dharma collections, and Dharma teaching places, offerings to all sages and monks).

Make offerings to the void throughout the dharma realm of all Buddha realms, make offerings to the Dharma Bodies, bodies, relics, and images of all Buddhas. There is a Buddha who is the Dharmakaya Buddha, there is a Buddha who is preaching the Dharma and appears in the body of Buddha. There are Buddhas who are physical bodies, like Śākyamuni Buddha who is physical bodies, there are Buddhas who enter Nirvana and leave behind relics. Make offerings to all Buddha statues, pagodas, temples, stupas, “ stupas ”[10] as towers and temples. All Buddhist work is “Buddha Treasury, Buddha Treasure”. Offer all the Dharma Jewels, as well as the place where the Dharma is preached. That offering includes the Dharma throne and Dharma hall to preach our Dharma in the present. We see people making offerings to us, do you see them or not? Can't see! Because those things are included in the offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, it depends on whether you believe or not? I advise everyone to trust. All the ashrams in the ten method precepts practice making offerings, that is, making offerings to the Buddha, making offerings to the Buddha's work, making offerings to the Dharma collection, as well as [making offerings to] places where the Dharma is preached, making offerings to all the sages and monks.

The offering of the Three Jewels has a huge scope, we cannot imagine! Let's expand our minds a little more, not limit ourselves. Do you know how great the Buddha's assets are, how wealthy the Buddha is? If you don't read the Avatamsaka Sutra, you won't know the Buddha's wealth. When you read the Avatamsaka Sutra, you will know that the Buddha's wealth is limitless and immeasurable. In this sutra, Ksitigarbha teaches you to make offerings to the Three Jewels infinitely and endlessly!

(Sutra) May all sentient beings practice. If you make offerings, you will gradually attain the Six Paramitas, the four immeasurable minds.
(Sutra: May all sentient beings practice. Offer like this finished, gradually achieving the Six Paramitas and the four immeasurable minds).

Next is sentient beings: Pray to all sentient beings, pray that all sentient beings are like me, what are you doing? Make offerings to the Three Jewels as mentioned above! After making offerings like that, you will have merit, merit, and wisdom. Without wisdom, it will be impossible to initiate such offerings. That offering increases your blessings and eliminates your karma. You gradually achieve the Six Paramitas and the Four Immeasurable Minds. The Four Immeasurable Minds are as people often remember, loving kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity. Six types of Paramita, including Generosity, Morality, Patience, Diligence, Meditation, Wisdom, those six types and the Four Immeasurables. So you use Almsgiving, Precepts, Patience, Diligence, Meditation, Wisdom, plus love, compassion, joy, and renunciation, that is, your own Four Immeasurable Minds, to make offerings, so that from the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death you can reach the other shore of Nirvana! Speaking of great vows, you must truly make your vows to call it “great vows”, to bring all sentient beings from the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death to the other shore of Nirvana. During that time, one will practice the Six Paramitas, the Four Immeasurable Minds, and the Ten Paramitas. That is called “the dharma of making offerings to the Buddhas” (using the dharma to make offerings to the Buddhas). Giving everything we have to sentient beings. Furthermore, when making offerings to the Sangha, one becomes pure and immaculate. Because of that kind of pure offering, you attain the Paramitas of Precepts. If there is no affliction in the mind, it is the Paramita of Diligence. All impurities and impurities will disappear and one will enter Zen; That is Paramita Meditation. A mind without anger is the Paramita of Forbearance. Abstaining from distractions is the Paramita of Diligence. There is no chaos at all, which is the Paramita of Tranquility and Meditation. Making all sentient beings happy is great kindness. Since it can give joy, it can give joy to all sentient beings, [causing them] to achieve happiness, causing sentient beings to have no suffering. How can we prevent all sentient beings from suffering? It is great compassion, compassion can end suffering. Words can bring joy. May all sentient beings be happy, so that they will be immeasurably happy. Your mind is always equal, there is no difference, especially in treating suffering sentient beings equally, without resentment. That is called Immeasurable Equanimity. Loving-kindness, compassion, joy, renunciation, the Six Paradigms, ten thousand virtues, the Four Immeasurable Minds.

(Sutra) Deep knowledge of all the dharma of the origin, tranquility, no birth, no death, one taste, equality, no mindfulness pure, all perfect.
(Sutra: Deeply know that all dharmas are inherently static, have no birth, no existence cessation, a taste of equality, pure mindfulness, ultimate perfection).

At the same time, we must visualize, reflect, and know deeply that all dharmas are inherently tranquil. This is using the power of visualization. You visualize that all dharmas have no birth and death, are inherently quiet, equal, have an equal taste, are pure from thought, and are ultimately perfect. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches sentient beings like that. When you have not used the Contemplation Wheel, before contemplation, expand your mind. Everyone listens to me read this sutra, you say: "In the end, is the Sutra on Contemplation of Karma the Mahayana or the Hinayana?" Please judge for yourself!

(Sutra) Praying for the mind system to make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, who is claiming his name. Nhuo silently chanted, single-mindedly declaring: "Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat". As she declares her name, she is full of contentment.
(Sutra: Also subduing the mind, dedicated to making offerings to me, that is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Bodhisattva Mahasattva, you should recite the name, or recite it silently, with one mind saying: "Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva".

You should tame the mind that insists on making offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. You must also sincerely and earnestly make offerings to me, or recite my name, use my name to make offerings, or use silent chanting to recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Silently chant, single-mindedly speaking. It's still not enough for you to simply chant, or just revere and worship. You still have to turn to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to narrate and present it to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Then recite “namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat”. Say the name and recite it a thousand times, a thousand sentences. What does this mean? If you want to use Chiem Sat Luan, you don't have to take out the wood wheel and plant it immediately. Isn't it like going to a fortune telling booth, giving the fortune teller a few coins, and he immediately calculates a hexagram for you!

(Sutra) The Sutra of Heavenly Thoughts and Children declares: “Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva is great, great. compassion, only vows to protect the thoughts and self of all sentient beings, quickly eliminate all obstacles, increase pure faith, and the contemplation of spiritual gold is truly appropriate."
(Sutra: Having recited the full number a thousand times, then said like this: “Ksitigarbha Bo Mahasattva Mahasattva of great kindness and compassion, respectfully pray for me and all sentient beings to quickly eliminate obstacles, increase pure faith, and make what I see correspond to the truth.

After reciting a thousand verses of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's holy name, you make a vow again, facing the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and saying: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you are a great and compassionate being. Please protect me and all sentient beings to quickly eliminate the obstacles, causing all the causes and conditions to hinder the path of the path." All children are eliminated. Now my faith is still not complete, please increase my pure faith." That is the request of Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, because our faith is not complete, it cannot be said to be steadfast, and when it comes to things that arise, they have not yet arisen. Therefore, "increase your pure faith, so that you sow the form of the wheel that will correspond to the truth. Otherwise, He will not be merciful, will not take care of you, and the form of the wheel will not correspond." That is to request Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's compassion, causing the thing we want to ask to be corresponding, meaning “suitable”. If you ask something, the general will answer it for you and what you should do. We don't know how to do it properly, so we use the wheel form to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for guidance. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells you to do like this and like that. “Presentation”: When we want to use the wheel form, we must first address it to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) The authortu natural language, natural defense clinging to the wood wheel, the purity of the upper and lower objects is overwhelming.
(Sutra: After saying this, then, holding the wood wheel in hand, sow it on a clean object).

“The authortest of the language”: After bowing like that, the explanation is complete and then sowing the wood wheel. It's not like taking the [wood wheel] and sowing it right away. Only then (when you have finished worshiping and making your vows) will you take it and sow it. There are three types of Wood Wheels, so don't plant [all three types] at the same time. It is necessary to sow in the early morning every day so that it will be sown in peace. You cannot sow all three types at the same time. If Luan is sown, there will be three cases: One is red or black. The second is a big red line, or a big black line. Third is the small red line, or the small black line. When you worship, you will sow those three types of chakra every day. If it is all red, it means pure repentance. At that time, what can you ask for? When sowing the wheel of rotation, you must place a clean towel, or clean cloth, or use a [clean] piece of plastic as well, so that the core is pure. [That is the meaning of the sentence] “planting your hands face down on a clean object”.

(Sutra) Like the desire to contemplate the dharma. Weak desires contemplate others, the heron is like this, and is aware of it.
(Sutra: If you want to meditate for yourself, do it this way. If you want to meditate for others, you should know: Everyone should do the same).

If something happens to you, you will cast the wheel to ask, so is it okay if I sow on behalf of others? Help others too! You can meditate yourself, or you want to meditate for others, it's okay! Contemplating others means you contemplate a certain person, or contemplate a certain teacher. Simply put, whether you think Mong Tham is a good monk or not, you should cast the wheel of the wheel once, and the wheel of the wheel will let you know. I won't tell you I'm not good, I still can't repent frankly before you like that, not yet! But you can ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: "Is this monk okay?" You cast the wheel of the wheel once, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will tell you: "If it's still acceptable, you can trust that person." Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will not deceive you. He said good is good, bad is bad, you can ask Him. If you want to worship someone as your master, you can ask “can I worship the master or not”, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will tell you. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not hide his shortcomings, nor does he hide my shortcomings for personal gain, nor because I am a worshiper of Him, or because I am His disciple, He hides my shortcomings, not at all! He will speak the truth. You can shop for yourself or for someone else!

There are so many of us. When everyone wants to learn the Dharma of Contemplation, there are many Dharma friends who all understand, can spread, and everyone learns from each other. The first thing is to be sincere, sincerity means “single-mindedness” as this sutra says. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught: The mind has an upper mind, a middle mind, and a lower mind. None of us can achieve the highest aspiration; Only a saint has the highest will; But we study the mind in the summer solstice, not letting it become confused, the mind is not confused. When you enter the repentance room, be sure to leave everything outside the door of the repentance room, don't bring them into the repentance room! Once inside the penitentiary, the mind does not have two thoughts. If you cannot, then “namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”. It is enough for you to imagine Ksitigarbha's appearance and recite the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. That is considered to have a single mind, every thought never leaves Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. You can't attain the purity of the wheel by repenting, but if you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name and bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, a lot of karma will also be eliminated. Because you have spent a lot, while you are dreaming, you encounter something unsatisfactory, or an unsatisfactory business, whatever problem you have can be resolved. But you yourself must have sincerity. You can deceive others, but you cannot deceive Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! I think everyone believes this! Therefore, you must sincerely and urgently tell the truth. Don't think that what you say in front of the [Bodhisattva] image will not be spiritual. It will be much more spiritual than what others say in front of you. We don't have that power, I certainly won't lie to you!

I have experienced these matters myself, but my karma is very heavy. I had just sent Dharma Master Hoang Nhat back to Xiamen, so I went into retreat in Qingdao[11] to bow to Chiem Sat Sam. After a few weeks of bowing, all the chakras were about to become pure when the Japanese occupied Qingdao. After the incident on July Seven[12], when the Japanese army attacked Qingdao, we had to completely stop worshiping. That is a huge obstacle. But after I unsuccessfully worshiped the wheel of repentance, several decades later, it was very painful and very miserable! It wasn't until several decades later, in 1989, that I was asked to preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma in New York in Manhattan. It was not a good thing! After that, another ten years later, from 1989 to 1999, he again preached the Sutra on Contemplation of Good, Evil, and Karma at Pho Tho Pagoda at Wutai Mountain. Then ten years later, this year is 2009, from 1989 until 2009, we can preach, explain, and study. The fate of everyone studying is like that, it's all inconceivable, it's all unimaginable!

I came to Taiwan because I wanted to exercise. I was not well in Wutai Shan, but I have just recovered a little. I said that in the mountains, my body was not strong, so I went down the mountain to exercise a little. Going to Thai Nguyen, staying in Thai Nguyen is also very good. I said I had to go a little farther, then I thought about going to Taiwan. As soon as I thought about it, I had an epiphany. Coming to Taiwan, I had absolutely no desire to preach the Dharma or lecture the Sutras again, feeling that I did not have that strength. Even though I'm not old yet, if you're ninety-five years old, you're still old enough! This story is extremely realistic; It's not up to you to admit it or not. It's the same if you admit it, but if you don't admit it, it's the same. If you get old, you'll already be old! Not only old age, but also death. If you haven't died yet, you can count as being blessed by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. How can you even think about preaching sutras? You don't have that strength! Now when I'm lecturing on the sutras, I see that after listening, people still haven't criticized or objected, but when I start lecturing, I'm still worried about whether I can finish the lecture or not? Now I see that there is basically no problem, I can finish teaching!

Contemplating good and evil karma, each of us has a small ruler in our hearts. Although the ruler is not long, it measures [your own mind] very clearly! Karma is not heavy and will not be born in Sa Ba. Our karma is very heavy, we were just born into Sa Ba, but we can all listen to Buddha Dharma, and we can also hear a lot of Buddha Dharma. Not only can you listen, but you can also follow. Having heard it, you can also think, think is visualization. Not only Tu, but also practice, administrative practice is Tu. Van Tu Tu samadhi is complete. After listening, then consider, we must do it. I also use this Contemplation Wheel method, I don't know how big or small my karma is. We realize: For all Dharma friends who come to attend the Dharma conference, your karma is not very big. If you were big, you wouldn't have encountered the title of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Not being able to hear this title, but still being able to study the Sutra on Contemplating Good and Evil Karma, studying the Ksitigarbha Sutra, there is no way, there is no way! Everyone must believe this story!

But our karma is light, we should be able to attain enlightenment, but while karma is neither heavy nor light, each Dharma friend [can achieve it or not], depends on how you recognize yourself, depends on each person's efforts! People say "karma is not heavy, it will not give birth to Sa Ba", I say "if you can listen to the Dharma in Sa Ba, your karma is not heavy". Being born in Sa Ba is a very heavy karma, but in this world of heavy karma, to be able to listen to Buddha Dharma, that is, in a place of heavy karma, your karma is not heavy! We should not just because the old monk said my karma is not heavy so we can indulge in promiscuity and not do anything! If so, then the karma is heavy, not that it isn't heavy! I say "karma is not heavy" because you can listen to the Buddha's teachings, can practice according to the teachings, and follow what the sutras teach you to do; But don't evaluate yourself too highly. Why? If you rate yourself too highly, you won't achieve anything. If you don't achieve it, you will become discouraged and gradually decline. After being able to listen to [Buddhism], it is best if you wish to worship and repent, first recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva ten thousand sentences. Every day, if you put your mind to it a little, it is very easy to recite ten thousand verses, and recite ten thousand verses of holy names. In the Ksitigarbha Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva advised us: "If you encounter any difficulty, recite my name ten thousand times". When I encountered difficulties, I planned to go to Taiwan. The first time I couldn't go, I recited ten thousand verses. Still can't do it, can't ask for permission! I recited ten times more, recited ten thousand sentences, but still couldn't do it! I'm a bit stubborn, there are many things I'm very stubborn about, I recite a million sentences. It didn't work, so I recited thousands of sentences, continuously chanting. I recited a hundred thousand sentences, I felt it myself, the passport procedures were completed. As for all dharmas, we should not think that they are difficult. Listening to the teachings of the sutras [feels] very difficult. [The sutra teaches to] be single-minded, I am not single-minded; It's okay! Just practice, practice a little and you will be determined!
