tom_tat: Volume 5 (Sutra) One who contemplates the cycle of manifestations, depending on the present karma, must be satisfied with the one true contemplation of experience, or the pure instrument of the Ten Virtues, or the pure instrument of the Ten Evils, or the mixture of good and evil, or pure good without any instrument, or pure evil without any instrument, like the karma of any human race...
noi_dung:
Lecture 5

(Sutra) Contemplation of the cycle of false appearances, depending on the current karma, must be the most consistent in contemplation, or the ten pure tools. Good, or purely mixed with the Ten Evils, or mixed with good and evil, or purely good, or purely evil, like different types of human karma. The habit of retribution, the differences, as the Buddha, the World-Honored One, expounds on it, with memories, thoughts, and contemplation of the current karma, the metal world's retribution, the experience of suffering, pleasure, auspiciousness, and harm, and the accumulation of afflictions in the karma, attaining the equivalent of falsehood and corresponding fame. Weaknesses are not equivalent, people have no heart, fame is vain.
(Sutra: Contemplating the wheel of signs, following the karma shown [by the wheel of signs], is recommended for each form If you contemplate carefully and contemplate, either pure enough of the Ten Virtues, or pure enough of the Ten Evils, or good and evil mixed together, or not completely pure good, or not completely pure evil, such different types of karma, habits, and consequences for each will be different, as the Buddha, the World-Honored One, has said in detail in other places (in other sutras). You should remember, reflect, and observe the karma that has appeared, if they are equivalent to the consequences, suffering, happiness, good, and bad things. etc. experienced in this life, and afflictions and karma, are called "corresponding". If they are not equivalent, it is because [the practitioner] has no ambition, it is called "illusory, misguided".

This passage teaches us: If you want to use the Contemplation Wheel, the Contemplation Wheel shows good or bad karma. Good karma is red, bad karma is black. If the [karmic strains] that have appeared [by the wheel of appearances] correspond to what you experience in reality, corresponding to all situations in life, then it is "suitable", very correct. If it doesn't correspond, then your afflictions are inherently very heavy, and your habit energy is also very heavy. Everything is unsatisfactory, showing that your karma is very heavy, yet when you use the wheel form, it all appears in good red color; that is “no correspondence”. The answer does not match the question, so it is called “not corresponding”. If the wheel form appears “not killing”, it is said that you have no killing karma, but you are sick and suffering for a long time, that means the wheel form does not appear accordingly! The universal appearance shows that you have no killing karma, the killing karma in the past was very light, so in this life there should be no illness, less suffering, and a long life, that is called “corresponding”. What does “Not corresponding” mean? When you use the wheel form, your mind is still not sincere, [so] the wheel form does not appear. It's a kind of phenomenon. While you request, worship, and want to use the wheel form, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not appear and the wheel form does not correspond. You pray once, twice, three times, even in one day, ten days, from beginning to end, the cycle of appearances does not correspond, because your mind is still not committed to taking refuge. That mind is false, so the universal form does not appear. Another type is when you feel something that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva still does not respond to. [Bodhisattva] does not respond, then the wheel of appearances does not correspond. Due to our past causes, the karmic causes and habits in the past, as well as the retribution in this life, must correspond to those shown by the wheel of appearances. That is called “correspondence”. [Correspondence] like that means you have asked for blessings from Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. That is called “corresponding”, but an answer that does not match the question is called “not corresponding”.

[The main sutra] teaches us: When you use the Contemplation Wheel, the first thing is to worship and practice single-mindedness. In the following section, the scriptures will explain in detail about the mind of determination: What is the highest mind, what is the middle mind, what is the mind of the lower mind? Will explain in detail, a lot! Normally, we don't observe this either. You also don't understand your own lack of ambition! [Just think] "Even if I don't have any false thoughts, that's my sincere mind", it's not that crude, [the sutra will explain] very meticulously! The sutras teach: When you contemplate the universal form, because of the different karma in countless past lives, you will have different habits that manifest differently in the present. Each individual has a unique habit, everyone pays attention, looks at each person's movements, [will notice] each person has their own movements, whether speaking or acting. That's called habit, everyone is different! If the manifestation of the wheel of rotation is not the same as the habits in your life, it means you are still not single-minded. Your mind still cannot reach the level of single-mindedness. So first of all you have to capture your mind to reach the ultimate mind, then you can contemplate the wheel of life.

(Sutra) Weakness in contemplation of the wheel of life, no good or bad karma will appear, test the cause to attain anaura of mind, seek diligently renunciation, disobedience, and worldly retribution. Those who have illegal karma develop weakness and their wings do not grow. Thi tried not to appear.
(Sutra: If one contemplates the wheel of life and neither good nor bad karma appears, [it is because] that person has The mind is free of asrava, dedicated to renunciation, no longer interested in receiving worldly retribution. The defilements gradually become weak and no longer grow. Therefore, they do not appear.

If when contemplating the wheel of life, your good and bad karma will not appear at all. Whenever you contemplate, the whole thing is empty (that is, all the wheels are blank, without words). Contemplation once is like that, contemplation twice is the same. Contemplate ten times, eight times, and they will not appear at all. Neither good nor evil appears. You yourself still do not know clearly, in fact, you have attained the wisdom of anasrava. Your mind has attained anasrava wisdom, so the Contemplation Wheel does not appear! Contemplation of the wheel of appearance refers to beings who are skeptical, and sentient beings who have not yet participated in the status, so they use Contemplation of the wheel. When you have decided to believe and have realized the results, the wheel of existence will not appear!

There is another type, that is, those whose hearts are not sincere, [the reincarnation] will not appear. There is another type where you attain the Eight Rings, the Eight Wisdoms, the Realm of View, the Mahayana scriptures call [that position] the Seven Pillars, that is, the Seven Pillars of the Mahayana. The Avatamsaka Sutra calls that position the First Pillar. Bodhisattva Bodhisattva's initial teachings do not have any form, [because], in the three worlds, all of your karma does not exist. Your three karma of body, mouth, and mind in this world have changed, because the Distinguishing Seeds of the three worlds have been cut off, so they do not appear. Why? Because you don't have that karmic cause, you don't receive that karmic result, so it doesn't appear.

The Karma Contemplation Sutra mainly helps you avoid karmic consequences in the next life. I deserve to fall into hell. If you pay homage, contemplate good and evil karma, worship and repent, you will not fall into hell. If one deserves to fall as a hungry ghost, [then due to the merit of repentance], one will not fall. You completely don't have that cause, have cut it off, so it doesn't appear. From now on, you can practice until you become Buddha. Therefore, at this time, that type does not appear. Pure goodness does not appear, because you have reached a state of pure goodness, [the physical form] does not appear. Purely evil is because that person's evil habit is too heavy. If you sow for a month or two, the wheel of rotation will absolutely not appear. Why? Evil karma is too heavy, so it does not appear. Then you must worship and worship until the universal form appears, and karma will gradually disappear.

(Sutra) Pure good has no substance, pure evil has no false substance, test whether the karma of good and evil of the two races does not appear. fake, the stage is weak, because the ability to shield the fruit. Ttrying to not appear.
(Sutra: Again, pure goodness is not enough, or pure evil is not enough, those two types of people all have good and evil karma If they do not appear, it is because they are weak and small and cannot lead to fruition, so they do not appear.)

Furthermore, “pure good, not complete” means it is not pure good, pure evil is not enough, it also means it is not pure evil. For middle level beings, good is good and evil is good, evil and evil are good, the wheel of rotation is extremely effective, that is, when good karma and bad karma cannot be decided, it will appear. The manifestation is intended to make you follow the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to practice. If you can achieve pure goodness, bad karma will gradually disappear, good karma will gradually increase. A purely good person is not complete, his universal form is extremely effective. For those who are not yet pure enough to be evil, their reincarnation is extremely effective. Therefore, whether good or evil karma does not appear is because your karma is weak, small, and cannot bear fruit. Good karma is also very small, weak, and cannot feel good results. Evil karma is also very small, weak, and cannot feel evil results. Because it floats half-heartedly like that, sometimes the wheel form does not appear. Even if you sow the wheel and the form does not appear, you must worship [until the wheel] appears and appears to tell you. In the main scriptures, it is said that because [karma] is weak and small, it cannot lead to results.

Good karma is the same, but bad karma is the same, it does not lead to retribution in the present, so sometimes it does not appear. Regarding this type of non-appearance, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: "You must practice Mind-Only Contemplation". That is the appearance of the realm in the second half [of this sutra]. Mind-Only Contemplation, or Contemplation of Consciousness-Only, belongs to the second half of the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. [Those contemplations] are taught in the second half of the series. If the good karma is strong, you will feel the good result. Strong negative karma, you will feel negative results. Neither good nor bad karma can lead to results for you to receive [then the wheel of existence will not appear]. When you worship, it will appear, showing you how you should practice!

Here talking about karma, “karma” means Use (effect). If good karma is good then you will feel good results, if you are evil then bad karma will feel bad results. That is called “karma”, just like when we do something now, that thing is called “karma”. When you create that karma, sometimes it is good karma and feels good results, sometimes it is bad karma and feels bad results. If good is not strong, and evil is not strong, then the results will not be felt. It is necessary to strengthen [that karma to experience the results]. Karma is what you create. That is using the word Application to explain. Whichever aspect of your karma you apply, whatever aspect of your mind you apply, will receive results in that aspect. Because as soon as we start thinking, we fall into two paths: One is good, the other is evil. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, it is the same for good, but also for evil, all must be observed properly. “Correct observation” means whether what you think in your mind closely matches the appearance shown by the Contemplation of the Sat Wheel or not. If it is not appropriate, it means it does not correspond, the answer does not match the question. As for those two types, one type is when you use the Contemplation Wheel, when you request saints, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not appear. [Bodhisattva] does not appear, you will not be able to contemplate. All appearances (appearances of the realm) are illusory. Until you pray earnestly, you will know your own karma. Each of us knows that whatever you do is not to your liking, whatever you wish for is not achieved, it is all against your will, it is all about dissatisfaction, afflictions, hindrances, hindrances, hindrances, obstacles, you immediately know that your own karma is very heavy. We often hear our Dharma friends say their karma is very heavy. I don't believe it, they don't tell me the truth! That's not polite! The karma is very heavy, you will not be able to hear the Buddha Dharma, you will not even hear the name of the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. This was said by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, not by me. When you hear the name of the sutra, it means you have a predestined relationship with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and a predestined relationship with this sutra.

Due to the things you think about that belong to greed, anger, ignorance, your body commits killing, stealing, prostitution, lying with your mouth, embellishing words, double-talking, and harsh speech. If you add the word Emptiness in front of those things, it will be the Ten Good Karmas; without the word Void, it is the Ten Evil Karmas. Every move and every move you make, your mind thinks, what your body does, and your mouth speaks every day, all belong to the ten karmas. If you do not belong to the Ten Good Karmas, you will belong to the Ten Evil Karmas and you cannot escape! Speaking of "escape", we are saints, have attained the Four Fruits of Arahatship, and are people who have no insight, so what is the use of contemplating the wheel of life? The form of the wheel does not appear, even if you contemplate it, it will not appear. The meaning of using the wheel form is that we deal with our own karma. You always say that your karma is very heavy, but to what extent, you don't know! This is not an object that can be weighed with a scale or measured with a ruler to know whether it is big, small, long, short, heavy, light, many, few. You use the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma as a measure, and you will know how heavy your own good karma is and what level of practice you have finally reached. Therefore, you will understand clearly for yourself: You completely do evil things, do all evil things, do not do any good things, or do purely good things, without any evil karma!

Those two types of people are very few, the vast majority are mixed good and evil. In everyone's daily life, sometimes good thoughts arise in their minds, and sometimes evil thoughts arise in their minds. The four assemblies of disciples, that is, monastics such as monks and nuns, [lay people including] upasakas and upasakas, of course are many good and few evil. Even though thoughts sometimes arise, but according to Hinayana teachings, thoughts that arise in the mind are not counted, because you do not take specific actions. According to worldly laws, can what we think in our mind be considered a crime? Not considered a crime! Even in the precepts established by the Buddha, such as talking about the precept of killing; As for the precept of killing, one must kill someone to be considered breaking the precept of killing. At that time, killed, but not yet dead; After that, being taken to the hospital and then dying, is a lower level crime, not completely considered murder, allowing repentance. Having killed that person, he died a month or two later. Due to injuries, according to the law, he also died from injuries. While killing, if [the killed person] stops breathing, it will be considered an accomplished killing karma. Later, if [the victim] dies from injury, you still have not committed the crime of murder. The precepts call it the crime of Saṃghāvaśeṣa, not yet committing the ultimate crime of killing. That is the karma that is analyzed very carefully.

You use the Contemplation Wheel in the same way, that fate will be promoted and achieved in time. Like the case of murder I just mentioned, [the victim] died as soon as he was killed, meaning the evil fate had ripened. If you don't kill him right away, the evil fate won't be as heavy! The law is analyzed very meticulously, and in the precepts it is also said to be very strict, at any time will it be considered a violation of the precepts! If you are a student of the precepts, you will know "the eight conditions that lead to breaking the precepts" (the eight conditions that create the breaking of the precepts); If those eight conditions are complete, you will violate that precept. Of the eight conditions, you only violate four conditions, if you violate half, it is easier to repent. If you lack just one of the eight conditions, it will not be considered a violation of the precepts. That is good or evil karma, weak and small, unable to give rise to results. If you kill someone, it will trigger very intense consequences. Not only must there be retribution, but there will also be flower retribution, retribution, and retribution. In the past, killing karma was very heavy, you paid your life debt, but in this life you still have many illnesses and disasters; That's called “reminder”. If you study the precepts, this story will be explained in detail. Each karma has many types of conditions. When all of these conditions are met, it is considered a transgression. If you lack one or two predestined conditions, you still haven't committed a sin, that is, when you repent of your sin, you can differentiate. The law in society is the same: If you kill at that time, the situation will be completely different! The crime is more serious. Killing before death, being taken to the hospital for treatment, or living for one, two, three months, that is called “death due to injuries”, the situations are different, the crimes are also different. Therefore, there must be a clear distinction between pure evil and pure good.

What I just said here has a broader scope than cause and effect, that is, in addition to cause and effect, there is also habit. When people of the Second Vehicle study the precepts, or study the law, study the scriptures, although they have cut off good and evil karma, have cut off Views and Thoughts, but Ignorance has not been cut off. The habit of good and evil karma has not yet been broken. We are many people, each individual's habits are different. Habits do not commit crimes, good habits have good habits, evil habits have evil habits. If one's compassion is too deep, one's compassion is very strong, one's compassion is very deep, and if one sees others suffering, one's mind is very miserable; That's called kindness, but it can't work, it can't help others avoid suffering. Only having an empty mind is not called “great compassion”. To spare others from suffering, or to suffer on their behalf, ordinary mortals cannot do this! Because if you want to suffer for others, you can't. You don't have that ability, but Bodhisattvas can. So your retribution has disappeared, but you still have habit energy. This story will be discussed again until the next part of the scriptures, because we still have to talk about how to use Chiem Sat Luan.

(Sutra) In the future, Buddha disciples, if you contemplate good and evil, you will attain the corresponding retribution, the five At the same time, when we educate people to get what they want, things become self-sufficient and lethargy arises. That is, following the thought: “Do the ego is like trying to promote good karma, the golden ego can test the results. The golden ego can turn its wings to practice, not satisfied with retirement”. Weakness creates yokes for all beings, all kinds of depression, unsatisfactory things, disturbances and sorrows, unsuitable times, longing for life, lack of spirit of regret, retreat from cultivating good karma. That is, thinking: "The birth is created by the ego, such as the evil karma, the golden eagle tries to report. The golden ego is regretting the evil karma, specializes in counter-cultivation, up-to-date and cultivates the good, in vain, only dwells, relaxes, is lazy, turns the wings of the Sangha to gather the species of suffering." The name Chiem Sat first wheel of physiognomy.
If you are satisfied with the objects of the five desires, you should not be indolent or lethargic, but immediately think: "Because of the good karma of my previous life, I have now achieved this retribution. I should now practice even more, and not stop." If you ever encounter disasters, mental breakdowns, or bad things that disturb you, causing you to be worried, afraid, or unsatisfied, you should be resigned, do not doubt, regret, and withdraw from cultivating good karma. You should think: "It's only because I created such evil karma in my previous life, and now I have to suffer this retribution. I should now repent of those evil karmas, focus on practicing to counteract them, and practice other good things, and should not stop, be lazy, let go, and turn into accumulating more sufferings."

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, talking about “the future”, that is, talking about the future, which means talking about the end of the Dharma. The Buddha's disciples are those who take refuge in the Three Jewels, bhikshus, bhiksunis, upasakas, and upasikas; Those who do not receive the Three Refuges are not counted. You have believed in Buddha for many years, but have not accepted the Three Refuges, then you are not counted as a disciple of Buddhism. One must receive the Three Refuges to count as “entering Buddhism”. If you are a Buddhist in the future, that is, in the next life, and have contemplated the corresponding good and evil consequences, that is, when you contemplate, what the scriptures have said corresponds to all of your thoughts and actions, then it is called “corresponding”. In your previous life, your killing karma was very heavy; In this life, you have to pay back, or you will be sick for a long time, everything will be unsatisfactory, and you will always be hurt and harmed. That is called “correspondence”.

In your previous life, your good karma was profound, you never killed anyone, you never got sick in this life, and no one hurt or harmed you. Regarding the five desires, everything is satisfied, satisfied with the realm of the five desires; At that time, you must pay attention, don't let go! Once satisfied, don't ask too much. How should we think? It is due to our past good karma that we can achieve this retribution in this life. Suppose from this basis, we practice again. “Conscientious practice” is to be courageous and diligent in doing good deeds, not doing evil things. This means advice and encouragement. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva advises you not to stop at the present, not to be satisfied with the present, but still to make every effort to cultivate, to make it better!

If in your current life, you encounter everything that is not to your satisfaction, encounter hardships, often encounter depression, are not good, always make you afraid, sad, dissatisfied, everything is against your will, how do you deal with it? Be willing to endure! Be patient, tell yourself that this is my karma in the past, don't do anything anymore, now I will receive the reward and repay it! You should be willing to endure. Don't doubt, don't regret! This is extremely important. Especially for the four disciples of the Buddha, i.e. Bhikkhus, Bhiksunis, Upasakas, Upasams, in the past, you did things that harmed others. In the past, harming others only caused pain to others and did not make others happy. In this life, you suffer and do not gain joy, nor are you happy. So what should you do? You should endure unpleasant things, that is, happily repay your debt. If not, you will have to pay additional "interest".

When you repay debt, you borrow money from someone else, don't you need to pay interest? For example, if we kill someone, we pay for that person's life [and that's it]. Where can it be! How many years ago, how many lifetimes, did you kill that person? Still have to add income. You have to pay that extra interest, which is called killing karma and there are consequences. Otherwise, you will see that the person will be upset and have no luck at all, which is a sign of negative consequences. You don't have any grudges with people, there's nothing wrong with you, you meet a lot of people on the road, people go back and forth, there's no psychological impact at all! You have no predestined relationship with that person, there is no predestined relationship whatsoever. When you see someone else, you feel very happy, which means you have some connection. When you see that person, you feel troubled, which means you have some connection. It's not love without reason, nor hate without reason. This happens to everyone, you can think for yourself.

Because in the past, you have created negative karma, in this life your body is often sick, with many unsatisfactory things, sadness for no reason, sadness for no reason, trouble for no reason. Yes or no? I think all of you Dharma friends have it. I don't understand why you can't hold it in your heart. Is there such a thing? Others see you as very good, but you yourself feel very troubled. When others see you enjoying yourself, you feel unsatisfied. Every Dharma friend has [such a feeling], for example, what afflictions do monks have? What burden is there? But you yourself have troubles arising for no reason, everything is unsatisfactory, you know that past karma is discovered, that is called “discovery of past karma”. Because of your past karma, because of the existence of karma, afflictions arise in you. You must be aware! You didn't realize it before, [now by] studying the Contemplation Sutra, you now realize it, so be patient and endure it! That patient mind needs to have wisdom, [recognize] the karma in the past discovered, that is called "cultivation". Not only by reciting Amitābha Buddha, but by worshiping and repenting, is practice. You can recognize your own karma, you can practice like that, that is true practice!

Therefore, if you meditate like that, on the path of spiritual practice, you will not relax, nor will you dare to slack off. Because one's own Views have not yet been cut off, not to mention the afflictions of Ignorance, That Ori is still very heavy! Must be diligent, causing all kinds of good karma to grow. That is the most basic requirement when using the wheel form of Chiem Sat Luan. Because you don't know, Contemplation Sat Luan immediately tells you: At present, whatever karma you discover, you immediately break through it. Why are we troubled without reason? Just like there are times when we flail our hands and feet for no reason, we don't understand why it's like that, we're extremely excited! Whatever makes you excited, you can't find the reason, your heart is extremely happy. It could be that today you go up and chant the exercises and then chant the corresponding chants, or you practice together with the assembly, or today you do a good deed. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, the Contemplation Wheel will let you know and will appear. Therefore, it is called Chiem Sat.

(Sutra) Good man! The desire to contemplate the past and accumulate karma is nine-closed, so that the strong, the weak, the big, the small are different, overcoming the wood and the three wheels. Body, speech, mind, the main wheel, the book of letters. Huu U Luan is the center of the book, the book is the plan, the spirit is rough and the school is full of friends. The second two sides, the book one plan, the spirit of the short, the story is not you. The third facet, the action is immense, as planned, and the spirit is profound. The fourth four-sided, the heron is penetrating, the spiritual history is thin. When you realize that good karma is dignified, it is like disaster, bad karma is damaged, it is like harm. The great person who plans to be long, shows that his good deeds come back nine, his karma is powerful, and his actions increase. A short person who plans to sacrifice, shows good deeds and is close to each other, tends to be reckless, and acts in vain. Qi overcomes the rough and profound, shows the evil and the future, the monks of the monks, and the queen of the herons. At times, the poor person shows signs of regressing to good, and practices evil deeds, so that his career will rise to the top. Or even though he begins to be seriously evil, he will gradually repent and test his taste for small evil.
(Sutra: Good man! If you want to contemplate the ancient karma accumulated in the past, it is a long time ago. or recently, strong, weak, big, small, different, you should again carve the wood into three wheels. Use the body, mouth, and mind as the master of each wheel, write the word to remember [which wheel corresponds to which of the three karma of body, speech, and mind]. Again, on one side [opposite the side where the letter is written], draw a line so that [the line] is thick and long until it meets the eyelids (the junction between the flat surface of the wheel and the two sharp ends). Then, on the second side, then draw a line so that [the line] is thick and long until it meets the eyelids (the junction between the flat surface of the wheel and the two sharp ends). Draw a thin, short line so that the line does not meet the eyelids. Then, on the third side, engrave near one edge of the wheel like a line, so that the engraving is rough and deep. Then, on the fourth side, also carve a line close to the edge of the wheel so that the engraving is shallow and small. You should know that good karma is dignified like a decorative line, bad karma is like a concave line. Small and short lines show recent accumulation of good deeds, slow foundation, small and thin deeds. Deep and coarse marks show that evil deeds have been done for a long time, and the remaining misfortunes are also thick. Small and shallow marks show a recent decline in good deeds, and the karma has not yet reached the level of improvement

Good man! If you want to contemplate the past karma that was performed in the past, whether it was long ago or recently, the karma created is strong, weak, big, and small differently. In the past, whatever we did, we feel the same result now. Like our four disciples, the Buddha's disciples belonging to two monastic communities and two lay communities, if in the past, you did not have good karma, created good karma, in this life you will not meet the Three Jewels. Even if you meet one, you won't believe it, because there is no fate. In the end, whether we practice good karma, big or small, long distance or close, the power of good karma is strong or weak, we already have awareness in our own minds. Everything is unsatisfactory, even though you believe in the Three Jewels, even though you have practiced a little in the Three Jewels, [your practice] is not great, not strong, your strength is very weak, then when you contemplate, the Contemplation of the Chakra will tell you: In the past, you sowed good causes that were not great at all. In this life, you must practice quickly; Otherwise, you will lose good people in this life. Make your own good karma grow, make your bad karma disappear, make good karma big, bad karma small, good karma strong, bad karma weak. That is the main reason for using Chiem Sat Luan. In it, if you say there is no great evil in evil, there is no great good in goodness. How should we increase the power of our own practice? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us the method; That is the true origin of Contemplation.

You should carve the wood into three circles, that is, use wood to sharpen it into three circles [also following the correct shape: The middle part is a cube, the two ends are pointed as in the previous section]. Of those three wheels, one wheel is concerned with verbal karma, one wheel is concerned with mental karma, and one wheel is concerned with body karma. That is, each of the three karmas of body, mouth, and mind has its own cycle. “Inscriptions of letters” [means] one wheel of body karma, one wheel of verbal karma, one wheel of mental karma, each karma corresponds to a wheel (each karma is written separately on a wheel) to contemplate the karma you have accumulated in the past. Our present karma is not one life, two lives, nor ten lives, eight lives, but hundreds of thousands of millions of lives, accumulated in the present body. Do you know whether those karmas are big or small? Your body is full of great good, or full of not so great good, or full of great evil, or not very great evil, or full of very big evil but small good, or very great good but small evil, or both equally, neither great evil nor great good, both in moderation. Goodness is not one lifetime, two lifetimes, but billions of years of doing good deeds. Good karma is very strong and sensitive, so in this life we ​​always meet good conditions and our minds are at peace. Entering Buddhism, always being courageous and diligent, not being lazy, being blessed by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, opening up wisdom, that is “great goodness”, belonging to the type of great goodness. The little good karma is not long gone, or it has just come to mind, which means the good karma is very small. Therefore, good is big and small, evil is big and small, there is bad karma that has been accumulated for a long time, and there is also bad karma that has not been completely formed for a long time. Small evils are like that, not yet reaching the level of elevation. You yourself should not understand the great good and the great evil very well, you need to contemplate the good and evil karma displayed from the wheel of life.

How is that wheel created? In the middle of one side, write a big, bold and long line, both big and long. That line is expressed very boldly, extending to the point where the face of the wheel of form meets the tip of the head [of the wheel of form]. The second side is a small and short line, showing that the good thing is not big, expressing the meaning of good karma that is not big, very small. On the third wheel, engrave a line so that it is a little rougher, to show that [that karma] is large, deep, and long-lasting, so it must be rough and long. One long, one short, one big, one small. Good karma is red, bad karma is black. If you look at the wheel of life in reality, you will know. For example, this wheel has four sides, two sides [with drawings or engravings] are red, one short red line, one long red line, one long black line, one short black line. For the red line, there is no need to engrave it deeply, drawing it on is fine, the black color must be engraved deeply. The four aspects [of the wheel form of the second type] are like that. If you want to make something, you have to do it according to the size. Is there a problem? The reason why this method cannot be widely spread is because it cannot control the Contemplation Wheel, and the sutra's teachings are not very clear. Long, short, square, round, in the end make the [wood wheel] big or small, as long as when you hold the wheel in your hand and plant it, it will rotate!

The big, long line, shown in red, means you have accumulated good deeds for a long time. Not only does it take a long time, but it also creates very strong and sensitive good karma. That's called “higher monk”. The short line [and red] means you haven't been doing good deeds for a long time. The line is both small and short, showing that your good deeds are very thin, very few, and have just changed. Evil deeds are the same. After committing evil deeds for a long time, the engravings are long, deep, and black. Not long after committing evil deeds, the engravings are both shallow and small; The black engravings are evil, but if they don't change, the short black engravings will turn into long ones, and light [evil karma] will turn into heavy ones. What is displayed by the wheel of appearance originates from the visualization in your mind: Loss and reduction is bad karma, growth is good karma. For good karma, your mind is very strong; When it comes to evil things, you are very scared, showing that your good roots are very thick.

(Sutra) Good man! Those who have not yet contemplated the beginning of the wheel of the wheel are able to fully understand the difference between good and evil karma in the world. They cannot understand the accumulation of the nine approaches and create the strong, weak, large, and small karma. She tried to meditate on the second wheel of meditation.
Good or bad karma is different, but it is impossible to know whether the karma accumulated in the past is long or recent, whether the karma done is strong, weak, big, or small. Therefore, it is necessary to contemplate the second type of rotation.

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: If you contemplate the first type of wheel, you will know whether our three karmas are good or bad, heavy or light, but you do not know how heavy or light that good is, whether the karma that has been accumulated for a long time is far or near, whether it is strong or weak. At that time, you should contemplate the second type of wheel.

(Sutra) The false dream of the second wheel of the wheel is the same as the first wheel of the central manifestation of the karma. Weakness belongs to the fake body, the body is full of appearances. Weakness belongs to the false mouth, and treats the speech rotation. Weakness belongs to the fake mind, controls the will of the general. Reluctantly try the three-wheeled form, one clear contemplation. Ying depends on the main thought of karma, is consistent with good and evil, depends on the wheel, and is separate from the dream.
(Sutra: If you contemplate the second type of wheel form, you should base it on the karma shown in the wheel form First, if [the existing karma] belongs to the body, sow the wheel of the body (i.e. the wheel with the word Body written on it). If it belongs to the mouth, if it belongs to the mind, do not use all three of these signs at the same time to contemplate the main karma. For each good or bad thing, use the corresponding wheel to contemplate.

Sowing the second type of rotation is not the same as sowing all three rotations at the same time. For the first type of wheel, ten wheels belonging to the three karma of body, mouth, and mind can be planted together. After sowing, you record it. If it is a physical karma, then only sow physical signs. If you belong to the mouth, you will only sow the wheel of the form that belongs to the mouth. If you belong to the mind, then only sow the rotation of the form that belongs to the mind. You can't cast three wheels at the same time! The side with red lines belongs to good, the side with black lines belongs to evil. If good karma is deep and heavy, it will be shown by a line that is both long and rough, and good karma [thin, little] will be shown by a line that is both short and thin, [both types] are red. Evil karma is the same: Heavy evil karma appears as a black and long line, light evil karma appears as a short and small line. You contemplate separately. These three wheels are the three wheels corresponding to the body, mouth, and mind. On each wheel, on the four faces, [each face will have a line]: A big black line, a small short black line, a big red line, a small short red line. Also write “body, speech, mind” [in one of those four faces]. If Luan belongs to Speech, write the word Mouth, if it belongs to Body, write the word Body, if it belongs to Italy, write the word Italy. The wooden wheel of the body is used to observe body karma, the wooden wheel of speech is used to observe verbal karma, and the mind wooden wheel is used to observe mental karma. Separate the three karmas to contemplate.

(Sutra) The second, the weak dream of the first wheel of the central character, the only good body, try the second wheel of the central character, the attainment An evil person's body has no ambition, no corresponding attainment, and a vain reputation. The person who has a good fortune does not correspond to the person who contemplates the beginning of the wheel of life, attains the karma of not killing, and attains the karma of the path; The master of the mind contemplates not killing karma, but in the second wheel of the cycle, he attains the body of an evil person and his name does not correspond to it. For the second time, the weak contemplation of the present moment of birth and return, does not ridicule killing karma, does not create killing crimes, has the intention of killing karma, but tries the second wheel of appearances, attaining the body of a great evil person, his position is not corresponding. Free speech, thought, and neutral karma do not correspond to the meaning. The heron is like this.
(Sutra: Again, if you contemplate the first type of wheel form, only the body is good, but in the form of wheel The second form, [sowing the wheel form] is an evil body, which means that [the person contemplating] has no intention, [so] it does not correspond, it is called illusory, misleading. Furthermore, when contemplating the first type of wheel form, there is no killing karma or stealing karma, intending to contemplate the karma of non-killing first, but in the second type of wheel form, the [result] is an evil body, then again, if one contemplates the present from birth Up to now, there is no liking for killing karma, no crime of killing, only killing karma in the mind, but in this second wheel form, it appears as a "great evil body", which is called non-corresponding. As for other non-corresponding meanings in speech and mind karma, you should also know that it is like that.)

When you contemplate the ten karma with the first type of wheel, your body karma is all red, which is good, but when you contemplate with the second wheel, [the result appears] the body is evil, that's not right! [The reason is because] you are not sincere and sincere. If you don't have the heart, the heart isn't sincere, if you sow casually, you'll be wrong! How to do? Again, worship and sow again. There are Dharma friends whose first contemplation did not correspond, so they continued to contemplate. It's gone wrong! Impossible! Why? Let's worship again! You follow the sadhana of repentance to bow and pray again. After repenting, you will sow again. I see a lot of Dharma friends who didn't have success the first time they sowed the wheel, [so they said] "Let's sow it again." I said it wouldn't work! You have to worship again before sowing again. Normally, today we sow no spirit, tomorrow you bow again, or you bow a second time. I tell my friends who are just learning to bow early in the morning and then meditate for the first time. After contemplation, if there is no correspondence, [knowing that the cause is your own] lack of ambition, throughout the day you recite Ksitigarbha's holy name, ten thousand sentences is fine, twenty thousand sentences is fine. Early the next morning, worship again, repent, and then sow. Sometimes we bow five times a day, bow four times, the first time we use Chiem Sat Luan, the second time, the third time we don't use it, because we still can't use it. Even when used, it still doesn't work. You spend a whole day today, bowing all day long, wake up early the next morning and contemplate first. After contemplating, worship again.

If you contemplate the first type of wheel form, the result will be good karma. If you contemplate the second type of wheel form, the body will be evil; That is called “no correspondence”. The reason for incompatibility is due to incompatibility. Why is it not suitable? It doesn't match the previous results, because your mind is not sincere. The sutras have taught: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, that person's heart is not sincere! If you are sincere, you will be effective; if you are not sincere, you will not be spiritual! If you get the result from the first type of wheel form which is “non-killing”, the second type of wheel form is killing, that is, from sowing the second type of wheel form, [the result] is again killing, no correspondence! If you plant the first type of wheel “there is theft”, if you plant the second type of wheel, “there is no theft” is also not compatible. If it is not correct, it is called “not corresponding”. If the answer is not correct, it is called “not corresponding”. So how do you do it? Today, you don't sow anymore, just pray again. Today you bowed three times and still did not sow. Wait until the next morning to sow again. After sowing, bow again. Starting from the time you yourself were able to understand the Buddhadharma, you did not like killing karma, never thought about killing, and when you saw insects, you did not think about hurting or harming them. You have not committed a crime that belongs to the karma of killing, but when you sow the wheel, it is said that your killing karma is very heavy and has killing karma. This is absolutely inconsistent. You still have to test your mind, until you plant the second form of the wheel and see that your body has committed great evil. That's called incompatibility. There is none, it does not correspond to the truth. That's called incompatibility. When "corresponding" and "not corresponding" means that when you sow the wheel form, [the manifest result] of the later wheel type does not match the previous wheel type. In your mind, you have never had the thought of killing, until you sow the wheel of the wheel, the wheel of the wheel says you have the karma of killing, is that possible? If it is not suitable, it is called "incompatible". That's called falsehood, you have to know and verify it yourself.

Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has taught us, we must correspond. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: You do not like killing karma, but the wheel form shows killing karma, which means it is not corresponding. Whenever the rotational form does not correspond, He teaches you to repent again before sowing again. There are many Dharma friends, when you sow the wheel, pay special attention: "Don't get discouraged because one or two days don't match." If you get discouraged, you won't use it anymore! One or two days, one or two weeks are not equivalent, just bow every day. Even though you have been bowing for seven days, you still use the wheel form and it is still completely inconsistent. Why? Because your mind has not yet been captured, you are still not single-minded, [so] the Bodhisattva does not appear. “Bodhisattva appears or not” is absolutely not the case that we will see the form of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, that is not the case! It's a question of whether the wheel form corresponds or not. If there is no correspondence, the Bodhisattva will not appear. If there is a correspondence, the Bodhisattva will appear. By worshiping and then reciting the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will eliminate your karma. To what extent can karma be eliminated? To the extent that you can be single-minded. Whenever you worship, your heart is filled with sincerity and earnestness. There are Dharma friends who worship to the point of heartbreak and crying, thinking about their own karma and the tribulations they have to endure in this life. [Then] it will be very easy to correspond. Therefore, considering contemplation of the universal form as predicting one's life and criticizing the eight characters is not right! For fortune-telling, you give [the fortune teller] a few coins and he will calculate a hexagram for you. [If you think that contemplation of the wheel form is the same] then it is not possible. It's not like you just prayed and then cast the hexagram and it will come true!

When you use the Contemplation Wheel, verify it yourself. At first I wanted to use [Chiem Sat Luan], [praying] one or two times but still didn't see the correspondence. First of all, repent of your current sins. Because we are so confused and our mind cannot be concentrated, how can we adapt to the corresponding form? Until you bow to one room or two rooms, people with light karma bow to one room and then use the corresponding wheel form. The karma is a little heavier, you have to bow twice. Some people bowed for three seven days, or twenty-one days, but the form of the wheel still remained and did not appear. Even if it appears, it does not correspond, it does not appear appropriately. Obviously, there is no killing karma, but the wheel form shows killing karma. Obviously you are not greedy, but the wheel of existence shows greed, or greed, anger, ignorance and afflictions. In normal times, you have never told a lie, but now you are lying, which means it is not appropriate! For example, you often like to provoke gossip, where Truong Tam accused Ly Tu, where Ly Tu spoke ill of Truong Tam; But the general says that you have not made the mistake of double-talking. You yourself still don't understand yourself and talk double-crosses all the time! You must repent of things that correspond to the wheel form for it to be effective, because you use the wheel sign [to repent in order to improve your karma], not to predict your life or criticize the eight characters, do you know that? What is that? Practice! When you practice, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva comes to prove it. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not come to prove it, your contemplation does not correspond, your questions are not answered correctly. That's called "no correspondence". You do not use good contemplation of the wheel. This is not a matter of "If I give you a few coins, it will be matched", not at all!

Repentance, the process of using the wheel of signs is the process of repenting for sins. What you can achieve is because the universal form shows you, you have repented of many sins, you must understand this principle. While you repent of your sins, grow in wisdom, that is, cultivate wisdom. Until your wisdom is opened, you will know the level of your own repentance: You have applied the Contemplation Wheel of Repentance, and there are also one hundred and eighty-nine explanations [for the third type of wheel of repentance]. Until you bow, [the reincarnation] will tell you what to do. In the following text, one hundred and eighty-nine types will be explained, that is, your six senses, six objects, six consciousnesses, plus basic ignorance into nineteen items, combined with ten lives, that is, nineteen multiplied by ten lives. Due to the past life, present life, future life, ten lives[13], these one hundred and eighty-nine things are created. Any number you have cannot go beyond one hundred and eighty-nine of those things. Six senses, six consciousnesses, six objects, three times six make eighteen realms, plus basic ignorance, there is nothing beyond these things. Contemplating like that, you will see your own good and evil from countless lifetimes up to now. Good or bad karma is created by six senses, six senses, six consciousnesses, and also the basic afflictions of ignorance. Because you worship every day to repent and eliminate your sins. When you repent accordingly, karma disappears and wisdom increases. The universal form is your own wisdom. Your wisdom will grow accordingly. You may wonder: Will I be able to be reborn in the Pure Land, can I develop great wisdom in this life, can I worship Contemplation Sama to the point of attaining the Four Fruits of Arhat, or attaining the status of Seven Pillars of Bodhisattva? Wait until you worship to the point of being formless, achieving formless, wishless, and you will be a great Bodhisattva. Therefore, when you still discriminate, when you use the universal form, when your wisdom opens and grows, your wisdom has grown, you will know that you have wisdom. Not only with the Buddha's teachings, but also with the reasoning taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, there will also be wisdom. When you deal with worldly matters, they will be handled quite appropriately. Regarding issues in family, society, and business, there will be wisdom and there will be no obstacles. We have not yet attained wisdom, and everything we do will not be appropriate, because we do not have wisdom. For those one hundred and eighty-nine things, you are not suitable because you do not have wisdom. Wait until you are suitable, whether good or evil. Once you are suitable, you will expand your wisdom. Having expanded your wisdom, you can then gain benefits. Luan General only teaches you that. But when using the dharma wheel, the first thing is to be patient, don't rush and rush, it's not like you do worldly things, hoping to achieve them quickly. There is no quick achievement!

(Sutra) Good man! In the future, all sentient beings, desiring to be free from birth, old age, sickness, and death, should study and develop their minds, practice Meditation, formless wise people, should be able to meditate on the world, so that the evil karma is minimal and important. Those who have bad karma have many consequences and cannot achieve it, that is, learn meditation, wisdom, and first practice the method of repentance. The reason why it's fake? If you try to accumulate evil thoughts that are strong and beneficial, in the present, you will definitely create evil and violate the serious prohibition. If he commits a serious offense, he will not repent, if he is pure and pure, if he cultivates Meditation, if he is wise, he will be able to overcome many obstacles and cannot overcome any plans. Either the mind is lost or deranged, or the mind is evil, or one accepts evil dharma and develops evil views. Thi Co, first practice the Dharma of repentance. Weakness in purity of precepts and keeping up with the world is a serious sin of committing sexual misconduct, eliminating all hindrances.
(Sutra: Good man! If all the sentient beings in the future want to pray To escape birth, old age, sickness, and death, to learn to develop the mind, practice meditation, formless wisdom, first of all, you should contemplate how much evil you have done in your previous life, whether it is heavy or light. If your evil karma is many and deep, you should not immediately learn to meditate and practice the method of repentance Most importantly, if you do not repent for purity and practice meditation and wisdom, there will be many obstacles, [making it] impossible to achieve. Or you will lose your mind, be confused, or suffer from external evil, or accept evil dharma, and develop evil views. Therefore, you must practice the method of repentance first.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: - Good man! If living beings in the future want to be saved from birth, old age, sickness, and death, that is, they wish to be free from birth, old age, sickness, and death, wish to develop the mind to study Buddha, wish to develop the mind to practice Meditation, practice formless wisdom, first of all, they should contemplate the evil karma created in the previous life, more or less, whether light or heavy. If your negative karma is many and deep, at that time, you should not study Meditation and wisdom, because even if you practice, you will not be successful, because you have very heavy karma and many obstacles. So what should we do? First of all, practice the method of repentance. That is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaching us to practice repentance, that is called “repentance”. Why do we use the Contemplation Wheel one time and not two times? Because you have karmic obstacles. When the karma disappears, it will immediately correspond. The karma disappears, the form of the wheel appears, which is also your wisdom growing, your karma disappears. It's not that it's all gone, but it's that our sins are lessened and our wisdom is increased. For Contemplation of the Wheel General, using the method of repentance, you will enter, that is called wisdom. But if you do not rely on the form of the wheel of life, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: If you have very thick negative karma and try to practice Meditation and learn wisdom, you will easily be relied on by demons and easily enter the demon realm. Actually, the method of repentance aims to eliminate evil obstacles, so demons will not appear. This is different from practicing meditation and wisdom. We are constantly in turmoil, our minds cannot be calm! If you practice the method of repentance and then practice Concentration, that Concentration will not have demonic obstacles. That is the blessing power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva due to practitioners relying on the method of repentance; The reason for using the Contemplation method is like that.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva speaks one more level deeper. “Why do you say that?”” means “why do you have to say that?” That person in the past was accustomed to very strong and sharp malice. That person's evil deeds are very strong, the roots of his past evil karma are very heavy, his evil habits are very deep. Due to bad karma and bad habits in the past, in the present that person will definitely do a lot of bad things and create a lot of evil. Even if you become a monk, you will still violate the precepts. The moral precepts are the four fundamentals (killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying). Suppose we do not repent purely, practice meditation, or practice wisdom, can we achieve it? The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is mainly for practice, making you first repent of your sins and then practice Meditation and wisdom, only then can you not give rise to wrong knowledge and wrong views, and only then will you not have wrong knowledge. Unrighteous understanding and improper understanding are all wrong knowledge and wrong views. In this way, evil views will increase. Therefore, if you want to practice Concentration and Wisdom, practice the method of Contemplation, or until you become Buddha, you must first practice the method of repentance. If repentance is pure, then, taking the Three Refuges, taking the Five Precepts, and even taking the Eight Precepts and Bodhisattva Precepts, the precepts are even more pure. Once you have received the precepts, you can keep them, which means that past karma is not too heavy; As long as you practice, there will be no obstacles. If you don't practice repentance and practice Concentration and Wisdom first, your own karma is too heavy, habit energy is too deep, evil habits and evil mental factors are too strong, not to mention the past, but your newly created karma in this life will be the cause and condition that hinders the practice of Concentration and Wisdom. Not only are you not cultivating successfully, but you are also being relied on by demons! Bhikkhus, bhiksunis, upasakas, and upasakas have received precepts but do not keep them, even violating the Three Refuges. The Three Refuges are the precepts! Having already received the Three Refuges, you still follow the belief in Catholicism (Christianity)! There are many people like that, not a minority. They even violate the Three Rules. The Tam Quy itself is also precepts, so it would be impossible not to fall into hell, that's for sure!

If you encounter the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma again, repent, repent, and repent again. I just said, after one or two days of repentance, the wheel form has never appeared, it is because the karma is very heavy. The karma you have created causes obstacles for you, even if you use this method you cannot use it. First of all, we must repent of those sins, then use the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, and then repent of our karma. Having said that, how do we recognize pity? If we use Mahayana teachings, "sin is inherently empty, only created by the mind". To create the mind, use the mind to repent. If the mind is destroyed, the sin is also gone. The loss of mind and the destruction of sin are both empty; That's called true repentance, have you done it yet? That is called formless repentance. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us that you must move from form to formlessness. If you can't do the repentance with a form, can you repent without a form? Therefore, in the second half of this Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, it is not like that, cultivating Concentration and cultivating Wisdom, two types of contemplation, the realm of One Truth, directly entering the dharma realm, that is the Avatamsaka realm. The main purpose of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra is that we cultivate to become Buddhas, the worldly appearance is mentioned along with it. You contemplate whether your own karma is light or heavy, how will you be able to practice Meditation, how will you be able to practice wisdom? Therefore, you must bow to Chiem Sat Sam. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's purpose of teaching us to use Contemplation and Contemplation is in the second half of the series. The first half [of this sutra] is for preparation, the purpose is to become a Buddha, not to learn wealth, fame, or gain in the world.

Having understood this principle, everyone knows that there are those who say "Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is the teachings of the Hinayana, not the Mahayana". In this sutra, there are no Arhats, only Kien Tinh Bodhisattva and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva preach the Dharma, no one else participates. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva requested, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said. At the same time, the second half teaches you that in the first half, the nature of sin is a reality, the second half then denies: "The nature of sin is inherently empty, the nature of sin does not exist, it is illusory, not real". [If your sin nature were] genuine, you would not be able to repent; Because it's not true, you can only repent! Sin is inherently empty, only created by the mind, but when created, the mind starts thinking, when creating sin, it is very quick and very easy. When repenting, it may not be easy, because we cannot achieve one mind. Being able to achieve one mind is of course very good! Now everyone knows how to develop Bodhi mind, if the mind is compatible, we practice the ten great vows of Samantabhadra; That is the “mind-only, unobstructed, unobstructed” method, can you correspond or not? Pay homage to all the Buddhas in the ten directions: The first great vow is to pay homage to the Buddhas in the ten directions. Can your mind reach that realm? If you recite Ksitigarbha, Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, or recite Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the Three Jewels are not separate from the mind, the mind is the Three Jewels. The mind that thinks of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the mind that thinks of Manjushri Bodhisattva is Manjushri Bodhisattva, can it be done or not? Therefore, while you have not repented of all your sins, you still owe a lot of debts that have not been paid off. If you want to become very rich, you will not be able to do it! You must pay off your debt first! First of all, pay off the poor!

Each great Bodhisattva, while benefiting sentient beings, first aims to make sentient beings “leave suffering and be happy”. It is for this purpose that each Bodhisattva and all great Bodhisattvas develop their minds. They do everything for the sake of saving sentient beings. Mahayana teachings teach: When Bodhisattvas practice the Bodhisattva path, they do not seek happiness for themselves, but only hope that sentient beings will be happy. May all sentient beings be free from suffering, and your mind will unite with the mind of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to become one. Ordinary people's minds quickly become Buddha minds, transforming ideas into Buddha minds. Is it possible? If you can't do that, then develop your mind to learn from Buddha, learn from Bodhisattvas, and transform your mind into Buddha's mind. If you can't do it, you will follow your own karma. Whatever karma you create, it will drag you to that place, that is, you will be turned around by karma. Those present were all determined to study Buddha, and told him how Buddha did it, so I did it. Can't do it! We can't even do it as Bodhisattvas, we can't even do it with the initial intention of Bodhisattva, we can only call ourselves Bodhisattvas! We have all received the Bodhisattva vows. There are people who have received all three great precepts. I wonder if the monks and nuns are Bodhisattvas or not? Bodhisattva! What does the Bodhisattva do, what is in the Bodhisattva's mind, what are the Bodhisattva's thoughts? If every thought you recite is the Bodhisattva's mind, your karma is extremely strong, then you will follow the Bodhisattva path. You often think about the karma of sentient beings: Suffering from illness and suffering occurs, suffering from illness and suffering turns around. If the food is delicious, eat two more bites. Not delicious, won't want to eat more! In all places, we can test our mind.

Now we can feel "The previous thought just started to be evil, the next thought does not arise", not allowing it to continue. Knowing that the karma that we have created in the past can now be cut off by a knife, body, speech, and mind, does it have that power? Thien Tai's pupil has [that power]. In the Lotus Sutra, dragon women also exist. Once you have it, you will become a Buddha. Without it, it will not be possible to eliminate [karma] at all. We don't have that strength, the nature of karma is inherently empty, created by the mind, but we cannot "empty" it! It is impossible to "no", the retribution will not be lost! Friends who study Mahayana teachings often say that “karma is inherently empty”, can you “empty” in retribution? The illness is fake, it doesn't help anything! [But] when you are seriously ill and can't get up, how do I think you do? It's fake, let's wake up and go to work as usual, can we do it or not? Anyone can talk big, but big things cannot be done! Saying “I suffer for all sentient beings”, that's great! Please change! You go to the hospital and tell all the patients: "I'm here for you. Please leave the hospital!" Can do it or not? While karma is present, speaking loudly is useless, the body is the body, the spirit is the spirit, can you separate the two? The doctor performs surgery and must inject you with anesthetic. You say: "There's no need for anesthesia! I'm not in pain, just go ahead and do the surgery." Do you have that certificate or not? Your body is sick, saying: "My mind is not sick, it's okay!" Can't do it! If you can do it, then you are a Bodhisattva. That is the miraculous use of a Bodhisattva. It is not about speaking loudly, but doing great things. Therefore, one must repent.

(Sutra) Good man! Those who practice repentance and repentance of the Dharma, stay in a quiet place, according to the power of their abilities, they decorate the room, internal knowledge of Buddha's affairs, update the Dharma sutras, and increase the level of mystery.
(Sutra: Good man! If you want to practice the Dharma of repentance, you should stay in a quiet place, depending on your needs. According to one's own strength, decorate a room, in which statues are placed, Dharma sutras are placed, and silk parasols are hung.

If you want to practice the method of repentance, you should find a pure place, and according to your strength, you can solemnize and purify a hermitage. In there, worship a Buddha statue and offer all kinds of offerings. There are also Buddhist scriptures, hanging phanks, and treasured parasols.

(Sutra) Praying for the practice of offering the scent of daffodils.
(Sutra: Search and collect incense and flowers to practice and make offerings).

Depends on your strength. If you don't have money, use paper cutouts. You can also use paper as an offering, it doesn't need to cost a lot. Offering like that. Because ordinary Dharma friends do not have the strength to decorate a pure room to worship Buddha. Offering seven precious gifts, eight precious gifts, you will have nothing to worry about! Depending on the situation, as long as your mind is true, it will be true.

(Sutra) Removes sexual desire from the body, cleans clothes, unclean spiritual objects.

Depending on the ten aspects, one and the same overall rule, thinking of the mind to pay homage to all Buddhas' physical bodies, relics, images, stupas, temples, and Buddha's affairs. Paying homage to all Buddhas in the ten directions and three worlds. Huu is thinking in his heart and making offerings to the ten directions, all the Dharma treasures. According to the ritual, in accordance with the theory of the crime, single-mindedly admonishing and praying to the great and compassionate beings of the ten directions, realize and protect the following thoughts: hybrid,Ten Evils, Four Elements, Five Contradictions, going crazy, blaspheming the Three Jewels I Xich Sin”. in the past and the fifty-three Buddhas. Next, for each of the ten directions, pay homage to all the bodies, relics, statues, stupas, and Buddhas of all the Buddhas. Next, pay homage to all the Buddhas in the ten directions. Next, pay homage to all the sages in the ten directions Pray to me, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. May all sentient beings quickly understand the source of the mind and permanently eliminate the roots of sin.)

“Durnal residence”: During the Buddha's time in the world, time in India was divided into three periods of day and three periods of night. Three times, recite the name and recite the holy name Ksitigarbha. Then worship again. Entering the repentance chamber, when practicing repentance, single-mindedly pay homage to the seven Buddhas of the past and the fifty-three Buddhas. In India at that time, in ancient times, the three times of the day were early day, middle day, and late day, [the three times of night] were early night, middle day, and late night. During the day is from morning to afternoon, at night is from early night, middle night, to late night, finally twenty-four hours of repentance.

While bowing, you must first pay homage to the seven Buddhas of the past. We are not talking about each one individually, everyone knows the seven Buddhas of the past. The three Buddhas in the Adorned Kalpa are Vipaśyin, the Shi Qi Buddha (Śikhin), and Viśvabhū, those three. The seven Buddhas are the three Buddhas in the Adorned Kalpa and the four Buddhas in the Good Kalpa. At present we belong to the Sage Kalpa, the four Buddhas in the [Human] Sage Kalpa are the Venerable Buddha (Kakucchanda), the Buddha Kūṣāmīni. (Kanakamuni), Kasyapa Buddha (Kāśyapa), and Sakyamuni Buddha (Śākyamuni). The Adorned Kalpa (Vyūhakalpa) and the Noble Kalpa (Bhadrakalpa) together, the three Buddhas in the Adorned Kalpa plus the four Buddhas of the Noble Kalpa make seven Buddhas first; then, bow to the fifty-three Buddhas href="#_ftn14" name="_ftnref14" title="">[14]. Those are the Buddhas who must bow before repenting, paying homage to all the Buddhas in the ten directions. will leave behind relics, have Buddha images, have temples, have stupas. These are all called "Buddhist things", they are all offered, in your mind you should bow to Chiem Sat Sam, in the text there is only the ritual of Chiem Sat Sam, that is, worship all the Buddhas of the three times, that is, make offerings to all the Buddha's treasures, that is, the Dharma Treasure. Paying homage to all the sages and monks of the ten directions is the Sangha Treasure. After bowing to the ten directions, individually pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. This is our Master of Repentance. Sometimes, we bow three times in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra. bow.

At the beginning of the repentance course, first of all, pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions. After that, differentiate and worship again. After such a ceremony, you should point out the crime you have committed. If you have made a mistake, you should say it. There are people who are shy and don't want to confess, so choose a time when there is no one in the Buddha's hall and confess to the Buddha; addressed Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in front of him. Repentance means expressing "I won't do it anymore!" Those things are bad things, I have repented, I will not do them again. May I and all sentient beings quickly destroy [the evil karma] from countless kalpas up to now, so far away! Because when we commit crimes, from countless eons up to now, we have created "ten evils, four serious crimes", that is, ten evil karmas and four serious crimes, five rebellions, insanity, slandering the Three Jewels, the crime of Nhat Xien De. Blaspheming Buddha is not just not believing. Xiancheng is defamation of Buddha. After reciting like that, you yourself then contemplate, “thinking” is visualization, saying those sins are crazy, illusory, not real. If it were reality, it would be impossible to repent. Since it is not reality, does it have a truly existing nature that can be achieved? No! There is nothing certain that can be achieved! The nature of sin is inherently empty, not extinguished, allowing all sentient beings to understand the mind, to attain the pure repentance of both mind and sin. The mind is inherently unborn and exists due to the environment. If the scene is gone, the mind is also gone. There is no scene, there is no mind, eliminating sin from the root.

But how can it be done? The first thing is to deeply believe in cause and effect. Cause and effect are immortal, all dharmas arise from conditions. Dependent birth has no nature, but it is not destroyed, it still has to be repaid. Sin has no nature, the mind is unborn, it only exists because of the scene. Because of the appearance of your realm, you commit crimes. At the same time, you must also believe, believe that cause and effect are not lost. The cause that you have created all at once will not be lost, not a dot, not a drop will be left behind, it will not be lost! Therefore, be ashamed. Whenever you enter a penitentiary, you must feel shame (shame). Shame is shame towards oneself, nobleness is shame towards others. You yourself commit crimes against others, hurting others for others, being disrespectful towards others, including many crimes! The two words Tam Quy include many things. Because of hurting so many people from countless lifetimes until now, they will definitely suffer retribution.

What we suffer in the present, the many tribulations in life, aren't you receiving retribution? People say "Suppose that for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, the karma does not perish, the causes and conditions meet, the retribution is self-lived" (suppose that in hundreds of thousands of kalpas, the karma done is not lost, when the causes and conditions meet, the retribution is still borne). Until you have to pay back, you will feel miserable! I have suffered from illness and imprisonment. That's called “retribution”. Without retribution, you will not suffer. If you have retribution or karma, you have to suffer; But when we commit crimes, it is a continuation, not one life, not two lives, but continuously creating evil. When a child is born, the mind of greed arises, that is, greed, anger, and ignorance; When I was a little dissatisfied, I burst into tears. As soon as the baby was born, he cried and was angry. It's unsatisfactory, so it's miserable, and because it's miserable, there's no way to express it, so it cries. That is the anger that comes into play. Too small, unable to speak, you asked him: "What are you doing?" He immediately cried, his anger was very heavy! As soon as he learned to speak, he grabbed everything he saw and assumed it belonged to him. I once knew a child, he was less than a year old, could not speak yet, gave him many things, held them tightly in both hands, and did not let others touch him! Evil habits are innate and come from the past. When it comes to sin nature, it is sin nature, continuing forever!

tom_tat: Volume 6 (Sūtra) The second request for encouragement and encouragement is to pray that all Bodhisattvas of the ten directions will all become Enlightened Ones, and may quickly attain Perfect Enlightenment. noi_dung:
Lecture 6

(Sūtra) This kind of request to make a wish, may the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions necessarily become Enlightened Ones, may quickly attain perfect enlightenment. If he becomes a fully enlightened person, he vows to always abide in this world, turn the wheel of Dharma, and not enter Nirvana.
(Sutra: Next, you should make a vowto encourage ask, pray give ten

All Bodhisattvas who have not yet attained Enlightenment, vow to quickly attain Enlightenment. If you have achieved Enlightenment, vow to always abide in this world, turn the wheel of Dharma, and not enter Nirvana.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches that people who want to use the Contemplation Wheel must first make a vow before they can use it. This is a vow of encouragement. Emitting this prayer of encouragement can make all our obstacles disappear. If we use the Contemplation Wheel and encounter obstacles or hindrances, it will be very difficult for you to respond. What the universal appearance shows to you is not accurate. Therefore, to be accurate, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: “You must make a vow to encourage”. Make a vow to all Bodhisattvas in the ten directions who have not yet become Buddhas, and vow that they will become Buddhas very quickly; Having become Buddhas, I pray that they will always stay in this world for a long time. “Abiding in this world” is turning the wheel of dharma. If a Buddha stays in this world, he will preach the Dharma. If he stays in this world for a long time, he will not enter Nirvana too early. Therefore, this vow can eliminate evil obstacles when we practice. Because when you have demonic obstacles, your practice will not be successful. At the same time, a Dharma friend told me that every time a Dharma Master preaches a sutra, that person also wants to come and listen, but as soon as he is about to go listen, obstacles arise. That person was in Shanghai on the Mainland. It wasn't like the car had trouble, someone called to say there was something that needed to be taken care of, which always made him unable to answer successfully. That is called an obstacle, a demonic obstacle. Why just wait until he is about to listen to a sutra, or wants to participate in a Dharma conference, will these obstacles appear? That's called karma, we can see it! There are things that are right when you do good deeds, as well as when practicing the Bodhisattva path, evil obstacles appear. When the Buddha was in the world preaching the Dharma, the demon king Ba Tuan often caused obstacles. Three Weeks often asked the Buddha to quickly enter nirvana. This happens often.

Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: If you want to use the Wheel of Contemplation, you must make a vow to encourage, you need to make a vow: Pray that Bodhisattvas who have not yet become Buddhas will quickly become Buddhas. May the Buddhas who have achieved it, advise them not to enter Nirvana, and stay in this world for a long time. That's called a prayer of encouragement. Praying for encouragement has the same meaning as inviting (inviting) to preach the Dharma, encouraging all to do Buddhist work. This implies “you must develop a kind heart”, what kind of mind is that? Bodhisattvas are invited to preach the Dharma.
