If we ourselves are in a penitentiary, or in a Buddha hall, when we recite sutras, the sutras teach you to invite all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to preach the Dharma. That is called “the great vow of encouragement”. As for all Bodhisattvas currently living in this world, I advise them to stay in this world and not enter Nirvana. Is it true that making a vow of encouragement will definitely produce results? Depending on your determination, each sentient being will develop the Bodhisattva intention. We often encourage Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to stay in the world. So what will you personally achieve? Be healthy, live long, and always be able to hear the Dharma sounds. That aspiration is very important.

Again, we should develop the vow to encourage and encourage all Bodhisattvas in the ten directions, because speaking according to Buddhist teachings, when the Bodhisattva participates in the Eighth Level, he considers himself to have reached perfection and no longer vows to practice higher to save sentient beings, [because of the misconception] that "he himself has cut off all karma, the career of saving beings." birth is complete", because he has not yet seen the basis of his own ignorance. That is the Eighth Bodhisattva Level. Therefore, the Buddhas of the ten directions came to advise him, advising him to continue practicing the Bodhisattva vows, telling him "you have not yet become a Buddha." We do not see this, nor do we know which one is the Eighth Ground Bodhisattva, but we advise all sentient beings, all Dharma friends, to stay in this world. That's the right thing to do. For example, most recently, Bodhisattvas continuously left. Among the current Venerables, everyone knows that Dharma Master Thanh Nghiem, Dharma Master Sam Van, Dharma Master Phat Nguyen in Mainland, within this half month, were all reborn one after another. We can see this. There are also Bodhisattvas of the ten directions that our physical eyes cannot see. Let us encourage them to stay long in this world with every thought. That great vow is to invite Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to stay in the world, hoping that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will bless us, so that we can cultivate the path of karma while we are still alive, destroy karma, and achieve achievements. That is the vow to encourage and encourage all Bodhisattvas, allowing them to stay in this world for a long time. Our physical eyes cannot see this, there are Bodhisattvas that you cannot see, but make this vow to mean "to make you soon one day be close to good friends, close to good knowledge". Due to this principle, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us that we should make such vows. This vow has been made...

(Sutra) The second thing is to arise according to the wish of joy, to pray for all sentient beings, to let go of jealousy forever. mind, in the middle of the three worlds, one must attain salvation, one must possess the merits of cultivating and learning, one will attain the status of a siddha, and all stages will be happy.
(Sutra: Next, you should make a vow of rejoicing, wishing you and all living beings to be perfect Forever abandon the mind of jealousy, in all three lifetimes, all lands, all the merits of cultivating and achieving, all will rejoice.)

Normally, in countless past lives, when we saw people skillfully doing good karma, even if all the careers in the world were better and stronger than ours, a kind of obstacle and jealousy arose. This Dharma of repentance has the vow of rejoicing to destroy the obstacle of jealousy from countless lives in our past, allowing us to see people who are superior to us, regardless of our belief in the Three Jewels, but also all our home affairs, we all praise and rejoice. At the same time, may all sentient beings become Buddhas. This rejoicing covers the ten dharma realms: Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and even sentient beings of the six paths. This principle is very deep. Because our one mind, that is, one thought in the present moment completes the ten dharma realms. Throughout the day, you start thinking, sometimes hoping to become a Buddha. When reciting the sutras, seeing the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they made a vow to hope that they themselves would soon become Buddhas. Your thoughts then belong to the Buddhadharma realm. Because you see others suffering, you hope to save them, protect them, and save them from all suffering. Because of that vow, you entered the Bodhisattva Dharma Realm. If you yourself feel that in life, everything is not in accordance with your mind, boring to leave the world, up to the dharma of Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions, that is the mind of the Second Vehicle. So is the Bodhisattva, and so is Thanh Van! On the one hand, we pray for all sentient beings, to save all sentient beings from birth and death; One way is to escape one's own birth and death. Furthermore, with regard to all good deeds (good actions) in the human world, all sentient beings in the six paths and we are all of the same mind, one nature, that is, we should not be greedy or jealous towards all sentient beings. Eliminate that mind! Just seeing someone else doing a little good deed, not only not being jealous, but also making a vow to be happy, that is, vowing to be happy for all sentient beings, in order to eliminate the mind of obstacles and jealousy from countless lives in the past. Whenever we see others seemingly superior to us, we become dissatisfied. Eliminate that karma!

In all the Buddha realms of the past, present, and future, in terms of time, there are three generations, in terms of place, all of the realms, there are Bodhisattvas practicing the Bodhisattva path, there are those who have perfected the Bodhisattva path and become Buddhas. Although our physical eyes cannot see it, our hearts rejoice, consider the merits of others as our own and praise them, rejoicing, it will be like achieving merits ourselves. The merit of praising and rejoicing is not only that our physical eyes cannot see it, but our physical eyes cannot see it, but your thoughts can be intentional, based on the Buddha's teachings. Until now, we have taught the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: If you want to use the Contemplation Wheel, first of all, you must generate joy. Rejoice in the merits of becoming Buddhas of all Buddhas in the ten directions and three times, and rejoice in the merits and virtues of practicing the Bodhisattva path of all Bodhisattvas in the ten directions. As for all the good karma of all sentient beings, you will rejoice. That current mind, your present mind can expand to such a great extent, above is rejoicing in all Buddhas of the ten directions, below is rejoicing in all sentient beings. For all the good karma, no matter how small or tiny, you should rejoice and praise it, thus destroying bad habits from countless lifetimes up to now: "Seeing others achieve what you have not achieved, you will not feel joy, but will also feel jealousy." Repenting of that bad karma is rejoicing in merit. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: When making this great vow, that is, the vow to rejoice in merit, it is the vow to repent of karma. These things belong to the ten great kings of vows.

Therefore, do not think that the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is Hinayana. [If understood like that], it would be an absolute mistake! It's not like we take the Cham Sat Luan and immediately cast it, it's impossible! First of all, you must make a vow. If you do not make a vow, you will not be able to use the Contemplation Wheel. Each vow agrees with Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's ten great vows. Everyone should understand this principle! For example, when we are walking in the dark, if someone uses a flashlight to illuminate our way and shine light, do we thank that person or not? We are in the three realms, which are the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm. In the three realms, there is darkness. If there is a Bodhisattva who uses light to guide us out of the darkness of the three worlds. That is “the Bodhisattva path”. Since we ourselves cannot do it, we rely on other Bodhisattvas to do it, such as Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Manjushri Bodhisattva, Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), and Maitreya Bodhisattva. Currently, we study according to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. For all the work done to benefit sentient beings by the Five Great Beings, we vow to rejoice in their work. Not only those five great Bodhisattvas, but also the Buddhas of the ten directions, such as Amitābha Buddha, have made forty-eight vows. We all rejoice, praise, and learn from the Buddha to make the same great vows. May it not create illusions. One thought of your present mind and Amitābha Buddha's mind are the same. Buddha's mind is your own present mind. Our mind is the Buddha's mind, until we rejoice in the good thoughts of the Bodhisattva, that means we have practiced the Bodhisattva path. As for all sentient beings in the ten dharma realms, when they have not yet become Buddhas, or are about to enter the Buddha position, if that person has a kind thought towards sentient beings, we will see the same thing we do ourselves, you will all praise and rejoice. That is called “wisdom of skillful means”. You should often make that wish.

Every Dharma friend should regularly make vows. That is exactly like in the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us to develop Bodhi mind and use our mind wisely. Everyone who has read the Pure Conduct chapter of the Avatamsaka Sutra must follow the teachings of Manjushri Bodhisattva to develop a mind of praise and joy. That is a pure mind. Buddha's path is the same, each Buddha's skillful means to benefit sentient beings are different, but to become a Buddha, the path and results are the same. Every Bodhisattva is like that. Because we don't make very clear distinctions between right, wrong, evil, and right, if you learn to use the Contemplation Wheel, relying on the compassionate power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we will learn to understand. What do you learn? Use your mind wisely. Contemplation Sat Luan guides us to use our mind wisely. While we have obstacles, many things cannot be decided, let's use Contemplation Sat Luan! Let's talk about a simple issue, like when you buy a house, is the house good or not? Is buying a house beneficial or not? You can also use the Contemplation Wheel, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will tell you the truth. You want to invest a sum of money for business, you are not sure whether the investment will be a loss or a profit, you can also use the Cham Luan Contemplation. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that if you can invest, you will be able to make a profit. If [Chiem Sat Luan] tells you that you cannot invest and that you will lose money, then you should not invest.

I say this seems to have nothing to do with religious practice. Surely there are Dharma friends who doubt whether Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is in charge of that matter or not? Compassionate Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, [the third type of wheel form in] Contemplation of the Wheel of Contemplation [showing numbers, constituting] one hundred and eighty-nine cases, expresses those problems. Why can Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in this world also help you like that? Makes you believe in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, making you gradually enter the Buddhist path. If at first it doesn't give you a little comfort, you won't believe it. If you pray for anything, let it be known to you with utmost precision. You will say that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is truly wonderful, and I will wholeheartedly believe in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. From the appearance of the world, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva gradually leads you to the world. From beyond the world, gradually teaching you to practice the Bodhisattva path. To truly escape birth and death, one must practice the Bodhisattva path. I hope to get rich, even if worldly wealth is developed, you cannot achieve it, it is not trustworthy. [Therefore], it will make you develop the Three Jewels of wealth and the Dharma wealth, which will never be lost. Therefore, “Buddhism in the world, not separated from the worldly enlightenment”, has this meaning. The sutra also has a sentence like this: “First of all, desire will overcome the shield, gradually the spirit will enter the Buddhist path” (First use desire to entice, gradually make you enter the Buddhist path). The realm of sentient beings is in the five desires. If you lead them to learn from the five desires, they will gradually enter the Buddhist path. Then, if you want to teach them, they will believe. Everyone sees that in the incarnations of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, there is an image of Bodhisattva holding a basket of flowers. How did that story arise? Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) transformed into a flower girl. Of course, the flower girl looked extremely beautiful. She carried a flower basket to sell flowers, and many people followed her, not to buy flowers, but because of her desire for beauty. Many people vied for her, hoping to marry her. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva immediately said: "Whoever among you can belong to the Avalokiteshvara Universal Sect, I will marry that person." The baccalaureates have up to ten or twenty people who can memorize it. The girl said: "There are so many of you, who should I marry? Whoever among you can memorize the Lotus Sutra in one day, I will marry that person." Such people are very few, there is only one scholar who memorizes the entire Lotus Sutra in one day. He immediately married the flower girl. As soon as she got married, when she entered the wedding room, she immediately died. That baccalaureate student saw that impermanence was true. That baccalaureate's last name is Ma, whose name is clearly mentioned in this story. From then on, he developed the mind to practice Buddhism. That is, from within all dharmas, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas first used desire to entice and gradually lead them to enter the Buddhist path.

Therefore, often great Bodhisattvas rejoice in the merits of sentient beings, follow their wishes, and fulfill their wishes. Through rejoicing, they will gradually lead them towards the Buddha path. Therefore, the fifth great vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is also the fifth great vow of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, which is the great vow to rejoice in merit. In rejoicing in merit, I give another example. I live in Ngu Dai Son, there are many Dharma friends who come to Ngu Dai Son to make offerings to Thien Sang Trai (to offer food to a thousand monks), there are also people who don't have much money, no money. Our Son Tay province is inherently very poor, especially like Phon Tri district. In the districts surrounding Ngu Dai Son such as Dai district and Phon Tri district, the farmers are extremely desperate, do they have money to worship the Sangha? Even their own lives have no way! I immediately advised them: "When people make offerings, you can praise and rejoice. You visualize yourself making offerings, praise and rejoice in their merit, and you will receive a part of their merit. Even though you don't spend a dime, if you praise and rejoice, is that okay or not?" That's called wishing to praise and rejoice. Here, when we talk about “rejoicing in merit” in the Samantabhadra vow, it means rejoicing in all the good deeds of all sentient beings, even if it's just a drop or a drop! Isn't it "why does he have so much money? Why am I so broke?" That's called the obstacle of jealousy. So not only is there no merit, but there is also sin. Therefore, isn't it very convenient to praise merit and rejoice in such important ways? The most convenient merit is to freely praise and rejoice. When you see someone else practicing, bow your head and worship there, you immediately praise and rejoice, and immediately receive half of that person's merit. Therefore, praise for merit and joy is inconceivable! But living beings, on the contrary, see others doing good things, but they themselves do not do them, causing troubles, obstacles, destruction, and giving rise to evil wishes. One side is good, the other side is evil, everyone can see this: "Buddha's disciples all praise and rejoice."

In the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, regarding the things Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us, you must think a lot and make vows. Once you have made those vows, you can use the Contemplation Wheel. From each vow, you should consider whether the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra is ultimately Mahayana or Hinayana? Every sutra, no matter which sutra the Buddha spoke, has Truth and Reason. Depending on the human world, the Principle is different, the Principle is always moving towards the Buddhist path. For example, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva transformed countless billions of bodies, and also had different types of realms to save sentient beings. We mortals do not see the shameful eyes. You just make a vow of praise, depending on your joy, you will receive a portion of the Bodhisattva's merit. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva made a vow, you then praised and rejoiced; Manjushri Bodhisattva made a vow, you then praised and rejoiced. Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara made a vow, I then praised and rejoiced. For all the vows of countless Bodhisattvas and all Buddhas of the ten directions, you all praise, and with joy, you will achieve something different! That is the great vow of rejoicing. When you see someone else doing something good, you should praise it and be happy. Don't be jealous or get in the way. That's called rejoicing in merit.

(Sutra) The second thing is to develop the aspiration of dedication, vowing to cultivate all merit and self-interest for all sentient beings. equal to the Buddha's wisdom, reaching Nirvana.
(Sutra: Next, you should again vow to dedicate, praying that all the merits you have cultivated will help May all sentient beings enter Buddha's wisdom and attain Nirvana.

At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also teaches us to make dedication vows. The dedication vow is to dedicate the good things that one has done, the same to worship, the same to chant the sutras, the same to listen to the sutras and listen to the Dharma, all the merits are dedicated to all sentient beings, that is called “lower transformation” (transforming sentient beings).. I don't have any strength, so I dedicate what I have heard, learned, and all those merits to all sentient beings. “Direction” is to give those merits to sentient beings, without being attached to ourselves. For example, here everyone listens to the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The merit of listening to this Dharma is unsurpassed, the most unsurpassed. I dedicate this most outstanding merit, almost to the whole of Taiwan, more broadly, the entire Mainland, and even larger, the entire Sa Ba world. Can you calculate how big or small the merit and virtue of that dedication is? Immeasurable merit! I use that merit to help all sentient beings. I pray that those who have not heard the Buddha Dharma can hear the Buddha Dharma. I pray that those who have heard the Buddha Dharma but do not practice it effectively will be able to practice successfully. Finally, may all sentient beings become Buddhas. Do you, my Dharma friends, make this vow or not? If it doesn't play; In the future, regardless of whether you do a little or a drop of good deeds, dedicate them all. The more you dedicate, the bigger and more effective it becomes! When you become a Buddha, think back for a moment and you will see that your cause to become a Buddha originates from that story. Using all my own good karma, I myself am not greedy, I direct it towards sentient beings, I use all the merit I have cultivated to help all sentient beings, I pray that all sentient beings in the future will all be able to become Buddhas like me, moving towards Buddha wisdom, to Nirvana!

In this passage, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: Do you want to use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate good and evil karma? You must make those great vows. After you have made these great vows, you can use the Contemplation Wheel. Whether that blessing is big or small depends on each individual's practice. We should not think that our strength is not enough, we have no wealth, our own life is also very difficult, what strength do we have to make offerings to sentient beings, to make offerings to the Three Jewels? When the Buddha was alive, there was a story like this: When the Buddha was alive, there was a woman who was very poor, to what extent was she poor? Begging, begging for food, nothing. Suddenly one day, on the road she picked up a gold coin. When she picked up that coin, she immediately thought: "Why am I so poor? Today, I picked up a gold coin, using it to cover my own life, I can last for a few months." She did not do so, wondering: "Why am I so poor? It is because I have never given alms, nor cultivated merit, that is why I am poor."

Therefore, she planned to use that gold coin to buy oil [to light a lamp] to offer to Buddha to cultivate blessings. When you go to the oil store to buy oil, you must bring a jar or bottle to store it. The shop owner asked her: "You want to buy oil, what should you use to put it in?" The poor woman said: "I have nothing to store." The shop owner said: "There's nothing to put it in! Where should I put the oil for you?" The shop owner then asked her: “What did you buy the oil for?” She said: "I'm so poor, I barely have a penny. From the past to the present, I have never cultivated merit, now I plan to buy oil to worship Buddha." The shop owner was moved by her and said: "I gave you an oil container, but this one coin is not enough to buy enough oil to fill it up." He still filled it up, saying: "The extra oil in this vase is my offering. If you make an offering to Buddha, it's as if I also have a part." Therefore, that poor woman brought oil to the Buddha's Ky Vien monastery, wanting to add more oil to all the oil lamps offered to Buddha, but could not, only enough to add one lamp. She then poured oil into the lamp to worship Buddha. At the same time, on that day, the current king, Ba Tu Nac, brought many carts of oil to make offerings to the Buddha, and every lamp was filled with oil. Early the next morning, it was already dawn, so the lights should be turned off. That day, the person on duty was Venerable Maudgalyayana. The Venerable extinguished each lamp. Only the small lamp offered by the poor woman could not be extinguished by Maudgalyayana. Maudgalyayana thought, "I cannot extinguish this lamp," so he used his supernatural powers to extinguish the lamp. The result is that it cannot be extinguished, but the light is even more overwhelming. At that time, the Buddha came out and told the Venerable Maudgalyayana: "Arahant's magical powers cannot extinguish this lamp! Why? She has exhausted all her strength to give alms". What does it mean to “exhaust yourself in giving alms”? Drain it all. Her entire fortune came from finding a single coin, and she didn't have anything else. That was called 'exhaustive almsgiving'. Devoted giving is pure. She can bring everything she owns as an offering to Buddha. That is the ultimate sacrifice. In her mind there was only one thought, what thought was that? Making offerings to Buddha: "Why was my blessing in the past so poor? Because I have never made offerings to the Three Jewels, now I should make offerings to Buddha."

It's just an old story. We must understand clearly: When people make offerings, it's not whether the material is more or less, but what is it? Your mind. Like you Dharma friends offering red envelopes, what kind of mind do you use to make offerings? Use sincerity and earnestness to respectfully make offerings to the Three Jewels, without distinguishing between ordinary people or saints, absolutely no distinction. That is called pure mind. Worshiping the Sangha is like worshiping the Buddha, without any distracting thoughts, using a pure mind to make offerings to the Three Jewels, the merit and virtue will be great. As long as there is quantity, measurement, and calculation, that merit becomes small. When making offerings, you must make a vow. After making a vow, you must also dedicate it. Remember especially: Making vows, dedicating, no matter how much or how little, big or small, your material things are, while you do a good deed, even though the power itself is small, your mental energy is great, material things change. Material things follow your mind. If the mind is big, the amount of matter will be huge. If the mind is small, the amount of matter will be small. King Basenac offered 100,000 lamps, which were not as good as a poor woman's lamp. The king doesn't take it seriously, he doesn't even come, he just sends his servants to make offerings. Therefore, use your mind to quantify!

We practice the same way. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, while you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, what mind do you use to recite? This problem is extremely serious, how serious is it? Due to a single thought of your mind, you will make offerings to all the emptiness throughout the dharma realm. Your mind will make offerings to all emptiness throughout the dharma realm, making offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. For example, when we recite Amitābha Buddha, your body is still in the Sa Ba world, but your mind has gone to the Pure Land. Not only to the world of Ultimate Bliss, but also to the world of Immobility, the world of the Oriental Medicine Master Lapis La Light King, your mind has all arrived. With both intention and thought, you have made offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Is your merit great, or is the merit of one thought or one offering great? What is that offering? Dharma offerings are supreme. Among all types of offerings, the dharma of offerings is supreme, because it is the mind that offers, not the form! Therefore, while making offerings, you must pay special attention!

(Sutra) Such as she dedicates her wishes, rests in a quiet room, sits with one mind, weakly chants, weakly recites The title of the ego is to reduce consciousness and drowsiness. Huo kissed a big man, and the middle of the ashram was filled with chanting.
(Sutra: Having made the dedication vow like that, enter the quiet room again, sit upright with one mind, or confess chanting, or silently chanting my name, you should reduce your sleep. If you are a lethargic person, you should circumambulate and chant in the ashram room).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: After you do such things, after making such dedication vows, you will begin to practice and begin to worship. We teach the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma for you to practice. You yourself build a quiet room, in there, chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, according to the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra to worship. Therefore, before you bow, you must make a vow, repent, and worship. After making the vow and dedication like that, depending on how big or small your strength is, you can set up a pure penance. If you have the strength, the better. If you don't have the strength, you can bow in your own bedroom. If you have the strength, you should set up a clean room, set up an altar, worship the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and an incense burner to burn incense. When you eat rice, first make an offering. Whatever you eat, just offer it as an offering!

At the same time, you also have to recite, either chanting the Ksitigarbha Sutra or chanting the Contemplation Sutra. If the original scriptures don't exist, then reciting my name is fine. Silently recite my name, recite Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. But the Bodhisattva teaches you to reduce sleep and rest, not to "kiss" (to be obscured by lethargy). “The” [here refers to] sleep, because it is covered by it, wisdom will not be revealed, covered by karma. But regarding the matter of being drowsy, a Dharma friend told me: That person does not go into a penitentiary and does not feel sleepy at all. Whenever I enter the penance room, sit down, I immediately become drowsy and fall asleep. Why did he ask me? I said: "It's because of bad karma. Your past karma is so heavy that you can't even do it when you want to repent!" Also, as mentioned in the previous section, the ghosts of Ba Tuan's children and grandchildren come and they don't let you practice. You practice well and escape the demon world; His children and grandchildren will lose one person. He doesn't want you to become enlightened, so he creates obstacles for you.

Therefore, you leave all disturbances and single-mindedly recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. When reciting, in your mind you contemplate, every thought comes from the mind, every thought never leaves the mind. How does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teach us to recite? It must be from the mind, not just reciting with the mouth, the mind and mouth must be in agreement! When reciting, each thought comes from within. Every thought arises from the mind, every word is clear and distinct. Thoughts arise from the mind, every thought arises from the mind, every thought never leaves the mind, that is “mind thinking”. Reciting continuously like that, in your mind there is no second thought, not even the slightest impurity. But little sleep, no need to sleep, sleep causes wisdom to be obscured. Thuy Mien Cai in the Five Things, which is wealth, beauty, fame, reputation, sleep, these five things obscure your wisdom. Sleep is one of the Five Things, so when practicing Ban Chau Samadhi (Pratyutpanna Samādhi), it does not let you sleep. That method is to circumambulate the room. If you feel too sleepy, don't sit down, stand up and walk around. While walking and still sleeping, sometimes while walking and still sleeping, that is a very heavy karma. The karma is very heavy, so you should recite Ksitigarbha's name single-mindedly and minimize sleepiness. At that time, if you sit and meditate, you cannot succeed!

Before repenting, you enter the ashram room. First, meditate while walking and recite in that room, reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Due to the reduction, you can remove the word Namo and recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Why does just reciting the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva have a premonition? Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has made a vow, we unite with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vow. His vow is "If anyone recites my name, I will definitely bless that person and help that person soon eliminate their karma". Therefore, while you recite the name, when you say the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, based on your vows, what you personally wish for, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will definitely fulfill your wishes, but your mind must recite in such a way that it is similar to the mind of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva makes a vow to mature all sentient beings. That is His great compassion. If you are sincere and earnestly chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's holy name, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will come down to bless you:

- One is because your mind and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind are in agreement. You do not have a second thought, only one thought of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, so you are equal to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Because your mind and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind are inherently equal, one is enlightenment, the other is delusion. You must transform delusion into enlightenment. Your mind, together with your physical nature and physical nature, is in harmony; your mind and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind are closely combined. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bless you.

- The second meaning is that sentient beings in this Saha world have karma with sixty-two billion Bodhisattvas, but the deepest karma is Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), followed by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Sutra says that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's karma is deeper than Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva's. In the twelfth chapter, the Knowledge and Benefits chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the Buddha advised Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and requested Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to propagate the Ksitigarbha Sutra. Actually, Quan Yin and Ksitigarbha are equal, just different causes and conditions. If you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, you will attain salvation quickly, or if you recite Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva's prayers, you will attain salvation quickly, and if you recite other Bodhisattvas' names, it depends on the fate. If you have a deep affinity with any Bodhisattva, reciting that Bodhisattva will have the greatest effect. Therefore, when we pray for Bodhisattva's blessings, we also have to see if there is a predestined relationship or not.

You yourself can feel it, without fate you won't meet, if you meet you won't be able to penetrate; Because this relationship, whether it is destined or not, is extremely huge. If you have the predestined relationship, you will be able to achieve it quickly. If you are not destined, you still have to get married first. Once you have made a relationship, you can be blessed. Therefore, due to causes and conditions, if you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will be more likely to correspond!

(Sutra) Thu even dau partakes in time, weak and present wishes, bright and false, three times the heron eagle respectfully worships seemingly, repent, make a vow. Weak is unable to clearly discern the false truth, so he stays in the quiet middle of the room, chanting single-mindedly.
(Sutra: Next, at night, if there are bright things like lights, torches, You should also respectfully make offerings, repent, and make vows three times. If you cannot take care of the light, you should stay in that quiet room, chanting single-mindedly.

At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You recite my name until night. Next, at night, if you have the strength, the torches, and the light, you should respectfully repent and make a vow. If you don't have the strength, you will be very poor, you won't be able to arrange the lights, you won't be able to light the lamps. In the past, oil lamps, or electric lamps [as in the present], both cost money. Keeping lights on all night costs money! Depending on your ability, you make offerings, repent, and make eternal vows that cannot be stopped and must be done regularly. If you have the strength to take care of the lights and torches, at night you must enter the retreat and still chant. But because it is impossible not to sleep, you must consider your own time, depending on your own strength, to recite the name with all your might for twenty-four hours. But normally, for example, we monastics in permanent residence do not have that power, nor do we have the cause and condition, how do you do it? In your mind, do not hurt others, do not disturb others. For example, when we join the assembly in reciting the Buddha's teachings in the main hall, or on the way, in your heart you silently chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, who knows? No one will bother you! For example, when we have to follow the crowd, or when you go to work, can you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? You can recite it silently in your mind, no one can know your mind! Each individual's practice depends on how you use your mind?

There are many things in our minds, you can all feel it, for a moment, your brain thinks this, thinks that. While you work, your brain also thinks about many things. While you are doing housework, you don't know how many thoughts have arisen in your mind, wandering around in many places. You can use the story of reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as a line [of thought], forever reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Remember when you eat, wear clothes, recite when you work, and over time it becomes natural. That is called skillful means. As it is now, our bodies are not that healthy and we cannot persevere. Especially for people with heavy Thuy Mien Cai, you should immediately recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to change the karma of Thuy Mien Cai. At first, the first week, or during the second week, you are still very sleepy. Wait until you have worked hard for three weeks, four weeks, up to five weeks or more, and the karma gradually disappears. Without sleeping that much, your gong power will strengthen. At first, you can only recite for four or five hours. After a few weeks, you can recite for up to eight or nine hours. Your practice has reached a certain level, you can chant for more than ten hours a day. The more time you spend reciting, the lighter the afflictions in your mind will be. If your afflictions are lightened, your power to use will increase. At that time, your gong power will increase, and one day you will be able to recite the holy name thirty thousand sentences or more. If you recite for a week or two, you will reach the response and feel extremely happy in your heart. That is called “blessing”. Perhaps you will also see a holy image, or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will appear. It is also possible that in a dream, you will see Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Even in the dream, he wakes up and prays. Having awakened from your dream, you can apply [the practice] while awake and dreaming exactly the same, showing that you have reached a certain level of practice, proving that your current afflictions have been reduced; But you should not be satisfied. During that time, you must pay special attention: Don't be arrogant at all! Whenever an arrogant mind arises, it will retreat and be immediately retreated.

Therefore, if you are someone who wants to practice Earth Store Repentance Dharma, you must make up your mind. First of all, don't assign too much to yourself. Set too much, you will encounter difficulties! First of all, you should set seven days, fourteen days, or twenty-one days, depending on your own merit. Or first set ten days, then increase it. Wait until you have practiced for a long time and applied it successfully, you have just created the idea of ​​Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, no disturbance can interrupt you, then it will be effective: Karma has also been eliminated, the situation has also changed favorably. You personally know this story, “everyone eats to their fullest” is the meaning. Until you apply effort to a certain level, you will generate experiences. At that time, you had wisdom. Your wisdom guides you. You hope to use your wisdom to benefit others, but at that time, you cannot do so yet, so you should benefit yourself first.

This method of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra is very favorable

By the way, why is it not propagated and not popular in China? Firstly, because we don't believe it, even if we see it, we don't believe it! Basically, it is impossible to meet, as the Avatamsaka Sutra teaches: "For example, if there are seven hidden gems, there is no light and no one can understand. The Buddha Dharma has no cause, but wisdom cannot be understood" (Like a treasure in a dark house, no light cannot be understood, no one speaks of the Buddha Dharma, even if wisdom does not understand). Buddhism is the method of enlightenment, but no one explains it to you. If you don't know how to enter that method of enlightenment, you still cannot enter. When I first started, I still couldn't master it at the same time, not yet! Wait until you use it effectively, gain its benefits, achieve its goodness, and you will understand. Why are some Dharma friends immediately enlightened as soon as they hear the Dharma? We see that our ancestors often became enlightened as soon as they heard it. [Actually, they] did not only practice in the present life, but because they had practiced for many lifetimes. Everyone knows the Sixth Patriarch, he was a firewood seller who heard someone upstairs reciting the Diamond Sutra. The person who recited that sutra still did not become enlightened. He down here heard it and became enlightened. How do you explain? Because of His past good roots, it is time to mature! Therefore, when we practice the Ksitigarbha repentance method, you should know how to do it! Now we explain the ritual, if you want to practice, first of all, you must understand the sadhana. The above is to teach you: If you want to practice this method, you must understand the ritual and follow it to do so.

(Sutra) The Sun and the Sun are like practicing repentance, disposing of spiritual objects. The weak cause is enough, there is always a good opportunity, temporarily enlightens the evil cause and effect, creates evil dharma, the sin is light, the mind is strong, the mind is strong, the sutra is lost in the sun, that is, one attains purity, eliminating all obstacles. Like all sentient beings, their karma has a silvery afterglow, all the faculties are confused, the difference is immeasurable, either through the two-seven-day sutra, the child attains purity, or the third-seven-day sutra, the mother-in-law or the seven-day-after-day sutra, the child attains purity. Weaknesses in the past and present are associated with high-ranking monks and serious sinners, or they can attain purity through the hundred-day-er cycle. Either the two-hundred-day sutra, the mother-in-law or the thousand-day-child sutra to attain purity. Those with extremely weak roots, the most serious sinners, can develop a strong mind at birth, without trying to save their lives and thoughts, often need to recite, stay completely disturbed, reduce their consciousness and drowsiness, repent and make vows, practice and make offerings, do not resolve, do not destroy, even if they lose their lives, the weak will not retire. If you are diligent, in the middle of the sun, everything will be pure.
(Sutra: Practice repentance every day like that, don't be lazy, let go. If you are a human being The previous life had a good foundation for a long time, because of temporary evil causes and conditions, evil deeds were created, the offenses were few, the mind was strong, sharp, and the will was strong. After seven days, they will be pure, except for such obstacles. Such beings have thick and thin karma, and immeasurable differences in benefits. Either after fourteen days, they will be purified, or after twenty-one days, or up to forty-nine days, they will be purified. If it is too late In the past and present, there are all kinds of high-level mortal sins. Either after a hundred days, one becomes pure, or after two hundred days, one thousand days, then one becomes pure. If one is extremely stupid, with the heaviest sin, one should only develop a strong mind, have no thoughts of regretting one's life, diligently meditate, walk day and night, reduce sleep, make repentance, make vows, joyfully practice and make offerings, not be lazy, not give up, until there is nothing. If you lose your life, you will not rest. With such diligence, in a thousand days, you will attain purity.)

Every day practice repentance like that, every day based on the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, he teaches repentance. Repenting from countless lifetimes until now is not just one or two mistakes! Sometimes we do something wrong and we still don't know it. How do you know what has been wrong since countless eons until now? You should just repent. Don't be lazy, don't be lazy, don't give up. For example, when we worship, I use myself as an example. In 1936-1937, I invited Dharma Master Hoang Nhat to Tram Son Pagoda. I invited him to speak the Dharma of Contemplation and Repentance. After seeing him off, I also learned to practice seclusion. Just when there was about to be some warmth[15], Qingdao was occupied by the Japanese. The Japanese took over Qingdao, I can't learn anymore! How many years has it been since then? Almost twenty years! After twenty years, he was imprisoned for thirty-three years, interrupted by an interruption of more than fifty years! Even the basic scriptures cannot be touched, completely cut off! Before, I still felt some warmth, but now the warmth is gone, turning into winter in the mountains! In winter there is no warmth in the mountains, there seems to be no heat at all, neither can you hear nor see it. Several decades ago, when I came to America, my friends invited me to talk about past karma. They invited me to preach the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. How many years ago was that? After preaching in New York, ten years later, when they came to Pho Tho pagoda, they invited me to preach the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. It was the year one thousand ninety-something. Now, after ten years, [this sutra is preached again]. All dharmas are not due to one's own will! You want to practice and study to escape karmic obstacles, but due to demonic obstacles, you cannot continue. Not being able to continue is because of karma.

After listening to the Dharma, why can't you be liberated? During the Buddha's time, whoever heard the Dharma would be liberated and attain enlightenment. I have thought long and hard about this issue. From the time I became a monk until now, as of this year, it has been eighty years, which seems like a very long time, but during that time, karma is discovered, a lot of karma hinders you. How do we think? All of us Dharma friends hope to become Buddha, but it's not like you can achieve it immediately if you want to! In it, there are many obstacles; Therefore, first you must repent and eliminate karma. If we plan to drive on a road with many obstacles, can you drive? You must remove obstacles to be able to drive! There is also a proverb: “If you have not yet achieved Buddhahood, you will first have a predestined relationship” (If you have not yet achieved Buddhahood, you will first have a predestined relationship with someone else). If you want to cultivate and become a Buddha, first of all, you must repent of your karma. The most important thing is to repent of karma. Next, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: Every day you practice repentance like that, every day repent like that, don't be lazy or give up. If you are lazy and wasteful, it proves that in the past you did not have good roots. If you are not lazy or give up and have this good cause for practice, your blessings will be the greatest! Speaking of blessings, practicing without obstacles is the greatest blessing. It's not about getting rich, it's not about fame and fortune in the world, but while you practice, because your good roots in the past are very deep, your faith in the Three Jewels never stops, you will attain enlightenment very easily. But in the middle, due to encountering evil causes and conditions, evil dharmas and evil causes are discovered by your sins and obstacles. If it's mild, you can overcome it, if it's strong, you won't be able to overcome it! There is also a type of combined karma, combined karma cannot be overcome. It's not just one or two people, it's the entire region, the entire country. Can you overcome it? Therefore, it will make your karma difficult to achieve. If you can bestow a very good cause and condition for you, you can use repentance to contemplate your appearance. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that after seven days of inspiration, your physical appearance will attain a pure appearance.

I personally feel that my own karma is very heavy, if it doesn't work for seven days then fourteen days, twenty one days. If you want to continue practicing, but don't have the opportunity, that is a great tribulation. When Japan invaded China, it was not [the personal karma of] one or two people, but a great disaster. It causes obstacles that you have no strength to eliminate. If you have the power to eliminate these obstacles, you can practice like that. You must rely on blessings to be able to practice in a quiet retreat. Like our Dharma friends, no matter whether you recite Buddha's name or practice other methods, it's the same. Like our Dharma friends in Taiwan, your good roots are very deep, and there aren't that many obstacles, but you yourself create obstacles for yourself, are you willing to practice or not? Listening to the Dharma, you have heard a lot of Dharma, are you willing to do it or not? If you don't do it, you won't achieve it! Good roots have mixed roots, the difference is especially large. Like seven days of attaining purity, "achieving purity" is not at all the attainment of enlightenment, but rather the attainment of the pure form of the wheel. Then, if you practice, you will attain enlightenment very quickly, without any karma. We often say that our own karma is very heavy, even in preaching the sutras we have karma. You wanted to come and listen to the sutra, but halfway there an obstacle occurred and you couldn't listen! Have you thought about this or not? You can't think about it, you don't know where it comes from, so it's called karma.

You have created karma, the discovery of karma will not be certain. Some people will achieve purity in seven days, some people will achieve purity in twenty-one days, some people will achieve purity in forty-nine days, some people will achieve purity in one year, two years, three years. But Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: If you practice for three years, you will be absolutely pure. But during those three years there are still other obstacles, either because of the past or because of the present or in the future, you still commit all kinds of serious sins, and will not achieve purity, it depends on the situation. If you celebrate Contemplation and Repentance for seven full days, practice for seven days and you will attain the pure appearance of the wheel. That is extremely light karma. Either it takes a hundred days to attain pure form, or it takes two hundred days, or it takes a thousand days, which is a period of three years. There are people whose inborn qualities are too dull, and their karma is very serious, but you must develop a strong mind, do not care about your life and life, and give up your current body and life in exchange for the life of the Dharmakaya. How to deal with heavy karma? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You should always diligently recite my name, don't be lazy, constantly recite my name. Whether day or night, circumambulate (walking meditation), circumambulation is walking meditation around your penance. Sitting down will make you feel sleepy, so move around. In the past, if you slept for ten hours to wake up, reduce it to eight hours, or reduce it to six hours, or reduce it further to three or four hours, do this to repent. The repentance ceremony to make vows, the more you practice, the more joy and happiness you will have, the more you practice, the happier you will be, it is called "happiness". After that, there is also the need to make offerings, these four words must be linked together, that is, “pleasant practice of offerings”. With great joy make offerings to the Three Jewels. Don't relax, don't let go like that, even if you lose your life, you won't give up. If you are diligent like that, you will attain purity for a thousand days. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that the longest time is a thousand days, you will definitely be pure.

This ritual aims to teach us that the ultimate goal is to achieve the three pure karma. If you pray to be born in this Pure Land, you will definitely be reborn. When you are born, you decide to be born, why? If I go, I really don't go. The Buddha said that being born in the Pure Land is not wrong, he decided that he can be born, but if he goes, he doesn't go. If he doesn't go, it's because he doesn't want to be born. Is this statement contradictory or not? No contradiction at all! “When you are born, you decide to be born” means you have done the work to be reborn, which makes you able to decide to be born. You do not do things to be born in the Pure Land, but only do things in the Sa Ba world. How can you be born in the Pure Land? No way! I see many Dharma friends, “Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha”, reciting Amitābha Buddha very well, but what is in their mind, only that person knows! There are many people who chant Amitabha with their mouths thinking about the Sa Ba world in the present, doing things in the Sa Ba world, [so] they cannot be reborn. It is absolutely impossible to be reborn!

If we use Chiem Sat Luan Tuong, how will it be different? It tells you that you are not pure. Now you are still doing evil, how can you be pure? The wheel of life changes every day. Currently, at Ngu Dai Mountain, I have a disciple practicing in seclusion, asking me: "Master! My physical appearance is all red, pure. After two months, why did it suddenly become black!" I said: "You ask me, I have to ask you in return. What are you thinking in your mind now? Forms arise from the mind. Whatever your mind thinks, the wheel form immediately appears. Your mind is thinking elsewhere, your body is still worshiping and chanting here, but your mind is not focused on it, the wheel form immediately appears." Each of us Dharma friends develops Bodhi mind and practices the Bodhisattva path. You can examine yourself, your mind has changed greatly. From dawn to dusk, in that short time, others don't know, but you can't lie to yourself. You must honestly examine your own mind! Suppose you do not withdraw, are diligent and do not withdraw, do not relax, do not give up, for a thousand days, you will be absolutely pure. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us like that! In forty-nine days, you can attain purity. Either two hundred days, or a thousand days. Your nature is extremely dull, extremely stupid, and your sins are very heavy, but as long as you practice like that and develop a strong mind, you won't even care about your life. After a thousand days, you will be absolutely pure. Hope everyone is absolutely pure.

tieu_de: Lecture 7: Ten Wholesome Paths & The Method of Wheel Divination
tom_tat: Volume 7: Because of their karma, living beings are thick and thin; The base is beneficial, dull, and immeasurably different, or after fourteen days it will be pure, or after twenty-one days, up to forty-nine days later, it will be pure. If past and present both have fish...
noi_dung:
Lecture 7

Such living beings have thick and thin karma because of their karma; The base is beneficial, dull, and immeasurably different, or after fourteen days it will be pure, or after twenty-one days, up to forty-nine days later, it will be pure. If both the past and present have committed grave sins, they will be purified after a hundred days. Either after two hundred days, or even after a thousand days, it becomes pure. If you are a person of extreme poverty, with the heaviest sin, you should only develop a strong mind, do not care about your life and life, diligently recite, circumambulate (walking meditation) day and night, reduce sleep, repent, make vows, enjoy cultivating and making offerings, do not be lazy, do not give up waste, even if you lose your life, do not stop. If you are diligent like that, in a thousand days, you will definitely achieve purity.

The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma uses the pure form of the cycle to prove, because we ourselves do not know whether our own karma is ultimately light or heavy. Before you worship, of course use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate; After that, start worshiping. Over the course of seven days, early every morning, in the Buddha hall, before worshiping, use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate whether your own karma is light or heavy. Of course, at first, when you start using the Contemplation Wheel, worshiping every day, the wheel will gradually change. There are also times when seven days or fourteen days go by and [the results appearing in the wheel of appearance] do not change significantly, showing that one's own karma is very heavy, or because while worshiping, one's mind is not sincere. If the mind is not sincere, one's karma cannot be eliminated! While worshiping, because you have created karma in the past, some karma is very heavy, some karma is very thin, not heavy. In each person's ability, there are those who have advantageous abilities and those who have dull abilities; Because of dull faculties, wisdom is very shallow and meager. Therefore, when you worship, it is very difficult to correspond. If it is not compatible, you should be even more sincere in your repentance. It's a very heavy past karma. Because of the temporary effectiveness of your repentance, you still won't achieve any results. That is, when you worship, you must use the Contemplation Wheel every day to contemplate whether you have currently repented of karma or not? Luan General will let you know. If you repent for seven days or fourteen days and [the results shown by] the wheel form are still the same, then there are two types of situations:

- One is heavy karma.

- Second, you are not sincere. When worshiping, don't be sincere!

When you enter the penitentiary, you must hope for the end of birth and death. You must have the mind that wishes to end birth and death to be able to change birth and death. If your mind looks down, your mind is arrogant, as if you follow the crowd's recitation of the Buddha's name, but your mind is not sincere, when you sow the wheel form, you will not achieve the pure form of the wheel. Because our base has advantages and disadvantages, the benefit base can be achieved very easily as soon as we bow. If you have a weak base, you can bow for seven days, fourteen days, or even for a month or two, but you still cannot achieve the pure appearance of the wheel, showing that your past karma is very heavy. You should regretfully repent, be sincere, and earnestly worship. Some people have to go through twenty-one days, or seven times seven, or forty-nine days, and still show that their [karma] is very heavy. You just continue to worship, because we worship for the purpose of achieving enlightenment. When your karma is very heavy, if you practice Contemplation or Concentration, you will not achieve success. You must, while worshiping, know that your own sins have been purified, that is called "karma is gone". After that, you practice Concentration and will be able to achieve success very quickly. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: Regarding the karma created, there is karma that is very heavy, very thick, and there is karma that is very light.

What about that person's fundamentals? “Found” means the six senses, i.e. eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, has beneficial sense and dull sense. There are also times when, while worshiping, you fall ill or develop other illnesses, [causing] your worship to be unsuccessful. There are many differences in it, not everyone can worship or be very pure. This is not like when we follow the crowd to recite the Buddha's name, we don't show it, we wait until we are alone to worship and we will [feel] very clearly. Many Dharma friends say that their own karma is very heavy, "my sin is very big". That's okay for that person to say for himself. Suppose someone else says "your sin is very big, your karma is very heavy", immediately, that person will get upset and arouse affliction immediately. That person himself is polite and humble, with that kind of meaning, but the universal form is not polite to you. Your karma is quite heavy, [the incarnation then manifests] quite heavy. People repent for seven days and then become pure. You repent for seventy days and your karma remains unchanged. That is truly called “heavy karma”.

The situations during repentance are different: Sometimes the [repentance] time is short and karma has been purified; After that, practice Concentration and Hue, it is very easy to open wisdom. Heavy karma will not open great wisdom, so you continue to worship. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that you can spend a hundred days, two hundred days, even a thousand days and still not have a pure form of samsara. Because that person is extremely ignorant, he has not heard the Buddha Dharma for many lifetimes. Therefore, this time you meet, although you meet, due to heavy karma in the past, [so] from beginning to end, it is not easy to achieve the pure form of the cycle. This is a person with a very dull base, who has not encountered the Buddha Dharma for many lifetimes, the heaviest sin. If it falls into this situation, the universal form will not appear, or it will still show very serious karma.

You must develop a strong mind and risk your life. Risking your life to fight against your own sins, not caring about your life and repenting like that. At the same time, one must always diligently recite the name, that is, recite the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, regardless of day or night, walking day and night. The heavier the karma, the more you have to cut down on sleep to repent more. You still have to practice making offerings, don't indulge like that. Don't give up, even if you die, from beginning to end, don't stop, just keep worshiping. When you are about to die, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears and eliminates karma for you. If you are diligent like that for a thousand days (roughly three years), you will definitely attain the pure form of the wheel.

In this passage, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to be brave and diligent, not to lose our way of mind. While praying, your mind makes a vow, what vow is that? Just reach purity! Your wish is that we must worship so that our three karma of body, speech, and mind are all pure. That is the basic achievement; After that, practice two types of contemplation and you will definitely be able to achieve it. If while worshiping and repenting there is no pure form of the wheel, if it is not pure, then when you cultivate the path you will not be able to achieve it. Therefore, first of all, you must repent and eliminate all sins. In the second half of this sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches you how to cultivate Concentration and how to cultivate Wisdom, that is, cultivating two types of contemplation in the realm of One Truth. If the wheel form is not pure, when you cultivate the path, you will not be able to achieve it!

You should also pay attention, when others look down on you, either in speech or behavior, that is the eradication of your sins, proving that [your sins from previous lives] have disappeared. The more people despise you, the more you can realize: "Because my own karma is heavy, I am not respected by others. It is time for me to repent of my sins carefully!" Because, when karma is heavy, your blessings cannot be expressed in money. Without merit, of course people look down on you. When you have merit, others will respect you. Friends of the two lay communities, when close to their monastic masters, often see that their master has disagreements with them, because the master is very polite towards others, while towards you he has an extremely unpleasant attitude. Of course, you feel troubled because you think the teacher is unfair, and you feel very frustrated in your heart, not knowing that the teacher is eliminating bad karma for you. In the past, during the Tang Dynasty, there was a Prime Minister named Ngu Trieu An. When the national teacher entered the royal palace to preach the Dharma, Ngu Trieu An[16] then turned to the national teacher to request the Dharma. The National Teacher ignored him and even criticized him. What Dharma did he request? He asked the national teacher: "Where does ignorance arise?" The national teacher said: "You are a slave, why do you still ask about Buddhism?" Ngu Trieu An was furious: "I am the emperor's slave, not your monk's servant! I am the Prime Minister, only below the emperor, but above all living beings, how dare you despise me like that?" He asked the national teacher: "Where does affliction arise? What is affliction?" [Actually] he asked about “ignorance”, we changed it to “afflictions” [to make it easier to understand]. "Where does ignorance arise? What is ignorance?" The national teacher not only did not answer, but also scolded: "You are a slave and still want to ask about Buddhism!" So he got angry. When he got angry, the national teacher said: "Ignorance arises from there. That is ignorance." Ngu Trieu An was immediately enlightened and paid homage to the national master. That is called “the cause and effect of preaching the Dharma”, because all sentient beings turn to others and say: “My karma is very heavy.” I often hear Dharma friends confess: "My karma is very heavy"; That person himself can say [so], but if you tell that person: "Your karma is very heavy, do you still come to study Buddhism?" That person will definitely be angry; that is a manifestation of karma!

When we repent, we ourselves worship, the one being worshiped is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is the master of repentance. While you were repenting for your sins, when you bowed to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva repented for you. While you bow to Quan Yin to repent, Quan Am repent for you. We ourselves should explain: All Dharma friends who worship, you turn to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to repent. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva blesses you and helps you repent, causing your karma to be purified very quickly. When you repent, because you are so anxious that you cannot immediately repent and purify your sins. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also made that wish, praying that all sentient beings would not have bad karma. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also helps you repent, but you must not regret your life to repent.

In history, there was a monk who practiced in a cave. He originally practiced in a cave. Because he felt that if he continued to practice like that, his chances of success were too small, he went out to the cave and sat on a steep cliff. In the cave, Thuy Mien Cai was very serious, her practice kept falling asleep. He put himself in death because he couldn't fall asleep sitting on that cliff. If you doze off, you'll fall down. Wouldn't that mean falling to your death? That is the meaning of “put yourself in death to survive!” He sat quietly on a cliff to practice Thinking (practicing Meditation). The body could not hold on for long, sitting still and falling into drowsiness, falling off the cliff. The guardian angel immediately pulled him up. Being supported by the guardian god, he said to the guardian god: "In Nam Thiem Bo Chau, there must be very few people who practice like me?" The Dharma Protector said: "There are too many cultivators like you. How many hairs does a cow have? A lot! Don't be arrogant or arrogant. For someone with an [arrogant] mind like you, who speaks [loudly] like you, for five hundred great kalpas, I will not come to protect you." The guardian angel left. That old monk thought: "At first, I didn't ask you to protect the dharma? Whether you protect me or not, I still practice the same way!" He sat again and used the Contemplation magic to practice. His body could not sustain it for long. As he sat still and fell asleep, he fell again. The protector saved him again. He asked the guardian angel: "You said you did not protect me in five hundred lifetimes, why do you come again?" The god said: "One thought of your diligent mind surpasses five hundred great kalpas", that is, it is because of one thought of diligent effort that surpasses more than five hundred great kalpas [that the dharma protector saved him].

From this story, we understand clearly: When we practice the method of repentance, you must be patient, diligent, and courageous, because all the dharma-protecting gods and Bodhisattvas protect you, no need to worry. The reason Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to recite His name is because saying His name is the easiest. You bow, pay respects, pay homage, and even recite sutras, that is, recite the name Ksitigarbha, but you must recite that name to the point of being single-minded and undisturbed. Until you recite to the point where your mind is extremely happy, and your recitation eliminates fatigue and drowsiness, that is the correspondence. Your mind and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind correspond, which is feeling. Whenever you feel a feeling, the Bodhisattva will respond. When we practice, we often seek inspiration. Don't ask for inspiration, just ask yourself how to practice? This is very clear to you, because your energy will naturally correspond. When you practice, you feel; Due to the power of feeling, the Bodhisattva immediately responded naturally. If you feel but don't have the strength, just pray for the Bodhisattva to appear, it won't be possible! Because this is not a one-sided matter, it must be bilateral. Therefore, when you practice the Way, you should only pray for yourself. Don't just start practicing and expect to be blessed and inspired by the Bodhisattva, it's impossible! When your vigor reaches a certain level, [Bodhisattva] will correspond to that level. You don't have the power, you won't respond!

(Sutra) Good man! Nhuoc Duc has attained pure knowledge of the false appearance, the concubine has practiced beyond the seven days of the sun, and when the sun and sun have passed away, the god of the sun is trieu dan, and the second wheel of the form is in the center, and the frequency is three times chi. If the body, speech, and mind are pure, the person will be pure, and his name will be pure.
(Sutra: Good man! If you want to know the pure form, initially after practicing for seven days, Every day, early in the morning, hold the second form of the wheel in your hand and sow it three times [for each karma]. If your body, mouth, and mind are all pure, it is called "achieving purity").

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said again: - Good man! If you wish to have a pure form of the wheel, after you have practiced, perform the Contemplation and Repentance ceremony for seven days. Do not use the Contemplation Wheel for the first seven days. Seven days later, early in the morning every day, when you have just entered the penitentiary, use the second type of wheel form. There are three types of wheel signs, the second type of wheel form has only three blocks, only for the purpose of determining whether your body, speech, and mind are pure or not? You use these three wheels to sow, to clearly identify the three wheels of body, speech, and mind. If the verbal karma is pure, [the wheel of appearances with the word “verbal karma”] appears in red. You look at your own body, speech, and mind, whichever karma is pure, [the wheel corresponding to that karma] will appear on the wheel in red. If your body, speech, and mind are not pure and still black, it means your practice has not yet reached the level of being able to change karma, you still cannot change or shake your karma. Therefore, karma remains exactly the same. If you sow all three times (sow the body wheel, speech wheel, mind wheel, each wheel once), if it is all red, no black, then it is pure good, pure. If there is a little bit of black, [that is] even if a wheel form has a small black line, it is not considered pure. But early this morning, you sowed the pure form, you worshiped all day, and early the next morning sowing the wheel, it was not pure, that is, your purity was not complete. It is necessary that every day, every time you sow, it is pure and red. You will know that your practice has been successful and you will not fall into the three evil destiniess. If you wish [to be reborn] in the Pure Land, you will definitely be able to be born!

In the future, in the midst of Buddha Dharma, all monks practice good deeds. Depending on the period of cultivating, merit and karma have consequences, silver, and different species. Thi co, are extremely pure at the time, the appearance of the heron is different: Either sentient beings attain the three pure good karma, that is, they attain all the good signs. Or if a sentient being attains the three forms of good karma, at one day and one night, he will see the light and change forever. Or Manjushri's special scent has a pleasant scent and makes the body and mind happy. Or create a good dream, dream of seeing the Buddha's body in the future, create a witness, hold the demon in the first stage, exclaim: "Good disaster! Pure gold, self will witness the same." Or dream of seeing the Bodhisattva's future body and witnessing it. Or dream of seeing the Buddha's image emitting light and witnessing it.
(Sutra: Sentient beings in the future can practice and repent like Therefore, because they have practiced from a long time ago until now, everyone has practiced good deeds in Buddhism. Depending on how they practice, their karma is thick or thin and of all kinds. Therefore, when they achieve purity, their appearances are also different. Either there are sentient beings who, when the three karmas are purified, immediately achieve other good appearances. Or there are sentient beings who achieve good appearances in the three karmas, and in one day and one night, they see light throughout the whole house. Or you smell a special, strange fragrance, your body and mind are happy. Or you have a good dream, dreaming of the Buddha personally coming to testify, touching your head, praising: "How good! Now you are pure, I come to testify for you." Or dreaming of a Buddha image personally coming to testify.)

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: If sentient beings in the future want to use Contemplation and Repentance to practice and repent, you do not know whether your karma that has existed in the past is long or recent, shallow or deep, in the past you have practiced the Buddha Dharma or not, have heard the Dharma very deeply or not, and have completed many merits. Whether you have virtue in Buddhism or not, you don't know. The karma created is heavy or light, thick or thin, all kinds of differences. Therefore, when you plant the pure Contemplation Wheel, it also shows different appearances. For example, if the verbal karma is pure, because of lying, embellishing words, double-talking, and uttering harsh words, all [those evil karmas have] disappeared, [the physical form] will show a long and big red line. If it's just a little red, it's just pure and light. Light, heavy, thick, thin, the same is said about evil karma!

When you plant the Wheel of Contemplation, because all three karma of body, mouth, and mind are pure, there is not the slightest blemish. “Nai even the remaining good signs” (Until other good signs): Because you have achieved the good signs of the three pure karma, there are other things that will follow. What things will follow? At night, light shines everywhere. In your penitentiary there is all light. The night is inherently dark, but your penance is full of light. That is a kind of [good appearance]. There is also a special, wonderful fragrance, not the same fragrance as burning sandalwood in the human world, smelling a special fragrance. At the same time, your body feels extremely happy. That joy is not our usual joy. That is called “good appearance”. Either you dream of being in the same place as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, or together with the great Bodhisattvas participating in a sermon meeting of a certain Buddha. Or dream of Buddha coming to testify for you: "Hey good man! You are pure." He raised his hand and rubbed your head, praising: "How good! How good! Because you are now pure, I have come to prove it to you." Or dream of a Bodhisattva coming to testify, or dream of a Buddha statue emitting light. I think all of you who are practitioners may have experienced it, but is that the end of life and death? “Death” is a temporary thing, good appearances cannot prove that [the practitioner] has finished birth and death. You still have to continue practicing. If this phenomenon occurs every day, it is a decision. Or while you are worshiping, there are times when there is a very corresponding phenomenon; After a while, there was none again, due to karma's discovery, still undecided. In other words, you have not yet participated in the First Pillar, because your faith is not yet complete! If this type of phenomenon often appears, it proves that your faith is complete, the three karmas are pure, that is, the three karmas of body, speech, and mind are all pure. Meanwhile, when you practice the Way, practice Concentration and then attain Concentration, practice Hue and then attain Hue. We give an example, either reciting the Lotus Sutra, reciting the Avatamsaka Sutra, reciting the Shurangama Sutra, or even reciting the Four Agamas, normally you watch it but don't understand the meaning. Until you have bowed to the pure wheel form, not only do you fully understand it, but you also enter it. That is called “opened wisdom”.

(Sutra) If a weak person attains the three good karma, the first vision of the text is like trying false things, it is an illusion, Stupid, deceitful, unkind.
That is a falsehood, a lie, a deception, a deception, not a good appearance).

If you do not have the appearance [of purity] in the three karmas, that is, the appearance of [purity] in the three karmas of body, speech, and mind, but before that, having heard others say it, you also think you have achieved it. That's called illusion, lies, deception, not real! Those things are absolutely not good appearances. This passage is intended to teach you: While you worship, there will be signs of realms arising. If your three karmas are not pure, then whenever those phenomena exist, they will be completely false and false. You must have attained the corresponding form! Why must there be a form of rotation and contemplation? Whenever the wheel of signs corresponds, some people see the signs of the realm in their dreams, which is true. [Or] suddenly I smell a very fragrant smell in my room, to see the penitential room radiating light, or to have a very good dream. But my physical form is not yet pure, proving that these things are all demons, demons coming to disturb you. You must worship until the wheel becomes pure; Then, meet those good deeds. That is called “the supreme realm”. Because when we worship, learn the Contemplative Repentance Dharma, learn the Tu Van Repentance Dharma[17], or study the Quan Yin Repentance Dharma, all repentance methods are the same: As long as your mind is still not pure and dreams of the realms, they are all false, deceitful, not true. must be genuine. Don't be moved by demons, don't be happy. If you get excited too early, you will easily enter the demon realm!

Why do we rely on Contemplation and Repentance to repent? Here, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bless us, so that you will not fall into the demon realm, rely on the dharma to seek, rely on the dharma to manifest, absolutely pure, not illusory or misleading. If we practice other repentance dharmas, or practice by reading and reciting other Mahayana dharmas, or dreaming about the signs of superior realms, you should not have a happy mind, because it cannot be authenticated. You rely on the Dharma of Repentance [in the Contemplation Sutra], the wheel form in the Dharma of Repentance is the confirmation. Because there are often people who encounter demonic karma: If you don't follow Buddha's teachings and have those [good] phenomena, if you get excited and think you have achieved success in your practice, you will be relied on by demons! Is it possible for demons to manifest [the form of] Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? Yes! You don't practice Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at all, or you practice without being sincere at all, and suddenly Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears. That's not true. For example, at the back mountain of Quoc Thanh Pagoda on Thien Thai Mountain, there is a practitioner who practices by himself. He called me several times, [telling me] he saw this general and that general.
