I said: "Please use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate a little, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will tell you whether it is true or false." Afterwards, he called me and said: "It's a ghost, it's not real. Because I'm sick, I can't bow!" He asked “how?” I said: "You just keep bowing according to the usual routine. No matter how you bow, keep bowing like that. Until you bow and eliminate that demonic karma, you will not be swayed by demons." Or when you practice repentance, as soon as you practice, there are many signs of the realm (realms of the realm) rushing in. Scenes are coming, you have to break through, they are not real!

If you follow the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in accordance with the dharma, when the wheel of rotation has not yet achieved the three pure karma, suddenly there will be such holy scenes appearing to disturb you in repentance; Or you smell a scent, the house radiates light, or a ray of light comes in from the window, don't pay attention to it, just keep repenting. As long as the wheel of existence appears pure, it is real. Why do we have to worship and pray for Bodhisattva to prove it? Don't accept false appearances! [If you accept it], you will easily enter a demon. Follow the teachings of the Bodhisattva, follow the teachings in the scriptures, then there will be no ghosts. Because the five demons of desire, i.e. wealth, beauty, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping, all have demonic obstacles. The first thing is to clearly analyze demons and righteousness. Otherwise, you will be destroyed if you cultivate yourself!

(Sutra) Weak people in this world are born with good intentions, take advantage of the strong mind, fall in the ears of time, whatever you like The person who saves the child appears, magnifies the light, the spirit is peaceful, separates all the rituals, or the magical power, the species changes. Either the sutras, the sutras, the actions of good and evil, or the whims of ridicule, the teachings of the profound dharma. The benevolent person immediately becomes enlightened, gains decisive faith, or gradually attains the fruit of the monkhood.
(Sutra: If anyone has a foundation of good roots in this world, their mind will be strong and sensitive, while Then, depending on the person's merit, I will manifest and radiate a great light of compassion, causing that person to be at peace, free from doubts and fears, or display supernatural powers and all kinds of transformations. Or I can make them remember the good and bad things they have done in previous lives, or according to their preferences, speak about all kinds of profound and important dharmas. That person immediately has decisive faith in the vehicle that he or she has turned towards, or gradually attained the path of monkhood).

If a person has a foundation of good roots in this world, and his mind is sharp and strong, at that time, I (Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva) will, according to [that person's base] what body he should use to attain salvation, manifest that body, radiating great light, making that person peaceful, free from doubts and fears. Either it shows all kinds of magical powers, or it makes the person remember the things he has experienced and the good and evil things he did in his previous life. Or depending on the person's preference, speak about profound and important dharmas. That person immediately turns towards the “excess” to which he himself has turned. “The vehicle of direction” is whether you practice Mahayana or Hinayana, then it is called “the vehicle of direction”. Will decide to trust that excess. “Studio for realizing the path and fruition of a monk” (Gradually attaining the path and fruition of a monk): Here we refer to the common path and fruition of a monk, [including] First Fruition Direction, First Fruition, Second Fruition Direction, Two Fruition, Three Fruition Direction, Three Fruition, Four Fruition Direction, and Four Fruition. The Four Directions and Four Fruits are called the path results achieved by monks.

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us again: People with good roots in the world, because they have good roots in the world, can also direct the good, can capture the mind with one mind, have few delusions, have few random thoughts, have a strong and sharp mind, can subdue delusions, can capture the mind to the level of the mind. When I come to [the part of the text that teaches about] single-mindedness, I will talk about this issue. After that, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva immediately appeared, depending on which body [he] was worthy of using to save him, he appeared in that body, magnifying the magnetic light. The incarnation can also be the appearance of Bodhisattva, depending on which dharma should be used to make you attain salvation, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva then manifests that appearance to you, making you feel peaceful, no longer skeptical, no longer afraid. At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also said: "I will display all kinds of supernatural powers and all kinds of transformations, making that practitioner (the person who worships) think for himself and remember his life in the past." “Satisfaction of life” means that all the practice in countless lifetimes in one's past life is present. There is also doing good karma, but also doing bad karma, there is also strong practice, and not strong practice. Depending on that person's preferences, he speaks about all kinds of profound and important dharmas. Depending on what you like, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will, according to the opportunity, tell you that Dharma. That person will gain decisive confidence in the vehicle he or she is aiming for, whether it is the Mahayana, the Middle Vehicle, or the Hinayana, and will have decisive confidence, no longer doubting. In this way, you will validate the dharma you have practiced, or you will gradually attain the enlightenment of a Samana.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's teachings on this passage are extremely important! In particular, we rely on the Contemplation Sutra to practice the method of repentance, in order to absolutely eliminate negative karma. As for the appearance of the evil realm, [sometimes] you only need to worship for one day and the appearance of the evil realm will follow and disappear from the manifestation [of the wheel of rotation]. Sometimes it takes a long time, sometimes it takes a short time. I don't have the manifestations like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said, but when I was in New York, for about three or four months, I dreamed every night. As soon as I put my head on the pillow to sleep, I dreamed until I woke up. The next day, just go to bed, put your head on the pillow and dream again. Roughly more than a hundred days, that is, everything experienced in the previous life appears. Sometimes practicing is very good, sometimes creating karma, sometimes repaying karma and then practicing again, from life to life without stopping. I myself had a dream, roughly starting from the end of the Tang Dynasty, the beginning of the Song Dynasty, until the present life, that is, the time I was in America. I told this story to Dharma Master Hoang Giac, but at that time, no decision arose, nor did I gain wisdom. You also don't have any karma, that is, regarding both good and evil, there is no deviation towards good, but also no deviation towards evil, it seems to be normal movement. That's called karma in the present and eternal life, what was done in the past flashes through each life like that!

(Sutra) Respect all sentient beings, although the ability to see the incarnation transforms, preaches, and studies. The mind, body, speech, and mind attain pure appearance, the ego protects the thoughts, the spirit of living beings quickly destroys all kinds of obstacles. Heavenly Demon Ba Tuan does not come back to destroy, even ninety-five kinds of pagan evil masters, must not come back to ghosts, gods, or herons. Possessing the Five Virtues, having the ability to practice Zen and wisdom.
(Sutra: Again, even though those living beings cannot yet see my transformation and preaching, they should only Studying with the mind, so that the body, mouth, and mind have achieved purity, I also protect and help those sentient beings to quickly destroy all kinds of obstacles. The Demon of Three Weeks does not come to destroy them, even the evil masters of the ninety-five types of heretics and all the ghosts and spirits do not come to disturb them.

“Serve and forgive all sentient beings” (Again, those sentient beings) refers to those who practice repentance. Those who do not practice Earth Store Repentance and do not practice Contemplation and Contemplation are not mentioned. “Bless all sentient beings” refers specifically to those who practice repentance. People who follow the Contemplative Contemplation Dharma, although they cannot see my reincarnation (Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva), nor can they hear my reincarnation preach the Dharma, they should learn with a sincere mind and that's it! As long as that person can make his own body, speech, and mind achieve a pure appearance [when contemplating with the Contemplation Wheel], I will also protect and recite that person. This sentence has that meaning. There are people who have worshiped to the point of purity of body, speech, and mind, but the phenomena mentioned above such as "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appears, or preaches the Dharma, or blesses you" even though they are not there, do not see my reincarnation, nor hear me preach the Dharma, that person should study the mind of the mind (in the following section, we will talk about the mind of the mind), so that his body, speech, and mind attain purity, I also protect the thoughts of that type of living beings. Protecting that person will cause all of that person's obstacles to be destroyed, and cultivating the path will be achieved very quickly.

“Protection” means that evil spirits such as the heavenly devil Ba Tuan, who attempt to destroy the power of that person's practice, will not be able to get close, meaning [that person has] been protected by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Even the evil masters of the ninety-five types of pagans cannot disturb that person. At that time, all of the five poor things, the Ten Hindrances, and everything else will be gone. That person can practice Meditation and can also practice wisdom. Wisdom is studying sutras and dharma, Meditation is practicing Concentration. The two disciplines of Dinh Hue, one is Chi, the other is Quan. If you can practice Samantabhadra, you will be able to attain enlightenment, but that is the person who has achieved the pure appearance of the wheel.

(Sūtra) For the second time, in the future, all living beings will be equal, even though no one seeks Meditation, the wisdom is essential. Dao, the birth of the race of yoke, poverty, misery, sadness and oppression, the heron reveres, worships, makes offerings, repent of evil deeds, constantly makes vows, always at the right time, the right place, diligently chanting the name of the self, spiritual spirit with sincerity, the heron is quickly getting rid of the race of brain failure. Xshe tries her destiny and is born in a good land.
(Sutra: Furthermore, if sentient beings in the future, although not seeking Meditation or wisdom, If the path is weak, you will only encounter all kinds of hardships, poverty, misery, and pressing worries. You should also respect, worship, make offerings, regret the evil things you have done, always make vows, in all times and all places, diligently chanting my name with sincerity, then you will quickly be freed from all kinds of depravity. If you give up this life, you will be born in a good place.

Furthermore, all sentient beings in the End of the Age, although not seeking Meditation, wisdom, or weak path, but when encountering all kinds of hardships, poverty, misery, and pressing worries, during that time, they should still respectfully worship, make offerings, and repent of the evil deeds they have done, and repent of the evil deeds they themselves have done. create. “Repenting for the evil you have done” is repenting for the evil deeds you have done in the past and your current evil karma. Always make a vow, often make a vow yourself. Fellow monks must make that vow every day, on the one hand, repentance, and on the other hand, dedication. To repent, we must repent every day, vow to help others, benefit sentient beings, and dedicate all the good things we have done to all sentient beings who are suffering and suffering. Repent for all the wrong things we have done. Poverty, misery, anxiety, and all kinds of oppression, when encountering the signs of that realm, one must revere, worship, and make offerings. These things are all evil karma that we have done in the past until now. You should repent and change. Recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to repent. If that negative karma is found to be not too serious, what should you do? At all times, in all places, regardless of any situation, proclaim my name in all times and in all places. When confessing, don't recite with false sentiments, be sincere and earnest, those mental disorders will disappear, let go of this body and be reborn in a good place. That's not to mention the vow [to help sentient beings] that has already been made. If you make another vow, praying to be born in the Pure Land, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bless you, causing you to be born in the Pure Land.

We sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending world are often oppressed by all kinds of causes and conditions in life. If you see a temple and can go to the temple to worship, [“temple” here] is not a temple to worship good gods, or a temple to worship all kinds of gods, but refers to a place to worship Buddha and Bodhisattva, but [you] do not have the mind of renunciation, nor do you pray for Concentration or Wisdom, nor do you wish to learn the essential Dharma. Many Buddhist disciples do not wish for those things, and do not earnestly wish for birth and death. They are not believers in Buddha. Disciples of the Three Jewels must endure life and death. We can ask ourselves: "Is it true that we pray for life and death every day?" Let's not talk about the two lay assemblies of Upasaka and Upasamī, let's just talk about our monastic friends who go to the main hall early every morning to chant the exercises. Do you make a vow to hope for the end of life and death? Every day make a vow "I hope to end birth and death, I must end afflictions". Whether you do so or not, you will understand clearly. Outsiders don't understand very well, only you can know clearly! Do you repent every day of the evil things you have done? Do they all vow to repent? Is it possible to escape mental breakdowns and endure tests? I understand best! Outsiders don't know, who knows what's in your mind? For example, people often think "when we are about to die, Amitābha Buddha and the saints will use incense and flowers to welcome me, making my mind not go crazy, so I can be reborn in the Pure Land"; can it be done or not? If you use a distracted mind, can you be reborn? The Amitabha Sutra says very clearly: Either one day, or two days, or three days, or four days, up to seven days, you can attain rebirth with one undisturbed mind. Being able to be reborn is because your mind is undisturbed; you cannot be reborn because your mind is scattered. Do you believe in yourself or not? Do you think you can be reborn? Say, "I can definitely be reborn because my mind is not scattered and my mind is not crazy." If you don't have any pressing illness or suffering, then the vow you have made will be able to be achieved. If the eight sufferings are burning together, between birth and death, is it still possible at that time [the mind is not crazy] like that?

There is a mantra to pray for birth in the Pure Land called “Mr., a-mi-ri-attained-virtue-cat-la-hong” (Auṃ amṛta tejehara hūṃ) consisting of ten words. If, at that time, you can still recite the sentence "You, a mi ri achieved the virtue of great success" then you will absolutely be able to be reborn. When the karma appears, the mantra will not appear! Normally, you recite it 100,000 times? No! Thirty thousand times? No! Recite ten thousand times? No! Even a thousand times, do you recite it a thousand times? Just every day reciting “He, a mi ri attains the virtue of perfect goodness and happiness” then you can absolutely be reborn[18]. At that time, karma will appear, you will forget all the mantras, and you won't be able to recite them! You must use effort every day to eliminate karma! Because until then, your single-minded belief will not change, even though there is still karma, but there is still Amitābha Buddha's mantra to bless you. That is called “rebirth of karma”, completely eliminating karma, bringing karma to rebirth in the world of Ultimate Bliss. When you are reborn, the karma will no longer exist, the karma will be gone. Therefore, our faith must be solid. No matter what dharma you study, the first condition is that your faith must be solid. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us like that, also to make us believe.

(Sutra) Resurrection, the time of the future, weak at home, weak to become a monk, desiring to receive the sound In the pure and wonderful precepts, there is a serious sin of not being able to accept the Buddha's teachings. Heron is like a superior person who practices repentance and repentance, with a spirit of spirit and mind, and attains a good body, speech, and mind with good characteristics, that is, the ability to receive.
(Sutra: Again, in the future, if lay or monastic beings want to receive the wonderful precepts pure, but previously committed a serious sin, so he did not receive it, he should also practice the method of repentance as above, to make his mind strong, achieve good appearance in body, mouth, and mind, then he is also worthy of receiving it).

“Future submission” is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva reminding us because in the Dharma-Ending Age, immediately in the future, lay or monastic beings want to pray for pure magical precepts such as the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, but in the past they have committed many sins and have no chance to receive the Three Refuges and Five Precepts. The ten precepts and eight precepts don't even need to be said anymore! That means there is no opportunity for us to receive the pure precepts. Even to receive the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, one must destroy serious sins. If it is a serious crime, can you have the opportunity to receive precepts? Can't, can't live! Because you have committed a serious sin, you cannot receive the precepts; But Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us a means, which is to practice the method of repentance, in order to achieve the will of mind and good appearance in body, speech, and mind. Just start from the heart and you will achieve it. Or you recite the Buddha's name, recite a sentence of Amitābha Buddha, you must recite it wholeheartedly. Without sincerity, it will not be effective. Once you reach the ultimate mind, you will be spiritual, receive the precepts and attain the precepts, eliminating disasters and avoiding disasters. If you have eliminated evil, evil will also be eliminated.

(Sutra) Weaving sentient beings with desires to practice Ma Ha Dharma, seek the Bodhisattva's life with the basic precepts, fulfill the vow of total life lay people, monastics, absolutely forbidden precepts, in the position of Taking the Law and Nghi Precepts, Receiving Good Dharma Realms, Receiving Good Transformations of Living Beings, I cannot attain good precepts as a good teacher, widely explaining the Bodhisattva Dharma Treasury, immortal practitioners, with the mind of the Bodhisattva, reverently making offerings, admiring the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, asking for their testimony, making single-minded vows, and explaining the precepts. It is said that the ten basic precepts are the main precepts, the second is the total election of the three precepts, and the self vows to receive the precepts. The heron attains the precepts.
(Sutra: If sentient beings want to practice Mahayana, seek the basic precepts of Bodhisattva, and receive all the forbidden precepts of lay people and monastics, that is, Taking the Precepts of Discipline, Receiving the Good Dharma Precepts, and Receiving the Transformation of Living Beings, but it is impossible to have a good teacher who can transmit the precepts and widely understand the Bodhisattva Dharma Treasury, then the practitioner should first be dedicated in the ashram, respectfully make offerings, tell the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, ask them to be teachers to prove, single-mindedly make a vow to read and clarify the precepts. First of all, talk about the ten basic precepts; then, generalize the three types of precepts. Thus, you can attain the precepts.

If living beings want to learn the Mahayana path, Mahayana (Mahāyāna) translates as Mahayana path. [That person] wants to study the Mahayana scriptures, or wishes to receive the Bodhisattva precepts. Our Dharma friends all received the Bodhisattva Precepts at the same time, many of us received the Bodhisattva Precepts. It is impossible not to violate the Bodhisattva Precepts! Especially with regard to the ten important precepts and the forty-eight minor precepts, you have just broken the precepts with just a thought, completely different from the precepts of bhikkhus, bhikshunis, Three Refuges, and Five Precepts. The Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, up to the eight precepts, the ten precepts, the bhikshuni precepts, the bhikshuni precepts are all considered according to appearance, only if you violate them [by specific actions] will you be considered an ultimate offender. The Bodhisattva Precepts are completely different! The Bodhisattva Precepts are the Truth. As soon as you think about it, you immediately violate the precepts without waiting for it to become a reality. Because that is the mind world, the mind world is the mind violation: As soon as your mind starts thinking, you have violated the precepts. Can we ordinary people not start thinking? Can't do it! However, “precepts” are general, because Nie Luat Nghi Precepts are the rules about walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. Thien Thien Dharma Realm determines good and evil dharma. This collection of precepts is deeper because the meaning of good dharma and evil dharma is deeper than the Law of Ritual Precepts. The Bodhisattva Precepts are the Precepts of Transforming Sentient Beings (precepts aimed at transforming sentient beings). There are quite a few skillful means to save sentient beings, but are the thoughts you use in your mind consistent with your great compassion and great compassion? This precept focuses on analyzing and focusing on the mind. “Chinh mind” means you control your mind in one place, because your heart is sincere and has no delusions.

In this passage, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: If you want to accept the Bodhisattva Precepts, or attain the basic precepts, up to the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, you ask the teacher to prove it. Who are you? Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions. I invite the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions to come and prove it to you. You must make a vow, make a vow with one mind, and focus on one place of mind. In the following section, we will specialize in one-pointedness. Willow clearly explains the appearance of the world, that is, “confessing the appearance of the world” . First of all, let's talk about the ten basic precepts [in the Brahma Vong Bodhisattva Precepts], which are called “heavy precepts”. Then, speaking of forty-eight light precepts, those precepts are called “light precepts”. Lightness and heaviness are both complete, because body, speech, and mind are all complete, before the Buddha, make a self-satisfaction vow. “To take the precepts by oneself” is in front of a Buddha statue, or a Bodhisattva statue, or in front of a Ksitigarbha statue, without a master giving us the precepts. I can't find a teacher to give me the precepts. You should accept the Buddha's precepts first, but you must be sincere. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said according to skillful means: If you can wholeheartedly face the Buddha and receive the precepts, you will also attain the precepts. That is receiving the Mahayana precepts. If you wish to practice the Bodhisattva path, you must take the Bodhisattva Precepts. The three pure precepts of body, speech, and mind are the three pure precepts, which are the Precepts of the Law of Requiem, the Precepts of Good Dharma Precepts, and the Precepts of Many Benefits and Friendships. Bodhisattvas must receive Many Benefits and Friendships, which means benefiting sentient beings. [Precepts] for the benefit of sentient beings include ten important precepts and forty-eight minor precepts. These are called the Bodhisattva Precepts, which are the precepts that benefit sentient beings. Normally, lay people have two collections of pure precepts, while monastics have five collections of pure precepts.

You must specialize in teaching a little about Mahayana Mahayana. We develop Bodhi mind and want to practice the Bodhisattva path. To develop Bodhi mind and practice the Bodhisattva path, you must receive the Bodhisattva Precepts. To receive the Bodhisattva Precepts, one must receive the basic Bodhisattva precepts. Once you have received the precepts, you must maintain the precepts, especially the Thien Thien Dharma Precept, which collects all good dharmas. “Nhi” means to receive (including receiving, holding), giving all good dharma to all sentient beings. That is speaking from the perspective of doing good deeds, speaking from the perspective of doing good things. But if you want to benefit all sentient beings, the first thing is to [practice] the Precepts of Reception. Bodhisattvas have Bodhisattva precepts, because the Bodhisattva Precepts include all the regulations and prohibitions for both the Hinayana and the Mahayana, including all the means to "prevent evil and do good". That is Nie Luat Nghi Gioi. Collecting all good dharmas, all good dharmas are given as alms to all sentient beings [is the Dharma Realm of Good Dharma Realm]. The Buddha also established the precepts in order to transform sentient beings (Nhih Many Benefits of Sentient Beings). If you want to save all sentient beings, pray for all sentient beings to become Buddhas, first of all, you must fulfill all the precepts.

There is no pure precept teacher, [that is] it is impossible to find a pure precept teacher. If you do not understand the precepts, you will not be able to transmit the precepts. That is called a pure monk. In the precepts, it is said that if a precept teacher is not pure, he cannot transmit precepts or preach the Dharma. Great Master Random Ich wanted to receive precepts. He observed that he could not find five pure precept masters in Nam Jambudvipa, there was none, it was impossible. He searched in the Tripitaka and found the Sutra [Contemplation] Good and Evil Karma. In the past, no one said this sutra. Starting from Great Master Nguoi Ich, he found [this sutra] from the Tripitaka. Having found it, he then relied on the [Contemplation] Sutra of Good and Evil Karma to repent, bowed to Chiem Sat Sam, attained the pure appearance of the wheel, and then attained precepts. But He did not know how to make the Contemplation Wheel. Therefore, this dharma cannot be spread. Until the time of Master Hoang Nhat, Master Hoang Nhat specialized in propagating the teachings of Master Nguoi Ich. He searched and created the Contemplation Wheel, and then vowed to propagate the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. He created the Contemplation Wheel, but did not preach the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. Great Master Nguoi Ich composed a set of Compendium of Contemplative Meanings for the Contemplative Sutra. Besides that commentary, there is no other commentary!

Here, [Bodhisattva] tells us: Good deeds belong to the Dharma Realm of Goodness, including all the precepts belonging to good dharma. In doing good, there are also rules for doing good. We do good things, make mistakes and still don't know it. Doing good things also has rules for doing good things. That's called Nhiep Thien Dharma Realm. The precepts say it very clearly. When you practice giving alms and taking care of living beings, do you have distracting thoughts in your mind? Is the mind pure or not? This has enormous implications; Therefore, it is necessary to think about it. At the same time, you must protect yourself. Just like we have unintentionally hurt and killed living beings without any reason, without even knowing it. For example, when we wake up in the morning, as soon as we walk, you know that under your feet you have crushed a few small insects to death. Do your physical eyes see the tiny little lives? This means that in the morning, as soon as you start walking, you must recite the verse: "Tung Trieu Dan dan directly to the grave, all sentient beings must return to their own devices, if the weak ones are buried in a strange form, may they immediately be born in the Pure Land" (From morning Tiger hour to dusk, all living beings guard themselves, if they lose their lives at my feet, may you immediately be born in the Pure Land). Every thought is a visualization that brings sentient beings to the world of Ultimate Bliss. Because you don't know whether you hurt them or not? Early in the morning, you must recite that verse; After that, get out of bed, put on your shoes and walk. Suppose you say "you accidentally trampled them to death, then brought them to the world of Ultimate Bliss, may you immediately be born in the Pure Land", do you have that power or not? It's not because of your strength, but because of the strength of all the Buddhas. You recite that verse, thanks to the power of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to show that every thought you recite will benefit sentient beings, and every thought will not hurt sentient beings. Because you recite this verse, you will feel the blessings of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

This verse is said by Bodhisattva Manjushri in the Pure Conduct chapter of the Avatamsaka Sutra. Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us: When you wake up early in the morning, when you put on your shoes and are about to walk, you must be extremely careful. First, recite this mantra once, that is, the mantra in that sutra, from early morning until evening, until you go to bed and stop walking. “Tung Trieu Dan Dan directly at the tomb, all sentient beings will return to the next stage, if the weak will be buried in a strange form, I will pray that they will immediately be born in the Pure Land”. That is a wish, but also a virtue. Pure Hanh is the great vow, that is, the great vow of Manjushri Bodhisattva, including a total of one hundred and forty things, which you can recite until you become a Buddha. After the disciple Thien Tai finished worshiping Maitreya Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva taught the disciple to return to visit Manjushri. Manjushri Bodhisattva taught his disciples to recite this (the vows in the chapter on Pure Conduct) and then allowed them to come and worship Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. Because in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, there are many verses of Hoa Nghiem, so Master Hoang Nhat determined that the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is Mahayana, not Hinayana, not like ordinary divination, eight-word criticism, and hexagrams! Absolutely do not be confused, because this dharma and those things are not similar. This dharma is a mind dharma, a mind-ground dharma because it skillfully uses the mind.

(Sutra) Resurrection, in the future all sentient beings are equal, desiring to become a monk, having the opportunity to become a monk, unable to attain it. good precept master, pure and pure Tassemblies, when the mind is doubtful, not able to attain the dharma, accept the forbidden precepts, naturally learn to develop the unsurpassed path mind, body, speech, and mind attain purity, some become monks, accept the dharma in the world, be obeyed by the dharma, follow the above vows, take the Bodhisattva's precepts of the three precepts, the code name is "Paradise plan". Moc Xoa renounced the precepts", the name of a Bhikkhu, Bhikkhunī. TIncredibly praying to the Sravaka Vinaya Pitaka, attaining the Bodhisattva practice of Magadhakāgarbha to accept, recite, observe and practice.
(Sutra: Again, all the sentient beings in the future who wish to become monks, and have become monks, If you cannot find a good teacher who transmits the precepts and the assembly is pure, your mind doubts [yourself] and you should not receive the forbidden precepts according to the dharma, you should only learn to develop the unsurpassed path mind, as well as make your body, mouth, and mind attain purity. If you are not yet a monk, you should take off your hair, put on the dharma robe, make a vow like the above, and swear to receive the three types of precepts in the Bodhisattva Discipline, then it is called "full observance." complete the precepts of Pāramātiṛkā to become a monk", called a bhikkhu or bhikkhunī. You should search for the Shravaka Vinaya Pitaka, and the Mātṛkā (Mātṛkā)[19] practiced by the Bodhisattva to receive, maintain and read. chanting, observing and practicing).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said again: - Furthermore, sentient beings in the future want to seek ordination, sentient beings in the future have the desire to leave this world, wish to become a monk, or have already become a monk and say: "We bhikshus and bhikshunis wish to attain precepts, but there is no good and pure teacher." During the Dharma Ending Period, at Nam Diem Phu De in the Ming Dynasty, Master Nguu Ich looked for five pure Bhikkhus but there were none. Even though they received the precepts, they did not achieve them. Currently, when giving precepts during the Dharma Ending period, there are many things that do not follow the Buddha's regulations! The Buddha stipulated "you can receive precepts at twenty years of age", but with skillful means we can still allow you to "borrow the age" [if we consider you qualified to receive great precepts]. For example, if I become a monk, I am only sixteen years old, how do I receive ordination as a monk? The monk who received the precepts let me "borrow" one year, the monk who ordained me "borrowed" another year, the great master let me "borrow" another year, my leader, the master of ceremonies, let me "borrow" another year, which is a full twenty years old! Can it be "borrowed"? That's called "covering your nose and covering your eyes" so that your eyes can't see and your nose can't smell. In fact, it is impossible to attain precepts! In Nam Thiem Bo Chau, looking for five pure monks, I couldn't find them! Great Master Ngu Ich also wanted to attain pure precepts, so he searched through the Tripitaka, found the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, and relied on the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to develop the unsurpassed mind. On contemplation, he used the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to achieve the three pure karma. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is a monk who has attained precepts. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is also a master of ceremonies. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is also the three masters, seven attainments[20], and leads the ceremony, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva alone is in charge. If you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, use the contemplation of the wheel and the wheel of contemplation to demonstrate the three pure karma, then you will attain precepts. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches like that!

If your mind has doubts, [worried about yourself] not being able to follow the Dharma of receiving the forbidden precepts, then what do you do? First of all, you learn to develop the unsurpassed path mind. The unsurpassed mind, simply put, is “developing Bodhi mind”, making your body, mouth, and mind pure. Generate the Bodhisattva mind; At that time, the body, mouth, and mind are pure, and before becoming a monk, one can become a monk; Once you become a monk, you must make a vow, what vow do you make? Taking a self-oath means swearing yourself, vowing to receive the Bodhisattva Precepts and receive the Three Pure Precepts (Nhi Lua Nghi Precepts, Nhat Thien Dharma Precepts, Many Useful Friendship Precepts). At that time, the full monastic precepts of Prātimokṣa (Prātimokṣa) are considered as bhikshus and bhikshunis. After that, after receiving the teachings, he studied the Vinaya Pitaka and the Bodhisattva Maākāgagarbha, received, maintained, read, recited, observed and practiced. Bhikkhus and bhiksunis belong to the pure Sangha. When they receive ordination, they are the most noble and unsurpassed, to what level? He is an exemplary teacher of heaven and man. Until you sow the wheel of the wheel and attain the purity of the wheel, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva transmits the three great precepts to you, [the three precepts] novices, monks, and Bodhisattvas.

However, regarding this issue, the Yogācāraṇa also says the same thing. The Dharma Phenomena period has passed, in the Dharma Ending period, wishing to receive precepts is extremely difficult, because there is no pure precept teacher, so you practice non-action, lawlessness, in order to receive the precepts of non-action. But you should not doubt in your mind. If you doubt that the teacher who transmits the precepts is not pure, if you doubt that the group participating in giving you the precepts is not pure, you will not be able to attain the precepts. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva practices skillful means, and He teaches us: If you want to attain precepts but do not have a teacher to transmit them, how do you do it? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught: Kneel before the Buddha and bow to Contemplation and Contemplation. Praying for repentance is nothing else but seeking to attain precepts. That is called “seeking precepts and worshiping” (bowing to ask for precepts), specifically seeking to attain precepts. At that time, one must develop the supreme path mind; The unsurpassed mind is Bodhi mind.

The supreme enlightenment is to develop the mind to become Buddha. But you sow the rotary signs of the three karma of body, mouth, and mind. If the rotary signs of all three karmas are pure, I (Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva) will let you receive precepts. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that the wheel of all three karmas of yours has been bowed to the point of purity. If you have not yet become a monk, you can shave your hair and wear dharma robes. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva accepts you as a disciple and imparts the three great precepts to you. However, it is impossible to fake the form of the wheel of purity that has been achieved. You must absolutely bow so that the three karmas are pure. That is called “self-ordination”. Great Master Ich took the precepts himself, so he proposed Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. That is the cause and effect of receiving His precepts.

(Sutra) Although he became a monk, he was a full-fledged twenty-year-old, and took the vow of the first ten fundamental precepts. Ordained as a novice monk, a novice monk possesses special precepts. Receiving the precepts, the name of Sa Di, Sa Di Ni. That is, being close to, making offerings to, granting former monks, learning the Mahayana mind, receiving precepts, praying to a monk, asking for precepts, practicing majestically, like a novice monk, a novice monk.
(Sutra: If even though you have become a monk but are not yet twenty years old, before finally, you should vow to receive the ten basic precepts and all the special precepts of a novice monk or novice nun. Having already received the precepts, you should be close to, make offerings to, and serve the person who has become a monk before, has the mind to study the Mahayana, has received the monastic precepts, and prays for him or her to be a medical teacher only to ask questions, so that he or she can be taught the proper practice according to the Dharma of the novice monks and novice nuns).

If, although you have become a monk, even though you have already become a monk, you are not yet twenty years old, then you can only make vows, you cannot receive the [Complete] precepts. First of all, vow to take the ten novice precepts (Śrāmaṇera), including the ten basic precepts, or take the novice precepts (Śrāmaṇeri). The sutra specifically points out: The same is true for the ordination of novices, they also use the method of sowing the wheel to receive the novice ordination or novice ordination. Just by following the Contemplation Sutra to receive precepts, one can also be called a novice or novice nun. But we should make offerings to those who have become monks before, that is, those who have received the Full Precepts and have the mind to study Mahayana. It is said very clearly here, “if you have the mind to study Mahayana”, you cannot study with Hinayana people. What will people with the mind to study Mahayana do? Only rely on him and honor him as your Physician. If you become a monk and have a Medical Teacher, then within five years, you must rely on that teacher, cannot leave him, and ask him at any time to teach you how to practice sadhana, how to maintain the novice precepts or novice precepts, so that he can teach you according to the opportunity. But depending on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to receive the precepts, if you are not yet twenty years old, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will not give you [the Full Precepts], you cannot be considered a Bhikkhu or Bhikkhuni! You must be twenty years old [or older]. First of all, you can take the ten basic precepts, or the special precepts of a novice monk, you can take the Bodhisattva precepts, but you are still a novice or novice monk. If we only take the Bodhisattva Precepts, we can only be a lay person, and cannot be considered a monk. If you do not take the Bhikkhu Precepts, but take the Bodhisattva Precepts, you cannot be considered a monk. One must receive ordination as a bhikshuni or bhikshuni to be considered a bhikshuni or bhikshuni. If I have become a monk but have not yet reached the age of twenty, I will not be able to receive the [Cul Tuc] precepts, because even if I receive the precepts, I will not attain the precepts! Therefore, regarding the issue of renunciation, ordination, and majesty, Master Nguich Ich attaches great importance.

At the same time, you rely on the scriptures and this method to receive precepts. To receive precepts, you must first get close to and make offerings to the Three Jewels. First, you must develop your mind and find a Mahayana teacher who has received the Complete Precepts to be close to and make offerings to. This means that if there is a person who became a monk earlier than you, has been [ordained] for a full ten years, and studied Mahayana, you can honor such a person as your teacher, to be close to him, make offerings to him, and follow him or her to become a monk. Don't rely on a person who has become a Hinayana monk, your three actions of body, speech, and mind always respect him. There is a huge difference in developing the mind here, developing a great path mind and not developing a great path mind, both sides have differences. To develop Bodhi mind is to be a Bodhisattva Bhikkhu. Generating the mind and not generating the mind, what is a Bodhisattva, what is an ordinary person, that is the difference in where the mind is generated. A person who has developed Bodhi mind is a Bodhisattva. Those who have not yet developed Bodhi mind are ordinary people.

(Sutra) Weakness cannot be ruled like a person of vision, only close to the Bodhisattva who cultivates Magadakāgarbha, chanting, thinking, observing, practicing. You need to make offerings to Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.
