Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: In the Dharma-Ending Age, Bhikkhus and Bhikkhunis do not rely on precepts to behave, because people under the age of twenty have received precepts and learned precepts! Having received the precepts, I have never read the Vinaya Pitaka. As far as I know, from my experiences, the vast majority are like that. Before receiving the precepts, even taking the novice precepts without learning the novice precepts, or receiving the monk precepts without learning the monk precepts. Before you receive the bhikkhu ordination, you cannot consider [the original precepts of] the bhikkhu ordination, because this was established by the Buddha. You should read the Abhidharma Pitaka and study the commentaries, but if you have received bhikkhu ordination, you should read the Abhidhamma Pitaka. Nowadays, regardless of whether we have received the Bhikkhu ordination or not, monks read the precepts and read the Vinaya Pitaka very little.

(Sutra) Nhua Sa Di Ni with ten years of practice, the heron takes the vows of the Bhikkhuni Pitaka with the middle knowledge of Xoa Ma. Na six precepts dharma, up-to-date study of Bhikkhunis necessarily gathering precepts. At the age of twenty years, she was able to attain the full life of the Bodhisattva of the three precepts.
(Sutra: If a novice monk is eighteen years old, he should also take the six precepts of Consciousness Xoa Ma Na. in the Bhikkhuni Pitaka, and fully study all the precepts of the bhikshuni. When she reaches the age of twenty, she can receive the three types of Bodhisattva precepts as mentioned above).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that if novices or novice nuns have turned eighteen years old, they should learn the precepts of Consciousness Xoa Ma Na (Śikṣamāṇā), which means studying Dharma women. But since [Saininis] only receive bhikkhuni ordination, they should learn the bhikkhuni precepts. At first, it took three years of study, the same for novice monks, the same for monks. When you turn twenty years old, in our country, in this world, when you turn twenty years old, you will receive three great precepts at the same time. It wasn't like that during the Buddha's time. When he was twenty years old, he could only receive the Bhikkhu Precepts, [those who wanted to receive] the Bodhisattva Precepts could only receive the Bodhisattva Precepts.

(Sutra) Natural queen, attained the title of Bhikkhu, Bhikkhunī.
(Sutra: Then called Bhikkhu, Bhikkhuni).

After you have received the precepts, you can be called a bhikshuni or bhikshuni. Currently, there are many novice monks who call themselves monks, have not yet received precepts but have already put on robes, and have a large assembly of monks as their entourage. There are people who pretend to be monks or nuns, do not receive precepts but still live with the Sangha; that is illegal. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that if bhikshus and bhikshunis, novices and novice nuns are eighteen years old, they should study the Dharma. Especially novice nuns, when they turn eighteen, must learn the six precepts[21] of Thuc Xa Ma Na. If you have not yet received the precepts, you can learn the sadhana of the precepts. Only when you reach the age of twenty can you receive the precepts. Currently, that is not the case, because there are many things that are not done according to the dharma. If you reach the age of twenty, follow the correct method of receiving precepts, and follow the correct method of learning precepts, then you will be considered a Bhikkhu and Bhikkhuni. If you do not receive the precepts, but still live with the Sangha, especially doing Buddhist work. “Buddhist work” as we say, is usually worship, they do not differentiate, just blend in with the Sangha. To do Buddhist work, there must be seven Bhikkhus, or Bhikkhunis; Because there weren't enough seven people, novice monks or novice nuns also participated in Buddhist activities there. That's illegal. We know this is okay. When you learn the precepts, that's okay, but if you say it in general, they won't accept our way of saying it. Because that is what the Buddha taught, according to the regulations in the precepts, you should do it like that, most people don't do it according to the precepts! Therefore, the Buddha called the present time the Dharma Ending, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also said that in the Dharma Ending period, do the same.

(Sutra) Although sentient beings study repentance, they are unable to be single-minded, unable to achieve good appearances, and set their lives on fire. thought, without name and attainment of world.
(Sutra: If those living beings learn to repent, but cannot mind, not attaining a good appearance, even if one has received precepts, is not called "attaining precepts").

During the Dharma-Ending Age, if you want to attain pure precepts, follow the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Here, we specialize in the method of repentance taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra. For those who study the method of repentance, the first requirement is that if you want to study the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, you must be sincere. If you do not attain the pure form of the wheel, but think that you have attained the precepts, it is wrong. Because we want to receive the novice or novice ordination, or want to receive the ordination as a bhikkhu or bhikkhunī without a teacher to transmit it, we can rely on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Contemplation and Contemplation to receive it; But it is necessary to achieve the pure form of the cycle. Not achieving the pure form of the wheel, just bowing and thinking that you have attained the precepts; like that, you won't attain the precepts!

“Not achieving a good appearance” (Not achieving a good appearance): Saying “I have achieved a good appearance”, how does one achieve a good appearance? If you worship, according to the method taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will definitely achieve purity in all three karmas. Therefore, pure repentance is called “good appearance”. When it comes to the universal form, there will be a clear distinction: "What is the universal form of achieving good form? What is not achieving good form?" very clear! If you do not attain that form, it is not called “ordaining”. Here, we specifically talk about whether or not monks or bhikshunis receive ordination. Like the monks and nuns who have received the three great precepts, when you sow the Samsattva form to see if I receive the three great precepts, is it significant or not? Nothing significant at all! One precept cannot be attained! [Because], it is not legal, not in accordance with the precepts. You rely on bowing to Chiem Sat Sam, I want to find a pure Bhikkhu, or pure Bhikkhuni, please base your decision on the wheel of Contemplation. Here we specialize in receiving precepts.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, keep pure faith Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asks Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat quote: "So the theory of the mind is different, there is a difference in the race? What is the ability of the mind to plan a good appearance?" Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat said: "Good man! The ego theory of one's mind is two-fold. One level two? One, initially learn to pray with one's mind. Two, one's mind is concentrated, achieving the corresponding strong mind. To test one's second mind, capable of planning good form. Try the second one's mind to subdue the lower, middle, upper three different types. One level, three? One, one mind. The system of thinking is not chaotic, the mind is not chaotic. The second person, the strong mind. So the person is dedicated to not solving the problem, not trying to save the life of the person. The person with the deep heart is corresponding with the method of salvation. If the weak person tries to repent, he will not be able to achieve the pure appearance of the second wheel.
(Sutra: At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva Bodhisattva said: "As mentioned above, there are many different types of determination. What kind of determination can one attain a good form?" Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat said: "Good man! As I said, there are two types of determination: One is the initial determination to pray. The other is the determination to concentrate, concentrate, and achieve strength. If you have the second type of determination, you will be able to attain the appearance of goodness. The second type of determination is There are three different types: lower, middle, and upper. What are the three? One is oneness of mind, that is, focusing on thinking without confusion, the mind is clear and focused. Second, the mind is strong, that is, dedicated to pursuit, not lazy, and does not care about the body and life. Third is the profound mind, that is, corresponding to the dharma, and ultimately not turning back. This is about contemplation of the second type of wheel.)

At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva Mahasattva asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva: "How many different types of determination are there as you said? Because of which type of determination, will one be able to achieve a good appearance?" Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: "When you want to bow to Chiem Sat Sam, you must have a sincere and earnest mind." Kien Tinh Bodhisattva immediately asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: "What is the sincere mind like you said? How many different types are there? How can it be considered a sincere mind? Only with a sincere mind can one achieve a good appearance, that is, a pure form. Then what is that sincere mind like? How can it be considered a sincere mind?" Kien Tinh Bodhisattva's request to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is to ask on our behalf: "Is there any difference in the sincere mind? How many types of sincere mind are there? How can it be considered sincere, to be able to see a good appearance? How can it be considered not sincere?" Please explain in detail about Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. That sincere mind, simply put, will be a pure thought, without impurities. We often say “sincerity and earnestness”, which means that in the mind of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva there is not a single stray thought! When you bow to Chiem Sat Sam, it's the same when you use the Contemplative Wheel, or you recite the Ksitigarbha sutra, you must recite it with sincerity and earnestness. If you are sincere, the effect will be much greater. If you are not sincere, you will have merit, but no wisdom! If you have wisdom, you will definitely be sincere. If you have merit, even if you are not sincere, if you keep reciting it, you can still reach your sincere heart.

King Tinh Bodhisattva asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to explain about the sincere mind. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat said: - Good man! Sincerity, as I said, there are two types of strategy.

What are the two types?

1) One is the sincere heart when first starting to study and pray. That is the first type of determination.

If you have these two types of mind, you will be able to achieve good form. At first, we must be sincere in our minds before we can learn. Don't we often say and think that we have sincere intentions? There is none! Because that mind is a mocking mind (a liking mind), not a sincere mind! I happily seek this Dharma. When you want to use the Contemplation Wheel General, there may be differences. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, "What is considered single-mindedness?", that is, when you use your mind, to what extent must you use it to be considered single-minded?

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva said: Pray, make your own vows, hope for satisfaction, pray wholeheartedly. Dedication corresponds to strong dedication to achievement, this is very difficult! We often say “praying single-mindedly”, which means capturing the scattered and turbulent mind so that it can control the mind in one place, calm down, and calmly worship in the penitentiary. Or calm your mind and calmly recite the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If you worship and pray like that, only then can you attain the pure appearance of the wheel, and only then can you be considered a person who worships [truly] praying for repentance. The second type of determination is very deep and must be matched with courage. The second type of will is divided again: What is considered truly strong will, and what is still not enough? Normally, after we enter the penitentiary, we hope for [purity of the three karmas]. The heart is hope, that is, the hope of achieving pure form. When we ask these questions, we hope Bodhisattva will be able to answer us truthfully. That is [the question] about the need to have determination.

Kien Tinh Bodhisattva feels that the two ultimate minds as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said are still vague, sentient beings cannot see clearly. Therefore, He earnestly requested: "What can be considered as having a sincere heart? What is considered as not having a single-minded mind?" Our praying heart is hope. We make a vow, hoping to use the Contemplation Wheel, the wheel will tell us how to do it? What is considered accurate? How is it incorrect? In general, we usually do three prostrations, then use the Contemplation Sat Luan to contemplate, or make a vow, but we still don't know how to concentrate and agree! Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: "You must have a sincere and urgent mind!" For example, when we enter the Buddha hall, bow three times, sit down, or start to worship, kneel down, you should put the external environment and other thoughts in your mind, let go of anything, without a single distracting thought. That is the will. I think that Dharma friends have the following phenomenon: I see many Dharma friends, when they come to the penitentiary to worship, after calming down, they are touched by good roots in the past. Discovered by good roots, he felt that the karma he had created in the past was very serious, so he became emotional, cried in pain, and worshiped. If there is a feeling, there will be a reaction, mutual feeling, just like when we invite a bell: If we don't invite the bell, the bell will not ring. As soon as you requested, the bell rang. You sincerely bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva like that, controlling your mind and bringing your mind back to one place. “Chuen” is not complicated, “chuan” is single-minded, just one night of repentance. Other ideas are completely cut off, non-existent! That is “pure” (pure). Pure to the point of maturity, one's mind is controlled, one is courageous and diligent. [That is] “diligence” (diligence).

If you don't know what your thoughts are during that time, I'll use an example to explain. After the things we eat and drink are digested in the stomach and intestines, the food residue will be excreted, [the body] absorbs the essence of nutrients and turns them into blood. The essence of the things you eat, forty drops of essence turns into one drop of blood. That blood is called “mixed blood” (mixed blood), not “pure blood” (pure blood). Forty drops of “mixed blood” turn into one drop of serum, that blood is pure. Usually, the blood that spurts out when a needle is inserted is mixed blood, not pure blood. Forty drops of pure blood turn into one drop of semen, forty drops of semen turn into divine energy. Saying someone is “very spirited”, where does that spirit come from? Because semen turns out. Say a person "spirit is very rich", the spirit is very full, in that transformation, at first, our mind is very excited, wait until you are quiet, reaching a pure mind. That pure mind successively went through the stage of "nothing of any trouble"; In that mind there is only Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, dwelling only in repentance. That is called “willedness”.

The first type of single-mindedness is to stay, stop distracting thoughts and delusions. The second type of will has a lower, middle, and upper mind:

- Summer Solstice means your thoughts are not chaotic, only this one thing, not disturbed by other things. Your own mind is clear and distinct. That is called “summer solstice”. Normally, we only use this type of determination, and we feel very determined, but not yet!

- The second type of single-mindedness is a brave mind, dedicated to seeking, not lazy, dedicated to seeking King Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, never having been idle before. This single-mindedness is even deeper, not caring about one's own life, even if one loses one's life, one's mind is not moved, specialized in reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva like that. This type is still not deep enough.

- The third type of mind is called the deep mind, that is, in the present moment, repenting of the dharma that you are bowing to, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva that you are reciting, as well as your mind combining with the dharma into one: The mind is the dharma, the dharma is the mind.

The first mind is an undisturbed mind, a clearly established mind. The second mind is brave and diligent, because of diligent pursuit and not laziness, rather than giving up one's life and life [not giving up practice]. The second type of ambition does not care about one's life or body. The third type of mind corresponds to the dharma, your mind and your worship combined with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva into one Body. We say: When we recite Amitābha Buddha with our minds, Amitābha Buddha is ourselves, we are Amitābha Buddha. Mind, Buddha, sentient beings, all three are no different!

When you practice the method of repentance, at least you must have a humble mind. You have not yet reached the point where you do not care about your life. Everything depends on that method of repentance. If you concentrate on one thought, using the Contemplation Wheel will be able to correspond. If you don't even have the will of a lower level, even if you worship every day, you bow for seven days and it still won't be effective. At least you have to reach your mind. We often say "I have one mind without chaos", but even a mind of the "one mind without chaos" type is still not a deep mind. If you don't study, you won't know. We say reciting Amitābha Buddha, reciting Amitābha Buddha in our hearts, but when we can reach the level of reciting Amitābha Buddha in our hearts, then we ourselves are Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha is us, because the mind and Amitābha Buddha are united. That is the true heart, truly reciting Amitābha Buddha.

The lower mind is that all impurities are absent, in the mind there is only Amitābha Buddha, reciting Amitābha Buddha. That is just the will of the lower level. As for reciting Amitābha Buddha to the point of not caring about one's life and life, letting go of one's entire body and mind; That is the second type of willpower. Reciting until the body and Buddha unite is the true depth of the mind. For example, when we worship and pray for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to appear, we think about our own crimes in the past, including all the crimes, suffering unjustly, and suffering all the persecution. Thinking about these things, while you bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will feel heartbroken and shed tears. Such determination is not enough, we must reach the level of “you are Ksitigarbha, Ksitigarbha is yourself”. “Earth” is the mind, one's own mind contains Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind includes us. Two minds merge into one. Earth is the great earth, Tang is the container, great earth contains all things. We ourselves are Ksitigarbha, Ksitigarbha is ourselves. The body that is worshiping and Ksitigarbha are united, that is the “deep mind”. While you are worshiping to the point of using your deep mind to worship, using the Contemplation Wheel will be corresponding. Having reached that level, there is no need to use the Contemplation Wheel anymore, [because], you see "all dharmas are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, like dew, like lightning", why still use the Contemplation Wheel? No need! But you must go through repentance to be able to reach that level, [that is] use the Contemplation Wheel to reach the point where you no longer need to use the Contemplation Wheel. That is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's request to us when we enter the repentance chamber, to be mindful and mindful, to abide in the third kind of single-mindedness. At the very least, you must clearly focus your mind, which means you must definitely achieve the first type of ambition. When you worship and repent, each sentence is clear, each word is clear, recite to the point of “without thought but reciting, reciting is without thought”, reaching the level of “the self is the other, the other is the self”. That is the true heart.

Think about it: Normally, when we recite Buddha's name, it's the same, we recite sutras, we practice any kind of power, can we reach this level of devotion? At the same time, you encounter the repentance method of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra and feel extremely victorious, because this is the real treasure, the supreme treasure. To speak a little more broadly, you believe in Buddha, believe in Buddha's teachings. The Buddha did not live in this world, the Buddha's teachings are scriptures. Even though the Buddha is not in this world, the Dharma Jewel is still there, the Dharma Jewel is the sutra. You can meet the dharma, meet this dharma, meet the Contemplation and Contemplation Dharma. You should consider it a priceless treasure, it will give birth to strength, you will give rise to strength. Now we see this Dharma Jewel, see this sutra, since the sutra was translated in China, absolutely no one has commented on it, and it has not been disseminated or propagated. In the Tripitaka, there are many things that correspond to us, but only if you browse the Tripitaka (see and read the Tripitaka) will you know, because no one preaches, no one talks, so you don't meet. There are people who hold scriptures and Dharma Jewels very casually, without taking them seriously at all! I see many Dharma friends holding sutras and waving them around, not knowing the serious nature of the Dharma Jewels, and not having the slightest bit of respect! Can you enter? If you don't even have the heart of a lower class, you don't even have the heart of reverence, how can you enter the Buddhadharma? Dear Dharma friends, we have worked hard to listen to this sutra. We do not dare to say that you do not have sincerity, but I feel that sincerity is not enough, because you do not know the nobility of the Dharma. Have you thought about this or not? Currently, printing technology is developing. Taking a book of scriptures, many copies can be printed at any time. Do you know how difficult it was to have scriptures [in the past]? I can tell you a little about this story.

In the past, during the Tang Dynasty, there were not many Indian masters who brought scriptures to China. Therefore, at that time, there were great monks who went to India to seek Dharma, such as Dharma Master Huyen Trang, Tripitaka Dharma Master Nghia Tinh, and Dharma Master Phap Hien, whom we all know, and they were successful. They were successful because they brought back many scriptures and translated many scriptures. There are also those who died on the way, even [having gone to India] returned [to China] without achieving anything, because they did not study any sutras. There are many such cases, one hundred people left, less than ten returned. At that time, going to pray for sutras was very difficult. From Truong An, it took several years to reach India. Currently, we have been on a plane for two or three hours to arrive, but even though you have arrived, the scriptures are no longer there! Now you go to India to look for scriptures, it's better to go to China to find scriptures, India no longer has scriptures, it's broken!

At that time, how difficult was it to request sutras? I simply introduce myself to everyone. Tripitaka Dharma Master Nghia Tinh has a poem that talks about the difficulty of requesting sutras. He said “Than, Song, Qi, Liang, Tang are great traitors” (during the Jin and Song dynasties[22], Qi, Liang, Tang), from the Jin dynasty until the Tang dynasty, there were many great monks who felt that there were not enough scriptures in the country (China) and had to go to India to request scriptures. “The monk sought the Dharma and left Chang'an” (The monk sought the Dharma and left the capital, Truong An), meaning that there were many people who made the effort to go to India to request sutras. “The past become hundreds, but return to the ten”: One hundred people leave, but less than ten return, even ten people return, can they translate? Does translation satisfy sentient beings?

Therefore, shaman Nghia Tinh lamented that: “In the Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, and Duong generations, high monks seek the dharma to leave Chang'an, the past causes become hundreds, return to the past, the later lives in peace, the former suffer hardships” (Tan, Song, Qi, Liang, Duong generations, high monks seek the dharma to leave Chang'an, hundred When a person leaves, not even ten have returned, the next person will not know the hardships of the previous person): The sages of future generations, the disciples who believe in Buddha hold the Buddhist scriptures, do they know where this sutra comes from? Do they know the hardships of the venerable monks requesting sutras? While asking for sutras, “lo vien bi thien wei lench cong” (long distance, blue sky, bitterly cold), passing through the desert, at noon it was like in the summer month, the early mornings and evenings were even colder than winter! That's why it's said “Lo Vien Bich Thien Duy Leng Cau”. You go to that place, right at the moment when the sandstorm is extremely big, the wind blows sand to cover the sun, "sa ha price of solar power" (flying sand covers the sun, your strength is exhausted). The body has no strength at all, is exhausted, so many people die on the road. “A later sage is like a monk” (People of later generations do not understand this): How do later people know how many difficulties the sages who requested sutras went through? "When you pass by, you despise the scriptures" (Usually look down on the scriptures), pick up the scriptures arbitrarily, don't value them, because you don't know where the scriptures came from!

I re-read this poem by Tripitaka Dharma Master Nghia Tinh again, hoping that everyone will always contemplate: “In Jin, Song, Qi, Luong, Tang great people, high monks pray for the Dharma to leave Truong An, past people become hundreds, return to ten. Later people know the past is difficult, the path is far away, the sky is only cold. In the past, the queen is as gentle as a monk, and in the past, she is awe-inspiring and contemptuous of the khan.". The Dharma friends of later generations do not understand [that hardship], and often easily ignore and despise the scriptures. How do they know how the ancients translated the scriptures? Furthermore, the translators at the ashram were thousands of people, and they were able to interpret the text. In order to improve the quality of the text, it is necessary to imitate each word to determine whether the word used matches the meaning [in the original Sanskrit text] or not, showing how difficult it is for the ashram to translate the sutras! Nowadays, when we look at the sutras, due to the development of printing technology, we can print as many copies as possible, so we hold the sutras and wave them around, without any reverence.

Therefore, there is very little enlightenment, little attainment of enlightenment, and even less attainment. Because you have to put your heart into it to be rewarded. You don't open your heart at all, you are arrogant and wish to become a Buddha, to attain enlightenment, to attain birth and death. Is it that easy? Karma from countless eons until now! Therefore, now that we have heard the Dharma, regarding the Dharma, we must definitely respect the Dharma. Now that we study this sutra, there are few people who use it!

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You must develop a determined mind. Not only for this dharma, but for any dharma you study, you must sincerely and earnestly enter into it to reap the benefits. Don't say that we study Buddhism, hope to become Buddha, hope to be born and die, look at the world: You hope to earn a few dollars, study from elementary school, high school, to university, to study graduate students, study a technical subject, learn skills to earn a living, so that you can eat a little better, make a little more money. You wish to end birth and death, learn Buddhism, and cut off the suffering caused by passing through countless lifetimes. That price is very high, how should you pay it? It's not something that can be achieved by a careless, arrogant mind! Let's see what the patriarchs accomplished in the past?

Speaking of enlightenment, everyone has heard "clear your mind, see your nature, cut down super directly, immediately attain Bodhi", so convenient! Zen subjects light a stick of incense, place a stick of incense and then meditate, immediately becoming enlightened. Everyone only saw it at that time, but that great monk of Zen Buddhism has been practicing for countless eons until now, you don't see it? Only see Him enlightened in the present! “Enlightenment” is just understanding. If as soon as he became enlightened he would become a Buddha, Śākyamuni Buddha would not receive the prediction. Everyone sees that there is only one successor to Śākyamuni Buddha, Maitreya Bodhisattva. In the past, when I was in Co Son, our Zen hall and school often argued and argued. The Zen hall says "when we become enlightened we become Buddhas", when will we become enlightened? They say: “Zen people light a stick of incense, the incense burns out and they become enlightened, cut down and enter, immediately attain Bodhi”. Is there such a thing as convenience? If it were that [easy], then [everyone] would become a Buddha, there would be no living beings left in this world! It's not like that! It's just that that person has been enlightened and understood. Do you know that he or she has practiced for countless lifetimes in the past? You only look at the moment, it's not good!

Therefore, our Dharma friends, when studying Buddhist scriptures, must respect the scriptures. You respect the Three Jewels, Buddha does not stay in the world, the Dharma Jewel is Buddha, you can treat the scriptures as Buddha, it will be much closer to "enlightenment, ending birth and death". You must be respectful, no matter which sutra. I see many Dharma friends reciting the Amitabha Sutra, waving and waving the Amitabha Sutra, without any reverence at all! So is it possible to be born in the Pure Land? I said decisively: "You don't respect the Amitabha Sutra, you recite the Buddha's name completely fake!" You must have a sincere heart.

(Sutra) Good man! The weak desire to contemplate the three worlds in the middle of life reports the wrong person, overcoming the wood and six wheels. U try the six wheels, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, ten one, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen equal numbers, the alphabet. The one number is the master of the three aspects, the second number is unfailing, is not disordered.
(Sutra: Good man! If you want to contemplate the difference in retribution in three lives, you should overcome Wood to make six wheels. For those six wheels, use the numbers one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen to write, each number is written on one side of the wheel [there are four sides], write the number on three sides, [the remaining side is left blank] so that the order of the numbers is not wrong or disordered.

Good man! If we want to observe the different retributions in the three lifetimes, we want to observe the past. As for the past, there is the past, present and future [of the past]; In the present, there is a past, present and future [of the present]; The future also has a present, a past and a future [of the future]. So three lives include nine lives, plus your basic ignorance, making ten lives. We often say “ten generations” (ten generations). To study the Contemplation Sutra of Good and Evil Karma, you must first know how to use the Contemplation Wheel. You carve the wood into six wheels. There are nineteen signs in all, [the first type is ten (corresponding to three karmas in the body, four karmas in the mouth, and three karmas in the mind), the second type includes three (corresponding to the body, speech, and mind). Here, Bodhisattva is talking about the third type of wheel consisting of six. First of all, for this third type of wheel, [the central part of each wheel] has four faces. Of those four sides, three sides have numbers written on them, one side is blank. One side is left blank with the meaning: That person has gone beyond numbers, no longer belongs to numbers. Of those six wheels, the first wheel engraves one, two, three, the next wheel engraves four, five, six, the next wheel engraves seven, eight, nine, the next wheel engraves ten, eleven, twelve, the next wheel engraves thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, the sixth wheel engraves sixteen, seventeen, eighteen. Why does each wheel leave one side blank? That side shows: When six wheels are sown at the same time and all come out blank, without a single word, it shows that the person has transcended the three realms, has achieved success, and can no longer use numbers to contemplate.

Because the wheel belongs to body, speech, and mind, there are three, because those numbers all belong to body, speech, and mind, combined together will be eighteen numbers. What do those eighteen numbers represent? Represents your six senses, six objects, and six consciousnesses. You use the Contemplation Wheel without leaving the six senses, the six senses, the six consciousnesses, three times six is ​​eighteen. When you create karma, whether you create good karma or bad karma, as long as you pay attention, you will not be separated from those eighteen things. If we want to ask the difference between good and evil in the past, present, and future, and ultimately whether it is good karma or bad karma, let's use those six wheels to contemplate. Just contemplating with this type of wheel will tell you whether the good karma in the past was heavy, or the bad karma was heavy, or the karma was not heavy. If it is not heavy, it will appear empty; The empty face represents karma that is not heavy. Add those numbers together, if they correspond to what you are thinking and your karma, if they correspond then it is appropriate. Because when we create karma, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, eye consciousness, ear consciousness, nose consciousness, tongue consciousness, body consciousness, consciousness, none of those eighteen items are lacking. If you separate from those eighteen items, you will have nothing. Why are there nineteen wheels? Because you have basic ignorance, those eighteen things all arise from basic ignorance.

(Sutra) Experiencing knowledge is like testing the numbers, the step by step is one number and the other arises, one is the origin. Such as the number of false appearances, showing that all sentient beings' six sense organs gather together, the stage of the Tathagatagarbha's self-nature is pure, the mind of the One True realm arises, the root of the One True realm is the basis. Based on the One Reality Realm of existence, ignorance, eternal ignorance, one dharma world, one's thoughts, false thoughts, one's present realm, one can distinguish one from the other. TIntegrate karma and cause and effect, the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are at the six sense bases. Based on the six internal roots, externally, sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma are equal to the six senses, giving rise to the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind are equal to the six consciousnesses. Because of the six consciousnesses, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, arising with perception, following perception, non-viable non-equivalent perception, giving rise to eighteen types of feelings.
(Sutra: You should know that such numbers all start from the number one, taking one as the root. General condition of Those numbers all show that the six senses of all sentient beings arise from the Tathagatagarbha's pure nature of mind in the realm of One True, relying on the realm of One True as the root. That is, because of relying on the realm of One True, there is ignorance, not understanding a dharma realm, thinking, thinking wrongly, appearing in a false realm, discriminating and holding on to it. Due to the causes and conditions of habitual karma, the six senses of eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are born inside, corresponding to the six senses, i.e. sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, and dharmas outside, six consciousnesses arise in the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Due to relying on the six consciousnesses, against sight, sound, scent, taste, touch, dharmas, arising thoughts that are contrary, thoughts that are favorable, thoughts that are neither favorable nor contrary, give birth to eighteen types of feelings.

You should know that such numbers all start from number one, one is the basis. Those dharma signs show the six senses of all living beings. Therefore, this sutra is also called “The Dharma Door of Roots Gathering”, because it is the Dharma door in which the six senses and six senses are gathered. Those six senses and six senses all arise from the pure nature of the mind, which is called the realm of One Truth, the appearance of the realm of One Truth. The second half [of this sutra] will explain the realm of One Truth. Because the One True realm is our basis, relying on the One True realm gives birth to ignorance. Because we do not know the nature of the Dharma Realm, do not clearly understand all of the Dharma Realms, we meditate, think wrongly, have false thoughts, and make false distinctions. Therefore, an illusory realm appears. Because of delusion, people take and give up. If it's good, you want to keep it, but don't let go of attachments. If you are bad, you don't want to get involved or do anything. That is called “great feeling karma”. Due to past causes and conditions of feeling, the six senses of eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are born. The inside is based on the six senses of eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, corresponding to the six sense objects, i.e. sight, sound, scent, taste, touch, and external dharma, while the Root corresponds to the Dust, giving birth to consciousness. Consciousness is differentiated, giving birth to six consciousnesses. If it suits your mind and follows your delusions, you will immediately enjoy it. That is called “favorable fate”. If it doesn't match your false thoughts, you'll be disgusted, but you can't leave it, that's called "vi-chan" (opposing fate). Until it is neither good nor evil, neither favorable nor contrary, changes arise. That's called Vo Ky. Vo Ky gives birth to changes, a total of eighteen things.

The reason this sutra is called the Root Gathering method is because the six senses, six objects, six consciousnesses gather together, plus the basis of ignorance. Again, the six senses are eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, six senses are sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, and dharma. The senses against the objects have no effect, but if in the middle there are six consciousnesses, namely Eye Consciousness, Ear Consciousness, Sick Consciousness, Tongue Consciousness, Body Consciousness, Consciousness, those six consciousnesses distinguish between the Senses and Objects. If you like it, you hope to achieve it, if you don't like it, you hope to abandon it. Wanting but not being able to achieve it, wanting to give it up but not being able to give it up are called “afflictions”. Therefore, the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma [teaches about this]. Because the karma you have created, whether it is good karma or bad karma, cannot be separated from those eighteen types. Therefore, those eighteen numbers, each number represents Can and Tran gathered. It also sparked a transformation, eighteen multiplied by ten generations, becoming one hundred and eighty. One hundred and eighty plus nine in the present life, [counting only] eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, [and the six consciousnesses], basic ignorance does not count, [multiplied by ten lives], plus the present, it becomes one hundred and eighty-nine types. The total number comes from adding it up like that. If you want to learn, I will use the wheel form as a detailed model for you, but when I explain the sutras, I can only say roughly that!

(Sutra) In the future, the Buddha's disciples, in the middle world, will experience the retribution, the desire to resolve doubts fake, eagle is in the third position, try the third cycle of generals, the prediction is compatible with the number. Contemplating the number of people determines good and evil. Such as contemplating the three worlds and the signs of good and evil retribution, including one hundred, eighty and ninety-nine species. Is it one hundred, eighty, ninety-nine races?
(Sutra: If the Buddha's disciples in the future, in the future, must suffer the retribution of three lifetimes, they wish to To eliminate doubts, you should cast this third type of wheel three times. Contemplate by combining the numbers you have planted to consider and determine the good and evil results in three lifetimes. What are the one hundred and eighty-nine types?

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: The Buddha's disciples in the future, that is, all the Buddha's disciples in the future. Why only talk about Buddhist disciples? The Root Gathering method is only used by Buddhist disciples. If a layperson sees this dharma as a form of divination to use, he will not be spiritual. We use it in “provision”, that is, when we are in retreat. Whoever uses the wheel to predict the lives of others, can they use it or not? If you use it [in that way], it won't be effective, hoping to make money won't do it! We monastics hope to make money, that is called “living without a life”, “hexagram” is not spiritual, nor does it appear, nor can it be accurate! We must understand: If we use contemplation of the wheel of appearance, we must know how to use Contemplation of the Wheel of Life. [If] someone else requests us, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva allows you to do it for someone else. Just do it for the benefit of living beings, don't make money. If you take money, it won't be flexible. When wanting to learn this dharma, [the teacher] must specifically say [clearly to the student: "This magic cannot be used as a divination game for profit"]. In the pulpit, there is no way to preach to everyone, to say it so that everyone understands clearly. You know the meaning of the one hundred and eighty-nine wheel signs!

In the future life, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: At the end of the Dharma, Buddha's disciples in the future life. He said it very clearly, he must be a disciple of Buddha! Buddha's disciples in the future will at least take refuge in the Three Jewels, including two lay assemblies and two monastic assemblies. As for the retribution in the past, present, and future, whatever the body suffers in the present, what it has to suffer is retribution. Don't you know the reason why our bodies are not as healthy as this? We have a friend whose body is very sick and his body is not healthy: "You ask why? In the past, your killing karma was very heavy." Your body is very healthy, but you can't study and have no wisdom. Do you also ask why? In the past, you created a lot of karma, and in this life you have no wisdom. Sowing the wheel of signs, [to seek to know yourself] what karma have you created in the end? That is, regarding the body, speech, and mind, which aspects are heavy? That is the focus of your repentance. You cast the wheel form, observing the total number of numbers appearing in the six wheel signs [of this third type]. After observing, you will clearly know your good and evil. There are many stories of this type. Unfortunately, that person doesn't know how to use the wheel, so he can't contemplate!

During the Tang Dynasty, at the Dai Hoa Nghiem Pagoda in Wutai Mountain, there was a master whose nickname was Niu Si Zen Master. Why is it called Niu Si (buffalo)? Everyone cursed him for being like a buffalo, because his mind was not clear, he could only cook for the masses, do heavy work, and do labor. Studying the Dharma, whether reciting Buddha's name, studying sutras, or praying, all of it cannot enter your mind. Not just ordinary stupidity, but absolute stupidity! Therefore, he felt ashamed, followed the mountain, worshiped the five peaks of Ngu Dai, hoping to meet Manjushri Bodhisattva [to ask]: Why is it that everyone who studies will understand a little, and after studying they will have success, but why can't he? When he paid homage to Ngu Dai, he met an old man herding buffaloes. This old man is the incarnation of Manjushri Bodhisattva. The old man said to him: "Master! I saw you wandering around for a long time on the mountain, what are you doing?" He said: "I hope to meet Bodhisattva Manjushri." The old man said: "What do you want to see Manjushri Bodhisattva for?" He said: "Everyone calls me a buffalo, saying I'm too stupid! What karma have I created?" At that time, he realized that this was the present Manjushri Bodhisattva. He immediately knelt before Manjushri Bodhisattva and insisted on asking Bodhisattva to save him. Manjushri Bodhisattva said: “Do you want to know your own karma?” Manjushri Bodhisattva immediately put the ring on the robe he was wearing, put it in his mouth, probed, and pulled out his heart: "Do you see that your heart is the heart of a buffalo? People call you Niu Si, right? In the past, you were a Dharma master who preached the Dharma, on the Dharma throne cursing the monks who listened to the sutras for being like buffaloes. It has been five hundred lives since the fall, forever and ever [to be punished like that]. Even though you have become a monk in this life, but due to the You have no wisdom in that mind. Now that you have repented, I will change your heart for you. As soon as he changed, he immediately began to be able to preach sutras to the monks. People gave him the nickname "Nuu Si Shaman", in history there was such a fate.

Saying one wrong sentence, scolding another person, all have cause and effect, you hope nothing happens, it doesn't! Especially as disciples of the Three Jewels studying the Dharma, you must pay special attention to every word and every action. Talking casually, creating karma but still not knowing. If we want to know the retribution we are suffering in the present [due to what cause], is it possible that every Bodhisattva Manjushri can tell you that? Can't meet you anywhere! Then meet Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, meet the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. You use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will tell you, there is no need to visit the mountains (to worship famous mountains and holy places). It's okay for you to sit in your house and pray. As soon as you sow, from among the one hundred and eighty-nine varieties, you can [know]. Wait until we explain the names and appearances of those one hundred eighty-nine things, you will know.

There are one hundred eighty-nine types, why only mention this number? Why are there one hundred eighty-nine types? You just need to rely on the three karma of body, mouth, and mind, plus the basic afflictions to become ten, ten multiplied by ten. That is, [three karmas] multiplied by three lives, plus one fundamental ignorance, becomes ten. Three times six is ​​eighteen karma in the present. [Those eighteen karma] are the six senses, six objects, six consciousnesses, those three types, [each type has six items], three times six makes eighteen. Eighteen multiplied by ten [karma just mentioned above] becomes one hundred eighty, plus the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind and body, speech, and mind in the present (which are nine items), becomes one hundred eighty-nine.

[To contemplate] this number, you must [plant all six wheels of this third type] three times. When casting the wheel, use the number from the sixth wheel and roll three times to get the number one hundred and eighty-nine. [The numbers in] the first wheel are one, two, three, until the sixth wheel is sixteen, seventeen, eighteen. Adding up the numbers from the three tosses, the largest number (total) will be one hundred and eighty-nine. [The reason] sowing three times is because of three generations of predestined relationships, so one must sow three times. If you roll three times [and all the wheels face up] all of them do not appear, that is, all the wheels appear blank, that is, the eighteen numbers (there are six wheels, each wheel has three numbers) do not appear, all are blank (the side without numbers), you have attained enlightenment, no longer belong to the numbers; But when you reach that level, you cannot use the Contemplation Wheel.

Because when you cast those numbers, while you use the Contemplation Wheel, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will definitely appear. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva shows money so each time you sow will be accurate. You bow one seven times (seven days), two seven days (fourteen days), but you sow the wrong number [of wheel signs], that is, what you think in your mind and the number that appears [in the wheel signs] as well as what is said in the Contemplation Sutra are not compatible, that is called “illusion”. So how to do it? Bow again, sow again. One day does not correspond, two days do not correspond, sometimes seven days, fourteen days still do not correspond. Why? Our karma is too heavy. First, you must bow for fourteen or twenty-one days to eliminate karma before sowing again. It's just that if it corresponds, it will correspond every day. You sow early in the morning every day, early in the morning every day accordingly.

In those one hundred eighty-nine numbers, each number has its own meaning. Below, we will read one hundred eighty-nine of those numbers.

(Sutra) The One, praying to the Upper Vehicle, attains no retreat.
(Sutra: One is that the Thuong Thua bridge can never fall).

Praying for the Supreme Vehicle to attain Non-Regression is number One. When you use the six wheel forms [of the third type] to sow, and sow three times, only the number one appears. What is that number one? If you pray for the Upper Vehicle, you will be able to achieve perfect fruition. In each of the six wheels, three sides have writing [representing a number from one to eighteen], one side is blank. Those six wheels were rolled three times, two times all the numbers were white, one time five rolls were all white, and one wheel came out number one. There are so many numbers in the wheel of the wheel, if you roll three times you will only get one. If Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not come, or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's guardian spirit does not come, you will not be able to sow. That is praying to the Upper Vehicle, because we develop the Bodhi mind to benefit sentient beings. To put it more easily, it is “seeking the Upper Vehicle, attaining Non-regression”. According to the Avatamsaka Sutra, the First Stage Bodhisattva, while in the Mahayana sutras, only those who have entered the Seven Grounds Bodhisattva can be said to be “non-regressing”, as well as the Second Vehicle who have attained Arhatship can be called “non-regressive”.

(Sutra) The second person, the desire for fruit is present.
(Sutra: Second, in the present you will realize the desired fruit).

Number Two [represents] what will achieve the desired result in the present. That is not praying to be born in the Pure Land. At present, I wish for achievement, attainment, attainment of enlightenment, which means all afflictions are cut off, thoughts and thoughts are cut off, and afflictions are cut off. This fruition is not certain, either you seek the First Fruition, the Second Fruition, the Three Fruition, or the Four Fruition, or you pray for the Bodhisattva Vehicle. Numbers one and two are roughly Mahayana.

(Sutra) Three falsehoods, praying to the Middle Vehicle to attain irreversibility.
(Sutra: Thirdly, if you seek the Middle Way, you will gain non-regression).

The number Three is because the person holds the wheel signs of this type and casts them three times, showing the number Three, [representing] the middle vehicle to attain Non-Regression. Middle Vehicle is Pratyekabuddha. The name Second Vehicle is a combination of the two primary and secondary vehicles. Middle Vehicle is Pratyekabuddha, Lesser Vehicle is Sravaka, Mahayana is Bodhisattva, forming Small, Middle, and Great in teachings.

(Sutra) The Four Noble Ones, praying to the Lower Vehicle, one can not retreat.

The number Four is the bridge to attain the lower inheritance and not retreat. The Lower Vehicle includes humans and heaven. If you want to be born in heaven, in Buddhism, wishing to be born in heaven is very easy! If you do a little good karma, if the good karma is accomplished, the retribution is that you can be born in heaven, have wealth in the next life, or be rich in the next life. [Enjoying good karma] in the human world is quite easy, but achieving the result will be difficult. The Lower Thua Bridge can be irreversible. First of all, in the one hundred and eighty-nine types of rotation, we cast three times, and only the number Four appears is not easy. If it were not for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, [that number] absolutely would not appear to you. Everyone has heard the sutra, but don't they expect to be able to use it immediately after using the Contemplation Wheel? I see very few people using it, but when you use it, you must understand: "We must have a pure and steadfast faith." It is only by relying on Faith that we can achieve success. Without that faith, those things cannot be accomplished. Why? Not achieved. You cannot achieve anything. Praying for the Lower Vehicle to attain Non-Regression, includes the story of us praying for blessings in heaven and earth.

(Sutra) Five false beings, pray for miracles to achieve achievements.
(Sutra: Five is to pray for miraculous powers to be achieved).

(Sutra) Six practitioners, cultivating the four dharmas and attaining achievements.
(Sutra: Sixth, cultivating the four types of holy conduct is achieved).

This purity is easy, Brahma is pure; But here there is another meaning involved, what does it imply? Purity is not Brahma in Brahma, it includes the meaning of cultivating the Four Brahma Virtues and then achieving it. The Four Pham Hanh are pure holy conduct. What is pure virtue? The Four Immeasurable Minds, i.e. love, compassion, joy, equanimity, are the four immeasurables. “Pham” represents purity, which means cultivating compassion, compassion, joy, and accomplishment. The mind is always complete with the four immeasurable thoughts of love, compassion, joy, and equanimity.

(Sutra) Seven practitioners, cultivating the Zen posture, attain achievement.
(Sutra: Seven is the practice of Zen and the world will be achieved).

(Sutra) The eight falsehoods, the desire to attain the wonderful world.
responsibility).

You worship, the purpose of worship is to achieve the universal form [purity]. When you attain the form of the wheel, you will attain the form of the physical world. When we seek precepts, if we do not attain the precepts, we use repentance to seek precepts and ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to transmit the precepts. “Destination” means we seek precepts, hope to attain precepts, and attain precepts. “Achieving the wonderful precepts” means having attained the precepts.

(Sūtra) Nine practitioners, able to attain full precepts.
(Sutra: Ninth is to attain complete precepts where the precepts have been received).

“Having received the precepts” (Having received the precepts) means that in the past, you have received the Five Precepts, the Eight Precepts, the Bodhisattva Precepts, or the Bhikkhu Precepts, the Bhikkhuni Precepts, the Novice Precepts, the Samaritan Precepts. You worship with the intention of attaining the precepts, the wheel of the wheel [will appear] showing that you have attained the precepts. If you attain purity, the wheel of the wheel will show the number nine, [that is] you roll three times, the numbers added together will be nine. It must be [the sum of the] numbers from the three casts, the number that appears in one hundred and eighty-nine cases is nine. You roll three times, the other sides are empty, adding [the numbers from the sides with the numbers shown] will be nine, then it is correct (corresponding) in this case.

(Sutra) Ten disciples, pray to the Supreme Being to maintain faith.
(Sutra: Ten is the bridge to the Upper Vehicle, but not yet established in faith).

If I seek the Dharma of the Upper Vehicle, I can only pray to gain faith in my mind. To abide in faith means faith is achieved.

(Sutra) The 10 greatest practitioners, praying for the position of faith in the Middle Vehicle. Twelve people, seek the trust of Ha Thua.
faith).

Now your faith is still not achieved, you still continue to practice. Regardless of whether we practice the Hinayana, Middle Vehicle, Mahayana, Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha, or Bodhisattva dharma, you still do not have achievements, the wheel of rotation will tell you that you have not achieved success. When you ask "have I attained the precepts", or "have I succeeded in cultivating or not", the wheel form will tell you "have not yet succeeded in cultivating!"

(Sutra) Thirteen falsehoods, contemplating the cause of good existence.
(Sutra: Thirteen: The person who is contemplated is a good friend).

That person wants to be friends with me, is he a good person or a bad person? Can I make friends with that person? You cast the wheel, add the numbers from the three casts to make the number thirteen, [indicating] that you observe that person as a good friend, a good person, a good person.

(Sutra) The Fourteen Authors, depending on the literature and Dharma.
(Sutra: Fourteen: What is heard is true law).

What you hear or see others say is all true Dharma, not wrong!

(Sutra) The fifteen falsehoods, contemplating the causes of evil.
(Sutra: Fifteen: Those who are contemplated are evil friends).

This is to see if we should make friends with that person or not? If you are a good friend, you can make friends. If [from contemplation of the wheel's appearance, the wheel's appearance says] that person is a bad person, you should not be friends with that person. If you want to make friends with someone, use the Contemplation Wheel to cast the wheel of the wheel and see if Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us whether we should make friends with that person or not? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that if that person is a good person, he can make friends. If you say that person is a bad person, you should not associate with them.

(Sutra) Sixteen fakes, depending on the non-Orthodox text.
(Sutra: Sixteen: What is heard is not the true teaching).

If you listen to people preach sutras, is there a place where sutras are preached that you want to listen to. First of all, please observe for a moment. [Luan Minister said] what that person preaches is not the true Dharma. What you hear is not the right teachings, what you hear that person say is not the right dharma.

(Sutra) The Seventeen Noble Ones, the meditation on human beings is truly virtuous.
(Sutra: Seventeen: The person who is contemplated has true virtue).

You see that person's appearance is not bright, nor is his appearance good. Then you sow the Contemplation Wheel a little. [Luan Xiang says] that person has true virtue; Virtue is not external, but internal. Contemplating that person has real virtue, that is, the heart contains virtue. We often say “inner penetration” (from the inside to the outside, meaning inner beauty).

(Sutra) Eighteen falsehoods, contemplation of causes without real virtue.
(Sutra: Eighteen: The person who is contemplated has no real virtue).

That person is not truly virtuous, but is not a bad person, that is

that person is not virtuous enough.

(Sutra) The ten sages, the contemplation of the meaning is not harmful. The two ten people, the place of contemplation means thi tao mau.
(Sutra: Nineteen: Contemplation of meaning is without error. Twenty: Contemplation of meaning is error. mistake).

Is the teachings stated in this sutra, or in this treatise, correct or incorrect? If there is no mistake then it is correct. The meaning that is contemplated is wrong. You see a book, you don't know, you can't judge whether what the book says is true or not? Then you should plant the Contemplation Wheel, [the wheel of the wheel] will let you know.

(Sūtra) The two twelve truths, the possession of the Buddha's teachings does not disappoint. Twenty-two people, all chanting and worshiping.
(Sutra: Twenty-one: What is recited is not wrong. Two twenty-two: What is recited is wrong).

This doesn't need to be explained, because everyone can understand.

(Sutra) Twenty-three fakes, the practice is not to be disappointed.
(Sutra: Twenty-three: Cultivation is not wrong).

The first thing is to recite; And this is practicing religion. Is it right to practice, or when you practice Concentration? If you cultivate Concentration and are afraid of following wrong concentration or going on the wrong path, use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate for a moment. If you don't make mistakes, you can continue to practice.

(Sutra) The twenty-four fakes, the knowledge of writing and showing good appearance. Twenty-five falsehoods, proven to be true.
(Sutra: Twenty-four: What is seen and heard is a good sign. Twenty-five: What has been witnessed is genuine).

This is what you have realized without realizing it, or having cut off afflictions, or broken habits, until you think you seem to have enlightenment, or understand clearly, then ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to confirm it for you.

(Sutra) Twenty-six fakes, possessing the knowledge of tao mau.
(Sutra: Twenty-six: What has been learned is wrong).

If you study that incorrectly, you should not study it!

(Sutra) Twenty-seven fakes, the knowledge of writing is not good.
(Sutra: Twenty-seven: What is seen and heard is not a good sign).

What is seen and heard is not a good appearance. This includes when you dream and see the Bodhisattva appearing! Either dream of Avalokiteśvara, dream of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or dream of Amitābha Buddha. You then cast the hexagram, [the reincarnation] will tell you that it is not a good appearance, but a demonic karma.

(Sutra) Twenty-eight false, possessing evidence that is not legitimate.
(Sutra: Twenty-eight: There are things that have been attained that are not true Dharma).

(Sutra) Twenty-nine practitioners, possessing plans of evil gods.
(Sutra: Twenty-nine: There are things achieved due to the protection of evil spirits).

If you feel there is Dharma protection, sow the Contemplation Wheel. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: These are evil gods, not true gods, you must cut them off.

(Sutra) Three dozen wise men, the ability to teach evil and wisdom.
(Sutra: Thirty: What can be said is argued by evil minds).

There are people who speak very well and explain many things. You ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, is he truly wise or not? He will teach: That is not true wisdom, but wrong knowledge and wrong views. He teaches you not to get too close.

(Sutra) The Three Noble Truths, non-human mystical knowledge.
(Sutra: Thirty-one: Knowing miracles is not a matter of strength people).

“Huyen” means “wonderful appearance”, or miraculous story. To say that a person does something magical, “magical” seems inconceivable. Magical phenomena cannot be achieved by human strength, but sometimes by the blessing of evil spirits. Regarding the magical story [represented by this number], it is known that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas bless it, because compared to the scriptures in the previous section, it is said: "The knowledge and writings are not good signs" (What is seen and heard is not a good sign).

(Sutra) The thirty-two sages, according to the immortal practice of wisdom.
(Sutra: Thirty-two: You should first practice contemplation of wisdom).

While you practice, it's good to not know what your own inborn ability is. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva immediately tells you: First of all, learn to visualize, that is, contemplate the path of wisdom, because you visualize, you will generate wisdom. “Dao” here refers to the Bodhi path. Because you visualize, you can enter the path, develop the Bodhi mind, and practice the Bodhisattva path.

(Sutra) Thirty-three falsehoods, following the practice of Zen meditation.
(Sutra: Thirty-three: You should first practice Meditation).

For your foundation and situation, practice whatever is right. [Place the wheel of the wheel, this number will appear, that is] Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches you to practice Meditation first. But friends who practice Zen meditation sometimes have to "train their thighs" first, that is, practice cross-legged sitting in the lotus position. It is not necessary to do that! When practicing Meditation, there are two types, one is sitting, the other is action. Meditation in action is Dynamic. You recite sutras the same way, because you do all the Buddha's things the same way, you can enter Samadhi. But the first thing is to regulate the body, then the mind. Once you have controlled your body and mind, you can practice Concentration. There are many methods of body conditioning, depending on which method you find most suitable.

Speaking of “meditation” (still sitting), your body must sit so that it does not bend forward, does not lean back, and must sit upright. Here, I don't need to elaborate on this. When you want to learn Meditation, you must first practice, and gradually you will be able to meditate. Or while explaining, you can also enter concentration; or while acting, it is also possible to enter concentration. But in this country, [to practice Meditation] our bodies should sit still. Only by sitting still will your mind be able to respond. For us, being still in the midst of movement is not easy! Be still to practice Concentration.

(Sutra) Thirty-four falsehoods, the practice of learning without obstacles.
(Sutra: Thirty-four: Contemplating what has been learned without hindrance).

If you want to learn a method, but you cannot decide whether it is right or not, you should use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate a little. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will teach you. He said you can learn without obstacles, you can achieve, you will learn.

(Sutra) The thirty-five hypocrites, the place of study, the place of comfort. The thirty-six scholars, contemplation of learning and non-questioning.
(Sutra: Thirty-five: Contemplation of what has been learned is appropriate. Thirty-six: Contemplating what has been learned is not appropriate).

Is what you learn appropriate [fundamental] or not? [Contemplation of Sat Luan] will let you know whether it is suitable or not. If it's not suitable, you don't need to study. If it is appropriate, you can gain benefits, you can advance, you should learn.

(Sutra) Thirty-seven scholars, the place of learning and gathering. Thirty-eight scholars, the school's non-resident study hall.
(Sutra: Thirty-seven: Contemplation learned is the dharma practiced from thirty-eight: Contemplate that what is learned is not a dharma practiced in a previous life).

Observe what you learn, because in the past, you have studied, [now], as soon as you learn, you will immediately enter. That is something that has been learned in previous lives. If what you learn has never been learned in the past, it will be very strange. Therefore, while you are studying, you do not know whether I have ever studied that method or not. Similarly, it seems like you have learned it, but it seems like you have never learned it. All of us who become monks have that feeling. You feel that in the past you yourself became a monk, in your previous life you became a monk, and now you have that feeling. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, it will tell you that in your past life you were a monk, so in this life you will be able to enter.

(Sutra) The thirty-nine practitioners, the practice of good learning increases.
(Sutra: Thirty-nine: Contemplation of learned things will increase good things).

Consider that if you study [that dharma, you will] be able to grow, [that is] increase your good roots, increase your virtue.

(Sutra) The Four Crosses, the study of the least means. Forty-one people, the school of learning without tons of beasts.
(Sutra: Forty: Contemplation learned is a small means. Forty-one: Contemplation is learned and not entered.)

Contemplating what you have learned, the means are few, [that is] you studying this method do not have enough skillful means. Without skillful means, you cannot enter, or enter with great difficulty. If we learn the precepts, you sow that morality, then you must first learn it. To uphold the precepts, you first need to know “declare, value, uphold, violate”. Each precept has many opening conditions. Regardless of the precepts, there will be eight conditions, or six conditions, or ten conditions. When we encounter obstacles when maintaining the precepts, what should we do? The Buddha has several types of precepts that do not violate the precepts. Each precept has [types of precepts]. If you have seen Master Hoang Nhat's Code of Precepts, you have not read the full text of the precepts, only seen the Code of Precepts, then you can understand what "declare, judge, uphold, violate".

(Sutra) The forty-two falsehoods, the attainment of attainment of fruition.
(Sutra: Forty-two: Haven't achieved the desired result in the present).

When we practice, we hope to attain enlightenment, even though we have not yet achieved it, in the future, you will be able to achieve it. Don't give up, just persevere. If you practice this method but cannot achieve it at present, and will not be able to achieve it in the future, why are you still studying it? You can let go of that dharma, no need to study anymore!

(Sutra) The forty-three falsehoods, the request for renunciation is now attained.
(Sutra: Forty-three: Pray for renunciation, you will become a monk).

I was planning to aspire to become a monk, so I asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to teach me whether it is possible to become a monk successfully or not? [Luan General] said "If you pray to become a monk, you will get it", you should become a monk! If you pray, you can pray!

(Sutra) The Fourteen Noble Phantasms, seek the Dharma to obtain teachings.
(Sutra: Forty-four: Seeking to hear the Dharma will be taught).

(Sutra) The forty-five practitioners, pray for the sutra book to be able to recite.
(Sutra: Forty-five: May the scriptures be recited).

Can obtain chanting, can obtain scriptures.

(Sutra) The Sixty-Six Phantasms, contemplating the actions of demons.
(Sutra: Forty-six: Contemplation of work is evil).

Don't do it, you do it that has nothing to do with your own practice, it has nothing to do with it, you're doing it wrong. You should not do it, if you do it will cause demonic obstacles.

(Sutra) The forty-seven practitioners, contemplating the accomplishment. Forty-eight falsehoods, contemplation of actions fails. Forty-nine people, pray for great wealth and prosperity.
(Sutra: Forty-seven: Contemplation of doing achievements. Forty-eight: Contemplation of doing nothing Forty-nine: Pray for great wealth and it will be filled.

The demand for great wealth was filled. This is speaking from the side of lay friends. If you wish to get rich, if you cast this number, you will be able to get rich.

(Sutra) The five-crossers, praying to officials, are achieving success. Five-ten first-class people, pray for a long life to attain a thousand years. Fifty-two people, praying to the world's immortals, are destined to achieve success.
(Sutra: Fifty: Pray for officials will be achieved. Fifty-one: Pray for longevity, will be increased in age life. Fifty-two: If you pray to become a fairy in this world, you will achieve it).

Praying for an official will be achieved, praying for longevity will be increased, praying for immortality in this world will be achieved. Studying Taoism, cultivating immortals, studying Qigong, when you study those things, use the Contemplation Wheel to contemplate, [the wheel of the wheel] will tell you that you can succeed, but [achieving those things] will not be able to put an end to birth and death, you can only achieve wealth in the world.

(Sutra) Fake fifty-three, the school has many achievements. The fifty-four scholars, contemplation of little attainment of education. If you pray to a master, you will get your wish. Fifty-six scholars, pray for the disciples to get their wish. Fifty-seven people pray for their parents to get their wish. Fifty-eight fake people, pray for men and women to get their wish. Fifty-nine men, praying for wives and concubines, get their wish. Sixty people, pray for companions to get your wish.
(Sutra: Fifty-three: Contemplation of much education. Fifty-four: Contemplation of education Fifty-five: Pray for your teacher and friend. Fifty-six: Pray for your disciple. Fifty-seven: Pray for your son, daughter, and concubine. Sixty: Pray for your friend.

Can satisfy your desire to seek spiritual education. Pray for your disciples to have their wishes fulfilled, pray for your parents to have your wishes fulfilled, pray for your sons and daughters to have their wishes fulfilled, pray for your spouse to have your wishes fulfilled, pray for your companions to have their wishes fulfilled.

(Sutra) The Sixty Ones, contemplating the attainment of harmony.
(Sutra: Sixty-one: Contemplation sees that the worries are fulfilled).

okay, very worried. [Luan General] said: You can do that, you don't need to worry, you can get along (ie the result will be according to your wishes).

(Sutra) Sixty-two falsehoods, the basis of contemplating human thoughts and thoughts.
(Sutra: Sixty-two: The person receiving the contemplation holds anger [towards me]).

You see that person seems uncomfortable, you observe [to know] why? [Luan General] says that person is very angry with you, you should not anger that person anymore. If you make him angry, he may take revenge and distance himself from that person a little.

(Sutra) Sixty-three fakes, pray for freedom from hatred and joy. Sixty-four people pray for harmony and get their wish.
(Sutra: Sixty-three: Pray without hatred, receive joy. Sixty-four: Pray harmonize as desired).

Consider the relationship between that person and us. I, you, others, humans are inseparable from the relationship “I, you, others”. Without anger, such a person can interact, and joy can arise on both sides. Those who harbor anger towards you will not be able to come to terms with you. That person is dissatisfied with you, if you stay close to that person, that person will retaliate. This shows that we interact with others, asking Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva whether or not Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can interact. This is to tell you about the relationships between people.

(Sutra) Sixty-five false figures, contemplating the joy of the human heart. Sixty-six people, the private department had a meeting. Sixty-seven people, the private department does not respond.
(Sutra: Sixty-five: Joy in the human mind. Sixty-six: Seeing the person I think of. Sixty-seven: The person I think of if I don't see him again).

“We won't see you anymore” is because that person is no longer in this world, or that person has lost their relationship with you!

Sixty-nine people, so monk o dac ly chi. Those who love and respect those who love and respect them gain access.
(Sutra: Sixty-eight: Those who are invited will come. Sixty-nine: Far away leave the person we hate. Seventy: Be close to the person we love and respect).

“The reason why you can invite a guest” is that you want to invite guests, you observe to see if you can invite them or not. Stay away from the person you hate, be close to the person you love and respect.

achieve harmony. Seventy-two people, contemplation of desires, gathering of disharmony.
(Kinh: Seventy-one: Shop, those who want to gather will gather. Seventy-two: Shop People who wanted to gather did not come.)

“Duc gather” (Want to gather) is to pray for wife and children, to pray for friends, to pray for six relatives to be able to gather together. Again, the people we want to gather cannot gather, cannot come, cannot gather together!

(Sutra) Seventy-three falsehoods, sometimes they cannot return. Seventy-four people, all the people will be determined.
(Sutra: Seventy-three: He who was called did not come. Seventy-four: He whom I expect it will come).

If you invite people, either because they don't have time, or because they don't want to come, you shouldn't invite them anymore. These numbers are meant to warn you that the person you invited will not come, and you don't need to invite anymore. The person you invite will come immediately, you don't have to wait. These are all times when you are in a hurry or are skeptical or impatient but can't invite someone, so you wonder if [the person you're expecting] will come or not? [Lan General] says "you can come", then you wait a little longer. If [Lan General] says "the person you invited cannot come", you don't need to wait anymore, they won't come!

(Sutra) The seventy-five falsehoods, all the causes of the future are eternal.
(Sutra: Seventy-five: The person we long to stay, will not come).

The person we expect cannot come.

These one hundred eighty-nine types are exactly what Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also told us. People who learn the Contemplation of Forms Dharma want to use it spiritually, no matter how big or small, they must go to the Buddha Hall to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, offer incense, pay respects three times, and plant the wheel of signs to request Bodhisattva's advice. It's not that if you worship every day [then you can use it right away], but until you complete your repentance, then use this method of Contemplation of the Wheel of Appearance, every time you use it, it's spiritual.
