[Preaching at the ashram] before...
noi_dung:
Lecture 9

When talking about “habits”, I refer to my habits, because when I went to class at the Buddhist Academy, I had the habit of taking textbooks and going to the front of the class to lecture, not in the habit of doing rituals [requesting a shaman, asking for help]. [Preaching the Dharma at the ashram], before ascending to the throne, this ritual must be performed. Over the years, I have roughly been lecturing the sutras for more than ten years. Because I only preached the sutras at the Buddhist Institute, I just took the book to the lecture hall and preached, without doing any Buddhist work, because I didn't have time. Habits are created like that, the power of habits! Now we learn Cham Luan Contemplation because we want to change the power of habit. The power of habit is birth and death, not birth and death. We must change the habit of birth and death into non-birth and death.

Numbers appear because of the desire to know something in our hearts. You want to invite someone, but you can't. Invite or call someone, but he does not come. But you hope that person will come, you are waiting impatiently, go to the Buddha hall and ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, "I invite that person, will he be able to come or not?" Here, there are some numbers; For example, starting from number seventy-three, you want to invite someone but he cannot come, or you want to invite someone, he can come. It may come, but it hasn't arrived yet. Number seventy-five is to invite someone who can stay at your place, [that person] accepts the invitation to stay at your place. You invite people, but they cannot stay at your place, but somewhere else. That number tells us: We want to invite someone who has a great relationship with us and can solve the problem, so you are very impatient. Then you ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, ask Ksitigarbha for help. You definitely want to invite that person, but he won't come. You then bow and repent, hoping that the Bodhisattva will bless you, that person will be moved and will be able to come!

(Sutra) Seventy-six fakes, the place of contemplation brings peace and happiness. Seventy-seven fake people, the place of contemplating people is insecure and auspicious.
(Sutra: Seventy-six: People who receive peace and goodness. Seventy-seven: People being contemplated is not peaceful or good).

Your relative is currently having problems and is not at peace or well. You can contemplate and ask questions. [Luan General] will tell you: The person being contemplated (ie the person being asked about the situation through the Universal General) is peaceful and good, there is no need to worry! Or tell you: The person you contemplate is not peaceful, good, not okay!

(Sutra) The seventy-eight falsehoods, the contemplation of the origin of the bodyless cause.
(Sutra: Seventy-eight: The person who has been contemplated has no longer a body).

The person you meditate on no longer has a body. Simply put, dead. There is another case where the person you contemplate has attained enlightenment. Once you have attained enlightenment, you will not have a body. Having cut off afflictions and attained the Truth of Emptiness, there is no more. Even though there is a body, it is like not having a body. For example, at Ngu Dai Mountain, a little devil wanted to capture a monk. That little ghost went to the mountain to look for that monk but couldn't find him, couldn't find him, so he asked the local people there: "This master was originally here, why isn't he present?" The earth native said: "He is entering Samadhi." This shows that: When you practice the Way, when you enter Concentration, ghosts and spirits do not see you, you feel empty. If anyone truly attains Emptiness, even though there is a physical body, ghosts and gods cannot see it, as if they did not exist. So you contemplate and see that that person does not have a body. In the case of death and cremation, there is no body.

(Sutra) The seventy-nine falsehoods, the wish to gain false knowledge. Eighty people, what do you want to see?
(Sutra: Seventy-nine: What you seek will be seen. Eighty: What you seek will be found).

Those who wish to see will be able to see. Anyone you seek can find you. The person you prayed for but did not see, did not see.

(Sutra) The eight ten false ones, pray for the knowledge of literature and good language. Eighty-two people, what they sought to see was not as expected.
(Sutra: Eighty-one: Pray to be heard, you will hear good words. Eighty-two: Pray to be seen it won't work).

Hearing good, beneficial, beneficial words for you. You all hear good things from the sutras. You listen to words that are of no use to you. For example, right now you come to listen to the sutra, we think it is very beneficial, so we ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches: - After hearing it, you don't focus your mind on it, there is no benefit to you at all.

(Sutra) The eighty-three are false, the contemplation of rituals is the truth.
(Sutra: Eighty-three: Contemplating doubt is the truth).

Listen to whether the words are useful or unhelpful to you, because you have questions

If you doubt, you should ask. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, please ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to tell you, that is because you have doubts. Whether you want to associate with someone who will be beneficial or harmful to you, or want to ask someone for help with something, whether they will help or not, you should observe and you will be able to know.

(Sutra) The eighty-four are false, the contemplation of doubts is not real.
(Sutra: Eighty-four: Contemplation that what we suspect is not true).

This is the assumption that doubting others is not genuine. You don't need to doubt! Do you doubt that the phenomenon you see is real? No need to doubt! Because you can't decide, you should use Chiem Sat Luan. Contemplation Sat Luan will tell you it's okay!

(Sutra) The eighty five falsehoods, the contemplation of causes are not in harmony.
(Sutra: Eighty-five: Those who are contemplated are not in harmony).

You and that person don't get along.

(Sutra) Eighty-six fakes, praying to Buddha will bring success. Eighty seven people, praying to the old man who is achieving success.
(Sutra: Eighty-six: Praying for Buddha's work will be achieved. Eighty-seven: Praying for offerings will be achieved).

We do a course of Buddhist work. When we do Buddhist work, we always hope for success, until we hope to achieve Dharma benefits (benefits of the Dharma). Before doing it, you should observe and ask questions. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will tell you: What you pray for Buddha will achieve! Or you can worship, worship Buddha, recite sutras, [Bodhisattva will tell you] it can be done, it can be done smoothly.

If we also wish for a certain type of offering, the offering we wish for will be attainable!

(Sutra) Eighty-eight falsehoods, pray for the wish to be born.
(Sutra: Eighty-eight: May the things needed for life be like idea).

When you pray for the things you need for life, [the universal form] will tell you: You can get it. “For sentient beings” includes things we use to build our lives, or things to worship Buddha. [If you sow this number, it means] you will be able to achieve what you want.

(Sutra) The eighty-nine falsehoods, pray for the least amount of birth and attainment.
(Sutra: Eighty-nine: Praying for things needed for life is only a small part).

Even though you have achieved very little, you are not satisfied.

(Sutra) Nine-crossed practitioners, possessing the attainment of attainment.
(Sutra: Ninety: Whatever you wish for, you will achieve).

Whatever you wish to achieve, you can achieve it.

(Sutra) The nine ten falsehoods, possessing the fruit of a quest is in vain.
(Sutra: Ninety-one: Even if you wish for something, you can't achieve it).

[Luan General] tells you: Can't achieve it.

“Eunuch” is a person who is sick or has had an accident. Generally speaking, illness is caused by the Four Elements, i.e. Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind, not being in harmony: too much Earth Element, too much Water Element, too much Fire Element, or too much Wind Element. Phong Dai is too much, everyone knows it. You see there are so many crazy people in the insane asylum because of Phong Dai! Surely everyone knows about leprosy? Leprosy spreads very quickly. Everyone with leprosy is isolated, lives alone, or lives in the mountains. Everyone has seen too much Fire Dai, the fever is high, the fever is so feverish that the mind is confused, and the spirit is erratic! Too much Water Dai causes scabies and pus to flow. Therefore, there are many diseases that doctors have no way to treat. If we get hit by the wind, have a cold, or have a runny nose, it's easy to treat. If you don't treat it, it will heal after seven or eight days. There are diseases that are not like that. Illnesses [like the flu] are easy to treat, but what about mental illnesses? Common illnesses are caused by external influences from Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind, but mental illnesses are not easy to treat. If the mind is sick, we must use the mind to treat it. On the contrary, for those who study Buddhism, you must consider what illness you are suffering from and what medicine to use to treat it.

[The numbers] above [from number one] to number one hundred and sixty are all real things that we encounter in current life. That is from real life, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has revealed to you, one hundred and sixty of these things to teach us from the beginning of the mind to what the body has to endure in the present life. From number one to number one hundred and sixty are all present, we must know the retribution and karma in the past. From the number one hundred and sixty-one onwards, we will talk about what we suffer because of previous lives. When we look at the current person, we will know which way he or she came from.

(Sutra) One hundred and sixty false, one part of hell and the middle path. One hundred and sixty two people, the animal lives in the middle path. One hundred and sixty-three people, along the road of ghosts and ghosts. One hundred and sixty four practitioners, along the middle path of Asura.
(Sutra: One hundred sixty-one: From the path of hell. One hundred sixty-two: From the path of animal birth come. One hundred sixty-three: From the hungry ghost path. One hundred sixty-four: From the Asura path).

Why do we know that person came from the hungry ghost path? How can one recognize a person from human reincarnation? Very little comes back from humanity! These three numbers refer to hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, these are called the “three evil destiniess”, they are born from the three evil destiniess into [the human world]. One hundred and sixty-four are born from the Asura Path.

(Sutra) One hundred six hundred and fifty fake people, part of the humane world. One hundred and sixty six people, the middle of the road is the same.
(Sutra: One hundred and sixty-five: Born from humanity. One hundred and sixty six: Born from heaven).

From humanity, from heaven, that is, from the path of goodness comes birth. We see people born from heaven or humanity, with very good personalities, not harsh, very peaceful.

(Sutra) One hundred and sixty seven fakes, part of the middle-aged family. One hundred and sixty-eight fake people, each of whom became a monk in middle childhood.
(Sutra: One hundred and sixty-seven: From home comes. One hundred and sixty eight: From renunciation comes).

Each person has their own habits. What is habit? In addition to body, speech, and mind, there are also habits. Because each person's living habits are different, each person has their own habits. The two numbers here are intended to examine each person's habit. You see that person is extremely kind and rarely gets angry. Even if you get angry, listen to others' advice and control yourself, very good manners. There are people who, no matter how much you advise, cannot advise them a little better. The more they advised, the more impatient they became, as if cheering them on. Because we cannot differentiate ourselves, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva says these things for us to differentiate. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, you must consider. When we see that person, you study the Contemplation Sutra. As soon as you see that person, you immediately know which way he came from. These Dharma friends are not from heaven, but from humanity. People who come from hell will not believe in Buddha. From the animal path of birth comes stupidity, ignorance, and brutality; Whatever that person wants to do, you advise him, but he doesn't listen. You can see each person's personality. As soon as you see it, you immediately know which way it came from, without needing to analyze it in detail. You can't say to someone: "You came from hell", it's strange that that person doesn't fight you! You observe, you can't talk to that person. Why observe like that? You want to help that person, want to practice the Bodhisattva path, want to save sentient beings. To save sentient beings, even if you don't understand them, how can you save them? For each person, you must clearly understand their personality; Only then will they be able to trust you. You see that person comes from heaven, or from humanity (humanity), it will be absolutely different. You observe other people, some people are monks, they have been monks for many lifetimes, and you can see their habits as soon as you look at them. You see that person's habits are completely different, because he or she has been a monk for life after life.

(Sutra) One hundred sixty-nine people, one after another, make offerings to the Buddha. One hundred, seven, and ten people, their relatives, made offerings to the sages. One hundred, seven, and ten people have attained profound knowledge and dharma.
(Sutra: One hundred and sixty-nine: Having met and made offerings to Buddha before coming. One hundred and seventy: Each destination One hundred and seventy-one: having heard the profound Dharma, come.

Or there are people who have made offerings to the Buddha or the Three Jewels and were reborn [in the human world]. Once with the sage monks, once heard the very profound Dharma and was born. These things don't need to be explained, because everyone will understand as soon as they read them, but knowing them is not easy, you have to have a predestined relationship. Without causes and conditions, “all methods will gather together, things will cluster together” (similar methods will gather into groups, all things will be divided into species). You see what kind of person a person is, what kind of people his friends are, completely different! That's called "The way things come together, things come together", belonging to any species will have feelings for people close to that species. That person plays with friends who are all of the same type. Because it is very difficult for people to get close to robbers, gangsters, and villains. When I was in Tibet, going to the countryside and meeting a lot of people, either in the Khang (Khams) area, or in the ethnic minority areas, their personalities were really not human. We often say "there is no human nature", affirming that they are born from the animal path or from the hungry ghost path. The way they eat is not the same as normal human eating, maybe people haven't seen it yet. From the phenomenon of perceiving nature, there are many things. When you look at the current situation, all the actions of others, you will know their nature. Wait until you have studied the Contemplation Sutra for a long time, you have learned the Contemplation Sutra quite well, sometimes you have to contemplate, sometimes you are already good, you don't need to contemplate anymore! You have been bowing to Ksitigarbha for a long time, bowing to Chiem Sat Sam for a long time, and as soon as you see it, your mind immediately understands. Without even contemplating, I knew right away. There are people who, based on their current actions, can you predict what path they will take when they die. You plant the Wheel of Contemplation, the wheel of the wheel will let you know.

(Sutra: One hundred and seventy-two: Having sacrificed his life, he went to hell).

There are people who do things that are no longer human, all about falling into hell. You tell me: If that person dies and doesn't go to hell, where will he go? Recently I saw a newspaper, [seeing a news report] that an American, a seventeen-year-old child, killed his entire family, father, mother, and grandparents, eleven lives, and they were not in the same place together. After killing one place, he drove to another place to kill again, killing eleven people. You say, is it still human? If he dies and gives up his life, won't he go to hell? Absolutely falling into hell.

(Sutra) One hundred seven and thirty false beings, letting go of the body, creating animals. One hundred seventy-four people, let go of their body, and act as hungry ghosts. One hundred and seventy-five practitioners, abandoning their body, create Asura.
(Sutra: One hundred and seventy-three: Having sacrificed oneself, one will become an animal. One hundred and seventy-four: Already If you give up your life, you will become a hungry ghost. One hundred and seventy-five: If you give up your life, you will become an Asura).

I met a user of Chiem Sat Luan who never had these numbers before. Because as long as Dharma friends can use the Contemplation Wheel, they will not enter the three evil realms, nor will they enter hell, hungry ghosts, or animals. [Those who fall there] do not have any good, are pure evil, have no good karma; even opening his mouth to curse others. Have you heard them say anything nice? Not yet! However, we do not come into contact with those people. They have done so much evil that after their death, they will definitely fall into the three evil realms, there is no way!

(Sutra) One hundred and sixty falsehoods, letting go of the body, giving birth humanely.
(Sutra: One hundred and seventy-six: After sacrificing one's life, one will be born as a human).

If you have given up this body and exchanged it for another, you are all good people.

(Sutra) One hundred and seventy-seven hypocrites, renouncing the body, are kings. One hundred, seven, and eight, let go of the body and be born in heaven. One hundred seven and ten nine people, abandoning their body, become the king of heaven. One hundred and eighty ten people, letting go of the body, writing deeply.
(Sutra: One hundred and seventy-seven: After sacrificing his life, he will become a king among humans. One hundred and seventy eight: After giving up one's life, one will be born as a god. One hundred and seventy-nine: After giving up one's life, one will become a heavenly king. One hundred and eighty: After giving up one's life, one will listen to the profound Dharma.

If you have sacrificed your life and then heard the profound Dharma, roughly speaking, after you have sacrificed your life, you will go to the Pure Land, or to the Buddha realms, to be able to hear the profound Dharma. Without being born in a Buddha land, how can one hear the profound Dharma?

(Sutra) One hundred and eight hundred falsehoods, renunciation of one's self and attainment of renunciation.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-one: Having given up his life, he became a monk).

This is the next life. Everyone sees that the monks and nuns did not [ordained] easily like that, but only achieved it after many lifetimes of practice. But once you have become a monk, you must practice more skillfully in order to increase your good deeds even more. Therefore, the Buddha taught us: "Try the body without saving the golden life, but try to save the body from the living world?" (If you don't save this body in this life, what other life will you wait until you die). If you cannot escape this life, how long will you wait? Wait until what lifetime will you be saved? The human body is difficult to obtain, [casting a wheel of signs to contemplate, if you cast this number,] after you have sacrificed your life, you can become a monk again.

(Sutra) One hundred and eighty-two hypocrites, letting go of the body, controlling the holy monks. One hundred and eighty-three false beings, letting go of the body, were born Tusita Heaven.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-two: After sacrificing oneself, one will meet the holy monk. One hundred and eighty-three: After giving up his life, he will be born in Tusita Heaven).

After giving up one's life, one will be born in Tusita Heaven. Tushita Heaven is the fourth heaven. Why only say Tusita heaven? Because at present, Maitreya Bodhisattva is in the inner courtyard of Tushita Heaven. If you are born in Tusita Heaven, you will be born in front of Maitreya Bodhisattva. Wait until Maitreya Bodhisattva is born and becomes a Buddha, you will become a Bodhisattva. Make a vow, make a vow

born in Tathagata.

(Sutra) One hundred and eighty-four falsehoods, letting go of the body and nature, rebirth in the pure Buddha land.
(Sutra: One hundred eighty-four: After sacrificing himself, swillbe born in the pure Buddha land).

Born in the pure Buddha land, your body is born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, that is the Pure Land. Being born in the realm of Medicine Master Lapis lazuli Light Tathagata is also the Pure Land. There are many pure realms of Buddhas, but our fate is not deep, so we don't know them. The Western Pure Land world has a very deep affinity with us, anyone who recites Amitābha Buddha's name can be born there. Whenever you recite Amitābha Buddha, you will be able to be reborn. If this life has expired, you will immediately be reborn in the Pure Land. If it is in the next life, it is not certain which world it will be in. No matter one lifetime or two lifetimes away, as long as you recite Amitābha Buddha's name and pray to be born in the Pure Land, in this life you have not yet been born, in the next life, in three lifetimes, no more than ten lifetimes, you will absolutely be able to be born, because you have made a vow to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss. In our human world, ten lifetimes seem very long, but Buddhas and Bodhisattvas see ten lifetimes as just one thought. Either has been born, or is now born, or will be born, why do you say will be born? If we are not born now, then in the future we will not fall into hell or do bad things. If you recite Amitābha Buddha as the seed, you will definitely be able to be born, depending on whether you yourself go there or not, “when you are born, you decide to be born, when you go, you really don't go”, that person doesn't want to go [how can you be reborn? To be reborn or not] you have to rely on yourself [do you really want to be reborn or not]? But if you recite Amitābha Buddha's name and pray to be reborn in the Pure Land, it won't take more than ten lifetimes [to be reborn]!

(Sutra) One hundred and eighty five falsehoods, letting go of the body, seeing Buddha.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-five: After sacrificing oneself, one sees Buddha).

Once you give up this body, you can see the Buddha. No Buddha has been mentioned yet; Therefore, it is not certain to be born in the Pure Land, any Buddha land is possible.

(Sutra) One hundred and eighty six falsehoods, letting go of the body, residing in the Lower Vehicle.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-six: After giving up his life, he lived in the Lower Vehicle).

If you release this body, you will immediately attain the Lower Vehicle. Thanh Van and Arhat both belong to the Lower Vehicle.

(Sutra) One hundred and eighty seven falsehoods, letting go of the body, staying in the Middle Vehicle.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-seven: After giving up his life, he lived in the Middle Vehicle).

The Lesser Vehicle is Shravaka, the Middle Vehicle is Pratyekabuddha, and the Mahayana is Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) One hundred eighty eight falsehoods, letting go of the body, reaping the fruition.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-eight: After sacrificing one's life, one attains the fruition).

“Realization” here it is not said what kind of fruit it is, First Fruit, Second Fruit, Third Fruit, Four Fruits are all called “certified fruit”, until the end of birth and death. We are generally at the mercy of birth and death.

(Sutra) One hundred and eighty nine, renouncing the body, abiding in the Upper World Excess.
(Sutra: One hundred and eighty-nine: After sacrificing his life, he lived in Heaven. Excess).

The Upper Vehicle is the Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) Good man! The name is one hundred, eight, nine, and nine types of good and evil have different consequences.
(Sutra: Good man! Those are called one hundred and eighty-nine different types of good retributions evil).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: I tell you one hundred eighty-nine good and evil retributions, the difference is extremely huge. That is to say there are many changes in it, where does that change come from? You bow and repent and then use the Contemplation Wheel. If you worship every day, with one corresponding thought, you will be completely transformed, from an ordinary person to a saint. Your karma will be eliminated, your wisdom will increase, and your virtue will become complete. Those are one hundred and eighty-nine types of wheel appearances.

(Sutra) Like trying contemplation, depending on the mind, you can contemplate the concept. If the combination of data is equal to fake, there is no catch. The weakness of the state, the combination of the number, the data of the mind, the thought of the main thought, are not equivalent, the mind is not even, the name is empty. If there are three people in the third generation, there will be no one who knows anything. Trying to find the right reason to get one, there will be no other people.
(Sutra: Dharma of contemplation like that, depending on what is mainly contemplated and thought about by the mind, if the number [The appearance of the wheel] is equivalent to the intention [of the person contemplating], then there is no error. If the [turn of the wheel] is cast and the total number is not equivalent to the main contemplation and thought of the mind, that means [the person contemplating] is not sincere, it is called illusory, mistaken.

After talking about the numbers in the wheel form, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: The way to contemplate the Wheel of Karma as I just said will depend on “the mental factor contemplating the main thing”, that is, what is in the person's mind that is mainly thought of and then contemplates that wheel. Regarding what the person wishes for, “the number that matches the evil intention is equivalent” means that the number shown by the wheel of appearance corresponds to what the person thinks in his mind, that is, what he thinks coincides with that number, it is a close match, there is no mistake, nothing is wrong. If what that person thinks does not correspond to the number [appeared by the wheel of rotation], then it is "not correct, not corresponding". If it doesn't correspond, it means your mind is not sincere, so [the physical form] still doesn't appear. The number you cast and the thing you are thinking are completely compatible is your will. [At least you must] have the will of the lower level, because if you don't have the heart to do this, if you use Chiem Sat Luan to worship without the heart, everything will be an illusion. Hope cannot be reality! Is there a case where you cast the wheel three times and it doesn't appear, meaning you didn't get any numbers? [If that's true], that person has gone beyond the world, one is to have attained emptiness, two is to have achieved the path of karma, so the wheel of existence does not appear.

Therefore, whatever you wish for in your mind, a number out of one hundred and eighty-nine numbers will appear in accordance with what you are thinking. If both of them match closely, it is called correspondence. After corresponding, if the situation is very bad, for example, if you ask about an illness, [the reincarnation says] the illness cannot be cured, doctors cannot treat it, if that is the case, how sad will our mind be? Don't be discouraged, continue to recite Ksitigarbha's holy name, pray to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for blessings, he will change. If you are sick, you plant the wheel of the wheel and know that you will die. You are panicked and don't want to die. You still can't help it. You still have six relatives, so please pray to the Bodhisattva! If you risk your life to increase your life span, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will prolong your life. If you do things and hope to do them successfully, ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for blessings. If you worship and repent accordingly, saying “corresponding” means you sow the wheel, [letters or numbers] will all appear in red, no black, there will be no karma, all good thoughts, all good intentions.

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! If you spontaneously generate your thoughts, contemplate the retribution that others will receive, and the heron will be in sync with your ears.
(Sutra: Come, good man! If you spontaneously contemplate the retribution you have to suffer from others, then do the same like that).

Instead of praying for ourselves, we use Chiem Sat Luan to pray for someone else. That person has a very dangerous illness. I will see if that person's life span has ended or not and then ask. [Luan General] will tell you: That person can heal, there is no need to worry. [Luan General] says that person is not good, you and that person are your closest friends, or that person is your relative, or your own parent, we can worship and pray on that person's behalf. That person must know, must clearly tell that person: "Now I bow to pray for you, I bow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for you." That person also knows in his heart that only then will it be effective and effective.

(Sutra) Weaknesses of others are unable to see for themselves, they ask for help, they seek to be contemplatives, and they are unable to contemplate for themselves. Generous, observing one's own mind, not greedy for the world, pure inner mind. The mother-in-law should be able to follow the highest respect, practice, make offerings, and wholeheartedly make a vow to contemplate, not to be greedy for worldly fame and fortune, like practicing the monk's way, but naturally chaos.
(Sutra: If there is someone else who cannot contemplate for themselves, come and request it [for me] You should think carefully, observe your mind, not be greedy for the world, with a pure mind. Then, you can follow the above instructions to respect, practice, make offerings, and wholeheartedly make vows for that person. Don't be greedy for worldly fame and fortune.

Or there are people who cannot use Contemplation, because they do not know how to use it, because they have never learned it, then you can contemplate for them. That person cannot contemplate for themselves, you can contemplate for that person, but your heart must be as sincere and urgent as when contemplating for yourself, and you must speak clearly to that person. Don't be greedy for fame and worldly gain! Don't say that we help others worship to pray for good reputation, or to receive offerings from others. [If you have thoughts of desire] like that, it won't work. Not only is it ineffective, but it is also a crime, what crime is it? Cheating for fame and profit. Whatever the reason for fame and profit, there will be no correlation! Your bowing is also in vain, and the wheel form is also fake, because it is not [sincere, selfless] like that! You must not be greedy for fame and worldly gain, and have a pure heart. Only then can we repent and contemplate the universal appearance of others. If you don't do that, you won't be able to observe for others! If it is not due to the desire for fame and profit, practice compassion and practice the teacher's way (the way of a teacher) like that. If that is not the case, we will create obstacles for ourselves and cause chaos (disturbing the wheel of life). Don't consider this dharma as a game of fortune-telling or criticizing the world's eight characters; [If you consider it as fortune telling or hexagram drawing] it will be an evil way. When you turn the Dharma into an evil destinies, it is not only ineffective, but also sinful. Due to improper use, the righteous dharma also turns into an evil dharma.

atrium.
(Sutra: If the mind is not pure, even if you contemplate it but it does not correspond, it is just an illusion It's an illusion, it's just a mistake).

At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: If the inner mind is not pure, because the inner mind of that person (the person using the Contemplation Wheel) is not pure, your contemplation is also not equivalent (inaccurate). Even though contemplation is still not equivalent, it is all “void”, which means illusion and error. That is the final advice of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: You should use the Contemplation Wheel, do not be greedy for worldly fame and gain! We cannot rely on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's magical powers to show off that we have magical powers, that's impossible! That is a fundamental transgression!

(Sutra) For the second time, in the future, all living beings are equal, necessarily thinking of nothing good, seeking nothing good. At the moment of attainment, the strain of worry and anxiety is overwhelming, and when one dwells in the stomach, one often needs to recite the name of the self. Weaknesses in the mind, the desire to dream, the pursuit of plans, and now brain failure.
(Sutra: Come here, nIf sentient beings in the future are at a time when all the things they contemplate are not good, their wishes are not achieved, they have all kinds of worries, sorrows, worries, and fears, they should diligently chant my name day and night. If they can be single-minded, then the things they contemplate will be good, their wishes will be achieved, and they will be free from mental depravities in the present).

Furthermore, if in the future life, living beings because of all the observations are not good. All the things contemplated are not good, no matter how many times you sow, they are not auspicious. Whatever you desire is not satisfied, you have all kinds of worries, troubles, fears, and panics, showing that your karma is very heavy. What should you do? Day and night, regardless of day or night, diligently chant my name day and night. Finally, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva advised: You use the wheel form, all of it is not good. Correspondence is correspondence, both are not good. You are scared about this, what should you do? Day and night, do not sleep, recite my name, that is, recite “namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”. [For the name of Bodhisattva] there are sutras that say there is the word King, that is “namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”, some sutras do not. Ksitigarbha Sutra (Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vow Sutra) is always recorded as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, [other sutras] have a translation as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and a translation as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If you do not achieve what you seek, the wheel of life is not auspicious. Because of this, you will be even more worried and miserable. At that time, there is no solution at all, you only have one way: Recite my name. Reciting my name will be able to avoid that accident. Then, if you contemplate, it will turn from not auspicious to auspicious, from undesirable to attainable!

That is how to use the wheel of appearance and the method of contemplation in the Contemplation of the General Dharma. If you want to learn, you still have to study well. From what has been said above, it is possible that when contemplation you still do not understand, you must use the Contemplation Sat Luan as a model. But if you don't worship, your contemplation will absolutely not be able to correspond! Even if it corresponds, it is not real, because if you contemplate casually, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will not appear. Until you pay the appropriate repentance, your mind corresponds to the dharma as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught; At that time, you use the Contemplation Wheel and it will be appropriate. Let's look at the second half of the book.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, keep pure faith Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asks Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat Proverb: "Van Ha opens the market to seek the means of attacking the beasts of the Mahayana?"
(Sutra: At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva: "How do you reveal the means of entry to those who wish to reach the Mahayana?")

After repentance, karma has been eliminated, you can practice. I wish to pray for Mahayana and develop the Bodhisattva mind to become a Buddha. The way to use the Contemplation Wheel mentioned in the above book is a skillful method of transformation for sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age. They are people with dull roots, not enough good roots. If the obstacles have been eliminated and there are no more obstacles, we often say “remove karma”. Having eliminated karmic obstacles, good roots grow. At that time, practice will begin. If you practice without obstacles, you will be able to achieve success and progress towards Mahayana. Therefore, the first half of the book is intended to prepare for practice in the second half of the book. You follow the first half of the book to thoroughly repent and eliminate karma; At that time, you will begin to practice the religion. Kien Tinh Tin asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: After repenting and wishing for the Mahayana, hoping to become Buddha, how should we practice? “Attachment” is to follow and advance towards Buddhahood. What skillful means should we use to practice to be able to achieve it?

(Sutra) Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva's words: - Good man! If all sentient beings desire the Mahayana, they will prophesy the most basic karma of action. The first stage of practicing basic karma is to rely on the realm of One True, to cultivate faith and understand. By cultivating faith and releasing strength, one can quickly attain the Bodhisattva nature.
(Sutra: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva said: - Good man! If there are assemblies If you want to move towards Mahayana, first of all, you should know the basic karma to practice at the beginning. The basic karma to practice at the beginning is to rely on the realm of One Truth to practice faith and understanding. Due to the growth of faith and understanding, you will quickly participate in the Bodhisattva nature.

“Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat said”, sometimes after the word Bodhisattva, Ma Ha Tat (Mahasattva) is added, that is, the great Bodhisattva among Bodhisattvas, denoting the Bodhisattva level from the birthplace (from the First Ground) upwards, the word Ma Ha Tat is added [after the name Bodhisattva]. Normally, we sentient beings, among the Dharma friends present, have received the Bodhisattva Precepts, or more broadly, anyone who has received the Three Refuges is called a Bodhisattva. When you say “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, at that time, you are a Bodhisattva, because you are a disciple of the Buddha. If you have not received the Three Refuges, you yourself have read many sutras, you cannot be called a Buddhist disciple, because you have not yet entered the Buddhist sect, you must take the Three Refuges, officially join the Buddhist sect, and truly become a Buddhist disciple, all of which are called Bodhisattvas. But it cannot be called a great Bodhisattva, nor can it be added [the title] Mahasattva. The term Bodhisattva is very popular, because anyone who has the desire to help others is called a Bodhisattva, helping others become enlightened. Because, in the name Bodhisattva, Bodhisattva (Boddhisattva) translated into Chinese is Enlightenment of Sentient Beings, because it enables all sentient beings to be clearly enlightened. Enlightenment is Buddha, that is, regarding Buddha Dharma, it will be possible to make [self and sentient beings] enlighten to Buddha Dharma clearly.

Therefore, Bodhisattva Firm and Pure Faith (Dṛḍhamati) asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: "If you want to practice the Bodhisattva path, what skillful means must you have to enter it?" Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told him (Pure Faith Bodhisattva): If there are sentient beings who wish for the Mahayana, the Mahayana and the Hinayana are related to the mind. A mind that is not entirely for oneself, wishing to benefit all sentient beings is called Great. Your mind only thinks of good things for yourself, ignoring others, only hoping for your own end of life and death, regardless of sentient beings, [that is Small]. Your mind thinks that all sentient beings will be subject to birth and death, whether or not you will be subject to birth and death, it doesn't matter at all! Let all sentient beings be born and die, that is the Mahayana mind, that is called Bodhisattva. So to practice the Bodhisattva path, what is the most basic thing? What karma should we do? How can we practice the Bodhisattva path?

What is basic training like? That is what he refers to in the realm of One Truth to practice faith and understanding. Due to the power of cultivating faith and understanding to increase the conditions, he quickly entered the Bodhisattva nature. If you want to achieve Bodhisattva status, how should you enter? Suppose there is a type of living being who wants to practice the Bodhisattva path and become a Bodhisattva; First of all, you must know the karma you have created yourself, the most basic karma you should do! For the basic karma that is practiced, the karma is the effect (effect), where is the most basic effect used? It is to rely on the realm of One Truth to cultivate faith and understanding. The One True Realm is “no realm”. That is “entering the Dharma precepts”. The Avatamsaka Sutra says we hope to enter the Dharma Realm, the Dharma Realm is the realm of One Truth. Dharma is mind, mind has no limits. We often talk about the dharma realm, the dharma realm has no limits, all dharmas have no limits. Furthermore, the dharma realm is the mind, the mind gives birth to all dharmas. In the Avatamsaka Sutra, the dharma realm is the mind. The realm of One True is one mind. Precepts are mind, there are no two, no difference, so it is called the world of One Truth. Whenever we hear about the dharma realm, dharma is the origin of all dharmas. What arises? Gender. Precepts are the mind, the mind gives birth to all dharmas, all dharmas return to the mind.

How can I enter? The realm of One True is the realm of "no realm". What is the realm of One Truth? Buddha realm. The Buddha realm is One Truth, everything else is an illusion. What is the Buddha realm? The realm has no realm. What realm does our mind have? We observe for a moment, that mind is not correct (it is not the true mind), [the mind as we often think, often talk about] is the present false mind. We still do not recognize the mind, because we still do not know that we have a false mind and a true mind. A false mind is based on the truth and hopes arise, and false thoughts arise because of the truth. Hope does not exist, it is born to respond to all situations and all things. “The mind is inherently non-born, it exists because of the environment” (The mind is originally non-born, it exists due to the environment). Our mind is inherently unborn; Because we have all the signs of the realm, we have all the minds. The realm is illusory, your false mind is also illusory, "The original mind has no birth, the cause exists" (The mind is inherently unborn, it exists because of the scene), what if the scene does not exist? Then the mind doesn't exist either! At that time, “the mind disappears, the scene is still, the two sentences are empty” (the mind is gone, the scene is quiet, both sides are empty). Neither side exists, it has been achieved. Shouldn't we repent? Truly repented. “The mind is gone, the scene is still, the two sentences are empty. This is called true repentance” (The mind is gone, the scene is quiet, both sides are empty. That is called true repentance). After understanding this principle, you will know that all dharmas are like that.

If what is practiced is said to be "basic", [also] "what is practiced fundamentally at the very beginning", what is that basis? It is to rely on the realm of One Truth. When you develop your faith, your faith has just become enlightened, the Dharma friends present have understood your faith, understood that you are in delusion, that you are inherently complete, no different, no two, no different from the Buddha. The mind of yourself and all the Buddhas of the ten directions, and all sentient beings, three things are no different, that is one mind. How was your mind born? The mind is inherently unborn. Infertility comes from the scene. Because the appearance of the external realm already exists, the mind also exists. When the scene is quiet, all the signs of the realm are calm, there is no more, there is no mind! When you "the mind is gone, the scene is quiet, both sides are empty", then all the sins and all the good things will not be established, because they are all non-existent.

The basic basis for practice at the beginning is to contemplate the mind, the mind is the root of all dharmas, or also known by another noun, “the Realm of One Truth”. First of all, cultivate faith in your mind. Once you have faith, you will begin to become enlightened. I have to explain this a bit. Currently, we believe in the Three Jewels, even when we practice, it is a mind of joy (love), a mind of great joy and desire. Mocking the mind is not believing in the mind. What is the expression of faith? Truly believe in the Three Jewels. If you truly have faith, you have standards. You yourself feel that in my mind there are no evil thoughts, there are no evil thoughts at all, there is only compassion, until you feel that my thoughts are not right, knowing that the previous thoughts started to be evil, you can immediately stop them, causing the next thoughts not to arise, [so] you have participated in the Faith. When a bad thought arises, it will immediately be destroyed, completely preventing it from continuing. That is called "having faith", having perfected the mind of the Ten Faiths, participating in the position of First Pillar. Having participated in the First Pillar position, one can manifest in the three thousand great thousand worlds to save sentient beings. That is the Hoa Nghiem realm. As for your mind, if you stay in that mind, what will you realize? Realize your own mind. Having been enlightened, understanding the mind and seeing its nature, that is enlightening the mind. Speaking according to Hoa Nghiem teachings, it cannot be said like in Zen "once the mind is enlightened, one becomes a Buddha", there is no such thing! Still have to practice the Bodhisattva path. There is no Buddha who does not save sentient beings! Is there any Buddha who does not save sentient beings? Without saving sentient beings, one cannot become a Buddha! It is necessary to save sentient beings in order to become a Buddha. But in the end, sentient beings are inherently empty. Buddha saves sentient beings, but he sees that all sentient beings are Emptiness, causing all sentient beings to enter the state of Emptiness. The Buddha saw that all dharmas are empty, but sentient beings cannot be “empty”. Why can't it be “no”? Because of the scene! Therefore, the dharmas have no birth and no death due to this meaning.

The basis for initial practice is to rely on the realm of One Truth; That is our basis, that is the basis of all living beings. But speaking according to the Awakening of Faith, from the True Door, you start cultivating one mind and two doors. Because he wanted to save sentient beings, he divided his mind into the Gate of Birth and Death and the Gate of Truth. In the Gate of Birth and Death, all dharmas are born and destroyed, they are not real, all dharmas exist. From the realm of One Truth, it is divided into two subjects, one is the Gate of Birth and Death, the other is the Mon of True Suchness, from birth and death enter True Suchness. The Mahayana Treatise on Arising Faith teaches this principle a lot. For us Buddhist students, while you practice in order, the first thing is to believe. Having believed it, then solving it, solving it is Learning. Right now, all of us are praying for solutions. To solve is to understand; Once you understand clearly, you will do it. That's Hanh. Practice is practice. Understanding clearly is not enough, we still have to follow what the Buddha taught us to do, so we obey the teachings and follow them. Having believed, having understood to the point of understanding, commonly speaking “enlightenment”, having enlightened, having learned clearly, we ourselves have developed clear self-realization, but because we have learned to understand clearly; That's the solution, it's solved and there's still work to do. “Doing” means practicing the Bodhisattva path. That is the benefit of sentient beings, that is, practice. The word Practice includes benefiting oneself and benefiting others.

tieu_de: Lecture 10: Contemplation on Karmic Retribution and Empty Nature
tom_tat: Lecture 10 At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: "Can you open your eyes to seek the means of attacking Mahayana beasts?" (How to reveal the means of entry to those who aspire to the Mahayana?) In the Upper Book, [Bodhisattva] taught...
noi_dung:
Lecture 10

At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: “How do you reveal the means of entry to the Mahayana path?” (How do you reveal the means of entry to those who wish to move towards the Mahayana?) In the Upper book, [Bodhisattva] taught us: “If you want to learn the Earth dharma, In the Contemplation Pitaka, one should use the Contemplation Wheel for contemplation. I have told everyone that this is not fortune-telling or eight-character magic! Chiem Sat Luan uses Chiem Sat Phap, what is its effect? That's because when we cultivate the path, according to Zen Buddhism, it is "clear mind and see nature". If we want to reach clear mind and see nature, understand our own mind and nature, can't we just sow or cultivate and then clear mind and see nature right away! It's not that easy! Therefore, in the teachings in China in the past, Zen Buddhism said "a stick of incense in the Zen gate, cut down and entered, immediately attain Bodhi". It's so easy and simple to say, but it can't be done! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: If you want to clear your mind and see your nature, first of all, you must know the consequences of good and evil karma. If you don't know even your own good and evil karma, where is your karma? Which karma is heavy? Karma does not exist, it exists due to circumstances. Because you have this physical body; Therefore, we must receive retribution. Having a physical body will certainly bring cause and effect retribution. Karma and retribution are three generations, ten generations, countless lifetimes up to now! The first half [of the Contemplation Sutra aims to teach] you how to use the Contemplation of Graphology. Bowing, bowing, repenting, using the Contemplation Wheel, the purpose is for you to practice the second half. Isn't it true that as soon as you sit down, you "In the Zen door, stick a stick of incense, cut down super directly, and immediately attain Bodhi". At that time, in China, that was always spread. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: First of all, you must repent of your good and evil karma, and must work hard for three years. The first half of [this sutra] says: Use three years to worship. Every person who has benefited from the root has done pure repentance before starting to practice. Having learned to understand the Dharma of Contemplation and Repentance, perform a pure Contemplation and Repentance ceremony before moving towards Mahayana.

At that time, according to the book Thuong, when bowing to the Dharma of Contemplation and Contemplation, the three karmas are pure and the appearance of purity has been achieved. At that time, how should one practice? Therefore, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: At that time, the person praying towards the Mahayana, we simply say “seeking towards the clear mind and enlightened nature”, how should he practice? We are ignorant, we have practiced repentance to eliminate obstacles, our three karmas have been purified, only then can we progress towards the Mahayana path. When you practice the Mahayana path, the first thing you need to do is to have skillful means. How to practice that skillful means? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: “Good man!” The word “good man” refers to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. At that time, sentient beings want to cultivate the Mahayana, practice the Mahayana dharma, practice the Bodhisattva path, and become Buddhas. That is the basic karma that you should know first. Basic karma is the minimum means for you to start practicing. What is basic karma? Realm One True. We call the One True realm “clear mind and see nature”, but in the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, it is called the Body, the Bright Body. The Clear Body is the clear mind. As for your most basic karma, “basic karma” refers to practice, not karma in karma. What is basic karma? The Realm of One Truth is the One True Dharma Realm mentioned in the Avatamsaka Sutra. In other sutras, it is called Tathatā, progressing towards Suchness. True Suchness is the basic karma, that is, the realm of One Truth.

But if you want to clear your mind and realize your nature, until you become Buddha, before that, you must also have a means, that is, practice Faith and practice Wisdom. By believing, you can enter and trust your own mind. The realm of One True is your basic karma. Believe that the mind is Buddha, mind and Buddha are not two, there is no difference. Mind, sentient beings, and all Buddhas, all three are one Body, the same thing? One mind! First of all, you must believe. “Trust is the source of the path, mother of merit” (Trust is the source of the path, mother of merit), only Faith can enter, Solution is understanding. Simply put, Solving is understanding your own mind. Realizing the mind: "The mind is Buddha, this mind is Buddha, this mind becomes Buddha". Having such confidence, believing that "your own mind is Buddha, there is no two, it is no different from Buddha". That is having the Bodhisattva nature. That belief is not easy to arise! The first half of this sutra is worship and repentance. [Due to that repentance] you can have such faith. If your karma is not eliminated and the afflictions of Self-Consciousness have not been cut off, your faith will not be able to arise! If you want to achieve the ultimate foundation, follow the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma to practice. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us the basic karma to practice. That basic karma, “karma” is understood in the sense of “action” (to do, to perform), let's refer to the realm of One Truth to believe and understand. [Just having] Faith is not enough, you also have to understand clearly, [that is the Solution]. Solution is "enlightenment", that is, through study, only after believing in the solution can you do it. “Doing” is practicing; Only by practicing can one attain enlightenment. In the first half, although you have eliminated karma, your faith in understanding is still not strong, and you still have not made the vow "I am Buddha, Buddha is me". You must have that faith, believe that you will definitely be able to become a Buddha. Why? Because there are Buddha seeds, all we need to do is create them and do it!

Once you have faith, you can solve it. Zen Buddhism calls the Solution enlightenment, or clear mind and see nature. Chinese Zen Buddhism says “enlightenment leads to Buddhahood”. Being enlightened is just a matter of understanding! According to teachings, you are enlightened, clear your mind, and only when you have clear your mind can you practice skillfully. You still have to practice, then you can practice the Bodhisattva path. If speaking according to the Avatamsaka Sutra, that position is Faithful (having perfected the mind of the Ten Faiths), participating in the rank of Bodhisattva. Having perfected the mind of the Ten Faiths, one participates in the Bodhisattva Pillars (the Bodhisattva positions belong to the Ten Pillars). He believes that he and the Buddha are no different, no different. Not only having faith, but then also being able to do (practice). How did Buddhas become Buddhas? They also practice like that, do like that, that is a strong power of understanding. The Dharma friends said: "We have entered Buddhism, believe in the Three Jewels, received the Three Refuges, and have even become monks for many years"; Suppose we say they don't have enough faith, they won't accept! But speaking according to the teachings, it is true that there is no faith. Each Dharma friend can follow the Buddha's teachings to think and compare like that!

Now we obey the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: “Strengthen your faith in understanding”. Only by strengthening can one begin to practice. Starting practice is not in the first half of this sutra! Paying repentance, worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, worshiping Buddha, praying for good looks; That's going one step deeper. Your faith is steadfast and has not wavered, and in addition, all ten karmas are pure. Body, speech, and mind are all pure. The mind that arises at that moment is based on the realm of One Truth. We say the One Reality Realm is simply “clear mind”. If we have been cultivating faith from past lives until now, worshiping the image of the Chakravarti will make our faith steadfast. The order of practice is “faith, understanding, practice, realization”. If you want to become a Buddha, you must practice Bodhi. If you do not follow the Bodhi path, you will not be able to become a Buddha. Rely on the Bodhi path; First of all, you must have faith and understanding, you must practice faith and understanding first. What do you rely on to practice faith and understanding? He refers to the realm of One Truth. What is the True Realm? Believe that your own mind and Buddha are not two, no different. The minds of sentient beings in the ten dharma realms are the same mind. You must definitely believe this, believe that you have a complete nature just like Buddha. After trust has arisen, we still need to ask for a solution, what is the solution? Understanding that all dharmas are born of causes and conditions, the nature of dharmas that arise because of conditions is Emptiness. Therefore, for the entire twelve Tripitaka, four words can be used [to summarize] as “dependently arising emptiness, dependently arising emptiness”. Because of emptiness, all dharmas can arise. All dharmas do not have an original nature, but due to dependent origination, they reach emptiness. When using “dependent arising of emptiness” as a topic; Previously, we had lectured, [that lecture was published] in a separate circulation version on dependent origination of emptiness. I preached at the Singapore Buddhist Association, the topic was “dependent arising of emptiness, dependent arising of emptiness”. Here, I have given a brief summary of evidence, dependent arising of emptiness!

After all dharmas are born, from Faith one can enter, only faith can one enter, what do you believe? Believe that all dharmas arise in dependently emptiness, in dependently arising emptiness. No matter which Mahayana sutras, they are all “emptiness that arises dependently, emptiness that arises dependently”. When we preach this sutra, it is the same. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that all dharmas are dependently arisen, dependently arising dharmas are based on emptiness. If you understand this principle, it is called Solution. Believe that our own mind is Buddha. Because your mind is a Buddha, you can cultivate to become a Buddha. If you do not have that faith, you will never be able to become a Buddha. Believing in the mind is Buddha, believing in the mind will become Buddha. Mind, Buddha, sentient beings, the three are no different; Though three, yet one, though one, yet three. I have said to many Dharma friends: "Human nature and Buddha's nature are not two, there is no difference". Their minds have understood. Look at the mosquitoes, look at the ants, look at the mayflies. Mayfly (mayfly) is the name of a type of worm, a small form that lives on the water surface, is born in the morning, and dies in the evening. It's been a lifetime. One hundred years of human life, just like fleeting, equal! Ephemera has Buddha Nature, it can become Buddha. It falls forever, the more it falls, the smaller it becomes, the more it falls, the smaller it becomes, until it recovers, it can restore its human body.

This principle is called Truth. True Suchness, depending on conditions, gives rise to all dharmas, all dharmas return to True Suchness. Mahayana Arising Faith Commentary says “one mind, two doors, three great things”, [two doors] are the mind of birth and death and the mind of True Suchness. The mind of birth and death and the mind of True Suchness both arise from one mind. The [Three Elements] are the Body Element, the General Element, and the Use Element. Due to one mind, the door of Truth and the door of birth and death are born. The two subjects do not go beyond the three great elements, which are Body, Form, and Function. I often say “The Contemplation Sutra is a part of the Avatamsaka Sutra”. Dai Phuong Quang: Dai is Body, Phuong is General, Quang is Use. The second half of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra talks about Body, Form, and Use. Dai Phuong Quang means Body, Form, Use. Mahayana Arising Faith Commentary says that the mind of Truth is the Body, the mind that arises and dies is the Form and Function, all are one mind. Separated from the mind, there are no two dharmas left. If we want to practice from the True Door, it will not be easy to enter. Then follow the door of birth and death to enter. How to enter through the door of birth and death? You should meditate from time to time, just like in the first half of this sutra, which is to worship and contemplate, in order to eliminate karmic obstacles. That is called the dharma that belongs to the door of birth and death. Therefore, you have repented of the three pure karmas, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said two types of contemplation for the realm of One Truth.

What is the True Realm? First of all, let's talk about the Nhat Tru realm, what is the Nhat Tru realm? If we want to explain, we must analyze what is the Reality of the Realm Realm? After Body comes Form; After General comes Tang. Originally it is Body, Form, Use, but in the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, it is called Tang, Tang means Use. Organ means “comprehensive”, containing countless wonderful uses. That content refers to Body, Form, and Use. Dharmakaya refers to the Body, which is the Buddha Nature that all sentient beings are complete, not two, no different from Buddha. That is the whole, that is Buddha Nature. The omnipresent Buddha Nature is also what is called the Dharmakaya in the sutras. Righteousness is Buddha Nature. General in Body, General, Use, Prajna. From the true cause of Buddha Nature, it is called the willow cause, that is, the willow cause of Buddha Nature. Because you have attained the Virtue of Liberation through practice, the Buddha Nature has reached liberation, truly achieved. The Buddha Nature of Willow is called the Virtue of Liberation, or Dharmakaya Virtue. Regarding the causes and conditions of Buddha Nature, all dharmas are born because of causes and conditions. Buddha Nature does not have all the dharmas, the dharmas that are born from causes and conditions are all empty meanings. "Dharma arises from causes and conditions, the ego theory means Emptiness, the name of the Middle Way means, the name means impersonation" (The dharmas are born because of causes and conditions, we say they are Emptiness. That is also called the meaning of the Middle Way, which is also called impersonation).

What is the true nature of this sutra? It is the realm of One Truth, but also the Three Contemplations (Emptiness, Falsehood, Middle) mentioned in the four teachings, or Absolute Emptiness as taught by the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Reason is unhindered, contained everywhere, all containing the meaning of the Three Contemplations. This will be quite a lot to explain, [in the Tripitaka] how many volumes of scriptures are used to explain this issue. Because, [the connotation of] the realm of One True includes so many things. That realm is called the One True realm. Speaking of Dharmakaya Virtue, Prajnaparamita Virtue, and Liberation Virtue, the three virtues are one, one is three. One and three do not hinder each other. Put together, it will be the realm of One Truth. Here, I will summarize a bit. The Realm of One Truth, even if taught for ten hours, still cannot be finished. Very deep meaning! In sutras such as the Lotus Sutra and Avatamsaka Sutra, the teachings are even broader, we only briefly mention them to everyone.

(Sutra) One True Realm of False Realms, sentient beings with the mind and body, the natural part of the body, no birth, no birth destroy. Self-nature is pure, unobstructed, unobstructed, like emptiness, free from discrimination.
pure nature without hindrances, without hindrances, like emptiness, due to separation).

Because the One True realm is the mind body of sentient beings, the essence of the mind of all sentient beings is called the One True realm. It is not born, not destroyed, not defiled, not clean. Its essence is pure and immaculate, without hindrances or hindrances. What do you use to visualize the mind and body? Like nothingness. Buddhas attain the essence, sentient beings are confused about the essence. Because sentient beings are confused, countless distinctions are born. Buddha, Bodhisattva, Sravaka, and Pratyekabuddha are called “the four holy dharma realms”, while heaven, human, Asura, hell, hungry ghosts, and animals are the six paths. We often say “six paths of reincarnation”. The four holy dharma realms combined with the six paths of reincarnation of sentient beings are called “ten dharma realms”. The ten dharma realms are one Body, one mind. No matter how small a life is, it has a soul and an essence, no different from us. Due to creating different karma, one falls into that path, but its essence is not lost. Its body and the Buddha's are not two or different, they are unborn, undying, and have never before had the appearance of birth and death. We must remember that the essence is not the appearance (appearance). The essence of the mind of living beings is inherently unborn and undying; That essence is forever pure, without obstacles. Like what? Like space, there is no distinction, no distinction. But as soon as the mind begins to think, as soon as it differentiates, it loses its essence. Whenever you lose your true self, you become confused, and while you are confused, you separate. The deeper the delusion, the deeper the fall. Delusion is dry, wisdom is still there! The ten dharma realms are divided by delusion or enlightenment and are all decomposed from that essence. The deeper the confusion about the essence, the deeper the fall!

This is talking about the mind, [or to be exact] the entire mind, no part is indispensable. That mind body has no opposites, no relative, it is absolute (cessation of discrimination). You cannot cut or split. If it can be cut or split, it will not be a mind body. It also has no direction, no East, West, South, North, nor people, sentient beings, or the ten dharma realms. The ten dharma realms have only this one mind body, there is no other second one, this is inconceivable! This is talking about the Body, where Buddha does not increase, where living beings do not decrease, equality is universal. The body pervades all places, just as space pervades all places. That mind body is perfect in the ten directions, ultimately one form, no two, no difference, no change, no strangeness, no increase, no decrease. A single thought represents the wealth of all sentient beings as incomparable, no different from the perfect Buddhahood attained by the Buddha. The Avatamsaka Sutra often uses the expression “transforms the ten directions” (horizontally, covering all ten directions) to express the idea: Speaking horizontally, East, West, South, North, and the middle are all complete; Speaking at the extreme vertical, there is no difference between the endless top and bottom. [That is to say] “perceiving the same dharma realm, it spreads across the ten directions” (, vertically to the end of the dharma realm, horizontally throughout the ten directions), imagining this mind, for example, is our present thought.

Everyone, think silently and experiment a little. Just think of the places you have been to, they will quickly appear. No matter how many places you have gone to, no matter if you go to New York in America, anywhere in this world, wherever you go, [when you think of it], it will appear immediately. As long as you calm down, think, and pay attention, it will appear in its entirety. Places you haven't been to because you don't know them will be unimaginable! Every place you've been to, any place you've imagined, can be fully manifested. Where you have not gone, is your mind completely omnipresent? Complete mind! Because now you are in a trance; Due to delusion, it is not complete. Currently, you use Consciousness, not mind. Because currently we don't even know the mind, we only use Consciousness, not reaching the mind. As long as you can reach your mind directly, you will succeed!

(Sutra) Universal equality, without any will, the perfection of the ten directions, the ultimate one form, non-dual, non-differentiable, unmatched changeable, undifferentiated, without increase, without decrease.
(Sutra: Equality throughout, nowhere to go, perfection in the ten directions, the ultimate form, no two, no difference, no change, no different, no increase, no decrease).

That mind is universally equal, goes nowhere, is perfect in the ten directions, what exactly is it? One general. One form refers to no form, there are no two signs, there is no other form. That mind will never change or be different, it does not increase in Buddha, it does not decrease in ordinary people. The mind body of a thought is present to us, vertically at the extreme end of the dharma realm, horizontally throughout the ten directions. You can't separate it, and you can't even think about it. It can cover the bodies and weapons of all sentient beings, meaning “universal equality”. Therefore, saying "complete the ten directions, all the dharma realms" (complete the ten directions, complete the entire dharma realm) is our present thought. We are still confused, still not enlightened, but because in the first half [of this sutra], we have bowed to repent of our karma, the three karmas have been purified, you practice, practice the mind-only method. The second half of this sutra is the mind-only method. First of all, [the main sutra] explains this mind as equal and universal.

(Sutra) The mind of all sentient beings, the mind of Shravakas, the Pratyekabuddha mind, the mind of Bodhisattvas, the one The mind of all Buddhas is unborn, undying, untainted, impure, true and like.
(Sutra: Due to the mind of all living beings, the mind of All Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, the minds of all Bodhisattvas, the minds of all Buddhas, are all the same without birth, without death, without contamination, without purity, the form of True Suchness.

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: - Divided by the minds of all living beings who are delusional or enlightened. Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Buddhas are the four holy dharma realms; It is because of confusion or enlightenment that this mind is differentiated into levels. The mind is not two, there is no difference, because of the difference between your delusion or enlightenment, it is divided into levels. The place of sentient beings does not decrease at all, the place of Buddhas does not increase at all! Our mind is not born, is not destroyed, does not increase, does not decrease, is not contaminated, and is not pure. That is called the appearance of Chan Nhu. In the previous section, we said “attain the form of True Suchness”. What is Chan Nhu's appearance? Explained like this: The entire ten dharma realms depend on the appearance of True Suchness, and can be distinguished from one characteristic of True Suchness. The mind of Suchness and the mind of birth and death, the mind of Suchness is our essence. We must restore that essence, all Buddhas have achieved [True Suchness]. [The True Mind] is different from the mind of birth and death. Regarding the arising and passing away of the mind, the Mahayana Arising Faith Commentary points out the appearance of karma, transformation, appearance, wisdom, continuity, grasping, beginning of karma, succession of self-name, and karma of suffering. Because karma binds you, you are always confused about everything. Now, from right in the karma of suffering (suffering due to being bound by karma), we destroy the karma of suffering. You will gradually grow, that is, grow in purity, destroy infection. If we want to correspond to Truth, we must destroy it. The first thing is to escape the karma of suffering first. When we bow to Contemplation and Repentance, we have destroyed the karma of suffering, there is no evil, we have pure goodness, the three cycles of body, speech, mind, and ten karma are all pure. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: At that time, only after living beings have achieved the pure form [from the wheel of rotation] can they begin to practice. When we worship and contemplate the Contemplation Wheel, our faith has reached purity. Right then, we use that pure, immaculate mind to begin practicing.

While you practice, you need to clearly understand the mind, understand the mind first. But without worshiping, our Dharma friends have never worshiped, then our minds still cannot reach purity, they are still mixed with good and evil, not pure goodness! But in the second half of this sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches: When practicing, the mind is pure and good, and the Ten Evil Karmas are completely gone. Compassionate Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, if you have bowed to Contemplation and Repentance for three years, and have been bowing for a full three years, although you still have not achieved the pure appearance of the wheel, you can practice, that is, you can practice the second half of the series, you can practice the contemplation of the mind in the second half of this sutra. All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and great Arhats have equal minds, there is no level, it's just that the level of confusion in the mind [is different], the mind is not pure, the impurities are not eliminated. For example, now when we bow to Chiem Sat Sam, we have achieved the pure appearance of the wheel. The pure appearance of the wheel means [having eliminated] the gross Or, not the subtle Or. [In other words], the afflictions of greed, anger, and delusion that are present in your body, speech, and mind are all gone, and those impurities have been eliminated; but because it is only [eliminating] the gross form, not the subtle form, it has not yet reached the status of “Buddha mind and sentient mind are equal”. The existing [Buddha mind] is equal, but in the process of practicing to purify defilements, it is still not equal. You can restore equality, restore our mind to Buddha's mind, restore our inherent true mind. Buddha mind, sentient mind, true mind, all three are equal. The mind is inherently unborn, undying, unmoved, unstill, unformed, impure, unincreasing, undecreasing, due to the afflictions of different beings. If you can restore tranquility, restore direct mindfulness of True Suchness, then it will restore our mind and body.

That mind covers the ten dharma realms, all scriptures talk about the “three thousand generals” (three thousand generals)>[24]. Mahayana or Hinayana, there is no dharma that is separate from the mind. Separated from the mind, all dharmas will not exist. That is the mind body. Because of the rise of Or contamination, the mind arises to discriminate. Although discrimination arises, all false mental distinctions are completely illusory, not at all true. There is nothing real because all dharmas arise from the mind. Everyone understands this: “When the mind arises, all dharmas arise; when the mind dies, all dharmas cease”. How to make our mind not arise? Ordinary people absolutely cannot do this, even the saints of the Second Vehicle, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas also have orders. The mind represents our money in one thought, completing the ten dharma realms. While you single-mindedly recite the Buddha's name, when your mind is directed towards the Buddha, you are the Buddha Dharma Realm. If you develop a compassionate mind to benefit sentient beings, practice the Bodhisattva path, and you will be a Bodhisattva Dharma Realm. If you wish to practice for the sake of ending birth and death, then you are a Thanh Van, a Pratyekabuddha Dharma Realm; As for all the minds such as the greedy mind, the arrogant mind, the angry mind... then that is the six mortal dharma realms. Based on your discriminating mind, determine your status. All the mental and physical bodies rise up to differentiate, they are just illusory realms, nothing is real. The last four verses in the Vajra Sutra: "All dharmas that exist are like dreams, illusions, robes, shadows, like revealing herons, like divination, and acting like visual contemplation" (All dharmas that are existent, like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, like dew, as well as lightning, should be contemplated like that). That is also the method of contemplating the mind.

Think about it: Of all the dharmas, which dharma is true? It's all an illusion, not real! Are the feelings, thoughts, actions, consciousness, sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, and Dharma that you use true? Is everything you see, hear, hear, and know true? Not at all! Because there are all kinds of scenes outside, all kinds of minds arise. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: One thought of mind fully represents all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, gods, humans, hell, hungry ghosts, animals, combined into one present thought. We must explain like that, must recognize like that.

(Sutra) Why is it fake? It is necessary for the conscious mind to differentiate between the false, the illusory, and the true non-existence. Consciousness, feelings, thoughts, actions, memories, predestined thoughts, dharma-level perception, mind-range, non-sound, non-yellow, non-red, non-white, non-mixed colors, non-existent, short, square, perfect, large, small, even reaching the end of the ten directions of emptiness necessarily in the world, seeking the shape of the mind, there is no one division of children who can attain enlightenment, giving rise to ignorance and delusion of sentient beings, gathering causes and conditions, dreaming realms, souls. born thoughts first. The taste of testing the mind is incapable of self-knowledge, false self-knowledge of existence, awakening of perception, next to self, ego, child is truly incapable of knowing the appearance of consciousness.
