Of course, the false mind is completely insubstantial and cannot be fixed.
(Sutra: Why is that? All those who have the mind to make distinctions are like illusions The dharmas called Consciousness, Feeling, Perception, Action, thinking, remembering, knowing, knowing, etc., all kinds of mental factors (mental factors) are not blue, not yellow, not red, not white, nor are they multi-colored, not long, short, square, round, big, small, all the way to all the worlds in the ten directions of nothingness, searching for the shape of the mind cannot find any individual distinctions, just because of the infinity of causes and conditions. The ignorance of sentient beings gathers to create a realm of illusion, causing them to give rise to thoughts. This is called a mind that cannot know for itself, falsely claiming to exist, giving rise to the idea of knowing, comparing ourselves and what belongs to us, but actually has no form of knowing because, ultimately, that false mind has no Body and cannot be seen.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is still afraid of sentient beings and does not understand why he said that, [so explain by asking questions] “why is it false?” (why). For all you who have a heart, pay attention! All people with minds make distinctions, but in that distinction, all conditioned dharmas are illusory, not real, [yet] sentient beings consider them to be real. Does the mind of sentient beings have anything real to express? Yes! In the Shurangama Sutra, the Buddha asked King Prasenajit: "Great King! How old were you when you saw the Ganges River?" King Basenac replied: "About when I was three years old! My mother took me to the Ganges River, I realized it was the Ganges River." Buddha asked again: "How old is the king this year?" The king replied: "Sixty-two years old." Buddha said: "The king now sees the Ganges River and when he was three years old saw the Ganges River, is there any difference?" King Ba Tu Nac replied: "When I was three years old, I saw the same thing, and I still see it the same way now." [Buddha taught]: "There is a difference in matter, there is a difference between three years old and sixty-two years old, there is a difference in the flow of the Ganges River, there is no difference in the King's Seeing. It is the same at the age of three, but it is still seen at the age of sixty-two. The Nature of Seeing is no different". When we see all dharmas, the Seeing is no different, but matter can change. All conditioned dharmas are false appearances. Impersonation will change at any time. The seeing effect of the Seeing nature does not change. The seeing ability (the subject of seeing, the seeing effect of the Seeing nature) looks at the seeing (what is seen), the seeing is all matter, is false, the Seeing nature of the seeing (the ability to see) is real. All dharmas arise from the mind, all dharmas cease from the mind. Because your mind discriminates, you see the appearance of an illusory realm, nothing is real. There is nothing real about any thing. From this place, you realize: You see the true nature of matter. The Seeing Nature is not the seeing seen by the eyes, but seeing the Nature [of matter]. Having clearly understood the nature of Seeing, if you are greedy for the world and seek something true, then everything will be gone! Therefore, the Diamond Sutra teaches: "All conditioned dharmas are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, like dew, and like lightning. You should contemplate like that". When you contemplate all dharmas, [you will see that they are] all illusory, nothing is real, nothing is unchangeable, not a single dharma is permanent. Please contemplate carefully!

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Tin these words aimed at the meaning of displaying the mind: “The mind is unchanging, the mind does not change according to the scene”. The mind can change the state, it will be like Buddha, [sutras often say] "the same Tathagata". If your mind is turned around by the appearance of the outside world, you will be an ordinary person. Whichever path you change into, you will fall into that path, depending on whether your change is big or small. This is related to your own life, please test your own moral power. If you become a monk, even if we don't become a monk, we believe in Buddha. How will Buddha teach us? It causes us to contemplate all dharmas that are born, exist, are different, die, are impermanent, change, and do not really exist. Because they are conditioned dharmas. All conditioned dharmas, such as dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows, you should contemplate. Contemplate your nature. The difference between all ordinary people and saints is whether “clear eyes, bright hearts” [or not]. The mind is confused, the eyes are not clear. “Eye” here does not mean the iris, but the nature of Seeing. However, in colloquial terms it is "clear eyes, bright heart", that is, the nature of mind, [or in a more limited way] the nature of Seeing. [In fact], the nature of Seeing is the nature of mind, the nature of mind is the nature of Seeing. All of our bodies, all of our Feelings, Thoughts, Actions, Consciousness, thoughts, memories, and our awareness. All dharmas are mental dharmas (mental factors, i.e. the properties of the mind, or in psychology, "psychological effects") that change many times. We are not talking about the Dharma Form, [in the Dharma Form of Consciousness Only], the mind has eight items (eight kings of mind, that is, eight consciousnesses, from eye consciousness to consciousness, plus Manhāna and Alai Da), the mental factor (mind number) has fifty-one items. These dharmas arise entirely depending on conditions, are false, and not real. This also means that we should not be greedy for all dharmas. All dharmas are selfless, all dharmas are impermanent, all dharmas are not real. That's analysis. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: All conditioned dharmas are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, and are not real. Living beings are not like that, depending on your level of awareness of all dharmas. We often say “discover, release” (, see through, let down). Saying “let go” means that in the mind there is no attachment to any dharma, no thoughts arise in the mind, can it be done or not? You yourself can know your own level: People beat you, curse you, insult you, and in your mind there is not a single thought. [Others] praise and praise you as well, completely equal. Regarding any thing, your mind is not crazy. The mind is not crazy, which means you are mindful and present, contemplating that all dharmas are empty, impermanent, and non-self. That way you will enjoy it, at any time, in any place, and still be free!

We give an example, such as talking about getting sick. When you get sick, reflect more. What contemplation is that? Where does that disease come from? What is disease? Suppose you don't have a physical body and if you are sick there will be no place to give birth. Where will you be born? Since you have a physical body, is that physical body real or fake? If I say this, someone will probably say: "This old monk is really confused! He doesn't even know if his body is real or fake!" I'm not confused, I understand clearly, the body is completely fake. Even our Consciousness and mind speaking at the moment are false. While you are very sick and suffering, can you separate your body and mind? For example, what do we do when we go to the hospital for surgery? The doctor must inject anesthetic to anesthetize you, causing your mind and body to separate. The consciousness that is unconscious will dissect the body, you will not feel pain. When the anesthesia wears off, you wake up. If you don't inject anesthesia, you use the power of visualization to separate consciousness and physical body. The body is not you, you have a separate Consciousness.

There was a person who had died three times and told me: When his consciousness separated from his physical body, his brain felt like it was being torn apart, causing extreme pain. My consciousness has left, I don't know anything. He saw that the ten directions of space were all dark. He thought: “Where do I go?” He wanted to touch his body, "I was just injured." Just thinking like that makes it worse! Just thinking, [divine consciousness] immediately returned to the physical body, the pain arose again! The pain was so painful that he lost consciousness. His consciousness left him again, a second time. Once separated, he felt no pain, it seemed like nothingness. He looked for a place, thinking to himself: "Where should I go to heal my wounds?" In my head I still knew I was injured. As soon as I think, my consciousness returns to my physical body. This time he couldn't be cured anymore, the pain was excruciating, the emergency staff took him for treatment. He said to me: "Think about this problem. When we suffer, it is possible to make the consciousness, which is still not the mind, but the consciousness, able to make the mind that is aware and the body that is known, separate the two. Is it possible to do that?"

At first, it won't work. You can usually do it. No need for anesthesia, you can do it yourself. What can be mastered? It's not me! That pain is not me. Therefore, the Shurangama Sutra says: “Enlightenment and enlightenment”, [meaning] if you have sentience, you will feel pain. “Infinite enlightenment”, that is, [pain is only in the body, but the mind] that feels that pain does not feel pain[26]. If we can separate the body and the sense of awareness, of course, at first, you will not be very proficient with that practice. It takes a long time to use it to become very proficient. Of course, even after a year or two of practice, it's still not enough. There will still be times when you feel pain. When you can really use it, your body won't need anesthetic injections, just operate! Everyone has read the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, [in which it is written] Quan Van Truong scrapes bones to cure poison. He is an ordinary person who has never studied Buddhism. While he was playing chess, he also [had the medicine man] carve out the flesh, [that is] cut out the poisoned flesh, and cut until the bone made a squeaking sound. Many people up and down who heard that scraping sound [felt] extremely painful, but he was at peace. Because he separated his own mind and body. I feel like that, I experimented. Last year, I suffered a lot from illness and felt pain, so I practiced this Contemplation method. Please experiment, at least it will reduce your suffering. In particular, my bone mass has increased (hyperplasia)[27]; Therefore, every day, every hour, he was subjected to very painful torment. Bone growth is very painful. Very naturally, there are two types: One type is pain that leads to coma. If you're in a coma, you won't know, and of course you won't feel any pain. When you feel a lot of pain and suffering, don't we often say "spirit overcomes matter"? The body is a type of matter, you use your spirit to overcome it. There are two types: One type is that person's affliction is extremely heavy, his anger is very great, and when someone beats him, he immediately hates: "I must take revenge." Ask the person: "Does it hurt or not?" No pain! That is affliction, not freedom. That person was really in pain and was beaten so severely that he fell into a coma. I just said that people who cultivate the Way do not fall into a coma, no matter how much pain they are in, they do not fall into a coma. Even though the physical body is destroyed, it still does not fall into a coma. Why are people who recite the Buddha's name reborn in the Pure Land, or people who practice the Dharma at the end of their lives can be free? That's due to daily practice.

Until then, until then [that elaborate practice] will not work! Because in all minds, there is already the mind of discrimination. If you don't have a discriminating mind, it will be "spirit overcomes matter" as said. Your body is material, it is not spiritual. Saying “already old”, your mind is very strong, in your mind there has never been the word Old, so overcome it. If you can't overcome it, saying "I'm old", your legs won't be strong, your mind will be dull, your arms won't be able to lift. Can it be fixed or not? I feel like I can fix it, because I've done it myself. Why did I leave Wutai Mountain? That's my fix! Last year, in the dark, I woke up about an hour or two and wanted to pee, but I couldn't get up! Can't move my arms! I'm not done saying this! If I can't lift this arm, my brain can't command it! The brain has lost its command function, the spirit can still command, I want to lift my arm but can't, look at it and it doesn't move! I said, "This demon thing is at work", at that time it was not half-body paralysis, but "whole-body paralysis". I tried my best to fight. Roughly from one hour to more than three hours, gradually the arm can function. I used that arm to shake the other arm, gradually they worked. Once I was able to function, I didn't dare lie down anymore, nor did I dare sleep, I just kept walking. About four or five hours later, I was so tired I couldn't walk anymore, so I sat down. Because of such activities, you become flexible and never get sick a second time. Suppose at that time, lying motionless, it is not that half of the body is paralyzed, it is also that the whole body is paralyzed, unable to move. You have a breakthrough, so mind can transform matter. Everyone should believe in this principle: “Mind can transform matter”. I went to class at Ngu Dai Son, couldn't speak, couldn't teach. Teaching the Shurangama Sutra, teaching it to the third session in the "ten visions" part (ten sessions clearly showing the Seeing), found it impossible to finish, so I had to stop teaching. To this day, it has not been taught again at Ngu Dai Son. What I say is that it's not possible, what's the point of living if you can't teach? Still have to preach! Is it because it's too cold at Ngu Dai Mountain? I immediately went to Thai Nguyen[28]. Arriving at Thai Nguyen, my delusions arose again and I planned to visit Taiwan. I immediately contacted friends in Taiwan, which is why I came here. Having come here, now I'm talking about it, it's also good!

Society often says “spirit overcomes matter”, while in Buddhism we say: “Mind arises, dharmas arise. Mind ceases, dharmas cease”. We can conquer our own body. What to use to win? Using the method taught by the Buddha "let go, see clearly", you will be free. If you are sick, it's three parts illness, plus seven parts worry, and that's it! You can't get up! As for cancer, I have rectal cancer[29]. Surely everyone knows that I am eighty years old and had a rectal tumor removed. The doctor told me: "Master! Once you recover, you won't live more than five years." Because of surgery at the age of eighty, a person with rectal cancer can live a maximum of five years. But now I have lived another fifteen years, which is more than enough! Everything depends on the mind, depending on how you use your mind. I say this with the meaning that all things that have a mind that makes distinctions, that is, your mind makes distinctions, consider all things as illusory, give rise to more joy, do not give rise to afflictions. Every day, if you laugh a few more times, whatever troubles happen to you will turn into an illusion. Don't let things turn around, you have to turn things around. No matter what is happening, you can turn it around. Anyway, this world is impermanent, suffering, empty, and false, all day long you should think like that. When you really encounter trouble arising, say it is fake. I remember the old magician De Nhan said something like that. When he was sick, his disciple asked: "Dear master! Don't you practice Quan?" The Master replied: “Contemplation is false, pain is still real”. But it must be “spirit transforming matter”. All dharmas are born from the mind, all dharmas are destroyed by the mind. Therefore, if ordinary people want to become Buddhas, you must transform reality.

Now we are in afflictions, the whole life is in afflictions, greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt, Personal View, Boundary View, Forbidden View, Wrong View, which have you escaped? Must transform them! Don't think about the past, the past is gone, why think about it? That is our biggest disease, still wanting to drag the past into the present. Can't stop thinking about the past all day! The past has passed, is it still there? Can't take it back! There is also a plan for the future of tens of thousands of years. No matter how much you plan, your life will last for decades! "People don't have a hundred good days, but they always have a thousand good days" (People don't have a hundred good days, but they always worry for a thousand days). The future hasn't come yet, don't worry! Come, let's talk. The past has passed, don't think about it. The future hasn't happened yet, so don't care! What about now? The present is non-stop. Yesterday is not today. Immediately finish teaching today, then wait until tomorrow to talk again; Let's not talk about tomorrow anymore! Tomorrow is tomorrow, the present does not exist! Suppose you can not think about yesterday's things, today's things that won't last, tomorrow's things that haven't come yet, just ignore it! You can reach that level, I say: Even if you have not attained enlightenment, at least there will be no afflictions!

How do human afflictions arise? You search and think for yourself! In the past, during the Tang Dynasty, there was a Prime Minister named Ngu Trieu An. The Emperor invited the state minister[30] to come, of course the Prime Minister had to serve the king. He asked the national teacher: "Dear national teacher! I want to ask you, where does affliction arise? What is affliction?" The national teacher rolled his eyes and said: "Your servant still asks about Buddhism." He immediately got angry and replied: "Even though I am a slave, I am the emperor's servant. I am the Prime Minister, above tens of thousands of people. Why do you despise me like that?" Got angry! The National Master said: "Don't be angry, afflictions arise from there. That is affliction. That is ignorance, ignorance arises from there." Immediately, Ngu Trieu An was enlightened, bowed his head, and thanked the national teacher. That is the opportunity to preach the Dharma. Everyone, think: Can we also be enlightened like that? It's usually because of a sentence that touches your premonition and you will immediately become enlightened.

Enlightenment is cumulative, do you believe it or not? I can testify for you! I hadn't finished elementary school, had no educational qualifications, and when I went to Co Son Buddhist Academy, they basically didn't accept me. Those who study the Avatamsaka Sutra are all university students, Hua Yan University! But after two or three years, why can I enroll? After that, I went to Qingdao, studied worldly dharma, the Four Books, the Five Classics, whatever it was, I studied it all. I am better than others in that I have a particularly agile mind, and once I learn, I don't forget. Currently, I tell everyone, even if I read a novel, I can tolerate it. Sometimes I tell old stories, especially about cause and effect, I tell everyone the story of Te Cong. Teaching in the countryside, many Dharma friends do not have any level of education! You have to tell stories, they will be very interested and will be able to enter fully. Karma and retribution are like that, they will believe. “Buddhism is in the world, never separates from the world to attain enlightenment” (Buddhism is in the world, never leaves the world to achieve enlightenment). As long as you clearly understand that worldly dharma is Buddha dharma, separate from life, where can you find Buddha dharma? Can you find it? In your daily life, you should at any time put down your discriminatory mind, visualize the things that are present, so that you do not have the idea of ​​discrimination. When you encounter trouble, you let it go, you don't have trouble, you know it's fake. When you have the most fun, you know it's fake, don't take it as real! There is nothing wonderful, everything passes. Especially when you are in tribulation, you should see all dharmas as illusory. I can testify to everyone. I was in prison for quite a long time, thirty-three years. Many young people have not been in prison as long as I have, from 1950 to 1982! [Starting from] January 1950 [I was in prison], very simply, you asked: "Old monk! Why did you commit a crime?" I replied: “I did not commit a crime!’ “If I did not commit a crime, why did I stay in prison for so long?” “People forced me to believe in the Chinese Communist Party, I didn't believe it. So just stay in jail!” The longer you stay in prison, the longer! Until now, I'm still like that. It's like that in the country! If you lock up then lock up, if you kill then kill, it doesn't matter! My beliefs have not changed! Surely everyone knows: That's my nature! It was like that when I was in Mainland, and it's like that now. In the future, forever!

Believe that all dharmas are born of causes and conditions, but that dharmas have been born of causes and conditions, causes and conditions can also destroy dharmas, and dharmas are also destroyed by causes and conditions. All those who have a mind that makes distinctions, illusions, untruths, nothing is real, why still don't think clearly? Currently, there are Dharma friends here who send me letters, [complaining] that in work, in life, in hope, there are many things that are not as expected. How can everything be as expected? You are born in the Sa Ba world, born in this afflicted [situation], unless you study Buddha, let go, see clearly, without afflictions, then you will get what you want. Make others please you? In this world, from a President to a beggar, you ask them, [you will see] they never have a satisfactory time! Unless you clearly understand, eliminate afflictions, study Buddhism deeply, and can practice, then you will get what you want. Every dharma learning method has a central thought. Regardless of any sutra, it all has a central idea. The central thought is one, not this sutra or that set of sutras [each sutra has its own separate thoughts], every sutra is “impermanent, suffering, emptiness, non-self”, but is separated into Hinayana and Mahayana. You must understand this principle, apply all the Buddha Dharma you have learned to your actions, especially your thoughts, then you will be successful, at least you can eliminate afflictions. Especially when it comes to unsatisfactory things, if you know how to think, you should think like this: "Human life is like that, accidents are like that." Many people ask me: "How did you survive thirty-three years in prison?" I said: "You see I'm living very well right now. Not only surviving, but living a long life."

Buddhism says “all things are mind-only”, now we are talking about “all things are mind-only”. This mind completes the ten dharma realms. The four teachings say that "the three thousand natures" are just a thought that is present in your mind. Can you explain it or not? The sutra teaches: You must use your mind to think and debate a lot. If not, how do you enter? You should not consider [Buddhism] as written words. Studying Buddhist scriptures is not about studying written words, but you must put your efforts into action. That is, the sutra teaches you how to do it, so do it! If you do it, try it and see, how does life and death come about? Every sutra teaches to let go of birth and death, teaches to let go, let go and become free. Those who cannot let go will be troubled. Many Dharma friends wrote to me, [complaining that they were full of] afflictions. I also can't tell them directly: "Where is the affliction? You take it out for others to see!" You can't get it out! Affliction is invisible, formless. Everyone understands that Phien is very unstable, one moment like this, another moment like that. You can [control] this body very easily, but you can't control your mind! One moment it runs here, the next moment it passes there! Now sitting here listening to a lecture, that person is thinking about cars, thinking about family outside, his mind is thinking a lot, he can't concentrate on one thought, can he not differentiate? Everything that has distinctions is an illusion, not real! You should meditate like that.

The so-called Consciousness, Feeling, Thought, Action, will include thoughts of remembering the past. The past also creates intention in thought: "I did this wrong, how should I fix it?" It's over, it's too late for you to fix it! Don't think about it, just let it go. Everyone practice, don't drag yesterday's things into today, let it go. You can let go like that, naturally you will be free, there will be no distinction, because it's all fake! Everyone knows this principle clearly, but cannot do it! What child is born to its mother and brings nothing with it? What does it bring? Think about it everyone, including ourselves, what did you bring here when you were born? There is nothing! When you leave, what can you take with you? The morality is very simple, everyone understands it clearly, but they cannot let go of their greed. If you are not dead, you are not yet free from greed. No matter how greedy you are, when you die, you can't take anything with you, including your own body. You die, are cremated, and turn into ashes. No matter how beautifully you build a tomb, it's still useless! Currently, in Mainland China, there are many cases of ancient tombs, where all the tombs from the Han Dynasty have been dug up! Graves for nearly two thousand years have been dug up. Two thousand years is still very short, what can you have left? No! There isn't anything! All dharmas are inherently empty, sentient beings cannot let them go! You can't let it go, [so] what can you keep? We can see with our own eyes, can what happened a hundred years ago still exist? When friends from Beijing come to visit me on Wutai Mountain, I often tell them: When I came to Beijing, Beijing had only twenty-six thousand residents. Currently there are more than one thousand thousand. The people of that time have long passed away; How do they know that Beijing's eight gates and eight gates will be completely destroyed? What else? Every phenomenon in all dharmas in the world and in everyday society reminds us that "is like an illusion, like a transformation". We are an infinite illusion, not real.

The so-called Consciousness, Feelings, Thoughts, Actions, thoughts, memories, predestined thoughts, awareness, all dharmas, all kinds of mental numbers, all kinds of thoughts that arise in the mind, you say, is it blue, is it yellow, is it red, or is it white? There is no color. All colors do not exist, mind is not colors. What about long, short, square, round, big, small? False thoughts and attachments! Therefore, speaking of all the worlds in the ten directions of nothingness, you want to find the shape of the mind, can you find it? No! Moreover, square can turn into round, round can turn into square, the phenomenon changes infinitely. The world has not always been [fixed] like that, so why be attached? Because of deep-rooted ignorance from the past. Simply put, ignorance is basically not understanding anything. Ignorance is not understanding clearly. What don't you understand? Not understanding clearly where birth and death come from, not understanding clearly what suffering is, what happiness is? Is there a standard? Suffering and happiness have no standard, they are all illusory realms. Why consider the illusory realm to be real? Because it's crazy. Therefore, it is called delusion; that is delusion; But our mind doesn't know, we ourselves don't know. Who can know himself? For example, if we will die tomorrow, no one knows, we always think that tomorrow we will absolutely not die. Tomorrow and tomorrow, there will be absolutely no death; That's all I think! Do you know what happened suddenly and unexpectedly? See that all conditioned dharmas are illusory and can disappear at any moment. The reason why you think of knowing and comparing "what is me and what is mine" is the truth that that awareness has no true appearance, it is just an illusion of comparison. Because of what is thought by that delusional mind, there is nothing real, cannot be seen, and has the nature of being "perishable". Who can find something indestructible in this world, yes or no? Who can find something indestructible? There is none in this world! All speech takes language as the standard. Can writing books and making theories be considered standards? The predecessors did [write books and make statements], and the successors negated those theories!

Actually there is nothing, it is due to the accumulation of your karma from beginningless lifetimes until now. According to the Mahayana Arising of Faith, the formation of causes and conditions is [like] when you enter a place where incense is made, so your body naturally has a fragrant scent. If there is a day, such as a person working as a fecal cleaner at the Beijing Sanitation Department, he or she has to touch human feces all day long, even if he showers several times a day, it still won't work! Others still stay away from that person, that person's body smells bad! Depends on what profession you do! You can choose your own karma, why don't you choose good karma, instead you only choose bad karma? We often talk about karma; that's one type. Another type is the accumulation of causes and conditions from beginningless kalpas up to now, which have considered all false illusions to be truly existent. For example, our physical body is inherently perishable, but in order to protect this body, I wonder how much brainpower is spent? No matter what method you use, you cannot preserve or protect the illusory realm! You must see clearly. As long as you want to live a few more years, the more attached you are, the more afraid you are, the more ghosts there are! There is a saying: "The more afraid, the more ghosts there are!" The more you hope to live a few more years, the shorter your life span will be. The more we talk about methods of protecting life, the more they cannot be maintained.

Currently, when it comes to cancers, cancer occurs without reason. If you have cancer, there is nothing you can do, there are many [cases where you have to give up]. Is it possible to choose by your will? Normally, if you want to live a long life, but on the other hand, you do all the bad things that cause your physical body to be consumed. How can you live a long life? Due to your delusional mind, all kinds of dharmas arise from your mind. These dharmas affect your mind, causing you to be attached to every thought and unable to let go. If you like something, you want to have it. If you don't like something, you want to throw it away. Because of that mentality of wanting to gain or lose, you don't know how much effort you've spent, but there's still no way, even if you give up, you can't give up! If you can't separate, you can't be separated, but if you hope to reach you, you can't achieve it. As long as you wish to achieve it, once you achieve it, it is still an illusion, because it has no real substance. Just because your physical eyes cannot see, your thinking mind cannot think. Because in the mind there is a collection of causes and conditions, karma from beginningless time until now, that is a collection of causes and conditions. Accumulation then creates the current, the current accumulates, accumulates and then turns into seeds. Therefore, all kinds of mistakes arise. If you want to clear away those mistakes, recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva a lot!

tom_tat: Volume 11 (Sutra) If one lacks the ability to distinguish and perceive, one cannot distinguish between the ten directions and three worlds, necessarily different realms and appearances. noi_dung:
Lecture 11

(Sutra) Weakness of the unconscious ability to distinguish the false, blocking the ten directions and three worlds from necessarily different realms and appearances.
(Sutra: If there is no perception to be able to distinguish, there will not be all the different realms in the ten directions and three lifetimes).

Last time, we talked about the mind and the external world, the external world is an illusion. The mind gives birth to all realms, so there are [all realms]. That is called “when the mind arises, all dharmas arise, when the mind ceases, all dharmas cease”. It is completely about our mind, making us understand our own present mind. We often talk about delusion, delusion is not real, it is a false imagination. The roots of that false imagination are very deep, where does the false imagination arise from? Depend on Truth to start. Because all sentient beings from time immemorial until now, have been brought together by ignorance and ignorance, they have manifested the form of the realm. That thought is the thought that comes from your awareness, it is the thought that comes from your thinking (thinking), it does not know itself. Each person is like that, the mind cannot know the mind itself, it is an illusion that it exists. At that time, from feeling arises awareness, from awareness comes thinking, from that way of thinking we divide what is us and what is mine. To tell the truth, these things have no signs of enlightenment, no awareness, no signs at all. Because our illusory mind has no real reality, it changes unpredictably. Can we see our own mind? No one can see the mind. If you see the mind, you will attain enlightenment! It is all due to the formation of external realms that appear; We call all the appearances that you can see “illusory realm appearances”. Form is born from the mind. In the sutras, the Buddha taught us that when your mind arises, all kinds of dharmas arise; when your mind ceases, all kinds of dharmas cease. All types of dharmas are one mind. The appearance of the external realm can be clearly seen; Although you can see the form, you cannot achieve it!

But the things taught in Buddhist scriptures sometimes specialize in mind dharma, taking away all the signs of the realm, all the signs of the realm are illusory. If we only discuss Eye Consciousness, Ear Consciousness, Sick Consciousness, Tongue Consciousness, Body Consciousness, Consciousness, the seventh consciousness of Manhāna, the eighth consciousness of Alai Da, these are called “eight minds” or “eight consciousnesses of mind”. When your mind contemplates all dharmas, when your mind confronts all dharmas that belong to the appearance of the external realm, when your consciousness distinguishes all dharmas, that is called "cognitive conditions", all of which are conditions that arise according to ideas. Therefore, we see all things, long, short, big, small, square, round, all things, all forms, in general are your false distinctions, allowing us to recognize all dharmas. All external appearances are called realms, but realm appearances are distinct. When we start thinking, attachments will arise. Attachment is to something good that we hope to have and take as our own; For things that are not satisfactory, one wishes to throw them away. From there, troubles arise, wanting to gain but not achieving, [the desire to get rid of] but not being able to give up. Because I want to get it but can't get it, I want to give it up but I can't give it up; That's why it's called “karma”. “Karma” means “creation”, created by oneself. Originally, everything was an illusion, non-existent; But we are deceived, thinking that the mind is real. It's your feeling and your discrimination. All distinctions are completely fake!

Therefore, in the scriptures it is said that you can know, distinguish, that is, distinguish the past, present, and future in the ten directions. The ten directions are places, “past, present, future” is time. Whether speaking in terms of space or speaking in terms of time, the appearance of different realms is entirely due to the mind. The sutra teaches: "When the mind arises, all dharmas arise. The mind ceases, all dharmas cease". Because we have “seeing, hearing, good, knowing”, then from seeing, hearing, knowing, knowing, discrimination arises: For what we ourselves like, we hope to achieve it, hope to maintain it, hope it will not change, impossible! What you hope to achieve is not achieved. What you don't want to achieve are things that you don't like and want to leave them, but you can't separate them. When you hope to gain but cannot get, wish to separate but cannot separate, at that time, many afflictions will arise. Everyone, please remember a little bit, are the things you have experienced all like that? It doesn't exist, but due to illusion, attachments arise, all things are fake. For example, if we “do business”, commonly called “trade”, whether you trade at a loss, make a fortune or lose capital are all born from your mind. Why lose money and not make money? The method is not correct! Why is the method incorrect? You have no wisdom, you cannot see! Not just business, even in life, you do all your careers like that. This story shows what [those things] are all about? It's all delusion, nothing is real. According to the concept of human life, what did you bring here when you were born? Bringing the afflictions of greed, anger, and ignorance here, everything else is gone! Is there any child born without anything? But when you die, when this life span has ended, you carry with you the karma you created in this life and cannot let it go. Besides karma, what else can you achieve? Burning that person's body is burning the physical body. Can karma be burned or not? Can't burn! Still continues to exist!

(Sutra) Of course, the dharma stage is incapable of self-existence, due to the inherent delusion of the mind. The position is necessarily the realm of non-thought as existence, perception as self, perception as other. The existence of all dharmas is incapable of self-existence, there is no difference, it only depends on the false mind, there is no understanding of the inner word without origin. The pre-existence knowledge of the realm, the perception of dharma, the perception of existence, the non-existence, the non-existence, the perception of existence, the perception of existence, the perception of non-existence, the perception of good, the perception of evil, the desire to give birth to limitless and boundless dharma perceptions. In the same way as knowing, all dharmas will be accompanied by false thoughts, depending on the original mind.
(Sutra: Because all dharmas cannot exist by themselves, they only depend on false discrimination. called all realms, each one does not think it exists. Knowing this is self, knowing that is other. Therefore, all dharmas cannot exist on their own, so there is no difference. Only depending on the false mind, not knowing, not knowing within itself (the false mind), thinking that there is a realm to know outside, mistakenly giving rise to all kinds of thoughts, thinking that there is, thinking that there is not, thinking that this, thinking that, Thinking that it is right, thinking that it is wrong, thinking that it is good, thinking that it is bad, leading to confusion gives birth to boundless and limitless dharma thoughts. You should know like this: All dharmas are born from delusion, relying on delusion as the root.

Therefore, in this passage of scripture, [Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva clearly teaches]: The nature of all dharmas is neither Existence nor Nonexistence. They are established due to the false thoughts of discrimination of sentient beings. Based on the discriminating minds of sentient beings, we establish all dharmas. All external realms arise from the mind, all dharmas arise from the minds of sentient beings. All dharmas are destroyed by the minds of sentient beings. Does the dharma itself consider it to be conditioned or unconditioned? Does it know that this is the Self and that other things are not the Self? There is no such distinction. Dharma itself has no distinction. You can take any dharma at will, all dharmas cannot exist on their own, and there is no difference, they are all determined by delusion. Because of that reason, I don't know, I'm not clear. Don't know, don't understand what? Inside, there is no such thing as non-existence, it is all an illusion. Why do we sometimes give birth to so many minds? Every Dharma friend is like that, because the appearance of the realm in front of the senses recognized in the present, including our body, our body is the appearance of the realm of the mind, everyone should contemplate like that, recognize like that, all are ways of thinking arising from delusion: "This is good, this is not good, this is good, this is evil!" Originally, all dharmas did not exist, [yet] falsehood arose in all dharmas, every thought was attached to it, and discrimination did not give up! Anything you don't like, want to get rid of, want to get rid of but can't get rid of! There is no inside or outside, there is no long or short, there is no big or small, there is no square or round.

Why are there such and such objects? Due to the false mind of comparison, it is all due to the false mind that clings and does not let go. All living beings are like that; that is affliction. Because when you hope to get something good, you hope to get it, but if you don't get it, troubles will arise. As for the realm you don't like, you don't want to see it, but you can't give it up. Isn't that what you want to have but can't get, what you want to give up but can't let go of? Isn't that affliction? Of all the dharmas, suppose you think that they do not really exist, are illusory, not real, very false, arising from false thoughts; As for false thoughts, we have no way. What you hope to achieve is nothing, basically there is nothing! If you want to quit, it's the same.

Therefore, based on what the scriptures said, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: All dharmas cannot be had by oneself. How does it exist? It is due to false discrimination that it exists, and it is born due to false discrimination. That is, all attachments, all the signs of the realm, each of them cannot be thought to exist. What is self? What is forgiveness? Know that it is an attachment. This body is called self, knowing that other body is someone else's body. All dharmas are not self-determined to exist, there is no difference, there is no disagreement, how do they arise? That is delusion. Don't know, don't understand clearly that there is nothing inside. We don't know this, we can't understand it, we can't understand it clearly. Our body is non-existent. It is the form of the realm; That is, all the signs of the external realm that we see are dharmas that belong to delusion. Due to all kinds of dharma thoughts (ways of thinking about dharmas) that are created by false thoughts, saying yes or no, saying that, saying this, saying right or wrong, saying bad things, saying good things, until the confusion arises of boundless dharma thoughts depending on the appearance of dharmas. You should only contemplate that all dharmas are illusory, not real. Truth is no change, no destruction, no difference. All dharmas do not really exist.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: It takes illusion as its basis. Delusion itself cannot exist, [so] can all dharmas born of delusion exist? They are born of illusion, yet [living beings] still cling to things that are born of illusion. They don't exist, they just pretend to be “generals of the realm”! People give it a fake name, not genuine. Because all external scenes are false, the delusional mind that arises is also false. The mind gives birth to all dharmas, your delusional mind gives birth to all dharmas. All dharmas are idealistic, still fake. That mind is not the true mind, but a delusional mind. The true heart has no words!

(Sutra) Of course, the mind is deluded without a self-determined form. try, talk about the mind.
thinking, knowing the previous realm, so it is called mind).

Can we find the form of that mind? The mind itself has no form. The mind in our body is the “flesh group mind” (heart of flesh), that is not the mind. The heart in your physical body is not a mind, it is just a form, depending on the outside world to give birth to all predestined thoughts. Due to the conditions of mindfulness, he confirmed all the signs of the external realm, so he named that badge the Mind. For example, the heart, spleen, lungs, and liver are all impostors. How does the mind arise? Due to the appearance of the external realm, it exists. Because there is a realm, there is a mind. The mind is born from the scene. The mind is inherently unborn and exists due to the environment. Due to the appearance of the external realm, the mind is born. Can the mind be found? Until you have recognized that mind, that is called “clear mind of seeing nature”, that mind is real, indescribable, indescribable. What shape does that mind have? That mind is achieved by us. If you go to Mainland China and look at the Zen halls in the temples and pagodas, [you will see] that place is always called the Selected Buddha School, implying that "the mind is empty before you can pass the exam". Your mind must be Empty to achieve success. Can our mind be empty?

(Sutra) Trying to deceive the evil mind in the foreground, although the sentence is similar, the origin is endless, the child tries to deceive the mind's energy. necessarily the original master realm. The reason why it's fake? The practitioner falsely believes that the mind is unaware of the one form of the dharma realm, trying to convince the mind that there is ignorance. Because of ignorance, the force of cause and effect leads to a false realm, but because of ignorance and destruction, the realm is necessarily destroyed. Non-clothing is necessarily a realm of self-perpetuity, it is said that the realm of existence is ignorance, and non-clothed herons are born of ignorance. Are Buddhas necessarily in a realm of no birth and ignorance? The realm of attachment is destroyed, the mind of ignorance is destroyed. Of course, the natural realm must come to pass, the physical nature will self-destruct, and the taste will be permanent. Humanity as a test of meaning, Thi Co Nhan theory necessarily all dharmas rely on the mind as the origin.
(Sutra: Again, that false mind and the previous realm (the external realm present in front of the senses) Although they all depend on each other, they cannot arise in order, but that false mind can be the origin of all realms. Why is it that because of the false mind, it is impossible to understand the dharma realm? Therefore, it is said that due to the power of ignorance, false realms appear, and all realms will be destroyed It is not possible to understand clearly. Saying "ignorance exists in the realm", nor does ignorance arise depending on the realm. Because all Buddhas in all realms do not give birth to ignorance, and do not destroy ignorance based on the realm, because all realms are inherently self-destructive, so it only means that "all dharmas depend on the mind as the root".

The minds we use in the present are all illusory realms, not your [true] mind; But that false mind of ours and all the appearances that appear before our eyes (the scriptures call those appearances “forerealm”) rely on each other. The mind arises from the scene, whatever you see, whatever you think, the mind is born. Scenes arise from the mind. When the mind is born, all dharmas arise; when the mind dies, all dharmas disappear. The mind and the appearance of the external realm, which comes first? Which comes later? You cannot find [the order] before or after. When the mind arises, there is no before or after. We believe that delusion is the source of all realms. When the mind is born, all dharmas are born. The mind is the master. If the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. Why say so? According to the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, due to a deluded mind one cannot know the one form of the Dharma realm; [The mind being talked about] here is a false mind, it will not know that the dharma realm is one form. Therefore it is said “the mind has ignorance”. Not knowing the one form of the Dharma realm is called “ignorance”. Depending on the power of ignorance, all realms are born. Because of non-existence we say existence, because of existence we say non-existence, existence and non-existence contrast each other. All the signs of the realm are destroyed, the realm cannot destroy itself. Due to the cessation of the mind, the scene is destroyed, due to the birth of the mind, the environment is born. The general realm has ignorance, ignorance means "not understanding". There is ignorance in the realm of the realm, does that ignorance arise from the realm? Realms give rise to ignorance, ignorance gives rise to all realms. Mahayana Arising the Faith says like that. That is the mind-ground method in studying Buddhism.

Everyone must listen patiently, you must contemplate: “When the mind arises, all dharmas arise”. As soon as you think, all dharmas arise. The destruction of the mind means you don't think about anything; When the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. Mahayana Awakening of Faith discusses this issue, many chapters [in that treatise] are all aimed at explaining this issue. An unconscious thought, initially due to lack of mindfulness (the mind is not mindful) in one thought, without awareness, there is ignorance. Due to ignorance, the karma of appearances, transformations, and manifestations arise. [This story is often described as] “one unenlightened thought gives birth to three manifestations” (due to one unconscious thought, three manifestations are born, i.e. the appearance of karma, the appearance of transformation, and the appearance of appearance). Those three signs are fundamental ignorance. Until those three manifestations are cut off, the Eight Bodhisattva Bodhisattvas can cut off the appearance, the Nine Bodhisattvas can cut off the transformation, and the Ten Bodhisattvas can cut off the karma. Wait until you reach the eleventh state, that is, becoming a Buddha, then you can in one thought end the fundamental ignorance in those three manifestations and achieve Supreme Enlightenment. Because when those signs arise, the karma of the signs will create karma. The appearance of wisdom, the appearance of continuity, the appearance of karma, the appearance of karma, the appearance of suffering, each after being coarser than the previous. The next appearance is coarser than the previous one, meaning the next thought is coarser than the previous thought. Because the next thought is coarser than the previous thought, it creates karma for sentient beings of the ordinary status. Karma immediately binds you (that is the karma system of suffering), making it impossible for you to escape; Now we are all bound by karma. When you quickly stop, you will know that the nature of karma is inherently empty, that the nature of karma does not exist, it is empty. Why is there? Because of the scene, karma is inherently empty. Because of the scene, there is [karma]. The scene is not real, it's all fake. If the scene disappears, all the signs of the realm will not exist. The realm no longer exists, the mind becomes clear. That "clarity" is just eliminating the signs such as karma, transformation, continuity, karma of suffering, starting karma, karma will not bind you. We are bound by karma. Your good karma is also karma, and your evil karma is also karma. Because there is evil, we must practice goodness, eliminate evil, and practice goodness. Evil is no longer there, evil is no longer established, good is no longer established.

Therefore, if ignorance is destroyed, the realm will be destroyed. When the realm is destroyed, all appearances are destroyed. Because the realm has ignorance; If there is no realm, can ignorance still arise? Ignorance arises in the realm. Without realms, we realize that all realms are false. Therefore, the Shurangama Sutra says: "the weakness of seeing the signs is not a sign" (if you see the signs that are not signs), all the signs of the realm are not real, do not exist, "you will not see the Tathagata" (then see the Tathagata). Until that time comes to practice, it is completely a mind-ground method. How does it arise? Fate, fateful thoughts. Due to the arising of all external conditions, new growth arises, from the appearance of karma, due to growth, new appearances appear. Appearance then accepts attachment, insists on attachment, attachment is removed. All dharmas come from just one thought in the mind. All dharmas, often called “ten thousand dharmas”, countless dharmas exist, depend on your mind to accept them. Where does the basis of all delusional minds, the search for all delusions, the basis of all delusional minds arise? The mind does not exist, there is no realm, then that mind appears. Because the mind is inherently unborn, it comes from the scene, does the scene come first, or does the mind come first? Please research this issue yourself! [As for the question] "Does the scene come first, or does the mind come first?", when the scene and mind arise, there is no before or after. Does the scene come first or the mind? Depending on the scene, the mind is born, and the scene depends on the mind to appear. Without mind, there will be no scene. How do all the basic realms arise? This principle, if stated out loud, would be very difficult to understand. Until you understand clearly, it will be impossible to describe. Cannot use language to express, can only use the mind to comprehend, cannot use language to convey.

A special feature of Chinese Zen Buddhism is enlightenment and enlightenment. Until a person has clearly understood his mind and seen his nature, ask him to say what is it like to clear his mind and see his nature? What is mind? [No matter what that person says], do you understand clearly? Not at all! Therefore, it is said that “language is cut off” (language is cut off), [that is] there is no language, it is cut off. What about the thinking mind? “The place of cessation of the mind” can only be understood by the mind, it cannot be described or transmitted. That is the “clear mind and see the nature” of Zen Buddhism. But speaking according to the teachings, in the present realm, your false mind arises. If you don't have false thoughts, you won't have the present realm; That is the scene that depends on the mind. If the mind has no scene, how can it arise? Because of the scene, the mind is born. Therefore, when it arises, in the end is it the appearance of the illusory realm that comes first, or the mind that comes first? Or is there a difference between mind and scene, are they definitely two things? Isn't it two things? One is the predestined thought, the other is the mind. When it arises, there will be no before or after! If you can find a before-and-after order, it is an illusion of discrimination, there is no before-and-after. Normally speaking, because our mind thinks, there is a realm, and because of the outside realm, your mind (delusional mind) arises. The realm is the source. If there is no such realm, your mind will not arise, because the dharma realm has no form. The Dharma Realm is formless. A deluded mind does not know the one form of the Dharma realm; If you want to distinguish and search for the source of the realm's appearance, you won't be able to find it! Why is that, what is the cause? Because we do not clearly understand the Dharma Realm's one form and meaning, that's what it means.

I often think like this, how do I think? I give an example for everyone to hear, such as talking about Truong Giang. The origin of the Truong Giang, we find in the upper reaches of Qinghai province. In Qinghai province, the Yangtze River is called Tongtian River. Thong Thien River is located between Ngoc Thu and Nang Lung districts of Qinghai province. On the map, the upper reaches of the Tong Thien River are called “Nian So River” by the Qinghai people. Nianchu (Nyang Chu tsangpo) is Tibetan, not Chinese. This area is a Tibetan ethnic area, inhabited by the Tibetan minority. But the Nien So River has no source, within a distance of two or three thousand miles, the water rises up. Everyone, don't think of this as listening to a story, but think that I want to talk about "mind source" (source of mind), so use this story as an example. Thong Thien River flows into the Tay Khang region, now in Sichuan province. Tong Thien River flows to Ngoc Thu district of Qinghai province, no longer called Tong Thien river, but changed its name to Jinsha Giang. Jinsha River flows from Sichuan province to Yunnan called Nojiang. When it flows through Sichuan, it changes its name to Jialing River. The Jialing River flows to Chongqing city and then downstream, there are many tributaries, not just one stream, [at that time, the river was] called Truong Giang. The Yangtze River flowing from Nanjing onwards is called the Yangtze River. Therefore, the Yangtze River flows into Shanghai, from Shanghai into the sea. Truong Giang from its origin, a stream of water with countless names[31]. It is still the same stream of water, just water, without a place name, whenever it flows to an area, it is named by the people living in that area. [Even though there are many different names], what difference does that country make? What name does the water itself have? Is there any area? Absolutely nothing, it is a stream of water like that.

The origin of the Yellow River is quite simple, right in Huangzhong district, Qinghai province, within a range of about six or seven hundred miles. If you want to build a road in Thanh Hai, that land is muddy, there is no way, people's feet sink, horses' hooves sink, how can we build a national highway? How to do it? Use salt from the Star Sea. Tinh Tu Hai is in the mountains on the border of Ngoc Thu district and Tay Ninh provincial capital of Thanh Hai province. Within a range of about a thousand miles, there is a “hai” on the left and a “hai” on the right. Why is it called Hai? Originally a small lake, but the water was salty, it turned into water in the summer and into a salt puddle in the winter. The Qinghai region of Tibet's Khang Khu (formerly Kham province of Tibet) uses salt from this place. In the summer, the lake is water, in the winter the water turns into salt, like the sea drying up. That place was about five or six meters deep and was all liquid mud. There was no way to build a road, so salt was poured in to fill it. You can use salt to build roads, but the source of the Yellow River is cut off and underground water can no longer rise! The Yellow River is caused by rain in the mountains of Qinghai and Gansu, small rivers drain into the main stream. The water from the source of the Yellow River at Yellow Central was cut off. We talk about all the signs of that realm according to their geographical appearance. When the mind arises, all dharmas arise, which are completely created by the mind. If it is changed by human power, it will no longer exist and will be completely destroyed. The mountains where the flow originates are all like that.

Dharmas depend on each other. You understand this principle: Our deluded minds become more and more deeply deluded, that is, they become more heavily infected, the more infected they become, the more seriously they become infected. Therefore, the Sixth Patriarch said "Originally there is no one thing" (initially there is not one thing), everything does not exist, "where is the earth stained with dust?" That is the basic source; But because of that person's attachments, false thoughts arise, everywhere are obstacles. Cultivators teach you "to defeat false thoughts, promise that the Dharmakaya will be active" (kill all false thoughts, let your Dharmakaya live). You don't kill false thoughts! You have been able to kill false thoughts, without giving rise to false thoughts, your true mind immediately appears. Now we have arisen all dharma appearances based on the power of ignorance. Ignorance is not clear, why is it called ignorance? I'm not clear, I want to be clear. “Praying for clarity” is broken, becoming more and more confused, more and more obscure, giving rise to all the realms of greed, anger, ignorance, and arrogance. If we know that all dharmas do not arise spontaneously, ignorance will be destroyed. If ignorance is destroyed, all realms will be destroyed. Therefore, the Origin of Faith Luan says: “One unenlightened thought gives birth to three sacrifices”, that is, every wrong thought will give birth to three manifestations (karma appearance, transformation appearance, manifestation appearance). “The realm is the condition” (The realm is the condition), the appearance of the external realm is the condition for you, in your mind you then recite the condition, “the six gross appearances grow” (the six gross appearances grow), becoming more and more coarse, that is, the origin of Or. Start Or then create karma. When you create karma, karma binds you. Once bound by karma, you will be attached and unable to let go, meaning you will be rotated within the framework. Therefore, karma arises from ignorance!

Due to this reason, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva to say: “All Buddhas are not necessarily born in ignorance” (In all realms, all Buddhas do not give birth to ignorance). Suppose we follow the Buddhas without giving rise to ignorance, that is, we do not follow all the signs of the realm. All realms do not give rise to ignorance. Therefore there is no destruction. All birth is no birth, is there still death? It also does not depend on the appearance of the realm to destroy, so there is no birth and death. Because if you destroy the mind of ignorance, the scene will disappear. The mind is gone, the scene is also destroyed, the scene is calm, “the mind is gone, the scene is still, two sentences are empty” (the mind is gone, the scene is quiet, both sides are empty). Both sides are completely absent. Originally it did not exist, that is, the nature of the unborn, undying self, which has never existed before. That is the dharma of existence (dharma that has never existed). Use this principle to say that all dharmas depend on the mind as the root. Based on this principle, it is said: "All dharmas depend on the mind. When the mind arises, dharmas arise; when the mind disappears, dharmas disappear". Therefore, when cultivating in the mountains, no signs are seen. What shop is that? Contemplate the mind. The mind is not born, the dharma immediately ceases, that is, the dharma is also quiet. That's why it is said that "when the mind arises, all dharmas arise; when the mind ceases, all dharmas cease". This morality is very deep.

For example, Zen Buddhism “point straight to the mind, see your nature and become Buddha”. Because our mind comes from the scene. For example, the Sixth Patriarch was in the Fifth Patriarch's ashram. The Fifth Patriarch prepared to hand over the throne, select the Patriarch, and select his successor. He told everyone to compose verses. At that time, Master Than Tu was the Supreme Master under the throne of the Five Patriarchs, everyone recognized him as a monk with great wisdom. The Fifth Patriarch told each person to compose a verse for the Patriarch to comment on. Master Than Tu wrote: “The body is the Bodhi tree, the mind is like a bright mirror, at all times it needs to be awakened, the objects are not exposed to the earth” (The body is the Bodhi tree, the mind is like a shining mirror, always diligently clean, don't let it be stained with dust). Everyone says this poem is so well composed: Our body is like a Bodhi tree, our mind is pure like a bright, clean mirror. You must regularly clean yourself, lest the dust covers your mind and it will no longer be clean. Regularly diligently clean and sweep, don't let dust cover you! At that time, the Sixth Patriarch arrived there, he had not yet become a monk, not even a novice monk, he had not shaved his head yet, he was a layman who believed in Buddha. He was assigned the job of pounding rice, that is, pounding rice into rice, pounding rice in the grinding room. He heard the story and immediately asked, others read it to him, praising Master Than Tu for being so brilliant! He said: "That verse is completely bad!" Others were very surprised. He also found a lay person and said, "I also compose verses, please write them for me." He said: “The original Bodhi tree, the clear mirror of the heron and the platform, originally had no one thing, who in the world is the earth?” (Bodhi is not the root, the mirror is not the platform, originally there was not a single thing, where was it stained with dust?) Originally there was not a single thing stained with dust. He also mentioned the verse. As soon as Master Five Patriarch Hoang Nhan saw it, he took off his shoes and wiped them away, saying "not good, not good". During the day he said "not good", at night, the Patriarch went to the Master's place to pound rice, impart the Dharma to the Sixth Patriarch, and said: "You should go immediately." Because everyone is fighting for the position, I'm afraid someone will hurt the master. Just like that, those who tried to hurt Him chased after Him. Therefore, the Sixth Patriarch lived in the group of bandits for fifteen years.

After that, the Master went to Quang Hieu Pagoda in Guangzhou. At Quang Hieu pagoda, two masters were arguing. They saw the phantom hanging there being swayed by the wind. One monk said it was the wind, the other said it was the wind. The two argued constantly. Master Sixth Patriarch told the two of them: "It's not the wind that moves, it's not the phan that moves, what moves? The mind pretends to move". Now we say this as “when the mind arises, all kinds of dharmas arise; when the mind dies, all kinds of dharmas cease”. After hearing that, the two monks were very surprised, then reported to Phuong Truong of Quang Hieu pagoda: "There is such a person coming here." At that time, the Master was a layman. Venerable An Tong immediately summoned ten great masters to perform the ceremony and ordain the precepts for the Master. After that, [Mr. An Tong] invited the Master to be the Phuong Truong of Quang Hieu pagoda, so that he could transmit the Dharma and preach the sutras. But preaching the sutras requires reading the sutras to others. The Sixth Patriarch was illiterate, but he could preach the sutras, and preached them very well, even though he was illiterate. That is, although the Basic Wisdom is complete, there is no skillful means. Why do Bodhisattvas have to learn the Five Insights? The reason is because of this. Basic Wisdom can enlighten enlightenment. Bodhisattvas from countless eons until now have learned about every matter of skillful means in the career of benefiting living beings. If they do not study, they will not know!

All Buddhas and all realms do not give birth to Ignorance. Furthermore, all realms do not exist. If the mind of ignorance is destroyed, basically all the signs of the realm do not exist, they will naturally disappear. Therefore, because of the mind, all dharmas are born; Because the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. That is called “cutting ignorance” (quickly ending ignorance). Chinese Zen Buddhism is “cutting off ignorance”. Even though we cut down ignorance, we still have to learn the career of benefiting others. That is why for the Five Insights, Bodhisattvas must learn the Five Insights. If you don't study something, you won't know it. When Buddhas and Bodhisattvas benefit sentient beings, each Bodhisattva's method of saving sentient beings is different, each using a different method. For example, we know the four great mountains, Ngu Dai Mountain Manjushri Bodhisattva takes great wisdom as the main essence. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at Cuu Hoa Mountain uses great vows as the main thing. Bodhisattva Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva considers great compassion as the main essence. Emei Shan Samantabhadra Bodhisattva in Sichuan takes great conduct as the main thing. Each Bodhisattva has a knack for benefiting living beings, and specializes in using the dharma he has attained to benefit living beings. Because of this principle, there are places where Buddhism is universal, and there are places where it is different. The Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma was asked by the Buddha to be spoken by the Bodhisattva of Persistence and Faith. The Buddha asked him to ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak. The meaning in the second half of the series is exactly the same as [other Mahayana sutras], the Mahayana teachings are all like that. However, the level of authority (the person who stands to request the Dharma) [in each sutra] is different, the form of language expressed in the preaching of the Dharma [of each sutra] is different. All realms that are inherently non-existent, the mind, the realm, and both are empty, all reach the meaning of Emptiness. That is true repentance. Using the wheel form to repent, the first half [of this sutra] is skillful means, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: In all the signs of the realm, all Buddhas do not give birth to ignorance. Because they do not pray for enlightenment, ignorance does not arise. Because if you don't depend on the signs of the realm of destruction, if you don't arise, you won't die. All dharmas are born due to causes and conditions, and once they are born due to conditions, they will definitely die due to causes and conditions. All dharmas arise due to causes and conditions. Once they arise due to causes and conditions, they will definitely also die due to causes and conditions. What if there is no birth? Without birth there is no death. Your mind of ignorance has been destroyed, your mind of ignorance is completely destroyed, all the signs of the realm are also destroyed. All realms have been destroyed, all dharmas depend on the mind as their root. Therefore, “mind only thinks of all things, all things only think of mind”.

(Sutra) Absolutely knowing that all dharmas are bound by the mind, their meaning is not different, they are fixed by the mind.
(Sutra: You should know that all dharmas are called mind, because the meaning is no different, they are all recorded taking in the mind).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: “You should know”; This is said to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. All dharmas are called mind. Because, using logic to say, The substance of all dharmas is mind. All minds are the Body of all dharmas. Mind and Body are no different. Because of using this principle to speak, it is said: "All dharmas are born from the mind". Separated from the mind, all dharmas will not exist. How to reveal our mind? Use all dharmas to manifest, mind only all dharmas, all dharmas only mind. When people study Vien Giao in Buddhism, they probably think that Vien Giao of Buddhism is extremely vague, just like we say "whenever we pull out a clump of hair and beard from a Ho person, we cannot distinguish between hair and beard". In fact, Vien Giao's teachings are divided very carefully! People feel confused because your wisdom is not up to the mark, you don't study well, so they criticize it as "vague". Why don't all sutras have as great a weight as the Avatamsaka Mahayana Sutra? You must know that the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra is the most complete, but there are too many methods for you to enter. All things are mind-only, where is the mind revealed? The mind is only the mind of all dharmas, all dharmas are only the mind. You turn it around: All things are mind, mind is all things. But do you understand clearly? Therefore, practice in Zen Buddhism has no other skillful means! Direct mind, mindfulness, idealism, [then again] direct mind, mindfulness, True Suchness, from our deluded mind we directly enter the true mind.

Therefore, we must practice for three great eons, [or according to Vien Giao, it would be] countless eons. You still have to practice faith, you have to ask for solutions, you have to practice, practice before you can attain enlightenment, [the order of practice is] “trust, resolve, practice, attain”. There is no need for Zen, Zen Buddhism says: “In Zen, one stick of incense, cut down super directly, immediately attain Bodhi”, immediately enlightenment. Can it be done or not? There are not many people who practice Zen, are they enlightened or not? Is it good to attain enlightenment? People who study Buddhism know that "being enlightened" is not at all true enlightenment, they still have to practice. When you carry out the career of benefiting living beings, you must study. Understanding your mind and seeing your nature is just that you have been enlightened, have clearly understood your mind, recognized your own mind, and absolutely do not have the skills to save sentient beings. The Avatamsaka Sutra is like that. No matter what position you reach, there is a method to gain birth [in that position]. Each position has its own method of benefiting, from the Ten Faiths to the Ten Pillars, the Ten Virtues, the Ten Dedications, the Ten Grounds, the Equal Enlightenment, the Wonderful Enlightenment, [reaching the Wonderful Enlightenment] is the ultimate attainment. In that situation, the student Thien Tai asked Manjushri Bodhisattva, and Manjushri Bodhisattva taught the student to worship Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. When worshiping Maitreya Bodhisattva, the student became Enlightened and reached the status of Buddha. Maitreya Bodhisattva taught his disciples to return to worship Manjushri Bodhisattva. That is Basic Wisdom. Manjushri Bodhisattva told his students to come and worship Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to learn skillful means. Gaining birth is not that easy! Therefore, the Bodhisattva must go through many great eons. We say “three great Asanga-kalpas”, that is the teachings of the Middle Vehicle, if according to the Avatamsaka Sutra, it would be countless, countless kalpas. Because of all the dharmas, if you don't study any subject you won't know, you must study it. Even though you have realized the Basic Wisdom, you have not yet achieved the Later Wisdom.

All dharmas are called mind. All dharmas are called mind because once you realize that the Body is no different, it is enough to realize the mind. All idealistic dharmas, why do you say that? All dharmas belong to the mind, the mind captures all dharmas, that is, the mind absorbs all dharmas. All dharmas still refer to the mind. Because all dharmas are mind-only, there is also a mind that gives rise to all dharmas. These two sentences can be said in reverse, meaning "the mind gives birth to all dharmas, all dharmas are only the mind". Only then can “the mind give birth to all dharmas”. Otherwise, the mind cannot arise, so all dharmas are called mind. Because of this principle, because it means “The body is one”, all dharmas also have the same mind, the thing that gives birth to all dharmas is the mind. The mind accomplishes all dharmas, completely belonging to the mind. Outside of mind there is no dharma, outside of dharma there is no mind. It's like that, please research! It contains countless meanings, it's not just that simple!

(Sutra) All dharmas are necessarily accompanied by the arising of the mind, the evil mind creates the appearance, harmony with children, co-living, Together and destroyed, together with non-existence Di necessarily the birth realm depends on the condition of the mind, ncontemplation continuously tries, children attain abbot, temporary existence.
(Sutra: Again, all dharmas arise from the mind, form the mind, and exist in harmony. The same birth, the same death, the same "no residence". Because all realms are conditioned only by the mind, connected in each thought, it is temporary.)

Because all dharmas arise from the mind, “when the mind arises, dharmas arise”. The mind gives rise to all dharmas; All dharmas and the effects of the mind are inseparable. Regardless of whether it is good or evil, in the end all dharmas are inseparable from the mind. The mind gives birth to good dharmas according to the Reality of True Suchness; When the mind gives rise to all evil things, it follows ignorance; Evil takes ignorance as its Essence. Therefore, dharmas and mind are in harmony, not two. The mind gives birth to dharmas; that is the mind that arises. The mind ceases, all dharmas cease. [That is] the mind and all dharmas are born and die together. The mind does not exist, the mind is empty. Since the mind is already empty, is there anything remaining? How to focus your mind? Doesn't stand! Basically, there is no mind, in what mind is there anymore? Everyone has read the Vajra Sutra and saw Subhūti asking the Buddha: “The clouds and clouds stay in the mind?”, [meaning] my mind cannot stay, how can I subdue the mind? Subhuti, who has cut off false views, is a Great Arhat, with the highest wisdom, so in the Vajra Sutra, he represents the question, or it can be said that he asks on behalf of the public.

In other words, although He has destroyed Thoughts and Thoughts, Ignorance and Tranquility have not yet been destroyed, His mind does not abide, nor can it subdue the mind. That's why he asked the Buddha how to control and subdue the mind. The Buddha taught: All dharmas have no place to abide, nor do they subdue the mind. The mind does not dwell anywhere, all dharmas originate from the human mind. Because the mind does not exist, all dharmas do not exist. All dharmas are appearances outside the mind. The mind gives birth to all dharmas, all dharmas are manifestations of the mind. Because the mind gives birth to all dharmas, it is said: "All dharmas are only the mind. All dharmas are the mind, the mind is all dharmas". Please research like that, you will clear your mind and realize your nature.

We just talk, not that we are enlightened. Ordinary people can rely on the teachings to understand, it can be said to be “equal to Buddha, equal to Buddha”, but the afflictions of Views and Thoughts will not be stopped! Buddha is the Omniscient One. [What we have presented above] is learning to follow Buddha, just learning to speak! What does it mean? [It means] not yet able to enter, not yet able to attain; But if you often practice like that, you will gradually enter. It is not mentioned in this sutra, but the Mahayana Arising Faith Commentary says there are two types of accumulation. If you practice regularly in that dharma, often study it with others, you will gradually enter it. That is “near pearls, one pretends to be red, one near wear, one pretends to be black” (near vermilion, it is red, near ink, it is black) as Mencius said. If you are near black substances, or near ink, it will naturally turn black. Whatever you see, learn it. There is another type of conditioning called “original nature” (existing in the original nature), and the other type is “cultivation training”, which is the external environment that trains your practice. Therefore, mind and scene are said in that way. Because all dharmas originate from the mind, they form the form of the mind. All dharmas form the appearance of the mind, all appearances are the mind, [so] the mind and dharmas are in harmony. Because the mind arises, dharmas arise; the mind ceases, all dharmas cease. That is the same birth, [the scriptures describe this as] “co-birth, same death” (same birth, same death). All dharmas are born, the appearance of all dharmas is conditioned by the mind.
