The mind is the condition of all dharmas, the condition of which there is no mind. Because the mind arises, [all dharmas exist], so the mind follows. What fate is that? Conditions follow all realms. The mind is not inherently born, it exists due to circumstances. Because it is conditioned to follow all the signs of the external realm, the mind is conditioned to follow the signs of the realm, and because of the scene, the mind is revealed. Fate has no self-nature, so why does it arise? Fate has no self-nature, it arises from the mind. From the mind, it returns to the mind.

Therefore, those who study Buddhism and study the teachings of the Complete Teaching will see that the words the Buddha taught us are completely perfect. If you want to look for edges, you won't find them, they're all stones! Where is the head? Where is the tail? No, it's round! Everyone must consider this, don't listen to the words or language, it won't work, you have to use your mind to enter into the contract. We see all things, we go to the department store, we go to Taipei City to see, your mind follows all kinds of things, it's the same with the department store, it's the same with tasting the food at the market. These things are born of the mind, all the signs of the realm are conditioned by the mind. Therefore, it is said that "the mind gives birth to dharmas; when the mind dies, all dharmas disappear." But that mind is continuous in each thought, forever and ever, and can maintain all dharmas. When it stays

Maintaining the dharmas is temporary.

This passage of scripture is intended to tell you: From the mind, all dharmas arise, that is called the General Part of the mind, that is, the General Part that arises from your own mind. All dharmas represent the mind, the mind is formless. [“Mind” mentioned here] is not the heart of flesh (carnal group of minds) in our chest. That mind (the group of fleshly minds) is not [the true mind], it is false, and will perish. Until our physical body perishes, that mind also perishes! [The mind mentioned] here is the true mind, not according to the General Part, but according to the General Part rising up to become the form of that mind. How is the mind revealed? From appearance, the mind is revealed. It is a little more distant, that is, it [is dependent on] General Part. That mind and Kien Phan[32] combine into one; Due to harmony, there are all the signs, that is, the Body of Dependent Origination. Buddhism calls this the Body Factors of Dependent Origination. Mind, View Part, Form Part combine into one, in harmony and have all the signs. When mind and scene combine, the scene can reveal the mind. The mind is the scene. Because of the mind, all dharmas are born. Because the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. The mind and all dharmas arise and pass away together. That is the meaning of “depending on fate”. Don't differentiate between the mind and the scene, what boundaries or limits there are! Nothing! There is no boundary, it is “same birth, same death”. Because all the signs of the realm are conditioned by the mind, it is said that "because the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed". When the mind is destroyed, of course what is conditioned by the mind also disappears. Therefore it is said that “mind arises, dharmas arise; mind ceases, dharmas cease”. If these two things are continuous in each thought, then we can maintain all dharmas. "all dharmas arise from the mind" is this principle. But that is temporary, all dharmas arise from the mind. After arising, it is temporary, it still has to pass away. All dharmas are born from the mind, all dharmas are also destroyed by the mind. Because the mind is destroyed, all dharmas will be destroyed!

(Sutra) Like the theory of false mind, there are two types of appearances. Ha class vi two? The one, the inner mind. The second person, the external mind. The internal appearance of the mind is false, and the two types of existence exist. Van Ha Vi Nhi? One false, true; false, false.
(Sutra: The meaning of mind as just said there are two types of appearance. What are the two? One is the internal appearance of mind, The second is the external mind. The internal mind has two things. One is the truth, the other is the illusion.)

Does the meaning of the mind as I (Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva) just said, have a form that can be expressed? Yes! There are two types of generals. The mind is inherently formless, how does one express that mind? Use form to express. What is morality that shows the mind? Use two types of appearances to express. There are two types of generals, what are these two? One is the internal mind, the other is the external mind; That is, the mind has an internal appearance and an external appearance. Mahayana Arising Faith Commentary teaches that this mind is divided into two subjects: One is the mind of Truth, the other is the mind of birth and death. One mind is divided into two doors. In the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva divides the mind into internal form and external mind, [He calls them] internal mind and external mind. Inner mind and outer mind, [each type] is also divided into two types. The internal form of the mind is unborn and immortal, the external form of the mind is birth and death. To put it this way, it seems like the mind has an inside and an outside. If you understand it like that, it's a mistake! The internal appearance is really not an internal appearance, the mind is not inside. External appearances are not external appearances, the mind is not outside. Not inside, not outside, but not in between. Out of concern for all living beings' attachments, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva immediately explained what the internal form of the mind is? What is the external mind? He explained each step. The internal form of the mind is also divided into two things, what is two? One is truth, the other is illusion. What is the internal form of the mind? There is truth in the mind and illusion in the mind. One side is the mind, the other side is the mental factor. Depending on the Reason of the mind, it arises, it is called by the name True Form, which is “the Realm of One Truth” as said in the previous half of the series. That Truth pervades the inside and out, pervades the mind of True Suchness, and also pervades the mind of birth and death. The mind that arises and dies is also the mind, the mind of True Suchness is also the mind. The inner mind is also the mind, the outer mind is also the mind. They have different effects, have different effects.

(Sutra) True speech, the mind and body of the original form, like no difference, pure and perfect, without obstacles, without obstacles. Obstacles, because of the hidden secret, it is difficult to see, the place of all changes, permanent and indestructible, established and born of all dharma try.
(Sutra: What is called "truth" refers to the original form of the mind and body as if it were no different, Perfectly pure, unobstructed, unobstructed, mysterious and difficult to see, because it pervades all places, is eternal and imperishable, establishes and grows all dharmas).

What is a footer? What is hope? “True Speech” (What is called Truth), Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva gave his own title to his explanation. The original form of the mind is the same, it is just one form. The original form of the mind is the formless form! “Such as” means “unmoving, unchanging”. “Not different as such”: Suchness and Suchness are no different. The form of the mind is no different, it is pure, perfect, without obstacles, [that is the meaning of the words] “unobstructed, unobstructed”. You want to see, but you still can't see, just use the meaning to explain, [the meaning] is mysterious, hard to see! That mind body is everywhere. It is indestructible, unchangeable, undifferentiated, not one, not two. Saying it's one is impossible, [we often mistakenly think] "If it's not one, then it's two", but saying it's two is also impossible! Not corrupted, not changed, always like that. Can give birth to all dharmas, all dharmas depending on it. All dharmas can be born, all dharmas depend on the basic nature of the mind. What is the form of being the refuge of all dharmas? Separation from the appearance of the mind. Using the mind's fate to meditate will not be possible. If you abandon all thoughts, you will not be able to recite. It is separate from the mind and from ideas. In the end, what shape is it? Whatever shape emptiness has, that form (the form of the mind) will have that shape. Therefore, it is equal to the realm of space, like the realm of space, permanent, indestructible, unchangeable, immortal. Because it can give rise to all dharmas, all dharmas arise from it, this is said to be “from the mind, dharmas arise”. All dharmas are destroyed from this, [it should be said] "because the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed". That is called the mind arising and passing away. As for the true mind, there are no words to say. True Suchness is without language, separated from the appearance of language, separated from the appearance of speech, separated from the appearance of Karma, separated from the appearance of Karma, separated from the appearance of suffering, everything does not exist. The True Mind is real, immovable, immovable, so how is it expressed? It is by the mind that arises and dies. It is all one mind, [but considered according to its Body or Form], then it becomes the mind of Truth or the mind of birth and death. Immediately use the mind of birth and death to express the mind of Truth.

Because when explaining, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva spoke very simply; Therefore, in the Mahayana Essay on Arising Faith written by Ma Minh Bodhisattva, He (Ma Minh Bodhisattva) divided it into one mind, two doors, and three great minds, that is, from one mind [which was divided into two doors:] the mind of True Truth and the mind of birth and death, [and the three great things are] Body, Form, Use. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches a great strategy. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches about the origin of the mind and the nature of the mind. Those are Body, Form, Use. I often say that the Contemplation Sutra and the Ksitigarbha Sutra both belong to the Avatamsaka system. Dai Phuong Quang Buddha Hoa Nghiem Sutra uses examples to understand, Dai is the mind, Phuong is the mind, Quang is the mind. [To put it together], Dai Phuong Quang is one's own Body, Form, and Use, but also the Body, Form, and Use of the Buddha. Then, say the word Buddha [in the title of the Avatamsaka Sutra, implying] How is Buddha manifested? [In the words] Dai Phuong Quang, i.e. Body, Form, Use of Buddha. Therefore, this passage has the same meaning, equal to the Avatamsaka Sutra.

What is “Foot”? The nature of the mind. Each of us has it, we all have it, but we can't use it, we can't see it, we still can't understand it, because our own mind doesn't know our own mind, we're deluded! How can it be explained? I give an example. When I was in the Mainland, I often mentioned the People's Bank of China [using it as an example]. For the Chinese [in Mainland], it is their bank. Can any Chinese person go to that bank to get a penny? Can't get it! The bank is yours, you just have a part, but if you want to use it, you can't use it! “Being” is like that! China People's Bank belongs to the Chinese people. The people are the owners, they open banks, but you can't even go to the bank to spend a penny! We are inherently complete in that Body, exactly like Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Because we are deluded, we do not have the right to [use] (that is, we cannot use the Use of the Body), we have lost it ourselves. How do you make it appear? Use the Right (Body) to appear.

The essence of the mind is “no difference”. The Dharma Just mentioned in the previous section is immovable, eternally unchanging, eternally the same, pure and perfect, without hindrances, without obstacles, mysterious, difficult to see. Can it be achieved without seeing it? Can't see it, doesn't have any effect. All sentient beings and Buddha are one and the same. We and the Buddhas are no different. As for the wonderful uses of the Buddhas, we don't have a single thing! Is it possible or not? No! The Buddhas are unobstructed, unobstructed, mysterious and difficult to see, in all places, at all times, without change or destruction. The mind can give birth to all dharmas, all dharmas are born from the mind. That is enlightenment. “Enlightenment” includes two types: One is enlightenment, the other is unconsciousness! They are all enlightenment, the same sense of enlightenment, but it has an enlightenment and an unenlightenment. Enlightened people are Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, while those who are not enlightened are ordinary beings of the six paths. It is the same sense that is conscious and unconscious. When talking about Truth, we are talking about the meaning of Enlightenment, those who are enlightened are Buddhas. Therefore, the mind, Buddha, sentient beings, the three are no different, just delusion and enlightenment. Once enlightened, you will be equal to the Buddhas. If you are confused, then you will be a sentient being. It's true, it's true!

(Sutra) The source of false speech, the originator of discriminating thoughts, perception, cause and effect, memories of equal things. Although it is continuous, it can give birth to all kinds of realms, but inside it is false and false, there is no truth, it cannot be fixed.
etc. Although it is possible to continuously give birth to all kinds of realms, all of them are illusory, not real, and cannot be seen).

The previous paragraph talks about enlightenment, and this paragraph talks about unconsciousness. There are many unconscious sequences that cannot be fully explained in just one or two sentences. Ma Minh Bodhisattva created the Mahayana Awakening of Faith Commentary, saying "one thought without enlightenment gives rise to three sacrifices", that is, talking about three sacrifices, which is already troublesome! Affliction arises from ignorance. “One unenlightened thought” refers to ignorance. “Three signs” are the appearance of karma, transformation, and appearance. When we ordinary people want to cut off those three types of appearances, we must reach the Eight Bodhisattva Levels to cut off the appearance, the Nine Bodhisattva Levels to cut off the transformation, the Ten Bodhisattva Levels to cut off the karma, but [to reach those positions], we must go through countless eons.

Here, [talking about internal appearance] is obviously speaking in general, [just saying simply] one side is the truth, the other side is illusion. When we face all things, whenever we start thinking, whenever we make distinctions, we hope to know clearly, that is, when we don't understand clearly about the problem, we want to know clearly. Starting the mind to think is starting up hope, that is, raising false thoughts, discrimination, knowing, remembering (thinking about a certain event or situation), hoping for enlightenment, thinking (thinking about a certain event or situation), and thinking. You have these appearances continuously without end, the more you think about them, the more coarse they become, the more you differentiate, the coarser they become, until karma arises. Whenever you create karma, you will be bound by karma. Good karma will bind you to good karma, bad karma will bind you to bad karma. Whenever the mind starts to think, it is called “starting karma” (arising karma). That karma will hold you, you won't be able to escape, it will be very difficult to break it. Why? The more contaminated it becomes, the coarser it becomes, and it constantly creates karma. Once you have created karma, hoping to restore it will be extremely difficult. Creating karma is easy, until you destroy the karma, you will have to pay ten times the price, and also pay a hundred or thousand times the price.

Now we want to clean it up, restore the original purity, because karma and karma have accumulated for many lives, many lifetimes, they hinder you from seeing the true nature. You want to wash away, but it's not what you created in one day, one year, two years, but countless lifetimes, so whether you can wash away easily or not depends on your strength! As in Zen Buddhism, "if you cut down and enter directly, immediately attain Bodhi" is not truly attaining Bodhi. “Immediately attain Bodhi” means to end afflictions and attain enlightenment. Having "realized", we still have to practice, we still have to practice gradually! Just like we did something wrong, because your mind is strong and sharp, you will immediately do it. Until you have a good heart and want to completely change that mistake, you will have to pay a lot. [We repent of karma] have the same principle, when we start thinking to create karma, the more it changes, the rougher it becomes, the more it changes, the rougher and heavier it becomes!

We even clearly understand that, when starting to study Buddhism, Buddhist disciples must first take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Sangha. We study ourselves and read many sutras, but we still cannot be considered Buddhist disciples, because we have not "take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha". You must take the Three Refuges and start taking refuge again! We often say that according to appearances, when taking refuge, there are Buddha statues, there are monks, and there is the Three Refuges Dharma. That's speaking according to generals. According to Ly, the Three Jewels are the self-nature of the Three Jewels, returning to the origin. When taking refuge in the Three Jewels, you restore your own Buddha's nature and your own Sangha's self-nature. Buddha and Sangha in harmony is the Dharma. Take refuge in the Buddha's nature, the Dharma and the Sangha, the Three Jewels. We often say: "I just need to rely on a master and take refuge in the Three Jewels to enter Buddhism." So not yet! From the monks who have become monks like us, to the lay followers, monks, bhikshunis, upasakas, upasakas, the four disciples start reciting the sutras every day, or you bow, and as soon as you start “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, we must recite the refuge of the Three Jewels. That is not yet taking refuge in the Three Refuges, taking refuge in the Three Jewels, but in every thought, constantly taking refuge in the Three Jewels, always taking refuge in the Three Jewels. Whatever sutra you recite, as soon as you open the sutra, you will definitely take refuge in the Three Jewels. If people recite the Avatamsaka Sutra, for example, the Avatamsaka Samantabhadra Vows; Among the ten great vows, taking refuge in the Three Jewels accounts for three great vows! Taking refuge in the Three Jewels is repenting of bad karma.

The Three Jewels always exist, not just for a short time. Why? That is called “perception”, or it is called enlightenment. Our own sense of meaning is not enough, the power of enlightenment is not enough, we must rely on the blessings of the Three Jewels, and never forget the Three Jewels with every thought. First, reciting the Three Jewels eliminates karma. There are many Buddhist disciples who believe in Buddha but are still relied on by demons. Their Buddhist hall still has misfortunes, and they feel that ghosts and gods are coming. That person himself does not know, [the reason is that] your refuge is not genuine. You have not truly taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and Three Jewels. If you truly take refuge in the Buddha Dharma, Sangha, and the Three Jewels, are there such disasters and can ghosts and spirits still come? When you take refuge in the Three Jewels, the guardian deities are with you. It's not that they protect you, but they protect the Three Jewels. Since you constantly remember the Three Jewels with every thought, every thought is protected by the Three Jewels. So, are there still ghosts and spirits that interfere? Many Buddhist disciples said they were "enchanted by demons" and that their Buddhist halls had ghosts and spirits appearing. So you have to ask yourself: Is it true that you take refuge in the Three Jewels? At least you have to ask that question. If you are sincere, how can this phenomenon still exist? Did you know: If you take refuge in Buddha, you will have many Dharma protectors? Are there many dharma protectors in taking refuge in the Dharma? Does taking refuge in the Sangha have many Dharma protectors? If the mind is sincere, the vow will be earnest. The heart is not sincere, the vow is not fervent, the protection power of the Three Jewels will not bless you! The Three Jewels bless you everywhere, [yet] you don't ask for the Three Jewels' blessings! You are full of false thoughts. If you say it a little harsher, say it a little more forcefully, it is "deceiving the Three Jewels". Everyone can think about this, but is it possible to reduce sin? Is there a blessing or not? The blessings are still there. We take refuge in the Three Jewels, regardless of whether you are fake, or whether you only perform on the outside, that blessing is the blessing of humanity, the blessing of wealth, in life, those things. But if you hope to attain enlightenment and achieve success, then when it comes to taking refuge in the Three Jewels, your mind must merge into one with the Three Jewels!

tom_tat: Lecture 12 Now we talk about the mind, talk about idealism. Idealism is not that simple. It is very difficult to understand idealism, to what extent? If you understand clearly, you will be enlightened. People say "clear mind and see nature"; Once you understand, you will leave...
noi_dung:
Lecture 12

Now we talk about the mind, talk about idealism. Idealism is not that simple. It is very difficult to understand idealism, to what extent? If you understand clearly, you will be enlightened. People say “clear mind and see nature”; Once you are clear, you will be free from birth and death. Here, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said the mind is divided into internal mind and external mind, true mind and false mind. Internal appearances are divided into two types, one is true, the other is illusion. When it comes to "truth", it is the original form of the mind and body, which the Buddhas have attained, and all sentient beings are confused. The original nature of the mind and body is pure, perfect, the same, unchanging. The original form of the mind body has no obstacles, but it is not easy to see, it is not easy to understand this meaning, it is not possible to realize the nature. That mind is omnipresent at all times, in all places, inherently untainted, pure, and perfect, but we cannot see it, it is mysterious and difficult to see! Because it is always like that, no change, no difference, no destruction; All dharmas are born from the mind. Because the mind is born, dharma is born. When the mind disappears, the dharma also disappears. It's about the mind and body. Is there an original form of the mind or body? Yes! What general is that? It is as it is, without any contamination, free of thoughts. That is called “reflecting on Truthfulness”. That is to say that the mind is inherently impure and false. Because you move thoughts, your mind moves thoughts, as soon as thoughts arise that are not pure, when thoughts arise, there is a distinction. That is called “the inherent appearance of the Original Enlightenment”. Whenever the mind begins to think, it will lose its existing appearance, and from the Original Enlightenment, enlightenment will arise. Originally, the original form is pure and perfect, as the Heart Sutra says, the original form of the mind is "without obstacles, without defects, without impurity, without increase, without decrease" (not entangled, not dirty, not clean, not increasing, not decreasing), without false thoughts.

Suppose you just raised an idea, raising an idea is an illusion. When talking about illusion, the ideas of discrimination, fate, seeing, hearing, good, knowing arise. That idea is continuous in each thought, forever without interruption. It will give birth to all realms. Normally, speaking according to Mahayana teachings, this mind is inherently unmoving. As soon as the thought is moved, three types of subtle signs will be born, thanks to external conditions, the realm as a condition, the more it grows, the coarser it becomes, giving birth to six types of gross signs (wisdom sign, continuity sign, clinging to the prime, following name and self, starting karma, and karma of suffering). When you first start thinking, the appearance conditioned by the mind does not leave the mind, it is still the true mind, but that True Suchness is called "abandoning the thought of True Suchness". As soon as your mind moves, it will differentiate the subtle into karma, transformation, and appearance. That is “one thought suddenly gives birth to three sacrifices”. As soon as the mind begins to think, it contains three types of appearances (three subtle appearances). “Karma” is what we mean by eight consciousnesses. When the original appearance of the eight consciousnesses has just transformed, it transforms into appearance. “Show” is a manifestation, the realm will appear; this is very subtle. When you start thinking and distinguishing, you think and remember things, gradually giving birth to the appearance of the realm. Among the three signs of the mind, there is no sign of the realm. At the end, it will be very difficult. Such a scene arises: Karma gives birth to changing signs, changing signs gives birth to appearing signs. Eight Bodhisattva Levels cut off appearances, Nine Bodhisattva Levels cut off changing signs, Ten Bodhisattva Levels cut off karmic signs. We must practice to reach the Eight Grounds kung fu, which is very difficult! I don't know how many lives I have to go through! Therefore, at that time, due to the more coarse and coarse the movement, thoughts have arisen, have distinguished, have remembered, thoughts will continue without end. We have not yet reached that realm.

Based on this already existing mind of Original Enlightenment, all appearances, subtle and gross, arise. When [that appearance] first arises, it is called subtle, from the subtle it becomes coarse. The more you move, the rougher it gets! Because it continues endlessly thinking, remembering, and distinguishing; At that time, if you want to distinguish those appearances, you will have wisdom in appearance, wisdom in “wisdom”. One must reach the Seven Bodhisattva Bodhisattva levels to attain wisdom. Whenever it arises, that is, whenever there is wisdom, there will be discrimination, the more discrimination, the coarser it becomes! That distinction does not stop, it continues continuously. It is called “continuous appearance” (continuous appearance, successive appearance). Due to continuity, attachments arise. If you're attached to [something] being good, you'll keep it; if you're attached to it being bad, you'll want to throw it away. The mind continuously gives rise to wisdom and continues to appear. Whenever you take it away, karma arises, that is, if it's good then take it, if it's bad then give it up. If you give up, you can't give it up. You want to get it, but you can't get it. These things all belong to our “seeing, hearing, knowing, knowing” distinction. We think about remembering, enlightenment, understanding, or wishing to know, but that mind seeking to know has discrimination, taking the good and leaving the bad. The more that mind arises, the more false it becomes, the further away it is from the truth. Even if you see it, you can't see it. Even if you try to touch it, you can't touch it. Currently, we have not yet reached that situation, but because the sutras, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas have taught, we know that the ideas we raise are all discrimination and delusion. Because you create false thoughts, thoughts, and thoughts that are attached to the appearance of the realm. Once an idea is born, it will create the appearance of the present realm. The appearance of that realm also depends on the Original Enlightenment. Relying on the Original Enlightenment to exist is an illusion, there is no true nature of illusion, it cannot be seen, nor can it be touched. Therefore, it is called “hope”. Meanwhile, it is still in the mind, not outside the mind. In the mind, the form is born by itself, the distinction is made by itself, and the fate is created by itself. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told us that our mind is divided into internal and external. The things just mentioned above are the internal appearance of the mind. What is the shape of the external mind?

(Sutra) The mind's words, external appearance, appearance, all dharmas of all kinds, all kinds of realms, depending on the thoughts, the present realm money. Trying to have an inner mind and a different inner mind.
(Sutra: Speaking of "mind and appearance" is saying that the realms of all dharmas are due to existence. concept, so the present realm knows that there is a difference between the inner mind and the inner mind.

Speaking of “external mind” refers to all appearances shown by all dharmas. Regarding the appearance of the external realm, you have just “recited”, “recited” means to think, and as soon as you think, you have the appearance of the external realm. The above concept is the predestined ability (the subject is predestined to follow a certain object, such as the external realm). The mental energy is conditioned by the condition (the object being conditioned), [or in other words], the mental energy is conditioned by the form outside the mind. “External appearance” is the realm. Raising attachment to the appearance of the realm, that is called “mind of external appearance”. Once you know the difference inside, it is from the inside that external appearances arise. External appearance is the fate part (ie the object is conditioned by the mind, also known as the appearance part). The mind that is conditioned by appearance (i.e. Kien Phan), in the above section [it is called] the condition of energy, but here it is said in detail. For all dharmas, [the text uses the word] “all dharmas” with a representative meaning. [You should understand] “all dharmas” is “all realms”. Because you are attached to the appearance of your current realm, differences arise within your heart. Because the appearance of karma, transference, and appearance in the previous section have not yet raised differences, from the appearance of wisdom and continuity onwards, differences will immediately arise. [Due to the attachment to the appearance of the present realm or not, the inner mind is divided into the mind of internal appearance and the mind of external appearance, that is, the inner mind is divided into two types of difference, so the main sutra says "the difference between the inner mind and the inner mind"].

(Sutra) As if in the present, one perceives false appearances, micro-causes, micro-substances. External false appearance, because of results, because of Use. Just like trying the same meaning, the theory of self says: "All dharmas are all named in the mind".
(Sutra: So you should know: The internal illusion is the cause, the Body, and the external illusion is the effect, is Use. Based on such meanings, we say: "All dharmas are called mind").

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You must know the false appearance (illusory appearance) in your heart. The appearance of false thoughts within the mind is false thoughts within the mind. We often talk about delusion; That is the cause, the Body. All of our false thoughts, from false thoughts, give birth to many things, so it is said that false thoughts are the mind, the Body, it is also the cause for all dharmas. The cause is bound to result, feeling suffering, receiving pleasure, receiving, feeling other wrong conditions. Due to false appearances (illusory appearances) within the mind, emotions appear in the external realm. That's called "fragile delusions", giving rise to all kinds of effects. But because all kinds of effects are inseparable from the mind, we often talk about this as "all things are mind-only".

If we say it in reverse, it would be “the mind gives birth to all dharmas, all dharmas are born from the mind, all dharmas return to the mind”. The mind gives birth to all dharmas and becomes the Body for all dharmas. The form and function born from the Body still return to one mind. When it arises, it is called the cause, the cause is bound to produce the effect, the cause is bound to produce the effect, and the effect is the Body. The body is bound to have an effect due to the mind. Cause or effect is the same, Body or Use is the same, due to only one mind. Outside of the mind there are no dharmas, all dharmas are born from the mind and return to the mind. Apart from the mind, there is no form whatsoever. Therefore, when the mind arises, all dharmas arise; When the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed.

Therefore, we know: The false appearance inside is the origin of all dharmas, the Essence of all dharmas, giving birth to false thoughts on the outside. The false appearance of the mind gives birth to the false appearance on the outside, the false appearance on the outside is the Use, the Fruit. Cause must have effect, Body must have Use. We say “cause, effect, substance, use”, which includes “origination, creation of karma”. In contrast, if we cultivate the Way, destroy Or, do not let it create karma, return the karma created to the mind. Because we cannot understand appearances (external appearances), that is the effect of delusion. As for external appearances, you cannot understand, do not know that external appearances are idealistic! All dharmas arise from the mind alone, but we do not know and cannot understand. Therefore, from the internal mind, the external mind is born; the internal and external are completely one mind. Therefore, Buddhism often says "all dharmas are mind-only", it arises from there!

(Sutra) Prosperity is knowing the mind and appearance of false appearances, like dreams and views, races of idealistic realms, unreal foreign affairs. All realms, all herons are like this. Di giai is ignorant of consciousness, dreams and views, false thoughts and delusions. Second, knowing the inner mind, thoughts and thoughts are not fixed, the view, the condition is necessarily the realm, the heron depends on the mind, the thoughts are not fixed. The origin of the mind arises, the species of dharma arises. The mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. The birth and destruction of the form, the birth of the name, is truly impossible to attain. The realm of the mind of never-returning, the realm of never-returning, the mind of non-returning, is like the symbol of no-return, no-past. Thien try, all dharma, seeking birth and destruction of the fixed form, will not be achieved. The reason why all dharmas are all non-existent, the origin is eternal, there is no birth or death.
(Sutra: Again, you should know: "External appearance of mind" is like what is seen in dreams. Things Realms are only created by the mind, there are no real things outside. All realms are like that, because they depend on ignorance and consciousness as seen in dreams, created by false thoughts. Furthermore, you should know that the inner mind in each thought does not exist, all the realms seen or conditioned also follow the mind, but every thought does not exist. destruction, only the name, is truly impossible. Because the mind does not reach the realm, the realm does not reach the mind, like an image in a mirror, it does not come, it does not go. Therefore, for all dharmas, looking for a certain form of birth and death, it is called that all dharmas ultimately have no essence, because they are inherently emptiness and do not really exist.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva again gave an example to explain what the external appearance of the mind is? Like when we dream and see all kinds of realms, that's what you imagine. That is, thoughts are created within the mind, or all external things are reflected in the mind, created by the mind. Therefore, outside the mind there is no dharma, everything is mind-only. That's what Buddhism says “all are idealistic”. Because all sentient beings are confused about external appearances, do not understand, and do not know that external appearances are born from mental factors. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: All realms are like that, they are only created by the mind, there are no external [realms], they are all created by the mind. Speaking from our side, all the signs of the realm arise from ignorance. If we do not understand ignorance, like we dream, the three signs of Karma, Transformation, and Present are the subtle signs, and the form of wisdom and continuity are called Consciousness, just like when we talk about knowledge, then Knowledge is the essence, Consciousness is the effect. At that time, there will be many distinctions. Therefore, that is the dependent origination of mind dharma. The mental conditions that cause the dharma to arise are all the signs that arise due to the conditions of our minds. We know that all the signs of the realm of dependent origination are not real, they are born from the mind. “Birth” is caused by the mind, “death” is also caused by the mind. When the mind arises, all dharmas arise; when the mind ceases, all dharmas cease.

This issue was only roughly discussed in the previous section, so Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva explains this issue again. Therefore, you should know: In our mind, every thought does not stay, there is no time to rest. If every thought does not stop, in other words, it would be “every thought does not stop”. For example, when we sleep, when we are not using our mind, our mind still works the same way, completely non-stop. This development is created by you yourself. The mind is constantly dreaming, deceiving the mind according to the deluded scene. Your inner thoughts do not stop, all the mental scenes you see, think about, and practice are unceasing in each thought. Therefore, Buddhism says: "The mind arises, the dharmas arise. The mind ceases, the dharmas cease". We say "all dharmas are mind-only" like that, but this principle is called "mind arises and disappears". Mahayana Arising the Faith says “one mind, three greats, two doors”, then which two doors are they? The mind of birth and death and the mind of True Suchness. Because if we talk about the appearance of birth and death, then the appearance of birth and death has no real entity, only a name, just a name. If you look for the real thing, it doesn't exist, it's really impossible!

In this passage, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You should know that your thoughts and thoughts do not stay in your mind. What you see is what your mind sees, depending on all the external realms. The appearance of that realm is also caused by your mind. The inner mind raises the appearance of the realm, the inner mind is conditioned according to the appearance of one's own realm, thoughts and thoughts do not stay. In terms of meaning, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: Whenever you give birth to your mind, all kinds of dharmas are born. If you do not have a mind, all dharmas will disappear. But these dharmas and their birth and death are only disguised. If you look for something that truly exists [in those dharmas and birth and death], you won't find it, nothing really exists, they are just pretend! Therefore, your mind should not dwell on the appearance of the realm. The mind does not reside in the realm of appearance, and all the appearances of the outside realm do not reach your mind. Because this principle is very difficult to understand, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva gives an example. For example, when you look in the mirror, is the appearance in the mirror real or fake? Is there a form in the mirror? No! When you don't look, there is no form in the mirror. Don't come, don't go! In all dharmas, looking for a certain sign of birth and death, we look for a certain sign, what will be the certain sign of birth and death? Since it belongs to the category of birth and death, there will be no definite appearance that can be said! Only having names is really impossible, it cannot achieve the truth. Our mind does not dwell in the form of the realm, nor does the appearance of the realm come to the mind. Therefore, use the appearance in the mirror like that to visualize. Forms do not come in the mirror, and mirrors cannot give birth to forms. You look in the mirror, is there anything else coming or going? No! Therefore, if you really want to seek the appearance of birth and death in all dharmas, to find a certain appearance of birth and death, how it arises and how it disappears, it will be impossible. Why can't it be? All dharmas ultimately have no essence. Their essence is Emptiness, always Emptiness. Since it is Emptiness, is there still birth and death? In Emptiness, there is no birth and death.

(Sutra) As the true dharma cannot be born nor destroyed, there are no different realms of appearance, the most tranquil The position and name of True Suchness, the First Noble Truth, is pure in nature and mind. Self-nature is pure and the mind is naturally perfect, without any distinction between appearances and origins.
(Sutra: All such dharmas truly have no birth and death, so they do not have all appearances. Different realms, one state of tranquility, is called the First Noble Truth, pure self-nature, pure mind.

This paragraph talks about "no birth and death". Birth and death are the mind, not the dharma. Because of the mind, all dharmas are born; Because the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. When we preach the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, we explain this very briefly, and it's just the same outline! Because the one in charge at that time is Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva. He said so, of course he knew that Kien Tinh Bodhisattva could definitely understand; But we sentient beings who want to learn deeply will not be able to penetrate in such a short time! From language to inner thinking, you rely on practice to authenticate, observe all the birth and death in your mind, [observe] the thoughts that arise throughout the day, we think that the mind arises and then passes away again. Birth is also mind, but death is also mind. We call it “thought”, and often like to talk about ideological issues. The problem of thought is the problem of birth and death, the problem of birth and death has no form of birth and death. In fact, the differences in all external realms are non-existent and are tranquil. That self-nature of mind has no self-nature, it is named "True Truth, First Meaning, pure nature of mind", the nature is pure, quiet, perfect, without any distinction.

Without any reason, it is able to maintain and establish all dharma.
(Sutra: “The form does not differentiate” in all places, everywhere, everywhere "Nowhere does not exist" because it can hold and create all dharmas).

Because all dharmas do not exist, they are unborn and immortal. “There is no birth and death” means that [all dharmas] do not exist. Since there is no form of birth and death, how can there be all dharmas? But in the realm of difference, in that difference, appearance will refer to Body, appearance will refer to nature. The characteristics of different realms will neither come nor go. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva gives [examples] the appearance in the mirror; Please tell me, is there any appearance in the mirror? There is none. When people don't look in the mirror, is there any form in the mirror? Not only about people, but even all the signs of the realm in the mirror are absent. There is no difference in the nature of appearance, why? Empty! It does not really exist, but it is also one taste, regardless of appearance. The mind of all of us sentient beings is a pure mind, neither does it decrease in ordinary people, nor does it increase in Buddhas and saints. That mind is equal, in the mundane it does not decrease, in the holy it does not increase, but also has no coming or going, formless! But that mind is all-pervading, like space, if you rely on it, you will be able to establish all dharmas.

“General” Which general is that referring to? Mind appearance. In the previous part, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva explained the mind to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, explained what shape the mind has, and explained the form of that mind. That form is still the mind, without any form. However, here it is very brief, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva did not speak to us in the mass, but spoke to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, speaking very deeply, but going into details is very brief. We often speak according to the teachings, or rely on the four teachings, or rely on the five teachings, or rely on Consciousness Only, we will talk a lot, from the crude to the profound. Here it is said that the mind is pure and has no distinction. There is no distinction, is there still a wheel of wood? The first half [of this sutra] talks about all ordinary people, the second half talks about all saints. If you want to enter this dharma, you must eliminate karma. Therefore, first of all, make you repent of your sins. Only then can one's sins be eliminated and one can learn the idealistic method. The second half is a mind-only method, talking only about the pure mind. What does a pure mind look like? There is no distinction, it pervades everywhere. There is a mind everywhere. Depending on it, all dharmas can be established.

All dharmas are mind-only, that is to say “mind gives birth to all dharmas”. That pure mind is perfect, without distinction, without duality, and is no different from Buddha. Buddha is practice, and we are available. If we do not inherently have that pure mind, no matter how you practice, you still cannot practice to become Buddha! You pick up a few rocks and cook them into rice, but it won't work. Stone is still stone, stone cannot be turned into rice. The pure mind has only one Body. All good dharmas rely on a pure mind to be established; All evil things also depend on a pure mind to be established. The mind has no good or evil. If you have a decisive nature, you will not be able to eliminate evil, and you will not be able to achieve success in cultivating goodness! Since it is not a decision, let's perceive our mind as such. Of course you must understand this! You also don't know how to use the Contemplation Wheel, use the Contemplation Wheel to manifest. Because, in the Buddha's world, the Dharma is all wonderful. The Buddha's benefit to sentient beings is all about Use, from Use comes appearance and mind. Buddha has infinite wonderful uses, great Bodhisattvas also have infinite wonderful uses. From Use the mind is manifested, ordinary people can understand the mind from the Body.

(Sutra) Respect the second, belittle the name of Tathagatagarbha. The endowed position is immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, pure, meritorious karma.
(Sutra: Again, that mind is called Tathagatagarbha, meaning: It is complete immeasurable, boundless, pure, inconceivable meritorious karma.

Therefore, this mind is called the Tathagata Treasury, complete with boundless, boundless, pure, inconceivable meritorious karma. Here, add the word Karma. Karma means “effect”, expressing the meaning “effect is practice to manifest”. Because of that, you can be complete. If it's not already available, even if you practice, you still won't practice. As in the example I just gave, if you cook ice and hope it turns into rice, it won't work! Because it (the mind) is available, it can do it. That mind is called Tathagatagarbha. Tathagatagarbha is explained as True Suchness. Why is it called Tathagatagarbha and not called True Suchness? Because there are two types of meanings included in it. Because True Tathagata is already in afflictions, it is called Tathagata Treasury. This meaning is said by the Mahayana Arising in Faith, and the Avatamsaka Sutra also says the same. The Tathagata Treasury is the True Suchness among ordinary people and is called the Tathagata Treasury. If True Suchness eliminates the afflictions contained within it, there will be no afflictions, so it is called the Dharmakaya. Dharmakaya is pure.

“Reveal, accept the name Tathagatagarbha” (Again, that mind is called Tathagatagarbha): That mind is a present thought of all sentient beings. The present thought of each of our Dharma friends is full of Tathagatagarbha Nature, which is the Essence of our one thought. The Body of a single thought in the present is complete and contains immeasurable karmic merits, everyone can cultivate to become a Buddha. Because everyone has the Tathagata Storehouse Nature, they can cultivate to become Buddhas. If you do not have [Tathagata Storehouse Nature], you will absolutely not be able to practice successfully. Because the present mind of sentient beings is full of immeasurable and boundless meritorious karma. You have all the immeasurable meritorious karma in the present, so that mind is called the Tathagata Treasury. That mind is equal to the mind of an accomplished person. Those who have successfully cultivated are the Buddhas who have attained that Dharma Body, while sentient beings are confused about that Dharma Body. What if sentient beings also become enlightened? Sentient beings who have attained enlightenment will no longer be called sentient beings, but Buddhas. That is talking about dependent origination. Dependent origination is practice, dependent origination is that the Tathagata has practiced everything, has practiced and attained the results, full of merit with the nature of anasrava. Why did all the Tathagata's inconceivable merits come about? It comes from actions. The Tathagata's merit comes from practice (practice), and is attained through practice.

If there is no meaning of Emptiness, that means there is no morality of this meaning of Emptiness, merit will not be able to be established! Where to establish? Because of relying on True Emptiness, we establish Miraculous Existence, containing "True Emptiness is not emptiness, Miraculous Existence is not existence". True Existence is not truly existent, True Emptiness is not emptiness. It is full of merit and has the nature of anasrava. Wonderful Being and non-existence means True Emptiness!

(Sutra) Of all Buddhas Dharmakaya, the pine of the beginningless origin, unobstructed, unobstructed, eternally free. It is necessary to transform the industry, to be permanent, and to increase the benefits. So the change is necessarily the world's business, the race and the benefit co. The one Buddha body means all the Buddhas' body, all the Buddhas' body means the one Buddha body. Possessing the most outstanding heron career. The position has no distinction between appearances, no thoughts or trials, and is equal and incomparable. Of course, based on the same dharma nature, there are karma, naturalization, The body is without distinction or difference.
All forms of transformation are always burning and never stop. That is to say, throughout all worlds, they perform all kinds of transformations, creating benefits. Because the body of a Buddha is the body of all Buddhas, all karmas are the same Depending on a dharma nature, there is karma to create, just like it naturally turns out, because the Body is no different).

As soon as you read this passage, you will feel that there are many places that cannot be explained and cannot be penetrated. Because, the meaning in this passage is all about revealing our nature, pointing out our mind and body, speaking according to Ly. Entering from reason is very difficult, so we have to borrow examples to illustrate, and rely on our living habits to confirm. If you apply these issues to life to explain, you will gradually be able to penetrate. In the Body, from beginningless time until now, all sentient beings and all the Buddhas of the ten directions are no two, no different, that is the essence. According to Ly, there are no obstacles. The Body itself has no birth and death, but Form and Use are completely different. In it, the karma is contained. Although the Body is the same, the Form and Use are different. Why aren't they the same? That is talking about selflessness. Living beings become arrogant and deluded, that is, they lose their Body; Because of ignorance, the Body immediately changes, so the Use will be different. Although the body is the same, the function is different. Regarding this principle, speaking according to the phenomena in life, we are all human, but everyone is greatly different. Humans have white, black, yellow, and red skin; That's the difference, but the bodies are all human, the humanity is the same. Although we and Buddha are not two or different, because of attachment, all sentient beings have the Human Ego, the Dharma Ego, and the obstacle of ignorance, which is the disagreement. The karma also pervades all places, pervades all times, sentient beings and Buddhas are different, that is different retributions. Buddhas are "cultivated", that is, they have successfully cultivated merit and restored the original Dharma Body, so in terms of cultivating virtue [between Buddha] and sentient beings, there will be a difference. Having cultivated to perfection, cultivating to the point where there is nothing left to cultivate, we know that "it's still just restoring what is already there". The karma of all Buddhas in the ten directions is to save sentient beings, but the karma is different. Amitābha Buddha manifested the world of Ultimate Bliss to save sentient beings, Śākyamuni Buddha manifested the Saba world to save sentient beings. That's the difference.

(Sutra) Just like the Buddhas Dharmakaya transforms into the universal land, perfect and immovable, subject to the test of all living beings, rebirth, constant action.
Following living beings who die here and are born there, always act as a refuge).

The Dharma Bodies of all Buddhas are the same, they are also complete in all places, they are all “Buddha, Buddha, path, perfect and immovable”. But they can follow the fate of living beings. Each Buddha saves each type of living being depending on the fate of living beings. The Dharma Bodies of Buddhas and Tathagatas pervade all places. The ten dharma realms all have Buddha nature, even the path of hell also has Buddha nature. That is called “Tathagata depends on sentient beings”, but sentient beings learn Buddha and gradually transform. Sentient beings who study Buddhism can also become Buddhas. That is “circulation”. All Buddhas and sentient beings are inseparable from each other and have the same nature. The essence is not separate, the Buddhas are always a place of refuge for sentient beings, and sentient beings can attain enlightenment by following the Dharma taught by the Buddha.

(Sutra) Like nothingness, it can accommodate all forms, shapes, and forms. Of course, all forms, species, and shapes are bound to exist in the void. They are created to grow, abide in the void, and reside in the land of nothingness. Because of nothingness, there is nothingness, nothingness can give rise to the false realm of nothingness. Duong tri: Sin the middle of the great form, the indestructible world of emptiness. Forms and appearances fade away, return to emptiness, and form emptiness, the original realm is non-increasing, non-decreasing, immovable, unchanging.
(Sutra: For example, space can contain all forms and forms. Since all forms and forms depend on emptiness, they are established, grow, and abide in emptiness. Because emptiness is the substance, no dharma can go beyond the realm of emptiness. You should know: In the form of emptiness, the realm of emptiness cannot be destroyed and return to emptiness, but the inherent limit of emptiness does not increase, it does not decrease, it is immutable, it does not change.

For this principle, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva gives an example. For example, space can contain all forms and shapes. Emptiness contains everything, any form can be expressed. All the different forms and shapes, including all sentient beings, animals, as well as inanimate things such as mountains, rivers, and earth, not a single thing is left out! But can they separate emptiness? Whatever is born cannot be separated from emptiness, it is all in emptiness. Emptiness is the Total, all forms are the Separate. That Special is all in the void, captured by the void. Nothingness is the essence of all matter. They depend on nothingness to be established. No thing can leave nothingness to live in one place alone. It's impossible! Outside of space, there is no place for you to stay. All forms are in emptiness. Nothingness will never be destroyed; All appearances change at any time. All things that have form, when destroyed, will return to nothingness. When the earth disappears and is destroyed, it will turn into subtle dust particles, and the subtle dust particles will return to nothingness. Is nothingness destroyed? Nothingness will never be destroyed. All things are born and destroyed, what is born is born in nothingness, what is destroyed is still in nothingness. In the void there is no increase, no decrease, motionless, unchanging. That is using nothingness as an example. Emptiness is the Body of all sentient beings, but it is also used to visualize the Dharma Body of the Buddhas.

(Sutra) All Buddhas, Dharma Bodies, dressed as they are, must be able to accept all sentient beings and receive retribution. Of course, the retribution of sentient beings of all races and species is inevitable, and in the presence of the Buddhas, the Dharmakaya is established, born, and abides in the Dharmakaya, and is the land of Dharmakaya. Because of the microscopic Dharmakaya, there is no ability to emerge from the Dharmakaya world. Dunderstands: Nall sentient beings are loyal, the Buddhas Dharmakaya is indestructible. When afflictions are destroyed, the Dharmakaya returns to the Dharmakaya, the Dharmakaya's original realm is non-increasing, non-decreasing, immovable, unchanging.
(Sutra: The Dharma Bodies of the Buddhas are like that, can endure all kinds of retributions All sentient beings. Because the karma of all sentient beings depends on the Dharma Bodies of the Buddhas to establish, grow, and abide in the Dharma Bodies. Taking the Dharma Bodies as their body, nothing can escape the limits of the Dharma Bodies: In the bodies of all living beings, the Dharma Bodies of all sentient beings cannot be destroyed destroying afflictions, one will return to the Dharmakaya, but the scope of the Dharmakaya does not increase, does not decrease, it is motionless, unchanging).

The Dharmakaya of the Buddhas is like that, like the void that can contain the retributions of all sentient beings. Because you create so many causes, the causes will definitely have effects. Living beings suffer different kinds of retributions. Where does the retribution of all living beings depend? The retribution of all sentient beings depends on the Dharma Bodies of the Buddhas to establish and grow. The Dharma Body of the Buddhas is the Dharma Body of sentient beings. The Dharma Bodies of sentient beings are the Dharma Bodies of Buddhas. The retribution of sentient beings is the Dharma Body of the Buddhas. The Dharma Body of the Buddhas embraces all sentient beings. The Dharma Body of all sentient beings and the Dharma Body of the Buddhas are not two or different. There are no sentient beings outside the Dharma Realm, they all belong to the Dharma Realm. Isn't that what we say "all dharmas are idealistic"? “Dharma” refers to the mind, the dharma is the mind. Mind is dharma. When the mind arises, all kinds of dharmas arise; When the mind is destroyed, all dharmas are destroyed. They all belong to the Dharmakaya, nothing can escape the limits of the Dharmakaya. You should know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: You must know that in the bodies of all sentient beings, the Dharma Bodhisattva of the Buddhas cannot be destroyed. The minds of all sentient beings will never be destroyed. Suppose sentient beings do not have all afflictions, and after eliminating ignorance and afflictions, they also return to the Buddha's Dharma Body. The Dharmakaya is neither increasing nor decreasing, not defiled, not clean, not changing, not moving. This is called Dharmakaya.

That is thanks to emptiness to simulate the Dharmakaya of the Buddhas, what kind of analogy is that? For example, our present retribution. The present karma of sentient beings is so different, each person has his or her own karma. “Beings” here includes not only humans, but also animals, [or more broadly] all sentient species are sentient beings. Speaking in this sense, the body of living beings is the Dharma Body of the Buddhas. The Dharma Bodies of the Buddhas contain the Dharma Bodies of all sentient beings. Therefore, the afflictions of sentient beings have ended and they have returned to the essence of the Dharmakaya. Those are also Buddhas. The Dharmakaya itself does not increase, it does not decrease, it is not born, it is not destroyed. Sentient beings were enlightened, so they restored the Dharmakaya. There is a saying like this: “Defeat false thoughts, promise that the Dharmakaya will be active” (Kill all false thoughts, let the Dharmakaya live). If you do not have false distinctions, you will naturally restore your own Dharmakaya. The Dharmakaya is unborn, immortal, non-dual, and no different from the Buddhas. The six ordinary dharma realms, i.e. heaven, humans, hell, hungry ghosts, animals, [Asura], and the four holy dharma realms which are Buddha, Bodhisattva, Pratyekabuddha, Sravaka, all ten dharma realms have only this one mind. The four saints are enlightenment. Due to the different levels of enlightenment, they are divided into four dharma realms and four types of appearances. Six mortals is delusion, six mortal dharma realms are different delusions. The Dharmakaya in ordinary people does not decrease, nor does it increase in Buddha's. The Dharmakaya is eternally motionless, indestructible, neither increasing nor decreasing. In the previous section, I talked about the meaning of space to visualize the Dharmakaya, that is, using space to compare the Dharmakaya. There is only a difference between delusion and enlightenment. If we eliminate ignorance, then we are no longer ordinary people. If you eliminate ignorance, you will become all saints; In the end, he became a Buddha.

(Sutra) Falling in the beginningless world, the evil ignorance of the mind, ignorance of causes and conditions gathers strength, present the realm of hope. Because of hoping for the realm of the accumulation of causes and conditions, giving rise to the corresponding mind, ego, ego, creating a collection of karma, experiencing birth and death, suffering, talking about the Dharmakaya, the name of them birth.
The illusion of ignorance appears, the realm of illusion appears. Due to the cause and effect of relying on the realm of illusion, the mind corresponding to illusion arises, comparing the self and the self (what belongs to us), creating karma, and suffering the suffering of birth and death, so we call that Dharmakaya a living being.

This paragraph says that your ignorant mind has arisen, that is, karma has arisen, so you create karma. Relying on the clear, pure, and immaculate true mind that you already have, you suddenly awaken. That true mind is called Original Enlightenment. Relying on the Original Enlightenment, unconsciousness arises, and basic delusion and ignorance are born. This principle is very difficult to explain clearly, it cannot be said clearly, it can only be understood with the mind. For example, in history, there have been many wise men and women who attained enlightenment in this way. I often mention that Mr. Ngu Trieu An of the Tang Dynasty asked the national master, "Where do troubles come from?" Or say: "Where does ignorance come from? What is ignorance?" The National Teacher did not answer him! If you answer, it won't be clear. The national teacher uses similes and skillful means! The Master said: "You are a slave and want to ask about Buddhism." The monk scolded the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister immediately became angry and replied: "I am a servant, but I am the emperor's servant. A Prime Minister is still above tens of thousands of people." That was his answer. The national teacher told him: "Ignorance arises from there. That is ignorance." Are you not asking me, "How is ignorance born? What is ignorance?" That is ignorance. If I explain, it won't be possible to describe it clearly. Wait until he gets angry, use the truth to explain to him, he will immediately be enlightened and understand. In Zen Buddhism, there are many sentences “the mechanism translates into translation”, to which basis the dharma is spoken. Therefore, the Buddha preached all the sutras, eighty-four thousand teachings, with the aim of speaking to eighty-four thousand faculties. Ignorance is the same. Ignorance is your unconsciousness. Where does that unconsciousness come from? From Original Enlightenment comes forth, from enlightenment comes forth. Only with Enlightenment can there be Unenlightened, relatively speaking!

In your foolish mind, the foolish mind is the dark mind. That dark mind and the essence of the Dharmakaya are two but one, but one but two. Dai Phuong Quang Buddha Hoa Nghiem Sutra talks about Body, Form, Use, Body is Form, Form is Body. Body and form then arise their effects (Use). Effects are Body and Form; Body and appearance are the effects. All three are one, mind body, mind form. Due to the delusion of that mind, all the effects are on living beings. To realize that mind is to be a saint. Because after falling in love with the Body, karma arises; Karma has arisen and has locked you down. That is called the suffering of birth and death. You have enlightened, understood, practiced, and restored your own Enlightenment; That is called “liberation”. Delusion is still this Dharmakaya, but enlightenment is still this Dharmakaya.

Therefore, while you are single-mindedly attached to all realms; At that time, the mind is controlled by delusion. Because everything is an illusion; Even when you practice the Dharma, until we recite Amitābha Buddha in the present, it is all false. The dharma you practice is also a dharma that belongs to the delusional mind. Depending on the delusional mind, you practice the dharma (illusory dharma). But there is truth in it: Buddha, Bodhisattva, Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha, heaven, human, Asura, hell, demons, animals, ten dharma realms have the same mind. If your mind rises to the realm of delusion, with delusion as the main focus, it is six mortals; Taking the pure mind as the master to give rise to all dharmas is the four saints. Hope is also this mind, truth is also this mind, enduring the suffering in the six paths of samsara is still this mind, becoming a Buddha, Bodhisattva, Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha is still this mind. Depending on which mind you correspond to, you belong to that dharma realm. Now you are a delusion. If you can cut off part of the delusion and release a part of the delusion, your afflictions will be relieved. Other people's attachments give rise to afflictions, but you do not give rise to afflictions and have no notion of distinction. Because it all depends on your attachments, ignorance and afflictions determine your position, neither saints nor mortals have certain standards. You have no afflictions, [but if] you have cut off all afflictions, you will be a saint. If you give birth to afflictions, then you are a sentient being.

The more severe the affliction, the deeper the fall. Falling into hell, falling into hungry ghosts, falling into animal birth, afflictions have reached their peak. In humanity, knowledge is power, knowledge is wisdom, and is the manifestation of afflictions. People with wisdom, their troubles are light; Those who have no wisdom have heavy afflictions. In society, it is also said "knowledge is power". Those without knowledge must always serve those with knowledge. Depending on how big or small your knowledge is, the greater your knowledge, the higher your status as an owner.

(Sutra) If living beings are in the midst of the world, the Dharmakaya gathers many powerful people, afflictions are spent, greedy world, seek Nirvana, believe in one truth, practice the Six Paramitas of the Bodhi level, part of the Dharma, and become a Bodhisattva.
(Sutra: If among living beings like that, due to the accumulation of Dharmakaya, afflictions will gradually arise. thin, can be bored with the world, seek Nirvana, have faith in the one truth, practice all the dharmas belonging to the Bodhi part such as the Six Paramitas, etc., then one is called a Bodhisattva).

This is taking the mind body of the Original Enlightenment as the Dharma Body, but that person uses good dharma to accumulate Truth, increase all good karma, and afflictions gradually become lighter. As for fame and fortune in the world, all dharmas in the world are dharmas that arise and pass away. That person wishes for a dharma that does not arise and die. Like those present here, we all seek the dharma that has no birth and death, we all hope to end afflictions, attain Bodhi, and overcome birth and death. That is learning the Dharma without birth and death. The word “listen to study” means to listen to the Dharma spoken by the Buddha. After listening, then think, think about how we should do it, “do” is to practice. Once you have done it, you will achieve it, and when you achieve it, you will attain enlightenment. The Mahayana Arising Faith Commentary says there are two types of tainted aggregates, one is pure tainted taints, the more tainted the coarser they are. Every day you spend time with someone who has a heavy killing mind, gradually your killing mind also becomes heavy! You stay with someone who is greedy, your greed also arises! Why will greed arise? There is no wisdom. That's called ignorance. If you see through a part, you will feel a part of it. This aspect is light, that aspect is heavy. Your greed, anger, and delusion will be lighter, while Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom will be deeper. Greed, anger, ignorance, precepts, concentration, wisdom; Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom are light, greed, anger, and ignorance are heavy!

(Sutra) If you are like a faithful Bodhisattva, practice all the good dharma completely, and attain ultimate liberation from ignorance and hypocrisy. changed his name to Buddha.
(Sutra: If among such Bodhisattvas, one can practice all good dharmas completely and thoroughly. leaving the sleep of ignorance, will change his name to Buddha).

What is Buddha? What are living beings? There are no standards; depends on your behavior to decide. If you practice all good dharmas and achieve them, that is called Buddha. If you practice evil deeds, a Chinese proverb often says "a place full of evil" (crimes pile up and overflow), that person cannot help but fall into hell, having practiced too much evil karma! Perfect Dharma is called Buddha. The good dharma is not yet complete and perfect, and is still a little worse than the Buddha, then he is called a Bodhisattva. Cessation of Thoughts and Thoughts is called Thanh Van and Duyen Giac. The ten dharma realms are determined by deep and heavy Or karma. Without Or karma, they are the four saints. That is using good and evil to distinguish between two paths, good and evil, depending on which path you follow!

(Sutra) Contemplating living beings, Bodhisattvas, Buddhas, worldly robes impersonating ancient sayings different, the body of the Dharmakaya has all wings and is equal, without any strange appearance.
(Sutra: You should know sentient beings, Bodhisattvas, Buddhas, etc. like that only depending on words impersonating the world, so there are differences, but the Body of the Dharmakaya is ultimately equal, with no other appearance).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: You should know that “living beings, Bodhisattvas, Buddhas” are all pretenders in the world. Relying on false identities to establish differences. In the previous section, it was said that the Dharmakaya's Body is everywhere, everywhere, all time, all sentient and inanimate, so that Body is equal, there is no difference.

(Sutra) Good man! Thi nam's brief theory of Nhat Tru realm meaning.
(Sutra: Hey good man! That's called speaking briefly about the meaning of the realm Nhat That).

The above is about attaining the realm of One Truth. What is the True Realm? It's the mind. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva preaches so much, just to explain the word Mind. That is True General. How to achieve True General? The ultimate means to enter is what you aim for, what you believe in, what you want to do, and if you do it right, you will advance towards the Buddha Vehicle. That is the means to advance. After you completely understand that situation, you will become enlightened. That's called Emptiness (dividing the Emptiness), [that is] through gradual analysis, you will understand. This is called Empty Contemplation. If you immediately realize the enlightenment, it is called the Emptiness, that is, there is no need to analyze, you immediately realize that the Essence [of all dharmas] is Emptiness. You realize that all things are Emptiness, originally everything does not exist, originally there is not a single material item, originally there is nothing, everything does not exist, originally it is empty. You increase a lot of afflictions, that is not Emptiness. Because we hope to cut off afflictions, increase a little more good karma and cut through afflictions, then we will attain Bodhi. That is “no Emptiness”. Good is in accordance with the meaning of Emptiness, and evil is contrary to the meaning of Emptiness. By doing good deeds and cultivating the Way, you will gradually be able to reach Li Kong. Doing evil is not easy, [because it] goes against the Principle of Emptiness. That is what Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: First of all, clearly explain the principle that there is only one mind.

(Sutra) Weak desire y Nhat Tru realm of cultivating faith and enlightenment, like learning two types of contemplation. Ha class vi two? One-person, mind-only contemplation. Second, the true Truth is contemplated. Studying the mind-only contemplation of the false consciousness, the taste depends on the time and place, depending on the body, speech, and mind, and the karma.
(Sutra: If you want to rely on the realm of One Truth to practice faith and understanding, you should study two What are the two? One is mind-only contemplation, the other is true mind-only contemplation. Learning mind-only contemplation is in all times, in all places, according to the karma created in the body, mouth, and mind).

If you practice, one is to learn mind-only contemplation, that is, mind-only contemplation. In all times, in all places, for the karma created in the body, mouth, and mind, in all times, that is, throughout the twenty-four hours, twenty-four hours day and night, you sleep the same, eat meals the same, dream the dream, work the same, your six senses, i.e. eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind have created, up to the Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma outside, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind correspond to Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Dharma, in which arise separate perceptions called eye consciousness, ear consciousness, nose consciousness, tongue consciousness, body consciousness, consciousness. These three types [Faces, Objects, and Consciousness] make up the eighteen realms. In all times, in all places, the karma you have created does not leave those eighteen types. Where did those eighteen types come from? Ignorance. In the previous section, we said: They arise based on ignorance, you should observe all dharmas, that is, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, eye consciousness, ear consciousness, nose consciousness, tongue consciousness, body consciousness, consciousness, those eighteen types. Those eighteen items, while you walk, sit, stand, lie down, sleep, talk, speak, including all movements, are inseparable from everything. You also cannot leave the realm (Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma)!

(Sutra) All things must be to observe, understand the mind, the mind, the absolute realm. Weakness in the mind that dwells on mindfulness, the stage of killing and understanding, and the spirit of the mind without knowing the conditions, without self-awareness. When thinking about time, one must observe and observe: Depending on the mind's condition, it completely uses the mind to rely on the thought, the mind knows itself. Inner soul remembrance arises spontaneously, not necessarily in the realm of thoughts and distinctions. The internal position of self-birth is "long, short, good, evil, good, bad, gain, loss, loss, benefit, existence, non-existence" of all views, immeasurable thoughts and realms necessarily arising from the rise of thoughts and discrimination. When knowing the absolute realm from non-discrimination, that is, from non-long, non-short, non-good, non-evil, non-existence, non-existence, non-non-existence, separate from the absolute form, observe it like this. It is necessary that the mind-only dharma arises. Weak history is centrifugal, there is no one dharma, one form, one can see right from wrong and separate from each other.
(Sutra: You should all observe, know that it is just the mind, even all the Realms, if the mind is focused, will observe and recognize, do not let the mind grasp and not be aware of it. In each thought, you should observe: Whenever the mind has something to think about, you should still let the mind follow that thought, knowing that it is your own mind that creates thoughts, not all realms have thoughts, there are distinctions. Right, wrong, gain, loss, loss, benefit, existence, non-existence, etc. are countless thoughts, but all realms have never had thoughts of distinction. You should know that all realms have no thoughts of distinction, that is, they are not long, not short, not good, not bad, to the point of not being, not being empty, observing like that, all dharmas are only born from the mind dharma, any form that can be seen differently).

Walking, standing, sitting, lying down, speaking, moving, Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, your every move all belongs to those twelve events. You learn to understand that it is all mind, it is all consciousness. You should observe those twelve types, as long as they are separated from my mind, from my consciousness, nothing exists. Don't give up any attachments to it. How to eliminate them? Don't you want to get rid of afflictions? Please put all your effort into these twelve events. You observe all appearances (appearing appearances, appearing appearances) outside, including your language, including actions, including the language, actions of everyone, all actions of "walking, standing, lying down, sitting", anyone is inseparable! Your eyes see all forms, your ears hear all sounds, your nose smells fragrant odors, your tongue tastes flavors, your ears hear sounds, and in your heart you recognize it. Those are all dharmas. All things recognized by the mind [the five sense objects, i.e., form, sound, smell, taste, appearing in the mind] are called Dharma.
