Among those twelve types of things, you should observe, is there any type that leaves your consciousness, leaves your mind? Please pay attention here! What's the blame? Perform elaborate practice. Separated from Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, is there anything else? If it doesn't exist, then those things will stop. When you observe, make those things stop, don't let them disturb your mind.

When you contemplate, you will have wisdom, clearly illuminating that everything is false, causing your mind to stay in thinking and start thinking, don't hold on to good things (phan condition), and don't hope to let go of bad things; that is, not making distinctions, not being attached to good things, not throwing away bad things. That is called “one mind without distinction”. We always have the tendency: We want to achieve good things, we wish to achieve them, we don't want to hear about bad things, but you can't help but listen, because of life you have to do it. Who is willing to be a coolie? Since there is no other way, I have to make a living! If you take life a little lightly, gradually step by step, you will find the source, go to the root. First of all, start from within yourself. The mind does not compare these things. When it comes to the things we like, we do not wish to achieve them, and achieving them is harmful. As for what you hate, you don't want to leave it, adapt to every situation, whatever realm you encounter, accept that realm!

But how to recognize it, how to recognize it? It's all fake, it's temporary, it's not permanent. The first thing is to contemplate this body, for a maximum of one hundred years, some people do not live to that age. We take the maximum limit of one hundred years to set this! Don't contemplate yourself, contemplate others! Observe that person being born, observe that person die, after death, what does that person take with him? When you are born, what do you bring with you? There is a Chinese proverb: "Birth never comes back, death never goes away" (Birth brings nothing with it, death brings nothing with it). Humans are all like that, some people know, some don't. What if you don't realize it? Desire never stops, forever pursuing, creating karma for the next life, that's all, grasping everywhere. That's called “phan dependent mind”. When that person is predestined (clinging to things), they still don't know, they are creating karma, that is, creating the karma of birth and death!

In every thought, you should observe: The things your mind is predestined to contemplate, think about, have [the idea] "for good things, the predestined thought does not give up", the more you think, the louder it gets! The more you pray for wealth, the better, the bigger the better, never ending, never ending! You yourself understand very clearly, you understand very clearly your own mind. What does it mean to achieve? Please speak from your own perspective, what can you ultimately achieve? In the end, just dying, isn't everything lost? Have you finally achieved all the signs of the external realm, such as wealth? Gained and lost! When you die, you can't take anything with you! That's observation at a crude level. Observing the subtleties, all things that have shape, form, awareness, or invisible things are created by your mind. They are the form of the mind. The mind is illusory, nothing really exists. At that time, you recite the Buddha, the Dharma, the Sangha, especially the Dharma, what dharma are you reciting? Birth and death, impermanence, suffering, all dharmas are not happy. We are greedy, think about birth, old age, sickness, death, love being separated, hatred and hatred having to meet, the Five Aggregates are burning, we cannot seek. Eight sufferings are burning together, which one can you get rid of? In your mind, you think: All of these things are idealistic and changing, there is nothing real or immutable. Thinking like that, mindfulness will appear.

Regardless of length, short, good, bad, gain, loss... these attachments, countless ways of thinking, observe for yourself: They are all distinctions, distinguished by your own mind. This distinction is problematic. You like good things, want to achieve them, and make them your own. Anything you don't like is not good, you want to get rid of it. You think about it, you take that thought as your own awareness. Does the mind have those characteristics or not? Please observe your own mind. If our disciples study Buddhism, have studied Buddhism, have entered Buddhism, you think of Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, there is that predestined mindfulness! Basically, if one has not heard the Buddha Dharma, even if one hears it, one does not believe it. Does that person have that predestined mindfulness? That person thinks about cars, money, how to get rich, [thinks about] beauty. Form includes all the things you like, all material things, what you like you hope to get, what you don't like you want to get rid of, until you have the concept of long, short, square, round, big, small, good, bad, your mind should always think that those things are all illusory, not real.

My inner desire is not to differentiate between those things, to stay away from those things. Those things don't have a certain standard. You think it's bad, others think it's good, you want to let go, others are greedy. Why? Due to the power of habit from beginningless kalpas to the present. The mind that creates karma has the power of habit. Many people, like us Buddhist disciples, see that this is not right, it is wrong, but there will be many people who think it is right, not wrong, [both sides] will be contradictory. There are people who follow the flow of life and death, creating karma to follow the flow of life and death. There are people who oppose birth and death, do not follow the current of birth and death, but go against the current, like us disciples of the Buddha. But no matter what, favorable circumstances, adverse circumstances, good, bad, right, wrong, all arise from the mind. Therefore, everyone should often think "mind arises, dharmas arise; mind ceases, dharmas cease", no dharma is separate from the mind! That mind is false, that is, a false mind. Separated from the mind, is there any dharma that can be independent? Between this dharma and that dharma, is there any difference? There is no difference! If the minds of sentient beings can reach that level, what is good and what is evil? "Dharma is born of causes and conditions, ego means emptiness" (Dharma is born of causes and conditions, I say it is emptiness). All dharmas are born from causes and conditions, good dharmas are also empty, and evil dharmas are also empty! Observing all dharmas like that, are only born from the mind. If you leave the mind, one dharma, one form, you will see that there is no difference. There is a difference because the minds of sentient beings differentiate, the dharma itself is not different.

noi_dung:
Lecture 13

(Sutra) Always satisfied like an inner keeper, ignorant of false thoughts, unreal realm, extinct animist. The name of a practitioner of Duy Tam Thuc Quan. The weak mind is indeterminate, not aware of the mind's own thoughts, that is, the pre-realm of existence, not named Mind-Only Consciousness. If you hold on to the false inner mind, you will block the knowledge of greed, anger, stupidity and wrong views, knowledge of good, knowledge of unwholesomeness, knowledge of neutrality, and knowledge of the laboring mind of all kinds of suffering.
(Sutra: Always keep in mind like that, knowing it is just an illusion, not the real world Don't give up. That's called practicing Mind-Only Consciousness. If the mind is neutral (neither good nor evil), and does not know one's own thoughts, then thinks there is a previous realm (realm before the six senses), then it is not called Mind-Only Contemplation, then knows greed, anger, and foolish thoughts, knows good, knows unwholesome, knows the suffering caused by the mind's hard thinking.

While we practice, we should know our mind. First of all, we must know the shape of the mind: What is the mind thinking, what is the mind remembering, how to eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance in the mind? How to transform them? That is the practice of Mind Only Consciousness. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You must know your mind, realize your own mind. Regarding all external realms, our eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are facing Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Dharma; Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Dharma are all realms (“foreground”). Those realm signs are “separate from the mind without any form”, [that is] separated from your mind, there will be no realm signs. You recognize it, all the signs of the realm are your mind. If you leave the mind, the appearance of the external realm will no longer exist. Because we are rotated according to the realm, the mind wanders outward, grasps, follows ideas to feel, raises awareness, but we want to stop the mind, not let it arise, it is impossible! What we can do is when your mind feels something wrong, recognizes that the previous thought has just raised something evil, immediately stops the next thought, doesn't let it arise, doesn't let it (that evil thought) continue. As soon as you realize [your mind] has an incorrect thought, you immediately stop it and don't let it continue. Because the thoughts and thoughts in our mind throughout the day correspond to few good dharmas, but many correspond to evil dharmas belonging to the realm of the six senses. Therefore, whenever you recognize the idea of ​​"greed, anger, ignorance" that has just arisen, immediately cut it off.

This passage teaches us that we can recognize the beginning of evil thoughts, then stop them, not allowing the next thoughts to arise. Such force is already very strong, making it impossible to continue. Right now we have not practiced to the point where all the thoughts that arise in our minds are good thoughts, we still cannot do that; But what you can do is recognize the wrong idea in your mind, stop thinking about it, and immediately control and stop it. Because whatever our minds think about is bad karma, because currently we sentient beings do not cultivate our minds, and our practice is not soulful! As long as you know that you are not thinking correctly, leaving the Three Jewels, leaving the Dharma, you can put an end to it. That strength is the strength born after hearing the Buddha's teachings. We often say "Recognizing the evil thoughts that arise in the past, being able to stop them and not allowing future thoughts to arise, is the Bodhisattva's awakening of mind". Do we ourselves feel that this is the normal way we practice? Is it possible to stop and not let thoughts arise? Not possible yet! When evil karma bears fruit, it means there is truth; does not create real evil karma, there will be no results! You have just started a thought and immediately stop, you will not be able to feel the results!

(Sutra) Weaknesses sit in the moment, depending on the mind's conditions, mindfully contemplating the birth and death of the mind. Forgiveness is like a stream of water, a flame, and no temporary residence. Tung Thi has attained the Samadhi of Sac Tich.
(Sutra: If when sitting (in meditation), depending on the condition of the mind [where], in each thought you contemplate there is only the mind that arises and dies. For example, like a stream of water or a fire in a lamp, there is never a moment of pause. From there, one will attain Samadhi of Form.)

When we practice static meditation, when we practice, your mind wants to practice Concentration, wants to sit down to concentrate, but you contemplate your own mind and can't concentrate, so you follow the signs of the realm that the mind is thinking about, no matter what realm, even the mind that is conditioned to good things is the same, and the condition is to follow evil thoughts as well, [those ideas] are all arising from the mind, belonging to the dharma of birth and death. If while meditating, no matter where the mind is, in each thought, you will see that [thoughts] are only caused by the mind arising and passing away. When you don't sit still and your thoughts are wandering, you don't know! Until you want to calm down and try to put in effort, then you raise your contemplation to contemplate the ideas in your own mind that are all dharma arising and passing away, like a stream of water [continuously flowing], or a fire in a lamp [continuously burning]. Is it possible to abide in non-thought? If you can temporarily make the mind calm, the mind is still and does not give rise to thoughts, if you can achieve such effort, you will achieve Samadhi of Form.

Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us that Samadhi of Form is in all places, all times, while you practice, when cultivating Quan Vien, generally speaking when cultivating Samadhi, right while you walk, stand, sit, lie down, when walking, or when not lying down, just sitting, in the four types of actions "walking, standing, sitting, lying down", you can all practice contemplation, you can all enter tranquility, but sitting is best, the power of contemplation is strong! When lying down, you will gradually fall asleep. When traveling, the mind easily wanders. Sit down, contemplate your own mind, contemplate how your own mind arises? Because the concept depends on the realm. The mind is inherently unborn and exists due to the environment. Your thoughts are inherently non-born, because of the realm [that thoughts arise]. The realm in the mind is due to thinking about the realm in the past, or thinking about the realm in the future. “The mind is inherently non-existent, it exists because of the scene”: Your mind does not exist, because of your thoughts, the world exists. At that time, you can make your mind quiet, there are no thoughts in your mind, you don't think about the past, you don't think about the present, and you don't even dream about the future. For an unenlightened thought, because in every thought, every thought feels determined, [so] there is no unenlightened thought, no unenlightened mind arises.

At the same time, at that time, you think, when you meditate, you contemplate, what is it? Contemplate that all things that have form are created by the mind. At that time, contemplate that all forms are just mind, there is only the birth and death of the mind. According to other Mahayana teachings, “when the mind arises, all dharmas arise, when the mind ceases, all dharmas cease”. All dharmas that arise are the same, and all dharmas die the same, they are all your thoughts. Quan means Projection. You sit still in order to practice. Practicing practice is to use your wisdom, that is, to use your thoughts to contemplate, to contemplate so that all movements (ideas operating in the mind) completely stop, no more thinking. Contemplation makes the mind without thoughts and calm. If you contemplate this mind with every thought, [you will see that this mind] is all "this thought arises, that thought disappears". Contemplate the birth and death in your mind to cut it off. Use mindfulness to cut off [thoughts that arise or disappear], there is no more thinking. That is exactly what Zen Buddhism often says "defeat false thoughts, promise that the Dharmakaya will be active" (kill false thoughts so that the Dharmakaya can live). Thoughts are calm, thoughts are calm, you realize that "mindfulness is inherently quiet". Once you can concentrate like that, the longer the concentration time, the better, and the mind will no longer be able to think. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You will attain Samadhi of Form; achieved at the initial level, you can practice gradually.

Ma Tha contemplate the mind, gain confidence Ba Xá Na contemplate the mind.
(Sutra: Having attained that samadhi, next, you should study faith in it contemplation of the mind with Xa Ma Tha and faith in mind contemplation with Bhikkhu Bà Xá Na).

After attaining that samadhi, you should study and trust the mind contemplation method by Xa Ma Tha. We often ask: "Do you have faith or not?" No faith! This is to teach us to practice faith. When you can concentrate, then you can contemplate and contemplate the mind so that you can gradually calm down. That is when there is Contemplation there is Contemplation, when there is Contemplation there is Contemplation; is called “Double Contemplation of Contemplation” (using both Contemplation and Contemplation). We say “Dinh Hue dual practice” with this meaning. Practice and believe in the method of contemplation of the mind with Xa Ma Tha, and at the same time also believe in the method of contemplation of the mind with Vai Ba Xa Na. This means applying Concentration and Hue together. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us that when we practice Samātha or Samādhi and practice Bhikārāna or Insight, that is, when we practice Samādhi, what do we practice in the meantime? Believe! We often think that with the Three Jewels, we ourselves have generated the power of faith, and have the power to generate faith. In fact, the power of faith is not yet there, faith has not yet "entered the position" (has not reached the level, or has not yet reached the minimum position of First Faith). Faith has not yet entered the position, how can it give birth to strength? Therefore, we must practice.

(Sutra) File Xa MaTha contemplates the false mind, the inner thoughts cannot see the form, perfect and immovable, no future, no past, the original nature is not born, is not destroyed, has no distinction.
(Sutra: Practicing faith in mind contemplation with Xa MaTha is the inner thought that cannot see the form, is perfect and immovable, does not come, does not go, the original nature is not born, is not destroyed, due to separation).

“Concentration Xa Ma Tha contemplation of the mind” is an inner mindset that cannot see the form, is perfect and motionless, does not come, does not go. The inherent nature, the inherent Being is inherently unborn, immortal, due to separation. That is the first step for us to practice Mind-Only Consciousness, achieving that all external environments do not exist, only the mind appears, there is only the internal mind, there is no external environment. How do we observe the appearance of the inner mind? Everyone, please contemplate what shape your inner mind has? It's completely impossible! Can't see the form, can't see the form of the inner mind. When you practice, you will feel that everything is "the cause and conditions that give birth to dharma, ego means Emptiness" (dharma is born because of causes and conditions, I say it is Emptiness). We often say that practicing Khong Quan is not that easy. Here there is a very long passage of scripture, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us how to practice Emptiness. Practicing Khong Contemplation is just the beginning, you should have faith like that, faith will give birth to strength. Having the power of faith, you think "you can't see your own mind, you can't see its appearance", but it is perfect, without defects. That is the original mind. Our true mind and Buddha's true mind are inherently two, no different, perfect, immovable, with no appearance of coming or going, no appearance of birth and death, and no appearance of distinction. Do we believe it or not? Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to practice Faith, which means to believe in this mind. The sutras often say “do you have faith or not?” There is no Dharma friend who answers "I have no faith", none at all! Without faith, how can one enter the Three Jewels? Have faith! In fact, we have not "entered the throne", our faith is "mao dao", [i.e. like a hair], as soon as the wind blows, it blows away. Uncertain trust, like a feather, cannot withstand the wind. If you get blown, you'll fly away! First of all, you must practice faith in Concentration, faith in Hue, and contemplate your mind.

(Sutra) Bhikkhu File Ba centrifugal, non-returning, non-returning, non-past, non-past, non-birth, non-birth, non-action, non-action.
(Sutra: Practicing faith in mind contemplation with the Bhikkhu Bà not not going, not being born, not not not being born, not doing, not not doing).

“ Focusing on Bhikkhu Bà Regarding “seeing internal and external colors” , what is the appearance of internal colors? What is the appearance of appearance? Follow the mind of birth, follow the mind of death. That general is impossible! Because the mind arises, it arises. The mind disappears, it no longer exists! You still have to practice, imagining seeing the Buddha's body: The Buddha's body and the bodies of sentient beings are the same, they also arise depending on the mind, and disappear according to the mind. Depending on the mind, it arises, depending on the mind, it perishes. Just as we contemplate the Buddha's form, the thirty-two [great man's] and eighty good qualities of the Buddha, they are also subject to birth and death in the same way: "The mind arises, the form arises; the mind disappears, the form disappears", they are all illusory! The shadow of the moon in the water at first glance seems to be there and cannot be retrieved. In fact, it doesn't exist. Is the appearance in the mirror present or not? Is the appearance in the mirror real? Everyone knows it's not real. All dharmas are like that: According to your mind, dharmas arise. According to your mind, the dharmas are destroyed, they are all illusory, not true. Therefore, like the shadow of the moon in the water, like the form in the mirror, when reflected in the mirror, the form appears, not the mind, not leaving the mind, not coming, not not coming, not going, not not going, not born, not not born, not doing, not not doing, all dharmas are like that. Yes or no? No! Is it no? Again, it's not a no!

Therefore, giving many examples like that, is to say that all dharmas are just the appearance of the mind-only realm, a realm conditioned by the mind, just the mind, outside the mind there is no dharma! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: While you practice all dharmas, know that all dharmas are Emptiness, all dharmas are False. Emptiness is practicing Emptiness; Forgery is to practice Jia Quan. Between Emptiness and Falsehood, there is something that is neither Emptiness nor Falsehood, that is called the Middle Way. Saying No and False means speaking according to the Truth. All things arise from Reason. There is no Emptiness, no Falsehood, showing "nothing beyond the Middle". Madhyamaka is Reason. Because the Middle Way can become a False Store, it can become an Empty Store. Without the Middle Way, there will be no Falsehood, nor will it become Emptiness. Reason can become all things, Things can manifest Reason.

We are attached to internal appearances; That's called Inner Sac. This passage teaches about the mind-only realm: Internal Form does not exist, it appears from the mind. Form is Reality, but it can reveal Reason. Without Truth, the Truth cannot be revealed. You are attached to Feelings, Thoughts, and Consciousness, these are "Things are also Reasons", but you can achieve Things. The possibility manifests itself. That is just the Form inside, called Internal Form. So what is Outer Color? External Form arises from seeing Internal Form. Internal Form depends on the mind. The form within is "when the mind arises, dharma arises; when the mind ceases, that form also ceases". Internal Form depends on the mind, but also depends on the mind. Ngo Sac is not like that. You don't think about External Form, it still exists. This is due to attachment; it doesn't matter whether you are attached or not. You are attached to Feeling and Form, or you are not attached to Feeling and Form. Feeling in Form, Feeling, Perception, Action, Consciousness means “receiving”. Regardless of whether you are attached or not, it still exists the same. That is External Sac. Internal Form depends on the mind to arise and die. Outside of Form, your mind is born, it also exists; the mind is destroyed, it still exists!

If we wish to see the birth and death of External Form, the sutra gives an example. Regarding the Buddha's physical body, we visualize the Buddha's thirty-two generals and eighty good qualities. You say, "My mind has been destroyed, [there should be] no Buddha form." [However], the Buddha's appearance still naturally exists, it does not follow your mind of birth and death. As for Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Arhats, Sravakas, up to heavens, humans, Asuras, hells, demons, animals, all forms in the ten dharma realms, all appearances in the ten dharma realms, created by whom? Due to artifacts? Or is it not thanks to creation that it still exists? Do the physical appearances of the ten dharma realms exist or do they not exist? [Determining it] as existence, non-existence, non-existence, non-existence, are not correct! What is right? Because all dharmas are natureless, have no essence, are dependently arisen, that is, arise due to causes and conditions. So will they disappear due to fate? Dharma also does not exist. It does not mean created, has no nature, is dependently arising.

The mind produces such visualization to contemplate all dharmas, that is called One Mind and Three Contemplations. The mind within the dharma, the mind outside the dharma, until for all the dharmas that arise, Emptiness, False Contemplation, Middle Contemplation, Emptiness is still the mind, False Contemplation is still the mind, Middle Contemplation is still the mind. When the mind arises, all dharmas arise; if the mind ceases, all dharmas cease. Therefore, it is called One Mind Three Quan. Just don't leave the mind, but Quan also doesn't leave the mind, only the mind! In this passage, it is the same for Bhikkhu Sāna, until cultivating Samādhi, practicing Contemplation, Lo Xāna nature, Bhikāra Sāna, Sāma Tha, both are [our mind], Samādhi and Contemplation are equal. Again, when it comes to Contemplation, Contemplation is Contemplation, that is, "motion is stillness, in stillness there is movement, in movement there is stillness. When there is Contemplation, there is Contemplation, when there is Contemplation, there is Concentration. Contemplation and Contemplation both apply". That is contemplation of Emptiness, contemplation that all dharmas are Emptiness, contemplation that all dharmas are false, but not departing from the meaning of the Middle Way, because of the Middle Way it appears. That's the explanation!

(Sutra) Good man! If you have the weak ability to concentrate on the two contemplations of your mind, you will quickly attain the path of the One Vehicle.
(Sutra: Good man! If you can practice faith in those two types of mind contemplation, you will quickly enter and comprehend the One Vehicle teachings.

At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also explained further: Good man! If you can practice faith in these two types of mind contemplation, you will quickly enter and comprehend the One Vehicle. The scriptures being taught here are all about Faith. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva only wants us to believe in the Mahayana Dharma, not to mention attainment, which is still very far away. We often think that we have faith. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said we have no faith. How does he teach to be considered trustworthy? You must practice, how long must you practice? Those who speak according to the teachings will know that it is ten thousand lifetimes. Ordinarily speaking, we take refuge in the Three Jewels and believe in Buddha's teachings. We have faith, but that faith has no roots and no understanding. Faith, Effort, Mindfulness, Concentration, Hue, whenever you have faith in your mind, you will diligently practice, not lazy, always recite the Three Jewels, do not lose mindfulness, wisdom always shines, do not let wrong ideas [grow]. As soon as you feel a thought arising, you shape it, every thought is based on the Three Jewels. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva explains this issue again and again for us to enter. What is entering? Confidence. Good man! To be able to practice faith in these two types of mind contemplation, one must have faith in the two types of contemplation of the path and the realm of One Truth. [All that the Bodhisattva taught] is only intended to make us believe. Once we believe, He will teach us how to enter and how to practice! You must enter two types of contemplation to be able to enter the One Vehicle path, to be able to enter the One Vehicle dharma.

(Sutra) When you know the Mind Only Consciousness Contemplation, the name of the supreme gate of wisdom, the power of the mind is powerful and powerful, chief believer

force, enter Emptiness, attain the unsurpassed Bodhi mind.

(Sutra: You should know that Mind Only Contemplation is called the ultimate wisdom, that is, because it has can make the mind sharp, increase the power of understanding, quickly enter the meaning of Emptiness, and give rise to the unsurpassed mind of great Bodhi).

What is this Quan practice called? Mind-Only Consciousness Contemplation. You should know Mind Only Consciousness Contemplation like that, all dharmas are mind only, all dharmas are only consciousness. You must use the power of contemplation to recognize what "all dharmas are consciousness only", what "all dharmas are only mind". That is the ultimate wisdom method. Because studying this wisdom method, we can make our minds sharp. “Strong, sharp” means like we do something very strong, agile, not afraid of danger. Once you have that faith, only when you practice in the Buddhadharma can you be strong, sensitive, and your understanding power can increase. Why do we not believe deeply? Because you don't explain! If you don't explain, your trust won't be deep. Until you understand and explain, your faith increases. What did you achieve? Quickly enter the meaning No. That is just the prelude to Khong Quan, that is, the means to practice Khong Quan. Without money and means, you will not succeed in practicing Emptiness. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told us: That is the wisdom, the ultimate wisdom. Everyone hopes to gain wisdom but there is none, there is still no door to enter! You don't even have a door to enter, how can you enter wisdom? What we have learned is Omniscience, not wisdom. Wisdom is the will of birth and death, achieving Nirvana. We are all the Wisdom of the world. Because we have faith, wisdom has grown, we have the strength, for the dharma spoken by the Buddha, you can understand, that is called “faith dissolving power”. If you don't believe it, how can you understand it? You must first gain faith and then you can understand.

Our explanation is similar. Having the power to understand, because of that power of understanding, one can understand and enter Emptiness. Only by understanding the meaning of Emptiness can the unsurpassed Bodhi mind arise. Each of us Dharma friends knows that developing Bodhi mind is fundamental. If you criticize someone, saying that he does not develop Bodhi mind, that person will absolutely not accept it. But you have to dig in and research a bit: How can one be considered to develop Bodhi mind? Achieving the position of the Ten Faiths, having the power to believe and understand to realize the meaning of Emptiness. Develop Bodhi mind, Bodhi mind is not Existence, but Emptiness; From Emptiness comes Being. Truly developing the great Bodhisattva mind, through analysis, we understand: This is the development of the great Bodhisattva mind, knowing that outside the mind there is no dharma. Cultivating Concentration and Hue like that is called “Only Contemplation”; That's called Vien Giao, Doan Giao. Everyone knows Master Tri Gia. Great Master Tri Gia founded the four teachings of the Thien Thai sect, all of us monks acknowledge his wisdom. Both lay disciples and monastic disciples acknowledge the wisdom of Great Master Tri Jia. When he passed away, his disciples asked him: "Master, what position have you attained now?" He replied: "If I don't build a pagoda and propagate the Dharma to benefit sentient beings, I can reach the First Pillar. Because of propagating the Dharma to benefit sentient beings, I can only reach the status of Five Products", which is the fifth position in the Faith Position of the Complete Teaching. Everyone knows: Judging by the power of Great Master Tri Jia's practice of Chi Quan and Citadel, he has reached the Fifth Grade position in Samadhi and Citadel, which means he has not yet reached the level of six senses of purity. Only when you reach the position of six pure senses can you participate in the First Pillar of the Vien Giao. In other words, still not participating in the position of First Tru.

Bodhisattvas have participated in the position of First Abode, and can manifest Buddha's body to make offerings to all Buddhas in the ten method realms. The Ten Faiths reach perfection, participate in the position of the First Pillar of Vien Giao, and enter the First Meaning Void. “Emptiness” is no obstacle, the ten precepts are no obstacle. That Bodhisattva will never fall as an ordinary person, nor will he fall into the Second Vehicle. This meaning is completely consistent with the meaning in the Avatamsaka Sutra. The Avatamsaka Sutra says so, the six senses are pure, the First Meaning is Emptiness, Emptiness is pure. When we say “pure”, we must have realized the meaning of Emptiness, to have realized the meaning of Emptiness means to have attained ultimate purity. Whenever we hear about Credibility, we feel that Credibility is very low. [Actually], Trustworthiness is also very high, Trustworthiness in Vien Giao is not easy! For the Believers of the Vien Teaching, when you perfect the Ten Faiths, you will never fall into the world, nor will you fall into the Second Vehicle. At that time, entering the First Pillar position of the Vien Teaching, that is "developing the great Bodhi mind". The position of the First Pillar in the Vien Teaching is the Pillar of Developing the Mind, so it is called “developing the Bodhi mind”.

into seeing, hearing, knowing, forever leaving all discriminating ideas).

(Sutra) Dac thi samadhi, that is, the ability to enter Nhat Hanh samadhi. Entering the Samadhi of Nhat Hanh, seeing countless Buddhas, developing a profound and generous mind, remaining steadfast in faith and belief, and feeling Xá Na, the two types of contemplating the path, deciding on faith and understanding, and determining direction.

can decide to follow [Buddhism]).

Having attained that samadhi (Samadhi of the Pure Mind), you can enter Nhat Hanh samadhi. Because you have attained the Samadhi of Mind, you can enter the Samadhi of Nhat Hanh. Having entered Nhat Hanh samadhi, you will be able to see countless Buddhas. The Buddhas of the ten directions can see it, develop a deep and wide mind, and abide in a position of steadfast faith. What do you firmly believe in? There are two types of contemplation: Xa Ma Tha and Vai Ba Xa Na. Not only believe, but can then solve; At that time, I decided to follow Buddhism. “Deciding direction” is deciding to follow the Buddhist path. What position is that? Complete the Ten Faiths. Only then is it called “having faith”. That is the person of perfect faith, that is the attainment of the person of perfect faith. What news? Believe in this Nhat Hanh samadhi. Nhat Hanh samadhi is due to contemplating the mind of Xa Ma Tha and the Samadhi of Bhikkhu Xa Na; At that time, countless Buddhas can be seen, giving rise to a vast mind. At that time, I started practicing. Believing in Vai Ba Xa Na Quan, believing in Xa Ma Tha Chi, is called “Double-movement Chi Quan”. This is called “Chi Quan Quan Dou”. Six pure senses: Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind are six pure senses, belonging to the position of steadfast faith. At that time, your faith will not falter, your strength will not falter, and you will achieve a steadfast position. What position is that? First position in Vien Giao. At that time, once again abiding in the Bodhi mind, practicing the Bodhisattva path, arousing the positions that belong to the mental conduct of the One Vehicle Great Bodhisattva in the Complete Teaching, the power of belief and understanding is complete.

(Sutra) According to the practice of studying the worldly practice of the Zen samadhis, without any ridicule, the mind will transform. necessarily good root Bodhi part of the Dharma. He is loyal to life and death, has no fear, and does not mock the Second Vehicle.
Completely practice all the good dharmas of the Bodhisattva part. In the midst of birth and death, do not be afraid or weak, and do not like the Second Vehicle.

At that time, that person believed and entered the true view of Truth. The Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, and Ten Dedications include thirty positions. Although there are thirty positions, entering the First Pillar and the final position is the Ten Dedications, although there are thirty positions [as just mentioned], in fact, [every position in the Tam Hien] has entered the six pure senses, that is, the six senses of eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are all pure.

(Sutra) Because of the ability to focus on the two contemplations of the mind, the most wonderful and cunning, the wise base their basic practice.
(Sutra: Being able to rely on, aiming to practice the Two Methods of Contemplative Practice of the mind is a miraculous skillful means That is the basis to rely on to apply wisdom.)

When practicing these two types of contemplation, his wisdom and skillful means increase. Practicing that dharma (two types of contemplation), will depend on the Bodhi mind similar to the true mind. Those thirty positions (Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications) are all similar to Bodhicitta. What is true? Participating in the First Stage, the Bodhisattva will truly attain Bodhi mind.

The Ten Pillars, the Ten Virtues, and the Ten Dedications are all called similar positions. Even though it is the First Pillar, up to the tenth position in the Ten Returns, although there are up to thirty positions, but according to the Principle, [those positions] are all the same. However, considering the general outline, there is a difference between shallow and deep. At that time, whoever abides in faith and achieves perfection will be like having attained Enlightenment, but it is only similar, not real. When you reach the First Level, it is true, you attain a part of the Dharmakaya. When participating in the First Pillar position, it is similar to attaining Dharmakaya, not truly attaining it.

(Sutra) Restore the second, practice like a superior believer and enlighten the false, two races of human beings. Ha class vi two? The best, the most beneficial. Second fake, padded base. The person with the benefit of knowledge has the ability to perceive all external realms, only mind-based actions, illusory and unreal, like a dream, like an illusion, determined to have no doubts. The warmth of the air is light, the mind is scattered and small. Like a person of the same level, that is, studying Truthfulness Contemplation. The person with the root of ignorance, the immortal has the ability to perceive all external realms, must only perceive the mind, which is false and unreal. Trying to be infected with the situation, obstacles arise, the mind is difficult to control. Ufirst learn Mind Only Contemplation.
(Sutra: Again, practicing faith and explanation as above, there are two types of people. What are the two? One is the benefit The second is the blind sense. First of all, those with good sense can know that all the external realms are only created by the mind, they are false, unreal, dreamlike, illusory, etc., and have no doubts. The light is less, the mind is less distracted. Such people should immediately learn to contemplate the Truth. is false, not real. Therefore, if you are deeply infected with attachment, obstacles arise many times, the mind is difficult to control. First of all, you should learn Mind-Only Consciousness.

There are roughly two types of people, which two types? What are these two? One is the person with good sense, the other is the person with stupid sense. Studying the same dharma together has beneficial roots and dull roots. What is the benefit of the situation? Those who have good sense are first able to know that all external realms are only created by the mind. When one who has the advantage of cultivating the Dharma, knows that all dharmas are manifested by the mental factors (psychological effects of the delusional mind), all dharmas are illusory, not real, not real, they are manifested by the mind. That person can know that all dharmas are false and not real, only created by the mind. What kind of realm do all dharmas represent? Just like we dream, or the illusory transformations in a circus act. At that time, [his mind] has no doubts or thoughts. Regarding all dharmas, we have doubts, thoughts, [the sutras often say] there are “doubts”. When reading the sutras, you harbor doubts about the teachings in the sutras. [Because those doubts] are so small, you cannot recognize them. If all dharmas are separated from the mind, there will be no dharma, only created by the mind, they are all illusory, not real, just like you dream, illusory and not real. A person who has just attained this position and has perfected the mind of the Ten Faiths will have no doubts, and will have no doubts about all dharmas.

Because Kettle is lighter, the mind is less scattered. There are five types of Skandhas, the Five Skandhas, or Five Aggregates. [What is] Five Things (the five things that cover up). Normally speaking, the Five Aggregates are Form, Feeling, Thoughts, Actions, and Consciousness, these things are called the realm of the Five Aggregates. What are aggregates? Aggregates mean “obscuring, obstructing”, [i.e. things] that obscure your True Nature. Those Karmas cover you up. Because you raise a lot of afflictions, those afflictions block your true mind. “What” is the Five Things, which are the dharmas of desire, anger, sleep, rhythm (lao chao), remorse (regret), and doubt. These dharmas are collectively called "afflictions". Doubt and Worship are just specific names for afflictions, they are all afflictions. You have been afflicted, causing your mind to be covered up, bound, obstructed, and your true mind cannot be revealed. Because it cannot be manifested, practice will not be effective. Without any of these, practicing will easily be effective. At that time, practicing towards the two types of contemplation, cultivating your own mind, you will be able to practice towards the two most skillful types of contemplation of the mind, and be able to use skillful means. That is the refuge of all wisdom, being able to practice the basic virtues. Of course, that person's ability to understand is complete, participating in the position of First Tru. Although it is not really enlightening the mind and seeing the nature, [it is] just similar to the enlightening mind and seeing the nature, belonging to a similar status, but that person has understood.

Furthermore, there are two types of people who practice faith and explanation as above, one type is the advantageous base, the other is the dull base. People with good faculties know that all external realms are created by the mind. Separated from the mind, outside there is no dharma, [often said] "outside the mind there is no dharma". All dharmas are mind, apart from dharma there is no mind. All dharmas are mind, mind gives birth to all dharmas, apart from dharma there is no mind. Right at that time, people with good sense can clearly understand, explain, and believe. Those with dull senses will not be able to understand. A person with good faculties has no doubts, the Five Aggregates and Five Aggregates are light, his mind is usually not scattered, his mind is always in Concentration. Concentration can give birth to Hue. People with good faculties can go one step further and practice True Contemplation. Why does the First Pillar Bodhisattva also see True Suchness? Because he can begin to practice True Contemplation. He has not attained enlightenment; Although he did not realize it, he believed. His faith is not like our faith. His right understanding is due to relying on the Truth and Ground to give rise to faith. He knows that all dharmas appear only in the mind. All dharmas are mind. That is the level of benefit.

A blind person can't do that. Regarding all external realms, the ignorant person does not have such complete faith and does not have such faith. Because that person is heavily infected with worldly habits, the Five Obstacles and Obstacles often arise and are not well controlled in the mind. Roughly speaking, [saying "the ignorant"] means talking about our masses. Nowadays, we are not skillful in taming our mind, often causing Evil and Obstacles to arise. So what should we do? Learn Mind Only Consciousness Contemplation. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us a method: Cultivating Mind-Only Consciousness. But to believe and understand the world of One Truth, we must practice the power of faith and release the power, that is, when we practice Mind-Only Contemplation to the point of truly entering, it is called the Name Tu Vi (The Name Is Buddha) in the Complete Teachings. Believing in the world of One Truth, cultivating faith, cultivating enlightenment, is called the Name Tu Vi in Vien Giao. Therefore, divided into neutral base and beneficial base. Loi Can practice a little faster, Ding Can practice a little more slowly, the method is a little different!

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught: If someone studies faith and explanation, learns faith, studies explanation like that, even though you learn faith and explanation, there are not enough good roots, there are many bad karma, good roots are weak. When it comes to cultivating the path to a higher level, the rate of progress is very slow, not as fast as someone with strong roots. Therefore, afflictions arise and you cannot overcome them. Now we cannot subdue the afflictions that arise in our minds, but we still do not recognize the afflictions. If you don't even recognize the affliction, how can you subdue it? For example, if we feel something is not right, the previous thought caused evil, don't let the thought arise again, we must stop it! If you can stop it, you will be a person of good taste. You will recognize that the previous thoughts are evil and stop them, not allowing the later thoughts to arise. That is "having good roots". Recognizing that the previous thought is evil and allowing it to continue, unable to stop it, or feeling that the previous thought that has just arisen is not right, [that thought] is far from the path of birth and death, we can immediately stop it. Very good! I'm just afraid of being moved by karma and following it! For cases like that, how should we practice? Subdue it gradually, subdue it slowly! But that person harbors doubt, fear, “fear” and is not brave. At the same time, fear of falling into hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, the three evil destiniess, very afraid of the three evil destiniess. Suppose in this life you fall into misfortune and fall into the three evil destiniess, what should you do? Or be born in the eight misfortunes, that is, be born in a place where there is no Buddha Dharma. In this life, if you don't encounter Buddha Dharma, if you don't encounter Buddha Dharma, the future will be difficult!

What are the eight obstacles? If one is born into the hell path or falls into the hell path, can one still practice? The Dharma is also not heard. Hungry ghosts, animals, and Bac Cau Lo Chau do not listen to Buddha's teachings. Truong Tho Thien, how can a blind, deaf, mute person learn Buddhism? Can't learn! There is also a very intelligent type, The Wisdom Wisdom, who claims to be intelligent and does not believe in Buddhism. There are also people born before Buddha, or born after Buddha. That is called “eight tribulations”. Now Śākyamuni Buddha has passed away, after the time when Śākyamuni Buddha was in this world, Maitreya Buddha has not yet been born, that is, before Maitreya Buddha's time in the world, we are in one of the eight tribulations, that is, "First Buddha, Later Buddha". But we can listen to Buddha's teachings again, now we can study the Ksitigarbha Sutra. This is a special dharma. Even if we avoid half of this disaster, we still have the Buddha's teachings to listen to. In a situation like this, called the Dharma-Ending Age, our minds are not so pure, it is very difficult to conquer, enter the path, cultivate the path, there are many obstacles, very difficult! We cannot believe in the world of One Truth, the mind of understanding cannot arise. We also cannot enter the position of Vien Giao's Name, nor can we be called “Vien Nhan”. People who believe in the Vien Giao Dharma are called “perfect people”. With complete people, nothing is incomplete. Our knowledge is truly incomplete, distorted, and misleading. What is the main obstacle? Seeing that other people are not right, I always feel like I'm pretty good. That is the main [obstacle]. The most important obstacle is not being empty-minded, not being able to respect all dharmas, and also not being able to respect all people. How can we give rise to complete enlightenment? Know that all realms are mind, apart from mind there is no dharma. If we could have that faith, it would be wonderful; That is called “complete explanation, complete text” (complete understanding, complete listening). What should I do if I have such a deep attachment?

(Sutra) One needs to recite the name of the self at all times, at all places.
(Sutra: Be at all times, in all places, always diligent ability to chant my name).

Finally, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: No matter what you study, you won't succeed, there's no way to do anything, so it's best to recite my name. Just recite “Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva” and you'll be fine! First, eliminate the accident, then enter. Finally, he said: Even though a person learns to believe and explain like that, the roots of good karma are thin, that is, good karma is fragile, unable to penetrate and move towards higher levels, evil afflictions cannot gradually disappear, unable to subdue [those afflictions], the mind of doubt is very heavy. Oh my! The Buddhist path is long and long, seeing that "if you enter into that faith, it will take that long to practice", immediately become discouraged, scared, and even afraid, afraid of falling into the three evil destiniess, afraid of falling into the eight tribulations, saying Bodhi path is long, impossible to achieve! There are all kinds of fears, all kinds of obstacles like that, for people like that, what should we do? Be diligent in chanting my name at all times and in all places. There is no other way! That is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva offering a convenient method, no matter what you practice, you cannot enter, that's okay! Please recite my name! Still can't recite? At all times and in all places, always chant my name diligently, without interruption. Reciting His name for a long time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva blesses you, will make your mind not scattered, and can attain concentration. Concentrate your mind first, then move on to the second step!

(Sutra) Weaknesses attain oneness of mind, good roots grow, thoughts are powerful, contemplating the Dharmakaya self, updating all beings Buddha Dharmakaya, self-centered, equal nature, non-dual, non-differentiable, unborn, immortal, permanent, happy, self, pure, full of merit, able to take refuge.
(Sutra: If you attain one mind, good roots grow, your mind is strong, sharp, you should contemplate the Dharmakaya mine and the Dharma Bodies of all Buddhas, together with my own body, are of equal nature, incomparable, no different, unborn, immortal, permanent, happy, self, pure, full of merit, worthy of taking refuge).

At that time, if you attain single-mindedness, your thoughts are mature, recite the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, rely on the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, your mind's delusions will be less, your mindfulness will be more, your good roots will grow, your thoughts will be strong and sharp. Once your thoughts are strong and sharp, you will not simply recite my name, but will also practice one step further and contemplate my Dharmakaya. My Dharma Body is the Dharma Body of all Buddhas, but also the Dharma Body of your own practitioners. Dharmakaya is not two, there is no difference. The Buddhas of the ten directions and all sentient beings of the ten directions have the same Dharma Body. Because of the nature of equality, no two, no difference, no birth, no death, permanent, happy, self, pure, full of merit, worthy of refuge. Everyone understands this. Therefore, diligently reciting my name will be able to eliminate lethargy and confusion for you. Because you recite the name for a long time, you will increase the power of your mind, and will gradually correspond to the realm of One Truth, which you can trust and enter. But you must regularly remember and observe Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. To observe Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is to observe all the Buddhas of the ten directions, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's mind is the nature of the Tathagata, not two, no different from the Buddhas of the ten directions. All Buddhas in the ten directions and all sentient beings are one mind, there are no two minds! The mind is one, there is only delusion or enlightenment. There is a big difference between delusion and enlightenment. All sentient beings are delusional, Buddhas in the ten directions are enlightened, but their original nature is no different. Delusion is still this nature, but enlightenment is still this nature. That nature has always been unborn from beginningless time, but is also unborn, undying, and eternal. If you stay forever, you will never die. We are complete and eternal. That is the permanent dharma, there is no opposition, there is no feeling of pain or pleasure at all! Forever is happiness. The bodies of living beings and the bodies of Buddhas are permanent, happy, self, and pure. Where is the difference? Two words! One side is delusion, the other side is enlightenment. Because we are confused and lost about this; Once enlightened, it will be restored!

(Sutra) Prosperity contemplates body and mind, impermanence, suffering, selflessness, impurity, such as illusory, transformed, and irresistible.
(Sutra: Also observe the appearance of your own body and mind as impermanent, suffering, impermanent self, impure, illusory, transformed, should be abandoned).

Go one step further, observe your own body or mind, which has no suffering or pleasure; But now we have become sentient beings, because we have become confused with the mind, so we are different. Don't consider those "suffering, emptiness, impermanence, non-self" as illusory or transformed. You should have a mind of boredom and detachment. Once the mind is bored and separated, the mind will be born wishing and praying for purity.
