Test the cause of giving up one's life, never fall into the evil realms, the realm of the eight tribulations, complete the Dharma, practice with faith, and with the ability to pray to be reborn in other pure Buddha lands.
(Sutra: If you can practice and learn the method of Contemplation like that, you will quickly grow your mind of pure faith, all The obstacles are gradually reduced. Why is that? That person is called learning to listen to my name, but can also learn to listen to the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, called learning to wholeheartedly worship and make offerings to me. He can also learn to wholeheartedly worship and make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, called learning to listen to the profound Mahayana sutras, called learning to accept, copy, make offerings to, and respect the profound Mahayana sutras, called learning to receive and recite the profound Mahayana sutras, called studying far away. Abstaining from wrong views and not falling into slander towards the righteous cause is called learning and understanding the First True Meaning which is very profound and profound. It is called being able to eliminate sin and hindrances. It is called being able to attain immeasurable amounts of merit. He sacrifices his life and does not fall into the evil realms and the eight tribulation places. He still listens to the Dharma, cultivates faith, and cultivates virtue, and can also wish to be reborn in a pure Buddha land in another direction.)

But pure dharma is also born from a single thought, impure dharma is also born from your mind, they are all your present nature. This encourages and encourages us: We and all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, up to Amitābha Buddha whom we often recite, all have the same Body as Amitābha Buddha. The essence of the Dharmakaya is the same, [it's just] delusion or enlightenment are different. If we can let go of delusion, get rid of delusion, and return to enlightenment, it will be okay! Thus, you should practice Samādhi. [For those] whose karma is heavy and unable to practice, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has a special means of “reciting His name” to eliminate karma. Increase your pure faith and then practice Chan Contemplation. Reciting His name like that, all obstacles will gradually be destroyed and damage reduced!

If someone practices like that, what is the reason that person does that? “Ha co co” (Why?) That person is called “learning to listen to my name”. Because he feels that he can't learn anything else, so he just practices [reciting the name]. Hearing my name, reciting my name, that is called “learning to listen to my name”. Why do we still need to study the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? That meaning is very deep. If we understand Earth as mind, Storehouse as container, what encompasses the minds of all of us sentient beings is Earth Store. Ksitigarbha is the mind of sentient beings. The mind-ground contains the nature of the outflow of merit, the same Body, not two, not different from the Buddhas, the same Body, not two, not different from Ksitigarbha. What is included in our mind is Ksitigarbha, Ksitigarbha is our mind. That is the Mahayana teachings, and according to the Hoa Nghiem teachings, they all say so. That person, the one who recites His name, is called “learning to hear my name”. I think everyone who hears “namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva” can recite it. If you don't succeed in practicing the two types of contemplation, you should recite “namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”, shouldn't you recite it? If you recite for a long time, your karma will disappear. Practice two types of contemplation. Once you study, you will succeed!

Why? That person is called learning to listen to my name, and can also learn to listen to the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions. Learning to listen to my name is to listen to the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions. Ksitigarbha is the Buddhas of the ten directions; The Buddhas of the ten directions are Ksitigarbha. We practice the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. Currently, there are many people who criticize us for not studying Mahayana teachings, but studying Hinayana dharma. Everyone has heard [like that], but after studying [this sutra] you immediately know, is this the Hinayana dharma or not? This sutra has teachings exactly the same as the Avatamsaka Sutra's teachings, exactly the same as the Lotus Sutra's teachings, equal; However, speaking is very shallow. Even very superficial seems to be guessing hexagrams, or fortune telling. These are all skillful means of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, to help us reach one mind. Although it is learning to listen to my name, it is also learning the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, which is called "learning to worship and make offerings to me". What is learning by reciting my name? Study with heart. Learning to listen to my name, reciting my name is making offerings to me. There is no need to make offerings anymore, just recite “nam-mo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva” then you take refuge in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, nam-mo is the refuge.

You can also learn to wholeheartedly worship and make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Making offerings and worshiping me is making offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. “The name of learning the profound Mahayana scriptures”: Just reciting the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is to study the profound scriptures of the Mahayana. Also known as “learning to accept, copy, make offerings to, and revere the profound Mahayana Sutras”: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us and tells us to recite the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. You make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, you also learn to listen to the profound Mahayana sutras, you also learn to accept, copy, make offerings, and revere the Mahayana sutras, it is called learning to receive, uphold, read and recite Mahayana sutras, it is called learning to stay away from wrong views, to be very deep in the righteous cause without falling into slander, it is called to learn to believe in and understand the ultimate and ultimate First True Meaning, it is called to be able to eliminate evil obstacles, it is called to gain immeasurable amounts of merit. That person who sacrifices his life, that is, the person who recites my name, when the Sambhogakaya has ended, will not fall into the evil realms or the eight misfortunes. After death, one does not fall into the three evil realms, nor does one fall into the eight misfortunes. You can also listen to the Dharma, practice faith and practice, and depending on your wish, you can be reborn in pure Buddha lands in other directions. By reciting the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, according to your wish, you can be born in any pure Buddha land. Not only the Western Pure Land world, but countless pure Buddha lands in the ten directions, you recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will take you there, but you must single-mindedly recite the name, and must also recite with one mind.

When pronouncing the name, observe the Dharmakaya of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Dharma Bodies are the same, don't be false and attached. Must be weary of attachments! Otherwise, how can you hear the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? All friends present should be happy, it is not easy to hear the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! You can hear the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and all disasters will disappear. If you have any difficulties or problems, don't practice other methods, just chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and that's it! This passage teaches us like that, said by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva himself. It was not said by any Buddha, but by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva himself. But reciting my name is not easy, you still have to learn it well, that is, learn the name Ksitigarbha well. Chanting the name Ksitigarbha can remove all obstacles, all obstacles will disappear.

(Sutra) Restore the minor, weak human desire to be born in other places in the present pure country, accept the name of the Buddha in the world chanting single-mindedly, single-mindedly, without distractions. Like a contemplative person, determined to attain rebirth in the Buddha's pure land, his good roots will grow, and he will never retreat.
(Sutra: Furthermore, if anyone wants to be born in pure realms in other directions in the present Now, you should follow the Buddha's name in that world, concentrate on reciting, with one mind without disturbance. Contemplate as above, and you will definitely be born in that pure Buddha land, your good roots will grow, and you will quickly achieve non-regression).

Furthermore, “weak human desires give birth to other places in the present false pure kingdom” (if there are people who want to be born in a pure realm in another direction in the present): There are people who want to be born in another pure Buddha realm in the ten directions in the present, then you should recite the name of the Buddha in that world. That is to say separately: If you want to be born in a pure Buddha land in another direction, whatever the holy name of the Buddha in that world is, you should concentrate on chanting [the name of] that Buddha, with one mind without disturbance, the Buddha that is recited will lead you. Contemplating as above, you will definitely be born in that pure Buddha land, grow good roots, and quickly achieve non-regression. Good roots grow very quickly, certainly will not decline.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is afraid that we will worry, afraid that we won't be able to believe, that faith won't arise, and once again tells us to "certainly not retreat". If a person who wishes to be born in the Pure Land wants to be born in a pure land in another direction in the present, or a person who wishes to be born in a pure Buddha land in another direction in the present time, all Buddha lands, the Western world of Ultimate Bliss, the Eastern world of Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli, the upper world of Real Estate, are all pure Buddha lands. According to the name of the Buddha in that world, concentrate on chanting, single-mindedly without distractions, observe as above, you will definitely be born in a pure Buddha land, absolutely be born in that pure Buddha land, good roots will grow, quickly attain non-regression, decide to grow good roots, you will definitely be able to be reborn.

(Sutra) When knowing as the highest mind, the mindset of the Buddhas is equal to the Dharmakaya, necessarily good roots in the middle of dark karma win. For those who need to practice, they often turn to Nhat Hanh samadhi. The unique disadvantage of Nhat Hanh samadhi is that he achieves a vast and wonderful mind and attains fame similar to the Dharma of Non-Birth forbearance.
(Sutra: You should know with one mind the egalitarian Dharmakaya thinking system of the Buddhas As above, that karma is the most superior of all good roots. That is called diligent practice, and can gradually lead to Nhat Hanh samadhi. If you reach Nhat Hanh samadhi, you will achieve the vast and wonderful conduct of mind, which is called attainment similar to the Non-Birth Dharma of Forbearance.

You should know, single-mindedly devote yourself to thinking about the Dharmakaya's equality

Buddhas as above, have a request, that is, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva requires us: If you want to be born somewhere, recite the Buddha's equal Dharma Body. That dharma body is inherently equal, the person who seeks birth and the body of the Buddha in the Pure Land that we hope to be born in are worlds and regions apart. Dharmakaya is equality, no two, no difference. Among all the karma of practice, in the accumulation of all good roots, the method of reciting the Buddha's name is the most superior. If you wish to be reborn in the Pure Land, recite Amitābha Buddha. There are people who want to work in medicine, hoping to cure other people's illnesses. Then you should recite Medicine Master Lapis la Light Tathagata. That is the world of Luu Ly, also a pure realm, also sublime. But you must be single-minded and undisturbed, and you must also observe that Buddha land, and you will definitely be able to be born again.

We recite Ksitigarbha Sutra, or recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, if you want to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, or if you want to be born in the world of Medicine Master Lapis la Light Buddha, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will take you there. In the previous sutra passage, it was said “pure Buddha lands of the ten directions”, whichever land you want to be born in, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can take you there. Why? The Dharmakaya is identical. Your Dharma Body and the Dharma Bodies of the Buddhas are equal, but because you have a distinction, you must concentrate on mindfulness and hope to be born in that Buddha land. You must recite the Buddha's name, day and night, with one mind without leaving, with one mind without disturbance, with every thought hoping to be reborn. That is called “one mind”. You should know: One mind system of thinking of the equal Dharmakaya of the Buddhas as above. That is what Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: You must attain one mind, focusing on the one mind system of mindfulness. In each thought, you have three minds, two thoughts, the mind does not recite, the mouth recites Amitābha Buddha, but the mind thinks of the Sa Ba world. One moment I think of Taichung, the next moment I think of Kaohsiung, I'm in trouble, I can't go, I can't get anywhere. You are still in Taiwan. Maintain a single mind with no distracting thoughts, it is very difficult to do this!

Contemplating the equal Dharmakaya of the Buddhas, this visualization is rarely practiced by many Dharma friends. The mouth chants Amitābha Buddha, but does not visualize Amitābha Buddha. It is not enough to recite it with your mouth, you have to contemplate it in your mind. Contemplation is not a thought, contemplation is a thought, a thought, in the mind the Dharmakaya is equal. While we recite Amitābha Buddha, many of our Dharma friends recite Amitābha Buddha, but very few people think "I, Buddha, and Amitābha Buddha are equal", there is no such idea. [Again, mistaken thinking]: "If we are equal, why would we still be born there? It's okay to be here!" That's not what it means! Reciting Buddha's physical body and reciting Buddha's Dharma body are different. Do you understand this principle clearly?

Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva specifically points out the Buddha's system of reciting the Dharmakaya of equality. Karma is the most superior of all good roots, only the method of reciting the Buddha's name is the most superior. If you practice diligently, that is called Nhat Hanh samadhi. The method of reciting the Buddha's name as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has said is Nhat Hanh samadhi. The person who practices this samadhi achieves a vast and wonderful mind, which is called “virtue of the mind”, which is called similar to the Dharma of Non-Birth forbearance.

tieu_de: Lecture 14: Contemplation of the One Reality Realm (Nhất Thực Cảnh Giới Quán)
tom_tat: Volume 14 (Sutra) Dien capable of attaining the teachings and names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, capable of attaining the teachings of the Buddhas of the ten directions, capable of attaining profound Mahayana sutras and offerings, capable of holding and holding...
noi_dung:
Lecture 14

(Sutra) It is possible to attain the teachings of the self, the name of the Buddha, the ability to attain the Buddha's name of the ten directions, the ability to pay heartfelt homage He worships, makes offerings to, and worships with all his heart, makes offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, and is able to attain the Mahayana profound sutras. He is able to accept, write, describe, and revere the Mahayana profound sutras. He is able to accept and uphold the profound Mahayana sutras. He is able to save and even deeply understand the First True Meaning. He is not afraid of being displeased. He is far from slander. He is able to attain the right view of the mind. He is able to confidently resolve the troubles. He is determined to eliminate all impeding sins. He can realize immeasurable merit and virtue. tried.
(Sutra: Because you can hear my name, you can also hear the name of Buddhas of the ten directions. Because you can wholeheartedly worship, worship, and make offerings to me, you can also wholeheartedly worship, worship, and make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Because you can listen to the profound Mahayana sutras, because you can accept, copy, make offerings to, and revere the profound Mahayana sutras, because you can receive and recite the profound Mahayana sutras, because you can have no fear of the very profound First True Meaning, then stay away from slander and attain the right mind. Because you can believe in understanding and decide to eliminate evil obstacles, you will attain immeasurable amounts of merit in the present.

This passage is intended to explain the meaning: When we recite the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we recite the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions. If you can wholeheartedly revere Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, in front of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's statue, you can also make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Because of that cause and effect, making offerings is like hearing Mahayana sutras, copying them, reciting them, and even using all the offerings to make offerings to all Mahayana sutras. For all your minds, all your actions, as long as you recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, it is no different from reading and reciting Mahayana sutras, equivalent to reciting the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, the merits are all equal. This passage gives us a profound explanation: Using our present body and mind to visualize, that is Transformation. Transformation depends on the Leopard, Leopard depends on the Dharmakaya. The Dharma Bodies of all sentient beings and the Dharma Bodies of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are equal. That is called One Mind Three Contemplations, the Avatamsaka Sutra refers to One Mind Three Contemplations. At the same time, we talk about samadhi, that is Nhat Hanh samadhi. If when we attain Prajnaparamita, practice Ban Chau samadhi, Ban Chau samadhi is Nhat Hanh samadhi. We hear the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we hear the names of all the Buddhas of the ten directions as equal. That is “full meaning”.

Therefore, this last passage of the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is purely the meaning in the Vien Giao. Because you listened to the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, you understood the full meaning. “Understanding” means that every thought is perfect. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You can take refuge with all your heart, even with your heart to pay homage, even with your heart to chant the name; These are all “complete meaning, complete writing, complete reflection, complete practice”, this practice of Contemplation of Hanh is called Nhat Hanh samadhi. The Sutra teaches Nhat Hanh samadhi very deeply; Here, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us a method called “complete writing, complete reflection, complete practice” to be able to reach Nhat Hanh samadhi. Practicing one dharma is [practicing] all dharmas. Samadhi in the common sense is Concentration, Concentration complete with Hue, that is, Concentration and Hue total maintenance. The general abbot of Dinh Hue is called Nhat Hanh samadhi. Therefore, you reciting one sutra is reciting all sutras, reciting the name of a Bodhisattva is reciting the names of all Buddhas. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: While you recite my name, you must visualize and visualize “hearing my name is hearing the names of all the Buddhas of the ten directions”. That is the meaning of “all-pervading”. Sincerely making offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva means making offerings to all the Buddhas of the ten directions. That's talking about Buddha.

Next is about France. Being able to receive, uphold, read and recite the profound Mahayana scriptures, one can not have fear of the ultimate First True Meaning being too deep. There are sentient beings who hear the profound meaning of the Mahayana dharma and hear that way of speaking, and will not dare to undertake it. In the Lotus Sutra, Bodhisattva Never Disparaging saw all sentient beings. He bowed and said "You are future Buddhas, I do not dare to disrespect you". The sentient beings did not accept him, used stones to hit him, scolded him and said slanderous words. Actually, the meaning [of that praise] is the deep meaning in Vien Giao. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's teachings here also have the same meaning! You hear one dharma that is all dharmas. Now we hear that the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra is a profound Mahayana sutra. If you can receive, uphold, read and recite the profound Mahayana sutras, can hear the profound and ultimate First True Meaning without giving rise to fear, listen to this type of sutra meaning (the meaning in the sutra) without giving rise to a feeling of fear, nor give rise to strange (especially strange) thoughts, stay away from slander, and attain the mind of right view, then that is called "right knowledge, right view". If it weren't like that, it wouldn't be right knowledge and right view. That's how we know "Mind, Buddha are equal; all dharmas are equal".

Currently, this passage talks about the position of Faith and Understanding, which is not practice, nor is it attainment, just being able to clearly understand, understand, believe, that is, to believe in yourself and the Buddhas as not two, not different, to believe in all the Mahayana sutras, not two, not different, to believe in the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma and all other sutras. Mahayana scriptures are not two, no different. But to be able to have such faith and understanding, if you are not a person with good roots, you will not be able to believe it! We can believe and believe in the Sutra of Contemplating Good and Evil Karma, then your mind is called right view, right understanding and right view. If you don't have a heart of faith, right knowledge, right view, you won't believe in the Sutra of Contemplating Good and Evil Karma, you won't be able to believe it!

At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also told us: Surely all sin obstacles can be destroyed, all your evil obstacles can be eliminated. All of these powers are born from your belief and understanding, your steadfast faith without doubt. Listening to the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, you can recite and recite, you can study, the merit is immeasurable, the “incarnation” (present body) can attain immeasurable merit. “Embodiment” is your body that is listening to the Dharma at the present time, and can gain countless amounts of merit, not just one or two merits, but countless merits, all of them gathered together. Therefore, when listening to the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, there is no doubt, no second thoughts, and profound belief in the Dharma taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

(Sutra) Why is it fake? The non-discriminating Bodhi mind, calm and clear mind, initiates the means of karma and vows to strive for good deeds. Inthe writer of the self, the person who has achieved the determination of faith in the benefits of the practice, the one who has the will to be able to attain it, attains the stage of non-regression of the One Vehicle of Cause and Effect.
(Sutra: Why is that? That is, because the Bodhi mind does not discriminate, wisdom is calm, giving rise to This kind of vow belongs to the expedient karma. To be able to hear my name is to gain decisive faith and beneficial conduct, until all those who can [hear and then believe], will not withdraw from the cause of the One Vehicle).

Why does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teach us like that? “The reason why it's fake?” Implication: For what reason do we say that? I say that because I am talking about Bodhi mind without distinction. That is the profound meaning of Mahayana Bodhi mind. There is no distinction, depending on the true mind, relying on the non-discriminating mind to generate Bodhi mind. That is the dual-function Chi Quan, calm wisdom then appears. Tranquility is Samadhi, wisdom is Hue, Concentration and Hue are balanced, Samadhi is dual practice. Because I say so, it is skillful means, allowing all sentient beings to develop the career of skillful means. You practice that karma, based on that karma to develop your mind, in order to generate faith and understanding. Because once you have faith and understanding, you can raise your vows. If you don't believe, you won't be able to understand, so how can you vow to practice? Relying on the power of understanding, you then vow to practice. Because you believe in it and vow to practice, you can hear my name. Speaking superficially, [here] Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells sentient beings of the Dharma-Ending Age in the future: "Hearing my name is not easy!" If you can hear my name, it is because you have had all kinds of faith and vows and have cultivated good roots in your previous life, and have had decisive faith, so in this life you can hear my name. That's not self-praise. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, for the benefit of sentient beings in the Dharma-Ending Age, said: "You should not feel contemptuous because of hearing my name." Don't! Because you will not gain any benefit. Don't be careless and arrogant! You can hear the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva not easily, it is not because of good roots in one or two lifetimes.

Why explain like that? Decided by trust and benefits. Hearing His name, you are born with faith. It is very difficult to cultivate the benefits of that faith. "If one has the right will, one must attain the cause of non-regression of the One Vehicle" (Until all who can [hear and believe], attain the cause of non-regression in the One Vehicle): Hearing my name arises, reciting the name is the same, worshiping it is the same, cultivating repentance, cultivating Nhat Hanh's contemplation, are all the causes of non-regression of the Mahayana, are the causes of the One Vehicle. The meaning here is “Bodhicitta has no distinction”. We often say “develop Bodhi mind”, to develop Bodhi mind, you must also have a discriminating mind to develop. When developing Bodhi mind like that, there is no discrimination, that is, you can believe in the realm of One Truth, you can believe in understanding the realm of One Truth, without needing to rely on the discriminating mind. If you have a discriminating mind, you will not be able to trust, and trust will not easily arise!

Furthermore, this passage talks about “quietly present wisdom”. If the mind is calm and present, you will believe in the mysterious Xa Ma Tha Chi Contemplation. In the previous text, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva mentioned the meaning of Samādhi, but you absolutely cannot enter, you cannot enter immediately. If you generate all kinds of vows and skillful means to practice and believe in this type of Bodhi contemplation, you will definitely gain benefits. Because if someone in the past did not have the power to believe and understand, but wished to hear the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, he would not be able to, not hear his name! Listening to the title also has some differences, the text below also explains more.

(Sutra) Weakness and confusion in the mind, but despite the self-proclaimed name, children are not named and written, unable to be born Decide to believe and understand, reap the world's good rewards, and gain immense and profound benefits.
(Sutra: If the mind is disordered and impure, even though one proclaims my name, one is not called Listening, due to not being able to generate faith and resolve, one can only gain good rewards in the world, not achieve vast, profound and mysterious benefits).

If the mind is confused and troubled, even if it hears my name, it cannot be called Listening; that's the distinction. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us: If you use a confused, scattered, arrogant mind, use a contaminated mind, even though you chant my name every day, it cannot be called Hearing. In this passage, He warns us: Although it is not easy to hear the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, when you hear it, you should not use a confused, contaminated mind to listen. Why? With a confused and contaminated mind, you will not be able to believe it. Your belief will be superficial. You cannot believe deeply that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can really save us, can really make us leave suffering and be happy, and cannot give rise to that mind. You cannot generate faith and decision, you cannot generate faith and decision. Even though you hear the name Ksitigarbha, it's like you don't hear it, it's like you don't see it! So is there merit or not? Yes! It is not the merit to cultivate and attain enlightenment, but the merit of the world, [but still helps] you to definitely leave the three paths.

Even though the mind is confused and bothered by hearing my name, it cannot achieve pure faith, but it is possible to achieve good rewards in the world. Achieving enlightenment is not easy, but worldly retribution can be achieved. It's just that we can't achieve profound, mysterious benefits, and we can't become saints! If the good roots are deep and thick, as soon as he hears the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, his hair will tremble, he can gain profound and great benefits, he can use that to cultivate the path, he can cut the Ordeal, and he can realize the truth. Due to a disordered and contaminated mind, one can also achieve blessings in heaven and earth, but one cannot achieve good karma in the world.

(Sutra) If the mind is confused in the world, cultivating all good things at any time will not be able to gain great benefits.
(Sutra: Such a confused and polluted mind can cultivate all good deeds, will not be able to achieve great and profound benefits).

This is to teach us: When reciting the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we should not have a confused mind, we should not have a contaminated mind. Because if you use a contaminated or disordered mind to hope to achieve pure karma, you will not be able to achieve it, you can only achieve worldly benefits. If you can, as soon as you hear it, immediately believe it deeply, develop complete knowledge, and believe that you and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva are one and the same. Ksitigarbha means oneself, oneself is Ksitigarbha. These are the kind of people who are excellent people, and thanks to the power of understanding and understanding like that, they will be able to achieve great benefits. It's the same belief, what does the mind believe? To give an example: I was in Wutai Mountain, there was a person who believed in Buddha and wished his company to prosper, so he recited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. He made a fortune, invested a profitable amount of money, and went up the mountain to make offerings to the monks. I used the meaning in this passage to explain to him: That is worldly benefit, you should not do it for the sake of worldly fame and fortune, but do pure good karma in the world; that's true. The appearance of the world will change at any time, if you have it, you will lose it! Suppose we use the mind that truly accepts birth and death, the mind that wishes to become a Buddha, it will be called “pure field of karma”, and will achieve eternal non-regression. Blessings and virtues in the world can be gained and lost. Good karma and merits beyond the world cannot be lost. That's called a profound, great benefit!

(Sutra) Good man! If you understand like this, you need to concentrate on cultivating the Formless Zen, without any ability to gain great benefits, and gradually become a Buddha.
(Sutra: Good man! You should know your mind and diligently practice Formless Zen as above, it won't take long. Afterwards, you will be able to gain great and profound benefits, and gradually you will become a Buddha.

What profound and great benefits can be achieved? Gradually becoming Buddha.

(Sutra) With profound benefits, the position of attaining the Dharma seat of Solid Faith and achieving Faith and Patience. Enter the position of Persistence and achieve Consistency and Patience. Entering the True Truth, achieving No Birth and Endurance.
(Sutra: “Great and profound benefit” means entering the Dharma with steadfast belief, due to achievements Faith in Forbearance. Enter the state of solid practice, due to the achievement of Perfect Forbearance.

In the previous paragraph, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said: If you can hear my name and have faith and understanding, you will certainly be able to gradually become a Buddha. At the same time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva answered [the meaning of] “great benefit” (profound, great benefit). What is the profound benefit? Participating in the position of Firm Faith, [the scriptures call this position] is “the position of firm belief in the Dharma”. That is the position of Patience, the achievement of Faith and Forbearance, the ability to “bear the ability” to believe in one's own faith. “Forbearance” is “admit”. “Forbearance” means to believe in yourself. One's own faith can be steadfast, without doubt, depending on the dharma nature, depending on one's own mind and body, so one can attain enlightenment. Entering the position of Righteousness, achieving Non-Birth Dharma Forbearance. That is called the Kien Tin position. According to your development of mind, the state of Firm Faith is the steadfast belief that you can definitely become a Buddha. You firmly believe that you can become a Buddha and do Buddhist work. Having that faith in mind, coming to seek the Dharma, either chanting sutras, or worshiping the Buddha, will gradually be able to achieve Dharma Forbearance, accept the Dharma, and then be able to become a Buddha. Only then can one develop steadfast and pure faith to practice. Our entire practice is like a feather in the wind, three days of practice, two days of wobbling, not practicing at all, sometimes advancing, sometimes retreating, unable to be steadfast. You must always be steadfast, practicing is very difficult! For example, when you first begin to develop your mind, tell me to recite one hundred verses of Amitābha Buddha's holy name every day. It's not much, just recite a hundred sentences, it takes less than ten minutes, and it's done after a few minutes. But you can recite every day on time and diligently without missing a single day. This is not easy! A temporary mind is easy to develop, but a long-term mind will be difficult. In general, there will be many obstacles that will prevent you from practicing.

Dharma friends, please think for a moment, since you started believing in Buddha, “take refuge in Buddha, take refuge in Dharma, take refuge in Sangha”, it's that simple! You can wake up every morning, your first thought is “take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha”, then you can do other things. Each of the four Dharma friends, whether they are monks, nuns, or lay disciples who believe in Buddha, if in three hundred and sixty days, you do not interrupt a single day, set the time, set the number, one hundred sentences, is not much, right? You sit down and recite for a few minutes, the amount is not large, but you can for a whole year, diligently, without missing a single day. No matter what obstacles, even during illness, suffering will not stop. No matter how little or how much you know, you can persevere every day without interruption. This is not easy! That is steadfast faith, without doubt! Normally, when we practice, we develop a strong mind that easily develops. Today, develop a strong mind and be very diligent and practice; Tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, we will gradually stop doing it! One month, two months, the third month, no more work! Every Dharma friend, please remember, persevere in one practice, but it is not a large amount, think about it: Every day without interruption, no matter what obstacles, this is very difficult! If you can be confident like that, you will enter the throne. The word Nhan means “promoting achievement”. Forbearance, admitting all adds the word Forbearance. That is to participate in the position of Kien Tu, through perseverance to achieve Patience. Speaking according to the dharma noun, it is No Birth Forbearance. Bodhisattvas belonging to the positions of the Ten Faiths who have just participated in the position of Faith are called Faith-Forbearance, until the Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, and Ten Dedications are called Thuan-Forbearance, due to following the dharma nature. The Bodhisattva's Enlightenment (who has attained the First Level or higher) is called Non-Birth Dharma Forbearance. Practicing the same way, with proper effort, is the Non-Sanh Dharma Forbearance. If you haven't reached it yet, it's up to you (Thuan Nhan). Now we grow, practice and nurture, make the good roots become more and more solid, bigger and bigger, nurture it.

(Sutra) Huu achieves Faith and Ninja, capable of creating Tathagata's inherent nature. Accomplished Thuan Nhan practitioner, able to understand the Tathagata's faults. Achieving the Unborn Ninja, attaining Tathagata's karma.
(Sutra: Again achieving Faith and Forbearance, because it can be the seed of the Tathagata. Achievement of Thuan Patience, due to being able to understand Tathagata's conduct. Achieving Non-Birth Patience, due to achieving Tathagata's karma).

Do we achieve Faith and Forbearance? If we believe, each of our Dharma friends says they believe in the Three Jewels, then will we reach the Faith or not? Sometimes I believe, sometimes I don't believe. A lot of time to believe, a little time to not believe; That's having a little morality. Never lost faith before, never had a thought to lose faith; That is called “entering the position of Faith”, [that is] entering the position of Faith and Forbearance. Faith in Patience is the achievement of faith, participating in the position of the First Pillar in the Ten Pillars, belonging to the Tathagata's race, but it is only similar, that is, similar to the Tathagata's race. Until the completion of the thirty minds, that is, the completion of the thirty minds belonging to the positions of the Ten Pillars, the Ten Virtues, and the Ten Dedications, participating in the First Ground, will not be similar, but will truly enter the Buddha nature, determined to be able to become a Buddha. Why? Only then will one's actions be incomparable, indistinguishable from the Buddha. The Bodhisattva's actions are unique, no different from Buddha. Each position must cut off ignorance and attain Dharmakaya. The Three Noble Bodhisattvas (Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications) are called Similar, belonging to the same position, similar entry; Actually, not really entered yet. A Bodhisattva's faith can still retreat, but a Bodhisattva's abode does not retreat. The status of the Ten Believers and ordinary people cannot yet be considered saints. As for us, we have not yet entered the position of Faith, we have not yet reached perfection, faith is progressing and retreating, not giving rise to decisive confidence. Deciding to believe means you have entered the First Pillar and will no longer change.

Therefore, speaking according to the teachings and teachings in the sutras, using the Holy Doctrine to measure yourself, you will know to what extent you truly believe in Buddha and practice. Only you will know for yourself. That belongs to the aspect of Action. With faith like that, only then can we never retreat, believe that we are not two, that we are no different from Buddha, believe that we have Buddha Nature, and we can definitely become Buddha. That's called "having faith". Like ordinary Dharma friends, who have entered Buddhism and received the Three Refuges and Five Precepts, they absolutely do not think they can become Buddhas, nor do they have such high expectations! In fact, you have just entered Buddhism and received the Three Refuges, then you call yourself “Buddhist”, [considered] to have entered Buddhism. Buddhists must practice Buddhism. You have received the Three Refuges, but still do not see the practice of Buddhism, you keep moving forward and backward. Why must we practice for countless lifetimes? The reason is right here, keep moving forward and backward. In this life you are diligent and brave, what about in the next life? Therefore, the Buddha taught us the method of skillful means, taught us to recite Amitābha Buddha's name, and be born in the Pure Land. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us to recite the holy name Ksitigarbha. This sutra teaches us that we should all use name as the main thing. He taught us to chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva blesses you, and can [bless] you forever until you become a Buddha. You can gradually become a Buddha, not immediately, so your faith must be solid and unwavering.

Fellow friends, please take a look at yourself: "No matter how many accidents you encounter, your faith will never retreat." The meaning in that is extremely profound. I was in prison, there were a lot of Dharma friends, a lot of people became monks. At that time, there were many people who were resentful, what resentment? The Buddha does not bless them, nor does the dharma-protecting god bless them! It's not that they don't protect you, it's that you yourself don't accept the protection, your spiritual mind recedes, you don't believe. Therefore, if you believe, even if you encounter accidents or misfortunes, it is absolutely not the case that "if you believe in Buddha, all misfortunes will be gone", it cannot be! We often say "If you can't be examined by demons, you can't become a Buddha". That is also a test for your spiritual practice. The more demons, the more obstacles. On your path to practice, there are obstacles everywhere! Why? There should be no obstacles in cultivating the path, right? In the past, I gave the following example: In the past, there was a very evil person, no one dared to touch him. He lacks money, and [the creditor] doesn't dare to ask for it. But if that person changes and wants to make things right, they will dare to claim you. At that time, you must pay! It seems that when we have not yet developed our mind and have not yet cultivated the Way, the obstacles are still a little less, and still quite favorable. As soon as that person believes in the Three Jewels, difficulties come, karmic obstacles come, illness suddenly comes, and all the causes and conditions that hinder the path come. That is your elaborate test. Because before, you wore the guise of "evil person", and were still doing evil, and people did not dare to touch you. Now that you have done good deeds, you should repay the old debt. Therefore, the four disciples must realize and realize what? Disaster! Your attainment of enlightenment is not a convenient matter; That's called practicing to test whether your faith is steadfast or not. The more you grind, the more steadfast you become, the more you grind, the brighter it becomes, that's called “steadfastness”. Faith is not strong, whenever challenged, one becomes discouraged and one's moral heart recedes. Especially when there is an accident, the country is in an accident, our entire Buddhist community is in an accident. It's not just words, it's what the body endures, it's the actions that test whether our faith is solid or not? Is it possible to follow Buddha's teachings? That is called Faith Forbearance, which means solid faith. Without solidity, is it possible to follow Tathagata's teachings?

(Sutra) The second shop of false Buddhas, the theory of existence and four species. Ha level vi four? One who fully believes in the Buddha's teachings. Based on the nature and nature of the land, he decided to believe that all dharmas are unborn, immortal, pure, equal, and impossible to pray for. Second, the solution is complete according to the Buddha's work. So the physician solves the ground of conduct, deepens the nature of solution, understands the Tathagata's karma, non-creation, non-action, birth and death, Nirvana, no dual thoughts arise, the mind has no preoccupations. The three falsehoods, attaining the fulfillment of the Buddha's dharma. So because of the pure ground of the mind, one can attain the wisdom of non-discrimination, tranquil dharma, without thinking about the natural karma, without seeking thoughts or thoughts. The four beings must have merit, virtue, and complete Buddha's writings. The Bodhisattva's ultimate robe is able to eliminate all the obstacles of ignorance and endless dreams.
(Sutra: Gradually becoming a Buddha, in general there are four types. What are the four? One is through faith. To become a Buddha is to rely on the ground of nature, to decide to believe in all dharmas that are unborn, immortal, pure and equal, and have nothing to pray for. Second, to fulfill the dharma, to become a Buddha, that is, to rely on the liberation of the ground to deeply understand the nature of the dharma, to know that the Tathagata's karma does not create or do anything, to have no thoughts about birth and death and Nirvana, the mind is not afraid ground, due to attaining the peaceful wisdom of dharma without distinction and natural karma, without thinking about it, without any thoughts of desire. Fourth, because of all the full merit and virtue, one can become a Buddha, that is, depending on the ultimate Bodhisattva ground, one can eliminate all obstacles and dreams of ignorance.

That said, there are four general types of faith. What are four?

1) One is that because of complete faith in the Dharma (belief in the Dharma's perfection), one becomes a Buddha, that is, depending on the ground nature, one decides to believe and understand. Faith explains what? Unborn, immortal. What is the explanation? Equality and purity. Buddhas and sentient beings, along with one thought of one's own present mind, three things combine, that is "mind, Buddha, sentient beings, all three are equal". We must develop a perfect mind, a Mahayana mind, to develop Mahayana meaning, there is nothing to pray for. That is the meaning of complete dharma. “Complete dharma” means “complete dharma” (complete dharma). What does “Dharma satisfaction” mean? It is the realm of One True perfection, with no dharma to distinguish, it is called “fulfillment of dharma”. By fulfilling the dharma, becoming a Buddha is precisely this meaning. Because everyone believes in the complete Dharma, they become Buddhas, but “Believing in the complete Dharma becomes Buddha” that means your nature is Buddha. Each person's nature and the Buddha's nature are not two or different. Also believe that all dharmas are unborn and undying. We cannot easily believe this! It is very difficult to have that faith. Even if you believe it, it's not solid. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: “That dharma without distinction is called the realm of One Truth”. You believe that all dharmas are unborn, immortal, pure, equal, not defiled, not clean, not increasing, not decreasing. That is what belongs to Faith. Can you trust it or not? There is no thought of doubt, always believing "I and the Buddha are not two, no different", [as well as] no two, no different from the great Bodhisattvas.

2) Second, by fulfilling the Dharma, one becomes a Buddha. The previous paragraph is about fully believing in the dharma of becoming a Buddha, and here it is explaining the dharma of becoming a Buddha, going even deeper. Explaining, not only believing, but also relying on the teachings taught by the Buddha to understand more deeply. “Dharma” here refers to the nature of dharma: The nature of all dharmas is radiant; The nature of all dharmas is not two or different. All sentient beings have to practice for many eons to become Buddhas. Only then will they realize that there is no creation and no practice. Becoming a Buddha is not about not cultivating successfully, it is about eliminating one's karma. Explaining this is very difficult, there is no difference between birth and death and Nirvana, such faith must arise. Because after having such faith, during the process of cultivating to become a Buddha, there will not be any feeling of fear, knowing that everything is fake. In the original nature there are no [those things], so it is said to be fake.

3) [Thirdly, because of achieving Dharma fulfillment, one becomes a Buddha], all Buddhas have proven to us, proving that everything is fake, nothing is true! Except for the essence of self-nature, everything is an illusion, all "images" (shadows of green objects reflected in the mind).

4) Fourth, because of the perfection of all merit and virtue, one becomes a Buddha, that is, relying on the ultimate Bodhisattva stage, one can eliminate all obstacles and end the dream of ignorance. We are dreaming, ignorance is the most basic thing. Due to ignorance, three sacrificial signs arise. The Abhidharma of Faith distinguishes [“three manifestations”] as the appearance of karma, transformation, and appearance, those three appearances. The three sacrificial signs are all manifestations of ignorance. If you can cut off the three sacrificial signs, you will attain the Eighth Bodhisattva Grounds. The Eight Bodhisattva Grounds can cut off appearances, the Nine Bodhisattva Grounds can cut off appearances, and the Ten Bodhisattva Grounds can cut off the appearance of karma. Therefore, this practice is very deep. Karma disappears, merit is present, all the karma created in practice, all the actions to accumulate merit are fully accomplished, and one becomes a Buddha. Becoming a Buddha is the ultimate attainment of Bodhisattva. The position of Bodhisattva will ultimately eliminate all obstacles and dreams of ignorance. Perfection of virtue and virtue is the disappearance of karma, restoring your inherently pure Dharma Body, having already become a Buddha.

Believing in becoming a Buddha, currently for everyone, must achieve the first belief of “becoming a Buddha”, that is, believing that you are a Buddha. To gain such faith, it takes quite a long time. Suppose someone asks me: "Are you Buddha?" I don't dare to take it on! Why? I'm afraid people will ask me to prove it in the present. [For example, they say]: "You are Buddha, should you give me some alms? Give me the arm of your body!" You don't become a Buddha because you don't dare to give it to that person. Are you willing to give it or not? Because, if you want to transform the minds of sentient beings into Buddha minds, that transformation will be quite difficult! How difficult is it? How many eons, not just a short time. We study the sutras, following the Buddha's teachings to study the sutras. We know and believe, but we do not dare to undertake them. Because right now, whenever we take charge, others will demand that we pay the real price. We really can't pay the price, so we don't dare to undertake it. Therefore, we must train the mind, what kind of training? Must take charge. Once you have taken charge, all the careers and merits you have done can be achieved. I believe that I can definitely become a Buddha. Why? Originally Buddha. If you do not have the seed of Buddha nature, do not have that seed, are not a Buddha, no matter what you do, you still cannot become a Buddha! You want to turn potatoes into rice, but you can't, the seeds are different! Or turn white cabbage into flour, different seeds, completely different! [Because living beings and Buddhas] have the same nature, [living beings] can absolutely become Buddhas.

All sentient beings are Buddhas, one is available, the other is cultivated. Buddhas are manifest, that is, they show what is available (Buddha Nature). The inherent nature of all sentient beings is plagued by afflictions, ignorance and all kinds of obstacles. They must be eliminated in order to become a Buddha. If people are willing to use Buddhism to distinguish and study, the great master Tri Gia of Thien Thai Tong has outlined the teachings of Six Buddhas, which we will not discuss in detail, because it would take too much time. We should understand the Six Buddhas.

Nthe practice of learning the worldly form of the Zen person,the three types of existence. Ha class vi tam? One person, without the means to believe and dispel the force of effort, takes part in the merits of the Zen samadhi, causing pride and arrogance. The Zen is blessed, and he withdraws from worldly pursuits. The second person, who has no means of faith to relieve the force of effort, uses Zen to give rise to hatred and renunciation, fearing birth and death, and regressing to the Second Vehicle. The three false ones, with means of believing in the power of liberation, sin the position of y pointing to the Real Realm, focusing on FarMaTha, Bhikkhu Bà Even though the worldly Zen masters have merit, they cannot resist before and do not give up, seeking the fruit of the three realms of existence. If Huu believes in life and death, that is, Nirvana, he is not afraid, and withdraws from the pursuit of the Second Vehicle.
(Sutra: Again, you should know: If you study the worldly form of Zen, there are three types. What is Third, due to not having the strength to believe in and understanding the merits of Zen samadhi, one becomes arrogant and falls behind in the bonds of Zen. Two, due to the lack of strength and means to believe and understand, one develops a tendency to be weary of life and death, and falls into the Second Vehicle. Third, one has the strength to believe and understand the path Xa Ma Tha and Bhikkhu Bà in the three realms. Because we believe that birth and death are Nirvana, we are not afraid and decline to seek the Second Vehicle.)

Again, let's know, we need to understand this step further. What should you know? Practicing the worldly form of Zen, from the beginning, [that is] starting to practice Zen. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us again: What is it like to practice Meditation with the form of the world? What is it like to practice Meditation beyond the world? What is it like to practice Meditation and ultimately become a Buddha? First of all, let's talk about cultivating worldly Concentration. Meditation is “stillness, thinking”. Simply put, it is Dinh. In Concentration there is Hue. The Zen world is divided into three types:

1) One type is the means of believing and dissolving power, that is, the worldly Zen is also called samadhi, this word means Concentration. Worldly Concentration is due to [achieving] the merits of samadhi, that person (the person who practices worldly Concentration) becomes arrogant. Just after achieving a little purity, arrogance arose. But because he doesn't have the means to believe and understand, he becomes arrogant. If one has the power to believe and understand, one will not become arrogant. If you are arrogant, not only will you not be able to practice Zen Concentration, but you will also be bound by Zen Concentration. Bound by Meditation, it will be impossible to be freed, turning into worldly Meditation. That is just quiet, just pure, not true Concentration. Worldly Meditation can be divided into many types, [often collectively referred to as] Four Meditations, Eight Concentrations, Nine Third Concentrations. We won't go into detail because it's too long. That is worldly Meditation.

2) Second, there is no means of understanding. From the First Meditation, one develops the tendency to be bored with separation, to fear birth and death, and to decline into the Second Vehicle. This is relying on Zen to give rise to a mind of boredom. From the mind of boredom and detachment, actions of the method of boredom and detachment arise. That kind of behavior does not have the power to understand, it is not a deep belief without doubt, it does not give rise to the power of belief and understanding, it only depends on Meditation to give rise to the power of concentration. Because of the act of being tired of leaving the world, because of the fear of birth and death, the fear of birth and death, one does not dare to pray for the Mahayana, [accepting] "it is enough to leave birth and death forever". Therefore, originally hoping to practice Mahayana Concentration, but regressed to the position of Second Vehicle, [thinking] that reaching the end of birth and death was the end, and had not yet developed the Bodhi mind. But that's not forever. If you don't become a Buddha, you absolutely cannot leave forever! Although the Part of Birth and Death has been resolved, the Change of Birth and Death still exists; Nhi Thua's goods cannot explain this matter. It is necessary to develop the mind of Mahayana, to cut off the two types of birth and death. Not only must we cut off the Parts of Birth and Death, but we must also cut off the Changes of Life and Death. That is the meaning because of the Small that misunderstands the Great!

Furthermore, assuming we can rely on the realm of One Truth, the realm of One Truth mentioned in the previous section, at first creating such a mind is to rely on the realm of One Truth, the meditation practice to practice is "Dual Contemplation of Two Movements". When practicing meditation, you will definitely have the power of wisdom and the power of insight. Due to the power of contemplation, one knows that all dharmas arise from the mind, and that all dharmas do not exist. When the mind arises, all dharmas arise, they all arise from thought. Because thoughts arise, they do not really have concrete existence. Therefore, the Diamond Sutra says: “All dharmas are like dreams, like illusions, like bubbles, like images”, because their Essence is neither real nor exists! There is no true entity, it is false and illusory. This type of Meditation can only achieve small enjoyment in the world, that is, it is concentrated, not troubled, or only reduces worldly troubles, cannot put an end to birth and death, and cannot attain Nirvana.

(Sutra) If you study with all Zen samadhis, you will possess the ten forms of the first signs, If you firmly grasp the karma of Meditation, the spiritual scholar will achieve corresponding achievements, without giving up or losing. Ha class vi ten?
(Sutra: Practicing all the Samadhi Zen methods like that, you should know that there are ten types of appearances Subjects in order, including the complete karma of Meditation, can cause the student to achieve corresponding achievements, no mistakes, no mistakes. What are the ten?)

Furthermore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us that this type of Meditation has ten forms. These ten generals are all brought about by Meditation, and Meditation brings about karma. Sentient beings practice worldly Concentration in accordance with their wishes, and the Concentration they cultivate is in accordance with worldly appearances. They do not gain [benefits] beyond the world, and cannot attain birth and death. Meditation to attain birth and death must also cut off Views and Thoughts. Worldly Meditation cannot cut off Mistakes. Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that sentient beings who want to practice and learn all the methods of Zen samadhi, should know that there are ten types of signs in order. Practicing Concentration has worldly Concentration and worldly Concentration, there is the Samadhi of Concentration with super direct entry, or practicing formless Meditation. Worldly Meditation is Meditation with forms, but in this type of Meditation there are ten types of forms, achieving the career of Meditation, achieving the effects of Meditation.

Practise and study all Samadhi Zen methods like that, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that if you study all Meditation, practice the Meditation method, you should know, you should understand, knowing that there is an order, you should understand clearly. How many types are there in order? Ten types. These ten types all receive the karma of Zen practice. Depending on which type of practice you choose, it will correspond to that type, there will be no mistakes or confusion. That is, in general, one must leave worldly appearances to practice formless Meditation, or rely on worldly appearances to practice formless Meditation. Formless Meditation and Formless Meditation is roughly divided into ten types of generals, that is, for Chi in "Dhammapada Samadhi", there are ten generals practicing Samadhi. “Just” is Meditation, Meditation is simply said to be Samadhi. If you do not practice according to the regulations of those ten subjects, Zen in the world cannot be achieved, and Zen in the world cannot be achieved! What do those ten types of subjects mean? Below will explain the names and appearances of those ten types of meditation practice. First Zen in the world is not easy to achieve.

We often lack Concentration, and our mind cannot decide anything. Because you cannot decide, you will make a wrong judgment: Is this right or wrong? What is the right way to achieve success? Because you are not concentrated, the wisdom mind, that is, the wisdom mind cannot arise. Wisdom is discernment and understanding. You can't decide whether you take it or leave it, because you don't have the power to concentrate. Like we do one thing, can that thing be done or not? There are people who come to you to cooperate in business. You want to do it, you also want to make money, but you're afraid of losing money. What should you do? Can't decide! Then you should practice. How to practice? Practice silence.

For example, when we normally do something, someone tells you, at that time, you don't dare to make a decision, "Wait for me to think for a moment!" “Waiting for you to think” is Concentration. Once determined, wisdom will be born. Think about it from beginning to end [so you can decide] whether you should do it or not. How many parts can be done, how many parts can't be done? [Consider the possibility] that you can do six parts, then you can do it. If you can't do six parts, then decide absolutely not to do it. This is my own judgment, this is still reasonable. While we practice, just rely on your wisdom to observe. When observing, there will be skillful means. Before practicing, there will be twenty-five types of means, we will not explain them one by one. Basically, just explaining a few cases, people can look it up themselves. In general, there are ten types of [generals].

(Sutra) One person, contemplate the means of form.
(Sutra: One is the medium of photography).

To practice Meditation, you must be skillful in capturing thoughts. If you have delusions, can you practice Meditation? “Night photography” is not easy to immediately capture thoughts. Think East, think West, let's unify our ideas. How to unify? It's not that simple! Eliminate the realm of the five desires: "money, beauty, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping." If you have "talent, beauty, fame, food, drink, sleep, etc.", can you still practice? Rebuke the Five Desires, abandon the Five Things. “Wealth, beauty, fame, food, drink, and sleep are the five roots of hell”, reprimand and throw them away. Control the five things, practice the five dharmas. That is the method of Ma Ha Prajnaparamita, simple practice.

(Sutra) Two people, desire abides in the realm of form.
(Sutra: Two is the general who wants to stay in the realm).

What is “desire to abide in the realm of appearances”? In is to contemplate your mind, that mind is motionless. The mind is bound to the external world. Every mind must be conditioned by the scene, stop all realms, and only concentrate on the mind. Simply put, you stop all the thoughts in your mind from thinking and quiet it down. The mind does not cling to anything, it does not grasp any external environment, it does not even recite the Buddha's name. You are calm, hoping to practice Concentration, but reciting Buddha's name cannot concentrate. You don't think, you calm down, you practice concentration, you don't have any distracting thoughts. That is called “direct mindfulness of True Suchness”. “Truth” is true, not false. “Likeness” is like immobility, restoring your inherent mind. Every time there is a thought, it will all be an illusion. The mind is quiet and stopped like that. Every mind has mental factors, mental factors will depend on the appearance of the realm, stop all of them. The means to meditate is like that. Wishing to stay in the general realm, causing the general realm to disappear. When [the mind] wants to abide in the appearance of the realm, make it not abide in the appearance of the realm. When we practice Contemplation, there are many methods. Practicing the Book of Contemplation to count numbers, counting numbers will make you calm, that is the method. That is to teach us to be mindful of Truth. Contemplate the Dharma of True Suchness as real, not false, unmoving as it is, cessation of all dharma conditions.

(Sutra) Three falsehoods, first abiding in the realm of discernment, knowing, knowing general.

Breath contemplation, also known as Breath Contemplation. You breathe out, breathe in, one breath out, one breath in; Initially, it is clearly aware, clear, and focused on the in and out breath. That is the method to practice Concentration, the preliminary method to practice Concentration. That is not the Mahayana realm, but a skillful means, that is, a skillful means to practice Concentration. Because of that skill, your mind can stay calm, you can make your mind stay calm. That's called breathing meditation, which is a common method of cultivating Concentration. You pay attention to the "import and exit moment", that is, the breath going in and out. Observe it and you will be concentrated, and all other distracting thoughts will no longer exist. Just observe the breath going in and out, the mind stays where the breath goes in and out. After your mind has become concentrated, practice the Truthfulness of General Contemplation again. True Emptiness General Contemplation is the first step to practice Absolute Emptiness General Contemplation. In the Avatamsaka Sutra, it is mentioned that the Perfect Contemplation of True Emptiness means that all dharmas are Emptiness. That Emptiness is False Emptiness, Contemplation is the Ultimate Emptiness. That is the first contemplation in the Hoa Nghiem Three Contemplations, that is, Absolute Emptiness Contemplation. True Emptiness is the absence of all appearances. Where should you put your mind? All dharmas are Emptiness, residing in Emptiness. During the process of practice, your mind can rest in Emptiness and will gradually become concentrated. It's not that at first we can immediately focus our mind on Emptiness, you have to train first on the in and out breath, you have to understand clearly. But when you start doing it, every thought is a wrong thought, every thought is a lost thought, and you have to pull your mind back. You must clearly observe the exhalation and inhalation, wait until for any thought, the inhalation and exhalation are no longer there, and you will be concentrated. That's the method!

(Sutra) The Four Noble Ones, good in the realm, attain solid form.
(Sutra: Four is a general that skillfully stays in the realm, achieving solidity).

Consider your breathing in and out, causing all delusions to disappear. That is the meditation on breathing in and out.

(Sutra) The Five Immortals, possessing powerful means of thinking to advance the beast general.

Cultivate the Truth as it really is. There is no breath in or out, empty. After that, enter the Real General Contemplation and then the Absolutely Empty General Contemplation. In the Avatamsaka Sutra, practicing Perfect Emptiness Contemplation means that all dharmas are not established and do not exist. In the mind, no other thoughts arise, there is no thought. As your concentration increases, the wisdom in your mind increases. With the concentration that you have practiced, you can be solid. At any time, sitting still can give birth to the power of Concentration. Concentration has clear illumination. At that time, superior merit will arise that can cure afflictions. The treatment of affliction is not to eliminate it, but to treat it, that is, to subdue it. At that time, all the thoughts in your mind can produce merit and benefits. When thinking (a thought arises), there is no evil thought, nor are there all the signs of the realm, and even good things do not arise. The two paths of good and evil are quiet, corresponding to your thoughts, ideas, and mind, and are not wrong or mistaken. According to teachings, this is called the Nine Second Concentration, because you enter and leave the worldly concentration from the worldly concentration. The concentration beyond the world is very deep.

(Sutra) The ten practitioners, the weak-winged cultivators, rely on the first to attain the means, the second achieves entering and exiting according to the mind, transcendence Vietnamese freedom in appearance.
(Sutra: Ten is the form if you practice more other methods, depending on what you have achieved before to start the method convenient, in order to achieve entry and exit according to the mind, transcendence and freedom).

Therefore, if you want to practice other dharmas, rely on the power you have previously achieved, that is, the power of Concentration, to give rise to the means, in order to achieve the appearance of entering and exiting according to the mind, transcending freedom. This type of realm still belongs to the Samadhi of the human world, to the Four Meditations of the Four Formless Samadhi. Use this concept to gather all the practice of Meditation and concentration in the human world. Speaking according to the teachings, that is the power and means of Meditation arising from the First Meditation. Again practice higher like that, in order of achievement; At that time, the mind entering and exiting raises ideas, or stops thinking, that is, the mind starts to move thoughts. At that time, regarding Being and Non-existence, that is, regarding existence and non-existence, emptiness and non-emptiness, there will be no concept of distinction. The mind does not have that distinction. Only then can we take the next step and observe the mind. All breaths in and out, thoughts starting and ending, all depend on the mind to be free. The tenth type of general is “first general” (ordinary general).

(Sutra) Name of the ten types of disciples, the branch of meditation practice.
(Sutra: These are called the ten generals in order, including the practice of Meditation career).

[Speaking of] cultivating this Meditation and the effects of cultivating Meditation, whether speaking according to Mind Only Contemplation, or cultivating True True General Insight, or Meditating according to worldly appearance, or beyond-worldly Meditation, it is all step by step, from worldly Concentration to reaching beyond-worldly Concentration. That's speaking in order, not Doan Sieu. Zen Buddhism does not say in this order: Enter directly into the transcendent, contemplate directly into the mind nature, contemplate only the present mind, all dharmas only mind, and purify the mind, then all the signs of the realm will be completely destroyed. “The scene ceases, the mind becomes pure”, that type of Meditation is great concentration, it is meditation beyond this world. But Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva like this: Ordinary people initially start practicing Meditation, from the First Zen Heaven to the Second Zen Heaven, Third Zen Heaven, Fourth Zen Heaven, that is close and shallow. When King Ksitigarbha told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva, in the shallow type of Meditation, there is a very deep Meditation. Do people understand the meaning of this? What is the disagreement with human ways of practicing Zen? That Meditation is not ultimate, it is the Meditation of skillful means. Therefore, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva's doubts arose.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, keep pure faith Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asks Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat saying: “The clouds and clouds cleverly speak of profound dharma and spiritual power

are sentient beings overcome with fear and weakness?"

(Sutra: At that time, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sat Ma Ha Tat said: "Why do you speak the profound Dharma so skillfully that sentient beings are freed from fear?")

Pure Faith Bodhisattva immediately said to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: You said this dharma is not a deep dharma, you should say a very deep dharma. The sentence "The clouds and rivers cunningly explain the profound dharma, empowering sentient beings to escape fear and weakness?" Meaning: This type of worldly Meditation is not a profound dharma, I still hope that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will skillfully explain more skillful means, in order to make sentient beings separate from the idea of ​​fear and weakness. “Khi” means not daring to practice. Khiep contains the meaning of Weakness (weakness), no strength. This type of sentient being is a sentient being who wishes to practice the Mahayana. The Three Contemplations of "Emptiness, Falsehood, and Middle" are determined by the four teachings [in the Tiantai sect], while the Avatamsaka Sutra is the Contemplation of Absolute Emptiness, the Contemplation of Unobstructed Reasons, and the Contemplation of Continuity and Consistency. Those types of Contemplation are Concentration, Concentration is Contemplation.

This passage carries the meaning: What skillful means must there be to enable them to practice Mahayana meditation, which can arouse very deep enlightenment. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva said: Up until now, you have been talking about worldly Meditation, which is a dharma that does not end birth and death. Hoping to overcome birth and death, attain Nirvana, practice meditation with Mahayana skillful means, meditation belongs to the realm of One Truth and wisdom is not like that. Isn't it true that Bodhisattvas always worry that sentient beings are stupid, unable to enter the Realm of One Truth, and also unable to understand, are these contemplations not contemplation practices of the Realm of One Truth? Therefore, Kien Tinh Bodhisattva invites Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to say the Contemplation of True Truth, the Contemplation of Unobstructed Reasons, and the Contemplation of Continuity and Consistency belonging to the realm of One Vehicle. Because we cannot believe in the realm of One Truth, we must rely on skillful means. Kien Tinh Bodhisattva again invited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak the Dharma very deeply, do not worry about sentient beings being frightened or weak. “Weakness” means not being able to enter the Mahayana dharma due to poor nature. This word has the meaning of inviting and encouraging Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to speak deeply of Concentration, to speak of profound wisdom. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva used skillful means to speak to Kien Tinh Bodhisattva.
