noi_dung:
Lecture 15

(Sutra) Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva's words: - Good man! When first learning to develop the intention, seeking to reach the Mahayana position of a confident person, the supreme path and profound dharma, joy gives rise to doubt and fear, the ego cunningly declares the peace of Tru Nghia Nhi, the soul is terrified and weak. Thien Thien Thien Thuyet, Thien An Commissioner. Van Ha An Commissar? Because of the ignorance of the small minds of living beings, the text is unsurpassed, the most sublime, the most wonderful, the mind is greedy, the mind is aspirational, and the thoughts are: "Praying for the unsurpassed path, it is essential to accumulate extensive merit, practice asceticism with difficulty, liberate oneself, save others, have a long life, live in the middle of life and death, endure suffering for the nine years, and attain success." When the city is exhausted, the mind becomes weak.
(Sutra: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva said: - Good man! You should know the novice If you learn to seek the Mahayana but have not yet achieved faith, you will have a deep sense of doubt and fear in the unsurpassed Dharma. I use skillful means to praise and show the true meaning to comfort them, so that they call me the Good Comforter. That is, for sentient beings with dull minds and narrow minds, I will listen to the highest, most wonderful way, and even though my mind is greedy. make a wish, but think: "To seek the highest path, one must accumulate immense virtue, practice difficult ascetic practices, save oneself and others for a long time, and endure long and hard suffering in life and death to achieve it." Because of that, their minds are terrified.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva said: Good man! You should know that beginners who set out to seek the Mahayana, but have not yet achieved confidence, are too deep in the unsurpassed path, and will be prone to doubt and fear. I will use skillful means to speak the truth. Tuyen spoke truthfully to comfort them and make them lose their fear and weakness. Therefore, I am called Thien An Commissar (one who speaks well of comfort). This passage of scripture means: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's skillful means can cause sentient beings who have no faith to develop a mind of faith. That is talking about sentient beings who do not believe in the Mahayana Dharma. Ordinary sentient beings aspire to become Buddhas, that is the Mahayana teachings. They did not dare to develop that mind, so Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva advised them to develop the mind to become Buddha, teaching them to seek and aim towards Mahayana. To them, if it is said "willow birth and death, achieve blessings in the human world", those living beings easily accept it. [Tell them] “Do good deeds, get good rewards”, they easily accept it. [If you tell them] “you should believe in Buddha, aspire to become Buddha”, [and they accept and follow], there are very few beings of this kind! There are many Dharma friends who, after believing in Buddha, I think they do not have the heart to become Buddha, almost like this passage of scripture says. We have already developed the mind to accept life and death quite well. We hope that life in the present will be comforted and that we can reduce uncaused disasters, which is already very satisfying. As for “developing the mind to become a monk”, until “developing the mind to believe in Buddha, only because we become Buddha do we develop the mind to believe in Buddha”, I have heard very few people like that. It really is! There are very few sentient beings in the Dharma Ending period who develop the mind to obey the Mahayana teachings, who develop the mind to "leave suffering and be happy", and even the mind to leave birth and death are very few! But those who are determined to gain some blessings in the human world and pray for comfort in the present life, there are quite a few of these types!

In this passage, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells the Bodhisattva of Steadfast Faith: Suppose there is a type of living being who wishes to seek the Mahayana, but faith is not enough, to the point that the person who has developed the mind to seek the Mahayana will easily retreat. Regarding this very profound Dharma meaning, they are skeptical. They see it said "all sentient beings can become Buddhas". Regarding the teachings in the sutras, one is not to believe, or two is to believe but be skeptical. To that type of living beings, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: “I use skillful means to comfort them, causing them to develop Bodhi mind”. I say this case a little more prosaically: At first you believe in Buddha, then you develop the mind to save sentient beings, that is called the Mahayana mind. If you believe in Buddha, you do not pray for peace and happiness for yourself, but for all sentient beings to be happy. That is called Mahayana mind. That is a very deep dharma. But if you've made up your mind, you doubt whether you can do it or not? I often hear Dharma friends say: "I can't even save myself, so can I still save others?" People say that a lot! Many friends have heard it. Hearing someone develop the Mahayana mind, how can we be considered to have developed the Mahayana mind? Up until now, we haven't talked about ourselves, we've only talked about how to make sentient beings hear the Buddha Dharma? How to make sentient beings leave suffering and be happy? Fellow Dharma friends can hear each other say that. Our friends believe in Buddha, not for ourselves, but only for others. Therefore, speaking according to the teachings of the Mahayana Sutra, we do not wish for peace and happiness for ourselves, we only wish for the happiness of all sentient beings. That is called the meaning “arising very deeply”. Why can't we develop such a mind? Due to fear. Think to yourself: "It is wonderful that I can put an end to life and death!" There is only the mind that seeks renunciation for oneself. Encountering those living beings who do not develop a great mind, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva skillfully comforts them, advises them to develop Bodhi mind, and advises them to practice the Bodhisattva path. That is specifically speaking to sentient beings who do not develop a great mind.

What is “Consolation”? How can we advise living beings to develop a great mind? Get rid of the small, fearful mind, get rid of the mind that only cares for yourself, and comfort them to help them develop the Mahayana mind. How to comfort? Use language to comfort. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva uttered words of comfort. Regarding sentient beings with narrow minds, that is, sentient beings who do not develop the Bodhi mind and only seek peace and happiness for themselves, it is said that the Bodhisattva method of practicing the path to Buddhahood has wonderful and sublime merits. This means: It is not enough that we ourselves can cut off greed, anger, and ignorance, but we must also cause all sentient beings to cut off greed, anger, and ignorance. Make them develop the mind, not only the mind to seek renunciation, but also the mind to move towards the Mahayana, advise all sentient beings to develop the mind to become Buddha, make the "vow to reach the Buddha vehicle, only think of the highest path". "The highest path" is specialized in talking about the Buddha Vehicle, reaching ultimate Buddhahood. But becoming a Buddha is not simply a sentence, you must be generous to all sentient beings, perfect and achieve your merits and benefits and the merits of sentient beings. This cannot be [accomplished] in a short period of time, but rather countless eons, and the time it takes to save oneself and save others can be very long. If it's just for the sake of ending birth and death for yourself, ending afflictions, until ending the End of Birth and Death, speaking in terms of morality, speaking through practice over time, it's still easy, but making all sentient beings become Buddhas [isn't easy]. That is the wish of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, wishing that all sentient beings become Buddhas. That's not just an empty wish! After vowing, there is action. Action is the development of Bodhi mind. Encouraging all sentient beings is Action.

In the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death, we are often able to escape ourselves. People in the midst of suffering always hope to find ways to escape from their lives, without even thinking about helping all sentient beings to leave. Forgetting one's own suffering, [dedicated to saving sentient beings from suffering], that is the person who develops a great mind. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said that he comforts those who do not develop the mind of enlightenment, [that is] those who have dull faculties. Their minds are very small, how to determine how big or small? With a small mind, it will be for yourself first, and then talk about saving others. A great heart first saves others, not oneself, so that all sentient beings can enter the profound and wonderful dharma of the Buddha path, vowing to become Buddha. At the same time, I also hope to accumulate all the merits and virtues. I must practice difficult austerities so that I can do things that ordinary people cannot do. Normally, people who practice the Bodhisattva path, even sacrificing their lives to help others, do not consider personal gain or loss. That is called “Practice Bodhisattva path”. Saving others is saving yourself.

I often think like this: Before we burn wood, or while burning wood, the fire has not yet risen, we must use a small stick to start the fire. That fire poker will make the fire rise higher. Only when firewood has air flowing in can it burn. That fire poker is like practicing the Bodhisattva path, saving all sentient beings, but also getting burned yourself, which has the same meaning. Using this as an example, while you save sentient beings and cause them to end their afflictions, your own afflictions are also ended, which has that meaning. But it takes a very long time, not just one or two lifetimes, but countless lifetimes, or [at least] three great lifetimes, which means an extremely long time!

Bodhisattva is not afraid of birth and death. When you save sentient beings, you must be in the tribulation of birth and death to save sentient beings. Just like we have the mind to seek rebirth in the Pure Land, to reach the Pure Land is for you to save others, or for others to save you? In the world of Ultimate Bliss, who do you save? Do you have any power to save others? But because our mind is weak, we are born in the Pure Land world to attain enlightenment and then return to Sa Ba to save sentient beings. If you are born in the Pure Land, how will you develop your great mind? We pray to be reborn in the Pure Land, just like we study skills to help others. Without the ability to help others, wanting others to escape suffering and be happy, but we ourselves do not have the method. Therefore, pray to be born in the Pure Land to study there, learn the method of benefiting beings and then return to save others. But the mind to seek birth in the Pure Land is not for oneself, but to benefit sentient beings, so one develops the mind to seek birth in the World of Ultimate Bliss. Everyone, please consider for a moment, these two things are the same: One is to develop the mind to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss to take care of life and death, the other is to develop the mind to go to the world of Ultimate Bliss to benefit sentient beings. That is called “developing Bodhi mind”.

But we are in samsara, suffering quite a lot of suffering in the six paths of samsara, we are not afraid, we spend many long lifetimes among all suffering beings to save suffering beings. You hope to save sentient beings, but do not enter among sentient beings, can you save sentient beings? Don't be afraid of birth and death, don't be afraid of all suffering, you must save all sentient beings. Praying for liberation for yourself is quite easy! If we were to make all living beings liberated, this would be extremely difficult. As soon as this Mahayana meaning arises, it declines, it is not easy to develop! For example, Sariputra wanted to develop the Bodhisattva mind to save sentient beings. He had just developed the Bodhi mind when Emperor Thich Thien immediately transformed into a human to test Him to see if His great Bodhi mind was real or fake. He immediately transformed into a poor girl, crying on the side of the road. Venerable Sariputta asked the girl: "What are you crying about?" The little girl replied: "My mother is sick. I can find medicine, but there is no drug carrier." Venerable Sariputta asked the girl: “[To obtain] that medicinal substance, what difficulties will there be?” The girl replied: "It's extremely difficult!" Venerable Sariputta asked: "What medicinal substance is needed?" The girl replied: "You have to find the eyes of a living person, you can't find the eyes of a dead person! You have to find the eyes of a living person." As soon as Venerable Sariputta heard this, he [thought]:

“I have just developed Bodhi mind and encountered this problem; should I let go or not? If I don't let go, I will have developed Bodhi mind. If I let go, giving away my eyes is very difficult, it is not money!” He was still steadfast in giving her, and immediately gouged out her left eye. The little girl said: "You hooked it wrong! I need the right eye!" Venerable Sariputta said: "Why didn't you speak up sooner?" He still had some regret in his heart, but he still hadn't completely retreated from it. His right eye was also gouged out for her: "Anyway, I have Thien Eye, it's okay! Gouge it out for her!" The child took the eye, smelled it, and criticized: "It stinks and makes me want to vomit! How can it be used as medicine?" Throw it on the ground and trample it. Sariputta immediately withdrew his mind from the seven paths and said "The Bodhisattva path is difficult to practice". This is not just empty talk!

Like Venerable Sariputta, [according to] the wisdom and merit he cultivated, Thoughts and Thoughts were all stopped, great Bodhi mind was developed, but still discouraged! We also often say: "If we as individuals also want to learn to develop Bodhicitta and help others, wait until we ourselves suffer hardship, and we will think that even helping ourselves is still difficult, how can we help others!" Why? During the tribulation, he doubted that Buddha and Bodhisattva were not spiritual. [Due to doubt] there is no spirit, doubt arises in the mind. If you consider yourself to have made no mistakes, why should you receive retribution? Those are all people who are ignorant of the Hinayana. If one develops the great mind of Bodhi, and develops the most sublime mind of the highest path, it is indeed very difficult. Having made a commitment, a vow, we make a vow every day. Every day we sing praises, that is, recite verses and chants about the Four Great Vows: “The vow to save sentient beings is boundless, the vow to end all afflictions is endless, the vow to learn countless Dharma methods, the vow to attain the unsurpassed Buddha path”. Not even one thing can be done! Empty vows! Whenever the realm appears, it will recede. If you encounter an accident, you will not immediately help others, but will also run away faster than anyone else! So how can we save sentient beings?

Therefore, sentient beings with dull faculties, Hinayana, wish to develop a mind of victory and miracles, but they cannot do it, asceticism is very difficult! We often hear "If we can't save ourselves, how can we save others?" That sentence is very often heard! But the Dharma disciples present all understand Buddhism. You can help those who do not believe to believe in Buddhism, which is not an easy thing. It's not like if you just advise them, they will believe you, you have to take a lot of measures. Having encountered many challenges, you don't dare to speak anymore. Especially for people who do not believe in Buddha, you advise them to believe in Buddha, that is still normal. But especially in times of danger, when you yourself are still in danger, let's say we are in the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death. We don't want to ourselves suffer in the sea of ​​suffering, and see someone else in trouble [so we first have the intention to help that person]; That is truly the benefit of sentient beings. Therefore, the practice of suffering, hardship, saving oneself, saving others, lasts a long time, not in one or two times, in one day, in one life, in two lives, not in our lifespan of one hundred years, but in immeasurable, immeasurable lives. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is good at comforting and skillful in explaining the means to this type of living beings. That is what we are talking about about the true definition of the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. [Yet] we just consider the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma sutra as an ordinary sutra, or think that the first half of the sutra is the Hinayana sutra, the second half is completely the Avatamsaka realm.

self, no action, no life, no self, no other, no action, no origin, no existence, no past, present, future, even the eightfold doctrine of emptiness, non-existence of birth and death, Nirvana. All dharmas have determined the true nature of the truth that can be attained. Huu Phu preaches that all dharmas are like an illusion, like a transformation, like a water moon, like a mirror, like a city of Gandharvas, like an empty cup, like a bright flame, like a robe, like a road, like a light, like a mote, like a dream, like electricity, like a cloud. The afflictions of birth and death are even weak and cannot be eliminated. Desperate for afflictions, birth and death are bound to be non-existent, wishes cannot be attained, the origin cannot be born, and truth is eternal. Self-nature is quiet, which means Nirvana.
(Sutra: For that person I will speak the true meaning, that is, the original nature of all Dharma syllables Emptiness, ultimate no-self, no action, no receiving, no self, no forgiveness, no going, no destination, no place, no past, present, future, up to and including eighteen types of Emptiness, etc. There is no birth and death and Nirvana, [as well as] no solid form of all dharmas that can be achieved. Moreover, they say all dharmas are like illusion, like transformation, like the moon in water, like an image in a mirror, like the city of Heaven. The Buddha is like the echo in an empty cave, like the ripples of sunlight, like water bubbles, like mist, like blind eyes, like lightning, like clouds. The nature of afflictions and birth and death is extremely weak, and is easily destroyed. Moreover, afflictions and birth and death are ultimately impossible.

Meeting that type of living beings, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva uses skillful means to tell them the true meaning. “The true meaning” is the meaning of becoming a Buddha. What is the true meaning? The nature of all dharma symbols is Emptiness; that is the true meaning. You see any method of Buddha, whether you see it with your eyes, hear it with your ears, think with your mind, and contact with the six senses, it all has the true meaning. First of all, you yourself need to explain this, because it all arises from self-nature. First of all, understand that self-nature is inherently empty, all dharmas are empty. Explain it yourself, and even preach that kind of method to all sentient beings, saying that all dharmas are selfless, without cause, without self, and without forgiveness. “All dharmas do not exist, they are Emptiness.” You realize it yourself, then tell others. I myself did not realize it, but I believed it. That is the Bodhisattva class of Faith. Then, propagandize towards others, saying "all dharmas are ultimately selfless", realizing that all dharmas are selfless. All Mahayana scriptures say so. In non-self, when we ourselves contemplate: This is Self-Clinging, not being attached to Self and Self-View; For all the problems that we see, we do not use the Ego View to see all the problems, reaching the level of "not using the Ego View to see all dharmas". Are you aware or not? There is no self, and there is no other person either. All dharmas are Emptiness. Without practicing, there is no cultivating the path, attaining enlightenment, nor is there any place, nor is there anything past, present, or future. That is to say “all dharmas are Emptiness”. Even because they say eighteen items of Emptiness, all dharmas are Emptiness, there is no birth, death and Nirvana. The eighteen items of Emptiness will be taught in the following section. Samsara and Nirvana are relative, all dharmas are Emptiness. Why? There is no real form that can be achieved.

Again, it is said that all dharmas are like illusions, like transformations, they are all illusory, not real. All dharmas are like the moon in water. The moon in the water is not real, it is a shadow, everyone understands this. All dharmas are like images in a mirror, their reflected appearance is identical [like an object reflected in a mirror]. “Like the city of Gandharva”: The other [similes] are easy to understand, [but for this example, further explanation is needed]. Among the eight groups of ghosts and gods, there is the demon god Gandharva (Gandharva). [City of Gandharva] sometimes appears, sometimes disappears. If you are in Shandong, Shandong province has Laoshan, sixty miles from Qingdao China[34]. We arrived at Laoshan, when the sun was about to rise, standing on top of Laoshan looking out over the East Sea, looking at the sea. At that time, in the sea there was an image that seemed to be a city. If the weather is very clear, sometimes you see [that image] just like in our human world. In it, many people walk, stand, sit, do whatever, it's all there. The sun has just risen, [that illusion] is no more. The city of Gandharva does not exist, it is just an [illusory] image. [The Sutra says] “like the city of Gandharva” to visualize “nothing, empty”; But sometimes it appears. In Lao Son, many people climb to the top of Lao Son mountain to see “hai thi, god lau” (city on the sea, castle of clams)[35]. Buddhist scriptures call “hai thi, Than Lau” as “City of Gandharva”. Among the eight orders of ghosts and gods, there is the species of Gandharva. That is their citadel, basically there is no citadel, it is just a shadow. There is also an empty cave. You enter a mountain cave, scream, the echoing sound is called Huong (echo, echo), it has no form! Like ripples of sunlight (yang diem, mirage, mirage in the desert), like foam on the surface of water. Like dew, as soon as the sun rises, it disappears. Like a lamp, like a dreamy eye, like a dream, like lightning, like a cloud. Those are words that visualize emptiness, that visualize empty meaning.

Using these things to compare our birth and death afflictions, do they exist or not? Vain! But we living beings cannot No! Trouble comes, you can't sleep, you can't eat, you can't Empty! Why not No? They are unaware and attached. Foam on the water, morning dew, lightning, flowers in the eyes, dreaming while sleeping. Can a dream be real? But ordinary people are attached, if they have good dreams, they will be happy all day. If you have a nightmare, you won't be able to rest for two or three days. It doesn't exist [but is still attached to it], that is called “false attachment”. Therefore, contemplate afflictions, contemplate birth and death like that. Our nature, the essence of our own nature, has no afflictions, nor does it have birth and death. In nature, it does not exist, that is, for the lifespan of each of us, the Buddha taught you to practice Contemplation, then said Falsehood. After birth, old age, illness, and death appear, you can determine that it is fake, and your suffering will be reduced. But we cannot practice. Even though in truth it is false, the real thing will be indestructible. Everyone believes that their own body is real, but it will perish. From the moment we are born to our parents, we are very small, gradually we become old, we grow old, then we die, and when we die, we are no more. That's how we perceive it. But what is destroyed is your appearance, not your nature. Regarding the afflictions of birth and death, you must know that [the afflictions of birth and death] have no real substance, they are false manifestations, and the real substance is indestructible. You wish for longevity, but you can't, you can't achieve it! If you attain non-birth, there is also no death. Without birth, there really is no death. The nature is stillness, we do not realize this. Even though we have not attained enlightenment, we understand clearly. How to understand clearly? Buddha taught us to understand clearly. Buddha said that birth and death is Nirvana. You are in samsara, can realize, can let go of samsara, attain Nirvana. Because birth and death are false, you must see that it is false, recognize that it is false, and you will be able to attain enlightenment, that is, to attain enlightenment. This is completely about the meaning of Emptiness, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva tells us about Emptiness. First of all, "No" is contemplated from those things. All things are the same, life and death are the same, but Nirvana is the same, all dharmas are not true, there is no certainty. That appearance is a fake appearance, why? The truth will not change. Each of us is like that, we are all changing. It changes forever, then it's no more, it's gone, it's dead. Afflictions, birth and death, Nirvana, are just pretending!

(Sutra) If you try to talk too much, destroy all views, damage your own mind, clinging to fixed thoughts, and be terrified. weakness.
(Sutra: Speaking like that can [cause the listener] to destroy all views and ideas. think of attachments to one's own body and mind, to be freed from fear and weakness).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: You must see your own Views, “View” is the way of looking at the problem, the power of view (the subject of seeing, our mind) looks at the view (object, thing, dharma being seen). The ability to see is your nature, and the ability to see is all appearances. Nang Kien looks at So Kien, for your body, for your mind, [or in general] for your body and mind, it is just an attachment, without real reality. Now we have a body, the body is perishable, it will disappear, it is not eternal. When you are ten years old, the time when you were one or two years old is gone, the time when you were nine years old is gone, the time when you were ten years old is still there. When you are twenty years old, the time of ten years old will no longer exist. That is called the dharma of birth and death, that is our attachment. We must destroy that attachment. Destroy all views, they are false views. Everyone who reads the Shurangama Sutra will know that seeing nature is revealed ten times. Attachment to body and mind in this body, attachment to it is Yes. Actually, it doesn't exist. But right now we have a body. When we have a body, we can realize that the body will definitely disappear. That is something that is certain and must be achieved. What did you achieve? Lost. Why? Hopeless. It's not real. Therefore, if you can get away from such a point of view, if you can penetrate, you can see clearly and let go of everything. That makes you “disrupt”, [that is, destroy] those false views.

(Sutra) Resurrecting sentient beings cannot understand the Tathagata's words only with intention, children are terrified and weak. By understanding the Tathagata's words and teachings, the Tathagata's vision of the One True Realm will help him attain separation from birth, old age, sickness, death, and all evil dharmas, and he will witness that the Dharma Body is eternal, pure, immutable, and has accumulated immeasurable merit. Serving the willow willow view of all sentient beings in the body and friendship as if it were true, wonderful, pure and meritorious, but ignorance is contaminated with blessings. Throughout life, old age, sickness, death, and countless sufferings, the Tathagata tried to give rise to great compassion, the spirit of desire must separate all sentient beings from all sufferings, share the Dharmakaya of the First Meaning of Bliss, and cherish the Dharmakaya without discrimination. Only has the ability to destroy false consciousnesses, not to give rise to false thoughts, to be able to attain all sentient beings, to constantly mock and discriminate, to be attached to all dharmas. Because of crazy thoughts and delusions, I experience birth and death. Thi co, The Tathagata, because of desire, refuses to discriminate, is attached to thoughts and ideas, teaches that the worldly dharma must be empty, non-existent, and will necessarily transcend the worldly dharma, all-winged dharma is empty, non-existent. The false exaggeration is like the Eighteen Voids. Such as it shows, all dharmas are inseparable from the Bodhi body. Bồ Đề thể giả, phi hữu, phi vô, phi phi hữu, phi phi vô, phi hữu vô câu, phi nhất, phi dị, phi phi nhất, phi phi dị, phi nhất dị câu, nãi chí tất cánh vô hữu nhất tướng nhi khả đắc giả. Because of the separation from all fixed appearances, the separation from all false appearances, the position cannot rely on words to defend, but in the Bodhidharma there is no false saying of existence, and there is no possibility of false sayings. It is impossible to understand with the mind, because in the Bodhidharma there is no grasping, grasping, no self, no other, separate from the characteristics of existence. Weakness distinguishes illusions from falsehoods and falsehoods, respectively.
(Sutra: There are sentient beings who do not understand the meaning of the Tathagata's words, so they are frightened and weak. You should know that the intention of the Tathagata's words is that the Tathagata, by seeing the realm of One Truth, is ultimately free from the evils of birth, old age, sickness, and death, and attains the eternal, cool, immutable Dharma Body, etc., immeasurable amounts of merit. Furthermore, one can clearly see that in the bodies of all sentient beings, there is such pure, subtle, and true merit, but it is obscured by ignorance, always in the long night of enduring birth, old age, sickness, and death, immeasurable. Therefore, the Tathagata aroused great compassion and wanted to make all sentient beings abandon suffering and attain the First Meaning of Dharma in the Dharma Body. However, the Dharma Body is non-discriminating and free from thoughts. Only those who can destroy false thoughts and not give rise to thoughts can achieve it. But all sentient beings often like to discriminate and cling to dharmas, so they suffer from birth and death discrimination, attachment, it should be said that all dharmas in the world are ultimately emptiness, non-existent. Even all dharmas beyond the world are ultimately emptiness, non-existent. If speaking broadly, it is like eighteen dharmas, showing that all such dharmas do not exist, are not non-existent, are not non-existent, are not both existent and non-existent, are not one, are not different, are not "not one", are not not. "Not different", not "both one and different", until ultimately there is no form that can be obtained, due to separation from all appearances. "Departing from all appearances" means not being able to rely on words to keep, because in the Bodhi dharma there is no one who receives the words, and also there is no one who can rely on the mind to know, because in the Bodhi dharma there is no subject to hold and there is no object to be kept, there is no self, no forgiveness, due to separation. If there is an idea of distinction, it will be false, it is not called correspondence).

Nowadays our mind is not big; Because I'm not old, I don't dare to contemplate myself like that, I don't know my own mortality. Even though I know clearly, I still don't dare admit it! Everyone knows the story of death: Until death, even if you don't let it go, you have to let it go. Even if you want to be attached, you can't be attached to it, it disappears. Please explain it like that. Don't give birth to thoughts of fear and weakness, don't give birth to thoughts of longevity. Be brave and contemplate these problems and they will eventually disappear. If you destroy it, you will definitely die. Therefore, the Buddha told us, birth, old age, sickness, death, up to Afraid Separation (love that must be separated), Oan Tang Hoi (resentment that must be met), Five Aggregates (the illustrious Five Aggregates), Praying for Unattainable (desiring but not achieving), those eight types are suffering. You must see clearly, you must perceive them: They arise according to Truth. From within the illusion and falsehood, we recognize something "unborn, immortal, unchangeable, no different, true" in it, that is, our nature. These things are called reaching the realm as mentioned in the previous text, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva now teaches us the realm of One Truth. The Dharma “realm of One Truth” is free from the sufferings of birth and death, birth, old age, sickness, and death, up to the eight sufferings, without those things. That is our inherent nature. That is the pure Dharmakaya, incomparable, no different from Buddha and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Where Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are merits, where we sentient beings are afflictions.

At the same time, you contemplate and know your own true nature like that. Every living being has its true nature, it is right in the body of the living being, but it does not leave the body. From within your body, you search for true nature, there is none! Your mind is consciousness, it is false, it is not real, but it is complete. The true mind is everywhere! If we do not have Buddha's knowledge, if we do not have a real part in Buddha, we will not be able to become Buddha! We and the Buddha are not two, no different. We can become Buddhas, but currently afflictions hinder you.

At the same time, you must see that in the bodies of all sentient beings there is the true, wonderful, pure merit of the Tathagata; that is available. Tathagata discovered it and clearly stated it through practice (practice through appearance). Practicing with what is available becomes one, all ignorance, ignorance, and obstacles are washed away. Suppose our body or clothes are dirty, if you wash it once it's not clean, if you wash it twice it's not clean, if you wash it three times it's clean. That is talking about our original nature and physical body, it is not the physical body (the flesh body), [original nature, physical body] has no birth, old age, sickness, death, nor suffering. Of course there is no suffering, no happiness, no all relative dharmas, no two, no different from Buddha.

In this passage of literature, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us: “All sentient beings can become Buddhas”. As long as you are willing to practice and follow the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, that is, [follow] the method and realm of One Truth as He taught in the previous scriptures; Please understand. If one can realize the realm of One Truth, one will be separated from birth, old age, sickness, and death. Birth, old age, illness, and death are illusions, not real. This type of practice is the same, whether you can practice it or not, you have to think like that in normal times. While you are most suffering, you can experiment with separating the painful feelings and the suffering of the body that is suffering. The Shurangama Sutra teaches us that we have a feeling, that feeling can be felt, that is, to feel the suffering that the body is suffering. The awareness of that feeling mind will not be painful, although it will feel the suffering it is experiencing. At the same time, I thought like this: When I was in the hospital and needed surgery, first of all, the doctor injected you with anesthetic to numb the nerves. No matter what he dissects, you don't feel anything, nor do you suffer. Wait until the anesthetic wears off and you will feel pain. If you don't inject anesthetic, you can control your own mind, separate your own mind and body. This requires effort over a very long period of time. Isn't it like I just said that you can do it right away after learning it! When your sensory power reaches a very great level, there is no need for anesthetic injections anymore: You see that your body and yourself have no relationship. It's a matter of mentality. In history, there are many of these types of characters. Everyone saw Quan Van Truong (Quan Cong) scraping bones to treat poison. Hua Tuo[36] carved out the flesh, used a knife to scrape on the bones, everyone else who heard that sound trembled, Quan Cong was still playing Chinese chess, nothing happened. That shows that his mind is very strong, his mind subdues his body. When we are most suffering, you separate body and mind, mind and body become two different things. Therefore, the Shurangama Sutra teaches us: “A unified sense of consciousness, a unified state of enlightenment” means: You have the feeling of recognizing pain, but that pain does not affect your feeling mind. But because we don't have that strength, the doctor has to inject anesthesia. Are there any cases where anesthesia is not injected? There was an old monk who, when entering the hospital for surgery, did not agree to let the doctor inject anesthetic. The doctor said: "You will be in so much pain that you will go into a coma." The monk said: "I'm not in pain, you guys just go ahead and do the surgery." This requires effort, it can't be achieved in a day or two! While you practice, separate mind and matter, the body is matter, the spirit is not matter, and will produce results. I have experimented, and it has produced [effect]. You see this in many patriarchs, people who practice the path can cause [body and mind] to separate.

You must achieve this kind of happiness. Therefore, the Tathagata aroused great compassion, wanting to help all sentient beings escape all suffering and attain the First Meaning of Bliss in the Dharmakaya. That's not the body. Just now we talked about the body, but the Dharma Body has no distinction, no distracting thoughts. When a person wants to achieve non-discrimination, no mixed thoughts, when one mind is pure, false thoughts do not arise, all thoughts can be stopped, that is called “corresponding to the path”. When you practice and reach this kind of realm, it means your form of consciousness is separate from the mind.

But all sentient beings often like to distinguish and cling to dharmas. Buddha attained "permanence, happiness, self, purity". We living beings make distinctions, discriminate against permanent happiness, and hold on to all dharmas; That is crazy delusion. Why do they want to be attached? Because we cannot let go of false thoughts; With a crazy attachment, you suffer the suffering of birth and death. The Tathagata Buddhas have stopped, when they have stopped, they have no distinguishing features, that is, they have achieved "permanence, happiness, self, purity", and have stopped the ideas of discrimination and attachment. This is thanks to the power of practice. I just said, if you practice correctly for a long time, making your mind and body separate, your mind is not bound by your body, you will gradually be able to reach this kind of realm. That bondage is an attachment: You think your body is yourself. Suppose you leave your body, it is not me. [The body] is not you, no matter how much suffering it is, it has nothing to do with you. This practice is not something you can give up in a day or two. There are no attachments or stubbornness!

In this passage, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us, “ultimately Emptiness, non-existence”. Speaking of "ultimately", in the essence of our mind, it is not the body, everything is Emptiness. The dharma of the world is Emptiness, the dharma that emerges from the world is also Emptiness, ultimately it is Emptiness, everything is non-existent. If speaking broadly, as the sutras often say, there are a total of eighteen types of Emptiness. Here, I won't go into detail, just point out the nouns to everyone. The manifest realms are all empty. Internal Emptiness, External Emptiness, inside and outside are all Emptiness. The physical body (physical body) is completely empty, the inner mind, five internal organs, and six organs are all empty. The external physical body is also Emptiness. Non-emptiness: Non-emptiness will not destroy; If it is not destroyed, it will not be destroyed. Your physical body will eventually die, everyone does. Inside is the body and mind, outside is the world, the entire world is changing. Your body and mind are Emptiness, the appearance of the outside world is Emptiness. That Emptiness is also empty, that Emptiness is also eliminated. Then, going one step further, it is called Dai Khong. Dai Khong goes one step further to De Nhat Nghia Khong. The First Meaning of Emptiness goes one step further: Emptiness of Non-Being, Emptiness of Existence, Emptiness of All Wings, Emptiness of No Beginning, Existence of Emptiness, Emptiness, Emptiness of Self, Emptiness of All Dharmas, Emptiness of Unattainable[37], there is no dharma, all dharmas do not exist. Why? Empty. There are dharmas, all dharmas of existence are also empty, dharmas of existence and non-actions are all empty. A total of eighteen types, showing, broadly speaking, eighteen items of Void like that. The meanings of the eighteen items of Emptiness are many, books only say [generally] Emptiness, only this Sutra exists.

It shows that all such dharmas do not leave the Bodhi Body, all dharmas are founded on Bodhi. We develop Bodhi mind, which is the whole. All dharmas are inseparable from Bodhi. Why say No? Aims to display Bodhi. What is Bodhi? Enlightenment, that is, enlightenment in enlightenment. Developing Bodhi mind means you develop a mind of understanding and enlightenment, it is called “developing Bodhi mind”. Bodhi is translated into Enlightenment in enlightenment. Enlightenment is understanding. What is Bodhi Body? It doesn't exist. If it is not Existence, it is Emptiness, which is Non-existence. [But] it is not Emptiness, it is not Void. Non-existence, non-existence (not existence, non-existence): Viewing it as existence or non-existence is incorrect, it is non-existence! Non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-non-on For “existence without sentence” (both existence and non-existence) also add a word Phi, which means “non-existence without sentence” (not both existence and non-existence). It is impossible to say one, that is “non-one”. It is impossible to say otherwise, it is “non-different” (no different). To this word Phi, add another word Phi, with the intention of eliminating: Non-one is not right, non-different is also wrong, non-non-existence, non-non-different. What must One and One be like to be correct? “The sentence is different” (It is both the same and different) is also wrong! Until All Wings Non-Existence (ultimately non-existent). This displays the connotation No; that is explaining the Emptiness. There is no form that can be achieved, no form that can be achieved. All movements of the mind are Emptiness. Fly! All appearances do not exist, all are not; That is the Body of Bodhi.

In the previous section, we talked about the One True realm, what is displayed here? Realm One True. [It can be temporarily understood that what has been said above] is the realm of One Truth, but it is still not the realm of One Truth, it must be in accordance with the mind. [Because, the things just presented above] are only words, words cannot express. Using words to express will have no real meaning. As long as there are words, there will be no real meaning. Because, the mind is pure, separate from the appearance of words, separate from the appearance of the mind, separate from all appearances. Is there a general or not? That is called Tathagatagarbha. The Tathagata Store contains all dharmas, contains all dharmas, including all the pure dharmas of the Tathagata. That Body, that is, the essence of the Tathagata Storehouse Nature, whether it is said to exist or not, is all nonsense. Why? No distinction! As soon as the mind starts thinking, as soon as there is a distinction, it is lost! You can only understand with your mind, you cannot use language to convey, you understand with your mind. When it comes to enlightenment, the mind can't understand it, it can't be expressed with language, language can't express it! As long as there are words, there is no real meaning, what is expressed in language is not true, it is only an image. Bodhi is to leave all appearances.

“Leaving all appearances” means not being attached, not relying on words. If we use language to preserve that Bodhi form, it will not be possible to maintain it, [because] speech has no true meaning. Because in the Bodhi Dharma, there is no form of speech, no form of the recipient, nothing that can be spoken, and also nothing that can be expressed by speech. There is no concept in the mind, based on the concept in the mind to know it is fake, not real. Bodhi Dharma cannot have something to hold on to (grasping), nor something to be held (cling to), there is no self, there is no forgiveness. Any distinction or discrimination is not right. If there is an idea of ​​distinction, it is false and does not correspond to the mind and Bodhi. Simply put, the Body of Bodhi is separate from all forms and all words. Using words to preserve the Body of Bodhi would not be right. Using all the forms to maintain the Body of Bodhi is also wrong, because your mind and perception are not correct. That is called “language ceases, mental activity ceases”. When you contemplate, you meditate with your thoughts. When contemplating, it is not the mind that starts thinking. When you have reached the point of no-mind, no-mind, if explained according to the meaning in Zen Buddhism, would be “mind-mind-mutu”. Meanwhile, speech stops, there are no thoughts in the mind, [so it is called] “the cessation of the mind”. Therefore, there is only talk, there is no “real meaning” (true meaning). Speech is intended to express and show you, but [Bodhi Body] is not speech. Speaking of “mind”, “mind” here is not the mind, but means “dharma”. Just like when we talk about "fire", "fire" is not real fire. If it were real fire, your mouth would be burned. Talking about "water" is not really water, it's just a word with an expressive meaning!

(Sutra) Such as it is, the base of sentient beings cannot be understood, the supreme path Tathagata Dharmakaya, the sole There is no dharma, all directions are non-possessive. KThe mind is weak, afraid of falling without attaining the center, or the birth and destruction of thoughts, the increase or decrease of views, turn to slander, self-contempt, contempt for others.
The body is nothing but emptiness, ultimately nothing." Their minds are frightened and weak, afraid of falling into "nothing to achieve", or giving birth to thoughts of annihilation, giving rise to views of increase and decrease, leading to slander and contempt for themselves and others).

Speaking Dharma like that, that is, with such doctrine, can beings with slow temperaments understand or not? Can't understand. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva preached the Dharma in that way, sentient beings with dull senses cannot understand it, nor can they understand the Dharma Body of the Tathagata, so he said: The unsurpassed path Tathagata Dharma Body is only the Dharma Emptiness. What is the Supreme Dharmakaya of the Tathagata? Are not! That Emptiness is not Ngon Khong (inert emptiness), it is not the Emptiness like we see in the empty space in the room, it is not that kind of Emptiness, but it is Dharma Emptiness. To put it simply, when it comes to Emptiness, you should not be attached to anything, you should not be attached to anything. We often say “see clearly, let go”, if you see clearly, let go, you will be free. Once you see clearly and let go, you will be free. Sentient beings with dull faculties have no way to understand, cannot understand. This is the unsurpassed path of the Tathagata Dharmakaya. Although it is Emptiness, it is ultimately non-existent. Wanting to achieve something, praying for something [from Dharmakāya] is not there.

Thus, for living beings who do not have strong mental power, because their mental power is not strong, fear and weakness arise. Once frightened, Bodhi mind cannot arise. [Misunderstanding that the Dharmakaya is empty] then everything is empty, so what should I practice? Is there anything else? There is no affliction, no Nirvana, no birth and death, no nothing; Isn't that the cessation of thought? It is not cessation. If the thought of cessation arises, the idea of ​​increase or decrease arises, both [the idea of] increase and cessation are impossible. Below, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva also explains himself.

(Sutra) The Self, that is, the Tathagata Dharmakaya is inherently empty, truly existent, immeasurably pure and complete. industry, without beginning of the world, naturally perfect, without cultivation, without work, the will of all sentient beings in the body of the heron stage is complete, unchanging, undifferentiated, without increase, without decrease.
The true Body, complete with immeasurable pure meritorious deeds. From the beginningless time until now, [that self-nature] is naturally perfect, uncultivated, unfabricated, until the bodies of all sentient beings are complete, without change, without difference, without increase, without decrease).

Saying “The Tathagata's Dharma Body is non-empty”, that is, the self-nature is non-empty. Tathagata's Dharma Body is non-empty, eliminating all attachments. If you accept Tathagata's Dharma Body as existence, it will be completely wrong! It is non-empty, non-existent! Not Emptiness, not Form to see the Tathagata. It is not Emptiness, nor does it have form. Seeing the Buddha like that, without emptiness, there is a true Body. The Tathagata's Dharma Body is non-empty and has a true Body. What is the true Body of the Tathagata's Dharmakaya? Immeasurable pure merit. That is the immeasurable pure merit in the Body of the Tathagata's Dharmakaya. What does pure merit look like? From beginningless time until now, natural perfection is not a practice, nor is it a creation, that is talking about the Dharmakaya. In the bodies of all sentient beings, they are complete, unchanged, no different.

Where Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not increase; where all living beings do not decrease. Isn't it true that between the Dharma Bodies of sentient beings and the Dharma Bodies of Buddhas, there is a difference in appearance? No! Dharmakaya has no form. Sentient beings are inherently complete, the Buddhas have cultivated into that completeness, that is, “cultivated”. Living beings are inherently delusional, but they never lose [the Dharmakaya]. Everyone has the complete Dharmakaya, everyone can become a Buddha. If you lose it, you will not be able to become a Buddha. No loss, no gain! Even if you lose it, you can't lose it; Even if it is possible, it is not possible! There is only a silent contract that cannot be expressed in words. Using language to express will not be able to express. The Great Zen Patriarch Li can only quietly contract, it is all a tacit contract. That is called “touting the Dharmakaya”. The Dharmakaya does not come from cultivation, it is an inherent merit, but it is no different from the Dharmakaya that is revealed through practice.

(Sutra) Like the teachings of equality, able to eliminate fear and weakness, comforting the name.
(Sutra: Saying it like that, it can eliminate fear and weakness, called "comfort").

Because talking about what is already there, that is called “speaking comfort”. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva uses this expression to eliminate the fear and weakness of sentient beings, [in order to make sentient beings] know that they can become Buddhas, know that they inherently have Buddha Nature. That Buddha Nature is not two, no different from Buddha. We often talk about “spiritual nature”, especially monastics, they have absolutely no training, but they understand things that ordinary people cannot understand. When we talk about enlightenment, that enlightenment has great enlightenment, small enlightenment, there are things that have been learned and practiced in the past, so it is called “collective practice”. Someone who has studied for decades is still not as good as someone who has not studied at all! Must include that person's previous life. [Otherwise], you won't understand [the reason]. You must know that in a previous life, or in countless lives, that person has already practiced. Therefore, when it comes to this matter, some cases are very clear, some cases are not clear, not clearly expressed.

Like there are religious people who have never studied worldly dharma, yet they all understand it clearly. For example, I have a friend I have known for a long time named old monk Tho Da[38]. We were in America. He returned to the country, returned to Ngu Dai Son, and met an old Dharma friend, [also an old monk]. That old monk also passed away. It's just that you can know, know in your mind, but can't have any effect, still haven't practiced successfully, still haven't practiced well. If it can give rise to effects, it will be successfully cultivated and can produce wonderful effects. Miraculous use is about benefiting sentient beings.

(Sutra) Conquering ignorance and steadfast attachment to living beings, the writing is like a theory, the heron gives birth to terror Weakness. Because they accept that the Dharma Body of the Tathagata is inherently complete and perfect, without the appearance of cultivation or creation, they arise [attachment to] the appearance of "nothing to be achieved", giving rise to fear and weakness, or accepting that it is natural, falling into crazy wrong views).

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: If sentient beings are foolish, that is, sentient beings who have attachments that do not let go, when their minds are towards the unsurpassed path, towards the Tathagata's Dharmakaya, although they are inherently complete [the unsurpassed path, Dharmakaya], but because they hold on to their ignorance, they do not believe. They do not believe that the Dharmakaya and Dharmakaya do not need to be practiced or created. After the [Dharmakaya] appears, it is still inherent, it is not increased by the Buddhas' cultivation, it is not there at all! It is not because sentient beings do not practice that they are reduced. There is none! Cultivating is also equality, but not cultivating is still equality; One appears, the other does not appear. What is it? Non-attainment, but after obtaining it, it is still non-attainment. We basically do not attain it, we are confused, and now we do not practice, [so] it (the Dharmakaya) does not appear. Is it really lost? No loss! It exists forever, its nature is complete.

For that type of living beings, if one talks about the appearance of “not cultivated, not created” in the Tathagata's Dharmakaya, they will be frightened by the unattainable [characteristics] of the Tathagata's Dharmakaya], or accept it as natural, thinking that it naturally exists, naturally falling into wrong knowledge and wrong views. After having fully attained Bodhi, there is absolutely nothing to achieve. Because there is nothing to achieve, there can be "nothing that cannot be achieved". It's not about achieving this and giving up that. Achieving perfection is called “non-attainment”, it will give rise to the present great use. That is the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, from realizing the complete form of the Body, great use arises. Great use is the career of benefiting sentient beings, at the same time, benefiting oneself and benefiting others are both complete.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva told Kien Tinh Bodhisattva: All good dharmas as I said before have fully increased, you should perfect those good dharmas. When good dharma increases, what is the appearance (appearance)? Giving birth to the physical body of Tathagata, that is the appearance of merit, that is, the appearance of all good dharmas. It is in the Dharmakaya of the Tathagata that, although there is no realm of speech, separate from the mind of remembrance, there is neither emptiness nor non-emptiness, nor can it be described or shown based on words, based on the pseudo-names of illusory causes and conditions that interact with each other in the World, it is possible to express and speak because the nature of Dharmakaya is truly undifferentiated. But the very deep meaning that I said is true, corresponding, without mistakes, without defects, without contradictions. I say there is no contradiction with the nature, there is no contradiction. When it comes to that true appearance, there is no speech, but must rely on speech to display it. If there is no speech, how can it be displayed? How can living beings understand? Therefore, we must rely on speech. Speech is false, intended to show off. I just told everyone, when you say "fire", it's not fire. If the “fire” in question is real fire, it will burn you. All dharmas and ideas in the mind cannot be recited through dependent mindfulness. Because our mind is a mind of delusion, the more we think, the more wrong it is, the more we think, the further away it is. Therefore, in other sutras, the Buddha taught: "Dharma arises from causes and conditions, the self theory is Emptiness, the meaning of the Middle Way" (The Dharma is born because of causes and conditions, we say it is Emptiness, also the meaning of the Middle Way). Because that is based on the Worldly Emperor to speak worldly dharma. The Dharma of the world fully completes the Truth, which is Truth; The true meaning of the world relies on it to show what has been said, but all dharmas are not true, but illusory. There is no way to express the nature of all Dharmakayas. It is not a distinction, language cannot express it! But if there is nothing to talk about, how can we compare? If we use the nature of the Dharmakaya to speak, there really is no distinction, no words. Without speaking, how can sentient beings understand? Just rely on words to show! The Dharmakaya's self has no form, nor does it have any other form, so how can it be displayed? Saying Emptiness, non-emptiness, there is no appearance of Emptiness, and also no appearance of Non-emptiness, until one is separated from all appearances. The Dharmakaya is formless, what shape is the Dharmakaya? No! The Dharmakaya is formless, because it is separate from all forms. Thinking is not correct. Dharmakaya cannot be recited, you also inherently have Dharmakaya.

There is no form to see and know for yourself that it exists. There is no general who knows for himself that he has seen "this is true" or "that is not true", it is impossible. Therefore, saying the meaning of Undecided is true and corresponds without error. Therefore, add Emptiness to reveal: The meaning of Emptiness is decisively true, not false, non-empty, no different, no mistake!

Therefore, you cannot be attached to any aspect! But without saying Emptiness, without saying Nonemptiness, then how will the dharma be revealed? That Dharma cannot be revealed. These things are all false words and false names. Don't be attached to them! Leave the appearance of mental conditions, leave the appearance of discrimination, leave the appearance of words. If you discriminate and contemplate, you will not be able to achieve True Suchness at all, you will never see, and you will also not be able to see the meaning of Emptiness. [Beings are attached to] “Nothingness is cessation”. If we gain cessation, why practice anymore? Non-emptiness is existence. If we say Non-emptiness, sentient beings are attached to: "Non-emptiness means existence, then my body is also real, my family is also real." They are attached to Being! So we must eliminate the attachments of sentient beings. Because we living beings rely on our conscious mind, on the eight consciousness conditions, all of which are illusions. [Dharmakāya] is true, does not change, is no different, has no form that can be destroyed or destroyed, has no increase, and no decrease.

Furthermore, [talking about] “the place of true reality without distinction” means talking about the Dharmakaya. In the previous section, it was said about the reality of the Dharmakaya: From beginningless time until now, it has been self-sufficient, inside is full of countless merits, is natural, does not depend on practice, does not depend on creation, to achieve, respectively. Saying “corresponds” means “fits closely.” Even if separation cannot be escaped. No separation, no escape, separation is not right, and not separation is also not right. That is “no instant, no separation, no escape”, Non-emptiness is described like that.

(Sutra) As it truly is, the accumulation of merit and virtue, all sentient beings, despite the existence of existence, are in the position of ignorance and poverty. Obstacles, children without knowledge, unable to plan the merits and benefits, evil and incomprehensible heretical theory of name and status. Only by transforming and cultivating all good dharmas to overcome all obstacles and see the Dharmakaya. The mother-in-law plans for merit and benefits. Thi tries, preaches cultivating necessarily good dharmas, giving birth to Tathagata's physical body.
(Sutra: The mass of merit is truly like that, although all living beings also have it, it is covered by ignorance obscured, obstructed, so not being able to see, not being able to gain merits and benefits, is no different from not having them, so it is said to be "not there yet". Because they do not know all the merits and benefits of that dharma body, those beings cannot enjoy them, [those merits and benefits] do not belong to them. They only rely on practicing all the good dharmas to overcome the obstacles in order to see that Dharmakaya Thus, it is said, "Practice all good dharmas and give birth to the Tathagata's physical body").

The mass of merit is truly like that. Although all sentient beings also have it, they are obscured and obstructed by ignorance, so they cannot see it. All sentient beings have complete Dharma Bodies, why can't Dharma Bodies appear? Because knowledge comes from ignorance and afflictions, it is obscured, even if you look, you cannot see, even if you think, you cannot think. So we must practice and eliminate these obstacles. But for us, although the Dharmakaya is complete, it does not exist. [Because], although the Dharmakaya is complete, everyone has the complete Dharmakaya, but everyone cannot manifest it, so it is said to "not exist". Because we cannot see and know the dharma body of the Dharmakaya, because even if we look, we cannot see, even if we think, we cannot think, and even if we think, we cannot think, but it can create meritorious karma and benefit all sentient beings, and has that effect. Each of us individually depends on the Dharmakaya to practice to increase progress, practice to restore the Dharmakaya. It is the basis for all good dharmas, the essence of all good dharmas. That means we practice the Bodhisattva path, benefiting all sentient beings; that is the greatest good dharma. When you benefit sentient beings and develop Bodhi mind, that is harmony with the Dharma. Because you have developed the Bodhi mind, you will be able to attain the Body of the Dharmakaya. Developing Bodhi mind is [arising] the mind of enlightenment. We cannot maintain that enlightened mind, it arises and then becomes confused, becomes confused and then arises again, even though it has arisen and then becomes confused again! Assuming non-regression, as in the previous section we said "participating in the position of Faith", from Faith enters the First Pillar, that is, the position of non-regression. Then your faith will no longer falter, that is the truth.

This is said very clearly: We have fulfilled our true merits in Faith, but because of the obstacle of ignorance we cannot achieve it, it is like losing it, actually not lost at all, but hindered by ignorance. But it's not lost forever! When you generate your mind, it seems to be restored, to arise again. You do not develop your mind and are completely confused by ignorance, that is, regarding the nature of the Dharmakaya, because we do not study Buddha and do not know the nature of the Dharmakaya. When we have studied Buddhism and Mahayana teachings, we will clearly understand the nature of the Dharmakaya. That is, if we do all the merits, do all the deeds, practice all the good dharmas, we will be able to enjoy them. All living beings can achieve it. When your good mind arises, it still arises from the Dharmakaya. Because your mind is already there and has this foundation, only good things can be born. Good dharma has arisen, then because good has arisen, evil will be destroyed. Although we cannot enjoy the merits of the Dharmakaya, we absolutely do not lose it, we are still complete. Therefore, we must practice all good dharmas. Good dharma is spoken in response to evil dharma, speaking according to the obstacles in your Dharmakaya. You practice all good dharmas, causing your Dharma Body to appear again, in order to overcome those obstacles. As long as there are no obstacles, nothing to cover or block, you will gradually be able to see the Dharmakaya.

Participating in the First Pillar is similar to seeing the Dharmakaya, which is not the truth. He (First Pillar Bodhisattva) understood clearly, but did not realize it. It is necessary to wait until we truly attain the First Stage, beyond the status of Tam Hien Bodhisattva. We are currently a mind of joy (joy). We must develop Bodhi mind, everyone must first develop Bodhi mind, generate that enlightened mind. Where does that enlightened mind come from? Still born from the Dharmakaya that we inherently have. Because of that enlightened mind, we gradually practice and practice. Training to reveal the inherent light, [that is] training allows the inherent light of the Dharmakaya to be revealed. Therefore, we must practice all good dharmas. At the same time, we must cultivate to become Buddhas and save sentient beings. We must have a physical body, which means achieving a good appearance. There is a Buddha of Retribution, there is a Buddha of Incarnation. The Incarnation comes from the Sambhogakaya. Practicing all good karma is the Sambhogakaya of Buddha, because the Sambhogakaya can harmonize with the Dharmakaya, it will be the three bodies of Dharma, Retribution, and Transformation. Now we are the Incarnation, that is, the karma of the Incarnation, not the merit of the Incarnation; but we transform the karma of the Avatara into the merits of the Avatara. The merit of the Incarnation comes from the Sambhogakaya. Therefore, now we develop the Bodhi mind and practice the Bodhisattva path, allowing us to successfully practice Dharmakaya Retribution.

(Sutra) Good man! Like the profound meaning of the ego, the decision is true, apart from the past, it is like knowing.

tom_tat: Lecture 16 1. How to use the Contemplation Wheel Friends! We have finished teaching the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma; But how to use [Contemplation of the Wheel] in the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma? How to reach the highest realm...
noi_dung:
Lecture 16

1. How to use Contemplation Wheel

Friends! We have finished teaching the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma; But how to use [Contemplation of the Wheel] in the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma? How can one reach the realm of One Truth? The first half of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra talks about Things; The latter part is all Ly, belonging to the Hoa Nghiem realm. This profound reason must be entered from Truth. We don't have such great wisdom, we can't understand it from Reason, we have to understand it from Facts. The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma has the most important relationship for us, because we have neither wisdom nor supernatural powers. Following the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, if we practice according to the method He said, we will all have miraculous powers. What magical powers do you have? You know what you did in your past life, whether it was good karma or bad karma, compare it with what you have to suffer in this life, and in this life you will enjoy the retribution of what you did in your previous life. In the future, if you give up this body and life, what retribution will you suffer in the future? That is called “three generations of cause and effect”. But we do not have that kind of magical power, so we rely on the magical power taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. That is the main content of the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. According to theory, the second half of this sutra is the meaning of the Avatamsaka Sutra. Reason must use Truth in the previous section to reveal.

Everyone knows that Contemplation Wheel is a special method of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. This sutra was initiated by the great master Nguoi Ich of the Ming Dynasty. Great Master Nguu Ich wanted to attain pure Bhikkhu ordination. Throughout Nam Diem Phu De, he wanted to invite five pure Bhikkhus, but there were none! He wished to find the Dharma, from the Tripitaka, he saw this Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma. According to the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, one must make a rotating appearance. That is based on the desired number [sown by the wheel to know the result]. Great Master Ich did not know how to make a wheel, there was no way. He wrote on paper [corresponding numbers], used the drawing of lots, saw which lot he drew and then calculated according to that card. Use that method to solve the problem. Due to this problem, [the practice of Contemplation] cannot spread, there is no way! Until the time of Master Hoang Nhat, old Master Hoang Nhat studied the art. He wished to continue to promote the virtues and merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, so based on the repentance dharma compiled by Master Nguu Ich, according to the original text of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra to create the Contemplation Wheel. Now I can present that set of generals.

There are nineteen in total. The first group consists of ten, explaining the three karmas of the body (killing, stealing, lust), the four karmas of the mouth (lying, embellishing, double-talking, harsh speech), and the three karmas of the mind (greed, anger, ignorance). Those are the ten cycles. The second group includes three wheels. In it, it is divided into three lives: past, present, and future. The past has three karmas of body, mouth, and mind of the past, the present has three karmas of body, mouth, and mind of the present, and in the future there are three karmas of body, mouth, and mind of the future. Those are three wheels. The karma in your body, mouth, and mind is heavy [represented] by the color black, [represented by a line] deep and large. Even though there is evil karma, the karma is small [represented on the wheel of appearance by] light and small lines. That is to divide [karma in] body, mouth, and mind into heavy and light. In real life, we must understand our own lives in the present. Why are some of our careers unsuccessful? Or is there any obstacle to cultivating the Way? Then you use the Contemplation Sat Luan to observe and see where the shortcomings are? After that, follow the teachings of Master Ngai Ich. He commented and explained based on the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. There are nineteen forms of the wheel, why are there nineteen wheels? Our three karma of body, mouth, and mind, plus basic ignorance, make ten. For the three lives of past, present, and future, use these three wheels specifically to sow for the past, present, and future. The third group includes six wheels, representing body, speech, and mind in the present life. Because from the three karmas of greed, anger, and ignorance, there will be ten karmas, each with a past life, present life, and future life, so this type of wheel has three groups, a total of nineteen.

Shaman Hoang Nhat knows how to make reincarnations. The current Luan Generals are all [modeled after] the fabrication methods of shaman Hoang Nhat. He followed the teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma regarding size and specifications, and based on that standard to do it. Those three types of wheels originally came from the scriptures, and the magician Hoang Nhat created these three types of wheels. The nineteen chakras arise from the karma of our body, mouth, and mind. There are nineteen in total, divided into three groups. But when making a wood wheel, the wood must be sandalwood. Actually there is no [that type of wood], you use another type of wood to replace it, preferably fragrant wood, to show the meaning of respect. Nineteen [fold appearances], divided into three groups. The size should not be less than one inch, the middle should be carved into a cube shape, the two ends of the flap gradually become smaller. That is the teaching in the sutra.

The reason the wooden wheel for contemplation is called Luan is because of the meaning “the wheel of dharma is constantly turning”. That wheel [is made] so that when you sow, you will sow easily. Hold the shake in your hand and you can turn it, like a wheel. Luan has the meaning “moving”, so it is called Luan, the dharma manifestation [of the rotation form] is “permanently moving dharma wheel”, meaning “everlasting without stopping”. [Luan] has the meaning “transform”, that is, “destroy our afflictions”. Our afflictions do not stop, that wheel crushes and cuts off our afflictions and habits. Suppose we have doubts and cannot decide, [for example] cannot decide on the method of practice. For example, early this morning, we woke up and felt uncomfortable in our hearts. It seems that today is very unfavorable, so you immediately sow the Contemplation Wheel and then leave. Luan General can tell you: What is the right path? What is evil? You can do it, or you can't do it. You can use [wood wheel] to ask for advice on every matter. When you use the Contemplation Wheel, both hands join together [to shake the wheel signs] to sow, then raise your hand and drop the wheel to one side. [The main scriptures] say “throw one's hand, bow down” (, raise one's hand, sow to the side) means sowing like that, has the meaning of [describing] the action. When using Chiem Sat Luan, use a clean cloth and use your hands to sow [the Luan General on it].

The first type of wood wheel consists of ten, [corresponding to] ten karma. The number Ten represents each karma of body, mouth, and mind: three karma of body, four mouth karma, three karma of mind, i.e. greed, anger, ignorance, killing, stealing, lust, lying, embellishing words, double talk, and harsh talk. Those are ten wheels, on each wheel is written [each of the ten karma], that is, double talk, harsh talk, greed, anger, ignorance... representing the ten karmas. When you sow the karma wheel of the first group, in your past life, what karma you ended up creating, you don't know clearly, so use those ten wheels to contemplate. [The middle part] has four sides, two sides [facing each other] have words, two sides are blank. “Leave blank” means that for that karma, you have neither light karma nor heavy karma, neither heavy nor visible. Those two sides of the wood wheel manifest without [that karma]. Regarding that karma, you are neither good nor evil, that is, neutral. The blank side represents no sign. The other two sides are opposite each other, one side is good, the other side is evil. Everyone can refer to the drawing printed by Phuong Quang[39], and follow that drawing to engrave. That painting was drawn by shaman Hoang Nhat. We follow the original to do it.

The second group of wheels, the second type of wood wheel, consists of three. Those three appearances represent whether the karma you created in the past was strong or weak, whether the karma you created was heavy or light. [The engraved line is] black, indicating that you have created very heavy karma. The red [engraved line] represents that you not only have no evil, but also have good. Red [corresponds to goodness], great goodness is represented by a very long red line; Tieu thien is a very short red line. It is in contrast to evil karma, evil is represented by black, while good is red. There are two sides without any number, which means there is no good, no evil, that is, indeterminate.

The first type of wheel form includes ten, the second type includes three, the third type includes six. In the third type, three sides have numbers written on them, one side has no numbers and is blank. But it is necessary to roll three times, the total of those numbers can be up to one hundred eighty-nine. Where does the number one hundred and eighty-nine come from? Retribution in three lifetimes, including one hundred and eighty-nine different types of good and evil. Why do we have to roll three times? Because once will not be enough. Three rolls add up to a total of [maximum] one hundred and eighty-nine. If you roll three times and no numbers appear, all are empty, showing that you have attained sainthood, have achieved success, and are pure. But this is very difficult, there are so many numbers but no number can be rolled. If you plant three times, there will be no number, which means you are pure and have attained Arhatship, but the Three Fruits saints have not yet achieved it (that is, you cannot cast all three times, all six wheels have no number).

If we want to practice contemplation of the wood wheel, it's not like we take the [wood wheel] and then sow it, we won't get it! When you want to use the Contemplation Wheel, when you practice, the desired purpose for us to use the Contemplation Wheel will all turn into pure form. Then you worship every day. If you practice for three years and the pure wheel form still does not appear, then Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will specially bless you. Due to your blessings, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will appear. But you must pray for three years, without stopping for a single day, praying to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to bless you. After three years, the pure wheel form still does not appear; At that time, you can just recite the holy name! Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will teach you. That's what the scriptures say, it's not me!

In the practice method, if you wish for the purity of the wheel, immediately contemplate it. [Contemplating the wheel form] belongs to the first group, the second group, and the third group to verify whether you are pure or not? That wheel will appear as pure or impure; When the universal form appears, you will understand clearly. If you want to use the pure wheel form, there is a sadhana. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva laid down the sadhana, and the places to practice were added by Master Nguich Ich. At the place of practice, you place the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Dear friends who want to practice the Contemplative Repentance Dharma, you should display a statue of Ksitigarbha, sincerely and earnestly, in front of the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to worship and make offerings. Make offerings according to your ability to manage. If you can't even worry about offering anything, then just use your mind to offer it! In your mind, you create the intention to make offerings, visualize incense, visualize flowers, visualize offerings. That is making offerings with thoughts.
