Answer: "In the Contemplation of Karma Sutra, volume Lower, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said to rely on the realm of One Truth to cultivate faith and understanding. If you are a person with good faculties, you should learn the contemplation of Truth and Reality. Those with dull faculties must first learn Mind-Only Contemplation, through Contemplation of Consciousness-Only, attain Samadhi of Form and Truth. Next, you should learn faith in contemplation. the mind with Xa Ma Tha and the way to contemplate the mind with Bhikkhu Pāsāna”. This passage you quote from the scriptures. "If that person has weak good karma, a mind of doubt and fear, at all times and in all places, he should often chant my name." That is the original teachings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Your doubts are too heavy, can repentance be successful? Do not believe in anything, even though you have studied Buddhism, your faith is not complete. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said you can't do anything else, it's best to recite His name. That is speaking to weak and fearful sentient beings. So do you do that or not? Please copy the scriptures and ask me. When I preach, you have already heard it. [Question] Contemplating Truth as It Really Is, Xa Ma Tha contemplates the mind, contemplates the Dharma Bodies of the Buddhas; Do these contemplations and their contents have a different order of depth and shallowness? Please review the Karma Contemplation Sutra, I told you a long time ago, I won't repeat it again!

* Question: 1) How to pray for liberation in a world of hardship?

2) When meditating, my legs immediately felt numb, the time was almost the same each time, so I wanted to stretch my legs out and stop meditating. During this period, there is no way for you to progress. Dear Venerable, I encounter such a deadlock, what should I do?

Answer: How to pray for liberation in a world of hardship? You are sentient beings in the world, wishing for liberation. When we preached the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, we said: "If you recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, bow to Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, you will be able to be liberated." If you sit still and your legs feel numb and you don't want to continue sitting, then you don't sit. Sometimes when I sat down I thought, "I should take a break because of this, there is no progress at this stage," and asked the old monk, "I have encountered such a problem, what should I do?" Even though you have not practiced, you have reached an impasse? When people reach a certain level of practice, they cannot progress to higher levels. As for you, even if you can't sit, you can't sit, you can't stand, you can't sit well, you can't meditate successfully, please calm your mind well. Your mind is not placed on the dharma, nor placed on the path, which means you have not yet entered the mind of faith. Get close to your fellow Buddhist monks, either at the temple you often go to, or the master you take refuge in, asking them to explain to you.

* Question: 1) When listening to the Dharma hearing sutra, it is easy to fall asleep, often like that. What fate is that, please? How to treat?

2) When sitting still, no thoughts arise, but images and sounds from the past still surface, what to do? What is the cause?

Answer: [Friend asked] "Whenever I listen to sutras or dharma, I will often fall asleep; what is the cause of that?" It's not due to any cause or condition, [it's due to] laziness and laziness. When you come here to listen to the sutra, you must develop faith, have a mind of liking, have a mind of leaving suffering, and be happy. If you want to pray for benefits, promotion, and fortune in society, you still have to have the mind to gain rank and fortune to be able to pray! There was once a Dharma friend who said, "I hope to get promoted, is reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva spiritual or not?" I said "so spiritual! Quite so spiritual". Getting rich is also spiritual, depends on how you recite? How to chant? Recite sincerely and urgently. Until you sincerely and earnestly recite to a certain level, you don't expect to get rich, don't expect to get rich but still get rich, like that! When meditating, I have no thoughts, but I hear sounds rising up, what do I do? Even the mind that meditates, the mind that wants to practice, you don't put your mind there, how can you meditate calmly! Do you have any idea why? You are quick and superficial. Whatever we do, we must first understand how to do it. You want to practice, in other words, why you practice, first of all, is because you have a wish, not blind. If you don't even have the will, your mind is confused so you meditate, what's the point of sitting still? “What is the purpose of meditation?” First of all, you must determine your purpose. Sitting still, we study with the hope of entering the path, causing our mind to stop being restless and agitated and become pure. Why? Only by being still is there wisdom. When you see the water rolling, there is nothing there. If the water is pure, you come and shine into the water, and your shadow will immediately appear. Please understand that meaning! Therefore, if you want to practice, first of all, you must quiet your mind. How to do it? You ask me how to do it, I immediately tell you: Calm down, let go of everything for an hour or half an hour. You meditate for half an hour, gradually increasing it more and more, until you decide to gain benefits from sitting still, so you practice longer. In general, there must be a purpose, no matter what you do, you must have a purpose, a goal. You're confused, you don't even have a goal, so why sit still? Why sit still? Too tired, sit down and rest!

* Question: Last year, the disciple had periodontal disease[40] (only one tooth was sick). Last year, due to fatigue, the muscles in my thighs became inflamed, all of which were not life-threatening illnesses, but have still not completely cured. Something bad happened like that, even though I went to see a doctor, there was still no way to cure it. Was it discovered by karma? Should I diligently repent or not? If you chant repentance sutras but still don't see any positive changes, is it because your efforts are not enough?

Answer: Last year, you had periodontal disease; Last year, my thigh got infected, but it wasn't a fatal illness. Even though it's not life-threatening, it's not good, it's so persistent that you have to go to the doctor and seek treatment. [You wonder] is it bad karma or not? You asked me, I tell you, you are right! That's called karma of discovery, it's true karma. Yet you chant sutras and repent, but don't see any good changes, because the practice doesn't come. Why is chanting sutras and repentance still not good? You are not a true chanter, your heart is not sincere, and the effect is not great. You have to control your mind in one place until you chant the sutras to the point where you forget all your illnesses, everything is gone, the effect will be good. Also, if you value this body very much, if you disregard chanting sutras, worshiping, reciting the Buddha's name, it will absolutely be forever useless! If you attach great importance to chanting and repentance, considering it more important than your body and life, your illness will absolutely get better. Let's talk both ways, that's what it means. That's right, you yourself said "your efforts are not enough", you don't need to ask me about this, just try your best. With enough effort, no disease or illness will be cured!

* Question: Both the Energy and So are lost, how can we meditate on the Energy that is also Emptiness? Furthermore, the Thien Thai sect talks about two levels: Nang and So. How should we explain? How is the word “nanh fortune” in “ren fortune present” explained?

Answer: First of all, you must clearly understand Nang and So. What energy is, is our power of contemplation. Nang Quan Quan Quan Quan. What is So Quan? Emperor! No, Gia, Trung are called Tam Quan. The True Truth, the Conventional Truth, and the Middle Truth are the Three Truths. Three Emperors and Three Quans. Contemplation is like us tapping on the head of a mallet, and Truth is like tapping on the handle of a mallet. The base is the handle. Emptiness then has the principle of Emptiness, speaking according to reason, that is Truth (truth, truth), [i.e. Emptiness Truth]. Jia then had Jia's morality, called Jia Emperor. Madhyamaka has the doctrine of Madhyamaka, called the Middle Truth. The Contemplation of Emptiness, Falsehood, and the Middle Three Contemplations correspond to the Contemplation of True Contemplation and Contemplation of Falsehood, that is, the Contemplation of Absolute Emptiness and Contemplation, the Contemplation of Unobstructed Reasons, and the Contemplation of Continuity and Consciousness. Tam Chi and Tam Quan are learning the teachings and meanings. The person who can ask about this issue is definitely a magician, because ordinary Dharma friends will not be able to think about this issue. The Three Contemplations and the Three Truths are all about wisdom, wisdom is the basis, wisdom is attainment, wisdom is discrimination. Wisdom illuminates Reason, wisdom illuminates Facts. In matters, everything is different, everything is a wisdom solution. In Ly, that is not the case; Where Ly is Wisdom, Tri is projection. Wisdom is illumination, like the sun illuminating the earth. The sun does not discriminate, nor is it biased, but depends on the person receiving the sun's light. If you are indoors, can the sun shine on you? You are the one who receives obstacles, but the sun shines everywhere. The True Truth: In reality, everyone is ready and equal, but you yourself have obstacles and karma. Once karma is eliminated, there will be no [obstacles]. The Three Contemplations are Energy, that is, what can contemplate the Truth, and Reason is what is contemplated. It's a pair of Nang - So. Among the four teachings (Tien Thai sect) are Emptiness, Falsehood, and Middle Ways, and among the five teachings (Hoa Yan sect) are Absolute Emptiness, Unobstructed Reasoning, and Continuity of Continuity. You use the Nang Quan position to manage the contemplation. The ability to manifest Reason; On the contrary, Reason can achieve Truth. But Reason and Truth are unobstructed, Reason can achieve Truth, Truth can reveal Reason, that is called Reason without Obstacle. This realm pervades all places, all times, contains everything, is completely nature, truly reaches one mind. One side is the ordinary person, the other side is the saint. At first, when practicing Contemplation, use Contemplation to reflect on the truth. Of course, right now we are all ordinary people, but we can practice. The first thing is that we contemplate that things in the world are impermanent, recognizing that they are impermanent. Impermanence is clearly Emptiness, all dharmas are in Emptiness. Even though it has form, it is all ultimately empty. In the future, definitely return to No. Your wisdom contemplates that all dharmas are Emptiness, without attachment.

But at first, while you contemplate, when you recognize the dharma, it has no true appearance, it is all false. Because it is fake, so you can know that it is ultimately Emptiness, from within Emptiness appears the image, it is not the truth, it is very fake. One side yes, one side no. In that existence and non-existence, there is the Middle Truth. When speaking according to Ly, the Middle Truth depends on conditions, which are also conditions according to Emptiness, but also conditions according to Falsehood. That is Tam Quan. But there is a wisdom that can understand things. That's called Nang. Having that wisdom is because each of our Dharma friends, because of the Buddha's teachings, was immediately born with wisdom. That wisdom is not ours, but is due to our application of teachings from the scriptures. The Buddha taught us, but we can use it to regularly practice and unite our minds with the Buddha. The ability to meditate with wisdom can produce effective results, by contemplating the scene being contemplated, for all scenes, one can realize that they are false, knowing that all dharmas are false, and the fate follows sentient beings. That's called contingent meaning. “Truth” means “inherently sufficient”, neither deviating from the Middle nor from the False; That's called the Middle Emperor. The Thien Thai sect talks about the Three Noble Truths, the Three Contemplations, the Middle Emptiness, the Three Contemplations of the True Truth, the False Truth and the Middle Truth.

* Question: Buddha is two thousand five hundred years away from us. Since the Buddha said that so many sutras are all Dharma, then what is the definition of Dharma?

Answer: What is Dharma? What is evil? How to distinguish between evil and right? Away from the mind, away from the minds of sentient beings, away from the minds of Buddhas, all dharmas outside the mind are all evil! Saying "all dharmas arise from the mind, all dharmas follow the mind to cease", in general all dharmas return to the mind; That is the Mahayana teachings. Anything that has form or form because of the mind will not be real at all. Why did the Buddha say all the precepts? You receive the Three Refuges, the Three Refuges are also precepts. Taking refuge in Buddha, you cannot take refuge in evil spirits or pagans. Take refuge in the Dharma, do not take refuge in false doctrines. All evil doctrines, down to the world's writings, are evil. The two paths, right and wrong, both arise from the mind, "when the mind arises, all kinds of dharmas arise, when the mind ceases, all kinds of dharmas cease". Why are the scriptures the true Dharma? It arises from the mind. You must learn the Dharma and return to your mind. It's not that outside the mind there is dharma, outside the mind there is no dharma. The dharmas are the mind; That's Chanh. Holding on to the dharma outside the mind is called evil. Outside of mind there is no dharma, how do you distinguish? Saying "when the dharma is completed by cause and effect, there is no dharma that is not complete": That person is a person who has a complete base, a complete base sees all dharmas arising due to causes and conditions, all dharmas are destroyed by causes and conditions. Everything that understands causes and conditions is called the Dharma. If you leave your cause and condition, it will be all fake and evil. Cause and effect is Emptiness, so the Buddha said "cause and condition give birth to dharma, self theory means Emptiness, the name of the Middle Way, the name of the Middle Way, the name of the false name" (the dharma born of causes and conditions, we say is Emptiness, also called the meaning of the Middle Way, also called false name). Those are all fake names, not genuine. But it displays the meaning of the Middle Way, so “her name is the meaning of the Middle Way, her name is a fake name”. That is the Dharma. Great Patriarch Li teaches us "to complete the Dharma, there is no Dharma that cannot be completed". The same goes for magicians who study dharma. They study the scriptures and understand the ultimate meaning, seeing that all dharmas are complete, they are dharmas born of causes and conditions, depending on the complete meaning to arise, there is no dharma that is not complete. Relying on the clear meaning to attain all dharmas. All dharmas have the ultimate meaning.

noi_dung:
Lecture 18

Compassionate Bodhisattvas! Compassionate friends! Everyone who has the intention to come to this Dharma assembly is a Bodhisattva, developing the Bodhi mind and practicing the Bodhisattva path. Originally, while I was preaching the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, a Dharma friend asked to teach the Three Refuges; Today is the time we have set to transmit the Tam Quy. But the Dharma friends who receive the Three Refuges hope that before imparting the Three Refuges to the Dharma friends, I will explain it to everyone. Simply discuss a little about the mind, just say a few sentences! I also satisfied everyone's wishes. I didn't expect today's Dharma conference to be so great, with so many Dharma friends participating!

Among the Buddhist disciples, currently everyone is a Buddhist disciple. In our present life, in this situation, in this form, we ourselves feel that it is not good, accidents often happen. We Buddhist disciples pray to the Buddha and Bodhisattva family, what should we do to contribute to all sentient beings suffering in the present time? “Dedication” means to suffer and suffer on behalf of everyone. I just called everyone a Bodhisattva. Bodhisattva is the great path of sentient beings. The Indian language is Bodhisattva Bodhisattva, translated into Chinese as Enlightened Friendship, making all sentient beings who are suffering and suffering happy and peaceful. First of all, Buddhist disciples should develop Bodhicitta, making them free from suffering and misfortune. We all rely on Buddha's teachings, Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us: For all disasters, during the time of Dharma Ending suffering, disasters often occur, how to save them? In the Pure Conduct chapter of the Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra, Manjushri Bodhisattva taught “skillful use of the mind”. Today I want to tell everyone about “skillful use of the mind”.

We Buddhist disciples all understand “mind gives birth to all dharmas, all dharmas are mind-only”. In today's life, where do the sufferings that you see, hear, and even think about come from? Do it yourself, bear it yourself! You yourself create the karma, you yourself bear the consequences. Currently, the biggest problem facing us is economic; The economic problem is to do it yourself and bear it yourself. I won't explain this in detail, I'm not an economist, I'm just talking based on the Buddhist law of cause and effect. People say "Good will be rewarded with good, evil will be rewarded with evil. If you don't report, it's not yet time!" Wherever heavy karma is created, the people there will suffer heavy consequences. Taiwanese friends can ponder for a moment, what are you pondering? Compare a bit. How to compare? Think about it on this earth, currently the most difficult place to make a living is not Taiwan. Other places like Europe, America, Africa, and Australia are all more serious than Asia. Compared to Asia, Taiwan is not serious. After all, we are suffering because of economic stagnation. We Buddhist disciples should pray to Buddha and Bodhisattva for blessings to change this type of situation.

How should we do it? Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us to “use the mind wisely”. Because the nature of disasters is entirely created by the minds of sentient beings. Because from the mind, it arises in the body and mouth, that is, greed, anger, and delusion in the mind arise into killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying in the body, and lying, embellishing words, double-talking, speaking harsh words in the mouth, which are the Ten Evils. The Ten Evil Karmas cover the entire earth. No matter where you go! Currently, in this Dharma conference, I feel that all Dharma friends are good-natured and have developed Bodhi mind. Even though we ourselves do not personally suffer, but when we see living beings suffer personally, we should consider the suffering of living beings as if we ourselves were suffering. Therefore, we study Bodhisattva Manjushri in the Pure Conduct chapter of the Great Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra. He teaches us to transform evil thoughts and evil deeds, to cultivate a pure mind and pure conduct. He taught us four words, covering the Pure Conduct chapter, which can also be said to cover the entire Mahayana Buddha Avatamsaka Sutra. What four words? “Use your mind skillfully”. Our mind is constantly active, constantly thinking, constantly thinking. You must guide your mind to use it well, first of all, transform yourself, then transform the people around you. At the same time, release that power into the four seas, causing it to generate a certain power. In the Pure Conduct chapter, Wisdom Hand Bodhisattva asks about one hundred and ten virtues, which include the misfortunes that sentient beings are suffering in the present, not only economic, but also killing, stealing, prostitution, and lying. If we want to eliminate all the minds that cause those accidents, what should we do to be able to eliminate those accidents? Bodhisattva Manjushri taught “use your mind skillfully”. The method to use skillfully is that in daily life, in thought and thinking, one must always have no separation from the Three Jewels, that is, [not separate from] Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, depending on the pure blessings of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, to transform all phenomena in society.

Therefore, Buddhist scriptures teach "when the mind arises, all dharmas arise, when the mind ceases, all dharmas perish". The mind gives birth to dharmas. Now in this association there are two or three thousand Dharma friends, each of you transforms ten people, those ten people in turn transform ten other people, the transformation power will be very great. Dharmas are born from the mind, dharmas are destroyed by the mind, such as people often talk about the word Greed. “Using your mind wisely” means saying you are not greedy. If there was no greed, all the resources to feed people in the current world would not be a problem. The four seasons of rain and wind nourish sentient beings, and the earth produces food to nourish sentient beings, but there are evil people who interfere, making it impossible to spread [food, other items necessary for life]. This place has no food, that place has countless piles of food. How to explain the problem of hunger? There are accidents that seem to be natural or man-made disasters; Actually, natural disasters are man-made. If humans did not create karma, there would be no disasters in heaven and earth. People in this place create very bad karma, heaven will bring disaster. We Buddhist disciples completely understand this principle: "Whatever karma you create will have its consequences." Suppose we can make everyone use their mind skillfully and not create karma.

Does not create bad karma, purely good karma. If you use your mind like that, heaven will reward you well, and good intentions will surely bring good rewards. Unfortunately, nowadays, such minds are too few, do you want to find them? Can only be found among Buddha's disciples! If you don't believe it, look around you, look at the city you live in, even a little bigger, expanding to this province of yours, until expanding to the whole of Taiwan. Anyone who is good at using a large mind can use the mind of enlightenment. In the above section, I called everyone a Bodhisattva. Bodhisattvas will practice the Bodhisattva path and give all happiness to the people. The Bodhisattva personally shouldered all disasters, which means his mind is great, and is called the Great Tao Mind of Living Beings. Assuming everyone in Taiwan can do the same, more than 20,000 of us will transform several billion people around the world, everyone will be good, the world will have no more disasters.

Unfortunately, this cannot be done. Why? Even for ourselves and this country of Taiwan, towards the people here, we still cannot make everyone turn towards goodness. How can we change the world? At the same time, each Dharma friend hopes that his six relatives, the people you know, the people you have come into contact with, will make them practice the Ten Virtuous Karmas. Can it be done or not? From that mind, we try our best to work with the living beings around us, to make them skillfully use their minds, to use our minds to do things that benefit others. That is called “Bodhisattva practice”, making our minds often think about creating happiness for others. In the scriptures, there are many teachings like that, our Buddhist disciples all know, "not for our own peace, but only for sentient beings to be happy", I think every Buddhist friend knows how to say that. But that is not just talk, it must be done, done with reality. Surely there are Dharma friends wondering "can we do it or not?" Making the entire world turn into [purely practicing the Ten Virtuous Karmas] is impossible, but you can do a little bit from the people around you, and it will have a widespread effect. For example, if we throw a stone into the sea, the water will ripple and spread in circles, the farther it spreads, the bigger it spreads. This means being able to influence understanding. You can make your own mind often think like that. That is called "skillful use of the mind", "the Bodhisattva path". Until then, you will skillfully use your mind to advance until you become a Buddha.

If explained carefully, “skillfully using the mind” includes the Four Immeasurable Minds “love, compassion, joy, equanimity”. If expanded, it would be almsgiving, morality, patience, and meditation. The six degrees and ten thousand actions that you perform all come from the mind, the mind gives birth to all dharmas. If in our current association there are two or three thousand people without greed, anger, or ignorance, each of us would influence ten people, or twenty people, without expecting too much! How many thousands of people will we affect with two thousand people? We take turns spreading outward, using that mind to influence others, the more influence we have, the greater. The power from that mind arises again, causing [karmas] in the body and mouth, such as for killing, stealing, sexual misconduct in the body, lying, embellishing words, double-talking, and harsh words in the mouth, there is an additional word No, that is, do not lie, do not embellish words, do not say harsh words, do not speak double-minded, do not give rise to thoughts of greed, anger, ignorance, do not commit murder, theft, or prostitution. That is called Thap Thien. If the influence spreads, all the friends in Taiwan can influence more than two million people. More than two million people will affect thirteen billion people on the Mainland. Expanding a bit further, thirteen million people could cover the entire world. The world's population is still very small. Buddhist scriptures say “countless billions”, so that number (thirteen billion people) is still a small number. Using the mind that way is called "skillful use of the mind". That is one way, using all kinds of application methods, all of which are the Ten Good Karmas.

The Ten Virtuous Karmas are the basis for practicing the Bodhisattva path. The Ten Good Karmas practice the Bodhisattva path; You use your mind of immeasurable compassion to act. Act with a mind of immeasurable kindness, immeasurable joy, and immeasurable renunciation; put together, it means “skillful use of the mind”. Friends who practice the Bodhisattva path do not sit in the Buddhist hall and recite a few sutras, or meditate dozens of times there, practice visualization, and enter Zen. Bodhisattva is not like that. A Bodhisattva takes all sentient beings as the basis for practicing the Bodhisattva path in every thought. He does not think about himself, and in every thought he does not leave sentient beings. Lay friends, when you recite sutras in your own Buddha hall, due to the power of visualization, you can visualize the people around you, up to visualizing the village, town, and district where you live, until expanding into a province. Depending on how big your mind force has reached, you will be able to use that big mind force and then diffuse your mind that much. You diffuse your mind power to the whole world, this world will have an immeasurable influence on other worlds. Believe it or not? It's the truth. Why does everyone who recites the Amitabha Sutra recite Amitābha Buddha? Amitābha Buddha is quite far from this world of ours. Between the Sa Ba world and the Pure Land world, there are countless worlds, each world has countless sentient beings. The World of Ultimate Bliss affects us. In a sense, as long as our Dharma friends make a sincere heart, you make an earnest vow, a sincere heart, a sincere wish, and it will come true.

Because our mind has a lot of Or (obstacles of afflictions), you still cannot believe in very deep principles. I have asked many Dharma friends, I said: "You are the future Buddha." They glared, protested, criticized me for talking nonsense, scolded me for saying bad things about them! Obviously I praise them, sincerity is like that. Until we preached the Sutra on Contemplating Good and Evil Karma, people thought that the Sutra on Contemplating Good and Evil Karma was Hinayana. Now I'm teaching the second half of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, everyone please listen a little, it's called the "mind-ground method". You can use your mind skillfully, "skillful use" is "knowing how to use". You use [your mind] a little bigger. At all times, in every thought, think about the happiness of all sentient beings, without thinking about yourself. What is Bodhisattva? The great path of sentient beings. When you use this mind skillfully, when you use this mind like that, you will attain supernatural powers. What is supernatural power? I think all Dharma friends hope to gain magical powers. What is “divine”? It's the mind! The natural mind. Each of our Dharma friends has a complete mind, a very large mind, but unfortunately we don't use it, we are completely lost! “Spirit” is mind, “understanding” is nature. “God” is called “heavenly mind”, that is, the natural mind that you inherently have. “Understanding” is called wisdom nature. “Wisdom” is the mind that naturally gives rise to immeasurable wisdom, wisdom that can solve everything, so it is called “magic power”. The true nature of your mind, wisdom, and nature are inherently available, called “mind nature”. Mind nature is magical power. Because now we don't have enough strength to practice, our strength is not that great, you practice even more, saying I hope to save sixty-seven billion people in the world, making them all happy. Every day you recite sutras, meditate quietly, think like that, think about others and all sentient beings. This meaning belongs to the meaning in Avatamsaka, it's not because of what Dharma you want to attain, what Hue you hope to attain, what achievement you hope to achieve, it's not all, but what is it? Make all sentient beings achieve success, without thinking about yourself. Therefore, the great path of Bodhisattva mind is like that. That is the highest realm. From now on, please use your mind wisely.

We say a little limit, when you do something good, when you finish it, bring the good merit from doing it, don't be attached to it, don't be attached, dedicate it to sentient beings, making them happy. Of course, the heart of dedication to all humanity and all sentient beings cannot be achieved immediately! First of all, let's start with the six relatives around us. When they have an accident, you vow to accept it for them. If you don't have that power, recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra to have the Ksitigarbha Sutra give you that power, or recite Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to have Samantabhadra Bodhisattva bless you with that power. When reciting the Universal Gate chapter, you can recite any sutra at your discretion, but you must recite it truthfully. I say “true recitation”, perhaps people are skeptical. It is not necessary to recite according to the text, you must pay special attention: The mouth recites, the mind must think. Don't recite it like you're reciting the cards. Every day you recite it slowly, every day you recite it by heart, but don't pay attention to it. When reciting sutras, while reciting and doing other things, your mind is thinking about other things, but your mouth is still reciting the sutras, the effect will not be great! When you recite any sutra, your mind is transformed by the sutra. I say “skillfully use your mind”, meaning your mind and the sutra you are reciting are the same. When reciting Avalokiteśvara Universal Door, the mind is like the mind of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. When reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the mind is like the mind of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. While you recite, your mind really enters, in the dream the signs of the realm appear. Don't tell others! You can only know for yourself, you can't tell others. No matter what sutra you pray for, if it has been blessed, you should not spread it out. This is not something to propagate, but for you to enjoy for yourself. Because you don't know the strength of the other person, nor do you know the good karma and good roots of the other person, you're afraid that speaking out will have the effect of making people not believe you, or they will even scold you for using false doctrine to mislead others. It's best if you cherish it in your mind, making it bigger and bigger. When you have been reciting a sutra for a long time, your true mind and reciting mind merge with the sutra into one entity, and it will give birth to an effective result. You do not pray for the end of birth and death, but your life and death end for yourself! You don't pray to avoid disaster, but disaster is naturally avoided!

“Smart use of the mind” has reached a deep level, now everyone should try using it a little. How to use? Separate mind and body; The mind is not the body, the body is not the mind. This concept of ours is extremely serious. When body and mind become one, we are ordinary people. If you can separate your mind and body, you will gradually enter the holy realm. When you first use it, it won't have any great effect for a year or two. You use it for ten years, eight years, thirty years or fifty years, and it will produce results. As the Shurangama Sutra says: “A sentient being is united in enlightenment, an inanimate enlightenment is united in enlightenment”, that is, it teaches us: You have perception, feel something that is uncomfortable, if you are injured, it will hurt, but that pain does not affect the Knowing, pain does not affect that awareness. The pain does not reach the senses. The feeling of pain is the body, but the feeling is not painful. If each Dharma friend used this practice a little more, while you suffered as well, as did any problem arising in your body, at first of course the effect would not be great. Until you have used the practice for a long time and produced results, the pain is not you, not your mind, but your body, you can feel that pain cannot hurt your awareness. If you use your mind like that, you will truly achieve “skillful use of the mind”. Let's try to see if it can be done?

In society, we often hear that “spirit transforms matter”. Matter can also transform spirit, but it is often said like this: We see that spirit and matter are unrelated! I have a relative who likes to do business. One time, carrying a boat of goods to France, that man's mind was completely focused on the goods on that boat, because that was his entire property. That commodity has nothing to do with his mind, and it also has nothing to do with his body. When the goods [purchased after selling all the shipments to France] were shipped to China, suddenly the boat sank, all the goods were lost. He is only forty years old, not very old! As soon as he received the telegram, he picked up the telegram and looked at the content. Others saw him suddenly motionless. Look, he was dead! There is no illness at all! There are many stories like that in history. That is not skillful use of the mind, the mind is attached to material things. Our body is matter, mind is not matter. When a person dies, the body is destroyed, but the spirit (mind) does not die at all! It will change, depending on the heavy good karma or heavy bad karma, depending on what it turns into, it's not the same! It is matter transforming spirit, spirit transforming matter. It can transform each other, that is you "skillfully use your mind".

I say the main topic is “skillful use of the mind”, that is, when we practice in ordinary times, no matter what method you use, when you use effort, you should learn “skillful use of the mind”. Bodhisattva Manjushri uses those four words to teach us, how to make what we have done pure? It is the chapter on Pure Conduct, the chapter on Pure Conduct comes from the mind, you should use your mind wisely. You skillfully use your mind, turning your entire pure conduct into pure, pure mouth, pure body, pure thoughts, pure thoughts. From this pure Pure Hanh chapter, you take another step to cultivate the Pham Hanh level. The Avatamsaka Sutra has an order, and that order is extremely strict. If you don't have Pure Hanh Pham, but want to advance to higher levels and cultivate Pham Hanh, that is, jump levels, you won't be able to do it! This is different from other teachings. But once you achieve one thing, have entered a door, “one is everything, once accomplished, all is accomplished”. If you know how to use your mind skillfully, you will become a Buddha. What the Buddha's mind is like, you can judge according to the teachings: That mind is enlightenment, there is nothing unknown, nothing incomprehensible, no accident that cannot be avoided, but there must be conditions. Buddha said "people without fate are difficult to save", without fate they cannot be saved!

Based on this principle, if each of us Dharma friends wants to have a relationship with Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, we must first take refuge in the Three Jewels. That's the basics. If you have not yet received the Three Refuges, look at the Buddhist scriptures yourself and learn how to study them. You will learn very well. You will not be considered a Buddhist disciple. As Buddhist disciples, the minimum starting point is that you first take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Sangha. Usually we use the image of the Three Jewels, that is, when we see Buddha statues, scriptures, and monks, it is called the world of the Three Jewels. But when you contemplate, it will not be the world of the Three Jewels, separate from the world of the Three Jewels, until ultimately reaching the ultimate from faith in action, the Three Jewels are one: All sentient beings are Buddhas, all dharmas are mind, Buddha and Dharma in harmony are the Sangha Jewels. That is the one mind of the Three Jewels. The Three Jewels transmitted by me are the appearance of the Three Jewels, completely different. From the world of the Three Jewels, you reach the one mind of the Three Jewels, entering the purity of the Three Jewels. The Three Jewels are one mind.

In a moment, there will be friends who receive the Three Refuges. Taking refuge in the Three Refuges means taking refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the Three Jewels. After that, you should learn to use this mind skillfully, so that your mind can be used like the Buddha's mind, which is the Buddha's Jewel. Your mind and the Dharma taught by the Buddha are the same, that is, the Dharma Jewel. The mind is the Dharma, the Dharma is the mind. All dharmas are mind; The harmony of mind and dharma is entrusted to the body of the Sangha, that is, the Sangha Jewel. There is also your self-nature which is complete with the Three Jewels. The essence of your being is the Buddha Jewel. All applied knowledge is the Dharma Jewel, your body and form are the Sangha Jewel. But when we receive [the Three Refuges], we rely on others to receive them, rely on teachers to teach us, and receive the appearance of the Three Jewels. Based on the Buddha statue, and based on the Three Refuges precepts to live. Taking refuge in the Buddha, taking refuge in the precepts is the Dharma, the text of taking refuge is the Dharma Jewel, and the master who transmitted it is the Sangha Jewel. Depending on the nature of the Three Jewels, you can skillfully use this mind and turn it into the self of the Three Jewels. The Three Jewels are oneself, one's self is complete with the Three Jewels, so they are even more profound. But taking refuge you have to practice every day. No matter which sutra you recite, at first you must take refuge in the Three Jewels, proving that we take refuge in the Three Jewels not just once or twice, but countless times, at all times, with every recitation, we take refuge in the Three Jewels. This is not a comparison of the appearance of merit, nor is it a comparison of the appearance of benefits. What we ourselves have received and achieved are given as alms, to whom? Giving alms to sentient beings who do not receive the Three Refuges allows them to all be blessed by the Three Jewels and to take refuge in the Three Jewels. That is skillful use of the mind, but also a way to apply "skillful use of the mind". The “skillful use of the mind” method includes boundless [methods], depending on how you think.

I often ask disciples who do business, I say: Suppose the Three Jewels bless you, making your business certain to be profitable and gain benefits. Once achieved, what will be done? The correct answer is what do we achieve? The first idea is to make offerings to the Three Jewels. There are no big offerings, at least you will light a few incense sticks and make a few prostrations, or on the first day or full moon day, when you eat, think of Buddha and Bodhisattva. First make offerings to Buddha, then use it yourself. That's called "skillful use of the mind". The scope of “skillful use of the mind” is extremely vast. Every move, every thought you have to use will be supported by the dragon, blessed by the Three Jewels, and naturally auspicious. Every time I encounter a place where there is an accident, or a disaster of war, where there is a Dharma friend or a disciple who takes refuge with me, I will definitely call and ask. I said: "Are the Three Jewels disciples being harmed a lot? Please investigate and see." Then, they answered: "There are no disciples of the Three Jewels." Why do I explain this? I also want to prove how great the blessing power of the Three Jewels is! But this is bilateral, not unilateral. Although the sky is wide, it cannot penetrate rootless grass. Without roots, it cannot be blessed. Wherever there are many evil people, the evil karma is very heavy, there is very little rain. That is the truth, you can investigate and research for yourself. Nowadays, there are frequent accidents in society, no matter which country, unusual things happen. Unusual is not the same as normal, called "accident". There are places where there are basically no Buddhist disciples, no Three Jewels, all Dharma friends can explain this: There are quite a few Dharma friends around the world. In each place on earth, disasters happen one after another, and the Three Jewels' disciples are harmed quite a few. But after you have taken refuge in the Three Jewels, you must actually do it. The blessing is not a matter of peace, but a matter of attaining enlightenment.

Therefore, the sentence “skillfully uses the mind”, if separated for analysis, would be too much. Any thing is involved in whether you use your mind skillfully or not, how do you use your mind? I repeat again, what is the greatest “skillful use of the mind”? How can you be considered skillful in using your mind? You are all about making others happy, your thoughts are always thinking about how to make all sentient beings happy. This place is very poor, very impoverished, how can we make all those living beings happy, without accidents, without thinking about themselves? Only then is it truly “skillful use of the mind”. I ask the Buddha's disciples present, all the Buddha's disciples present here, to think of the suffering of all sentient beings, not to pray for peace for themselves! The same is true when you recite sutras, no matter what you do, think of all sentient beings who are suffering, think of all sentient beings who are in disaster. That is “skillful use of the mind”. Today I make offerings to everyone, I dedicate myself to everyone, I hope that all Dharma friends can use their minds wisely!

* The majestic spirit of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Like Hue Khanh

Indulgence[47] read the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, praising the Bodhisattva's merits in saving sentient beings. At ten o'clock, the boat started rowing. I immediately comforted and told the four merchants sitting on the boat not to be afraid, but to single-mindedly recite the Bodhisattva's holy name. I did not dare to set out because I was afraid of difficulties. Therefore, I discussed with a fellow participant: The next morning we started going up the mountain. The mountain road is winding, there is a meter of snow, there is no road recognition, the north wind is like a knife. Crossing several mountain ranges, the mountain road becomes more dangerous and bumpy, and the snow and ice become more slippery. All suffering was immediately relieved. Staggering, holding on, climbing over a mountain range, looking up at all four directions: Vast, endless white snow; The mountain ranges have no clear shape, only the high and low peaks can be seen. At that time, I had exhausted all my strength to walk for half a day. The fellow participant's hands and feet were cold, his face was bitten by the wind as if being stabbed by a knife, and he could no longer walk. We built a fire to warm ourselves, felt a little warm, so we continued on our way. As afternoon fell, the air turned cold and the wind and snow became more intense. The mountains were high, the road was slippery, gradually night fell, my whole body trembled, my teeth chattered. The mountains are high and low and winding, making it even more difficult to travel. Seeing a dim tower top in the distance ahead, knowing that the Bodhisattva's holy land was near, he was so happy that he forgot his fatigue, his steps were naturally light, and he reached the mountain. Coming to the mountain, we stopped at Quang Te Pagoda, not far from the stupa. That evening, he went to the court tower to worship and worship the Bodhisattva's golden body. Watching the tower all night, praising the Bodhisattva's merits like that, making wide and deep vows, made me plant five feet close to the ground, respectfully bowing four hundred times. Remember in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the World-Honored One proclaimed Bodhisattva to have an inconceivably great and compassionate power in the world of the ten directions, helping and protecting all sinful and suffering sentient beings. The Buddha's golden mouth spoke like that, making everyone extremely moved, crying, and worshiping without tiring. Early the next morning, we went to all the temples. Famous mountains and holy places all have highly virtuous monks who burn their fingers, burn their arms, light lamps, and make offerings in all kinds of ways. Hearing that style, no one could help but praise him. Unfortunately, after several years of war and chaos, pilgrims were few and far between, and temples were in ruins. There were also several famous pagodas such as Dong Nhai, Long Hoa, etc., which were all set on fire and destroyed by dwarf invaders. The crime of destroying temple towers, not being able to repent, destroying the family and losing the country, is not enough to atone for the crime!

Considering the Nine Flowers mountain area is the merit ashram of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, with ninety-nine peaks, towering, towering, very difficult to climb. Because the Bodhisattva vows to spread deeply and has great karma with living beings, in peaceful times, pilgrims are crowded, the whole road is black, as if walking on flat land. * Notes on the story of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva releasing light

Duong Dong To write

On the full moon day of the second month of the 33rd year of the Republic of China (1944), early in the morning, I went to My Lau's canopy to worship Buddha. Next, recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva a thousand verses. When he was about to chant the full number, he suddenly saw a bright light, as big as a bowl, shining brightly like a lamp, three meters to the left of the statue of Avalokiteśvara. At first, I suspected that someone was carrying a lantern across the yard, the light shining on the wall. But when I turned my head to look out the window, the moon had not yet risen, the yard was deserted, there were no passersby at all. Next, thinking that it must be a mistake in vision, he looked at that place, suddenly [the light] disappeared, and could no longer be seen. Then he returned to his original place, chanted the same name, and the light lit up again, a little higher than where he had appeared before. I just thought, that place worships a standing statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, which is a painting drawn by my younger brother Tri Phuong last year. Later, the tomb collection was printed out to give to people in the country to widely make offerings, so he was sure that the Bodhisattva was emitting light without any doubt. So last night [the Bodhisattva] emitted light, it was really the Bodhisattva who manifested his strangeness to solidify the faith of my brothers. Therefore, the whole family rejoiced and praised, believing that their parents' illness would definitely improve soon. Bodhisattva's kindness is truly memorable and deeply appreciated. The Original Vows Sutra teaches: "In the future, if there are good men and good women, the desires of the present, in the future, hundreds of thousands of millions of equal wishes, hundreds of thousands of millions of equal wishes, take refuge, contemplate, make offerings, praise the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Such wishes, all wishes will be accomplished" (If in the future life, there are good men and good women, who want hundreds of thousands of millions of wishes, hundreds of thousands of millions of things. In the present, you should only take refuge, worship, make offerings, and praise the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. All your wishes and prayers will be fulfilled. Anyone who encounters illness, disaster, or harm, if they can sincerely pay respect to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, they will be able to be protected and saved by the Bodhisattva. The merit and virtue of reverence is inconceivable, it can only be determined by people in the world. The next day of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's light release day in the second month of the year Giap Than (1944), disciple Duong To Dong in Nhu Cao, dharma name Nhan Sang Kinh Thuat.

* Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's majestic record

Phuong Duc Hue writes

In the spring of the 34th Republic year (1945), the enemy was raging, this unfilial person served his mother in Shanghai. The older sister's house is also in Hu (Shanghai), but the father is stuck in Tran Giang because of work. On the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month (ie the seventeenth day of the third lunar month), a telegram came from Tran Giang saying that his father suddenly became seriously ill. I discussed with my mother and sister, planning to go there and take care of her. Mom said the traffic wasn't convenient, the car rental was too expensive and hard to find, and there were bad people watching, pretending to be evil, and being a weak girl who shouldn't leave carelessly, so she couldn't go. Because he was worried about his elderly father, his heart was in turmoil. The next day, I went over to her house to discuss. Because it was already dark, she stayed and slept in the same room as her niece. In that area, the fire control was very strict. At ten o'clock at night, the electricity was cut off and one had to go to bed before ten o'clock. This ungrateful person was worried about his old father and couldn't sleep. The bedroom is on the third floor, there are windows front and back.

It was late at night, the moonlight shone brightly, while in contemplation, suddenly saw many people flocking to the house, standing outside the door of the house, only one person passed everyone in, clearly the old father. While I was in doubt, my father came and stood in front of the bed, mournfully calling out the first name of this ungrateful person, saying: "My life is over, I'm gone, do you know?" Right at that moment, my heart knew it was something unusual, because my father's face was very sad, I could only suppress the pain, reluctantly consoled him: "I already know, father, don't be sad. Life and death have a fate, the body of flesh and blood, no one can keep forever. Except for Buddha's power, there is no other method of liberation! Over the past few years, I have tried my best to advise you to recite Buddha's name precisely for today! Even though you have not listened, but because of that, I have made a vow to take refuge. Because of a good thought, it is not necessarily true. did not enjoy the benefits. Please finally listen." Father's face became even sadder and he said: "It's too late, I'm about to follow them." As he spoke, he raised his hand and pointed outside the house. People outside the house also poked their heads inside many times as if urging them. Father turned his head and said back to them: "Since you have allowed me to come here, please wait a moment. I have a few words to advise my daughter." He turned around and said to this unfilial person: "Hue child! I need you to recite Buddha's name to transcend and save the world. I deeply regret not listening to your advice every day." After speaking, he looked out again and said: "I will go now." Then patted this ungrateful person, saying: "Dad, I'm going! Remember, great salvation for you." After that, he calmly turned on his heels and left. Unfilial, he quickly asked his father if there was anything else he wanted to say? Father turned his head, looked at me and said: "Nothing more. Just remember that I am waiting for you to be blessed and saved." Father raised his hands to cover his face, seemingly hiding his tears. I'm so filial that I'm crying, I can't bear it anymore! Walking to the door, my father looked back again and said: "I'm waiting for you to overcome me and save me." Outside, among the group of people, there was a man holding a long object, like an iron chain, around his father. Seeing the filial piety from afar, he became impatient and raised his hand to stop: "That is my father. I believe in Buddhism and am confident that I can pray to the Buddha's power to absolve him of his sins. My father is determined not to stay too long in the dark place. He will use one month as a limit, vowing to transcend and save him. Please have mercy and be merciful, and your kindness will surely be rewarded." That person indeed withdrew his hand and instructed everyone to drag my father away. In a moment, all the generals disappeared. I tried calling the children, they were all sleeping soundly, not yet awake. Fortunately, what happened at that time did not alarm anyone.

Furthermore, my sister's husband has a shy personality, and she is conceited and not superstitious, so I kept [it] a secret and did not say anything. But knowing that my father must have passed away, I did not sleep all night, silently chanting Buddha's name. In the morning, return to school very early. My colleague gave me a telegram, saying it was sent last night. With tears streaming down my face, I knew my father had indeed passed away yesterday. Alas, what a pain! Starting from that day, I recited Buddha's name for my father. Although Duc Hue has taken refuge in Buddha for several years, he has never read the sutras and only knows how to uphold his name. Therefore, to pray for my father, I can only sincerely chant the names of Buddha and Bodhisattva, wholeheartedly bow and pray.

On the twenty-fifth of February, father passed away eight days ago. During the night, when I was just kneeling and chanting, I suddenly saw a beam of Buddha light, shining straight to the Northeast, stretching like a white silk sheet, and my father was kneeling in it. From then on, I chanted morning and night and saw that light. At first, I saw only my father worshiping in the light. Gradually, the light shone farther and farther, and more and more people followed him to pay respects. There are people wearing robes and crowns, shaped like government officials, and also setting up incense burners to bow in the light. The strangest thing is that the light must point straight to the Northeast corner, nothing can be seen in other directions.

Until the eighth day of the fourth month, the birthday of Śākyamuni Buddha, on that day, when I offered fruit, worshiped, chanted, I saw many people worshiping in the light, just like a few days before. At night, recite the recitation as usual, then bow your head and chant the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Suddenly, seeing the Bodhisattva appear in the form of the Sangha, holding a staff and hitting the ground, a golden light shot up, forming a large halo with a very strong impact. I had just seriously knelt down, my body was shaking violently, I couldn't control it. In the light, there were also quite a few people who were cheerful and joyful, spreading out in all directions. A few people still leisurely jumped into the air, seemingly being born into a good path. At that time, the Buddha's light was so bright that it was impossible to look at it for long, and there were many people [appearing in the light]. Some people flew up, some people spread out in all directions, some people were leisurely, some people were in a hurry, it was unclear what his father's condition was? After chanting the title of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, he followed the order of worship, reciting the title of Buddha and Bodhisattva. Looking closely, he could no longer see the pure light in the Northeast. The thief's heart felt comforted, knowing that my father would rely on Buddha's grace to escape. Counting back the time, it took twenty-one days. Buddha's grace is deep, Buddha's power is great, it is inconceivable, sadness and joy are mixed together, we worship and thank him endlessly.

Woke up on the morning of the 9th day, according to the usual rituals, randomly looked to the West, suddenly saw a group of low-lying houses, unexpectedly there were a hundred or dozens of houses. The rooms are all narrow and small, but quite neat and beautiful, close together in straight rows, as if forming a village. A few steps away from that village, there is a small house built in a strange way, the four sides are not luxurious, gorgeous, the walls are newly clean. My father was in there, walking around the house without stopping, seemingly bored, but with nothing to entertain himself. I know my father's soul must be lurking in the grave. The houses seen are the public graves of the church. Because times were not peaceful, they did not dare to bury the coffin at the funeral home, so they relied on someone to go to Tran Giang to buy a plot of land, bury it temporarily in a foreign land, and wait for the future to move back to their hometown. The land is close to a Catholic public cemetery, so it looks like that.

Therefore, I sincerely pray silently, pray for my father, worship him, ask for Buddha's grace, [make him] have steadfast faith forever, always keep good thoughts. After praying for a while, I saw my father prostrate on the ground. After that, every time the ceremony was performed, I immediately saw my father in the West in a small house, bowing to perform the ceremony. If you see your father spinning around, you should pray to Buddha. When you see your father, he immediately prostrates himself on the ground and worships. React quickly, just like talking to someone in front of you. Oh! Strange! After nine days of chanting, I looked at the map and realized that Tran Giang was indeed to the west of Yet Pho[48], proving that what I had seen was not an illusion.

Furthermore, on the Twenty-fifth day of March when I first saw the Buddha's light, it was only limited to the Northeast corner. At that time, I did not understand the reason. One day, I was reading the book Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Spiritual Inspiration. There was a story about the death of Governor Dang Tong in Duong Chau during the Tang Dynasty. A messenger from the underworld took him to visit hell, saying it was in the Northeast. He was startled and understood the reason. In the secular world, there is a theory that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva used his staff to break through the gates of the Nine Underworld prison. Now, because of what I have personally experienced, [I know] that theory is of course the truth. The majesty of Buddhism is truly inconceivable. I then respectfully wrote down the story based on the truth, hoping to have the opportunity to teach good believers to all, so as to propagate the Dharma, hoping that the Buddha's light would shine through and widely save those lost in the three paths. The female disciple of the Three Jewels, Phuong Duc Hue, respectfully recorded it two months after her father passed away.
