I then advised his relatives to quickly request the traveler to recite the seven volumes of Ksitigarbha Sutra and the ten thousand verses of Ksitigarbha's holy name, and they will be able to heal the Bodhisattva family. Next, I advised him to concentrate on reciting the holy name and then say goodbye.

On the sixth day of the twelfth month, on the day of Lien Xa's gathering, Kinh Nhan went there to attend the gathering, and immediately heard the layman Tran Gia Tuan say: "The layman has been waiting for you for many days. He was sick, received the blessings of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and got better and better every day. The day before, after reciting seven sets, he immediately saw the miraculous effect. Now he vows. He recited one hundred and eight sets. Now his spirit is getting better and better, like an ordinary person. Currently, he sold the gold watch he loved very much, and spent a sum of money, waiting for him to come, he asked him to worship the Buddha and Bodhisattva's holy name Trai will gradually move towards becoming a vegetarian. He wishes he would come."

When he met Kinh Nhan, he immediately clasped his hands in thanks and told of the Bodhisattva's premonition. From then on, every wish was exactly as Mr. Tran said. He again begged me to help him write a memoir recording the story of inspiration to show the Bodhisattva's holiness. Kinh Nhan is not good at writing, he only respectfully writes down the truth like that. Again, I pray that all fellow human beings will have righteous faith and fulfill the Bodhisattva's great vow to save all sentient beings. How fortunate is society and how fortunate is the Dharma?

(Excerpt from Hoang Hoa Nguyet Magazine published in March of the Republic of Korea year 33 - 1944).

* May Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva know his father's full name

Set Bar

I was three years old when I said goodbye to my parents, changed my last name, and was adopted by someone else. By the time he became a monk at the age of twenty-four, his biological parents had passed away early. From the moment I took refuge in the Buddha, I often had the thought of praying for my parents' rebirth, but I suffered from not knowing my parents' names and having no way to dedicate them. Recently, due to seeing Hong Phiet Duong at Putuo Mountain, there will be a Buddhist event explaining the Great Precepts on April 18th. I then discussed with the Abbot, Mr. Chieu Cong. The Master said: "If you don't know their names, you won't be able to transmit them." When I heard that, my heart became even more painful, so I asked: "Is there any other way to gain salvation?" Chieu Cong said: "Or maybe you should earnestly, sincerely, and sorrowfully ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to teach you the names of your parents, then it will be convenient. Forget this method, there is no other way!"

I immediately followed the teachings, sincerely and earnestly, worshiped and prayed before Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's seat. At around the hour of the Rat on the night of the 17th day, in the dream I clearly saw a piece of paper written with my father's name written on it, the three words Kim Chung Lien. Suddenly I was extremely happy and woke up. Wait until the next day, notify Chieu Cong, and tell the monks in the temple, they all praise this rare thing. Bodhisattva's great vow, great power, depending on his wish to satisfy his wishes, is truly inconceivable. I'm telling this story now, not to brag about being different, but because I'm afraid that people in the world will have people as sad as me, so that they can all make up their minds and follow suit.

Furthermore, the Bodhisattva's heart is profound, his compassion is great, and he is in tune with living beings. Except for those who are not sincere in their hearts and do things that go against the Buddha, I'm afraid it will be difficult to gain sympathy. If you are sincere and earnest in your prayers, in accordance with the Buddha's teachings, and with righteous faith in your wishes, you will naturally feel an understanding, like a stick being tapped on a drum [sounds will immediately resound]. Therefore, write it down to hope that whoever wishes it can indirectly help!

(Hoang Hoa Nguyet San, released in July of the Republic of Korea year 33 - 1944).

* Notes on the inspiration during the Ksitigarbha Dharma meeting at Lac Thanh Lay Buddhism

1. Emitting light shows good omen

On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month in the year of the Ox, for the first time, the Ksitigarbha dharma conference was opened at Lac Thanh Hongqiao (in Zhejiang province), the initiators were Trieu Thuong Hoa, Truong Trong San, Quy Thach Than, Vuong Mong Ngan, Trinh Ky Xuan, Thuong Chi Khoan, etc. From that morning, the Ksitigarbha Buddha Seven was celebrated. The message is just to pray for peace for the people there. In the morning, recite Ksitigarbha's name. At two o'clock in the afternoon, invite layperson Ho Thien Boc to preach the Ksitigarbha Sutra. The teaching will be divided into seven sessions. Every day the audience is more than a thousand people, with the greatest solemnity ever. On the evening of the Twenty-Fourth, from eight o'clock until the rooster crowed, the neighboring residents saw a bright light shining in the air, shining straight into the roof of the Ku Si Lam main hall, almost a dozen oil lamps. At that time, a patrol officer of the area passed by, saw that light, suspected that there was something unusual going on in Cu Si Lam, so he climbed up the wall to look in, only to see that the area was quiet, no sound, only saw a light spot the size of a pea in front of the Buddha's lamp-lit table! The patrol staff was extremely surprised, four or five nights in a row were emitting light like that. That person's suspicions could not be resolved. For seven days, he sent someone to secretly monitor him, but he did not see any strange actions!

On the first day of the seventh lunar month, the dharma assembly had not yet been disbanded, the area patrolling staff came to Cu Si Lam to question the source of the light at night, everyone said "don't know". The regional officials did not believe it at all, going around the rooms looking for oil lamps, but there were indeed no lamps! Layperson Truong Van Loi said: "The ashram radiates light, everywhere, there has never been anything strange! Light appears, there is nothing that is not shown by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as a good omen." The area staff no longer asked any questions, they were all full of strange compliments!

Therefore, after the inspiration, the lay people became more and more confident, and the membership increased to more than three hundred people. Because the ashram radiates light, everyone sees and harmonizes together. The villages in Lac Dong simultaneously established the Ksitigarbha Assembly, with a total of three places: One is at Tho Xuong Co Tu, Dam Khe village; The second is Quang Ung Pagoda in Vong Hanh village, the third is Sacred Palace of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in the Nam Pho mountain area. Each place had one or two hundred people attending. The prosperity of Buddhism in the Lac Dong region all originated from the story of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva releasing light.

2. Dreaming about someone asking for your head

In this hamlet, Mr. Tu Doan Vuong is a Christian. When his mother died, his friends advised him to recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra. At first, Mr. Tu did not think it was right. Later, thinking of his parents' gratitude, he could not help but repay it. He felt that what Buddhism said was very correct, so he vowed to recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra. He himself was still sick and had not recovered for many years. Suddenly I dreamed that an old man told me to drink a decoction from the Le Tay Qua plant, and my illness would be completely cured. Immediately offered Chuong[50] wood to Moc Tieu Pagoda to carve three holy statues. One night, he dreamed again that someone came to demand three heads. He was afraid that he would encounter a strange disaster, and he would feel restless morning and evening. A few days later, the monks of Moc Tieu Pagoda came to report that the Buddha statue had been carved, and three heads were missing. Mr. Tu then understood the meaning of the dream and offered the remaining Chuong wood. From then on, he devoted himself to worshiping Buddha, chanting without tiring.

3. Critical illness heals quickly

The son of the leader of the dharma conference in Nam Pho, lay practitioner Vuong Kinh Hoa, was seriously ill, unable to get out of bed for several months, medicine and prayers were ineffective. While organizing Ksitigarbha, Mr. Vuong single-mindedly took care of the affairs of the Dharma conference and did not go home to visit his children. Before the Buddha, he vowed to shoulder the responsibility of propagating the Buddha's teachings, silently praying to the [Three Jewels] to help his son recover from his illness. One day, a neighbor came to the mountain and told layman Vuong: "Your son is sick, and now he has suddenly recovered completely." Layman Vuong did not believe it and returned home to visit his child. Sure enough, seeing that my child was able to walk alone in the yard, he quickly thought about eating and drinking. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's premonition was so quick!

4. Rescue people who stumble over cliffs

On the first day of the seventh leap month last year, in Nam Dang town of Lac Thanh, the administrators of the Sacred Palace of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha in the Nam Pho mountain area were two lay people Chau Loc Minh and Chau Van Thuyen. Due to the incident of emitting strange light at this association (Lien Xa in Hong Kieu, Lac Thanh), they also initiated the celebration of Ksitigarbha Buddha That, and also invited Dharma Master De Nhat of this association to preside over Buddha That, along with layperson Lam Hao Si to preach the Ksitigarbha Sutra. The audience was more than six hundred people. That temple is on the top of Nam Pho mountain, drinking water has to be carried halfway down the mountain, a walk of more than six hundred steps. The mountain road is winding and difficult to navigate. A man made a vow that the water used during the seven-day Dharma conference would be carried by him alone. The weather is hot, there are many people, and every day we use up to twenty barrels of water. On the morning of the second day, as soon as the rooster crowed, he woke up to fetch water. It was raining, it was muddy, I quickly stumbled and was about to fall down the mountain, when suddenly someone next to me grabbed my armpit, very strong. At that time, he was stunned, breathing heavily, suddenly saw someone supporting and helping, immediately shouted "thank you, thank you", but no one heard anything! Looking closely, all around was dark, no trace of anyone could be seen, only the light of the lantern dimly shining on the burden. He quickly returned and told everyone about it in detail. No one who listened could not help but choke! Dharma Master De Nhat told the crowd: "Fortunately, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva manifested his soul to save your life. Otherwise, the honor of the Dharma assembly would be damaged. This man made a vow to carry water for the crowd, his merit was very great. Therefore, in danger, Bodhisattva helped him". This makes local believers more respectful and deeply interested in benefiting sentient beings. There are a few Christians who also take refuge in Buddhism.

5. Dreaming of Bodhisattva

The administrator of the Ksitigarbha dharma conference in this town is the layman Quy Thach Than who always does good deeds. One day, he recited the Ksitigarbha Sutra, knowing the miserable situation in hell, his mind was extremely frightened. Again, it is said in the sutra that if you want to know where your parents were born, you can recite the Bodhisattva's Original Vows Sutra and you will be taught by the Bodhisattva. Therefore, he made a vow, fasted, and chanted sutras. For more than thirty days, in a dream, he saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva sitting on a lotus, radiating good light, illuminating the entire earth, his Dharma form was solemn, and told the lay people: "Your parents are still in the underworld." Immediately leading him to a place, he saw his parents sitting in the palace, reciting the Buddha's name. Before he could say anything, the rooster crowed, he woke up startled, lit incense, knelt before the Bodhisattva, and made a great vow again, praying that his parents would soon be reborn in the Pure Land, fasting all his life, and abstaining from killing. Every day, despite being busy with hundreds of thousands of tasks, he recites one variation of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, taking on the responsibility of propagating Buddha Dharma to save suffering sentient beings. The past few years have never been tiring at all. Organizing the Ksitigarbha dharma conference, lay people put in most of their efforts.

6. The dead child was born into heaven

Layman Trieu Gia Cau is a resident of Cu Do, Thien Thanh village in this hamlet, and believes in Buddhism extremely strongly. His son fell ill and died early. Trieu layman, in his grief, made a wish to pray for his son's liberation. He recited the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva nearly ten thousand times. In panic, he saw the child sitting up from the corpse, gradually ascending, wearing a fur coat, walking on rattan shoes, eyes clearly visible, he looked stunned, but could no longer see it. Millions of lay people saw that strange appearance and believed that the Bodhisattva had a premonition, knowing that the dead child was born in heaven. There was no doubt!

7. Dreaming about seeing the Dharma form

Mr. Lam Hien Phap in Dong Street of this town does not believe in Buddha at all. One night, in a dream, I saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva descending from heaven, wearing a ka-sa, wearing a lotus crown on his head, resplendent in his majesty, and did not dare to look at him. Next to it was a pair of parallel sentences, including a Khuyen written diagonally and a Ngon word in the middle that he did not recognize. The next day, when he asked someone else, he found out that it was the word Hell. He could remember the summary, and when he read it together, it became the words “hell is not empty”, and then he realized that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva had become a saint. He immediately made a vow to recite Buddha's name, participate in the assembly, and serve with utmost dedication.

8. Use the water wheel to pump out the pond to release creatures without drying up

Hong Kieu Cu Si Lam is a few steps from Tinh Tong Pagoda. The monks in the pagoda specialize in Pure Land practice, are full of morality, and are respected by everyone. The two gentlemen Hue Trac and Duy Tay were even more outstanding. In the temple there is a pond to liberating living beings (life release), raising many aquatic species. After liberation (after the People's Republic of China was established), local people used paddlewheels to drain water from ponds to catch fish for profit. The monks in the temple turned to them to advise them, saying all kinds of reasonable things, but they did not listen, they still gathered together and slapped water. From morning to night, not a meter of water could be drained, and the waterwheels were greatly damaged. Everyone shouted loudly, it was a strange thing: "The water in the pond is pumped all day long without drying up; there must be a reason for it!" They then broke the water wheel and left.

8. Eliminate nightmares

Mr. Tiet Ky Cao's mother in this town is a neighbor of layperson Trieu Thuong Hoa. Mrs. Tiet often has nightmares at night and screams loudly. Neighbors were shocked and could hardly sleep. Mr. Trieu told the old lady: "The Ksitigarbha Sutra teaches that when you have many nightmares at night, recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name ten thousand times and you will have no more nightmares." The old lady said: "If there really is such a thing, I will try it." The old woman then recited the name Amitābha Buddha and the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva day and night. From then on, no more nightmares.

* Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's inspiration

Do Hue Bon writes

In the spring of the 45th Republic year (1956), layperson Ly Van Khai advised me to recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra. Therefore, starting from the end of the third lunar month of this year, every early morning, I recite a Ksitigarbha sutra, reciting the holy name for several hundred verses. Thinking to myself that my karma is deep, my karma is heavy, my blessings are thin, my wisdom is shallow, when I recite, false thoughts arise, and I cannot concentrate single-mindedly on reciting. But within the past two years, I have dreamed of seeing the ghosts of my relatives and friends, and no one has been saved by the Bodhisattva, making the immortal spirits happy. In a person's life, ten things usually end with eight or nine unsatisfactory things. Sentient beings have created evil karma through many eons up to now, achieving all kinds of afflictions. Since I chanted the sutra until now, unpleasant things have gradually decreased. When it comes to life's affairs, following my wishes, adversity rarely appears. Sometimes, by using reason without self-nature to contemplate the dharmas that arise from causes and conditions, the anger in the mind is gradually suppressed. My chanting efforts are shallow and fragile, and there is still no special or extraordinary miracle, but in my personal microcosm, I have enjoyed blessings, a light body and mind, and peace. Enough to see the great compassion of Bodhisattva, protecting sentient beings, no small thing cannot be understood.

For the sake of his mother, Śākyamuni Buddha preached the Dharma in the Dao Loi heaven, starting to speak this Ksitigarbha Sutra to make full filial piety. The main truth in the sutra is that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vows of filial piety to save his mother were practiced while cultivating. Everyone who reads and recites this sutra should, first of all, respect their parents like a Buddha living in the house. If your parents have passed away, use the merit of chanting sutras to dedicate them. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will cause happiness to leave suffering. The Book of Premonitions Luc has facts to prove.

The sutra teaches: “Good men, good women, desire now and in the future, make hundreds of thousands of millions of wishes, hundreds of thousands of millions of things, take refuge, worship, make offerings, praise the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, as you wish, seek, all stages are achieved” (Good men, good women, If you want to pray for hundreds of millions of wishes, hundreds of thousands of millions of things in the present and the future, just take refuge, worship, make offerings, and praise the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If you make such wishes, all your wishes will be fulfilled. The sutras also teach: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's emanations are all over hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of countless worlds. Each world transforms into hundreds of thousands of millions of bodies, each body transforms into hundreds of thousands of millions of people, causing them to revere the Three Jewels, forever leave birth and death, and achieve the joy of Nirvana. That transformation covers almost the entire universe of space. We read and recite sutras, pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, pray to be absorbed in the Bodhisattva's ocean of compassionate vows, attain Prajna Paramita, and at the same time develop the Bodhisattva mind and be generous to sentient beings. In this way, you will be able to save yourself, save others, and achieve Bodhi.

* Record of personal inspirations experienced over forty years

Nhi Van Dai writes

In the winter of the year of Tuyen Thong (1908) of the former Qing Dynasty, my wife, Lady Tieu, suffered from eclampsia[51], trembling and unconscious. After giving birth, she fell into a coma, did not wake up, closed her eyes, and did not speak for two days and nights. I sat next to the bed, not knowing what to do. The patient suddenly opened his eyes and called my name and the child's name: "Quickly pay homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva." I asked: "Where is Bodhisattva?" My wife said: “On the windowsill.” After we finished the ceremony, the patient was able to open his eyes, clear his mind, and speak as usual. I asked: "What clothes does the Bodhisattva wear?" My wife replied: "Wear a white robe, embroidered with swastikas." The following year, my wife specially sewed a long robe embroidered with swastikas, and I personally went to Putuo and offered it to the temple. Luckily, there was Dr. Ngu Dinh Phuong sitting in the same boat. He spoke strongly about the benefits of vegetarianism. From then on, I stopped eating meat, and that fate was very strange! My wife followed my mother's teachings, every month on the 9th day of the month, she recited Avalokitesvara Trai, offered incense, and worshiped. When my mother was critically ill, [my wife] often cut the meat from her arm and cooked medicine to give to her, out of sincerity and filial piety. So while she was sick, she was saved by the Great Master's epiphany, which was not a coincidence.

In the 13th year of the Republic (1924), I failed in business and closed my doors to reflect on my mistakes. Every day recite the Diamond Sutra and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Universal Sect. I was alone in a small room on the third floor, a round room with a glass top and very bright. There was nothing in that room, only a reading table and a chair where I chanted. One day, while reciting the Pho Mon chapter, I suddenly smelled sandalwood, but I didn't have an incense burner at all. After reciting the sutras, I went to the ancestral hall to see, but there was no one burning incense. That was the first time I smelled the scent.

In the first lunar month of the 15th year of the Republic of China (1926), I went to Suzhou, staying at the house of layperson Ly Bach Nong. The layman taught me to chant Shurangama with concentration[52] with only seven sentences. He told me: "This mantra has impermanent power, reciting it will have great benefits." That night, on the Lunar New Year (full moon day of the first lunar month), the lay people and I went to the wasteland in Nam Vien to walk to see the moon. There are very few people in that land, they all live by growing vegetables. At night, every house closes its doors, it's quiet, there's no sound. I silently recited the mantra I had learned during the day, and when I came to a wild prayer, I suddenly heard a strange scent filling my nose. Within a hundred steps, there was absolutely no house. I asked layperson Ly: "Do you smell the scent?" The layman said: "I smell it, are you reciting a mantra?" That scent is magical, more fragrant than agarwood, obviously caused by a spell.

In the 15th year of the Republic (1926), every morning, I and other lay people like Ngo Giac Chu, etc., read a book of the Avatamsaka Sutra Samantabhadra and Virtue Vows. Mr. Pho Han Phi is an international student who graduated from the textile industry in the US and works in Hang Phong factory. Every morning I also come to chant. One day, in the middle of winter, right at the time of chanting, suddenly I heard the smell of cinnamon flowers. Four people chanting and smelling together. After reciting the sutras, when you go into the house and ask other people, they can also smell the scent. There really aren't all fragrant things!

In the 17th year of the Republic (1928), I was in the main house, after bowing in front of the Great Master's statue, I went upstairs to my mother's room. Mom asked: "The incense you just burned has a very pleasant smell. It's not an ordinary scent." I replied: "Yes! There is agarwood in it." But how can mom smell? This is strange, because for the past ten years, my mother's sense of smell has not been able to distinguish between fragrant and rotten, and even if she holds it close to her nose, she cannot recognize the smell. Therefore, ask your mother: "Yesterday I mixed red spirit pills[53] with musk and mothballs in this room, do you also smell the scent?" Mother replied: "I can't smell it!" I said: "I'm facing the Great Master because I'm secretly praying for your mother's understanding." Mother was very happy, because the place where the incense was burned downstairs was very far from her mother's room upstairs, yet she could smell the very fragrant scent. If that's not a strange manifestation of Great Si's vision, then what is it?

In the 16th year of the Republic of China (1927), I led layman Guo Ham Trai in Xiangyin to worship Putuo. Therefore, go to Duc Vuong pagoda to worship the relics. First, go to Thien Dong Pagoda to worship Buddha. Thien Dong Pagoda is a famous ancient ashram, very close to Duc Vuong Pagoda. At the end of the Qing Dynasty, the monk Bat Chi Dau Da became the abbot of this pagoda. Bat Chi Dau Da was originally the child of a farmer. His father was a tenant for the layman Quach's house. As a child, the layman often played with the monk. Later, the Master's father entrusted Dau Da to the monk in the temple as his disciple. The monk did not study. He only learned how to read and read at the temple. The master considered it a pity that his talent was dark and stupid, and that the meaning in the sutra could not be understood, so he said goodbye to his teacher, paid homage to Putuo, and went to Duc Vuong pagoda to worship the relics in order to expand his wisdom. The monk stayed at Duc Vuong Pagoda for several years. On the day of Buddha's birthday, the Master burned two fingers to worship the Buddha, leaving only eight fingers, so he called him Bat Dau Da. The following year, he still felt that his wisdom and enlightenment had not yet opened, so he cut out the flesh on his back, lit a wick, and poured oil in to light the lamp. Returning to Truong Sa, when passing Dong Dinh lake and going up to Nhac Duong pagoda, the Master suddenly thought of a verse: “Dong Dinh ba tong nhat Tang lai” (Dong Dinh waves sent the monks away). Arriving at Truong Sa, he met a monk who was famous for his good poetry, so he asked him about that verse. The monk said: "This sentence is very good. You will definitely become a poet in the future." The monk then taught the Master to read three hundred Tang poems, because the Master had never read any ancient poems before!

After returning from Duc Vuong Pagoda, the Master was able to understand the scriptures, abstain from them accordingly, and was respected by the Sangha, but Dau Da still practiced asceticism, such as leftover rice in the dog's bowl, rice picked up in the kitchen, which he ate. He was famous for his talent in writing poetry. The great poet of the late Qing Dynasty, Vuong Nham Thu, often sang poems with him. Later, he went to Ninh Ba to work as a monk at Thien Dong Pagoda for more than ten years before passing away. The stupa (the tomb of the monk who founded the stupa) is outside Thien Dong Pagoda. Next to the tower is a three-compartment temple, inside worshiping a painted statue of Dau Da. I went to the temple to listen to the sutra lecture. Layman Quach went to Dau Da's temple tower to recite Buddha's name for more than two hours, saying he was chatting with old friends. Just leaving the pagoda, in front of the pagoda there was a large forest, about a mile wide. We walked in the deep forest, Mr. Quach's palanquin walked in front of me. After walking a few dozen steps, Mr. Quach raised his head, looked back, and asked me: "Do you smell good?" I replied: "I don't smell it." Going a few dozen more steps, Mr. Quach asked again, I answered "I can't smell it". Later, Mr. Quach said: "The scent reached deep in the forest before it stopped." Obviously Dau Da shows premonition.

In the past, great virtuous people in Zen Buddhism achieved incalculable enlightenment, and there were also those who attained Van Tu Prajna (wisdom). Dau Da developed wisdom and enlightenment through ascetic practice. He was a person who had never learned to write poetry but was suddenly able to write poetry, and had such great talent that it was hard to imagine! After Dau Da passed away, poet Tran Tan Nguyen engraved and printed the Master's writings. Mr. Vuong Nham Thu wrote the foreword as follows: “Dau Tuo's poetic style is sublime, comparable to that of the monks... of the Tang Dynasty”. The next year, he wrote another preface, with a passage that reads: "Last year I wrote a preface, saying that Dau Tu's poems could be compared to the monks... of the Tang Dynasty, but now that I think about it, saying that is not very appropriate! Because Dau Tu's poetic style is sublime, that monk cannot compare!" Both prefaces were engraved in that collection of poems, enough to show their utmost admiration and admiration.

Poetry is religion, ordinary people cannot easily understand it! In the ancient Qing Dynasty, everyone wrote poetry, so much so that the Academy especially considered people who were talented at writing poetry to be important. It's mostly called "clever", meaning rhyming rhymes, well-crafted and polished words, but from the poet's point of view, [writing poetry like that] is only worth covering up, it can't reach the level of great elegance! At first Dau Da had not read ancient poetry, but was able to write elegant poetry. Later, of course, the Master also read ancient poetry, but he read very few books, of course he couldn't write beautifully or glossily. That is the beauty and beauty of his poetry, which is pure simplicity and naturalness, using the immediate situation in front of him to honestly write it down. Same, with style, rhyme, supreme meaning, that is called “improvisation” (new trend literary man Mr. Lam Ngu Duong selected ten great authors of the Ming and Qing dynasties, took improvisation as the main standard. Nine of them were all Buddhist students). After being enlightened in Zen Buddhism, one can open one's mouth and speak freely, with unhindered eloquence, as well as other stories of Prajnaparamita. Due to the manifestation of this fragrant premonition, Dau Tu also knew that Dau Tu's enlightenment and attainment were very high. Again, considering the great poets of the Jin, Wei, Six Dynasties, Tang, and Song dynasties, among the ten, eighty-nine were Buddhist scholars, or inherited the belief in Buddhism, it is enough to see the relationship between Buddhism and Chinese poetry, because Buddhism considers eliminating the Ego as a meticulous effort to thoroughly understand before and after. Ego Attachment has been eliminated, true nature is revealed.

Layman Quach and I went to Duc Vuong pagoda to worship relics (relics are Buddha's body when cremated, the bones form into small, glittering, round particles). Two years ago I had a funeral once. The relics are kept in a small iron tower, with a gap on the side so you can look in. The relics are as big as a peppercorn, and a small metal handle is used to make a hook inlaid with the relics and hang them suspended, like a bell or gong. Last time, I saw the relics and the hanging handle were both golden in color. This time, layperson Guo and I both saw a gloomy blue color and thought it was unusual, so we repented before the Buddha. At night, each person bows ten times to Buddha. Early the next morning, I asked to observe again. Both people saw that they were all golden, exactly like I had seen the previous year. I thought the relics were originally plated with gold on the outside, but somehow the previous day it had turned blue, and early the next morning it had turned golden. Monks, nuns and lay people from all over come to the mountain to worship Buddha and relics every day, up to dozens of people. After worshiping, the monk on duty in the temple will bring out the [tower of relics] from the altar in the temple, lead [everyone] to the skylight at the back of the temple, kneel on the cushion to see. Each viewer sees different colors, some see white, some see red, or see black, or see nothing. I've asked many people and they're all different. It depends on each person's karma.

* Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's magical power of induction

Layman writes

Son returned, hundreds of mixed emotions. One day, in Samadhi, I thought I had been in the Flesh Body Palace (the shrine to the physical body of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva), had worshiped and requested the Deity Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat to bless his disciples so that their minds could be mindful, never regress, and promote their strengths and benefit sentient beings. Going higher is imitating the Deity to spread vows, save sentient beings, [causing them] to leave suffering and be happy. Because of the initial practice of Meditation, I sincerely desired to be able to once again admire and worship the Deity Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva. Therefore, depending on the breath, repeatedly recite the name Namo Deity Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva. Until the breath is smooth, then while visualizing the solemn appearance of Ksitigarbha's clone in the Body Hall at Nine Flowers, leisurely, recite "Namo great compassion, great vow, great saintly great kindness to the deity Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat", one after another like when circumambulating the stupa chanting the name of Ksitigarbha. Suddenly, everything was gone, everything was gone, even the tongue pressing against the palate, the body, speech, and mind were all gone, and a large stream of air rushed straight to the top of the head in the chest. Although he was surprised for a moment, by chanting the name Ksitigarbha, his mind quickly calmed down. From the chest to the top of the head, suddenly a golden light flashed, as empty as a divine consciousness traveling in the void, making people inconceivably happy. After a while, it was as if I had just woken up from a dream and returned to the real world, hearing noises around me. However, after having that overwhelming experience, I treat the world with more tolerance, compassion, and selflessness. I hope I can always keep that concern until I reach the realm of No-Wisdom Paramita "no self, no human, no sentient beings, no fake life" as the Diamond Sutra wrote, if we reach Nirvana of no birth and no destruction, then we will not disappoint Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for his compassion.

He graduated from Hoa Nghiem University of shaman Nguyet Ha, then studied Thien Thai teachings with monk To An of Ngoc Tuyen pagoda in Duong Duong district (Hubei province); recognized as a descendant of the Lam Te sect. During this time, the Master also focused on studying the teachings of the Thien Thai, Phap Tuong, Hoa Nghiem, Tam Luan, Luat Tong and Pure Land sects. In 1922, after reading the book Falun Bao Sam, he had the will to revive Tang Mi. Realizing that the Eastern Secret lineage was still flourishing in Japan, the Master went to Kōyasan Temple in Ky Y Peninsula (Kii Hanto) to study with Kim Son Muc Thieu A Xa Le of Co Nghia Shingon Sect to learn two sets of empowerments of Vajra Precepts and Thai Tang Precepts. After that, the Master also studied Thai Mat (Tet Buddhism of the Thien Thai sect) at Ty Due mountain (Hiei). Returning to China, he focused on propagating Dong Mi. He stayed in mainland China after the Chinese Communist government was established. In 1966, the Cultural Revolution broke out, and he and his disciples were kicked out of Tinh An pagoda by the government. The monk passed away in 1972 in Shanghai.
